declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFinite_adicFibre_iso_of_tower
declarations.doc:
**Algebraization of a finite tower over the adic fibres.**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring
complete along `I`, `S = Spec A`, and `f : X ⟶ S` a separated morphism of finite type of algebraic
spaces with adic fibres `X_n = X ×_S S_n`.  Let `y_n : Y_n ⟶ X_n` be algebraic spaces over the
adic fibres with transitions `t_n : Y_n ⟶ Y_{n + 1}` making cartesian squares over the transitions
`X_n ⟶ X_{n + 1}`, with `Y_0 ⟶ X_0` finite and `Y_0 ⟶ S_0` proper.  Then there is a finite
`π : Y ⟶ X` with `Y` proper over `S`, and isomorphisms `Y_n ≅ Y ×_S S_n` lying over `X_n`,
compatible with the transitions, and exhibiting `Y_n` as `Y ×_X X_n`.

The tower is indexed from `0`: `S_n` is `Spec (A / I ^ (n + 1))`, so the `n`-th term here is the
`(n + 1)`-st term `Y_{n + 1}` of Stacks, and `Y_0 ⟶ X_0`, `Y_0 ⟶ S_0` are Stacks' `Y_1 ⟶ X_1`,
`Y_1 ⟶ S_1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinite_adicFibre_iso_of_tower [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (hsep : IsSeparated B (Spec (.of A)) hA f) (hft : IsFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f)
    (Y : ℕ → AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA) (y : ∀ n, Y n ⟶ adicFibreSpace A I B hA hX f n)
    (tY : ∀ n, Y n ⟶ Y (n + 1))
    (hcart : ∀ n, IsPullback (tY n) (y n) (y (n + 1)) (adicFibreSuccHom A I B hA hX f n))
    (hfin0 : IsFinite B (Spec (.of A)) hA (y 0).hom)
    (hprop : IsProper B (Spec (.of A)) hA ((y 0).hom ≫ adicFibreSnd A I B hA f 0)) :
    ∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpaces B (Spec (.of A)) hA) (π : Z ⟶ ⟨X, hX⟩),
      IsFinite B (Spec (.of A)) hA π.hom ∧ IsProper B (Spec (.of A)) hA (π.hom ≫ f) ∧
      ∃ e : ∀ n, Y n ≅ adicFibreSpace A I B hA Z.2 (π.hom ≫ f) n,
        (∀ n, (e n).hom.hom ≫
          adicFibreMap A I B hA (contains_adicThickening A I B hA) π.hom rfl n = (y n).hom) ∧
        (∀ n, tY n ≫ (e (n + 1)).hom =
          (e n).hom ≫ adicFibreSuccHom A I B hA Z.2 (π.hom ≫ f) n) ∧
        (∀ n, IsPullback ((e n).hom ≫ adicFibreFst A I B hA Z.2 (π.hom ≫ f) n) (y n) π
          (adicFibreFstHom A I B hA hX f n))

declarations.name: exists_henselization
declarations.doc:
Every pair `(A, I)` has a henselization: there is a henselian pair `(Aʰ, IAʰ)` under `(A, I)`
which is initial among henselian pairs under `(A, I)`. Equivalently, the inclusion of henselian
pairs into pairs has a left adjoint.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_henselization (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) :
    ∃ (Ah : Type u) (_ : CommRing Ah) (ι : A →+* Ah),
      HenselianPair Ah (I.map ι) ∧
        ∀ (B : Type v) (_ : CommRing B) (J : Ideal B),
          HenselianPair B J →
            ∀ f : A →+* B, I ≤ J.comap f →
              ∃! g : Ah →+* B, g.comp ι = f ∧ I.map ι ≤ J.comap g

declarations.name: isHenselization_of_henselizationPair
declarations.doc:
A henselization of the pair consisting of a local ring and its maximal ideal is a henselization
of the local ring. In particular, the target is local and the structural map is a local ring
homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isHenselization_of_henselizationPair
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (Ah : Type u) [CommRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
    (hh : HenselianPair Ah
      ((maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A Ah)))
    (hι : ∀ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (J : Ideal B),
      HenselianPair B J →
        ∀ f : A →+* B, maximalIdeal A ≤ J.comap f →
          ∃! g : Ah →+* B,
            g.comp (algebraMap A Ah) = f ∧
              (maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A Ah) ≤ J.comap g) :
    ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing Ah) (_ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap A Ah)),
      IsHenselization A (ResidueField A) Ah

declarations.name: henselization_preserves_filtered_colimits
declarations.doc:
Henselization of pairs commutes with filtered colimits. More precisely, for a filtered diagram
of pairs and its naturally induced diagram of henselizations, any colimit of the latter is a
henselization of the colimit of the former. Its extended ideal is the supremum of the images of the
extended ideals at the stages.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselization_preserves_filtered_colimits
    {K : Type v} [SmallCategory K] [IsFiltered K]
    (F Fh : Functor K CommRingCat.{max u v})
    (I : ∀ k, Ideal (F.obj k))
    (hI : ∀ ⦃j k⦄ (f : j ⟶ k), Ideal.map (F.map f).hom (I j) ≤ I k)
    (η : F ⟶ Fh)
    (hFh : ∀ k, HenselianPair (Fh.obj k) (Ideal.map (η.app k).hom (I k)))
    (hη : ∀ k (B : Type w) (_ : CommRing B) (J : Ideal B),
      HenselianPair B J →
        ∀ f : F.obj k →+* B, I k ≤ J.comap f →
          ∃! g : Fh.obj k →+* B,
            g.comp (η.app k).hom = f ∧ Ideal.map (η.app k).hom (I k) ≤ J.comap g)
    (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c)
    (ch : Cocone Fh) (hch : IsColimit ch) :
    let ηc : c.pt →+* ch.pt := (hc.desc (Cocone.mk ch.pt (η ≫ ch.ι))).hom
    let Ic : Ideal c.pt := ⨆ k, Ideal.map (c.ι.app k).hom (I k)
    Ideal.map ηc Ic =
        (⨆ k, (Ideal.map ((ch.ι.app k).hom.comp (η.app k).hom) (I k) : Ideal ch.pt)) ∧
      HenselianPair ch.pt (Ideal.map ηc Ic) ∧
      ∀ (B : Type w) (_ : CommRing B) (J : Ideal B),
        HenselianPair B J →
          ∀ f : c.pt →+* B, Ic ≤ J.comap f →
            ∃! g : ch.pt →+* B,
              g.comp ηc = f ∧ Ideal.map ηc Ic ≤ J.comap g

declarations.name: isDerivedComplete_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A05.** A pseudo-coherent object over a ring that is derived complete with respect
to `I` is itself derived complete with respect to `I`. Pseudo-coherence is spelled out as in
Stacks 064Q (2): `K` is represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_of_isPseudoCoherent
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    [HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))] :
    IsDerivedCompleteModule I (ModuleCat.of A A) →
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A),
        (∃ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ,
            ((∃ b : ℤ, E.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
              ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (E.X i) ∧ Module.Free A (E.X i)) ∧
            Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ≅ K)) →
          IsDerivedComplete I K

declarations.name: AdicCompletionCohomology.derivedCompletion_homology_iso_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
If every cohomology module of a complex over a Noetherian ring is finite,
then the cohomology modules of its derived completion are the adic completions of the original
cohomology modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedCompletion_homology_iso_adicCompletion
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : ∀ n : ℤ,
      Module.Finite A ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) n).obj K)) :
    letI : HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (ModuleCat.{u} A) :=
      moduleCat_hasExactLimitsOfShape_discrete.{u} A ℕ
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete I L
    ∀ (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory),
      (C ⊣ P.ι) → ∀ n : ℤ,
        Nonempty
          (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) n).obj
              ((C ⋙ P.ι).obj K)) ≅
            ModuleCat.of A
              (AdicCompletion I
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) n).obj K)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A07.**  Let `f : (Sh(C), 𝒪) ⟶ (Sh(C'), 𝒪')` be a morphism of ringed
topoi.  Then `Rf_*` commutes with `R\lim`: if a distinguished triangle
`L ⟶ ∏ K_n ⟶ ∏ K_n ⟶ L[1]` exhibits `L` as the derived limit of a countable inverse system
`(K_n)` of objects of `D(𝒪)`, then the product of the `Rf_* K_n` exists in `D(𝒪')` and `Rf_* L`
is the derived limit of the system `(Rf_* K_n)`.

Here `f` is an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag 01D3 (a morphism
of the underlying topoi together with the structure map), with no functor between the sites.
The proof is the source's adjunction argument: `Rf_*` is exact, and it is a right adjoint by
Tag 07A6 (`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPullbackOfToposHom.derivedAdjunction`), so it preserves the
products of `D(𝒪)`; `Stacks.Injectives.isDerivedLimit_map_rightAdjoint` is the abstract form.
The two `UnivLE` hypotheses only place the site of `X` below its module universe, which is what
makes `Mod(𝒪)` a Grothendieck abelian category (`SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian_of_univLE`)
and hence `Rf_*` exist.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_map_derivedPushforward (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit K L) :
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ (derivedPushforward (X := X) (Y := Y) f).obj (K.obj ⟨n⟩)),
      @IsDerivedLimit
        (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{w'} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
        _ _ _ _ _ _
        (K ⋙ derivedPushforward (X := X) (Y := Y) f) h
        ((derivedPushforward (X := X) (Y := Y) f).obj L)
declarations.comment:
for a morphism of ringed topoi in the two-field sense of Tag 01D3, part (2) --
a morphism of the underlying topoi together with the structure map, with no continuous functor
between the underlying sites; `R lim` is the derived limit `IsDerivedLimit` of a countable
inverse system, given by its defining distinguished triangle

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLimitAcyclic.isLimit_cohomology_of_isDerivedLimit_of_acyclic_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project Tag 0A09.** Cohomology commutes with a derived inverse limit if there is a
class of objects covering the site on which all positive cohomology of the cohomology sheaves
vanishes and the towers of their sections have vanishing first derived inverse limit.

The conclusion records the canonical limiting cone: the legs of the cone on the system of
degree-`q` cohomology sheaves are induced by the projections of a derived-limit triangle for
`L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimit_cohomology_of_isDerivedLimit_of_acyclic_cover
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit K L)
    (B : ObjectProperty X.C)
    (hB : X.J.HasEnoughObjects B)
    (hacyclic : ∀ U, B U → ∀ q : ℤ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ r : ℕ, 0 < r →
      haveI := evaluation_additive (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) (op U)).rightDerived r).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) q).obj
          (K.obj ⟨n⟩))))
    (hlimOne : ∀ U, B U → ∀ q : ℤ,
      IsZero (Rlim.firstDerivedLimit
        (K ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) q ⋙
          sectionsOverObject X U)))
    (q : ℤ) :
    ∃ p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩,
      (∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
        Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
              K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
          distTriang
            (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) ∧
      ∃ τ : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) q).obj L) ⟶
          K ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) q,
        (∀ n : ℕ, τ.app ⟨n⟩ =
          (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) q).map
            (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)) ∧
        Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ τ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDual_of_isHomotopyColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0A.**  Let `(Kₙ)` be a system of objects of `D(O)` and let `K = hocolim Kₙ`.  For
every object `E` of `D(O)`,

`RSheafHom(K, E) = R lim (E ⊗^L_O Kₙ^∨)`,

granted the two inputs the source's proof uses and the library does not have: that the canonical
map `RSheafHom(⊕ Kₙ, E) ⟶ ∏ RSheafHom(Kₙ, E)` is an isomorphism, and that the canonical map
`E ⊗^L_O Kₙ^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(Kₙ, E)` of Stacks 08JD is an isomorphism for every `n`, which is
clause 3 of Stacks 08JJ and is where the perfectness of the `Kₙ` is used in the source.

Given the second hypothesis the tensor-dual system is isomorphic to the system
`n ↦ RSheafHom(Kₙ, E)`, so the assertion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_derivedSheafHom_of_isHomotopyColimit` transported
along that isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDual_of_isHomotopyColimit
    (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hcomp : IsIso (Pi.lift (fun n : ℕ ↦
        ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).flip.obj E).map (Sigma.ι F.obj n).op) :
      ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).flip.obj E).obj (op (∐ F.obj)) ⟶
        ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ (derivedSheafHomSystem X F E).obj (op n)))
    (hdual : ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (derivedTensorDualToSheafHom X T (F.obj n) E))
    {K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (hK : IsHomotopyColimit F K) :
    IsDerivedLimit (tensorDerivedDualSystem X T F E)
      (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).flip.obj E).obj (op K))
declarations.comment: the stated identity `RSheafHom(K, E) = R lim (E ⊗^L_O Kₙ^∨)` for `K = hocolim Kₙ`, with two inputs of the source's proof assumed rather than proved: `hcomp`, that the canonical map `RSheafHom(⊕ Kₙ, E) ⟶ ∏ RSheafHom(Kₙ, E)` is an isomorphism, which is the last step of the proof; and `hdual`, clause 3 of Stacks 08JJ, that the canonical map of Stacks 08JD `E ⊗^L_O Kₙ^∨ ⟶ RSheafHom(Kₙ, E)` is an isomorphism, which no declaration of this library asserts. The perfectness of the `Kₙ` is used in the source only to invoke that clause, so it is not assumed here, and the existence of the direct sum `⊕ Kₙ` and of the two products is not assumed either, being supplied by the instances of Stacks 07D9; everything else of the tag is proved, in particular the whole comparison of triangles.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedHom_isDerivedLimit_tensorDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0A: derived internal Hom out of a homotopy colimit of perfect objects.** Let
`(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `(Kₙ)` be a system of perfect objects of `D(𝒪)`, let
`K = hocolim Kₙ` and let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪)`. Then

`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(K, E) = R lim (E ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 Kₙ^∨)`.

Perfectness of the terms turns the system of tensor products with the duals into the system
`n ↦ R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Kₙ, E)`, by Stacks 08JJ and its contravariant naturality; the latter system
has `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(K, E)` as its derived limit for every system with derived colimit `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHom_isDerivedLimit_tensorDual
    (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (K E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hF : ∀ n : ℕ, X.IsPerfect (F.obj n))
    (hK : IsHomotopyColimit F K) :
    IsDerivedLimit
        (tensorDerivedDualSystem X (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X) F E)
      (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op K)).obj E)
declarations.comment: the identity `R𝑆heafHom(K, E) = R lim (E ⊗^L_O Kₙ^∨)` for a system of perfect objects `Kₙ` with derived colimit `K`, at the hypotheses of the source: the perfectness of each `Kₙ` and `K = hocolim Kₙ`. The direct-sum comparison and the identification of Stacks 08JJ that the source's proof uses are both proved in the library, so this needs nothing beyond those two hypotheses: the ringed site carries no hypothesis, the sheafification and additivity instances the statement's constructions need being synthesized rather than assumed, and the existence of `⊕ Kₙ` and of the products coming from the instances of Stacks 07D9

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDual_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0A for a system of perfect objects.** Let `(Kₙ)` be a system of perfect objects
of `D(𝒪)` whose direct sum exists and let `K = hocolim Kₙ`. For every object `E` of `D(𝒪)`,

`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(K, E) = R lim (E ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 Kₙ^∨)`,

the derived tensor product being the canonical one of [Stacks, Tag 06YU].

Both inputs of the source's proof are discharged: the direct-sum comparison
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(⊕ Kₙ, E) ⟶ ∏ R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Kₙ, E)` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedSheafHomSigmaComparison`, and clause 3 of
[Stacks, Tag 08JJ] by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorDerivedDualSystemIsoOfPerfect`, which
is where perfectness is used — exactly as in the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDual_of_isPerfect
    (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasCoproduct F.obj]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (derivedSheafHomSystem X F E).obj (op n)]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (tensorDerivedDualSystem X
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct.{u} X) F E).obj (op n)]
    (hF : ∀ n : ℕ, X.IsPerfect (F.obj n))
    {K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (hK : IsHomotopyColimit F K) :
    IsDerivedLimit (tensorDerivedDualSystem X
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct.{u} X) F E)
      (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).flip.obj E).obj (op K))
declarations.comment: the stated identity `RSheafHom(K, E) = R lim (E ⊗^L_O Kₙ^∨)` for `K = hocolim Kₙ` with the `Kₙ` perfect, for the canonical derived tensor product, with both inputs of the source's proof proved rather than assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_globalSectionsRestriction_closedFibre_of_henselianPair_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
For `(A, I)` a henselian pair and `f : X ⟶ Spec A` proper, restriction to the closed fibre
`X ×_{Spec A} Spec (A ⧸ I)` is bijective on global sections of every sheaf of sets on the space
of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_globalSectionsRestriction_closedFibre_of_henselianPair_of_isProper
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : HenselianPair A I) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f]
    (F : TopCat.Sheaf (Type u) (TopCat.of X)) :
    Function.Bijective (Stacks.globalSectionsRestriction
      (Set.range (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))))) F)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_globalSectionsComparison_closedFibre_of_henselianPair_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0C].** Let `(A, I)` be a henselian pair and let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be proper.
For every sheaf of sets `ℱ` on the small étale site of `X`, restriction of global sections to the
closed fibre `Z = X ×_{Spec A} Spec (A ⧸ I)` is bijective: the canonical comparison
`Γ(X, ℱ) ⟶ Γ(Z, i_{small}^{-1}ℱ)`, natural in `ℱ`, is an isomorphism.

This is [Stacks, Tag 09ZF] for the closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X`, whose two hypotheses are
[Stacks, Tag 0A0B] for `f` and for `Y ⟶ X ⟶ Spec A`, `Y ⟶ X` finite.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.bijective_globalSectionsComparison_app_closedFibre_of_henselianPair_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0C], sheaf by sheaf.** Let `(A, I)` be a henselian pair and let
`f : X ⟶ Spec A` be proper. For every sheaf of sets `ℱ` on the small étale site of `X`, the
restriction map `Γ(X, ℱ) ⟶ Γ(Z, i_{small}^{-1}ℱ)` to the closed fibre
`Z = X ×_{Spec A} Spec (A ⧸ I)` is bijective. This is the component at `ℱ` of
`isIso_globalSectionsComparison_closedFibre_of_henselianPair_of_isProper`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_globalSectionsComparison_app_closedFibre_of_henselianPair_of_isProper
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v))) :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem_koszulPowerSystem_derivedCompletion_over
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0E] at a sheaf of ideals of finite type.** Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let
`ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` be a sheaf of ideals of finite type and let `E ∈ D(𝒪)`. Let `U` be an object of `𝒞` and
`g_1, …, g_s` sections of `𝒪` over `U` generating `ℐ|_U`. Then the derived completion `E^∧` of
[Stacks, Tag 099F] satisfies

`E^∧|_U = R lim (E|_U ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_U} K_n)`,  `K_n = Hom_{𝒪_U}(K(𝒪_U, g_1^{n+1}, …, g_s^{n+1}), 𝒪_U)`,

the derived tensor products of `E|_U` with the duals of the Koszul complexes on the positive
powers of `g_1, …, g_s`.

The Koszul complexes of the formula are formed from a finite family of sections generating the
ideal sheaf, and a finite-type `ℐ` carries one only locally; the objects `U` that carry one cover
the site, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coversTop_eq_idealOfGlobalSections_overIdeal_of_isFiniteType`,
and `exists_coversTop_isDerivedLimit_koszulPowerSystem_derivedCompletion`
below states this formula over such a covering family. When `ℐ` is generated by finitely many
global sections of `𝒪` the formula holds on `𝒞` itself; that is the source's own display,
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem_koszulPowerSystem_completion`.

Three inputs, each proved: the identification of the reflector of [Stacks, Tag 099F] with
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(K, -)` for the complex of [Stacks, Tag 099E]; the restriction of that to the slice
over `U` as the Čech completion of [Stacks, Tag 099B] at `g`, which is
`derivedCompletionOverIsoCompletionFunctor`; and the source's display on the ringed site
`(𝒞/U, 𝒪_U)`, where `g_1, …, g_s` are global sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem_koszulPowerSystem_derivedCompletion_over
    (U : X.C) {s : ℕ}
    (g : Fin s → Presheaf.globalSections ((X.over U).O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}))
    (hg : idealOfGlobalSections (X.over U) g = overIdeal I U)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    IsDerivedLimit
      (tensorDerivedDualSystem (X.over U)
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct (X.over U))
        (koszulPowerSystem (X.over U) g ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
        ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E))
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((derivedCompletion X I).obj E))
declarations.comment: the stated formula `K^∧ = R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 K_n)` for the derived completion of `K ∈ D(𝒪)` along a sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` **of finite type**, with `K^∧` the derived completion functor of [Stacks, Tag 099F] and `K_n` the Koszul complex on the powers of generators of `ℐ` in the cochain grading of the source's proof, that is the `𝒪`-dual of `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.koszulPowerComplex`. The tower of the formula is built from a finite family of sections generating `ℐ`, which a finite-type ideal sheaf carries over the objects of a covering family, so the formula is stated over each object `U` carrying such a family `g_1, …, g_s`, where it reads `K^∧|_U = R lim (K|_U ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_U} K_n(g))`; that those objects cover the site is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coversTop_eq_idealOfGlobalSections_overIdeal_of_isFiniteType`. `R lim` is a predicate rather than a functor, so the source's equality is read as the restriction being a derived limit of the tower. The finite-type hypothesis is the source's own, and the only one: the countable products and coproducts a derived limit needs in order to be written down are supplied here rather than assumed. The source's display at an ideal sheaf generated by finitely many global sections of `𝒪` is the companion registration `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem_koszulPowerSystem_completion`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem_koszulPowerSystem_canonical
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0E].** Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `f_1, …, f_r` be global sections
of `𝒪` and let `K` be an object of `D(𝒪)`. Then the derived completion
`K^∧ = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)` of [Stacks, Tag 099B] along the ideal sheaf generated by
`f_1, …, f_r` is a derived limit of the tower

`n ↦ K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 K_n^∨`, `K_n = K(𝒪, f_1^{n+1}, …, f_r^{n+1})`,

the derived tensor product being the canonical one of [Stacks, Tag 06YU].

The three inputs of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem_completionFunctor` are all
discharged. The derived-colimit presentation of the Čech complex by the Koszul complexes is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isHomotopyColimit_koszulPowerSystem`, which is [Stacks, Tag 0913]
followed by [Stacks, Tag 0949]; the direct-sum comparison is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedSheafHomSigmaComparison`; and clause 3 of
[Stacks, Tag 08JJ] — the hypothesis `hdual` of that statement — is not needed at all. The proof
of [Stacks, Tag 0A0A] uses that clause for one purpose only, an isomorphism of the tower
`n ↦ K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 K_n^∨` with the tower `n ↦ R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(K_n, K)`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorDerivedDualSystemIsoOfPerfect` builds that isomorphism from
the perfectness of the `K_n` alone, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPerfect_koszulPowerComplex`. The canonical map of
[Stacks, Tag 08JD] therefore never enters.

The tower is the one of `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorDerivedDualSystem`,
`n ↦ K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 K_n^∨` with `K_n` the Koszul complex in degrees `0, …, r`; that is the spelling
in which [Stacks, Tag 0A0A] is stated, and it is the source's `K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 K_n` for the source's
`K_n`, which is the `𝒪`-dual of the complex in degrees `0, …, r` and so sits in degrees
`-r, …, 0`, as the proof of the tag records.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem_koszulPowerSystem_canonical
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasCoproduct ((koszulPowerSystem X f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q).obj)]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
      (derivedSheafHomSystem X (koszulPowerSystem X f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) K).obj (op n)]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
      (tensorDerivedDualSystem X (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct.{u} X)
        (koszulPowerSystem X f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) K).obj (op n)] :
    IsDerivedLimit (tensorDerivedDualSystem X
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct.{u} X)
        (koszulPowerSystem X f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) K)
      ((completionFunctor X f).obj K)
declarations.comment: the formula `K^∧ = R lim (K ⊗^L_O K_n)` for the derived completion along the ideal sheaf generated by global sections `f_1, …, f_r`, at the canonical derived tensor product, with the Koszul tower spelled as the duals `K_n^∨` of the Koszul complexes in degrees `0, …, r`, which is the spelling of Stacks 0A0A and the source's own `K_n`; the tower is indexed by `n : ℕ` carrying the exponent `n + 1`, the source's positive powers

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_tensorKoszulComplex_completionFunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `f_1, …, f_r` be global sections of `𝒪` and let `K ∈ D(𝒪)`.
The derived completion `K^∧` of [Stacks, Tag 099B] along the ideal sheaf generated by `f_1, …, f_r`
is `R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 K_n)`, where `K_n` is the Koszul complex on `f_1^n, …, f_r^n` over `𝒪`, in
degrees `-r, …, 0`.

Here `K^∧` is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completionFunctor X f`, the tower is indexed by the
positive exponents `n + 1`, `K_{n+1}` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.koszulNaiveDualComplex X f n` (the `n`-th member of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.koszulNaiveDualSystem X f`), `⊗^𝐋_𝒪` is the canonical derived tensor
product, and `R lim` is read as the predicate `CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_tensorKoszulComplex_completionFunctor
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    IsDerivedLimit
      (koszulNaiveDualSystem X f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X).tensor.obj K)
      ((completionFunctor X f).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem_koszulPowerSystem_completion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0E].** Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `f_1, …, f_r` be global sections
of `𝒪` and let `K ∈ D(𝒪)`. The derived completion
`K^∧ = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)` of [Stacks, Tag 099B] along the ideal sheaf generated by
`f_1, …, f_r` is a derived limit of the tower

`n ↦ K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 K_n`, `K_n = Hom_𝒪(K(𝒪, f_1^{n+1}, …, f_r^{n+1}), 𝒪)`,

the derived tensor products of `K` with the duals of the Koszul complexes on the positive powers
of `f_1, …, f_r`.

The two inputs the source's proof uses are discharged, not assumed: the derived-colimit
presentation of the Čech complex by the Koszul complexes is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isHomotopyColimit_koszulPowerSystem` ([Stacks, Tag 0913] followed
by [Stacks, Tag 0949]), and the identification of the tower with
`n ↦ R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(K^n, K)` is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.koszulTensorDualSystemIso`, which
goes through the interchange morphism of [Stacks, Tag 0BYU] rather than through clause 3 of
[Stacks, Tag 08JJ] — see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem_koszulPowerSystem_completion
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasCoproduct ((koszulPowerSystem X f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q).obj)]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (derivedSheafHomSystem X
      (koszulPowerSystem X f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) K).obj (op n)]
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ (tensorDerivedDualSystem X
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X)
      (koszulPowerSystem X f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) K).obj (op n)] :
    IsDerivedLimit (tensorDerivedDualSystem X
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X)
        (koszulPowerSystem X f ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) K)
      ((completionFunctor X f).obj K)
declarations.comment: the stated formula `K^∧ = R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 K_n)` for the derived completion of `K ∈ D(𝒪)` along the ideal sheaf generated by global sections `f_1, …, f_r` of `𝒪`, with `K_n` the Koszul complex on `f_1^n, …, f_r^n` in the cochain grading of the source's proof, that is the `𝒪`-dual of `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.koszulPowerComplex`. `R lim` is a predicate rather than a functor, so the source's equality is read as `K^∧` being a derived limit of the tower; the `HasProduct`/`HasCoproduct` arguments are what lets a derived limit be written down at all and always hold, by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_isDerivedLimit_tensorDerivedDualSystem`. Nothing is assumed: both inputs of the source's proof are proved here.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletion_restrict
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0F]: derived completion commutes with localization.** Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a
ringed site, `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` a sheaf of ideals of finite type, `K ↦ K^∧` the derived completion functor
of [Stacks, Tag 099F] and `U` an object of `𝒞`. Then `K^∧|_U` is the derived completion of `K|_U`
along `ℐ|_U`:

* `K^∧|_U` is derived complete along `ℐ|_U`, for every `K`;
* hence there is a canonical map `a : (K|_U)^∧ ⟶ K^∧|_U`, natural in `K`, compatible with the
  completion maps — its composite with `K|_U ⟶ (K|_U)^∧` is the restriction of `K ⟶ K^∧` — and
  it is the only such map (`eq_derivedCompletionRestrictComparison_of_derivedCompletionUnit_comp`);
* `a` is an isomorphism, for every `K`.

The completion functor on `𝒞/U` is that of [Stacks, Tag 099F] for the ringed site
`(𝒞/U, 𝒪_U)` and the restricted sheaf of ideals `ℐ|_U`, which is of finite type
(`isFiniteType_overIdeal`); `a` is `derivedCompletionRestrictComparison`, and the resulting
natural isomorphism is `derivedCompletionRestrictIso`. The source proves the invertibility of `a`
"from the construction in the proof of the proposition"; so does this library: both completion
functors are `R𝑆heafHom(K₀, -)` for the map `K₀ ⟶ 𝒪` of [Stacks, Tag 099E] on the respective site,
the one on `𝒞/U` may be taken to be the restriction of the one on `𝒞`
(`isGlobalExtendedCech_restrict`), and `R𝑆heafHom` commutes with restriction by
[Stacks, Tag 08JB]. The Remark's second argument — the map `b : K^∧ ⟶ Rj_*((K|_U)^∧)` and the
verification that its adjoint inverts `a` — is the companion registration
`derivedCompletion_restrict_secondMap` of `LocalizationCompletionPushforward.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCompletion_restrict :
    (∀ K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))),
      IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (X.over U) (overIdeal I U)
        ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          ((derivedCompletion X I).obj K))) ∧
    (∀ K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))),
      (derivedCompletionUnit (X.over U) (overIdeal I U)).app
          ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) ≫
        (derivedCompletionRestrictComparison X I U (overIdeal I U) (fun _ _ hg ↦ hg)).app K =
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
          ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) U).mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((derivedCompletionUnit X I).app K)) ∧
    (∀ K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))),
      IsIso ((derivedCompletionRestrictComparison X I U (overIdeal I U)
        (fun _ _ hg ↦ hg)).app K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletion_restrict_secondMap
declarations.doc:
**The second half of [Stacks, Tag 0A0F]: the map `b` and its adjoint.** Let `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` be a
sheaf of ideals of finite type, `U` an object of `𝒞` and `j` the localization morphism.

* `Rj_*` carries objects derived complete along `ℐ|_U` to objects derived complete along `ℐ`
  ([Stacks, Tag 099J] for `j`);
* hence for every `K` there is a unique `b : K^∧ ⟶ Rj_*((K|_U)^∧)` whose composite with the
  completion map `K ⟶ K^∧` is the adjunct `K ⟶ Rj_*((K|_U)^∧)` of the completion map of `K|_U`,
  under the adjunction `(-)|_U ⊣ Rj_*` (`overFunctorDerivedAdjunction`);
* the adjoint `K^∧|_U ⟶ (K|_U)^∧` of `b` is the inverse of the canonical map
  `a = derivedCompletionRestrictComparison` of `derivedCompletion_restrict`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCompletion_restrict_secondMap :
    (∀ E : DerivedCategory
        (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (X.over U).O))),
      IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (X.over U) (overIdeal I U) E →
        IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I ((localizationDerivedPushforward X U).obj E)) ∧
    (∀ K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))),
      ∃! b : (derivedCompletion X I).obj K ⟶ (localizationDerivedPushforward X U).obj
          ((derivedCompletion (X.over U) (overIdeal I U)).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
              ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)),
        (derivedCompletionUnit X I).app K ≫ b =
          (overFunctorDerivedAdjunction X U).unit.app K ≫
            (localizationDerivedPushforward X U).map
              ((derivedCompletionUnit (X.over U) (overIdeal I U)).app
                ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
                  ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))) ∧
    (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
      (b : (derivedCompletion X I).obj K ⟶ (localizationDerivedPushforward X U).obj
          ((derivedCompletion (X.over U) (overIdeal I U)).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
              ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))),
      (derivedCompletionUnit X I).app K ≫ b =
          (overFunctorDerivedAdjunction X U).unit.app K ≫
            (localizationDerivedPushforward X U).map
              ((derivedCompletionUnit (X.over U) (overIdeal I U)).app
                ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
                  ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)) →
        ((overFunctorDerivedAdjunction X U).homEquiv _ _).symm b ≫
            (derivedCompletionRestrictComparison X I U (overIdeal I U) (fun _ _ hg ↦ hg)).app K =
          𝟙 _ ∧
        (derivedCompletionRestrictComparison X I U (overIdeal I U) (fun _ _ hg ↦ hg)).app K ≫
            ((overFunctorDerivedAdjunction X U).homEquiv _ _).symm b = 𝟙 _)
declarations.comment:
the Remark's second argument: `Rj_*` carries objects derived complete along
  `ℐ|_U` to objects derived complete along `ℐ`, so there is a unique map
  `b : K^∧ ⟶ Rj_*((K|_U)^∧)` compatible with the completion maps, and the adjoint of `b` under
  `(-)|_U ⊣ Rj_*` is the inverse of the map `a` of `derivedCompletion_restrict`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` of [Stacks, Tag 0A0G].** It exists because
`Rf_*(K^∧)` is derived complete, by [Stacks, Tag 099J], so the universal property of derived
completion applies to `Rf_*K ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`. Built as a mate, so that it is natural in `K`.

This is the map the tag asserts to be invertible, and it is invertible at every object of
`D(𝒪')` at the tag's own data — `ℐ` of **finite type** and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` — by
`RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType`
of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionLocalToGlobal.lean`; that statement localizes the globally
generated case,
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf`
of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`. Here `ℐ` and `ℐ'` are an arbitrary pair of
sheaves of ideals subject only to `hI`, which is where the construction already makes sense.
declarations.comment:
the canonical map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` whose invertibility the tag asserts,
  constructed as a mate and hence natural in `K`, at an arbitrary pair of sheaves of ideals
  subject only to the relation of [Stacks, Tag 099J] between them. Its invertibility at every
  object of `D(𝒪')`, which is the tag's assertion, is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType`
  of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionLocalToGlobal.lean`, at the tag's own data: `ℐ` of finite
  type and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isIso_map_unit
declarations.doc:
**A criterion for `Rf_*` to commute with derived completion at `K`.** If `Rf_*` applied to
the unit `K ⟶ K^∧` is invertible, then so is the comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`.

Indeed `Rf_*(K^∧)` is derived complete, so an invertible `Rf_*(K ⟶ K^∧)` makes `Rf_*K` derived
complete too, whence its unit `Rf_*K ⟶ (Rf_*K)^∧` is invertible; and the comparison map is the
second factor of that unit followed by itself in
`derivedCompletionUnit_comp_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isIso_map_unit
    {K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (hK : IsIso ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).map
      ((derivedCompletionUnit X I').app K))) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison f I I' hI).app K)
declarations.comment:
the criterion: `Rf_*` commutes with derived completion at every `K` for which
  `Rf_*(K ⟶ K^∧)` is invertible; the source proves it for every `K`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0G] at a derived-complete object.** For `K` in `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')` the
canonical map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible, so `Rf_*(K^∧) = Rf_*K = (Rf_*K)^∧`: the
unit `K ⟶ K^∧` is invertible on a derived-complete `K`.

The general case of Tag 0A0G, for an arbitrary `K`, is proved at the tag's own data — a sheaf
of ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` of finite type and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` — by
`isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType` of
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionLocalToGlobal.lean`. Equation 52.7.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0A0I], in
its own setting of a morphism of schemes and a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`
`.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf` of
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionFiniteType.lean`. The statement here is the case of an independent
pair of sheaves of ideals subject only to the relation of [Stacks, Tag 099J], at a
derived-complete object. It also carries part (3) of
[Stacks, Tag 099N], with the restrictions named on `derivedCompletePushforward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isDerivedComplete
    {K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (hK : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I' K) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison f I I' hI).app K)
declarations.comment:
for `K` in `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')`, where the unit `K ⟶ K^∧` is invertible, at an
  arbitrary pair of sheaves of ideals subject only to the relation of [Stacks, Tag 099J]. The
  tag's assertion for an arbitrary `K` is
  `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf`
  of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`, at the tag's own pair of sheaves of ideals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0G] for the canonical comparison map and an arbitrary object, at two
sheaves of ideals generated by finitely many global sections.** Let
`f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a morphism of ringed sites, let `t_1, …, t_r` be global
sections of `𝒪` generating `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪`, let `g_i = f^♯(t_i)` generate `ℐ' ⊂ 𝒪'`, and let
`K ∈ D(𝒪')` be **arbitrary**. Then the canonical map

`(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`

of `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonGeneratedIdealSheaf` is
invertible: `Rf_*` commutes with derived completion, through the map the tag says it does.

Both derived completion functors are the reflector of [Stacks, Tag 099F], produced from the
generators by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf`, so no
conclusion of that tag is an input; and the relation `PushforwardIdealCompatible` between the two
sheaves of ideals that the comparison map needs is proved from `hg`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.pushforwardIdealCompatible_of_pushGlobalSectionsCompatible`.

The proof is `isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_nonempty_iso` fed with
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedPushforwardDerivedCompletionGeneratedIdealSheafIso` of
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionCech.lean`, which runs the source's own computation through the
Čech presentation of the two completions and gives the display at every object. The Koszul
Hom-tower form of the display,
`RingedSite.nonempty_iso_derivedPushforward_derivedCompletion_generatedIdealSheaf`,
would serve equally except that it carries `Limits.HasCoproduct` on the two Koszul towers as
instance binders — countable coproducts of a derived category, which K-injective resolutions do
not produce — and the Čech form needs no coproduct in a derived category at all, so this
statement carries no such binder.

The source's `ℐ` is of finite type, hence only *locally* generated by finitely many sections;
[Stacks, Tag 099F] at such an `ℐ` rests on [Stacks, Tags 099D and 099E], and the module
documentation of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionGenerated.lean` records what stands in the way of
the local-to-global descent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonGeneratedIdealSheaf f g t
      (pushforwardIdealCompatible_of_pushGlobalSectionsCompatible f t g hg)).app K)
declarations.comment: the tag's conclusion for the **canonical** comparison map and an **arbitrary** object: `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible for every `K` of `D(𝒪')`, at a morphism of ringed sites and at `ℐ = (t_1, …, t_r) ⊂ 𝒪` and `ℐ' = (f^♯t_1, …, f^♯t_r) ⊂ 𝒪'` generated by finitely many global sections of the two structure sheaves — the regime the source's own proof reduces to, and the regime in which [Stacks, Tag 099F] is available here, so that both derived completion functors are produced from those generators and no conclusion of that tag is an input. The relation between the two sheaves of ideals is proved from `g_i = f^♯(t_i)` rather than received, and no countable coproduct in a derived category is assumed. The restriction is on the data alone: the source's `ℐ` is quasi-coherent of finite type, hence only *locally* generated by finitely many sections, and [Stacks, Tag 099F] at such an `ℐ` rests on [Stacks, Tags 099D and 099E]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0G] for the canonical comparison map and an arbitrary object, at the
source's own ideal sheaf `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`.** Let `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a
morphism of ringed sites carrying a terminal object `T` of the target site to a terminal object,
let `ℐ = (t_1, …, t_r) ⊂ 𝒪` be generated by finitely many global sections, and let `K ∈ D(𝒪')`
be **arbitrary**. Then the canonical map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible, the completion
on the source being taken along `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`.

That ideal sheaf is built here from `f` and `t`, as the one generated by `f^♯t_1, …, f^♯t_r`,
and is the source's own: it receives `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ)` and is least among those that do, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.eq_generatedIdealSheaf_pushGlobalSections`. The terminal objects
are what make a global section of `𝒪` transportable along a general morphism of sites; they are
present at ringed spaces and at schemes, where `f.u` is `Opens.map` and carries `⊤` to `⊤`.

This is `isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf` at
`g = pushGlobalSections f hT' t`, whose relation to `t` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.pushGlobalSectionsCompatible_pushGlobalSections`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonInverseImageIdealSheaf f hT hT' t).app K)
declarations.comment: **the ringed-sites case** for the **canonical** comparison map, at the tag's own pair of sheaves of ideals and for an **arbitrary** object. The tag states a morphism of ringed *topoi*; this is a morphism of ringed *sites*, which is how the sibling [Stacks, Tag 099J] is recorded in this directory (its full sites case is deliberately untagged and the attribute sits on the topos-level theorem). Concretely: `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible for every `K` of `D(𝒪')`, where `ℐ = (t_1, …, t_r) ⊂ 𝒪` is generated by finitely many global sections and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X ⊂ 𝒪'` is constructed from `f` and `t` as the ideal sheaf generated by `f^♯t_1, …, f^♯t_r` and characterised as the least one receiving `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ)`. The morphism of ringed sites carries a terminal object of the target site to a terminal object, as at ringed spaces and at schemes; both derived completion functors are produced from the generators of `ℐ`, so no conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 099F] is an input. The restriction is on the data alone: the source's `ℐ` is of finite type, hence only *locally* generated by finitely many sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedPushforwardDerivedCompletionGeneratedIdealSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tags 0A0G and 0A0I] for an arbitrary object, at two sheaves of ideals generated by
finitely many global sections.** Let `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a morphism of ringed
sites, let `t_1, …, t_r` be global sections of `𝒪` generating `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪`, let `g_i = f^♯(t_i)`
generate `ℐ' ⊂ 𝒪'`, and let `K ∈ D(𝒪')` be **arbitrary**. Then

`Rf_*(K^∧) ≅ (Rf_*K)^∧`:

`Rf_*` commutes with derived completion. Both derived completion functors are the reflector of
[Stacks, Tag 099F], produced from the generators by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf`, so no part
of that tag is an input.

The reflector at a globally generated ideal sheaf **is** the Čech completion
`R𝓗om(Č(-), -)` of [Stacks, Tag 099B]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.reflectorIsoCompletionFunctor`), the source's Čech complex is the
derived inverse image of the target's, and the adjoint formula moves `Rf_*` across the internal
Hom. No countable coproduct in a derived category is assumed, and the isomorphism is produced
rather than shown to exist; see the module documentation for the comparison with the
derived-limit form.
declarations.statement:
def derivedPushforwardDerivedCompletionGeneratedIdealSheafIso
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj
        ((derivedCompletion X (generatedIdealSheaf g)).obj K) ≅
      (derivedCompletion Y (generatedIdealSheaf t)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj K)
declarations.comment: `Rf_*` commutes with derived completion, `Rf_*(K^∧) = (Rf_*K)^∧`, for an **arbitrary** object `K` of `D(𝒪')`, at `ℐ = (t_1, …, t_r) ⊂ 𝒪` and `ℐ' = (f^♯t_1, …, f^♯t_r) ⊂ 𝒪'` generated by finitely many global sections of the two structure sheaves — the regime the source's own proof reduces to, and the regime in which [Stacks, Tag 099F] is available here, so that both derived completion functors are built from those generators and no part of that tag is an input. The display is produced as an explicit isomorphism from three identifications: derived completion along a globally generated ideal sheaf is the Čech completion of [Stacks, Tag 099B]; `Lf^*Č(𝒪, t) ≅ Č(𝒪', g)`; and the adjoint formula `Rf_* R𝓗om_{𝒪'}(Lf^*A, M) ≅ R𝓗om_𝒪(A, Rf_*M)` at arbitrary `A` and `M`. Restrictions on the data only: the object is arbitrary, and no countable coproduct in a derived category is assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonInverseImageIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` of [Stacks, Tag 0A0G] at the source's
own ideal sheaves.** It exists because `Rf_*(K^∧)` is derived complete, by [Stacks, Tag 099J];
it is built as a mate and is therefore natural in `K`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonGeneratedIdealSheaf`
at `ℐ = (t_1, …, t_s)` and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`. It is invertible at every object of `D(𝒪')`,
which is the tag's assertion:
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf`
of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`, and
`isIso_natTrans_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf` there for the
whole natural transformation.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonInverseImageIdealSheaf :
    derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom ⋙
        derivedCompletion Y (generatedIdealSheaf t) ⟶
      derivedCompletion X (generatedIdealSheaf (pushGlobalSections f hT' t)) ⋙
        derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom
declarations.comment: the canonical comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` that the tag asserts to be invertible, at a morphism of ringed sites sending a terminal object of the target site to a terminal object of the source site, with `ℐ` generated by finitely many global sections of `𝒪` and the completion on the source taken along `f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` — the ideal sheaf Section 52.7 builds out of `ℐ`, which here is constructed from `f` and the generators of `ℐ` and identified as that ideal sheaf by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.eq_generatedIdealSheaf_pushGlobalSections`. Both derived completion functors are produced from the generators, by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf`. This map is invertible at every object of `D(𝒪')`, which is the tag's assertion, by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf` of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`. At the tag's own `ℐ`, which is of finite type and hence only *locally* generated by finitely many sections, the derived completion functors come instead from [Stacks, Tag 099F] at a sheaf of ideals of finite type, `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isIso_map_unit
declarations.doc:
**A criterion for `Rf_*` to commute with derived completion at `K`, at the source's own ideal
sheaves.** The comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible as soon as `Rf_*` applied to
the completion map `K ⟶ K^∧` is.

This is
`RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf_of_isIso_map_unit` at
`ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`. By `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_iff` its
hypothesis `hK` holds exactly when `Rf_*K` is already derived complete, so this is the criterion at
those objects; for an arbitrary `K` the invertibility comes from the source's computation, run in
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf`
of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isIso_map_unit
    {K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))}
    (hK : IsIso ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).map
      ((derivedCompletionUnit X
        (generatedIdealSheaf (pushGlobalSections f hT' t))).app K))) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonInverseImageIdealSheaf f hT hT' t).app K)
declarations.comment: the criterion that the comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible as soon as `Rf_*(K ⟶ K^∧)` is, at a morphism of ringed sites sending a terminal object of the target site to a terminal object of the source site, with `ℐ` generated by finitely many global sections of `𝒪` and the completion on the source taken along the ideal sheaf `f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` of Section 52.7, built here out of `f` and the generators of `ℐ`. This is the reduction the source's own proof makes before its local computation, and by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_iff` it covers exactly the objects with `Rf_*K` already derived complete. For an arbitrary object the source's computation is run in `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf` of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`, which gives the tag's assertion at this very pair of sheaves of ideals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tags 0A0G and 0A0I] at a derived-complete object, at the source's own ideal
sheaves.** The comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible for every `K ∈ D(𝒪')`
derived complete along `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`, so that `Rf_*(K^∧) = Rf_*K = (Rf_*K)^∧` there.

This is
`RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf_of_isDerivedComplete`
at `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`. The same invertibility holds for an **arbitrary** `K` at this very pair of
sheaves of ideals, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf`
of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`; the point of the statement below is that at a
derived-complete `K` it needs none of that computation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isDerivedComplete
    {K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))}
    (hK : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X
      (generatedIdealSheaf (pushGlobalSections f hT' t)) K) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonInverseImageIdealSheaf f hT hT' t).app K)
declarations.comment: the display `Rf_*(K^∧) = (Rf_*K)^∧` for a **derived-complete** `K`, at a morphism of ringed sites sending a terminal object of the target site to a terminal object of the source site, with `ℐ` generated by finitely many global sections of `𝒪` and the completion on the source taken along the ideal sheaf `f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` of Section 52.7 — built here out of `f` and the generators of `ℐ`, and identified as that ideal sheaf by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.eq_generatedIdealSheaf_pushGlobalSections`. Both derived completion functors are produced from those generators. The tag's assertion is this display for an arbitrary `K`, and at this very pair of sheaves of ideals it is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf` of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`; what the statement here adds is that at a derived-complete object the display needs none of that computation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_natTrans_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0G]: `Rf_*` commutes with derived completion.** For a morphism of ringed
sites `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)`, a sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` of **finite type** and
`ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` the ideal sheaf Section 52.7 builds out of `ℐ`, the canonical natural
transformation

`Rf_* ⋙ (-)^∧_ℐ ⟶ (-)^∧_{ℐ'} ⋙ Rf_*`

of [Stacks, Tag 0A0G] is **invertible as a morphism of functors**. This is the tag's own
phrasing: the two functors are identified, not merely their values at one object.

It is `isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType` —
the invertibility at each object, for an arbitrary object and the tag's finite-type ideal sheaf
— assembled over all objects by `CategoryTheory.NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app`, which applies
because the comparison map is a natural transformation by construction.
declarations.statement:
theorem
    isIso_natTrans_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType :
    IsIso (derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison f I (inverseImageIdealSheaf f I)
      (pushforwardIdealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf f I))
declarations.comment: `Rf_*` commutes with derived completion, as the tag phrases it: the canonical natural transformation `Rf_* ⋙ (-)^∧ ⟶ (-)^∧ ⋙ Rf_*` is invertible **as a morphism of functors**, for a morphism of ringed sites, a sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` of **finite type** and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` the ideal sheaf Section 52.7 constructs out of `ℐ`. The finite type of `ℐ'` and the relation of [Stacks, Tag 099J] between the two sheaves of ideals are proved, not assumed. No hypothesis is placed on the object, none on the generating family, and the identification is the canonical comparison map characterised by its compatibility with the two completion units, so the two functors are identified by the map the tag names

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonGeneratedIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` of [Stacks, Tag 0A0G], at ideal
sheaves generated by global sections.** It exists because `Rf_*(K^∧)` is derived complete, by
[Stacks, Tag 099J], so the universal property of derived completion applies to the natural map
`Rf_*K ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`; it is built as a mate and is therefore natural in `K`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison` with both of its
instance hypotheses discharged from the generators, by
`isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf` on either site. The comparison map is
what [Stacks, Tag 0A0G] asserts to be invertible and what the display of [Stacks, Tag 0A0I]
compares its two sides by.

It is invertible at every object of `D(𝒪')` as soon as the two generating families correspond,
`g_i = f^♯(t_i)`:
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf`
of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`, and
`isIso_natTrans_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf` there for the whole
natural transformation. Here the two families are independent and related only by `hI`, which is
all the construction needs.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCompletionPushforwardComparisonGeneratedIdealSheaf :
    derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom ⋙
        derivedCompletion Y (generatedIdealSheaf t) ⟶
      derivedCompletion X (generatedIdealSheaf g) ⋙
        derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom
declarations.comment: the canonical comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` that the tag asserts to be invertible, constructed with nothing assumed, for two **independent** families of global sections of the two structure sheaves generating `ℐ` and `ℐ'` and related only by the hypothesis of [Stacks, Tag 099J] — the regime in which [Stacks, Tag 099F] is proved in this library, by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf`, so that both derived completion functors are produced from the data. Its invertibility at every object of `D(𝒪')`, which is the tag's assertion, holds as soon as the two families correspond, `g_i = f^♯(t_i)`, as the tag's own `ℐ'` does: `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf` of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`. At the tag's own `ℐ`, which is of finite type and hence only *locally* generated by finitely many sections, the derived completion functors come instead from [Stacks, Tag 099F] at a sheaf of ideals of finite type, `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf_of_isIso_map_unit
declarations.doc:
**A criterion for `Rf_*` to commute with derived completion at `K`, with nothing assumed.**
At ideal sheaves generated by finitely many global sections, the comparison map
`(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible as soon as `Rf_*` applied to the completion map
`K ⟶ K^∧` is.

Indeed `Rf_*(K^∧)` is derived complete, so an invertible `Rf_*(K ⟶ K^∧)` makes `Rf_*K` derived
complete too, whence its own completion map is invertible; and the comparison is the remaining
factor.

This is `isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isIso_map_unit` with both instance
hypotheses discharged from the generators. By
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_iff` its hypothesis `hK` holds
exactly when `Rf_*K` is already derived complete, so this is the criterion at those objects. For
an arbitrary `K`, with no condition on `Rf_*K`, the invertibility is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf`
of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`, once the two generating families correspond.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf_of_isIso_map_unit
    {K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))}
    (hK : IsIso ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).map
      ((derivedCompletionUnit X (generatedIdealSheaf g)).app K))) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison f (generatedIdealSheaf t)
      (generatedIdealSheaf g) hI).app K)
declarations.comment: the criterion that the comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible as soon as `Rf_*(K ⟶ K^∧)` is, proved with nothing assumed at two independent families of global sections of the two structure sheaves generating `ℐ` and `ℐ'`. This is the reduction the source's own proof makes before its local computation, and by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_map_derivedCompletionUnit_iff` it covers exactly the objects with `Rf_*K` already derived complete. The tag's assertion for an arbitrary object is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf` of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`, which runs the source's computation at two corresponding families `g_i = f^♯(t_i)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tags 0A0G and 0A0I] at a derived-complete object, with nothing assumed.** At
ideal sheaves generated by finitely many global sections, the comparison map
`(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible for every `K ∈ D(𝒪')` that is derived complete along
`ℐ'`, so that `Rf_*(K^∧) = Rf_*K = (Rf_*K)^∧` there.

This is `isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isDerivedComplete` with both instance
hypotheses discharged from the generators. What it asks of the object it does not ask of the
data: the two generating families are independent, related only by `hI`. For an arbitrary object
the two families have to correspond, `g_i = f^♯(t_i)`, and then the display holds by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf`
of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf_of_isDerivedComplete
    {K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))}
    (hK : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X (generatedIdealSheaf g) K) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison f (generatedIdealSheaf t)
      (generatedIdealSheaf g) hI).app K)
declarations.comment: the display `Rf_*(K^∧) = (Rf_*K)^∧` for a **derived-complete** `K`, proved with nothing assumed at two **independent** families of global sections of the two structure sheaves generating `ℐ` and `ℐ'` and related only by the hypothesis of [Stacks, Tag 099J] — the regime in which [Stacks, Tag 099F] is proved here, so that both derived completion functors are produced from those generators. For an **arbitrary** `K` the display holds once the two families correspond, `g_i = f^♯(t_i)`, as the source's own `ℐ'` does: `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf` of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionCanonical.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.nonempty_iso_derivedPushforward_derivedCompletion_generatedIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tags 0A0G and 0A0I] for an arbitrary object, at two sheaves of ideals generated by
finitely many global sections.** Let `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a morphism of ringed
sites, let `t_1, …, t_r` be global sections
of `𝒪` generating `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪`, let `g_1, …, g_r` be global sections of `𝒪'` with `g_i = f^♯(t_i)`
generating `ℐ' ⊂ 𝒪'`, and let `K ∈ D(𝒪')` be **arbitrary**. Then

`Rf_*(K^∧) ≅ (Rf_*K)^∧`:

`Rf_*` commutes with derived completion. Both derived completion functors are the reflector of
[Stacks, Tag 099F], produced from the generators by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf`, so no
part of that tag is an input here.

The proof is the source's own. `K^∧` is the derived limit of the Koszul Hom tower
`n ↦ R𝓗om_{𝒪'}(K(𝒪', g^{n+1}), K)` by
`isDerivedLimit_derivedSheafHomSystem_derivedCompletion` ([Stacks, Tag 0A0E]); `Rf_*` carries
that derived limit to one of the pushed-forward tower by
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforwardOnRingedTopoi.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedPushforward`
([Stacks, Tag 0A07]); `derivedPushforwardKoszulSheafHomSystemIso` identifies the pushed-forward
tower with `n ↦ R𝓗om_𝒪(K(𝒪, t^{n+1}), Rf_*K)`, whose derived limit is `(Rf_*K)^∧` by the same
presentation on the target; and two derived limits of isomorphic towers are isomorphic, by
`Rlim.Pro.nonempty_iso_of_isDerivedLimit_of_natIso` ([Stacks, Tag 0H9L]).

The conclusion is the display as the source writes it, an isomorphism of the two objects, rather
than invertibility of the canonical comparison map
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison`: the uniqueness of derived
limits produces a non-canonical isomorphism. The source's `ℐ` is of finite type, hence only
locally generated by finitely many sections; [Stacks, Tag 099F] at such an `ℐ` rests on
[Stacks, Tags 099D and 099E].
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_derivedPushforward_derivedCompletion_generatedIdealSheaf
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasCoproduct ((koszulPowerSystem X g ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q).obj)]
    [HasCoproduct ((koszulPowerSystem Y t ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q).obj)] :
    Nonempty ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj
        ((derivedCompletion X (generatedIdealSheaf g)).obj K) ≅
      (derivedCompletion Y (generatedIdealSheaf t)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj K))
declarations.comment: `Rf_*` commutes with derived completion, `Rf_*(K^∧) = (Rf_*K)^∧`, for an **arbitrary** object `K` of `D(𝒪')`, at **any** morphism of ringed sites and at `ℐ = (t_1, …, t_r) ⊂ 𝒪` and `ℐ' = (f^♯t_1, …, f^♯t_r) ⊂ 𝒪'` generated by finitely many global sections of the two structure sheaves — the regime the source's own proof reduces to, and the regime in which [Stacks, Tag 099F] is available here, so that both derived completion functors are built from those generators and no part of that tag is an input. The argument is the source's: the two completions are the derived limits of the Koszul Hom towers ([Stacks, Tag 0A0E]), `Rf_*` exchanges with `R lim` ([Stacks, Tag 0A07]), and the two towers are identified by `Rf_* R𝓗om_{𝒪'}(Lf^*A, M) ≅ R𝓗om_𝒪(A, Rf_*M)` naturally in both variables together with `Lf^*K(𝒪, t^n) ≅ K(𝒪', g^n)`. Restrictions on the data only: the object is arbitrary

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.nonempty_iso_derivedPushforward_derivedCompletion_pushGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tags 0A0G and 0A0I] for an arbitrary object, at the source's own ideal sheaf
`ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`.** Let `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a morphism of ringed sites
carrying a terminal object `T` of the target site to a terminal object, let
`ℐ = (t_1, …, t_r) ⊂ 𝒪` be generated by finitely many
global sections, and let `K ∈ D(𝒪')` be **arbitrary**. Then

`Rf_*(K^∧) ≅ (Rf_*K)^∧`,

the completion on the source being taken along the ideal sheaf generated by `f^♯t_1, …, f^♯t_r`.

That ideal sheaf **is** the source's `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`: it receives `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ)`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.pushforwardIdealCompatible_pushGlobalSections`, and is least among
those that do, by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.generatedIdealSheaf_pushGlobalSections_le`,
which together pin it down —
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.eq_generatedIdealSheaf_pushGlobalSections`. So the relation
between the two sheaves of ideals is built from `f` and `t` here rather than given, and the
statement depends only on `f`, on the two terminal objects and on `t`.

The terminal objects are what makes a global section of `𝒪` transportable along a general
morphism of sites: `f^♯` produces sections only over objects in the image of `f.u`, and a
section over a terminal object is a global section. They are present at ringed spaces and at
schemes, where `f.u` is `Opens.map` and carries `⊤` to `⊤`.

This is `nonempty_iso_derivedPushforward_derivedCompletion_generatedIdealSheaf` at
`g = pushGlobalSections f hT' t`, whose relation to `t` is
`pushGlobalSectionsCompatible_pushGlobalSections`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_derivedPushforward_derivedCompletion_pushGlobalSections
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasCoproduct ((koszulPowerSystem X (pushGlobalSections f hT' t) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q).obj)]
    [HasCoproduct ((koszulPowerSystem Y t ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q).obj)] :
    Nonempty ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj
        ((derivedCompletion X (generatedIdealSheaf (pushGlobalSections f hT' t))).obj K) ≅
      (derivedCompletion Y (generatedIdealSheaf t)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj K))
declarations.comment: `Rf_*` commutes with derived completion, `Rf_*(K^∧) = (Rf_*K)^∧`, for an **arbitrary** object `K` of `D(𝒪')`, with the source's own ideal sheaf `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` built from `ℐ` rather than given: at a morphism of ringed sites carrying a terminal object of the target site to a terminal object — as happens at ringed spaces and at schemes — `ℐ'` is the ideal sheaf generated by `f^♯t_1, …, f^♯t_r`, which receives `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ)` and is least among those that do, and the display holds at that pair for every object of `D(𝒪')`. `ℐ = (t_1, …, t_r)` is generated by finitely many global sections, which is the regime the source's own proof reduces to and the regime in which [Stacks, Tag 099F] is available here, so both derived completion functors are built from the generators

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0G] at a sheaf of ideals of finite type, for an arbitrary object.** Let
`f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a morphism of ringed sites, let `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` be a sheaf of ideals
**of finite type** and let `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` be the ideal sheaf Section 52.7 builds out of
`ℐ`. Then the canonical comparison map

`(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`

is invertible for **every** object `K` of `D(𝒪')`, the completion on the target being taken
along `ℐ` and the one on the source along `ℐ'`.

The proof is the source's own localization. `ℐ` of finite type is generated by finitely many
sections above a covering family `{V_i}` of the final object of the target site
(`exists_coversTop_eq_generatedIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType`); on each `𝒟/V_i` the comparison map
of the localized morphism of [Stacks, Tag 04J0] at `(ℐ|_{V_i}, ℐ'|_{u(V_i)})` is invertible,
because both of those sheaves of ideals are globally generated there
(`isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_localized_overIdeal`); the restriction coherence
`derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_localized` identifies the restriction of the comparison
map of `f` with it up to three isomorphisms — the two comparison maps of [Stacks, Tag 0A0F],
invertible because `ℐ` and `ℐ'` are of finite type, and [Stacks, Tag 0D6G]; and invertibility in
the derived category of sheaves of modules is local on the site
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_of_coversTop_mapDerivedCategory`).

Finite type of `ℐ'` is not a hypothesis: it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isFiniteType_inverseImageIdealSheaf`, and it is what makes the
derived completion functor along `ℐ'` exist at all, by [Stacks, Tag 099F].
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison f I (inverseImageIdealSheaf f I)
      (pushforwardIdealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf f I)).app K)
declarations.comment: **the ringed-sites case**, in full for that case: the **canonical** comparison map, at the tag's own data and for an **arbitrary** object. The tag states a morphism of ringed *topoi*; this is the statement for a morphism of ringed *sites*. That is how the sibling [Stacks, Tag 099J] is handled in this directory — `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedPushforward_isDerivedComplete` is its full sites case and is deliberately untagged, the attribute sitting instead on the topos-level theorem reached by [Stacks, Tag 03CR] transport. The topos-level comparison map and its universal property are in `PushforwardCommutesCompletionTopoi.lean`, and the invertibility criterion in `PushforwardCommutesCompletionToposCriterion.lean`; what the transport still owes is a topos-level `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ)·𝒪`, submodule transport along the dense-subsite replacement, and derived completion across that equivalence. Concretely here: for a morphism of ringed sites, a sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` of finite type and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` the ideal sheaf Section 52.7 constructs out of `ℐ`, the canonical map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible for every `K` of `D(𝒪')`. Both derived completion functors come from [Stacks, Tag 099F] at a sheaf of ideals of finite type — `ℐ'` is of finite type because `ℐ` is, by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isFiniteType_inverseImageIdealSheaf` — and the relation of [Stacks, Tag 099J] between the two sheaves of ideals is proved from the construction rather than assumed. The hypotheses are the source's: no object is excluded and no generating family is assumed global; the source's own reduction to the globally generated case by localization on the target site is the proof

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0G].** Let `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a morphism of ringed topoi, let
`ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` be a sheaf of ideals **of finite type** and let `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` be the sheaf of
ideals generated by `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ)` that Section 52.7 builds out of `ℐ`. Then the canonical
comparison map

`(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`

is invertible for **every** object `K` of `D(𝒪')`, the completion on the target being taken along
`ℐ` and the one on the source along `ℐ'`.

Both of the properties `ℐ'` has to have are theorems about the construction rather than
hypotheses: the relation of [Stacks, Tag 099J] between `ℐ` and `ℐ'`, which the comparison map
needs in order to exist, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.idealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf`, and finite type of
`ℐ'` — which is what makes the derived completion functor along it exist at all, by
[Stacks, Tag 099F] — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isFiniteType_inverseImageIdealSheaf`.

The proof is the source's reduction to a morphism of ringed *sites* by [Stacks, Tag 03CR]; see the
module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType
    (K : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.toRingedSite.O)))) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison f I (inverseImageIdealSheaf.{u} f I)
