      (idealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf.{u} f I)).app K)
declarations.comment: **the tag's own statement, for a morphism of ringed topoi.** For a morphism of ringed topoi `f`, a sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` of finite type and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` the sheaf of ideals generated by `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ)` that Section 52.7 builds out of `ℐ`, the canonical comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible for every object `K` of `D(𝒪')`. The hypotheses are exactly the source's: the relation of [Stacks, Tag 099J] between the two sheaves of ideals is a theorem about the construction, `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.idealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf`, and so is finite type of `ℐ'`, `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isFiniteType_inverseImageIdealSheaf`; no object is excluded and no generating family is assumed global. The proof is the source's reduction to a morphism of ringed sites by [Stacks, Tag 03CR], whose ringed-sites case is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType`. Two results make that reduction go through: the sheaves of ideals that the square's arrows build agree where the applications meet, by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.inverseImageIdealSheaf_denseSquare`, and the square's 2-isomorphism costs no coherence because `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_nonempty_iso` reduces invertibility of the canonical map to a display of objects quantified over all objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Equation 52.7.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0A0I] at Section 52.7's own data, for an arbitrary
object — and so the analogue for complexes of quasi-coherent modules of [Stacks, Tag 0AKL].** Let
`f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_S` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite
type and let `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` be the sheaf of ideals Section 52.7 builds out of it. Then the
canonical comparison map

`(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`

is invertible for **every** object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)`, the completion on `S` being taken along `ℐ`
and the one on `X` along `ℐ'`. In particular it is invertible for every complex of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, with no derived-completeness or nilpotence restriction.

`ℐ` is an `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData`, read on the small Zariski ringed site by
`Stacks.Algebraization.idealSheafSiteSubmodule`, and "of finite type" is
`SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType` (automatic on a locally Noetherian scheme, by
`Stacks.Algebraization.isFiniteType_idealSheafSiteSubmodule`). The sheaf of ideals `ℐ'` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.inverseImageIdealSheaf`, the image of `f^*ℐ ⟶ 𝒪_X`; that `f^♯`
carries `f^{-1}ℐ` into it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.pushforwardIdealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf`, and that it is of
finite type — so that the derived completion along it exists, by [Stacks, Tag 099F] — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isFiniteType_inverseImageIdealSheaf`. Neither is a hypothesis.

This is
`RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType`,
the ringed-sites case of [Stacks, Tag 0A0G], at the morphism of ringed sites
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.toRingedSiteHom f` underlying `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf
    [(idealSheafSiteSubmodule I).toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType]
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (Stacks.RingedSpace.toRingedSite X.toRingedSpace).O)))) :
    IsIso ((RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison (toRingedSiteHom f)
      (idealSheafSiteSubmodule I)
      (RingedSite.inverseImageIdealSheaf.{u} (toRingedSiteHom f) (idealSheafSiteSubmodule I))
      (RingedSite.pushforwardIdealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf.{u} (toRingedSiteHom f)
        (idealSheafSiteSubmodule I))).app K)
declarations.comment: Equation 52.7.0.1 in the display's own setting and at Section 52.7's own data, for an **arbitrary** object, as an invertibility of the **canonical** comparison map `(Rf_*ℱ)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(ℱ^∧)`: a morphism of **schemes** `f : X ⟶ S`, a **quasi-coherent** sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_S` **of finite type** — an `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData` read on the small Zariski ringed site — and the completion on `X` taken along the sheaf of ideals `f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` built out of `ℐ`, the image of `f^*ℐ ⟶ 𝒪_X`. No restriction on `ℱ`: every object of `D(𝒪_X)`, in particular every quasi-coherent `ℱ`. That `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ) ⊆ f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` and that this sheaf of ideals is of finite type, so that [Stacks, Tag 099F] produces the derived completion along it, are theorems about the construction, not hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cohomology_isLimit_of_isDerivedLimit_of_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0J.** The degree-`q` cohomology sheaf of a derived inverse limit of
a tower with quasi-coherent cohomology and surjective transition maps on cohomology is the
ordinary inverse limit of the degree-`q` cohomology sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cohomology_isLimit_of_isDerivedLimit_of_epi
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory.{u + 1} X.Modules)
    (L : DerivedCategory.{u + 1} X.Modules)
    [HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩]
    (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hL : ∃ δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
      Triangle.mk p
        (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
          Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
              K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (DerivedCategory X.Modules))
    (hqc : ∀ (n : ℕ) (q : ℤ),
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).obj (K.obj ⟨n⟩)).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hsurj : ∀ (n : ℕ) (q : ℤ),
      Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).map
        (K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)))
    (q : ℤ) :
    ∃ τ : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).obj L) ⟶
        K ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q,
      (∀ n : ℕ, τ.app ⟨n⟩ =
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).map
          (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ K.obj ⟨n⟩) n)) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ τ))
declarations.comment: cohomology_limit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isDerivedLimit_single_limit_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0J.** For a tower with quasi-coherent cohomology and surjective
transition maps on cohomology, the ordinary inverse limit of each tower of cohomology sheaves,
placed in degree zero, is its derived inverse limit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDerivedLimit_single_limit_homology
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory.{u + 1} X.Modules)
    (hqc : ∀ (n : ℕ) (q : ℤ),
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).obj (K.obj ⟨n⟩)).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hsurj : ∀ (n : ℕ) (q : ℤ),
      Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).map
        (K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)))
    (q : ℤ) :
    let F := K ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ =>
        (F ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ⟨n⟩),
      @IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory X.Modules) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (F ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0) h
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (limit F))
declarations.comment: derived_limit_sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cohomology_limit_homology_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0J.** The inverse limit of a degreewise-surjective tower of
quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves has no higher cohomology on an affine open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cohomology_limit_homology_of_isAffineOpen
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (K : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory.{u + 1} X.Modules)
    (hqc : ∀ (n : ℕ) (q : ℤ),
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).obj (K.obj ⟨n⟩)).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hsurj : ∀ (n : ℕ) (q : ℤ),
      Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).map
        (K.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)))
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (q : ℤ) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    let F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules := K ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q
    let h : HasLimit F := inferInstance
    IsZero (Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf U p (@limit _ _ _ _ F h))
declarations.comment: affine_limit_acyclic

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isDerivedLimit_single_limit_powerQuotients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0K, part (4).** The ordinary inverse limit of the coherent adic
quotient tower, placed in degree zero, is its derived inverse limit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDerivedLimit_single_limit_powerQuotients
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] :
    let S := (powerQuotientSystem I F
      (isQuasicoherent_of_isCoherent F)).system
    ∃ h : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ =>
        (S ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ⟨n⟩),
      @IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory X.Modules) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (S ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0) h
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj (limit S))
declarations.comment: part (4), `lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ = R lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ`: for a coherent module `ℱ` on a locally Noetherian scheme and an arbitrary quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘`, the **ordinary** inverse limit of the adic quotient tower, placed in degree zero, is a **derived** inverse limit of that tower, with nothing assumed. The terms of the tower are quasi-coherent, hence acyclic on the affine opens, and its transitions are surjective on affine sections, hence Mittag-Leffler, and those are the two hypotheses [Stacks, Tag 0BKS] consumes. Existence of the product the derived limit is written with is part of the conclusion rather than a hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isZero_cohomology_limit_powerQuotients_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0K, part (5).** On a locally Noetherian scheme the ordinary inverse
limit `lim ℱ/ℐⁿℱ` of the adic quotient tower of a coherent module has no cohomology in positive
degree over an affine open.

The terms of the tower are quasi-coherent, so Serre vanishing gives their acyclicity on the
affine opens, and the transition maps are epimorphisms of quasi-coherent modules, hence
surjective on affine sections, so Mittag-Leffler gives the vanishing of `R¹ lim` of the sections
there. Those are exactly the two hypotheses of
`Stacks.Cohomology.SpaceInverseLimits.isZero_cohomology_limit_of_isBasis` on the basis of affine
opens.

The object is the ordinary limit `lim ℱ/ℐⁿℱ`, which is what the source's own argument for this
part is about: parts (4) and (5) are both read off [Stacks, Tag 0A0J] for the quotient tower,
and it is the tag's part (3) that then names that limit `ℱ^∧`. In this library part (3) at the
tag's own hypotheses is
`Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonDerivedCompletionLimitAdicQuotient` of
`Completion/AdicQuotientSliceTowerKoszul.lean`, and part (5) stated on the derived completion `ℱ^∧`
itself, in every degree `p ≠ 0` of either sign, is
`Stacks.Algebraization.isZero_homology_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_of_isAffineOpen` of
`Completion/CoherentCompletionAffineVanishing.lean`, which is derived from this statement through
that isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cohomology_limit_powerQuotients_of_isAffineOpen
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (U : X.affineOpens) (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (Hgroup X.ringCatSheaf U.1 p
      (show X.Modules from limit (adicQuotientSystem I F)))
declarations.comment: part (5), `H^p(U, ℱ^∧) = 0` for `p ≠ 0` and `U ⊂ X` affine open, read on the ordinary limit `lim ℱ/ℐⁿℱ` — the object [Stacks, Tag 0A0K] part (3) names `ℱ^∧` — for a coherent module `ℱ` on a locally Noetherian scheme and an arbitrary quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ`, with nothing assumed: the terms of the adic quotient tower are quasi-coherent, hence acyclic on the affine opens, and its transitions are surjective on affine sections, hence Mittag-Leffler, and those are the two hypotheses [Stacks, Tag 0BKS] consumes

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.nonempty_iso_homology_derivedCompletion_limit_adicQuotientSystem
declarations.doc:
**Part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0A0K].** For a pseudo-coherent object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` on a locally
Noetherian scheme `X` and an arbitrary quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘`,

`H^q(K^∧) ≅ lim_n H^q(K)/𝓘ⁿ H^q(K)`.

The isomorphism is `Stacks.BasisRestriction.moduleSheafIsoOfBasisSectionsIso` applied to the
affine comparisons `Stacks.Algebraization.adicQuotientLimitSectionsComparison`, which are
bijective and compatible with restriction, against the unit of sheafification on the degree-`q`
hypercohomology presheaf of `K^∧`; the sheafification of that presheaf is the cohomology sheaf by
[Stacks, Tag 0BKV].
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_homology_derivedCompletion_limit_adicQuotientSystem :
    Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules q).obj
          ((AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletion (opensRingedSite X.sheaf)
            (idealSheafSiteSubmodule 𝓘)).obj K) ≅
        limit (C := X.Modules)
          (adicQuotientSystem 𝓘 (homologyCoherentModule K hK q).obj))
declarations.comment: part (2), `H^q(K^∧) = lim H^q(K)/𝓘ⁿ H^q(K)`: for a **pseudo-coherent** object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` on a locally Noetherian scheme `X` and an **arbitrary** quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘`, the degree-`q` cohomology sheaf of the derived completion `K^∧` is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the adic quotient tower of the coherent module `H^q(K)`, with nothing further assumed — no quasi-compactness of `X`, no generation of `𝓘` by global sections, no Mittag-Leffler hypothesis and no appeal to part (1) of the tag. The limit is the same object parts (3), (4) and (5) are registered over, `Stacks.Algebraization.adicQuotientSystem`, read at the coherent module the tag's own footnote names. The isomorphism is non-canonical in the statement only because the source's canonical maps go the other way; it is produced by gluing the canonical affine comparisons, which are unique

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonDerivedCompletionLimitAdicQuotient
declarations.doc:
**Part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0A0K]: `ℱ^∧ = lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ` with an ordinary inverse limit.** Let `X`
be a locally Noetherian scheme — **not** assumed quasi-compact — let `𝓘 ⊂ 𝒪_X` be an arbitrary
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then the canonical
comparison

`c : ℱ^∧ ⟶ (lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ)[0]`

from the derived completion of `ℱ` along `𝓘` to the ordinary inverse limit of the adic quotients,
placed in degree zero, is an isomorphism.

The comparison is the unique map compatible with the completion unit of `ℱ` and the limit lift
`ℱ ⟶ lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ` (`Stacks.Algebraization`
`.existsUnique_comparison_derivedCompletion_limit_adicQuotientSystem`), so the statement is about
a named map and not merely the existence of an isomorphism — which is what makes it provable at
these hypotheses at all, invertibility of a named map being local on the site
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_of_coversTop_mapDerivedCategory`).

`Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparison_of_affineOpens_sliceTower` reduces it to the per-affine-
slice presentation `Stacks.Algebraization`
`.exists_isDerivedLimitWithProjections_completionToAdicQuotientSliceTower`, which is the Koszul
chain of `DerivedCompletionRinged/` run on the slice over an affine open, where the restricted
ideal sheaf is generated by finitely many sections and the Artin–Rees level is computed once over
a single Noetherian model.

`Stacks.Algebraization.nonempty_iso_completion_limit_adicQuotientSystem` of
`Completion/KoszulAdicCompletionLimit.lean` is the other registration of this part: it runs the
same chain on `X` itself, which costs `[CompactSpace X]` and a global generating family for `𝓘`
and delivers the non-canonical isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 0H9L] in place of the invertibility of
`c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_comparisonDerivedCompletionLimitAdicQuotient :
    IsIso (comparisonDerivedCompletionLimitAdicQuotient I ℱ)
declarations.comment: part (3), `ℱ^∧ = lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ` with an ordinary limit, at the source's own hypotheses: for a coherent module `ℱ` on a locally Noetherian scheme `X`, which is **not** assumed quasi-compact, and an **arbitrary** quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘` — with no global generating family — the canonical comparison `c : ℱ^∧ ⟶ (lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ)[0]` from the derived completion of `ℱ` along `𝓘` to the ordinary inverse limit of the adic quotients `ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ`, placed in degree zero, is an isomorphism. The comparison is the unique map compatible with the completion unit and the limit lift, so the statement identifies a named map rather than asserting an abstract isomorphism. The source's `=` is also read as such an abstract isomorphism by `nonempty_iso_completion_limit_adicQuotientSystem`, which buys quasi-compactness of the scheme and a global generating family for the ideal sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isDerivedLimit_adicReductionTower_derivedCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 0A0K].** On a locally Noetherian scheme `Y`, for an arbitrary
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘` and an arbitrary object `K` of `D(𝒪_Y)`, the derived
completion `K^∧` along `𝓘` is a derived limit of the tower `n ↦ K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y/𝓘ⁿ⁺¹`.

See the module documentation for the proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_adicReductionTower_derivedCompletion
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.opensRingedSite Y.sheaf).O)))) :
    IsDerivedLimit
      (adicReductionTower (Stacks.SheafOfModules.opensRingedSite Y.sheaf)
        (idealSheafSiteSubmodule 𝓘) K)
      ((derivedCompletion (Stacks.SheafOfModules.opensRingedSite Y.sheaf)
        (idealSheafSiteSubmodule 𝓘)).obj K)
declarations.comment: part (1), `K^∧ = R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 𝒪/𝓘ⁿ)`, at the source's own hypotheses: on a locally Noetherian scheme `Y`, for an **arbitrary** quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘` and an **arbitrary** object `K` of `D(𝒪_Y)`, the derived completion `K^∧` along `𝓘` (the reflector of Tag 099F) is a derived limit of the tower `n ↦ K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y/𝓘ⁿ⁺¹`. No quasi-compactness of `Y` and no generation of `𝓘` by global sections is assumed. `R lim` is a predicate rather than a functor, so the source's equality is read as `K^∧` being a derived limit of that tower, the same reading as the tag's part (4); the tower over the positive powers `𝓘ⁿ⁺¹` is cofinal in the one over all powers

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isZero_homology_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_of_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
**Part (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0A0K]: `H^p(U, ℱ^∧) = 0` for `p ≠ 0` and `U ⊂ X` affine open.** Let
`X` be a locally Noetherian scheme — not assumed quasi-compact — let `𝓘 ⊂ 𝒪_X` be an arbitrary
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then for every affine open
`U ⊂ X` and every integer `p ≠ 0` the degree-`p` hypercohomology over `U` of the derived
completion `ℱ^∧` of `ℱ` along `𝓘`, an object of `D(𝒪_X)`, vanishes.

Part (3) (`Stacks.Algebraization.isIso_comparisonDerivedCompletionLimitAdicQuotient`) identifies
`ℱ^∧` with `(lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ)[0]`; below degree zero the vanishing is left t-exactness of `RΓ(U, -)`,
and above it is the vanishing of the higher cohomology of `lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ` over an affine open,
`Stacks.Algebraization.isZero_cohomology_limit_powerQuotients_of_isAffineOpen`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_of_isAffineOpen
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (ℱ : X.Modules)
    [ℱ.IsCoherent] (U : X.affineOpens) (p : ℤ) (hp : p ≠ 0) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) p).obj
      ((derivedSections (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace) U.1).obj
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletion (opensRingedSite X.sheaf)
            (idealSheafSiteSubmodule I)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj ℱ))))
declarations.comment: part (5), `H^p(U, ℱ^∧) = 0` for `p ≠ 0` and `U ⊂ X` affine open, on the derived completion itself: for a coherent module `ℱ` on a locally Noetherian scheme `X`, which is not required to be quasi-compact, and an arbitrary quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘`, the degree-`p` hypercohomology over an affine open `U` of the derived completion `ℱ^∧` of `ℱ` along `𝓘`, an object of `D(𝒪_X)`, vanishes for every integer `p ≠ 0`, negative degrees included. The proof reads `ℱ^∧` as `lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ` in degree zero by part (3) and applies the vanishing on that limit

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.nonempty_iso_completion_limit_adicQuotientSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0K, part (3).** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme,
let `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪_Y` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals generated by the global sections
`f_1, …, f_r`, and let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_Y`-module. Then the derived completion `ℱ^∧` of `ℱ`
along `ℐ` is isomorphic, in `D(𝒪_Y)`, to the **ordinary** inverse limit `lim ℱ/ℐⁿℱ` of the adic
quotients, placed in degree zero.

`R lim` is a predicate rather than a functor here, and a derived limit is unique only up to a
non-canonical isomorphism, which is why the conclusion is `Nonempty` of an isomorphism — exactly as
in [Stacks, Tag 0H9L], `_root_.Rlim.Pro.nonempty_iso_of_isDerivedLimit_of_pro_isomorphism`, which
is the last step of the proof.

The ideal sheaf is not a parameter with a generation hypothesis: it is
`Stacks.Algebraization.koszulIdealSheafData`, the extension to `Y` of the ideal of global
functions spanned by `f_1, …, f_r`, whose affine components are computed by
`Stacks.Algebraization.koszulIdealSheafData_ideal`. Nothing is lost by fixing it, because an
`IdealSheafData` is determined by its affine components and so every ideal sheaf generated by
those sections equals this one, which is
`Stacks.Algebraization.eq_koszulIdealSheafData`.

`[CompactSpace Y]` is a genuine hypothesis and not an artefact: the Artin–Rees level behind the
pro-vanishing of the Koszul cohomology sheaves below the top degree is produced one per member of
an affine cover, and the proof takes the maximum over a *finite* cover. See the section "The
hypotheses, and what they are for" of this file. The source asks neither for quasi-compactness
nor for `ℐ` to be globally generated; the module documentation of
`Completion/AdicQuotientDerivedLimit.lean` records what a proof at the source's own hypotheses
would take, namely a canonical comparison, which is what this route does not produce.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_completion_limit_adicQuotientSystem :
    Nonempty
      ((RingedSite.completionFunctor (Stacks.SheafOfModules.opensRingedSite Y.sheaf) f).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (RingedSite.singleSheafComplex
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.opensRingedSite Y.sheaf) ℱ)) ≅
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Y.Modules 0).obj
          (limit (adicQuotientSystem (koszulIdealSheafData Y f) ℱ)))
declarations.comment: part (3), `ℱ^∧ = lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ` with an ordinary limit: for a coherent module `ℱ` on a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme `Y` and the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘` generated by global sections `f_1, …, f_r` of `𝒪_Y`, the derived completion `ℱ^∧` along `𝓘` is isomorphic in `D(𝒪_Y)` to the ordinary inverse limit of the adic quotients `ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ`, placed in degree zero. The ideal sheaf is the extension to `Y` of the ideal those global sections span, so its generation by them is a definition and not a hypothesis, and every ideal sheaf so generated equals it. The isomorphism is non-canonical because a derived limit is, which is the form [Stacks, Tag 0H9L] takes

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.isDerivedLimit_derivedTensor_adicQuotientSystem_completion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0K, part (1).** Let `Y` be a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme,
let `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪_Y` be the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals generated by the global sections
`f_1, …, f_r`, and let `K` be an arbitrary object of `D(𝒪_Y)`. Then the derived completion `K^∧`
of `K` along `ℐ` is a derived limit of the tower `n ↦ K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y/ℐⁿ`:

`K^∧ = R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y/ℐⁿ)`.

`R lim` is a predicate rather than a functor here, exactly as in the tag's part (4)
`Stacks.Algebraization.isDerivedLimit_single_limit_powerQuotients`, so the source's equality is
read as the object `K^∧` being a derived limit of the tower; no comparison map has to be
produced, and nothing is weakened by that reading.

The proof is [Stacks, Tag 0A0E] — `K^∧` is a derived limit of `n ↦ K ⊗^𝐋 (K^n)^∨` — together
with the pro-isomorphism of the dual Koszul tower with `n ↦ 𝒪/ℐⁿ`, whiskered by `K ⊗^𝐋 -`. The
coefficient object enters both towers as that same whiskering functor, so the two meet with no
constraint of the derived tensor product used.

`[CompactSpace Y]` is a genuine hypothesis of this route and not an artefact: the Artin–Rees
level behind the pro-vanishing of the Koszul cohomology sheaves below the top degree is produced
one per member of an affine cover and the proof maximises over a *finite* cover. See the section
"The hypotheses, and what they are for" of this file. The source asks neither for
quasi-compactness nor for `ℐ` to be globally generated; `Completion/AdicQuotientDerivedLimit.lean`
records what a proof at the source's own hypotheses would take.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_derivedTensor_adicQuotientSystem_completion
    (K : DerivedCategory Y.Modules) :
    IsDerivedLimit
      ((adicQuotientSystem (koszulIdealSheafData Y f)
            (SheafOfModules.unit
              (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
                (Stacks.SheafOfModules.opensRingedSite Y.sheaf).O)) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Y.Modules 0) ⋙
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.opensRingedSite Y.sheaf)).tensor.obj K)
      ((RingedSite.completionFunctor
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.opensRingedSite Y.sheaf) f).obj K)
declarations.comment: part (1), `K^∧ = R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 𝒪/𝓘ⁿ)`: for an **arbitrary** object `K` of `D(𝒪_Y)` on a quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme `Y` and the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `𝓘` generated by global sections `f_1, …, f_r` of `𝒪_Y`, the derived completion `K^∧` along `𝓘` is a derived limit of the tower `n ↦ K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_Y} 𝒪_Y/𝓘ⁿ`. `R lim` is a predicate rather than a functor, so the source's equality is read as `K^∧` being a derived limit of that tower, which is the same reading the tag's part (4) is registered with. The ideal sheaf is the extension to `Y` of the ideal those global sections span, so its generation by them is a definition and not a hypothesis, and every ideal sheaf so generated equals it. The object `K` carries no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.adicCompletion_homology_derivedSections_iso_derivedCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0L, the second equality.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme,
`𝓘 ⊂ 𝒪_X` a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and `K` a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)`. For an
affine open `U`, with `A = Γ(X, U)` and `I = 𝓘(U)`, and any left adjoint `C` to the inclusion of
the derived-complete objects of `D(A)`, the `I`-adic completion `lim H^p(U, K)/IⁿH^p(U, K)` of
`H^p(U, K)` is the derived `I`-adic completion of the `A`-module `H^p(U, K)`, read in degree zero.

This is [Stacks, Tag 0A06] for the complex `H^p(U, K)[0]`, which is legitimate because
`H^p(U, K)` is a finite module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_homology_derivedSections_iso_derivedCompletion
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (𝓘 : X.IdealSheafData)
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (U : X.affineOpens)
    (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) ⥤
      (show ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1))) from
        fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (𝓘.ideal U) L).FullSubcategory)
    (adj : C ⊣ (show ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1))) from
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (𝓘.ideal U) L).ι)
    (p : ℤ) :
    Nonempty
      (ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U.1) (AdicCompletion (𝓘.ideal U)
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) p).obj
            ((derivedSections (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace) U.1).obj K))) ≅
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) 0).obj
          ((C ⋙ (show ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1))) from
              fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (𝓘.ideal U) L).ι).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) 0).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) p).obj
                ((derivedSections (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace) U.1).obj K)))))
declarations.comment: the second equality `lim H^p(U, K)/IⁿH^p(U, K) = H^p(U, K)^∧`, the right hand completion being the derived completion of the module `H^p(U, K)` along `I = 𝓘(U)`; the first equality is `homology_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_iso_adicCompletion`

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.homology_derivedCompletion_derivedSections_iso_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0L, the first equality, read on the module side.** Let `X` be a
locally Noetherian scheme, `𝓘 ⊂ 𝒪_X` a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and `K` a pseudo-coherent
object of `D(𝒪_X)`. For an affine open `U`, with `A = Γ(X, U)` and `I = 𝓘(U)`, the degree-`p`
cohomology of the derived completion in `D(A)` of `RΓ(U, K)` is the `I`-adic completion
`lim H^p(U, K)/IⁿH^p(U, K)` of `H^p(U, K)`.

Everything the source's first equality needs beyond the identification `RΓ(U, K^∧)
= RΓ(U, K)^∧`: `A` is Noetherian and `H^n(U, K)` is a finite `A`-module in every degree
(`Stacks.Algebraization.finite_homology_derivedSections_of_isPseudoCoherent`, which is where
pseudo-coherence and the locally Noetherian hypothesis of the tag are used), so [Stacks,
Tag 0A06] applies to `RΓ(U, K)` along `I = 𝓘(U)`.

The derived completion of `A`-modules is produced, not assumed: the first conjunct exhibits a
left adjoint `C` to the inclusion of the derived-complete objects of `D(A)`, by
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_derivedCompletionAdjunction`, and the second conjunct holds for
every such `C`, so no choice of reflector enters.

The left hand side is the cohomology of `C(RΓ(U, K))`, not of `RΓ(U, K^∧)`; passing between the
two is [Stacks, Tag 0CQI], which
`exists_adjunction_and_homology_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_iso_adicCompletion` below takes
as an input and
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_iso_homology_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_whole` of
`Completion/FormalFunctionsPseudoCoherentWhole.lean` discharges.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homology_derivedCompletion_derivedSections_iso_adicCompletion
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (𝓘 : X.IdealSheafData)
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (U : X.affineOpens) (p : ℤ) :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1))) :=
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (𝓘.ideal U) L
    (∃ C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory,
        Nonempty (C ⊣ P.ι)) ∧
      ∀ C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory, (C ⊣ P.ι) →
        Nonempty
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) p).obj
              ((C ⋙ P.ι).obj
                ((derivedSections (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace) U.1).obj K)) ≅
            ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U.1) (AdicCompletion (𝓘.ideal U)
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) p).obj
                ((derivedSections (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace) U.1).obj K))))
declarations.comment: the first equality `H^p(RΓ(U, K)^∧) = lim H^p(U, K)/IⁿH^p(U, K)` on the module side: its left hand side read at the derived completion in `D(A)` of the derived sections `RΓ(U, K)`, for `A = Γ(X, U)` and `I = 𝓘(U)`, which is [Stacks, Tag 0A06] applied to `RΓ(U, K)` together with the finiteness of the `H^n(U, K)`; the second equality is `exists_adjunction_and_adicCompletion_homology_derivedSections_iso_derivedCompletion`

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_iso_homology_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_whole
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0L.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪_X` a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and `K` a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)` with derived
completion `K^∧`. Then for every affine open `U ⊂ X`, with `A = Γ(X, U)` and `I = ℐ(U)`, and
every `p`,

`H^p(U, K^∧) = lim H^p(U, K)/IⁿH^p(U, K) = H^p(U, K)^∧`,

the completion on the right being the derived completion of the `A`-module `H^p(U, K)` along `I`,
read in degree zero.

Both equalities, at the source's own hypotheses. The first is
`exists_adjunction_and_homology_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_iso_adicCompletion`
with its input — the identification `RΓ(U, K^∧) = RΓ(U, K)^∧` of [Stacks, Tag 0CQI] — discharged by
`Stacks.Algebraization.nonempty_iso_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_affine`; the second is
`Stacks.Algebraization.adicCompletion_homology_derivedSections_iso_derivedCompletion`, which is
[Stacks, Tag 0A06] for the finite module `H^p(U, K)` placed in degree zero. Pseudo-coherence and
the locally Noetherian hypothesis enter through the finiteness of `H^n(U, K)`, which is
`Stacks.Algebraization.finite_homology_derivedSections_of_isPseudoCoherent`.

Derived completion of `A`-modules is produced, not assumed: the first conjunct exhibits a left
adjoint `C` to the inclusion of the derived-complete objects of `D(A)`, by
`Stacks.Algebraization.exists_derivedCompletionAdjunction`, and the second holds for every such
`C`, so no choice of reflector enters. The derived completion `K^∧` on `D(𝒪_X)` is produced too:
`ℐ` is of finite type on a locally Noetherian scheme
(`Stacks.Algebraization.isFiniteType_idealSheafSiteSubmodule`), so the reflector of [Stacks,
Tag 099F] exists along the tag's own ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_homology_derivedSections_derivedCompletion_whole
    (hK : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) K) (p : ℤ) :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1))) :=
      fun L ↦ IsDerivedComplete (𝓘.ideal U) L
    let Hp := fun (L : DerivedCategory X.Modules) ↦
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) p).obj
        ((derivedSections (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace) U.1).obj L)
    (∃ C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory,
        Nonempty (C ⊣ P.ι)) ∧
      ∀ (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory) (_ : C ⊣ P.ι),
        Nonempty
          (Hp ((AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletion (opensRingedSite X.sheaf)
              (idealSheafSiteSubmodule 𝓘)).obj K) ≅
            ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U.1) (AdicCompletion (𝓘.ideal U) (Hp K))) ∧
        Nonempty
          (ModuleCat.of Γ(X, U.1) (AdicCompletion (𝓘.ideal U) (Hp K)) ≅
            (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) 0).obj
              ((C ⋙ P.ι).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(X, U.1)) 0).obj (Hp K))))
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, at the source's own hypotheses — `X` a locally Noetherian scheme, `𝓘 ⊂ 𝒪_X` a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and `K` a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)`: for every affine open `U`, with `A = Γ(X, U)` and `I = 𝓘(U)`, and every `p`, both equalities `H^p(U, K^∧) = lim H^p(U, K)/IⁿH^p(U, K) = H^p(U, K)^∧`, the right hand completion being the derived completion of the A-module H^p(U,K) along I read in degree zero. The left hand side is read at the derived completion `K^∧` on `D(𝒪_X)` along `𝓘` itself, which exists because a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of a locally Noetherian scheme is of finite type, so [Stacks, Tag 099F] applies; the passage `RΓ(U, K^∧) = RΓ(U, K)^∧` is [Stacks, Tag 0CQI] at an affine open, where the chosen generating family spans `𝓘(U)` itself. The reflector onto the derived-complete objects of D(A) is produced out of [Stacks, Tag 0920] and the conclusion quantifies over it

declarations.name: Stacks.Algebraization.exists_shortExact_adicCompletion_cohomology_whole
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A0M.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal,
`f : X ⟶ Spec A` a Noetherian scheme over `A` and `ℱ` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose cohomology
modules `H^p(X, ℱ)` are finite over `A` — the hypotheses of the source, and nothing else. Write
`𝓘 = I · 𝒪_X`. Then for every `p`:

* the `I`-adic completion of the `A`-module `H^p(X, ℱ)` sits in a short exact sequence of
  `A`-modules

  `0 ⟶ R¹lim H^{p-1}(X, ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ) ⟶ H^p(X, ℱ)^∧ ⟶ lim H^p(X, ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ) ⟶ 0`,

  whose left term is the cokernel of `1 - shift` on the product of the degree-`(p-1)` cohomology
  tower and whose right term is the inverse limit of the degree-`p` cohomology tower; and
* **if `f` is proper the `R¹lim` term is zero**.

Both are the source's own assertions, at the source's own hypotheses, with nothing assumed. The
sequence is `Stacks.Algebraization.exists_shortExact_adicCompletion_cohomology`, whose single
input — the identification `RΓ(X, ℱ)^∧ ≅ RΓ(X, lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ)` of [Stacks, Tag 0BLX] — is supplied
by `Stacks.Algebraization.hBLX_baseIdealSheaf`: `A` being Noetherian, `I = (a_1, …, a_r)`, and
`I · 𝒪_X` is then the ideal sheaf generated by the global sections `ρ a_i`, where the Koszul
identity of [Stacks, Tag 0BLX] and part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0A0K] are both available. The
properness clause is
`Stacks.Algebraization.isZero_firstDerivedLimit_cohomology_adicQuotients_of_isProper_int`, which
rests on the Mittag-Leffler condition of [Stacks, Tag 02OB] and through it on the proper mapping
theorem [Stacks, Tag 02O5].

Derived `I`-adic completion is never introduced as data: a reflector onto the derived-complete
objects of `D(A)` exists by [Stacks, Tag 0920] and is produced inside the proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_adicCompletion_cohomology_whole
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hfinite : ∀ p : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) p).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F))))
    (p : ℤ) :
    let T : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) :=
      adicQuotientSystem (baseIdealSheaf A I f) F ⋙
        DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0 ⋙ derivedGlobalSectionsOver f
    let H : ℤ → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A := fun q ↦
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) q
    (∃ (i : CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A (T ⋙ H (p - 1)) ⟶
        ModuleCat.of A (AdicCompletion I
          ((H p).obj ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F)))))
      (q : ModuleCat.of A (AdicCompletion I
          ((H p).obj ((derivedGlobalSectionsOver f).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj F)))) ⟶
        limit (T ⋙ H p))
      (w : i ≫ q = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk i q w).ShortExact) ∧
    (AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper f →
      IsZero (CompletionSequences.firstDerivedLimit A (T ⋙ H (p - 1))))
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, at the source's own hypotheses — `A` Noetherian, `I ⊆ A` an ideal, `f : X ⟶ Spec A` a Noetherian scheme over `A` and `ℱ` a coherent `𝒪_X`-module with every `H^p(X, ℱ)` finite over `A`: for every `p` the short exact sequence of `A`-modules `0 → R¹lim H^{p-1}(X, ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ) → H^p(X,ℱ)^∧ → lim H^p(X, ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ) → 0` whose middle term is the I-adic completion of the A-module H^p(X,ℱ), together with the vanishing of the R¹lim term for a proper f. The ideal is arbitrary: the identification of the middle term is the identity `RΓ(X,ℱ)^∧ = RΓ(X, lim ℱ/𝓘ⁿℱ)` of [Stacks, Tag 0BLX], got from the Koszul identity of that tag at the ideal sheaf generated by the images of a generating family of I — which a Noetherian A provides — and part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0A0K]. The properness clause is the Mittag-Leffler condition of [Stacks, Tag 02OB], discharged from [Stacks, Tag 02O8]. The reflector onto the derived-complete objects of D(A) is produced in the proof out of [Stacks, Tag 0920]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_isClosedImmersion_app_of_isLimit_of_initiallySmall
declarations.doc:
`AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_isClosedImmersion_app_of_isLimit` with the index universes
independent of the scheme universe, at the cost of `CategoryTheory.LocallySmall.{u}` and
`CategoryTheory.InitiallySmall.{u}` on the index category.

This is the faithful rendering of Tag 0A0N: the source's limit is indexed by a directed set, so
the index is small relative to the schemes and the smallness is part of the statement rather than
an addition to it. See the module documentation, and compare
`AlgebraicGeometry.eventually_isAffineHom_of_isLimit_of_initiallySmall` (Tag 09ZM), which carries
the condition for the same reason and whose counterexample shows it cannot be dropped.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isClosedImmersion_app_of_isLimit_of_initiallySmall (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj S) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (f : c.pt ⟶ S)
    (hf : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const I).map f)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    [∀ i, CompactSpace (D.obj i)] [∀ i, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsClosedImmersion (D.map g)]
    [∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (t.app i : D.obj i ⟶ S)] [IsClosedImmersion f] :
    ∃ i : I, ∀ {j : I} (_ : j ⟶ i), IsClosedImmersion (t.app j : D.obj j ⟶ S)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isLimit_isProper_finiteType_arrow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0P.** A proper morphism onto a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme is the
inverse limit, over a directed set, of an inverse system of proper morphisms whose targets are of
finite type over `ℤ` and whose transition morphisms are affine on both sources and targets.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_isProper_finiteType_arrow
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f]
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirectedOrder I)
      (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Arrow Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D),
      (∀ i, IsProper (D.obj i).hom) ∧
      (∀ i,
        LocallyOfFiniteType (terminal.from (D.obj i).right) ∧
          QuasiCompact (terminal.from (D.obj i).right)) ∧
      (∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (g : i ⟶ j),
        IsAffineHom (D.map g).left ∧ IsAffineHom (D.map g).right) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit c) ∧ Nonempty (c.pt ≅ Arrow.mk f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegral_pushforwardAlgebra_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0Q, first assertion.**  For a universally closed morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
algebraic spaces over `S`, the direct image `f_*𝒪_X` is integral over `𝒪_Y`.

The assertion is étale local on `Y`: on an affine étale scheme chart `V` of `Y` the sections of
`f_*𝒪_X` are the global regular functions on the algebraic space `X ×_Y V`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.directImageSectionsToGlobalFunctions`, which is injective), the
projection `X ×_Y V ⟶ V` is universally closed because `f` is, and the global functions of a
universally closed algebraic space over an affine base are integral over the base
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegral_globalFunctions_of_universallyClosed`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegral_pushforwardAlgebra_of_universallyClosed (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (huc : UniversallyClosed B S hS f.hom) :
    (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsIntegral
declarations.comment: first sentence: f_*O_X is integral over O_Y; only universal closedness of f is used

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_pushforwardAlgebraMap_toNormalizationInQcqsOver_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0Q, second sentence: the normalization of `Y` in `X` is
`\underline{Spec}_Y(f_*𝒪_X)`.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated and
universally closed morphism of algebraic spaces, and let `X ⟶ Y' ⟶ Y` be the normalization of
`Y` in `X` (Stacks 0822; `ν : Y' ⟶ Y` is affine).  Then the map `ν_*𝒪_{Y'} ⟶ f_*𝒪_X` of
`𝒪_Y`-algebras induced by the canonical morphism `f' : X ⟶ Y'` is an isomorphism, so
`Y' = \underline{Spec}_Y(f_*𝒪_X)` and `f'` is the canonical morphism of Stacks 081X.

The map induced by `f'` is `ν_*𝒪_{Y'} ≅ 𝒪' ⊂ f_*𝒪_X`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pushforwardAlgebraMap_toNormalizationInQcqsOver`), and the inclusion
of the integral closure `𝒪'` is all of `f_*𝒪_X` because `f_*𝒪_X` is integral over `𝒪_Y`, the
first sentence of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pushforwardAlgebraMap_toNormalizationInQcqsOver_of_universallyClosed :
    IsIso (pushforwardAlgebraMap B S hS (toNormalizationInQcqsOver f hfqc hfqs))
declarations.comment: second sentence: the normalization X ⟶ Y' ⟶ Y of Y in X induces ν_*O_{Y'} ≅ f_*O_X, i.e. Y' = Spec_Y(f_*O_X) with the factorization of 081X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_iso_normalizationInQcqs_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0Q, second sentence, as an identification of factorizations.**  For a
quasi-compact, quasi-separated and universally closed `f : X ⟶ Y`, every factorization
`X ⟶ Z ⟶ Y` of `f` of the kind Stacks 081X constructs — `Z` affine over `Y` and the induced map
`(Z ⟶ Y)_*𝒪_Z ⟶ f_*𝒪_X` an isomorphism, i.e. `Z = \underline{Spec}_Y(f_*𝒪_X)` with its
canonical morphism from `X` — is the normalization of `Y` in `X`: there is a unique isomorphism
`Y' ≅ Z` over `Y` from the normalization carrying the canonical `f' : X ⟶ Y'` to `X ⟶ Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_normalizationInQcqs_of_universallyClosed
    (Z : AffineOver B S hS Y) (g : Over.mk f ⟶ Z.obj)
    [IsIso (pushforwardAlgebraMap B S hS g)] :
    ∃! k : (normalizationInQcqsAffineOver B S hS f hfqc hfqs).obj ≅ Z.obj,
      toNormalizationInQcqsOver f hfqc hfqs ≫ k.hom = g
declarations.comment: second sentence: the normalization of Y in X is, uniquely, the factorization X ⟶ Spec_Y(f_*O_X) ⟶ Y of 081X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_integralClosureInclusion_pushforwardAlgebra
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces whose direct image `f_*𝒪_X` is integral over
`𝒪_Y`, the inclusion of the integral closure `𝒪'` of `𝒪_Y` in `f_*𝒪_X` is an isomorphism of algebra
sheaves, so `𝒪' = f_*𝒪_X` and the normalization of `Y` in `X` — the relative spectrum of `𝒪'`,
Stacks 0821 — is the factorization `X ⟶ Spec_Y(f_*𝒪_X) ⟶ Y` of Stacks 081X.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_integralClosureInclusion_pushforwardAlgebra (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsIntegral) :
    IsIso (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureInclusion (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)))
declarations.comment: second assertion: the normalization of Y in X is the factorization through Spec_Y(f_*O_X), with the integrality of f_*O_X assumed rather than proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eventually_isFinite_of_isLimit_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0S.** Let `X = lim X_i` be a directed limit of algebraic spaces over an algebraic
space `Y`, with affine transition morphisms. If `Y` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, every
`X_i` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the transition morphisms are finite, every
`X_i → Y` is locally of finite type and `X → Y` is integral, then `X_i → Y` is finite for all
sufficiently large `i`.

The limit `X` is an algebraic space by Stacks 07SF
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_limit_of_isSiteSmall`), so that is not assumed.
Every input of the source's proof is discharged: the affine étale chart of `Y` by Stacks 03H6,
the affine stage of the base-changed system by Stacks 07SQ, the finiteness of the base-changed
stages descending to finiteness over `Y` by Stacks 03ZQ, and the scheme case by Stacks 09ZN. The
index set is asked to be small compared to the cofinality of the site's size cutoff, the Stacks
07SF bound that both Stacks 07SQ and the passage from the site to schemes carry here.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isFinite_of_isLimit_of_isIntegral
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (hI : #I < B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
    (p : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (f : c.pt ⟶ Y)
    (hf : ∀ i : I, f = c.π.app (op i) ≫ p.app (op i))
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hD : ∀ i : I, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj (op i)))
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y)
    (hDqc : ∀ i : I, IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS (D.obj (op i)))
    (hDqs : ∀ i : I, IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ (D.obj (op i)))
    (haffine : ∀ {i j : I} (h : i ≤ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.map (homOfLE h).op))
    (hfinite : ∀ {i j : I} (h : i ≤ j), IsFinite B S hS (D.map (homOfLE h).op))
    (hfiniteType : ∀ i : I, IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (p.app (op i)))
    (hintegral : IsIntegralHom B S hS f) :
    ∀ᶠ i : I in Filter.atTop, IsFinite B S hS (p.app (op i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eventually_isClosedImmersion_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0T.** Let `Y` be an algebraic space over `S` and let `X = lim X_i` be a directed
limit of algebraic spaces over `Y` with affine transition morphisms. Assume `Y` is quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, the `X_i` are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the transition morphisms
`X_{i'} ⟶ X_i` are closed immersions, each `X_i ⟶ Y` is locally of finite type, and `X ⟶ Y` is a
closed immersion. Then `X_i ⟶ Y` is a closed immersion for `i` large enough.

Closed immersions are affine, so the source's assumption that the transition morphisms are
affine is implied by the assumption that they are closed immersions and is not stated
separately.

The proof is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eventually_isClosedImmersion_app_of_isRepresentable_stage`,
which is the source's argument down to its appeal to Stacks 07SR, fed with the stage that Stacks
07SR provides: the limit of the system base changed along an affine étale surjective chart of
`Y` is a closed subspace of an affine scheme, hence a scheme, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isRepresentable_system_obj_of_isSiteSmall` makes
some stage of that base changed system a scheme.

The index type is `I : Type u` and its cardinality is asked to be small compared to the
cofinality of the site's size cutoff, as in Situation 084R
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.LimitSituation`) and as in every result of that family which this
library proves — Stacks 07SF, Stacks 0827, Stacks 084T, Stacks 086X, Stacks 07SQ and
Stacks 07SR. The bound is used only to invoke Stacks 07SR.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_isClosedImmersion_app
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I]
    {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (f : c.pt ⟶ Y)
    (hcomm : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS c.pt)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj (op i)))
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y)
    (hDqc : ∀ i, IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS (D.obj (op i)))
    (hDqs : ∀ i, IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ (D.obj (op i)))
    (hClosed : ∀ {a b : Iᵒᵖ} (φ : a ⟶ b), IsClosedImmersion B S hS (D.map φ))
    (hFT : ∀ i, IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (t.app (op i)))
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) (hI : #I < B.cutoff.ord.cof) :
    ∀ᶠ i in atTop, IsClosedImmersion B S hS (t.app (op i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isLimit_closedSubspaces_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over `S`,
with `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then `X` is a directed limit `X = lim X_i`: there are a
nonempty directed index set and an inverse system of closed subspaces `X_i ⊆ Y` whose transition
morphisms are closed immersions and whose inclusions `X_i ⟶ Y` are closed immersions of finite
presentation, together with a limiting cone with vertex `X` whose legs `X ⟶ X_i` compose with the
inclusions to `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_closedSubspaces_of_isClosedImmersion (Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y.1) (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y.1)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y.1)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (_ : Nonempty I)
      (Z : I → ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (hZ : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄, i ≤ j → (Z j).1 ≤ (Z i).1)
      (hle : ∀ i, Subfunctor.range f ≤ (Z i).1),
      (∀ ⦃i j : Iᵒᵖ⦄ (g : i ⟶ j), IsClosedImmersion B S hS
        ((closedSubspaceDiagram B S hS (fun i => (Z i).1) hZ).map g)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsClosedImmersion B S hS (Z i).1.ι ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS (Z i).1.ι) ∧
      (∀ i, ((closedSubspaceCone B S hS (fun i => (Z i).1) hZ (Subfunctor.range f) hle).extend
        (Subfunctor.toRange f)).π.app (op i) ≫ (Z i).1.ι = f) ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit ((closedSubspaceCone B S hS (fun i => (Z i).1) hZ (Subfunctor.range f)
        hle).extend (Subfunctor.toRange f)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasClosedSubspaceApproximation_of_invariantIdeals
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0U.** Let `S` be a scheme and let `X ⊆ Y` be a closed subspace of an algebraic
space `Y` over `S`.  Then `X` is a directed inverse limit `X = lim X_i` of closed subspaces of
`Y` whose transition morphisms are closed immersions and whose structure morphisms `X_i ⟶ Y` are
closed immersions of finite presentation, as soon as the ideal sheaf cut out by `X` on a
surjective étale scheme chart `V ⟶ Y` is the supremum of a monotone family of invariant ideal
sheaves of `𝒪_V` each of which cuts out a closed subspace of finite presentation over `Y`.

The approximating family is the hypothesis: it is what Stacks 0829 supplies for the ideal sheaf
of `X`, read on the chart `V`, together with Stacks 084Q for the finite presentation of the
stages.  Everything else is proved here and unconditionally: each member of the family cuts out
a closed subspace of `Y` by étale descent, its chart ideal on `V` is the given ideal sheaf, the
family of subspaces is antitone with `X` contained in every member, and the inclusions exhibit
`X` as the inverse limit.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasClosedSubspaceApproximation_of_invariantIdeals [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (i₀ : I) (X : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1) (hK : Monotone K)
    (hsup : (⨆ i, K i) = etaleChartKer B S hS Y X (chartOfSurjectiveEtale B S hS Y he))
    (hfp : ∀ i, IsFinitePresentation B S hS
      (invariantSubspace B S hS φ (Subobject.mk (K i).subschemeι)).ι) :
    HasClosedSubspaceApproximation B S hS Y X
declarations.comment: given the approximating family of invariant ideal sheaves on a chart, which is Stacks 0829 for the ideal sheaf of `X` read on that chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isLimit_isProper_isFinitePresentation_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, with `Y` quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. Then `X` is the directed limit, along closed immersions and over `Y`, of algebraic
spaces proper and of finite presentation over `Y`, the projections from `X` being closed
immersions.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_isProper_isFinitePresentation_of_isProper
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsProper B S hS f)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (_ : Nonempty I)
      (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y)
      (π : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D),
      (∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsProper B S hS (t.app i) ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS (t.app i)) ∧
      (∀ ⦃i j : Iᵒᵖ⦄ (e : i ⟶ j), IsClosedImmersion B S hS (D.map e)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsClosedImmersion B S hS (π.app i)) ∧
      π ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f ∧
      Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk X π))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isLimit_isProper_isFinitePresentation_arrow_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces over `Spec ℤ`, with `Y`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then `f` is the limit of a directed system of proper morphisms
of finite presentation `X_i ⟶ Y_i` between algebraic spaces of finite presentation over `Spec ℤ`,
the systems `X_i` and `Y_i` having affine transition morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_isProper_isFinitePresentation_arrow_of_isProper
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : ((BigFppfOver B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B _ hZ X) (hY :
      IsAlgebraicSpace B _ hZ Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsProper B _ hZ f) (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B _ hZ Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B _ hZ hZ Y) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·))
      (DX DY : DescentSituation B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ hZ I) (φ : DX.system ⟶ DY.system)
      (eX : DX.limitCone.pt ≅ X) (eY : DY.limitCone.pt ≅ Y),
      (∀ i : I, DX.limitCone.π.app (op i) ≫ φ.app (op i) =
        eX.hom ≫ f ≫ eY.inv ≫ DY.limitCone.π.app (op i)) ∧
      (∀ i : I, IsProper B _ hZ (φ.app (op i)) ∧ IsFinitePresentation B _ hZ (φ.app (op i))) ∧
      (∀ i : I, IsFinitePresentation B _ hZ (terminal.from (DY.system.obj (op i))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsGeometricallyConnected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A0Z.** A presheaf on the big fppf site over a field `k` — in particular an
algebraic space over `k` — is *geometrically connected* when for every field extension `K/k`
whose spectrum lies in the chosen big fppf site the base change `X_K` has a connected space
of points.
declarations.statement:
def IsGeometricallyConnected (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyConnected_iff_relocalizeRestrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A10.** A presheaf on the big fppf site over a field `k` — in particular an
algebraic space over `k` — is geometrically connected over `k` if and only if its base change
to a field extension `k'` of `k` is geometrically connected over `k'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyConnected_iff_relocalizeRestrict (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (k k' : Type u) [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k']
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hk' : B.Contains (Spec (.of k')))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsGeometricallyConnected B k hk X ↔
      IsGeometricallyConnected B k' hk'
        ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (fieldExtensionMap B k k' hk hk')).obj X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_connectedComponents_pullback_of_isGeometricallyConnected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A11.** Let `k` be a field, let `X` and `Y` be algebraic spaces over `k` and
assume `X` is geometrically connected over `k`. The projection `X ×_k Y ⟶ Y` induces a
bijection between the sets of connected components of the two point spaces.

The projection is open on points because `X ⟶ Spec k` is universally open (Stacks 06DN), and
its fibre over the point represented by a field-valued point `Spec K ⟶ Y` is the image of
`|X_K ×_k Spec K|`; that fibre product is the base change `X_K` of `X` to `K` viewed again over
`k`, whose point space is homeomorphic to `|X_K|` and so is connected. Stacks 0378 then gives
the bijection.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_connectedComponents_pullback_of_isGeometricallyConnected
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk Y)
    (hXconn : IsGeometricallyConnected B k hk X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hk))))
    (g : Y ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hk)))) :
    Function.Bijective
      (continuous_pointsMap B (Spec (.of k)) hk
        (pullback.snd f g)).connectedComponentsMap

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.bijective_connectedComponents_relocalizeRestrict_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A12, the bijection on connected components.** Let `k` be a separably closed
field, let `K/k` be a field extension whose spectrum lies in the chosen big fppf site and let
`X` be an algebraic space over `k`. The map `|X_K| → |X|` induced by the base change is a
bijection between the sets of connected components.

Viewed again over `k`, the base change `X_K` is the product `Spec K ×_k X`
(`CategoryTheory.OverShriek.isPullback_relocalizeRestrictCounit`), and `Spec K` is
geometrically connected over `k`, so Stacks 0A11 applies to the projection to `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_connectedComponents_relocalizeRestrict_of_isSepClosed [IsSepClosed k]
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    Function.Bijective
      (continuous_pointsOfRelocalizeRestrict B (Spec (.of K)) (Spec (.of k)) hK hk
        (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK) X
        (isAlgebraicSpace_relocalizeRestrict B (Spec (.of K)) (Spec (.of k)) hK hk
          (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK) X hX)).connectedComponentsMap
declarations.comment: bijection on connected components

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A12, geometric connectedness.** Over a separably closed field an algebraic space
is geometrically connected exactly when its space of points is connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_of_isSepClosed [IsSepClosed k]
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsGeometricallyConnected B k hk X ↔ ConnectedSpace (points B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
declarations.comment: geometric connectedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_sepClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A13.** Let `k` be a field, let `K` be a separable algebraic closure of `k` whose
spectrum lies in the chosen big fppf site and let `X` be an algebraic space over `k`. Then `X`
is geometrically connected over `k` if and only if the base change `X_K` has a connected space
of points.

Geometric connectedness over `k` is geometric connectedness of `X_K` over `K` by Stacks 0A10,
and over the separably closed field `K` that is connectedness by Stacks 0A12.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_sepClosure (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsSepClosure k K]
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsGeometricallyConnected B k hk X ↔
      ConnectedSpace (points B (Spec (.of K)) hK
        ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK)).obj X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.galoisActionOnBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A14, the action.** The canonical action of the opposite group of `k`-algebra
automorphisms of `K` on the base change `X_K`, viewed again as a presheaf over `k`. For a
Galois extension `K/k` this is the Galois action on `X_{\overline{k}}`.

The action is over `k`, not over `K`: an automorphism changes only the `K`-coordinate of a
section.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def galoisActionOnBaseChange :
    Action ((BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (MulOpposite (K ≃ₐ[k] K))
declarations.comment: the action

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.galoisActionOnBaseChange_ρ_app_fst
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A14, the action on the `K`-coordinate.** An automorphism `σ` acts on a section
of `X_K` over a `k`-scheme by composing its morphism to `Spec K` with the automorphism of
`Spec K` induced by `σ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem galoisActionOnBaseChange_ρ_app_fst (σ : MulOpposite (K ≃ₐ[k] K))
    (W : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ)
    (x : ((OverShriek.relocalizePresheafFunctor (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK)).obj
      ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK)).obj X)).obj W) :
    (((galoisActionOnBaseChange B k K hk hK X).ρ σ).asHom.app W x).val.1 =
      x.val.1 ≫ siteMapAlgAut B k K hK σ.unop
declarations.comment: the action on the K-coordinate of a section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.galoisActionOnBaseChange_ρ_app_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A14, the action on the section.** An automorphism leaves the section of `X`
itself untouched. The equality is heterogeneous because the type of the section is indexed by
the morphism to `Spec K`, which the action does change.
declarations.statement:
theorem galoisActionOnBaseChange_ρ_app_snd (σ : MulOpposite (K ≃ₐ[k] K))
    (W : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ)
    (x : ((OverShriek.relocalizePresheafFunctor (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK)).obj
      ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK)).obj X)).obj W) :
    HEq (((galoisActionOnBaseChange B k K hk hK X).ρ σ).asHom.app W x).val.2 x.val.2
declarations.comment: the action on the section

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finite_subextension_descending_isQuasiCompact_open
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over a field `k` and let `K/k` be an algebraic field extension. A
quasi-compact open subspace of the base change of `X` to `K` is the base change of a quasi-compact
open subspace of the base change of `X` to a finite subextension of `K/k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_subextension_descending_isQuasiCompact_open (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k K]
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (V : Subfunctor ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK)).obj X))
    (hV : IsOpenSubspace B (Spec (.of K)) hK V)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B (Spec (.of K)) hK V.toFunctor) :
    ∃ (E : IntermediateField k K) (_ : FiniteDimensional k E)
      (hE : B.Contains (Spec (.of E)))
      (V' : Subfunctor
        ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (fieldExtensionMap B k E hk hE)).obj X)),
      IsOpenSubspace B (Spec (.of E)) hE V' ∧
        IsQuasiCompactSpace B (Spec (.of E)) hE V'.toFunctor ∧
        Subfunctor.preimage V
            (eqToHom (relocalizeRestrict_fieldExtensionMap_comp B k E K hk hE hK X)) =
          OverShriek.relocalizeRestrictSubfunctor (fieldExtensionMap B E K hE hK) V'
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_open_subgroup_fixing_isQuasiCompact_open
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over a field `k` and let `K/k` be a Galois extension. A
quasi-compact open subspace of the base change of `X` to `K` is fixed by an open subgroup of
`Gal(K/k)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_open_subgroup_fixing_isQuasiCompact_open [IsGalois k K]
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (V : Subfunctor ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK)).obj X))
    (hV : IsOpenSubspace B (Spec (.of K)) hK V)
    (hVqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B (Spec (.of K)) hK V.toFunctor) :
    ∃ H : Subgroup Gal(K/k), IsOpen (H : Set Gal(K/k)) ∧
      ∀ σ : Gal(K/k), σ ∈ H →
        Subfunctor.preimage (galoisOpenSubfunctor B k K hk hK X V)
            ((galoisActionOnBaseChange B k K hk hK X).ρ (MulOpposite.op σ)).asHom =
          galoisOpenSubfunctor B k K hk hK X V
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_closed_subset_with_preimage_eq_of_galois_invariant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A16.** Let `K/k` be a Galois extension whose spectra lie in the chosen big fppf
site, and let `X` be an algebraic space over `k`. A closed subset of the points of the base
change `X_K` which is invariant under the action of every `k`-algebra automorphism of `K` is the
inverse image of a closed subset of the points of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_closed_subset_with_preimage_eq_of_galois_invariant (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsGalois k K]
    (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k))) (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X)
    (Tbar : Set (points B (Spec (.of K)) hK
      ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK)).obj X)))
    (hTbar : @IsClosed _ (pointTopology B (Spec (.of K)) hK _) Tbar)
    (hstable : ∀ σ : K ≃ₐ[k] K, galoisPointsAction B k K hk hK X σ ⁻¹' Tbar = Tbar) :
    ∃ T : Set (points B (Spec (.of k)) hk X),
      @IsClosed _ (pointTopology B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) T ∧
      pointsOfRelocalizeRestrict B (Spec (.of K)) (Spec (.of k)) hK hk
          (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK) X ⁻¹' T = Tbar

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isGeometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_finite_separable
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` be an algebraic space over `k`. Then `X` is
geometrically connected over `k` if and only if the base change `X_{k'}` has a connected space of
points for every finite separable field extension `k'/k` whose spectrum lies in the chosen big
fppf site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGeometricallyConnected_iff_connectedSpace_finite_separable (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hk : B.Contains (Spec (.of k)))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of k)) hk)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of k)) hk X) :
    IsGeometricallyConnected B k hk X ↔
      ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [FiniteDimensional k K]
        [Algebra.IsSeparable k K] (hK : B.Contains (Spec (.of K))),
        ConnectedSpace (points B (Spec (.of K)) hK
          ((OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict (fieldExtensionMap B k K hk hK)).obj X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_toNormalizationIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A19, clause (1): `f'` is universally closed.**  By Stacks 04NX part (1), since the
composite `f = f' ≫ π` is universally closed and `π` is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_toNormalizationIn
    (hfuc : UniversallyClosed B S hS f.hom) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS (toNormalizationIn B S hS E C f hqc hqc' hid).left.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): the morphism to the normalization is universally closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompact_toNormalizationIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A19, clause (1): `f'` is quasi-compact.**  By Stacks 03KS, since the composite
`f = f' ≫ π` is quasi-compact — a universally closed morphism is quasi-compact by
Stacks 04XW — and `π` is quasi-separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_toNormalizationIn
    (hfuc : UniversallyClosed B S hS f.hom) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS (toNormalizationIn B S hS E C f hqc hqc' hid).left.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): the morphism to the normalization is quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiSeparated_toNormalizationIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A19, clause (1): `f'` is quasi-separated.**  By Stacks 03KR, since the composite
`f = f' ≫ π` is quasi-separated.  Nothing is required of `π`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparated_toNormalizationIn
    (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom) :
    IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (toNormalizationIn B S hS E C f hqc hqc' hid).left.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): the morphism to the normalization is quasi-separated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_toNormalizationIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A19, clause (1): `f'` is surjective.**  The scheme-theoretic image of `f'` inside
the normalization `Y'` of `Y` in `X` is a closed subspace, hence integral over `Y`, through
which `f` factors; the characterization of Stacks 0823 therefore retracts `Y'` onto it, and
`f'` has closed image because it is universally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_toNormalizationIn
    (P : RelativeSpecUniversalProperty B S hS E C) (D : IntegralAlgebraDictionary B S hS E)
    (hloc : (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsIntegralLocalOnAffineCharts)
    (hfuc : UniversallyClosed B S hS f.hom) :
    IsSurjective B S hS (toNormalizationIn B S hS E C f hqc hqc' hid).left.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): the morphism to the normalization is surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIntegralHom_normalizationIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A19, clause (2): `π` is integral.**  This is clause (1) of Stacks 0823 for the
same factorization, proved as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_toNormalizationIn`, and it carries that
theorem's inputs: the universal property `P` of the relative spectrum, the dictionary `D` of
Stacks 03ZP between integral morphisms affine over `Y` and integral algebras, and the clause
`hloc` of Stacks 0820 that a locally integral section over an affine chart is integral.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegralHom_normalizationIn
    (P : RelativeSpecUniversalProperty B S hS E C) (D : IntegralAlgebraDictionary B S hS E)
    (hloc : (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsIntegralLocalOnAffineCharts) :
    IsIntegralHom B S hS (normalizationIn B S hS E f hqc').obj.hom.hom
declarations.comment: part (2): the normalization morphism is integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_steinFactorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A19, clause (5): `Y'` is the normalization of `Y` in `X`.**  The factorization
`f = f' ≫ π` has the two properties of Stacks 0823 which characterize the normalization:
`π` is integral, and every factorization of `f` through an integral morphism of algebraic
spaces to `Y` receives a unique compatible morphism from `Y'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeNormalization_steinFactorization
    (P : RelativeSpecUniversalProperty B S hS E C) (D : IntegralAlgebraDictionary B S hS E)
    (hloc : (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)).IsIntegralLocalOnAffineCharts) :
    IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f.hom
      (normalizationIn B S hS E f hqc').obj.hom.hom
      (toNormalizationIn B S hS E C f hqc hqc' hid).left.hom
declarations.comment: part (5): the intermediate space is the normalization of Y in X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.steinFactorization_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A19 (Stein factorization).**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a universally closed and
quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`.  It is quasi-compact (Stacks 04XW); let
`Y'` be the normalization of `Y` in `X` (Stacks 0822), with `π : Y' ⟶ Y` and the canonical
`f' : X ⟶ Y'`.  Then `f = π ∘ f'`, and

1. `f'` is universally closed, quasi-compact, quasi-separated and surjective;
2. `π` is integral;
3. `f'_* 𝒪_X = 𝒪_{Y'}`: the structure map `𝒪_{Y'} ⟶ f'_* 𝒪_X` is an isomorphism;
4. `Y' = \underline{Spec}_Y(f_* 𝒪_X)`: `π` is affine and the map `π_* 𝒪_{Y'} ⟶ f_* 𝒪_X` of
   `𝒪_Y`-algebras induced by `f'` is an isomorphism;
5. `Y'` is the normalization of `Y` in `X`, here in the characterizing form of Stacks 0823 (it is
   that normalization by construction).

Moreover formation of the factorization commutes with flat base change: for a flat `g : Y₁ ⟶ Y`,
a fibre product `X₁ = Y₁ ×_Y X` with `f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁`, a fibre product `P = Y₁ ×_Y Y'` with
`p : P ⟶ Y₁`, and the base change `h : X₁ ⟶ P` of `f'`, the morphism `f₁` is again universally
closed and quasi-separated (so quasi-compact), the factorization `X₁ ⟶ P ⟶ Y₁` is the normalization
of `Y₁` in `X₁` in the sense of Stacks 0823, and it is identified with the factorization of `f₁`
through its own normalization by a unique isomorphism compatible with both factorizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem steinFactorization_of_universallyClosed (huc : UniversallyClosed B S hS f.hom)
    (hfqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom) :
    let hfqc := isQuasiCompact_of_universallyClosed B S hS X.2 Y.2 f.hom huc
    toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs ≫ normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs = f ∧
      (UniversallyClosed B S hS (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom ∧
        IsQuasiCompact B S hS (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom ∧
        IsQuasiSeparated B S hS (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom ∧
        IsSurjective B S hS (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom) ∧
      IsIntegralHom B S hS (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs).hom ∧
      IsIso (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs)).fSharp ∧
      (IsAffineHom B S hS (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs).hom ∧
        IsIso (pushforwardAlgebraMap B S hS (toNormalizationInQcqsOver f hfqc hfqs))) ∧
      IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f.hom (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs).hom
        (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom ∧
      ∀ {X₁ Y₁ P : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} {g : Y₁ ⟶ Y} {f₁ : X₁ ⟶ Y₁} {g' : X₁ ⟶ X},
        IsPullback g' f₁ f g → IsFlat B S hS g.hom →
        ∀ {q : P ⟶ normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs} {p : P ⟶ Y₁},
          IsPullback q p (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs) g →
          ∀ h : X₁ ⟶ P, h ≫ q = g' ≫ toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs → h ≫ p = f₁ →
            UniversallyClosed B S hS f₁.hom ∧
              ∃ (hf₁qc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f₁.hom) (hf₁qs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f₁.hom),
                IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f₁.hom p.hom h.hom ∧
                  ∃! e : normalizationInQcqs B S hS f₁ hf₁qc hf₁qs ≅ P,
                    toNormalizationInQcqs f₁ hf₁qc hf₁qs ≫ e.hom = h ∧
                      e.hom ≫ p = normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f₁ hf₁qc hf₁qs
declarations.comment: all five clauses and the compatibility with flat base change, for the factorization through the normalization of Stacks 0822

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_toNormalizationInQcqs
declarations.doc:
**`f'` is surjective**, which is the remaining assertion of clause (1) of Stacks 0A19.  The
factorization `f = f' ≫ π` has the characterizing property of Stacks 0823
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_normalizationInQcqs`), and `f'` is
quasi-compact and universally closed, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSurjective_of_isRelativeNormalization` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSurjective_toNormalizationInQcqs (hfuc : UniversallyClosed B S hS f.hom) :
    IsSurjective B S hS (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom
declarations.comment: clause (1): the morphism f' : X ⟶ Y' to the normalization of Y in X is surjective, for a universally closed f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.connectedSpace_geometricFiber_iff_forall_scheme_etaleNeighborhood
declarations.doc:
