declarations.name: isFiltered_prod
declarations.doc: The product of two filtered categories is filtered.
declarations.statement: theorem isFiltered_prod [IsFiltered I] [IsFiltered J] : IsFiltered (I × J)

declarations.name: isEssentiallyConstantInd_iff_comp_prod_snd
declarations.doc:
For filtered `I` and any `M : J ⥤ C`, essential constancy of `M` is equivalent to essential
constancy of `M` precomposed with `Prod.snd I J`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantInd_iff_comp_prod_snd [IsFiltered I] (M : J ⥤ C) :
    IsEssentiallyConstantInd M ↔ IsEssentiallyConstantInd (CategoryTheory.Prod.snd I J ⋙ M)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantInd.isEssentiallyConstantInd_iff_exists_subcategory
declarations.doc:
Stacks 0A2E (1). Let `M : I ⥤ A` be a diagram over a filtered category in a preadditive
Karoubian category. Then `M` is essentially constant if and only if `colim M` exists and there are
a cofinal filtered subcategory `I'` of `I` (a filtered category `I'` with a faithful final functor
`H : I' ⥤ I` injective on objects, i.e. an isomorphism onto a subcategory) and, for each `i' : I'`,
a direct sum decomposition `M (H i') ≅ X_{i'} ⊕ Z_{i'}` such that `X_{i'}` maps isomorphically to
`colim M` and `Z_{i'}` maps to zero in `M (H i'')` for some `i' ⟶ i''` in `I'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantInd_iff_exists_subcategory [IsFiltered I] [IsIdempotentComplete A]
    (M : I ⥤ A) :
    IsEssentiallyConstantInd M ↔
      ∃ (_ : HasColimit M) (I' : Type u') (_ : Category.{v'} I') (_ : IsFiltered I')
        (H : I' ⥤ I) (_ : H.Faithful) (_ : Function.Injective H.obj) (_ : H.Final), ∀ i' : I',
          ∃ (X' Z' : A) (b : BinaryBicone X' Z') (_ : b.IsBilimit) (e : b.pt ≅ M.obj (H.obj i')),
            IsIso (b.inl ≫ e.hom ≫ colimit.ι M (H.obj i')) ∧
            ∃ (i'' : I') (f : i' ⟶ i''), b.inr ≫ e.hom ≫ M.map (H.map f) = 0

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.EssentiallyConstantPro.isEssentiallyConstantPro_iff_exists_subcategory
declarations.doc:
Stacks 0A2E (2). Let `M : I ⥤ A` be a diagram over a cofiltered category in a preadditive
Karoubian category. Then `M` is essentially constant if and only if `lim M` exists and there are
an initial cofiltered subcategory `I'` of `I` (a cofiltered category `I'` with a faithful initial
functor `H : I' ⥤ I` injective on objects, i.e. an isomorphism onto a subcategory) and, for each
`i' : I'`, a direct sum decomposition `M (H i') ≅ X_{i'} ⊕ Z_{i'}` such that `lim M` maps
isomorphically to `X_{i'}` and `M (H i'') ⟶ Z_{i'}` is zero for some `i'' ⟶ i'` in `I'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantPro_iff_exists_subcategory [IsCofiltered I] [IsIdempotentComplete A]
    (M : I ⥤ A) :
    IsEssentiallyConstantPro M ↔
      ∃ (_ : HasLimit M) (I' : Type u') (_ : Category.{v'} I') (_ : IsCofiltered I')
        (H : I' ⥤ I) (_ : H.Faithful) (_ : Function.Injective H.obj) (_ : H.Initial), ∀ i' : I',
          ∃ (X' Z' : A) (b : BinaryBicone X' Z') (_ : b.IsBilimit) (e : b.pt ≅ M.obj (H.obj i')),
            IsIso (limit.π M (H.obj i') ≫ e.inv ≫ b.fst) ∧
            ∃ (i'' : I') (f : i'' ⟶ i'), M.map (H.map f) ≫ e.inv ≫ b.snd = 0

declarations.name: hasColimit_biprod_iff
declarations.doc:
In a Karoubian additive category, the pointwise biproduct functor `F ⊞ G`
has a colimit iff both `F` and `G` do.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasColimit_biprod_iff
    {I C : Type*} [Category I] [Category C]
    [Preadditive C] [HasBinaryBiproducts C] [IsIdempotentComplete C]
    (F G : I ⥤ C) :
    HasColimit (F ⊞ G) ↔ HasColimit F ∧ HasColimit G
declarations.comment: iff

declarations.name: colimitBiprodIso
declarations.doc:
In a Karoubian additive category, if both `F` and `G` have colimits, then
the colimit of the pointwise biproduct is canonically isomorphic to the
biproduct of the colimits.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colimitBiprodIso
    {I C : Type*} [Category I] [Category C]
    [Preadditive C] [HasBinaryBiproducts C] [IsIdempotentComplete C]
    (F G : I ⥤ C) [HasColimit F] [HasColimit G] :
    haveI := hasColimit_biprod_of_hasColimit F G
    colimit (F ⊞ G) ≅ colimit F ⊞ colimit G
declarations.comment: iso

declarations.name: colimitBiprodIso_of_hasColimit_biprod
declarations.doc:
In a Karoubian additive category, if `F ⊞ G` has a colimit, then it is canonically isomorphic
to the biproduct of the colimits of `F` and `G`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colimitBiprodIso_of_hasColimit_biprod
    {I C : Type*} [Category I] [Category C]
    [Preadditive C] [HasBinaryBiproducts C] [IsIdempotentComplete C]
    (F G : I ⥤ C) [HasColimit (F ⊞ G)] :
    haveI := hasColimit_of_hasColimit_biprod_left F G
    haveI := hasColimit_of_hasColimit_biprod_right F G
    colimit (F ⊞ G) ≅ colimit F ⊞ colimit G
declarations.comment: iso_from_biprod

declarations.name: isEssentiallyConstantInd_biprod_iff
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be a filtered category and `C` an additive Karoubian category. For
two functors `F, G : I ⥤ C`, the direct sum `F ⊞ G` is essentially constant
iff both `F` and `G` are essentially constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEssentiallyConstantInd_biprod_iff
    {I : Type u} [Category.{v} I] [IsFiltered I]
    {C : Type u'} [Category.{v'} C] [Preadditive C]
    [HasFiniteBiproducts C] [IsIdempotentComplete C]
    (F G : I ⥤ C) :
    haveI : HasBinaryBiproducts C := hasBinaryBiproducts_of_finite_biproducts C
    IsEssentiallyConstantInd (F ⊞ G) ↔
      IsEssentiallyConstantInd F ∧ IsEssentiallyConstantInd G

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.twoCocycleOfLift
declarations.doc:
**Equation 59.61.5.1.** The two-cocycle attached to a family of lifts with central defect:
the scalar `g̃_σ⁻¹ g̃_{σ τ} σ(g̃_τ⁻¹) ∈ Kˣ`.
declarations.statement:
def twoCocycleOfLift (i : n) (lift : G → GL n K)
    (hc : ∀ σ τ, liftDefect lift σ τ ∈ Subgroup.center (GL n K)) : G × G → Kˣ
declarations.comment: the two-cocycle

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.scalar_twoCocycleOfLift
declarations.doc:
**Equation 59.61.5.1**, as displayed: the scalar matrix of the two-cocycle at `(σ, τ)` is
`g̃_σ⁻¹ g̃_{σ τ} σ(g̃_τ⁻¹)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem scalar_twoCocycleOfLift (i : n) (lift : G → GL n K)
    (hc : ∀ σ τ, liftDefect lift σ τ ∈ Subgroup.center (GL n K)) (σ τ : G) :
    Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.scalar n (twoCocycleOfLift i lift hc (σ, τ)) =
      (lift σ)⁻¹ * lift (σ * τ) *
        Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G K σ) (lift τ)⁻¹
declarations.comment: the displayed formula

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.twoCocycleOfLift_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A2I.** The scalar defect of a lift of a projective crossed
homomorphism satisfies the multiplicative two-cocycle identity
`c(σ τ, υ) c(σ, τ) = σ(c(τ, υ)) c(σ, τ υ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem twoCocycleOfLift_mul (i : n) (lift : G → GL n K)
    (hc : ∀ σ τ, liftDefect lift σ τ ∈ Subgroup.center (GL n K)) (σ τ υ : G) :
    twoCocycleOfLift i lift hc (σ * τ, υ) * twoCocycleOfLift i lift hc (σ, τ) =
      Units.map (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom G K σ : K →* K)
          (twoCocycleOfLift i lift hc (τ, υ)) *
        twoCocycleOfLift i lift hc (σ, τ * υ)
declarations.comment: the two-cocycle identity

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.twoCocycleOfPGLCocycle
declarations.doc:
**Equation 59.61.5.1** for the absolute Galois group: the scalar two-cocycle
`(σ, τ) ↦ g̃_σ⁻¹ g̃_{σ τ} σ(g̃_τ⁻¹)` attached to a lift of the projective cocycle classifying a
central simple algebra of degree `d`.
declarations.statement:
def twoCocycleOfPGLCocycle (hd : 0 < d) (g : PGLCocycle K Ksep d)
    (lift : (Ksep ≃ₐ[K] Ksep) → GL (Fin d) Ksep)
    (hlift : ∀ σ, Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup.mk (lift σ) = g.toFun σ) :
    (Ksep ≃ₐ[K] Ksep) × (Ksep ≃ₐ[K] Ksep) → Ksepˣ
declarations.comment: the Galois two-cocycle

declarations.name: Stacks.GaloisCohomology.isMulCocycle₂_twoCocycleOfPGLCocycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A2I.** The scalar defect of a lift of the projective cocycle of a
central simple algebra is a two-cocycle of the absolute Galois group with values in `(Kˢᵉᵖ)ˣ`,
for the action of `Gal(Kˢᵉᵖ/K)` on units used by the crossed product construction.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMulCocycle₂_twoCocycleOfPGLCocycle (hd : 0 < d) (g : PGLCocycle K Ksep d)
    (lift : (Ksep ≃ₐ[K] Ksep) → GL (Fin d) Ksep)
    (hlift : ∀ σ, Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup.mk (lift σ) = g.toFun σ) :
    IsMulCocycle₂ (twoCocycleOfPGLCocycle hd g lift hlift)
declarations.comment: the Galois two-cocycle identity

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BrauerScheme.IsSimilar
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of Tag 0A2J.** Two sheaves of `𝒪_S`-algebras `A` and `B` are similar if
there are finite locally free sheaves of `𝒪_S`-modules `F` and `G` of positive rank at every
point of `S` with `A ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝓗om(F,F) ≅ B ⊗_{𝒪_S} 𝓗om(G,G)` as `𝒪_S`-algebras. The Brauer
group of `S` is the set of equivalence classes of *Azumaya* `𝒪_S`-algebras for this relation,
with the operation induced by the tensor product.
declarations.statement: def IsSimilar (A B : AlgebraSheaf S) : Prop
declarations.comment: the equivalence of Azumaya algebras

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BrauerScheme.IsAzumaya
declarations.doc:
**The Azumaya condition of Tag 0A2J.** A sheaf of `𝒪_S`-algebras is Azumaya if it is étale
locally a matrix algebra: there is an étale covering `{φ_i : U_i → S}` of `S` and integers
`d_i ≥ 1` with `φ_i^* A ≅ Mat_{d_i}(𝒪_{U_i})` as `𝒪_{U_i}`-algebras. An
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Cover` at `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etalePrecoverage` packages both
halves of "étale covering": every `𝒰.f i` is étale, and the family is jointly surjective.

The pullback `φ_i^*` of the sheaf of algebras is `algebraPullback`, which transports the
multiplication along the tensor comparison of Tag 01CD — the map
`φ^*(A ⊗ B) ⟶ φ^*A ⊗ φ^*B` of `Stacks.RingedSpace.comparison`, see `monoidalModulePullback`.
declarations.statement: def IsAzumaya {S : Scheme.{u}} (A : AlgebraSheaf S) : Prop
declarations.comment: the Azumaya condition

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BrauerScheme.BrauerGroup
declarations.doc:
**The Brauer group of a scheme**, Tag 0A2J: the set of equivalence classes of Azumaya
`𝒪_S`-algebras for the equivalence of `IsSimilar`. The operation induced by the tensor product
is `BrauerGroup.mul`.
declarations.statement: def BrauerGroup (S : Scheme.{u}) : Type (u + 1)
declarations.comment: the Brauer group

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BrauerScheme.BrauerGroup.mul
declarations.doc:
**The operation of the Brauer group of Tag 0A2J**: the one induced by the tensor product of
sheaves of algebras. It is well defined because a tensor product of Azumaya algebra sheaves is
Azumaya (`IsAzumaya.tensor`) and because similarity is compatible with the tensor product
(`IsSimilar.tensor`).
declarations.statement: def BrauerGroup.mul {S : Scheme.{u}} : BrauerGroup S → BrauerGroup S → BrauerGroup S
declarations.comment: the operation of the Brauer group

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_invertible_tensor_iso_of_endomorphism_algebra_iso
declarations.doc:
An isomorphism of the endomorphism algebra sheaves of two positive-rank vector
bundles is conjugation by an isomorphism after an invertible twist.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_invertible_tensor_iso_of_endomorphism_algebra_iso
    (S : Scheme.{u})
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S.sheaf))
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (C := Opens S)
      (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology S) F]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (C := Opens S)
      (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology S) G]
    (hF : ∃ q : SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData F,
      q.IsLocallyFreeData ∧ ∀ i, Nonempty (q.generators i).I)
    (hG : ∃ q : SheafOfModules.LocalGeneratorsData G,
      q.IsLocallyFreeData ∧ ∀ i, Nonempty (q.generators i).I)
    (HFF : SheafHom S.sheaf F F) (HGG : SheafHom S.sheaf G G)
    (α : HFF.obj ≅ HGG.obj)
    (hα_one : ∀ U : Opens S, HGG.sectionsEquiv U
      (α.hom.val.app (op U) ((HFF.sectionsEquiv U).symm (𝟙 (F.over U)))) =
        𝟙 (G.over U))
    (hα_comp : ∀ (U : Opens S) (f g : F.over U ⟶ F.over U),
      HGG.sectionsEquiv U
        (α.hom.val.app (op U) ((HFF.sectionsEquiv U).symm (f ≫ g))) =
      (HGG.sectionsEquiv U
        (α.hom.val.app (op U) ((HFF.sectionsEquiv U).symm f))) ≫
      (HGG.sectionsEquiv U
        (α.hom.val.app (op U) ((HFF.sectionsEquiv U).symm g)))) :
    ∃ L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S.sheaf),
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible S.sheaf.obj (structureSheaf S.sheaf).property L ∧
      ∃ e : (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨((S.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)).presheaf,
            ((S.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F)).obj (L)) ≅ G,
        ∀ (U : Opens S) (s : HFF.obj.val.obj (op U))
          (f : F.val.obj (op U)) (l : L.val.obj (op U)),
          ((HGG.sectionsEquiv U (α.hom.val.app (op U) s)).val.app
            (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).hom
              ((e.hom.val.app (op U)).hom
                (toTensorSheafSection S.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace F L (op U)
                  (f ⊗ₜ[(O S.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace).obj (op U)] l))) =
            (e.hom.val.app (op U)).hom
              (toTensorSheafSection S.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace F L (op U)
                ((((HFF.sectionsEquiv U s).val.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).hom f) ⊗ₜ[
                  (O S.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace).obj (op U)] l))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BrauerScheme.brauerClass_pow_eq_one_of_rank
declarations.doc:
**The class in `Br(S)` of an Azumaya `𝒪_S`-algebra whose underlying sheaf of modules is
finite locally free of rank `d ^ 2` is annihilated by `d`.**

This is [Stacks, Tag 0A2L]. The case `d = 0` is `pow_zero`; for `d ≥ 1` the reduction
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BrauerScheme.brauerClass_pow_eq_one_of_isTrivialClass_natTensorPow`
leaves exactly Saltman's construction,
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.BrauerScheme.isTrivialClass_natTensorPow_of_rank`.
declarations.statement:
theorem brauerClass_pow_eq_one_of_rank (A : Azumaya S) {d : ℕ}
    (hrank : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (C := Opens S)
      (J := Opens.grothendieckTopology S) A.1.X (d ^ 2)) :
    brauerClass A ^ d = 1

declarations.name: Soberification.exists_universal_quasiSober
declarations.doc:
For any topological space `X`, there is a canonical continuous map `c : X → X'` from `X`
to a sober topological space `X'` which is universal among continuous maps from `X` to sober
topological spaces. Moreover, the assignment `U' ↦ c⁻¹(U')` is a bijection between opens of `X'`
and `X` which commutes with finite intersections and arbitrary unions. The image `c(X)` is a
Kolmogorov (`T0`) topological space and the map `c : X → c(X)` is universal for maps of `X` into
Kolmogorov spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_universal_quasiSober :
    -- Sober target with continuous canonical map and universal property
    ∃ (X' : Type u) (_ : TopologicalSpace X') (_ : QuasiSober X') (_ : T0Space X')
      (c' : X → X') (_ : Continuous c'),
        (-- Universal property among sober spaces
         (∀ (Y : Type u) [TopologicalSpace Y] [QuasiSober Y] [T0Space Y]
            (f : X → Y), Continuous f →
              ∃ f' : X' → Y, Continuous f' ∧ f' ∘ c' = f ∧
                ∀ g : X' → Y, Continuous g → g ∘ c' = f → g = f') ∧
         -- Bijection between opens, commuting with finite intersections and arbitrary unions
         (∃ φ : TopologicalSpace.Opens X' ≃ TopologicalSpace.Opens X,
            (∀ V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X', (φ V : Set X) = c' ⁻¹' (V : Set X')) ∧
            (φ ⊤ = ⊤) ∧
            (∀ V W : TopologicalSpace.Opens X', φ (V ⊓ W) = φ V ⊓ φ W) ∧
            (∀ {ι : Sort*} (V : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X'),
                φ (⨆ i, V i) = ⨆ i, φ (V i))) ∧
         -- c(X) is T0 (Kolmogorov)
         T0Space (Set.range c') ∧
         -- Universal property for c : X → c(X) into Kolmogorov spaces
         (∀ (Y : Type u) [TopologicalSpace Y] [T0Space Y] (f : X → Y),
            Continuous f →
              ∃ f' : Set.range c' → Y, Continuous f' ∧
                (∀ x : X, f' ⟨c' x, ⟨x, rfl⟩⟩ = f x) ∧
                ∀ g : Set.range c' → Y, Continuous g →
                  (∀ x : X, g ⟨c' x, ⟨x, rfl⟩⟩ = f x) → g = f'))

declarations.name: TopCat.exists_eq_iUnion_preimage_of_isOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2P** (part 1). Let `C` be a limit cone over a cofiltered diagram `F : J ⥤ TopCat`.
Every open subset `W` of `C.pt` is `⋃ j, C.π.app j ⁻¹' U j` for open subsets `U j ⊆ F.obj j`.

The tag takes the union over a subset of the index category. The whole index category always
works, since `U j` may be empty.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eq_iUnion_preimage_of_isOpen (hC : IsLimit C) {W : Set C.pt} (hW : IsOpen W) :
    ∃ U : ∀ j, Set (F.obj j), (∀ j, IsOpen (U j)) ∧ W = ⋃ j, C.π.app j ⁻¹' U j

declarations.name: TopCat.exists_isOpen_subset_preimage_subset_of_isCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2P** (part 2), general form. Let `C` be a limit cone over a cofiltered diagram
`F : J ⥤ TopCat`. If `K` is a quasi-compact subset of an open subset `W` of `C.pt`, then
`K ⊆ C.π.app i ⁻¹' U ⊆ W` for an index `i` and an open subset `U ⊆ F.obj i`.

The tag's statement, `TopCat.exists_isOpen_eq_preimage_of_isCompact_of_isOpen`, is the case
`K = W`.

declarations.name: TopCat.exists_isOpen_eq_preimage_of_isCompact_of_isOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2P** (part 2). Let `C` be a limit cone over a cofiltered diagram `F : J ⥤ TopCat`.
Every quasi-compact open subset `W` of `C.pt` is `C.π.app i ⁻¹' U` for an index `i` and an open
subset `U ⊆ F.obj i`.

This is the case `K = W` of `TopCat.exists_isOpen_subset_preimage_subset_of_isCompact`.

declarations.name: TopCat.isLimit_of_basis_of_preimages
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2Q.** Let `J` be a cofiltered category, let `F : J ⥤ TopCat` be a diagram of
topological spaces, and let `c` be a cone on `F`. Assume:
1. the underlying type-level cone `(forget).mapCone c` is a limit cone, so `c.pt` is the
   set-theoretic limit with projections `c.π.app j`, and
2. the family of preimages `c.π.app j ⁻¹' V`, for `j : J` and `V` open in `F.obj j`, is a
   topological basis for `c.pt`.

Then `c` is a limit cone in `TopCat`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimit_of_basis_of_preimages
    {J : Type v} [Category.{w} J] [IsCofiltered J]
    {F : J ⥤ TopCat.{u}} (c : Cone F)
    (hForget : IsLimit ((CategoryTheory.forget TopCat.{u}).mapCone c))
    (hBasis : IsTopologicalBasis
      {U : Set c.pt | ∃ (j : J) (V : Set (F.obj j)), IsOpen V ∧ U = c.π.app j ⁻¹' V}) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit c)

declarations.name: spectralMap_continuous_withConstructibleTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2S** (continuity in the constructible topology).
A spectral map `f : X → Y` is continuous for the constructible topologies on `X` and `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralMap_continuous_withConstructibleTopology
    (f : X → Y) (hf : IsSpectralMap f) :
    Continuous
      (fun x : WithConstructibleTopologyTypeSynonym X =>
        WithConstructibleTopologyTypeSynonym.of (f (WithConstructibleTopologyTypeSynonym.out
            x)))
declarations.comment: continuity in the constructible topology

declarations.name: spectralMap_fibre_isCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2S** (quasi-compact fibres).
The fibres of a spectral map between spectral spaces are quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralMap_fibre_isCompact
    (f : X → Y) (hf : IsSpectralMap f) (y : Y) :
    IsCompact (f ⁻¹' {y})
declarations.comment: quasi-compact fibres

declarations.name: spectralMap_range_isClosed_withConstructibleTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2S** (closed image in the constructible topology).
The image of a spectral map between spectral spaces is closed in the constructible topology on the
target.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralMap_range_isClosed_withConstructibleTopology
    (f : X → Y) (hf : IsSpectralMap f) :
    IsClosed (Set.range (fun x => WithConstructibleTopologyTypeSynonym.of (f x)))
declarations.comment: closed image in the constructible topology

declarations.name: UniversalSoberMap.compactSpace
declarations.doc:
**Statement (1).** If `X` is quasi-compact, then so is `X'`.
This is the first part of Stacks Project Lemma 5.23.15 (tag `0A2T`).
declarations.statement:
theorem UniversalSoberMap.compactSpace
    {X X' : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace X']
    (c : UniversalSoberMap X X') [CompactSpace X] :
    CompactSpace X'
declarations.comment: part (1): quasi-compactness

declarations.name: UniversalSoberMap.spectralSpace
declarations.doc:
**Statement (2).** If `X` is quasi-compact, has a basis of quasi-compact opens, and the
intersection of any two quasi-compact opens of `X` is quasi-compact, then `X'` is a spectral
topological space. This is the second part of Stacks Project Lemma 5.23.15 (tag `0A2T`).
declarations.statement:
theorem UniversalSoberMap.spectralSpace
    {X X' : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace X']
    (c : UniversalSoberMap X X')
    [CompactSpace X] [PrespectralSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] :
    SpectralSpace X'
declarations.comment: part (2): spectral

declarations.name: UniversalSoberMap.noetherianSpectralSpace
declarations.doc:
**Statement (3).** If `X` is Noetherian, then `X'` is a Noetherian spectral space.
This is the third part of Stacks Project Lemma 5.23.15 (tag `0A2T`).
declarations.statement:
theorem UniversalSoberMap.noetherianSpectralSpace
    {X X' : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace X']
    (c : UniversalSoberMap X X') [NoetherianSpace X] :
    NoetherianSpace X' ∧ SpectralSpace X'
declarations.comment: part (3): Noetherian spectral

declarations.name: SpectralLimits.isCompact_limitSubset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2V (1).** For a diagram of spectral spaces along spectral maps and subsets
`Z j ⊆ F.obj j` closed in the constructible topology, the subset
`{x ∈ lim F | ∀ j, π j x ∈ Z j}` of the limit is quasi-compact for the limit topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompact_limitSubset
    (hF : ∀ {j i : J} (a : j ⟶ i), IsSpectralMap (F.map a).hom) (Z : ∀ j, Set (F.obj j))
    (hZ_closed : ∀ j, @IsClosed _ (constructibleTopology (F.obj j)) (Z j)) :
    IsCompact (limitSubset F Z)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: SpectralLimits.compactSpace_limit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2V (2).** The limit of a diagram of spectral spaces along spectral maps is
quasi-compact. This is part (1) with `Z j = univ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSpace_limit (hF : ∀ {j i : J} (a : j ⟶ i), IsSpectralMap (F.map a).hom) :
    CompactSpace ((limit F : TopCat.{max v u}))
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: SpectralLimits.nonempty_limitSet_inter_of_isClosed_constructible
declarations.doc:
A compatible cofiltered system of nonempty constructibly closed subsets of a spectral diagram
has nonempty limit.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_limitSet_inter_of_isClosed_constructible [IsCofiltered I]
    (Z : ∀ i, Set (F.obj i)) (hZ_ne : ∀ i, (Z i).Nonempty)
    (hZ_cl : ∀ i, @IsClosed (F.obj i) (constructibleTopology (F.obj i)) (Z i))
    (hZ_comp : ∀ ⦃j i : I⦄ (a : j ⟶ i), F.map a '' Z j ⊆ Z i) :
    { x : ∀ i, F.obj i | x ∈ limitSet F ∧ ∀ i, x i ∈ Z i }.Nonempty
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: SpectralLimits.nonempty_limitSet
declarations.doc: The cofiltered limit of a diagram of nonempty spectral spaces is nonempty.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_limitSet [IsCofiltered I] (hX_ne : ∀ i, Nonempty (F.obj i)) :
    (limitSet F).Nonempty
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: SpectralLimits.preimage_limit_π_subset_iff_exists_map_preimage_subset
declarations.doc:
Let `J` be a small cofiltered category and let `F : J ⥤ TopCat` be a diagram of spectral
spaces such that, for every morphism `a : j ⟶ i` in `J`, the underlying map
`F.map a : F.obj j → F.obj i` is a spectral map. Let `X := limit F` with projections
`π_i := limit.π F i : X → F.obj i`. For every object `i : J` and any subsets `E, G ⊂ F.obj i`
where `E` is closed in the constructible topology and `G` is open in the constructible topology,
we have
`π_i ⁻¹' E ⊆ π_i ⁻¹' G ↔ ∃ (j : J) (a : j ⟶ i), (F.map a) ⁻¹' E ⊆ (F.map a) ⁻¹' G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preimage_limit_π_subset_iff_exists_map_preimage_subset
    {J : Type u} [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J]
    (F : J ⥤ TopCat.{u})
    (hF_spec : ∀ j, SpectralSpace (F.obj j))
    (hF_map : ∀ {i j : J} (a : j ⟶ i), IsSpectralMap (F.map a))
    (i : J) (E G : Set (F.obj i))
    (hE : @IsClosed _ (constructibleTopology (F.obj i)) E)
    (hG : @IsOpen _ (constructibleTopology (F.obj i)) G) :
    ((limit.π F i) ⁻¹' E ⊆ (limit.π F i) ⁻¹' G) ↔
      (∃ (j : J) (a : j ⟶ i), (F.map a) ⁻¹' E ⊆ (F.map a) ⁻¹' G)

declarations.name: descend_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
For a cofiltered diagram `D` of spectral spaces with spectral transition maps, every
constructible subset `E` of the inverse limit `D.invLimit` is the preimage under some projection
`D.projFun i` of a constructible subset of `D.F.obj i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem descend_isConstructible
    {E : Set D.invLimit} (hE : IsConstructible E) :
    ∃ (i : J) (E_i : Set (D.F.obj i)), IsConstructible E_i ∧ D.projFun i ⁻¹' E_i = E

declarations.name: descend_isConstructible_isOpen
declarations.doc:
If the constructible subset of the inverse limit is moreover open, the constructible subset it
descends from on the factor can be chosen open.
declarations.statement:
theorem descend_isConstructible_isOpen
    {E : Set D.invLimit} (hE : IsConstructible E) (hEopen : IsOpen E) :
    ∃ (i : J) (E_i : Set (D.F.obj i)),
      IsConstructible E_i ∧ IsOpen E_i ∧ D.projFun i ⁻¹' E_i = E
declarations.comment: open refinement

declarations.name: descend_isConstructible_isClosed
declarations.doc:
If the constructible subset of the inverse limit is moreover closed, the constructible subset
it descends from on the factor can be chosen closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem descend_isConstructible_isClosed
    {E : Set D.invLimit} (hE : IsConstructible E) (hEcl : IsClosed E) :
    ∃ (i : J) (E_i : Set (D.F.obj i)),
      IsConstructible E_i ∧ IsClosed E_i ∧ D.projFun i ⁻¹' E_i = E
declarations.comment: closed refinement

declarations.name: spectralDiagram_invLimit_spectralSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2Z** (inverse limit is spectral).
The inverse limit of a cofiltered diagram of spectral spaces with spectral transition maps is
a spectral topological space.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralDiagram_invLimit_spectralSpace
    {J : Type v} [Category.{v'} J] [IsCofiltered J] (D : SpectralDiagram.{v, u} J) :
    SpectralSpace D.invLimit
declarations.comment: inverse limit is spectral

declarations.name: spectralDiagram_proj_isSpectralMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A2Z** (projections are spectral).
Each projection from the inverse limit of a cofiltered diagram of spectral spaces to a
component of the diagram is a spectral map.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralDiagram_proj_isSpectralMap
    {J : Type v} [Category.{v'} J] [IsCofiltered J] (D : SpectralDiagram.{v, u} J) (j : J) :
    IsSpectralMap (D.projFun j)
declarations.comment: projections are spectral

declarations.name: SpectralLimits.descent_of_quasiCompact_opens
declarations.doc:
For every quasi-compact open `U` of the limit `lim F`, there exist an index `i` and a
quasi-compact open `Ui` of `F.obj i` whose preimage under the projection equals `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem descent_of_quasiCompact_opens
    [∀ i, SpectralSpace (F.obj i)]
    (hF : ∀ ⦃i j : J⦄ (a : i ⟶ j), IsSpectralMap (F.map a))
    (U : Set ((limit F : TopCat))) (hUopen : IsOpen U) (hUcpt : IsCompact U) :
    ∃ (i : J) (Ui : Set (F.obj i)), IsOpen Ui ∧ IsCompact Ui ∧
      (limit.π F i) ⁻¹' Ui = U
declarations.comment: part (1): descent of quasi-compact opens

declarations.name: SpectralLimits.descent_of_inclusions
declarations.doc:
If two quasi-compact opens `Ui ⊆ F.obj i` and `Uj ⊆ F.obj j` have nested preimages in the
limit, the inclusion already holds after pulling back along a span `a : k ⟶ i`, `b : k ⟶ j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem descent_of_inclusions
    [∀ i, SpectralSpace (F.obj i)]
    (hF : ∀ ⦃i j : J⦄ (a : i ⟶ j), IsSpectralMap (F.map a))
    (i j : J) (Ui : Set (F.obj i)) (Uj : Set (F.obj j))
    (hUi_open : IsOpen Ui) (hUi_cpt : IsCompact Ui)
    (hUj_open : IsOpen Uj) (hUj_cpt : IsCompact Uj)
    (h : (limit.π F i) ⁻¹' Ui ⊆ (limit.π F j) ⁻¹' Uj) :
    ∃ (k : J) (a : k ⟶ i) (b : k ⟶ j),
      (F.map a) ⁻¹' Ui ⊆ (F.map b) ⁻¹' Uj
declarations.comment: part (2): descent of inclusions

declarations.name: SpectralLimits.descent_of_finite_unions
declarations.doc:
If, in the limit, the preimage of a quasi-compact open `Ui` equals the union of the preimages
of finitely many quasi-compact opens `U s` (`s : Fin n`), then this equality already holds after
pulling back along some `j ⟶ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem descent_of_finite_unions
    [∀ i, SpectralSpace (F.obj i)]
    (hF : ∀ ⦃i j : J⦄ (a : i ⟶ j), IsSpectralMap (F.map a))
    (i : J) (n : ℕ) (Ui : Set (F.obj i)) (U : Fin n → Set (F.obj i))
    (hUi_open : IsOpen Ui) (hUi_cpt : IsCompact Ui)
    (hU : ∀ s, IsOpen (U s) ∧ IsCompact (U s))
    (h : (limit.π F i) ⁻¹' Ui = ⋃ s, (limit.π F i) ⁻¹' (U s)) :
    ∃ (j : J) (a : j ⟶ i),
      (F.map a) ⁻¹' Ui = ⋃ s, (F.map a) ⁻¹' (U s)
declarations.comment: part (3): descent of finite unions

declarations.name: SpectralLimits.descent_of_finite_intersections
declarations.doc:
If, in the limit, the preimage of a quasi-compact open `Ui` equals the intersection of the
preimages of finitely many quasi-compact opens `U s` (`s : Fin n`), then this equality already
holds after pulling back along some `j ⟶ i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem descent_of_finite_intersections
    [∀ i, SpectralSpace (F.obj i)]
    (hF : ∀ ⦃i j : J⦄ (a : i ⟶ j), IsSpectralMap (F.map a))
    (i : J) (n : ℕ) (Ui : Set (F.obj i)) (U : Fin n → Set (F.obj i))
    (hUi_open : IsOpen Ui) (hUi_cpt : IsCompact Ui)
    (hU : ∀ s, IsOpen (U s) ∧ IsCompact (U s))
    (h : (limit.π F i) ⁻¹' Ui = ⋂ s, (limit.π F i) ⁻¹' (U s)) :
    ∃ (j : J) (a : j ⟶ i),
      (F.map a) ⁻¹' Ui = ⋂ s, (F.map a) ⁻¹' (U s)
declarations.comment: part (4): descent of finite intersections

declarations.name: SpectralSubset.characterizations_equiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A31, the equivalence.** For a subset `W` of a spectral space the five conditions
(1) intersection of constructibles and stable under generalization, (2) quasi-compact and stable
under generalization, (3) the generalizations of a quasi-compact set, (4) an intersection of
quasi-compact opens, (5) a directed intersection of quasi-compact opens, are all equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem characterizations_equiv [SpectralSpace X] (W : Set X) :
    (IsStableInterConstructible W ↔ IsStableCompact W) ∧
      (IsStableCompact W ↔ IsGeneralizationsOfCompact W) ∧
        (IsGeneralizationsOfCompact W ↔ IsInterCompactOpen W) ∧
          (IsInterCompactOpen W ↔ IsDirectedInterCompactOpen W)
declarations.comment: equivalence of the five characterizations

declarations.name: SpectralSubset.spectralSpace_of_isStableCompact
declarations.doc:
Conclusion (a): under the equivalent conditions, `W` (with the
subspace topology) is itself a spectral space.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralSpace_of_isStableCompact [SpectralSpace X] (W : Set X) (h : IsStableCompact W) :
    SpectralSpace W
declarations.comment: conclusion (a): W is spectral

declarations.name: SpectralSubset.exists_homeomorph_invLimit
declarations.doc: Conclusion (b): the canonical map `W → InvLimit U` is a homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homeomorph_invLimit
    {I : Type*} [Nonempty I] (U : I → Set X)
    (hdir : ∀ i j, ∃ k, U k ⊆ U i ∩ U j)
    (W : Set X) (hWeq : W = ⋂ i, U i) :
    ∃ φ : W ≃ₜ InvLimit U,
      ∀ w : W, ∀ i, ((φ w).1 i : X) = (w : X)
declarations.comment: conclusion (b): W ≅ lim U_i

declarations.name: SpectralSubset.exists_subset_of_subset_isOpen
declarations.doc:
Conclusion (c): with the family `U_i` from condition (5), every open
subset `V` of `X` containing `W` contains some `U_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_subset_of_subset_isOpen [SpectralSpace X]
    {I : Type*} [Nonempty I] (U : I → Set X)
    (hU : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i) ∧ IsCompact (U i))
    (hdir : ∀ i j, ∃ k, U k ⊆ U i ∩ U j)
    (W : Set X) (hWeq : W = ⋂ i, U i)
    (V : Set X) (hVopen : IsOpen V) (hWV : W ⊆ V) :
    ∃ i, U i ⊆ V
declarations.comment: conclusion (c): some U_i ⊆ V

declarations.name: SpectralDiagram.canonicalMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `colim_{a : j → i} (f_a⁻¹𝒢)(f_a⁻¹ U) → (p_i⁻¹𝒢)(p_i⁻¹ U)`, induced by pulling
sections back to the limit along the projections.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalMap [UnivLE.{max v v', max v u}] :
    colimit (D.sliceFunctor U 𝒢) ⟶ (D.sliceCocone U 𝒢).pt
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: SpectralDiagram.bijective_canonicalMap
declarations.doc:
For `i` an object of the cofiltered index category, `𝒢` a sheaf of sets on `X_i` and `U ⊆ X_i`
a quasi-compact open, the canonical map `colim_{a : j → i} (f_a⁻¹𝒢)(f_a⁻¹ U) → (p_i⁻¹𝒢)(p_i⁻¹ U)`
is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_canonicalMap [UnivLE.{max v v', max v u}] (hU : IsCompact (U : Set (D.F.obj i))) :
    Function.Bijective (D.canonicalMap U 𝒢)
declarations.comment: bijectivity of the canonical map

declarations.name: SpectralSheafSystem.stageColimitMap
declarations.doc: **The canonical map of Stacks 0A33**, `colim_{a : j → i} F_j(f_a⁻¹U) → F(p_i⁻¹U)`.
declarations.statement:
def stageColimitMap [UnivLE.{max v v', max v u}] : colimit (S.stageFunctor U) ⟶
    (S.colimitPullback).obj.obj (op (S.diagram.comapProj i U))
declarations.comment: the canonical map

declarations.name: SpectralSheafSystem.bijective_stageColimitMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A33.**  Let `J` be a cofiltered index category, `j ↦ X_j` a diagram of spectral
spaces with spectral transition maps, `F_j` a sheaf of sets on `X_j` for each `j` together with a
compatible system of `f_a`-maps, and `F = colim_j p_j⁻¹F_j` on the limit `X = lim_j X_j`.  Then for
every `i` and every quasi-compact open `U ⊆ X_i` the canonical map
`colim_{a : j → i} F_j(f_a⁻¹U) → F(p_i⁻¹U)`
is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_stageColimitMap [UnivLE.{max v v', max v u}]
    (hU : IsCompact (U : Set (S.diagram.F.obj i))) :
    Function.Bijective (S.stageColimitMap U)

declarations.name: InverseSystemOfSites
declarations.doc:
An *inverse system of sites with finite coverings*, following the Stacks
Project tag `situation-inverse-limit-sites`.

The data consists of:

* a cofiltered index category `I`;
* for each `i : I`, a (small) category `C i` equipped with a Grothendieck
  topology `J i` such that every covering sieve admits a finite generating family;
* for each morphism `a : i ⟶ j` in `I`, a functor `u a : C j ⥤ C i` continuous in the sense of
  Stacks 00WV and giving a morphism of sites in the sense of Stacks 00X1 (note the reversed
  direction: the morphism of sites `f a : C i ⟶ C j` is given by `u a : C j ⥤ C i`);
* compatibility with composition `u (b ≫ a) = u a ⋙ u b` and identities
  `u (𝟙 i) = 𝟭 (C i)`.
declarations.statement: structure InverseSystemOfSites

declarations.name: InverseSystemOfFiniteSites
declarations.doc:
An *inverse system of sites with finite coverings* (Stacks 0A34), carrying the finiteness
condition the source actually imposes.

In Stacks 00VH a site is a category together with a collection of *coverings*, each of which is a
*finite* family of morphisms with a common target, and its Grothendieck topology is the one those
coverings generate. So the content of "the coverings of `C i` are finite" is that the finite
covering families generate `J i`, that is: every covering sieve `S` of `J i` **contains** a finite
covering family. That is the `finiteCoverings` field here.

`InverseSystemOfSites.finiteCoverings` instead asks that every covering sieve be **generated** by a
finite family, which is strictly stronger: `InverseSystemOfSites` is the special case of this
structure in which every covering sieve happens to be finitely generated. Nothing of the kind is
available on the sites this situation is meant for — on `Spec k[t]` the sieve generated by all the
standard opens `D(f)` is a covering sieve of the Zariski, hence also of the étale, topology and is
dominated by no finite subfamily — so no inverse system of étale sites satisfies the stronger
condition and Stacks 09YL could not be applied to one. Every such system does satisfy the
condition below.

Every other field, and the record-level data, is literally that of `InverseSystemOfSites`, so the
two structures are interchangeable wherever `finiteCoverings` is not used; and a strong system is a
weak one, `InverseSystemOfSites.toInverseSystemOfFiniteSites`.
declarations.statement: structure InverseSystemOfFiniteSites

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sites.InverseSystem.InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.exists_isMorphismOfSites_sections_pullback_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
**The colimit of an inverse system of sites.** In the situation of Stacks 0A34, let the
functors `u i : D.C i ⥤ C` exhibit the small category `C` as the colimit of the `D.C i` (`hu`,
`hobj`, `hhom`, `hhom_inj`) and let `K` be the collection of coverings of `C` of Stacks 09YL, the
images under the `u i` of the finite coverings of the `D.C i` (`hK`).

Then each `u i` defines a morphism of sites `f_i : C → C_i` between `(C, K.toGrothendieck)` and
`(D.C i, D.J i)`: it is continuous and `f_i^{-1}` is exact (Stacks 00X1). Moreover, for every
object `U` of `D.C i` and every sheaf of sets `F` on `D.C i`, the canonical maps
`θ a : f_a^{-1}F(u_a U) → f_i^{-1}F(u_i U)`, indexed by the arrows `a : j ⟶ i` of `D.I`, exhibit
`f_i^{-1}F(u_i U)` as their filtered colimit: every section of `f_i^{-1}F` over `u_i U` is `θ a t`
for some `a` and some section `t` of `f_a^{-1}F` over `u_a U`, and two sections of `f_a^{-1}F` over
`u_a U` with the same image under `θ a` agree after pullback along `D.u b` for some `b : k ⟶ j`.
This is equation (09YM) of the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.exists_isMorphismOfSites_sections_pullback_of_colimit
    {C : Type w} [SmallCategory C] (D : InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.{u₁, u₂, w}) (u : ∀ i, D.C i ⥤ C)
    (hu : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : i ⟶ j), D.u a ⋙ u i = u j)
    (hobj : ∀ X : C, ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i), (u i).obj Y = X)
    (hhom :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (f : (u i).obj X ⟶ (u i).obj Y),
        ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (g : (D.u a).obj X ⟶ (D.u a).obj Y),
          (u j).map g =
            eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) X) ≫ f ≫ eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) Y).symm)
    (hhom_inj :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (g₁ g₂ : X ⟶ Y),
        (u i).map g₁ = (u i).map g₂ → ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i), (D.u a).map g₁ = (D.u a).map g₂)
    (K : Precoverage C)
    (hK :
      ∀ (X : C) (R : Presieve X),
        R ∈ K X ↔
          ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i) (h : (u i).obj Y = X) (S : Presieve Y),
            S ∈ (D.J i).toPrecoverage Y ∧ S ∈ Precoverage.finite (D.C i) Y ∧ R = h ▸ S.map (u i)) :
    ∃ hf : ∀ i, (u i).IsMorphismOfSites (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck,
      haveI _hcont : ∀ i, (u i).IsContinuous (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck := fun i =>
        (hf i).isContinuous
      haveI _hcontu : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : i ⟶ j), (D.u a).IsContinuous (D.J j) (D.J i) := fun a =>
        D.continuous a
      ∀ (i : D.I) (U : D.C i) (F : Sheaf (D.J i) (Type w))
        (θ :
          ∀ {j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i),
            (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj U)) →
              (((u i).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck).obj F).obj.obj
                (op ((u i).obj U))),
        (∀ {j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i),
            θ a =
              (((D.u a).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).map
                      ((((D.u a).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).homEquiv F
                            (((u j).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type w) (D.J j)
                                  K.toGrothendieck).obj
                              (((u i).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck).obj
                                F))).symm
                        (((u i).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type w) (D.J i)
                                K.toGrothendieck).unit.app
                            F ≫
                          (Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousComp' (eqToIso (hu a)) (Type w)
                                (D.J i) (D.J j) K.toGrothendieck).inv.app
                            _)) ≫
                    (Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousComp' (eqToIso (hu a)) (Type w) (D.J i)
                          (D.J j) K.toGrothendieck).hom.app
                      _).hom.app
                (op U)) →
          (∀ s :
              (((u i).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck).obj F).obj.obj
                (op ((u i).obj U)),
              ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (t :
                (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F).obj.obj
                  (op ((D.u a).obj U))),
                θ a t = s) ∧
            ∀ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i)
              (t t' :
                (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F).obj.obj
                  (op ((D.u a).obj U))),
              θ a t = θ a t' →
                ∃ (k : D.I) (b : k ⟶ j),
                  (((D.u b).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type w) (D.J j) (D.J k)).unit.app
                          (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F)).hom.app
                      (op ((D.u a).obj U)) t =
                    (((D.u b).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type w) (D.J j) (D.J k)).unit.app
                          (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F)).hom.app
                      (op ((D.u a).obj U)) t'
