declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sites.InverseSystem.InverseSystemOfSites.exists_isMorphismOfSites_sections_pullback_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
**The colimit of an inverse system of sites.** In the situation of Stacks 0A34, let the
functors `u i : D.C i ⥤ C` exhibit the small category `C` as the colimit of the `D.C i` (`hu`,
`hobj`, `hhom`, `hhom_inj`) and let `K` be the collection of coverings of `C` of Stacks 09YL, the
images under the `u i` of the finite coverings of the `D.C i` (`hK`).

Then each `u i` defines a morphism of sites `f_i : C → C_i` between `(C, K.toGrothendieck)` and
`(D.C i, D.J i)`: it is continuous and `f_i^{-1}` is exact (Stacks 00X1). Moreover, for every
object `U` of `D.C i` and every sheaf of sets `F` on `D.C i`, the canonical maps
`θ a : f_a^{-1}F(u_a U) → f_i^{-1}F(u_i U)`, indexed by the arrows `a : j ⟶ i` of `D.I`, exhibit
`f_i^{-1}F(u_i U)` as their filtered colimit: every section of `f_i^{-1}F` over `u_i U` is `θ a t`
for some `a` and some section `t` of `f_a^{-1}F` over `u_a U`, and two sections of `f_a^{-1}F` over
`u_a U` with the same image under `θ a` agree after pullback along `D.u b` for some `b : k ⟶ j`.
This is equation (09YM) of the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem InverseSystemOfSites.exists_isMorphismOfSites_sections_pullback_of_colimit
    {C : Type w} [SmallCategory C] (D : InverseSystemOfSites.{u₁, u₂, w}) (u : ∀ i, D.C i ⥤ C)
    (hu : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : i ⟶ j), D.u a ⋙ u i = u j)
    (hobj : ∀ X : C, ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i), (u i).obj Y = X)
    (hhom :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (f : (u i).obj X ⟶ (u i).obj Y),
        ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (g : (D.u a).obj X ⟶ (D.u a).obj Y),
          (u j).map g =
            eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) X) ≫ f ≫ eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) Y).symm)
    (hhom_inj :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (g₁ g₂ : X ⟶ Y),
        (u i).map g₁ = (u i).map g₂ → ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i), (D.u a).map g₁ = (D.u a).map g₂)
    (K : Precoverage C)
    (hK :
      ∀ (X : C) (R : Presieve X),
        R ∈ K X ↔
          ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i) (h : (u i).obj Y = X) (S : Presieve Y),
            S ∈ (D.J i).toPrecoverage Y ∧ S ∈ Precoverage.finite (D.C i) Y ∧ R = h ▸ S.map (u i)) :
    ∃ hf : ∀ i, (u i).IsMorphismOfSites (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck,
      haveI _hcont : ∀ i, (u i).IsContinuous (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck := fun i =>
        (hf i).isContinuous
      haveI _hcontu : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : i ⟶ j), (D.u a).IsContinuous (D.J j) (D.J i) := fun a =>
        D.continuous a
      ∀ (i : D.I) (U : D.C i) (F : Sheaf (D.J i) (Type w))
        (θ :
          ∀ {j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i),
            (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj U)) →
              (((u i).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck).obj F).obj.obj
                (op ((u i).obj U))),
        (∀ {j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i),
            θ a =
              (((D.u a).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).map
                      ((((D.u a).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).homEquiv F
                            (((u j).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type w) (D.J j)
                                  K.toGrothendieck).obj
                              (((u i).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck).obj
                                F))).symm
                        (((u i).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type w) (D.J i)
                                K.toGrothendieck).unit.app
                            F ≫
                          (Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousComp' (eqToIso (hu a)) (Type w)
                                (D.J i) (D.J j) K.toGrothendieck).inv.app
                            _)) ≫
                    (Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuousComp' (eqToIso (hu a)) (Type w) (D.J i)
                          (D.J j) K.toGrothendieck).hom.app
                      _).hom.app
                (op U)) →
          (∀ s :
              (((u i).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) K.toGrothendieck).obj F).obj.obj
                (op ((u i).obj U)),
              ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (t :
                (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F).obj.obj
                  (op ((D.u a).obj U))),
                θ a t = s) ∧
            ∀ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i)
              (t t' :
                (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F).obj.obj
                  (op ((D.u a).obj U))),
              θ a t = θ a t' →
                ∃ (k : D.I) (b : k ⟶ j),
                  (((D.u b).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type w) (D.J j) (D.J k)).unit.app
                          (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F)).hom.app
                      (op ((D.u a).obj U)) t =
                    (((D.u b).sheafAdjunctionContinuous (Type w) (D.J j) (D.J k)).unit.app
                          (((D.u a).sheafPullback (Type w) (D.J i) (D.J j)).obj F)).hom.app
                      (op ((D.u a).obj U)) t'
declarations.comment:
The functors `u_i` from the members of an inverse system of sites to its colimit
  define morphisms of sites, and the sections of `f_i^{-1}F` over `u_i(U_i)` are the filtered
  colimit of the sections of `f_a^{-1}F` over `u_a(U_i)`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RaviCech.isZero_cechCohomology_of_surjective_restrictions
declarations.doc:
If restriction from the covered open to every union of nonempty finite intersections of
members of the cover is surjective, then the positive-degree Čech cohomology of the cover
vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma isZero_cechCohomology_of_surjective_restrictions
    (U₀ : Opens X) (hcover : U₀ = ⨆ i, U i)
    (hres : ∀ (V : Opens X) (hVU : V ≤ U₀),
      (∃ S : Set (Finset ι), (∀ s ∈ S, s.Nonempty) ∧
        V = ⨆ s : S, ⨅ i : (s : Finset ι), U i) →
      Function.Surjective (F.obj.map (homOfLE hVU).op))
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero
      (((CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor (A := AddCommGrpCat.{v}) U).obj F.obj).homology p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpectralLimit.SpectralAbelianSheafSystem.nonempty_and_isIso_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A37, over a quasi-compact open of a stage.**  For a cofiltered system of spectral
spaces `Xⱼ` with spectral transition maps and abelian sheaves `𝓕ⱼ` with compatible `f`-maps, the
limit `X = lim Xⱼ` with the sheaf `𝓕 = colim pⱼ⁻¹𝓕ⱼ` on it (a limiting cone `c` of the diagram
of abelian sheafed spaces), a stage `i`, a quasi-compact open `Uᵢ ⊆ Xᵢ` and `p ≥ 0`, the
cohomology cocone `colim_{a : j → i} Hᵖ(f_a⁻¹ Uᵢ, 𝓕ⱼ) ⟶ Hᵖ(pᵢ⁻¹ Uᵢ, 𝓕)` exists and its
comparison out of the colimit is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_and_isIso_comparison (c : Cone S.E) (hc : IsLimit c) (i : J)
    (U : Opens (S.E.obj i)) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set (S.E.obj i))) (p : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (CohomologyCocone ((Over.forget i) ⋙ S.E) (c.whisker (Over.forget i))
      (S.stageOpenCone c i U) p) ∧
    ∀ D : CohomologyCocone ((Over.forget i) ⋙ S.E) (c.whisker (Over.forget i))
      (S.stageOpenCone c i U) p, IsIso D.comparison
declarations.comment: quasi-compact open: colim_{a : j → i} Hᵖ(f_a⁻¹(Uᵢ), 𝓕ⱼ) = Hᵖ(pᵢ⁻¹(Uᵢ), 𝓕) for every p ≥ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SpectralLimit.SpectralAbelianSheafSystem.nonempty_and_isIso_comparison_global
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A37, the global statement**: for a limiting cone `c` of the system and `p ≥ 0`, the
cohomology cocone `colim Hᵖ(Xᵢ, 𝓕ᵢ) ⟶ Hᵖ(X, 𝓕)` exists and its comparison out of the colimit is
an isomorphism, that is `Hᵖ(X, 𝓕) = colim Hᵖ(Xᵢ, 𝓕ᵢ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_and_isIso_comparison_global (c : Cone S.E) (hc : IsLimit c) (p : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (CohomologyCocone S.E c (S.globalOpenCone c) p) ∧
    ∀ D : CohomologyCocone S.E c (S.globalOpenCone c) p, IsIso D.comparison
declarations.comment: in particular Hᵖ(X, 𝓕) = colim Hᵖ(Xᵢ, 𝓕ᵢ) for every p ≥ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.ConstantIntegerSubsheaves.exists_filtration_of_finitelyGeneratedByCompactOpenSections
declarations.doc:
A subsheaf of the constant sheaf of integers generated by finitely many sections over
quasi-compact opens, on a space whose quasi-compact opens are closed under intersection, has a
finite filtration `0 = F₀ ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ F_n = F` by abelian subsheaves whose successive quotients fit into
short exact sequences `0 ⟶ j'_! ℤ_V ⟶ j_! ℤ_U ⟶ F_i / F_{i - 1} ⟶ 0` with `V ⊆ U` quasi-compact
opens.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_filtration_of_finitelyGeneratedByCompactOpenSections [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (F : Subobject (integerConstantSheaf X))
    (hF : FinitelyGeneratedByCompactOpenSections X F) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : Fin (n + 1) → Subobject (integerConstantSheaf X))
      (hG : Monotone G),
      G 0 = ⊥ ∧ G (Fin.last n) = F ∧
        ∀ i : Fin n,
          ∃ (U V : Opens X),
            V ≤ U ∧ IsCompact (U : Set X) ∧ IsCompact (V : Set X) ∧
              ∃ (a : integerExtensionByZero X V ⟶ integerExtensionByZero X U)
                (b : integerExtensionByZero X U ⟶
                  cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (G i.castSucc) (G i.succ)
                    (hG i.castSucc_le_succ))),
                ∃ hab : a ≫ b = 0, (ShortComplex.mk a b hab).ShortExact

declarations.name: ClosedImmersionSheaves.supportedSectionsOnClosed_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A3A.** Sections of an injective abelian sheaf supported on a closed
subset form an injective abelian sheaf on that subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportedSectionsOnClosed_injective {X : TopCat.{u}}
    (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (I : X.Sheaf AddCommGrpCat.{u})
    [Injective I] :
    Injective ((supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor Z hZ).obj I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.derivedPushforwardAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3B (1), as a term.** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X` and let
`i : (Z, 𝒪_X|_Z) ⟶ (X, 𝒪_X)` be the inclusion. The functor `D(𝒪_X|_Z) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` induced by
`i_*` is left adjoint to the right derived functor `RH_Z : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X|_Z)` of sections
supported on `Z`.

This is the adjunction whose mere existence is
`derivedPushforward_adj_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed`, and its unit is the canonical
comparison by `derivedPushforwardAdjunction_unit_app`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedPushforwardAdjunction (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier)
    (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X Z
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X Z hZ
    (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory ⊣
      derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ
declarations.comment: the adjunction i_*^D ⊣ RℋZ as a term, not an existence statement

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.derivedPushforwardCompDerivedSupportedSectionsIsoId
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3B (2) as a natural isomorphism.** Composing `RH_Z` with the derived pushforward
from the closed subset is the identity on `D(𝒪_X|_Z)`, the isomorphism being the inverse of the
unit of `derivedPushforwardAdjunction`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedPushforwardCompDerivedSupportedSectionsIsoId (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X Z
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X Z hZ
    (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ ≅
      𝟭 (DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
        (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z))))
declarations.comment: RℋZ ∘ i_*^D ≅ 𝟭, as a chosen natural isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.derivedPushforward_adj_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3B (1).** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X` and let
`i : (Z, 𝒪_X|_Z) ⟶ (X, 𝒪_X)` be the inclusion. The right derived functor
`RH_Z : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X|_Z)` of sections supported on `Z` is right adjoint to the functor
`D(𝒪_X|_Z) ⥤ D(𝒪_X)` induced by `i_*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPushforward_adj_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X Z
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X Z hZ
    Nonempty
      ((modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory ⊣
        derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ)
declarations.comment: adjunction

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.exists_isIso_unit_derivedPushforward_adj_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3B (2).** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X` and let
`i : (Z, 𝒪_X|_Z) ⟶ (X, 𝒪_X)` be the inclusion. For `K` in `D(𝒪_X|_Z)` one has
`RH_Z(i_* K) = K`: the unit of the derived adjunction of Stacks 0A3B (1) is an isomorphism. The
adjunction is pinned down by the compatibility of its unit with the unit `M ⟶ H_Z(i_* M)` of the
underived adjunction, which identifies the invertible map as the canonical comparison.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIso_unit_derivedPushforward_adj_derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z) :
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteLimits X Z
    letI := pushforward_preservesFiniteColimits X Z hZ
    ∃ Ad : (modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategory ⊣
        derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ,
      (∀ M : HomotopyCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
          (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z))) (ComplexShape.up ℤ),
        Ad.unit.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj M) ≫
            (derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosed X Z hZ).map
              ((modulePushforward
                (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.hom.app M) =
          DerivedCategory.Qh.map
              ((Adjunction.mapHomotopyCategoryAdjunction
                (modulePushforward_supportedSectionsOnClosed_adjunction X Z hZ)
                (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).unit.app M) ≫
            (derivedSupportedSectionsOnClosedUnit X Z hZ).app
              (((modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).mapHomotopyCategory
                (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M)) ∧ IsIso Ad.unit
declarations.comment: pushforward identity

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SupportedComplexes.isZero_rightDerivedPlus_supportedSectionsOnClosed_modulePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3B (3).** Let `Z` be a closed subset of a ringed space `X`, let
`i : (Z, 𝒪_X|_Z) ⟶ (X, 𝒪_X)` be the inclusion and let `𝒢` be a sheaf of `𝒪_X|_Z`-modules on
`Z`. Then the higher derived sheaves of sections supported on `Z` of the pushforward of `𝒢`
vanish: `H^p_Z(i_* 𝒢) = 0` for `p > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerivedPlus_supportedSectionsOnClosed_modulePushforward
    (X : RingedSpace.{u, u}) (Z : Set X.carrier) (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing (closedSubsetRingedSpace X Z)))
    (p : ℤ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    letI : EnoughInjectives (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X)) :=
      IsGrothendieckAbelian.enoughInjectives
    IsZero (((supportedSectionsOnClosedFunctor X Z hZ).rightDerivedPlus p).obj
      ((modulePushforward (closedSubsetInclusion X Z)).obj G))
declarations.comment: higher vanishing

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.isIso_cohomologyOfGeneralizationsMap
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a spectral space, let `F` be an abelian sheaf on `X`,
let `E ⊆ X` be quasi-compact and let `W` be the set of points of `X` which specialize to a point
of `E`. Then for every `p` the canonical map

`colim_{E ⊆ U quasi-compact open} H^p(U, F) ⟶ H^p(W, F|_W)`

is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cohomologyOfGeneralizationsMap (hE : IsCompact E)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (p : ℕ) :
    IsIso (cohomologyOfGeneralizationsMap E F p)
declarations.comment: cohomology_of_neighbourhoods

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.isIso_cohomologyOfComplementGeneralizationsMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3D] (2).** Let `X` be a spectral space, let `F` be an abelian sheaf on `X`,
let `E ⊆ X` be quasi-compact and constructible and let `W` be the set of points of `X` which
specialize to a point of `E`. Then for every `p` the canonical map

`colim_{E ⊆ U quasi-compact open} H^p(U \ E, F|_{U \ E}) ⟶ H^p(W \ E, F|_{W \ E})`

is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cohomologyOfComplementGeneralizationsMap (hE : Topology.IsConstructible E)
    (hEc : IsCompact E) (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (p : ℕ) :
    IsIso (cohomologyOfComplementGeneralizationsMap E F p)
declarations.comment: cohomology_of_complements

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.higherDirectImageStalkIso
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a spectral map of spectral spaces, let `y` be a point of `Y`, let `E` be the
set of points of `Y` specializing to `y` and let `F` be a sheaf of abelian groups on `X`. Then for
every `p` the stalk at `y` of the `p`-th higher direct image of `F` is the `p`-th cohomology of the
restriction of `F` to `f⁻¹(E)`:

`(R^p f_* F)_y = H^p(f⁻¹(E), F|_{f⁻¹(E)})`.

Here `f⁻¹(E)` is `Stacks.Topology.specializationFiber f y`, the set of points of `X` whose image
specializes to `y`, and cohomology is the right derived functor of global sections.
declarations.statement:
def higherDirectImageStalkIso (hf : IsSpectralMap f) (p : ℕ)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :
    ((pushforwardSheafFunctor f).rightDerived p ⋙ sheafStalkFunctor y).obj F ≅
      ((sectionsFunctor (TopCat.of (specializationFiber f y))).rightDerived p).obj
        ((restrictionFunctor X (specializationFiber f y)).obj F)

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.cohomology_subsingleton_of_isProfiniteStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3F.** On a profinite space every positive-degree sheaf cohomology group of every
abelian sheaf vanishes.

Global sections is exact on a profinite space, because local lifts along a cover may be refined
to lifts along a *disjoint* finite clopen cover (Stacks 08ZZ) and those glue with no
compatibility to check. Sheaf cohomology is `Ext` out of the constant sheaf `ℤ`, and the
constant-sheaf functor is left adjoint to global sections, so exactness of global sections makes
that constant sheaf projective and every `Ext` out of it vanishes in positive degree.

This is the `Sheaf.H` (that is, `Ext`) formulation; the right-derived-functor formulation is
`Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.isZero_abelianSheafCohomology_of_isProfiniteStacks`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomology_subsingleton_of_isProfiniteStacks
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [HasExt.{w'} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w})]
    (hX : IsProfiniteStacks X)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w})
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) : Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w', w, u, u} F q)
declarations.comment: sheaf cohomology as Ext out of the constant sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.isZero_abelianSheafCohomology_of_isProfiniteStacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3F.** If `X` is profinite, then every positive-degree cohomology group of
every abelian sheaf on `X` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_abelianSheafCohomology_of_isProfiniteStacks
    [(Opens.grothendieckTopology X).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (hX : IsProfiniteStacks X)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w})
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) :
    IsZero (abelianSheafCohomology q F)

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.cohomology_subsingleton_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3G, clause (1) in dimension zero.** Let `X` be a spectral space of Krull dimension
`0` and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on `X`. Then `H^q(X, F) = 0` for every `q > 0`.

This is the base case of the induction on the dimension in Stacks 0A3G: a zero-dimensional spectral
space is profinite
(`isProfiniteStacks_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero`), and on a profinite space positive-degree
cohomology vanishes (`cohomology_subsingleton_of_isProfiniteStacks`).

The hypotheses are satisfiable: `X = Spec R` for a zero-dimensional ring such as a field, a
finite product of fields, or `ZMod 4`, has `topologicalKrullDim X = 0`, and the conclusion is
then a genuine statement about every abelian sheaf on a nontrivial space.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomology_subsingleton_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [HasExt.{w'} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w})]
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{w})
    (q : ℕ) (hX : topologicalKrullDim X = ((0 : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hq : 0 < q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w', w, u, u} F q)
declarations.comment: clause (1) for dimension zero

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafH_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
declarations.doc:
Let `Y` be a spectral space of Krull dimension at most `d` and let `G` be an abelian sheaf on
`Y`. Then `H^q(Y, G) = 0` for every `q > d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_of_topologicalKrullDim_le :
    ∀ (d : ℕ) (Y : Type u) [TopologicalSpace Y] [SpectralSpace Y]
      (_hs : HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) AddCommGrpCat.{u})
      (_he : HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) AddCommGrpCat.{u}))
      (G : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (q : ℕ),
      topologicalKrullDim Y ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞) → d < q →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u, u, u, u} G q)
declarations.comment: clause (1): on a spectral space, sheaf cohomology vanishes above the dimension

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafH_above_topologicalKrullDim
declarations.doc:
Let `Y` be a spectral space of Krull dimension at most `d` and let `G` be an abelian sheaf on
`Y`. Then `H^q(Y, G) = 0` for every `q > d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_above_topologicalKrullDim {Y : Type u} [TopologicalSpace Y]
    [SpectralSpace Y]
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    (G : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (d q : ℕ)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim Y ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (hq : d < q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u, u, u, u} G q)
declarations.comment: clause (1): on a spectral space of Krull dimension at most d, sheaf cohomology vanishes in every degree above d. The same statement as the induction carrier subsingleton_sheafH_of_topologicalKrullDim_le, whose explicit HasSheafify and HasExt arguments are instance arguments here

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.surjective_cohomologyPresheaf_map_top_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a spectral space of Krull dimension at most `d` and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on
`X`. Then the restriction `H^d(X, F) → H^d(U, F)` is surjective for every quasi-compact open
`U ⊆ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_cohomologyPresheaf_map_top_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (d : ℕ)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (U : Opens X)
    (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) :
    Function.Surjective
      ((F.cohomologyPresheaf d).map (homOfLE (show U ≤ ⊤ from le_top)).op)
declarations.comment: clause (2): surjectivity of the restriction H^d(X,F) → H^d(U,F) for U quasi-compact open

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_sheafH_and_surjective_and_subsingleton_supported_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3G].** Let `X` be a spectral space of Krull dimension `d` and let `F` be an
abelian sheaf on `X`. Then

1. `H^q(X, F) = 0` for `q > d`;
2. `H^d(X, F) ⟶ H^d(U, F)` is surjective for every quasi-compact open `U ⊆ X`;
3. `H^q_Z(X, F) = 0` for `q > d` and every constructible closed subset `Z ⊆ X`.

Cohomology is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`, the `Ext`-groups out of the constant abelian
sheaf `ℤ` on the site of opens; cohomology over an open is the value of
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cohomologyPresheaf`, so that clause (2) is a statement about the restriction
map of that presheaf; and cohomology with support in `Z` is the right derived functor of the
sections over `X` of the subsheaf of sections supported on `Z`.

Each clause is proved in the file named beside it below, where it is proved under the weaker
hypothesis that `d` bounds the dimension rather than equalling it. Here they are put together
under the source's hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_sheafH_and_surjective_and_subsingleton_supported_of_topologicalKrullDim_eq
    {X : TopCat.{u}} [SpectralSpace X]
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (d : ℕ)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    (∀ q : ℕ, d < q → Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{u, u, u, u} F q)) ∧
      (∀ U : Opens X, IsCompact (U : Set X) → Function.Surjective
        ((F.cohomologyPresheaf d).map (homOfLE (show U ≤ ⊤ from le_top)).op)) ∧
      (∀ Z : Set X, IsClosed Z → IsConstructible Z → ∀ q : ℕ, d < q →
        Subsingleton (((supportedSectionsEvaluation Z ⊤).rightDerived q).obj F))
declarations.comment: the whole proposition: (1) sheaf cohomology on a spectral space of Krull dimension d vanishes above degree d, (2) restriction to a quasi-compact open is surjective in degree d, and (3) cohomology with support in a constructible closed subset vanishes above degree d

declarations.name: Stacks.CohomologyVanishing.subsingleton_rightDerived_supportedSections_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3G], clause (3).** Let `X` be a spectral space of Krull dimension at most
`d`, let `F` be an abelian sheaf on `X` and let `Z` be a constructible closed subset of `X`.
Then the cohomology of `F` with support in `Z` vanishes in every degree `q > d`.

Cohomology with support in `Z` is the right derived functor of the sections over `X` of the
subsheaf of sections supported on `Z`. The proof is the source's: the long exact sequence of the
pair `(X, X ∖ Z)`, built on an injective resolution, together with clause (1) for `H^q(X, F)`
and clause (2) for the surjectivity of `H^{q-1}(X, F) → H^{q-1}(X ∖ Z, F)`, the complement of a
constructible closed set being a quasi-compact open.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_rightDerived_supportedSections_of_topologicalKrullDim_le
    [SpectralSpace X]
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (d q : ℕ)
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsClosed Z)
    (hZc : IsConstructible Z) (hq : d < q) :
    Subsingleton (((supportedSectionsEvaluation Z ⊤).rightDerived q).obj F)
declarations.comment: clause (3): cohomology with support in a constructible closed subset vanishes above the dimension

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage_of_flat_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A3H.** For `f : T ⟶ S` flat and quasi-compact with geometrically
connected fibres, the *canonical* comparison `Γ(S, F) ⟶ Γ(T, f⁻¹F)` is an isomorphism for every
sheaf of sets `F` on the small étale site of `S`, naturally in `F`. This is the form in which
the source asserts the tag — it writes `Γ(S, F) = Γ(T, f⁻¹F)` for the canonical map, and proves
that map injective and surjective — and it is stronger than the bare existence of an isomorphism
of global-sections functors, which would not say that the isomorphism is restriction of
sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage_of_flat_quasiCompact
    {T S : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S) [Flat f] [QuasiCompact f] [GeometricallyConnected f] :
    IsIso (globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} f)
declarations.comment: the form the source asserts: the canonical comparison on global sections, rather than a bare isomorphism of global-sections functors

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso_of_flat_of_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A3H.** Pullback along a flat quasi-compact morphism with
geometrically connected fibres preserves global sections of every sheaf of sets on the small
étale site, naturally in the sheaf. The isomorphism is the canonical comparison, which
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImage_of_flat_quasiCompact`
inverts.
declarations.statement:
public def globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso_of_flat_of_quasiCompact
    {T S : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ S) [Flat f] [QuasiCompact f] [GeometricallyConnected f] :
    Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology S) (Type (max (u + 1) v)) ≅
      smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v} f ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology T) (Type (max (u + 1) v))
declarations.comment: the natural isomorphism of global-sections functors, with no hypothesis beyond the source's

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso_of_isSepClosed
declarations.doc:
For a scheme `S` over a separably closed field `k` and any field extension `K/k`, pullback
along the projection `S ×_{Spec k} Spec K ⟶ S` preserves global sections of every sheaf of sets on
the small étale site, naturally in the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public def globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageIso_of_isSepClosed
    (k K : Type u) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (f : S ⟶ Spec (.of k)) :
    Sheaf.Γ (smallEtaleTopology S) (Type (max (u + 1) v)) ≅
      smallEtaleInverseImage.{u, v}
          (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))) ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ
          (smallEtaleTopology (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))))
          (Type (max (u + 1) v))

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.constantArtinSchreierSequence_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**The Artin–Schreier sequence.** For a scheme `X` of characteristic `p`,

`0 ⟶ 𝐙/p𝐙 ⟶ 𝐆_a ⟶ 𝐆_a ⟶ 0`

is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, the second map being
`x ↦ x ^ p - x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantArtinSchreierSequence_shortExact :
    (constantArtinSchreierSequence.{u, v} X hp hX).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.subsingleton_etaleH_constantZMod_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime and let `S` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme of
characteristic `p` and of dimension at most `d`. Then `H ^ q (S_étale, 𝐙/p𝐙) = 0` for every
`q ≥ d + 2`. Only the upper bound on the dimension of `S` is needed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_etaleH_constantZMod_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_unconditional (p : ℕ)
    [Fact p.Prime] (S : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (hS : (p : Γ(S, ⊤)) = 0)
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (S : Type u) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : d + 2 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w, u + 1} (etaleConstantZMod S p) q)

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.subsingleton_etaleH_constantZMod_of_isAffine_constantSequence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3K] (1).** Let `p` be a prime and let `S` be an affine scheme on which `p`
vanishes. Then `H ^ q (S_étale, 𝐙/p𝐙) = 0` for every `q ≥ 2`.

The cohomology of the structure sheaf of an affine scheme vanishes in positive degree by
[Stacks, Tag 01XB], so the Artin–Schreier degree shift applies with `n = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_etaleH_constantZMod_of_isAffine_constantSequence (p : ℕ)
    [Fact p.Prime] (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] (hS : (p : Γ(S, ⊤)) = 0)
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w, u + 1} (etaleConstantZMod S p) q)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.subsingleton_etaleH_constantZMod_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_constantSequence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3K] (2).** Let `p` be a prime and let `S` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme on which `p` vanishes and of dimension at most `d`. Then
`H ^ q (S_étale, 𝐙/p𝐙) = 0` for every `q ≥ d + 2`.

The underlying space of `S` is spectral, so the cohomology of the structure sheaf vanishes above
its dimension by [Stacks, Tag 0A3G], and the Artin–Schreier degree shift applies with `n = d`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem subsingleton_etaleH_constantZMod_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_constantSequence
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (S : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (hS : (p : Γ(S, ⊤)) = 0)
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology (S : Type u)) AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    (d : ℕ) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (S : Type u) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : d + 2 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w, u + 1} (etaleConstantZMod S p) q)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: fixedPoints_finiteDimensional_of_frobenius_semilinear
declarations.doc:
The fixed points of a Frobenius-semilinear additive endomorphism of a
finite-dimensional vector space are finite-dimensional over the prime field.
declarations.statement:
theorem fixedPoints_finiteDimensional_of_frobenius_semilinear
    (hF : ∀ (c : k) (x : V), F (c • x) = c ^ p • F x) :
    letI : Module (ZMod p) V :=
      Module.compHom V (ZMod.castHom (dvd_refl p) k)
    FiniteDimensional (ZMod p) (AddMonoidHom.ker (F - AddMonoidHom.id V))
declarations.comment: kernel_bound

declarations.name: finrank_fixedPoints_le_of_frobenius_semilinear
declarations.doc:
The dimension over the prime field of the fixed points of a
Frobenius-semilinear additive endomorphism is at most the dimension of the
original vector space.
declarations.statement:
theorem finrank_fixedPoints_le_of_frobenius_semilinear
    (hF : ∀ (c : k) (x : V), F (c • x) = c ^ p • F x) :
    letI : Module (ZMod p) V :=
      Module.compHom V (ZMod.castHom (dvd_refl p) k)
    Module.finrank (ZMod p) (AddMonoidHom.ker (F - AddMonoidHom.id V)) ≤
      Module.finrank k V
declarations.comment: kernel_bound

declarations.name: frobeniusSemilinear_sub_id_surjective
declarations.doc:
Let `V` be a finite-dimensional vector space over an algebraically closed field `k` of
positive characteristic `p`. If the additive endomorphism `F` is Frobenius-semilinear, then
`F - 1` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem frobeniusSemilinear_sub_id_surjective
    {p : ℕ} (k : Type*) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    (V : Type*) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V]
    (F : V →+ V) (hF : ∀ (a : k) (v : V), F (a • v) = a ^ p • F v) :
    Function.Surjective (fun v ↦ F v - v)
declarations.comment: surjectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteDimensional_cohomologyOverField_of_finiteType_of_dimension_zero
declarations.doc:
For `X` of finite type over a field `k` with `dim(X) = 0` and `ℱ` coherent, every
`Hⁿ(X, ℱ)` is a finite-dimensional `k`-vector space.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_cohomologyOverField_of_finiteType_of_dimension_zero
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) = 0)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (n : ℕ) :
    FiniteDimensional k (cohomologyOverField k f F n)
declarations.comment: the case `dim X = 0`, in every degree and without the separatedness hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteDimensional_topCohomology_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an affine scheme separated and of finite type over a field `k`, let `ℱ` be a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `d = dim(X)`. Then `H^d(X, ℱ)` is a finite-dimensional `k`-vector
space.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_topCohomology_of_isAffine [IsAffine X] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (d : ℕ)
    (hd : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    FiniteDimensional k (cohomologyOverField k f F d)
declarations.comment: the case of an affine `X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteDimensional_cohomologyOverField_topologicalKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3M].** Let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type over a field `k` and let
`ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then `dim_k H^d(X, ℱ) < ∞`, where `d = dim(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_cohomologyOverField_topologicalKrullDim (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [IsSeparated f] (F : X.Modules) (hF : _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    FiniteDimensional k (cohomologyOverField k f F d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeFiniteness.finiteDimensional_topCohomology_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type over a field `k`, let `ℱ` be a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module and let `d = dim(X)`. Then `H^d(X, ℱ)` is a finite-dimensional `k`-vector space.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_topCohomology_of_isSeparated {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    FiniteDimensional k (cohomologyOverField k f F d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteDimensional_topCohomology_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3M].** Let `X` be a separated scheme of finite type over a field `k`, with
structure morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec k`, let `ℱ` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `d = dim(X)`.
Then `H^d(X, ℱ)` is a finite-dimensional `k`-vector space.

Nagata's compactification theorem ([Stacks, Tag 0F41],
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasCompactification_of_compactSpace_quasiSeparatedSpace`, applied over the
affine base `Spec k`) factors `f` as a quasi-compact open immersion followed by a proper
morphism, and `finiteDimensional_cohomologyOverField_of_isImmersion_of_isProper` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteDimensional_topCohomology_of_isSeparated {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    FiniteDimensional k (cohomologyOverField k f F d)
declarations.comment: the full statement: for X separated and of finite type over a field k, F a coherent O_X-module and d = dim X, the k-vector space H^d(X, F) is finite-dimensional

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.subsingleton_etaleH_constantZMod_of_isAlgClosed_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be separated and of finite type over an algebraically closed field `k` of
characteristic `p > 0`, and let `d` be a natural number with `dim X ≤ d`. Then

public theorem subsingleton_etaleH_constantZMod_of_isAlgClosed_unconditional {p : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p)

    [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] [IsSeparated f]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    (d : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : d + 1 ≤ q) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H.{w, u + 1} (etaleConstantZMod X p) q)

Let `X` be a scheme proper over an algebraically closed field `k` of characteristic `p > 0`.

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.bijective_etaleCohomologyBaseChangeMap_constantZMod
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be proper over an algebraically closed field `k` of characteristic `p > 0`, and let
`k'/k` be an extension of algebraically closed fields. Then the restriction map
`H ^ q (X_étale, 𝐙/p𝐙) ⟶ H ^ q (X_{k'}, 𝐙/p𝐙)` to the scalar extension
`X_{k'} = X ×_{Spec k} Spec k'` is bijective.

public theorem bijective_etaleCohomologyBaseChangeMap_constantZMod {p : ℕ} (hp : 0 < p)

    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (scalarExtension k k' f).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    (q : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective
      (etaleCohomologyBaseChangeMap.{u, 0, w} k k' f (etaleConstantZMod X p) q)
declarations.comment: part (2): restriction to the scalar extension X_{k'} is bijective on H^q(X_et, Z/pZ)

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.finite_etaleH_constantZMod_of_isProper_of_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3P] (1).** Let `X` be a proper scheme over an algebraically closed field `k`
of characteristic `p > 0`. Then `H ^ q (X_étale, 𝐙/p𝐙)` is finite for every `q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_etaleH_constantZMod_of_isProper_of_isAlgClosed {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharP k p] {X : Scheme.{u}}

declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.bijective_etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_constantZMod
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3P] (2).** Let `k ⊆ k'` be an extension of algebraically closed fields of
characteristic `p > 0` and let `X` be a proper scheme over `k`. Then restriction along
`X_{k'} ⟶ X` is bijective on `H^q(X_étale, 𝐙/p𝐙)` for every `q`.

The target of the restriction map is the cohomology of the inverse image of the constant sheaf,
which is the constant sheaf `𝐙/p𝐙` on `X_{k'}` by
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleAbelianInverseImageConstantIso`.

    Function.Bijective (etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap.{u, 0, w} (scalarExtensionFst k k' f)
      (etaleConstantZMod X p) q)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.curveStatements_extensionByZero_constantSheaf_of_prime
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Lemma 0A3Q.** In Situation 0A52 — `k` algebraically closed, `X` separated,
of finite type and of dimension at most one over `k` — assume `X` is reduced. Let `j : U → X` be
an open immersion, `ℓ` a prime, and `F = j_! 𝐙/ℓ𝐙` the extension by zero of the constant sheaf
on `U_étale` with value any abelian group `E` cyclic of order `ℓ`. Then statements (1) -- (8) of
Situation 0A52 hold for `F`, in the sense of `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.CurveStatements`, at every
coefficient universe and every `Ext` universe.

The sheaf `F` is killed by `ℓ`, hence torsion, so this is the reduction theorem
`curveStatements_of_torsionSheafProperty_max` applied with Lemma 0A5B on smooth curves
(`curveStatementsConstantOnSmoothCurves_of_prime`).
declarations.statement:
theorem curveStatements_extensionByZero_constantSheaf_of_prime {k : Type u} [Field k]
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X U : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSeparated π]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType π] [QuasiCompact π] [IsReduced X] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (E : AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (hE : Nonempty (E ≃+ ZMod ℓ))
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})] :
    CurveStatements.{u, v, w} π ((extensionByZero.{u, v} j).obj
      ((constantSheaf U.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj E))

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_primeToEll_finiteEtale_constantFiltration_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A3R.** Let `S` be a connected scheme, let `ℓ` be a prime number and
let `F` be a finite type locally constant sheaf of `F_ℓ`-vector spaces on `S_étale`. Then there
is a finite étale morphism `f : T → S` of degree prime to `ℓ` such that `f⁻¹F` has a finite
filtration whose successive quotients are the constant sheaf `Z/ℓZ_T`.

The filtration is a chain of subobjects of `f⁻¹F` running from the zero subobject to the whole
sheaf, each step having the constant sheaf as its quotient. The local constancy of `F` enters
through the dictionary of Tag 0DV5 (3), which is
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.nonempty_fundamentalGroupFGModuleDictionary`.

The dictionary is read at a geometric point, which the statement does not mention: a connected
space is nonempty, and `AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricPoint.ofPoint` puts a geometric point of `S`
above any of its points, so one is produced inside the proof rather than assumed. `NeZero ℓ`,
which the dictionary needs for the finiteness of `F_ℓ[K]`, comes from the primality of `ℓ`
likewise.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_primeToEll_finiteEtale_constantFiltration_unconditional {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime)
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace S]
    (F : Sheaf (smallEtaleTopology S) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) v} (ZMod ℓ)))
    (_hF : Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant (ZMod ℓ) (smallEtaleTopology S) F) :
    ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (d : ℕ), IsFinite f ∧ Etale f ∧
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d ∧ ¬ ℓ ∣ d ∧
      ∃ X : RelSeries (ConstantRankOneStep ℓ ((smallEtalePullbackZMod ℓ f).obj F)),
        IsZero (Subobject.underlying.obj X.head) ∧ IsIso X.last.arrow

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.exists_primeToEll_finiteEtale_relSeries_constantRankOneStep
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A3R.** Let `S` be a connected scheme, `ℓ` a prime number and `F` a
finite type locally constant sheaf of `F_ℓ`-vector spaces on `S_étale`. Then there is a finite
étale morphism `f : T → S` of degree prime to `ℓ` such that `f⁻¹F` has a finite filtration
whose successive quotients are isomorphic to `Z/ℓZ_T`.

The filtration is a chain of subobjects of `f⁻¹F` running from the zero subobject to the whole
sheaf, each step having the constant sheaf `Z/ℓZ_T` as its quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_primeToEll_finiteEtale_relSeries_constantRankOneStep {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime)
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace S]
    (F : Sheaf S.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ZMod ℓ)))
    (hF : IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant (ZMod ℓ) S.smallEtaleTopology F) :
    ∃ (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (d : ℕ), IsFinite f ∧ Etale f ∧
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank f d ∧ ¬ ℓ ∣ d ∧
      ∃ X : RelSeries (ConstantRankOneStep.{0} ℓ ((smallEtalePullbackZMod.{0} ℓ f).obj F)),
        IsZero (Subobject.underlying.obj X.head) ∧ IsIso X.last.arrow

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_globalSectionsComparison_closedFibre_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3S].** Let `A` be a henselian local ring, let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be proper
and let `X₀ = X ×_{Spec A} Spec κ(A)` be the fibre of `f` over the closed point. For every sheaf of
sets `ℱ` on the small étale site of `X`, `Γ(X, ℱ) = Γ(X₀, ℱ|_{X₀})`: the canonical comparison of
global sections along the inclusion of `X₀`, natural in `ℱ`, is an isomorphism.

This is [Stacks, Tag 0A0C] for the henselian pair `(A, 𝔪)`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.bijective_globalSectionsComparison_app_closedFibre_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A3S], sheaf by sheaf.** Let `A` be a henselian local ring, let
`f : X ⟶ Spec A` be proper and let `X₀ = X ×_{Spec A} Spec κ(A)` be the fibre over the closed
point. For every sheaf of sets `ℱ` on the small étale site of `X`, restriction of global sections
`Γ(X, ℱ) ⟶ Γ(X₀, ℱ|_{X₀})` is bijective. This is the component at `ℱ` of
`isIso_globalSectionsComparison_closedFibre_of_isProper`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_globalSectionsComparison_app_closedFibre_of_isProper
    [HenselianLocalRing A] (F : Sheaf (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology X) (Type (max (u + 1) v))) :
    Function.Bijective ((globalSectionsSmallEtaleInverseImageComparison.{u, v}
      (closedFibreInclusion A f)).val.app F)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.isIso_properGeometricFibreComparison_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A3T.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be proper and `x : Spec Ω ⟶ S` a geometric
point (`Ω` separably closed). For every sheaf of sets `F` on `X_étale` the canonical map
`(f_* F)_x ⟶ Γ(X_x, F_x)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_properGeometricFibreComparison_of_isProper
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω]
    (x : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) :
    IsIso (properGeometricFibreComparison.{u, 0} f x)
declarations.comment: for every sheaf of sets on the small étale site of `X`, naturally in the sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A3V.** The dimensions of the fibres of a finite-type morphism to a
quasi-compact scheme are bounded by a single natural number.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_topologicalKrullDim_fiber_le
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [CompactSpace Y] :
    ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ y : Y, topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber y) ≤ n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.valuativeCriterion_existence_iff_lift_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**For a separated morphism of algebraic spaces, allowing a dominating extension of the
valuation ring does not change the existence half of the valuative criterion**: the criterion
holds exactly when every valuative square already has a lift over the original valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem valuativeCriterion_existence_iff_lift_of_isSeparated
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Existence f ↔ ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, Nonempty q.Lift

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.valuativeCriterion_existence_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_universallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3X, part (1).** A quasi-separated universally closed morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` satisfies the existence part of the valuative criterion.

A valuative square for `f` presents the generic point of its valuation ring `A` as a point of
the base change `P = X ×_Y Spec A`, through a section `g : Spec K ⟶ P`. Quasi-separatedness of
`P ⟶ Spec A` makes `g` quasi-compact (Stacks 03KS), the morphism `Spec K ⟶ Spec A` being
affine, so the points of the scheme-theoretic image `Z ⊆ P` of `g` are the closure of the
image of `g` (Stacks 082Z). Universal closedness makes the image of that closed set in
`|Spec A|` closed, and it contains the generic point, hence everything; so some point of `|Z|`
lies over the closed point of `Spec A`. Stacks 089B realizes that point by a valuation ring
`A'` with fraction field `K'` and a square `Spec K' ⟶ Spec K`, `Spec A' ⟶ Z`; composing with
`Z ⟶ P ⟶ X` gives the lift, and `A'` dominates `A` because the closed point of `Spec A'` maps
to the closed point of `Spec A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuativeCriterion_existence_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_universallyClosed
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) (huc : UniversallyClosed B S hS f) :
    ValuativeCriterion.Existence f
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_iff_valuativeCriterion_existence_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A3X, part (2).** A quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` is universally closed exactly when it satisfies the existence part of the valuative
criterion.

One direction is Stacks 03KA, the other is part (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_iff_valuativeCriterion_existence_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    UniversallyClosed B S hS f ↔ ValuativeCriterion.Existence f
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.universallyClosed_tfae_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact separated morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S`, universal
closedness, the existence part of the valuative criterion of Stacks 03IX, and the existence of a
lift in every valuative square for `f` over the valuation ring itself are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem universallyClosed_tfae_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [UniversallyClosed B S hS f,
        ValuativeCriterion.Existence f,
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, Nonempty q.Lift]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSeparated_and_universallyClosed_tfae_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S`,
being separated and universally closed, satisfying the valuative criterion of Stacks 03IX, and
having exactly one dotted arrow in every valuative square over the given valuation ring are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSeparated_and_universallyClosed_tfae_of_isQuasiCompact_of_isQuasiSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsSeparated B S hS f ∧ UniversallyClosed B S hS f,
        ValuativeCriterion f,
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, Nonempty q.Lift ∧ Subsingleton q.Lift]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_tfae_of_isFiniteType_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S` which is of finite type and
quasi-separated, being proper, satisfying the valuative criterion of Stacks 03IX, and having
exactly one dotted arrow in every valuative square over the given valuation ring are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProper_tfae_of_isFiniteType_of_isQuasiSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsProper B S hS f,
        ValuativeCriterion f,
        ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, Nonempty q.Lift ∧ Subsingleton q.Lift]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_iff_valuativeCriterion_of_isFiniteType_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is of finite type and quasi-separated is proper
exactly when it satisfies the valuative criterion of Stacks 03IX.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProper_iff_valuativeCriterion_of_isFiniteType_of_isQuasiSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsProper B S hS f ↔ ValuativeCriterion f
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isProper_iff_forall_unique_lift_of_isFiniteType_of_isQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is of finite type and quasi-separated is proper
exactly when every valuative square for it has exactly one dotted arrow over the given valuation
ring, which is the valuative criterion of Schemes, Stacks 01KD.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isProper_iff_forall_unique_lift_of_isFiniteType_of_isQuasiSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsProper B S hS f ↔ ∀ q : ValuativeSquare f, Nonempty q.Lift ∧ Subsingleton q.Lift
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: exists_filteredColimit_henselianLocalGRing
declarations.doc:
A henselian local ring is a filtered colimit of henselian local G-rings
with local transition maps.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_filteredColimit_henselianLocalGRing
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A] :
    ∃ (J : Type u) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsFiltered J)
      (F : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) (c : Cocone F) (_ : IsColimit c),
      (∀ j, HenselianLocalRing (F.obj j) ∧ IsGRing (F.obj j)) ∧
        (∀ ⦃i j⦄ (f : i ⟶ j), IsLocalHom (F.map f).hom) ∧
        Nonempty (c.pt ≅ CommRingCat.of A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_algebraization_adicBaseChangeMap_holds
declarations.doc:
**Algebraization of a compatible system of morphisms over the adic thickenings.** Let `A` be a
Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, write `S = Spec A` and `Sₙ = Spec (A / Iⁿ)`,
and let `fX : X ⟶ S` be proper and `fY : Y ⟶ S` separated of finite type. A compatible system of
morphisms `gₙ : Xₙ ⟶ Yₙ` over `Sₙ` comes from a unique morphism `g : X ⟶ Y` over `S` whose base
change to each `Sₙ` is `gₙ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_algebraization_adicBaseChangeMap_holds
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (hcomplete : IsAdicComplete I A) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (fX : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) (fY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [IsProper fX] [IsSeparated fY] [LocallyOfFiniteType fY] [QuasiCompact fY]
    (g : ∀ n, adicBaseChange A I fX n ⟶ adicBaseChange A I fY n)
    (g_over : ∀ n, g n ≫ pullback.snd fY (adicThickeningι A I n) =
      pullback.snd fX (adicThickeningι A I n))
    (g_compatible : ∀ n, adicBaseChangeSucc A I fX n ≫ g (n + 1) =
      g n ≫ adicBaseChangeSucc A I fY n) :
    ∃! algebraization : {h : X ⟶ Y // h ≫ fY = fX},
      ∀ n, adicBaseChangeMap A I algebraization.1 algebraization.2 n = g n
declarations.comment: at the source's hypotheses and with no further input: A Noetherian and I-adically complete, fX : X -> Spec A proper (source hypothesis 1), fY : Y -> Spec A separated of finite type (source hypothesis 2), and a compatible system of morphisms over the adic thickenings, concluding that it comes from a unique morphism X -> Y over Spec A. The halg and hrig binders of AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_algebraization_adicBaseChangeMap are discharged here, by AlgebraicGeometry.adicFiniteAlgebraization_holds and Stacks.AdicClosedSubschemeRigidity.adicRigidity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smoothAt_of_smooth_infinitesimalNeighbourhoods
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism locally of finite type to a locally Noetherian scheme and let
`i : Z ⟶ S` be a closed subscheme. If the base change `Xₙ = Zₙ ×_S X ⟶ Zₙ` of `f` to the `n`th
infinitesimal neighbourhood of `Z` is smooth for every `n`, then `f` is smooth at every point of
`f⁻¹(Z)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smoothAt_of_smooth_infinitesimalNeighbourhoods
    {X S Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hsmooth : ∀ n : ℕ, Smooth (pullback.snd f (Stacks.Thickenings.nthOrderToBase i n)))
    (x : X) (hx : f x ∈ Set.range i) :
    InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt f x
declarations.comment: smooth

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_etale_infinitesimalNeighbourhoods
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism locally of finite type to a locally Noetherian scheme and let
`i : Z ⟶ S` be a closed subscheme. If the base change `Xₙ = Zₙ ×_S X ⟶ Zₙ` of `f` to the `n`th
infinitesimal neighbourhood of `Z` is étale for every `n`, then `f` is étale at every point of
`f⁻¹(Z)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem etaleAt_of_etale_infinitesimalNeighbourhoods
    {X S Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (f : X ⟶ S) (i : Z ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hetale : ∀ n : ℕ, Etale (pullback.snd f (Stacks.Thickenings.nthOrderToBase i n)))
    (x : X) (hx : f x ∈ Set.range i) :
    EtaleAt f x
declarations.comment: etale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mono_supportedSectionsPushforwardInclusion_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A45.** The sections with support in the closed subscheme include into an abelian
sheaf: the first map of the sequence `0 ⟶ i_*ℋ_Z(F) ⟶ F ⟶ j_*(F|_U)` is a monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mono_supportedSectionsPushforwardInclusion_app
    (F : SmallEtaleAbelianSheaf B X) :
    Mono ((supportedSectionsPushforwardInclusion B i).app F)
declarations.comment: exactness of 0 ⟶ i_*ℋ_Z(F) ⟶ F ⟶ j_*(F|_U): the first map is a monomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedSectionsShortComplex_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A45.** The sequence `0 ⟶ i_*ℋ_Z(F) ⟶ F ⟶ j_*(F|_U)` is exact at `F`: a section
restricting to zero on the open complement has support in the closed subscheme.  Together with
`mono_supportedSectionsPushforwardInclusion_app` this is the exactness of that sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem supportedSectionsShortComplex_exact (F : SmallEtaleAbelianSheaf B X) :
    (supportedSectionsShortComplex B i F).Exact
declarations.comment: exactness of 0 ⟶ i_*ℋ_Z(F) ⟶ F ⟶ j_*(F|_U): exactness at F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyWithSupportSequences
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A45.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of schemes and let `j : U ⟶ X` be
the inclusion of the complement of `Z`.  For an abelian sheaf `F` on `X_étale` there is a
distinguished triangle

`i_*Rℋ_Z(F) ⟶ F ⟶ Rj_*(F|_U) ⟶ i_*Rℋ_Z(F)⟦1⟧`

in `D(X_étale)`, hence a four-term exact sequence

`0 ⟶ i_*ℋ_Z(F) ⟶ F ⟶ j_*(F|_U) ⟶ i_*ℋ¹_Z(F) ⟶ 0`

and isomorphisms `R^p j_*(F|_U) ≅ i_*ℋ^{p+1}_Z(F)` for `p ≥ 1`.

All three assertions are stated at once, as the three fields of
`AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologyWithSupportSequences`.  The triangle is given for an arbitrary
triple of right derived functors of `i_*ℋ_Z`, of the identity and of `j_*(-|_U)` on the whole
unbounded derived category, so it applies to every model of `i_*Rℋ_Z` and `Rj_*(-|_U)` and is
functorial in the object; the other two assertions are given at every abelian sheaf, naturally
in it.  The open complement `U` and its inclusion `j` are constructed from `i` rather than
assumed.

`R^p` is Mathlib's `ℕ`-indexed `CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerived`; the comparison with the
`ℤ`-indexed `CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedPlus` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_rightDerivedPlus_supportedSections_pushforward` ([Stacks, Tag 09XR])
is `Stacks.DerivedIndexing.rightDerivedIso`.
declarations.statement: public def cohomologyWithSupportSequences : CohomologyWithSupportSequences B i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedCohomologyEtaleIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A46, clause (1).**  For a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` and a closed subset `Z`
of a scheme `X`, cohomology with support in `Z` of the associated sheaf `Fᵃ` on the small étale
site of `X` agrees, in every degree, with cohomology with support in `Z` of `F` on the small
Zariski site.

Both sides are right derived functors of the functor of global sections vanishing on the open
complement of `Z`, taken on the respective site.  There is no hypothesis beyond those of the
source: the vanishing of the higher direct images `R^nε_*(Fᵃ)` for `n > 0` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_rightDerived_pushforward_opensToEtale` and the identification of
`ε_*(Fᵃ)` with `F` is `AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleSectionsUnitIso`, those two being the two
halves of Stacks 03P2 for `𝒞 = X_étale`.
declarations.statement:
public def supportedCohomologyEtaleIso (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (q : ℕ) :
    ((smallEtaleSectionsWithSupport X Z hZ).rightDerived q).obj
        (smallEtaleAssociatedSheaf X F) ≅
      ((SmallEtale.zariskiSectionsWithSupport X Z hZ).rightDerived q).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf X.ringCatSheaf).obj F)
declarations.comment: clause (1): cohomology with support in a closed subset agrees between the small etale site and the Zariski site, for a quasi-coherent module, in every degree, with no hypothesis beyond the source's. Clause (2) is supportedCohomology_isQuasicoherent_and_associatedSheaf, on the size-bounded small etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedCohomology_isQuasicoherent_and_associatedSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion whose open complement is retrocompact in `X`, and let
`𝓕` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  Then for every `q` the Zariski sheaf `i_*ℋ^q_Z(𝓕)` is a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, and the étale sheaf `i_*ℋ^q_Z(𝓕ᵃ)` is its associated sheaf
`(i_*ℋ^q_Z(𝓕))ᵃ`.

The étale `i_*ℋ^q_Z` is the library's, on abelian sheaves of the small étale site with
coefficients in the universe after that of the schemes, and `𝓕ᵃ` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleOfSheaf`, read as an abelian sheaf and then by the
universe lift, which is fully faithful and exact; see the implementation notes.  The first half
is [Stacks, Tag 0G7G] (1) in one degree, the second
`AlgebraicGeometry.supportedCohomologyAssociatedSheafIso`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem supportedCohomology_isQuasicoherent_and_associatedSheaf
    (hU : IsRetrocompact (Set.range (B.inclusion.map i).base)ᶜ) (𝓕 : X.obj.Modules)
    [𝓕.IsQuasicoherent] (q : ℕ) :
    (((supportedSectionsFunctor X.obj.toRingedSpace
        (Set.range (B.inclusion.map i).base)).rightDerived q).obj 𝓕).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      Nonempty (((supportedSectionsPushforward B i).rightDerived q).obj
          ((Stacks.Sheaves.UniverseLift.uliftSheafFunctor.{u + 1, u}
            (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} (SmallEtale.structureSheaf B X.obj X.property)).obj
              ((SmallEtale.associatedModuleOfSheaf B X.obj X.property).obj 𝓕))) ≅
        (Stacks.Sheaves.UniverseLift.uliftSheafFunctor.{u + 1, u}
          (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)).obj
          ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} (SmallEtale.structureSheaf B X.obj X.property)).obj
            ((SmallEtale.associatedModuleOfSheaf B X.obj X.property).obj
              (((supportedSectionsFunctor X.obj.toRingedSpace
                (Set.range (B.inclusion.map i).base)).rightDerived q).obj 𝓕))))
declarations.comment: clause (2): for a closed immersion with retrocompact open complement and a quasi-coherent module F, i_*H^q_Z(F) is quasi-coherent and i_*H^q_Z(F^a) = (i_*H^q_Z(F))^a on the small etale site, for every q

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.exact_affineLineBoundary
declarations.doc:
**The exact sequence `k[x] ⟶ k[x] ⟶ H¹(𝐀¹_k, 𝐙/p𝐙) ⟶ 0`.** Let `k` be a field of
characteristic `p > 0`. The boundary of the Artin–Schreier sequence on the affine line is onto
`H¹(𝐀¹_k, 𝐙/p𝐙)` and its kernel is the image of `f ↦ f ^ p - f`.

The source states this for `k` algebraically closed; only the characteristic of `k` is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_affineLineBoundary :
    Function.Exact (ringArtinSchreier k[X] p) (affineLineBoundary.{w} k p) ∧
      Function.Surjective (affineLineBoundary.{w} k p)
declarations.comment: the exact sequence k[x] → k[x] → H¹(A¹_k, Z/p) → 0, first arrow f ↦ f^p - f

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.existsUnique_affineLineBoundary_eq
declarations.doc:
**The representatives, read in cohomology.** Let `k` be an algebraically closed field of
characteristic `p > 0`. Every class in `H¹(𝐀¹_k, 𝐙/p𝐙)` is the boundary of exactly one polynomial
`∑_{p ∤ n} λₙ xⁿ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_affineLineBoundary_eq [IsAlgClosed k]
    (c : Sheaf.H.{w} (etaleConstantZMod (affineLine k) p) 1) :
    ∃! f : k[X], (∀ n, p ∣ n → f.coeff n = 0) ∧ affineLineBoundary.{w} k p f = c
declarations.comment: every class of H¹(A¹_k, Z/p) is the image of exactly one sum over p ∤ n of λ_n x^n

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.not_surjective_etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_affineLine
declarations.doc:
**`H¹(𝐀¹_k, 𝐙/p𝐙) → H¹(𝐀¹_{k'}, 𝐙/p𝐙)` is not surjective.** Let `k` be an algebraically closed
field of characteristic `p > 0` and `k'/k` an extension with `k' ≠ k`. Then the restriction map
`H¹(𝐀¹_k, 𝐙/p𝐙) → H¹(𝐀¹_{k'}, 𝐙/p𝐙)` along `𝐀¹_{k'} ⟶ 𝐀¹_k` is not surjective — in particular not
an isomorphism: for `λ ∈ k' ∖ k` the class of `λ x` is not in its image.

The source takes `k'` algebraically closed; that is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_surjective_etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_affineLine [IsAlgClosed k]
    (hk : ¬ Function.Surjective (algebraMap k k'))
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (affineLine k).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (scalarExtension k k' (affineLineStructure k)).smallEtaleTopology
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})] :
    ¬ Function.Surjective (etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap.{u, 0, w}
      (scalarExtensionFst k k' (affineLineStructure k))
      (etaleConstantZMod (affineLine k) p) 1)
declarations.comment: H¹(A¹_k, Z/p) → H¹(A¹_{k'}, Z/p) is not surjective when k ⊊ k'

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.exists_not_bijective_etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_affineLine
declarations.doc:
**The restriction map is not an isomorphism in general.** For every algebraically closed field
`k` of characteristic `p > 0` there is an algebraically closed extension `k'/k` — an algebraic
closure of `k(t)` — for which `H¹(𝐀¹_k, 𝐙/p𝐙) → H¹(𝐀¹_{k'}, 𝐙/p𝐙)` is not an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_bijective_etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_affineLine [IsAlgClosed k] :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k') (_ : IsAlgClosed k'),
      ∀ [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (affineLine k).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
        [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (scalarExtension k k' (affineLineStructure k)).smallEtaleTopology
          AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})],
        ¬ Function.Bijective (etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap.{u, 0, w}
          (scalarExtensionFst k k' (affineLineStructure k))
          (etaleConstantZMod (affineLine k) p) 1)
declarations.comment: so H¹(A¹_k, Z/p) → H¹(A¹_{k'}, Z/p) is not an isomorphism in general

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.bijective_etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_affineLine_of_isUnit
declarations.doc:
**The phenomenon only occurs with `p`-power torsion coefficients.** Let `k'/k` be an
extension of algebraically closed fields and let `n` be invertible in `k`. Then
`H^q(𝐀¹_k, 𝐙/n𝐙) → H^q(𝐀¹_{k'}, 𝐙/n𝐙)` is bijective in every degree `q`: this is statement (6)
of Situation 0A52 (Tag 0A58) for the affine line. In characteristic `0` every `n ≥ 1` is
invertible, so the base change map is an isomorphism for every finite cyclic coefficient group.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_affineLine_of_isUnit {n : ℕ} (hn : IsUnit (n : k))
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (affineLine k).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf (scalarExtension k k' (affineLineStructure k)).smallEtaleTopology
      AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})] (q : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap.{u, v, w}
      (scalarExtensionFst k k' (affineLineStructure k))
      ((constantSheaf (affineLine k).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj
        (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{max (u + 1) v} (ZMod n)))) q)
declarations.comment: only in characteristic p with p-power torsion: bijective for Z/n, n invertible in k

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.not_bijective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_affineLine
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A47]: `π₁(𝐀¹_{k'}) → π₁(𝐀¹_k)` is not an isomorphism.** Let `k'/k` be an
extension of algebraically closed fields of characteristic `p > 0` with `k' ≠ k`. Then for every
geometric point `x` of `𝐀¹_{k'}` the map of étale fundamental groups
`π₁(𝐀¹_{k'}, x) → π₁(𝐀¹_k, x)` induced by `𝐀¹_{k'} ⟶ 𝐀¹_k` is not bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_bijective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_affineLine {p : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    [IsAlgClosed k] [IsAlgClosed k'] (hk : ¬ Function.Surjective (algebraMap k k'))
    (x : GeometricPoint (scalarExtension k k' (affineLineStructure k))) :
    ¬ Function.Bijective
      (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (scalarExtensionFst k k' (affineLineStructure k)) x)
declarations.comment: π₁(A¹_{k'}) → π₁(A¹_k) is not an isomorphism for algebraically closed k ⊊ k'

declarations.name: Stacks.ArtinSchreier.exists_not_bijective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_affineLine
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A47]: the étale fundamental group of the affine line depends on the
algebraically closed ground field.** For every algebraically closed field `k` of characteristic
`p > 0` there is an algebraically closed extension `k'/k` — an algebraic closure of `k(t)` — for
which `π₁(𝐀¹_{k'}, x) → π₁(𝐀¹_k, x)` is not bijective at any geometric point `x`.

The source concludes that the étale homotopy type of the affine line depends on the algebraically
closed ground field; the étale homotopy type is not available here, and this statement, with
`Stacks.ArtinSchreier.exists_not_bijective_etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_affineLine` for `H¹`, is
the content of that conclusion for the invariants `π₁` and `H¹` of the homotopy type.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_bijective_etaleFundamentalGroupMap_affineLine {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime]
    [CharP k p] [IsAlgClosed k] :
    ∃ (k' : Type u) (_ : Field k') (_ : Algebra k k') (_ : IsAlgClosed k'),
      ∀ x : GeometricPoint (scalarExtension k k' (affineLineStructure k)),
        ¬ Function.Bijective
          (etaleFundamentalGroupMap (scalarExtensionFst k k' (affineLineStructure k)) x)
declarations.comment: so the étale fundamental group of A¹ depends on the algebraically closed field

declarations.name: Polynomial.existsUnique_sub_mem_range_ringArtinSchreier
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A47], the representatives of the cokernel.** Let `k` be an algebraically
closed field of characteristic `p > 0`. Every polynomial `g ∈ k[x]` is congruent modulo the image
of `f ↦ f ^ p - f` to exactly one polynomial `∑_{p ∤ n} λₙ xⁿ`, that is, to exactly one
polynomial with no coefficient in a degree divisible by `p` (the degree `0` included). In other
words these polynomials form a set of representatives for the cokernel of
`k[x] → k[x], f ↦ f ^ p - f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_sub_mem_range_ringArtinSchreier [IsAlgClosed k] (g : k[X]) :
    ∃! f : k[X], (∀ n, p ∣ n → f.coeff n = 0) ∧
      g - f ∈ (ringArtinSchreier k[X] p).range
declarations.comment: the polynomials sum over p ∤ n of λ_n x^n represent the cokernel of f ↦ f^p - f

declarations.name: Polynomial.exists_sub_mem_range_ringArtinSchreier_of_perfectRing
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A47], the parenthetical case of a field that is not algebraically closed.**
Let `k` be a perfect field of characteristic `p > 0`. Then the representatives of the cokernel of
`f ↦ f ^ p - f` on `k[x]` need constants added: every `g ∈ k[x]` is congruent to a polynomial
`∑_{p ∤ n} λₙ xⁿ + c`, and two such polynomials are congruent exactly when their coefficients
`λₙ` agree and their constant terms differ by a value `a ^ p - a` of `k`. So the constants needed
are a set of representatives of `k / {a ^ p - a}`, which is zero for algebraically closed `k`.

The source says "if `k` is not algebraically closed"; perfectness is needed and is assumed here:
over an imperfect field the description fails, by
`Polynomial.not_exists_sub_mem_range_ringArtinSchreier_of_not_pth_power`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sub_mem_range_ringArtinSchreier_of_perfectRing [PerfectRing k p] :
    (∀ g : k[X], ∃ f : k[X], (∀ n, 0 < n → p ∣ n → f.coeff n = 0) ∧
      g - f ∈ (ringArtinSchreier k[X] p).range) ∧
    ∀ f f' : k[X], (∀ n, 0 < n → p ∣ n → f.coeff n = 0) →
      (∀ n, 0 < n → p ∣ n → f'.coeff n = 0) →
      (f - f' ∈ (ringArtinSchreier k[X] p).range ↔
        (∀ n, n ≠ 0 → f.coeff n = f'.coeff n) ∧
          f.coeff 0 - f'.coeff 0 ∈ (ringArtinSchreier k p).range)
declarations.comment: if k is not algebraically closed, constants have to be added (k perfect)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isFinite_of_henselianLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0A48 for a finite morphism.** If `A` is a henselian local ring and `f : X ⟶ Spec A` is
finite, then base change to the closed fibre `X ×_{Spec A} Spec (A ⧸ 𝔪) ⟶ X` is an equivalence on
finite étale covers.

A henselian local ring forms a henselian pair with its maximal ideal
(`henselianPair_maximalIdeal`), so this is the case `I = 𝔪` of
`isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isFinite_of_henselianPair`. As there, no algebraization
is used: the general proper case of Tag 0A48 needs Grothendieck existence together with Artin
approximation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isFinite_of_henselianLocalRing
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsFinite f] :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange (pullback.fst f
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)))))).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: for a finite morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec A`, which is the case of a proper `f` in which no algebraization is needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isProper_of_henselianLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A48.** Let `A` be a henselian local ring and `X` a proper scheme over
`A` with closed fibre `X₀ = X ×_{Spec A} Spec (A ⧸ 𝔪)`. Then base change
`FÉt_X ⥤ FÉt_{X₀}, U ↦ U ×_X X₀` is an equivalence of categories.

The three stages of the source's proof are composed by
`properHenselianFiniteEtaleEquivalence_of_adicFiniteAlgebraAlgebraization`; its one input,
Grothendieck existence for finite sheaves of algebras over a proper scheme over a complete local
Noetherian ring, is `adicFiniteAlgebraAlgebraization_of_isProper` (from Stacks 088C).
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isProper_of_henselianLocalRing
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A))
    [IsProper f] :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange (pullback.fst f
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (maximalIdeal A)))))).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_specMap_algebraMap_of_isAlgClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A49.** Let `k ⊆ k'` be an extension of algebraically closed fields and
let `f : X ⟶ Spec k` be proper. Then base change along the projection `X_{k'} ⟶ X`, that is
`U ↦ U_{k'}`, is an equivalence between the category of schemes finite étale over `X` and the
category of schemes finite étale over `X_{k'} = X ×_{Spec k} Spec k'`.

This is `isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_specMap_algebraMap_of_properHenselian_of_isAlgClosed`
with Tag 0A48 supplied by `properHenselianFiniteEtaleEquivalence`. The stand-in
`ProperHenselianFiniteEtaleEquivalence` cannot be discharged inside
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FundamentalGroup.FiniteEtaleAlgClosedExtension` itself, since the
module proving it imports that one; this module is where both inputs are supplied.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_specMap_algebraMap_of_isAlgClosed
    {k k' : Type u} [Field k] [Field k'] [Algebra k k'] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsAlgClosed k']
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] :
    (finiteEtaleBaseChange (pullback.fst f
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k'))))).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: Complete, under exactly the source's hypotheses: `k ⊆ k'` algebraically closed, `X` proper over `k`.

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleAbelianSheafDerivedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
The base change map for a single abelian sheaf `F` on `X_étale`, placed in
degree zero: the canonical morphism `g^{-1} Rf_* F ⟶ Rf'_* (g')^{-1} F` in the derived category
of `Y'_étale`, attached to a commutative square `g' ≫ f = f' ≫ g` of schemes. It is the
component of `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.etaleAbelianDerivedBaseChange` at `F[0]`.
declarations.statement:
public def etaleAbelianSheafDerivedBaseChange
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    (etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, v} g).obj
        ((etaleAbelianDerivedDirectImage.{u, v} f).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
            (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) 0).obj F)) ⟶
      (etaleAbelianDerivedDirectImage.{u, v} f').obj
        ((etaleAbelianDerivedInverseImage.{u, v} g').obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
