declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.curveStatements_constantSheaf_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Lemma 0A5B.** In Situation 0A52 — `k` algebraically closed, `X` separated,
of finite type and of dimension at most one over `k` — assume `X` is smooth over `k` and let
`F = 𝐙/ℓ𝐙` be the constant sheaf on `X_étale` for a prime `ℓ`, with value any abelian group `E`
cyclic of order `ℓ`. Then statements (1) -- (8) of Situation 0A52 hold for `F`, in the sense of
`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.CurveStatements`, at every coefficient universe and every `Ext`
universe.

On the smooth curve components of `X` this is `curveStatementsConstantOnSmoothCurves_of_prime`
(Cases I and II of the source); the reduction theorem
`curveStatements_of_torsionSheafProperty_max` carries it to `X` and to the coefficients
`AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}`, the constant sheaf with finite value being torsion.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveStatements_constantSheaf_of_smooth {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsSeparated π] [LocallyOfFiniteType π]
    [QuasiCompact π] [Smooth π] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) {ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime)
    (E : AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) (hE : Nonempty (E ≃+ ZMod ℓ))
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})] :
    CurveStatements.{u, v, w} π
      ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj E)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.CurveStatements.of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
Let `0 → F₁ → F → F₂ → 0` be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on the small étale
site of a Noetherian scheme `X` over a field. If statements (1) -- (8) of Situation 0A52 hold for
`F₁` and `F₂`, then they hold for `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem CurveStatements.of_shortExact (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : CurveStatements.{u, 0, w} π S.X₁) (h₃ : CurveStatements.{u, 0, w} π S.X₃) :
    CurveStatements.{u, 0, w} π S.X₂
declarations.comment: all eight statements of 0A52 at once, at the coefficients AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.curveCohomologyStatements_X₂_of_shortExact_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A5C.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, let `π` be a morphism from `X`
to the spectrum of a field, let `i` be a morphism of schemes to `X`, and let
`0 → S.X₁ → S.X₂ → S.X₃ → 0` be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on the small étale site
of `X`. If the eight statements of Situation 0A52 hold for `S.X₁` and for `S.X₃`, then they hold
for `S.X₂`.

The eight statements, bundled as `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.CurveCohomologyStatements`, are: the
vanishing of `H^q(X, -)` above degree two; its vanishing above degree one over an affine `X`; its
vanishing above degree one for coefficients of `l`-power torsion; the finiteness of `H^q(X, -)`
for constructible coefficients of torsion prime to `p`; its finiteness for constructible
coefficients over a proper `X`; the bijectivity of restriction along `i` for coefficients of
torsion prime to `p`; the bijectivity of restriction along `i` over a proper `X`; and the
surjectivity of restriction along `i` in degree two. In the source `l` and `p` are the
characteristic and the exponential characteristic of the base field, and `i` is the projection of
a scalar extension along an extension of algebraically closed fields in statements (6) and (7)
and the inclusion of an open subscheme in statement (8); none of those identifications is imposed
here, so this statement is stronger than the one the source makes.

Constructibility of an abelian sheaf is `AlgebraicGeometry.IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf`,
read on the small étale site of Stacks 021B across its dense subsite comparison with the site
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.smallEtaleTopology` that carries the cohomology. Its descent to the sub-
and the quotient sheaf of a short exact sequence, which statements (4) and (5) need, is
Proposition 09BH (2) and is what the Noetherian hypothesis is for; the other six transfers use no
hypothesis on `X` at all. Situation 0A52 asks `X` to be separated of finite type over an
algebraically closed field and of dimension at most one, and asks the sheaves to be torsion;
finite type over a field makes `X` Noetherian, and the remaining hypotheses are not used and so do
not appear.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveCohomologyStatements_X₂_of_shortExact_isConstructible [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (π : X.obj ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (l p : ℕ) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : CurveCohomologyStatements.{u, u + 1, w} i π l p
      (IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf B X) S.X₁)
    (h₃ : CurveCohomologyStatements.{u, u + 1, w} i π l p
      (IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf B X) S.X₃) :
    CurveCohomologyStatements.{u, u + 1, w} i π l p
      (IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf B X) S.X₂
declarations.comment: the eight statements of Situation 0A52 pass to the middle term of a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves, with constructibility of the sub- and the quotient sheaf supplied by Proposition 09BH (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.finite_etaleCohomology_X₂_of_shortExact_of_isPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
**Statement (4) of Situation 0A52 passes to extensions, for constructible coefficients.** Let
`X` be a Noetherian scheme, let `p` be a natural number — the characteristic of the base field in
the source — and let `0 → S.X₁ → S.X₂ → S.X₃ → 0` be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on
the small étale site of `X`. If the finiteness of étale cohomology for coefficients that are
constructible and torsion prime to `p` holds for the sub- and the quotient sheaf, then it holds
for the middle sheaf.

This is `finite_etaleCohomology_X₂_of_shortExact_of_isPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion` with the
coefficient condition taken to be constructibility of an abelian sheaf and its descent to the sub-
and the quotient sheaf *discharged*, by Proposition 09BH (2), rather than assumed: that descent is
what Tag 0A5C cites at this point, and it is the only use of the Noetherian hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_etaleCohomology_X₂_of_shortExact_of_isPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion_isConstructible
    [IsNoetherian X.obj] (p : ℕ) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf B X S.X₁ →
      Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion X.obj.smallEtaleTopology p S.X₁ →
      ∀ q : ℕ, Finite (Sheaf.H.{w} S.X₁ q))
    (h₃ : IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf B X S.X₃ →
      Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion X.obj.smallEtaleTopology p S.X₃ →
      ∀ q : ℕ, Finite (Sheaf.H.{w} S.X₃ q))
    (hc : IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf B X S.X₂)
    (ht : Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion X.obj.smallEtaleTopology p S.X₂)
    (q : ℕ) :
    Finite (Sheaf.H.{w} S.X₂ q)
declarations.comment: statement (4): the finiteness of etale cohomology for constructible coefficients of torsion prime to the characteristic passes to the middle term of a short exact sequence, with the constructibility of the sub- and the quotient sheaf supplied by Proposition 09BH (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.finite_etaleCohomology_X₂_of_shortExact_of_isProper_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
**Statement (5) of Situation 0A52 passes to extensions, for constructible coefficients.** Let
`X` be a Noetherian scheme, let `π` be its structure morphism to the spectrum of a field, and let
`0 → S.X₁ → S.X₂ → S.X₃ → 0` be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on the small étale site
of `X`. If the finiteness of étale cohomology for constructible coefficients over a proper `X`
holds for the sub- and the quotient sheaf, then it holds for the middle sheaf.

This is `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.finite_etaleCohomology_X₂_of_shortExact_of_isProper` with the
coefficient condition taken to be constructibility of an abelian sheaf and its descent to the sub-
and the quotient sheaf discharged by Proposition 09BH (2), exactly as in statement (4). The
properness condition constrains the scheme and is passed to the outer terms unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_etaleCohomology_X₂_of_shortExact_of_isProper_isConstructible
    [IsNoetherian X.obj] {k : Type u} [Field k] (π : X.obj ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf B X S.X₁ → IsProper π →
      ∀ q : ℕ, Finite (Sheaf.H.{w} S.X₁ q))
    (h₃ : IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf B X S.X₃ → IsProper π →
      ∀ q : ℕ, Finite (Sheaf.H.{w} S.X₃ q))
    (hc : IsConstructibleEtaleSiteAbelianSheaf B X S.X₂) (hπ : IsProper π) (q : ℕ) :
    Finite (Sheaf.H.{w} S.X₂ q)
declarations.comment: statement (5): the finiteness of etale cohomology for constructible coefficients over a proper scheme passes to the middle term of a short exact sequence, with the constructibility of the sub- and the quotient sheaf supplied by Proposition 09BH (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.CurveStatements.directImage_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Lemma 0A5D.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of schemes over a field
`k`, with `X` Noetherian, and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on `X_étale`. If statements (1) -- (8)
of Situation 0A52 hold for `F`, they hold for `f_* F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem CurveStatements.directImage_of_isFinite [IsNoetherian X]
    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    {F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}}
    (h : CurveStatements.{u, 0, u + 1} (f ≫ π) F) :
    CurveStatements.{u, 0, u + 1} π ((etaleAbelianDirectImage.{u, 0} f).obj F)
declarations.comment: all eight statements of 0A52 at once, at the coefficients AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}; only f finite and X Noetherian are used

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.curveCohomologyStatements_smallEtaleDirectImageAb
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of schemes and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small
étale site of `X`. If the eight statements of Situation 0A52 hold for `F`, relative to the
structure morphism `f ≫ π` of `X` and to restriction along `j`, then they hold for the direct
image `f_* F`, relative to the structure morphism `π` of `Y` and to restriction along `i`.

The input is the comparison `c` of the étale cohomology of `F` with that of `f_* F`, which for a
finite morphism comes from the vanishing of the higher direct images and the Leray spectral
sequence. Beyond it the proof needs that the side conditions of the eight statements move between
the two sheaves. The two conditions on the scheme move by finiteness of `f`: an affine `Y` forces
an affine `X`, and a proper `π` forces a proper `f ≫ π`. The three conditions on the coefficient
sheaf are carried: `hprimePower` and `hprimeToChar` for the two torsion conditions and
`hconstructible` for constructibility, each in the direction from `f_* F` to `F`, which for a
finite morphism holds because the stalks of `f_* F` are the sums of the stalks of `F` over the
fibres.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveCohomologyStatements_smallEtaleDirectImageAb {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (π : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (l p : ℕ) [IsFinite f]
    {constructibleSource : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} → Prop}
    {constructibleTarget : Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} → Prop}
    (c : DirectImageCohomologyComparison.{u, v, w} f i j F)
    (hprimePower : Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimePowerTorsion Y.smallEtaleTopology l
        ((smallEtaleDirectImageAb f).obj F) →
      Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimePowerTorsion X.smallEtaleTopology l F)
    (hprimeToChar : Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion Y.smallEtaleTopology p
        ((smallEtaleDirectImageAb f).obj F) →
      Stacks.Torsion.IsPrimeToCharacteristicTorsion X.smallEtaleTopology p F)
    (hconstructible : constructibleTarget ((smallEtaleDirectImageAb f).obj F) →
      constructibleSource F)
    (h : CurveCohomologyStatements.{u, v, w} j (f ≫ π) l p constructibleSource F) :
    CurveCohomologyStatements.{u, v, w} i π l p constructibleTarget
      ((smallEtaleDirectImageAb f).obj F)
declarations.comment:
the eight statements of Situation 0A52 pass to a finite direct image, over the
Leray comparison and over the transfer of the torsion and constructibility side conditions

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.curveCohomologyAssertions_smallEtaleDirectImageAb
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of schemes of finite type over `k`,
and let `F` be an abelian sheaf on the small étale site of `X`. If statements (1) – (8) of
Situation 0A52 hold for `F`, then they hold for `f_* F`.

Statements (1) – (8) are `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.CurveCohomologyAssertions`, read on `X`
relative to its structure morphism `f ≫ π` and on `Y` relative to `π`, with constructibility read
in a big étale site `B` containing both schemes. The remaining hypotheses of Situation 0A52 —
that `k` is algebraically closed, that `X` and `Y` are separated of dimension at most one, and
that `F` is torsion — are not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveCohomologyAssertions_smallEtaleDirectImageAb (π : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType π] [QuasiCompact π] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsFinite f]
    {F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}}
    (h : CurveCohomologyAssertions B hX (f ≫ π) F) :
    CurveCohomologyAssertions B hY π ((smallEtaleDirectImageAb f).obj F)
declarations.comment: statements (1)-(8) of Situation 0A52 pass to f_* for finite f

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.bijective_etaleConstantCohomologyRestriction_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5G reduced to an `Ext` computation.** Restriction to the closed fibre is bijective
in degree `q` exactly when the étale inverse-image functor along the closed-fibre inclusion is
bijective on `Ext^q` out of the constant sheaf `ℤ`: the two maps differ by composition with the
two canonical constant-sheaf comparison isomorphisms, and composing with an isomorphism is
bijective on `Ext`.

Nothing here is special to a proper morphism over a henselian local ring, and nothing here
computes either side. What Stacks 0A5G asserts is that in degree one the right-hand side holds
when `A` is henselian local, `f` is proper and `M` is finite; that is the geometric content, and
it rests on Stacks 03AJ, 03RV, 0A48 and 0A0C.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_etaleConstantCohomologyRestriction_iff :
    Function.Bijective (etaleConstantCohomologyRestriction.{u, v, w} A f M q) ↔
      Function.Bijective
        ((etaleAbelianInverseImage.{u, v} (closedFibreInclusion A f)).mapExtAddHom.{w, w}
          ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).obj
            (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift ℤ)))
          (etaleConstantSheaf.{u, v} X M) q)
declarations.comment: the reduction of the tag to an Ext computation, in every degree q: the canonical map H^q(X, M) -> H^q(X_0, M) is bijective if and only if etale inverse image along the closed-fibre inclusion is bijective on Ext^q out of the constant sheaf Z. The geometric content of the tag -- that this holds in degree one for a proper morphism over a henselian local ring -- is not proved here. The inputs the source's degree-one argument needs ARE available: Stacks 03AJ as Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.torsorIsoClassesEquivH1, Stacks 03RV as AlgebraicGeometry.finiteLocallyConstantFiniteEtaleEquivalence, and Stacks 0A48 as AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_finiteEtaleBaseChange_of_isProper_of_henselianLocalRing. What is missing is the bridge between them: no result transports an Ext^1 or Sheaf.H map along a CHANGE OF SITE into torsor language -- torsorIsoClassesEquivH1_naturality is naturality in the coefficient sheaf on a fixed site -- and the restriction map here lives on Mathlib's Scheme.smallEtaleTopology while 03RV lives on SmallEtale.topology of a BigEtaleSite, with no comparison. Nor does anything say that a torsor under a finite constant sheaf is finite locally constant

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.bijective_etaleConstantCohomologyRestriction_one_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
For `A` a henselian local ring, `X` proper over `A` and `M` a finite abelian group,
restriction `H¹(X, M) ⟶ H¹(X₀, M)` to the closed fibre is bijective.

Surjectivity is `surjective_etaleConstantCohomologyRestriction_one_of_isProper`. Injectivity
(`Stacks.EtaleCohomology.injective_etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_constantSheaf_one`): a class on
`X` dies on a surjective finite étale cover `π`, hence is a boundary of a section of the quotient
`Q` of `M ⟶ π_* π⁻¹ M`; restriction to `X₀` is surjective on sections of `π_* π⁻¹ M` and injective
on sections of `Q`, both being finite locally constant and base change to `X₀` being fully faithful
on finite étale covers (Stacks 0A48).
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_etaleConstantCohomologyRestriction_one_of_isProper
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [IsProper f] (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] [Finite M] :
    Function.Bijective (etaleConstantCohomologyRestriction.{u, 0, u + 1} A f M 1)

declarations.name: derivedCategory_termwiseDirectSum_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0A5L**, the concrete identification of the coproduct in `D(A)`: for a countable
family `K : J → CochainComplex A ℤ`, the termwise direct sum `∐ K`, with the images under `Q` of
the canonical injections `Sigma.ι K j`, is a coproduct of `(Q (K j))ⱼ` in `D(A)`.

`[HasCoproduct K]` records that the termwise direct sum exists in `CochainComplex A ℤ`; it
follows from `h.hasCoproducts` and `Countable J`, but is assumed so that `∐ K` and `Sigma.ι K`
are well-formed in the statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategory_termwiseDirectSum_isColimit
    (h : HasExactCountableDirectSums A) (J : Type) [Countable J]
    (K : J → CochainComplex A ℤ) [HasCoproduct K] :
    Nonempty (IsColimit
      ((DerivedCategory.Q (C := A)).mapCocone (Cofan.mk (∐ K) (Sigma.ι K))))

declarations.name: derivedCategory_hasCountableCoproducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0A5L**: if the abelian category `A` has exact countable direct sums then its
derived category `D(A)` has countable direct sums.

A countable family in `D(A)` is, up to isomorphism, the image under `Q` of a family of complexes,
by essential surjectivity of `Q`; the termwise direct sum of the latter is its coproduct.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategory_hasCountableCoproducts
    (h : HasExactCountableDirectSums A) :
    HasCountableCoproducts (DerivedCategory A)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ProjectiveDimension.HasProjectiveAmplitude
declarations.doc:
An object of `D(R)` has **projective amplitude in `[a, b]`** if it is represented by a
complex of projective `R`-modules whose terms vanish outside degrees `a` through `b`.
declarations.statement:
public def HasProjectiveAmplitude
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (a b : ℤ) : Prop
declarations.comment: projective amplitude

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ProjectiveDimension.HasFiniteProjectiveDimension
declarations.doc:
An object of `D(R)` has **finite projective dimension** if it is represented by a bounded
complex of projective `R`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public def HasFiniteProjectiveDimension
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) : Prop
declarations.comment: finite projective dimension

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ProjectiveDimension.hasProjectiveAmplitude_iff_ext_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5P.** Projective amplitude in `[a, b]` is equivalent to vanishing of all Ext
groups outside degrees `[-b, -a]`; equivalently, it can be detected using upper cohomology
vanishing and Ext groups above degree `-a`, or using cohomology outside `[a - 1, b]` and the
single Ext degree `-a + 1`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasProjectiveAmplitude_iff_ext_vanishing [Small.{v} R]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (a b : ℤ) :
    let moduleObject := fun N : ModuleCat.{v} R ↦
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N
    let projectiveAmplitude := HasProjectiveAmplitude K a b
    let extOutsideVanishes := ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (i : ℤ),
      i ∉ Set.Icc (-b) (-a) → Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) i)
    let upperVanishing :=
      (∀ n : ℤ, b < n → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) n).obj K)) ∧
        ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (i : ℤ), -a < i →
          Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) i)
    let endpointVanishing :=
      (∀ n : ℤ, n ∉ Set.Icc (a - 1) b →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) n).obj K)) ∧
        ∀ N : ModuleCat.{v} R,
          Subsingleton (DerivedCategory.Ext K (moduleObject N) (-a + 1))
    (projectiveAmplitude ↔ extOutsideVanishes) ∧
      (extOutsideVanishes ↔ upperVanishing) ∧
      (upperVanishing ↔ endpointVanishing)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ProjectiveDimension.dualNumber_quotient_eps_periodic_resolution_infinite_dimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Q.** For the ring `R = k[ε]` of dual numbers over a field and `M = R/(ε)`, the
module `M` is represented by the periodic free complex with all differentials multiplication by
`ε`, but `M` has infinite projective dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dualNumber_quotient_eps_periodic_resolution_infinite_dimension
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} (DualNumber k))] :
    let R := DualNumber k
    let ε : R := DualNumber.eps
    let M := ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ Ideal.span {ε})
    projectiveDimension M = ⊤ ∧
      ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ,
        Nonempty
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ≅
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj M) ∧
          (∀ i : ℤ, 0 < i → IsZero (P.X i)) ∧
          ∃ e : ∀ n : ℕ, P.X (-(n : ℤ)) ≅ ModuleCat.of R R,
            ∀ n : ℕ,
              P.d (-((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) (-(n : ℤ)) ≫ (e n).hom =
                (e (n + 1)).hom ≫
                  ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.mulLeft R ε)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.HasInjectiveAmplitude

declarations.name: StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.HasFiniteInjectiveDimension

An object of a derived category has *finite injective dimension* if it has injective

declarations.statement: public def HasFiniteInjectiveDimension (K : DerivedCategory C) : Prop
declarations.comment: finite injective dimension

declarations.name: StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.hasInjectiveAmplitude_iff_ext_vanishing_iff_quotient_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5T.** An object of the derived category of modules has injective amplitude in
`[a, b]` if and only if its Ext groups from all modules vanish in degrees outside `[a, b]`; this
is in turn equivalent to testing the same vanishing only on quotients by ideals.
declarations.statement:
public lemma hasInjectiveAmplitude_iff_ext_vanishing_iff_quotient_vanishing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) (a b : ℤ) :
    (HasInjectiveAmplitude K a b ↔
      ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (i : ℤ), i < a ∨ b < i →
        Subsingleton
          (DerivedCategory.Ext
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N) K i)) ∧
    ((∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (i : ℤ), i < a ∨ b < i →
        Subsingleton
          (DerivedCategory.Ext
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj N) K i)) ↔
      ∀ (I : Ideal R) (i : ℤ), i < a ∨ b < i →
        Subsingleton
          (DerivedCategory.Ext
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj
              (ModuleCat.of R (Shrink.{v} (R ⧸ I)))) K i))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.dualNumber_residueField_infinite_injectiveDimension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5U.** Let `R` be the ring of dual numbers over a field and let `M = R/(ε)`.
Then `R` is injective as an `R`-module, `M` is quasi-isomorphic to the left-unbounded complex of
copies of `R` whose differentials are multiplication by `ε`, and `M` has infinite injective
dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dualNumber_residueField_infinite_injectiveDimension (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    let R := DualNumber k
    let M := ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({DualNumber.eps} : Set R))
    Module.Injective R R ∧
      (∃ (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)
          (e : ∀ (i : ℤ) (_ : i ≤ 0), K.X i ≅ ModuleCat.of R R)
          (q : K ⟶ (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat R) 0).obj M),
        QuasiIso q ∧
          (q.f 0 = (e 0 (by omega)).hom ≫
            ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.mkQ (Ideal.span ({DualNumber.eps} : Set R)))) ∧
          (∀ (i : ℤ) (hi : i < 0),
            (e i (by omega)).hom ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom (LinearMap.mulLeft R DualNumber.eps) =
              K.d i (i + 1) ≫ (e (i + 1) (by omega)).hom) ∧
          (∀ (i : ℤ), 0 < i → IsZero (K.X i))) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, ¬ HasInjectiveDimensionLE M n)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.hasFiniteInjectiveDimension_of_bounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5V.** A bounded object of the derived category of modules has finite injective
dimension if all its cohomology modules have finite injective dimension. Likewise, a derived
object represented by a bounded complex whose terms all have finite injective dimension has
finite injective dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasFiniteInjectiveDimension_of_bounded
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) :
    ((∃ a b : ℤ, K.IsGE a ∧ K.IsLE b) →
      (∀ i : ℤ, ∃ n : ℕ,
        HasInjectiveDimensionLE
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj K) n) →
      HasFiniteInjectiveDimension K) ∧
    (∀ (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ),
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ K) →
      (∃ a b : ℤ, L.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ L.IsStrictlyLE b) →
      (∀ i : ℤ, ∃ n : ℕ, HasInjectiveDimensionLE (L.X i) n) →
      HasFiniteInjectiveDimension K)

declarations.name: homComplexHomologyAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5X**.
The canonical identification `Hⁿ(Hom^•(L, M)) ≃+ Hom_{K(C)}(L, M⟦n⟧)` of the degree-`n`
cohomology of the Hom complex with morphisms in the homotopy category.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homComplexHomologyAddEquiv
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] (L M : CochainComplex C ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    (L.HomComplex M).homology n ≃+
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient C (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj L ⟶
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient C (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (M⟦n⟧))

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.Currying.curryIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Y**.
The canonical tensor–Hom currying isomorphism of complexes of `R`-modules
`Hom^•(K, Hom^•(L, M)) ≅ Hom^•(Tot(K ⊗_R L), M)`, given in each degree by transposing a
degreewise linear map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def curryIso (K L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) :
    HomComplexR R K (HomComplexR R L M) ≅ HomComplexR R (K ⊗ L) M

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.Currying.curryIso_hom_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Y**.
The currying isomorphism sends a cochain `α` to the cochain whose value on the summand
`K^r ⊗ L^s` of `Tot^t(K ⊗ L)` is `x ⊗ y ↦ α^r(x)(y)`. This determines it in every degree and on
every summand.
declarations.statement:
lemma curryIso_hom_apply (K L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (n r s t p : ℤ)
    (hrs : r + s = t) (htp : t + n = p)
    (α : Cochain K (HomComplexR R L M) n) (x : K.X r) (y : L.X s) :
    ((((curryIso K L M).hom.f n).hom α).v t p htp).hom
        ((ιTensorObj K L r s t hrs).hom (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)) =
      (((α.v r (r + n) (by omega)).hom x).v s p (by omega)).hom y

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.Currying.curryIso_naturality_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Y**.
Currying is contravariantly natural in the first complex: precomposing with `f : K' ⟶ K` inside
the iterated Hom complex corresponds to precomposing with `f ▷ L` on the total complex.
declarations.statement:
lemma curryIso_naturality_left {K K' L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ} (f : K' ⟶ K) :
    Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R K' K (HomComplexR R L M) f ≫ (curryIso K' L M).hom =
      (curryIso K L M).hom ≫ Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R (K' ⊗ L) (K ⊗ L) M (f ▷ L)

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.Currying.curryIso_naturality_middle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Y**.
Currying is contravariantly natural in the middle complex: precomposing the inner Hom complex
with `f : L' ⟶ L` corresponds to precomposing with `K ◁ f` on the total complex.
declarations.statement:
lemma curryIso_naturality_middle {K L L' M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ} (f : L' ⟶ L) :
    Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R K (HomComplexR R L M) (HomComplexR R L' M)
        (Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R L' L M f) ≫ (curryIso K L' M).hom =
      (curryIso K L M).hom ≫ Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R (K ⊗ L') (K ⊗ L) M (K ◁ f)

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.Currying.curryIso_naturality_right
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Y**.
Currying is covariantly natural in the target complex.
declarations.statement:
lemma curryIso_naturality_right {K L M M' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ} (f : M ⟶ M') :
    Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R K (HomComplexR R L M) (HomComplexR R L M')
        (Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R L M M' f) ≫ (curryIso K L M').hom =
      (curryIso K L M).hom ≫ Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R (K ⊗ L) M M' f

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TensorHomEquiv.tensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Z.** Linear maps into a module of linear maps are canonically equivalent to
linear maps out of the corresponding tensor product: `Hom_R(K, Hom_R(L, M))` is identified with
`Hom_R(K ⊗_R L, M)` by sending `f` to the map determined by `x ⊗ y ↦ f(x)(y)`.
declarations.statement: alias tensorHomEquiv

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TensorHomEquiv.tensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Z.** Linear maps into a module of linear maps are canonically equivalent to
linear maps out of the corresponding tensor product: `Hom_R(K, Hom_R(L, M))` is identified with
`Hom_R(K ⊗_R L, M)` by sending `f` to the map determined by `x ⊗ y ↦ f(x)(y)`.
declarations.statement: alias tensorHomEquiv

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TensorHomEquiv.tensorHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Z.** The tensor–Hom equivalence sends `f : K →ₗ[R] L →ₗ[R] M` to the linear map
taking the pure tensor `x ⊗ y` to `f x y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomEquiv_apply {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (K L M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup K] [AddCommGroup L] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R K] [Module R L] [Module R M]
    (f : K →ₗ[R] L →ₗ[R] M) (x : K) (y : L) :
    tensorHomEquiv (RingHom.id R) K L M f (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) = f x y

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TensorHomEquiv.tensorHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Z.** The tensor–Hom equivalence sends `f : K →ₗ[R] L →ₗ[R] M` to the linear map
taking the pure tensor `x ⊗ y` to `f x y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomEquiv_apply {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (K L M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup K] [AddCommGroup L] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R K] [Module R L] [Module R M]
    (f : K →ₗ[R] L →ₗ[R] M) (x : K) (y : L) :
    tensorHomEquiv (RingHom.id R) K L M f (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) = f x y

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TensorHomEquiv.tensorHomEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Z.** The inverse of the tensor–Hom equivalence sends `g : K ⊗[R] L →ₗ[R] M` to
the map `x ↦ y ↦ g (x ⊗ y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomEquiv_symm_apply {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (K L M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup K] [AddCommGroup L] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R K] [Module R L] [Module R M]
    (g : K ⊗[R] L →ₗ[R] M) (x : K) (y : L) :
    ((tensorHomEquiv (RingHom.id R) K L M).symm g) x y = g (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.TensorHomEquiv.tensorHomEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A5Z.** The inverse of the tensor–Hom equivalence sends `g : K ⊗[R] L →ₗ[R] M` to
the map `x ↦ y ↦ g (x ⊗ y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomEquiv_symm_apply {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (K L M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup K] [AddCommGroup L] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R K] [Module R L] [Module R M]
    (g : K ⊗[R] L →ₗ[R] M) (x : K) (y : L) :
    ((tensorHomEquiv (RingHom.id R) K L M).symm g) x y = g (x ⊗ₜ[R] y)

declarations.name: ChainEvaluation.chainEvaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A60**.
The canonical morphism of complexes `Tot(Hom^•(J, I) ⊗ K) ⟶ Hom^•(Hom^•(K, J), I)`. On
homogeneous elements it sends `f ⊗ k` to the map `g ↦ f (g k)`, with the Koszul signs of the
total and Hom complexes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chainEvaluation
    (K J I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) :
    (HomComplexR R J I ⊗ K) ⟶ HomComplexR R (HomComplexR R K J) I

declarations.name: ChainEvaluation.chainEvaluation_natural_K
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A60**.
Evaluation is natural in the complex `K` being evaluated at: tensoring with `f : K ⟶ K'` and
then evaluating is evaluating and then precomposing the outer Hom complex with `f^* :
Hom^•(K', J) ⟶ Hom^•(K, J)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem chainEvaluation_natural_K
    (K K' J I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (f : K ⟶ K') :
    (HomComplexR R J I ◁ f) ≫ chainEvaluation K' J I =
      chainEvaluation K J I ≫ Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R (HomComplexR R K' J)
        (HomComplexR R K J) I (Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R K K' J f)

declarations.name: ChainEvaluation.chainEvaluation_natural_J
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A60**.
Evaluation is natural in the middle complex `J`: precomposing the inner Hom complex with
`f : J ⟶ J'` on the source corresponds to postcomposing `Hom^•(K, J) ⟶ Hom^•(K, J')` on the
target.
declarations.statement:
theorem chainEvaluation_natural_J
    (K J J' I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (f : J ⟶ J') :
    (Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R J J' I f ▷ K) ≫ chainEvaluation K J I =
      chainEvaluation K J' I ≫ Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.precomp R (HomComplexR R K J)
        (HomComplexR R K J') I (Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R K J J' f)

declarations.name: ChainEvaluation.chainEvaluation_natural_I
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A60**.
Evaluation is natural in the target complex `I`: postcomposing with `f : I ⟶ I'` commutes with
evaluation.
declarations.statement:
theorem chainEvaluation_natural_I
    (K J I I' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (f : I ⟶ I') :
    (Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R J I I' f ▷ K) ≫ chainEvaluation K J I' =
      chainEvaluation K J I ≫ Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.postcomp R (HomComplexR R K J) I I' f

declarations.name: ChainEvaluation.chainEvaluation_tmul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A60**.
The homogeneous formula for `chainEvaluation`: the image of `φ ⊗ k` sends a cochain `ψ`
to `φ (ψ k)`, up to the Koszul sign `(-1)^(s + (-a) s)` of evaluation.
declarations.statement:
theorem chainEvaluation_tmul
    (K J I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)
    (t s n q p a : ℤ) (hn : t + s = n) (hq : q + n = p)
    (ha : s + q = a) (hp : a + t = p)
    (φ : Cochain J I t) (k : K.X s) (ψ : Cochain K J q) :
    ((((chainEvaluation K J I).f n).hom
      ((ιTensorObj (HomComplexR R J I) K t s n hn).hom (φ ⊗ₜ[R] k))).v
        q p hq).hom ψ =
      (s + (-a) * s).negOnePow •
        (φ.v a p hp).hom ((ψ.v s a ha).hom k)

declarations.name: ChainEvaluation.chainEvaluation_eq_tensorHomEquiv_symm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A61**.
The canonical map `Tot(Hom^•(L, M) ⊗ K) ⟶ Hom^•(Hom^•(K, L), M)` of Stacks 0A60 obtained from
the symmetric monoidal structure agrees with the direct construction `chainEvaluation`: it is the
transpose, under the tensor–Hom adjunction of Stacks 0A5Y, of the arrow
`Hom^•(L, M) ⊗ K ⊗ Hom^•(K, L) ⟶ M` that swaps the last two factors with the Koszul sign and then
applies the evaluation maps `Hom^•(K, L) ⊗ K ⟶ L` and `Hom^•(L, M) ⊗ L ⟶ M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.ChainEvaluation.chainEvaluation_eq_tensorHomEquiv_symm {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (K L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) :
    ChainEvaluation.chainEvaluation K L M =
      (Stacks.HomComplex.MonoidalClosed.tensorHomEquiv (HomComplexR R L M ⊗ K)
        (HomComplexR R K L) M).symm
        ((α_ (HomComplexR R L M) K (HomComplexR R K L)).hom ≫
          (HomComplexR R L M ◁ (Model.complexSwap R K (HomComplexR R K L)).hom) ≫
          (HomComplexR R L M ◁
            Stacks.HomComplex.MonoidalClosed.tensorHomEquiv (HomComplexR R K L) K L (𝟙 _)) ≫
          Stacks.HomComplex.MonoidalClosed.tensorHomEquiv (HomComplexR R L M) L M (𝟙 _))
declarations.comment: the monoidal construction of the evaluation map of 0A60 (Koszul swap of the last two factors, two evaluations, transpose) equals chainEvaluation

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.Phi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A62**.
The morphism of complexes of `R`-modules `Φ_{K,L} : K ⟶ Hom^•(L, Tot(K ⊗_R L))` whose degree-`n`
component sends `β ∈ K^n` to the cochain `y ↦ β ⊗ y`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Phi (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) :
    K ⟶ CochainComplex.HomComplexR R L (K ⊗ L)

declarations.name: Stacks.HomComplex.TensorHomMap.Phi_natural_mixed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A62**.
For `f : K ⟶ K'` and `g : L ⟶ L'`, postcomposing `Φ_{K,L}` with `Tot(f ⊗ g) = f ⊗ₘ g` equals
`f ≫ Φ_{K',L'}` followed by precomposition with `g`; both send `β` and `y` to `f(β) ⊗ g(y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Phi_natural_mixed (K K' L L' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L ⟶ L') :
    Phi R K L ≫ postcomp R L (K ⊗ L) (K' ⊗ L') (f ⊗ₘ g) =
      f ≫ Phi R K' L' ≫ precomp R L L' (K' ⊗ L') g

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.homInternalHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A63.** The canonical characterization equation in `D(R)`:
`Hom(K, RHom(L, M)) ≃+ Hom(K ⊗ᴸ L, M)`. The bifunctors and the equivalence are
transported from the fixed K-flat/K-injective construction, with compatibility given by
`derivedTensorULiftIso` and `derivedHomULiftIso`. No adjunction or scalar equivalence is
supplied as a parameter. The ring, module enlargement, and derived-morphism universes are
independent.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def homInternalHomEquiv {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)]
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R)) :
    (K ⟶ (derivedHomAdjunctionOverRing R).hom.obj (Opposite.op L, M)) ≃+
      ((derivedHomAdjunctionOverRing R).tensor.obj (K, L) ⟶ M)

declarations.name: homComplex_of_isKInjective_represents_RHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A64**.
If `I` is K-injective, then the degree-`n` cohomology of the Hom complex `Hom^•(L, I)` is
canonically identified with the morphisms `L ⟶ I⟦n⟧` in the derived category; equivalently, when
`I` represents `M`, this is `Hⁿ(RHom(L, M)) = Hom(L, M⟦n⟧)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homComplex_of_isKInjective_represents_RHom (L I : CochainComplex C ℤ) [I.IsKInjective]
    (n : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun (c : CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass L I n) ↦
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map
          (CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv c))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomCurrying
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A65.** Derived Hom satisfies the canonical currying isomorphism
`RHom(K, RHom(L, M)) ≅ RHom(K ⊗ᴸ L, M)`, functorially in `K`, `L`, and `M`.
On K-flat/K-injective representatives this is the Hom-complex currying map of Stacks 0A5Y.
On degree-zero cohomology this is the derived tensor--Hom equivalence of Stacks 0A63.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def derivedHomCurrying {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{v} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] :
    DerivedHomCurrying (derivedHomAdjunction (R := R))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.projectiveHomComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A66.** A bounded-above complex of projective modules computes the derived
internal Hom against every target complex. The comparison is natural in both variables,
recovers the defining K-injective model, and hence is the comparison induced by a
K-injective resolution in the proof of the source lemma.
declarations.statement:
def projectiveHomComparison {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] : ProjectiveHomComparison R

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.projectiveHomComparisonULift
declarations.doc:
The comparison of Stacks 0A66 in an independently chosen module universe. The lifted
ring is canonically isomorphic to `R`, and retains all naturality and model comparisons.
declarations.statement:
abbrev projectiveHomComparisonULift {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{max u v} (ULift.{v} R))] :
    ProjectiveHomComparison (ULift.{v} R)

declarations.name: cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A66**.
Let `P` be a bounded above complex of projective `R`-modules and `L` a complex of `R`-modules.
The degree-`n` cohomology classes of `Hom^•(P, L)` are canonically *isomorphic as abelian groups*
to `Hom_{D(R)}(P, L⟦n⟧)`, the isomorphism sending a class to the image under
`DerivedCategory.Qh` of the corresponding morphism `P ⟶ L⟦n⟧` in the homotopy category. This is
the assertion that `Hom^•(P, L)` represents `RHom_R(P, L)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv (P L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (d n : ℤ)
    [P.IsStrictlyLE d] [∀ i, CategoryTheory.Projective (P.X i)] :
    CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass P L n ≃+
      (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (L⟦n⟧)))

declarations.name: homComplexHomologyRHomAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A66**.
The comparison isomorphism of [stacks 0A66] read on the homology of the Hom complex: for `P` a
bounded above complex of projective `R`-modules,
`Hⁿ(Hom^•(P, L)) ≃+ Hom_{D(R)}(P, L⟦n⟧)`, so `Hom^•(P, L)` represents `RHom_R(P, L)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homComplexHomologyRHomAddEquiv (P L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)
    (d n : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE d] [∀ i, CategoryTheory.Projective (P.X i)] :
    (P.HomComplex L).homology n ≃+
      (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (L⟦n⟧)))

declarations.name: homComplex_represents_RHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A66**.
Let `P` be a bounded above complex of projective `R`-modules and `L` a complex of `R`-modules.
For every `n : ℤ`, the map from degree-`n` cohomology classes of `Hom^•(P, L)` to
`Hom_{D(R)}(P, L⟦n⟧)`, sending a class to the image under `DerivedCategory.Qh` of the corresponding
morphism `P ⟶ L⟦n⟧` in the homotopy category, is bijective; that is, `Hom^•(P, L)` represents
`RHom_R(P, L)`.

This is the pointwise shadow of `cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv`, from which it is derived.
declarations.statement:
theorem homComplex_represents_RHom (P L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (d n : ℤ)
    [P.IsStrictlyLE d] [∀ i, CategoryTheory.Projective (P.X i)] :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun (c : CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass P L n) =>
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map (CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv c))

declarations.name: cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv_naturality_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A66**.
Naturality of the comparison isomorphism in the first variable: for `f : P' ⟶ P` a morphism of
bounded above complexes of projectives, the square formed by `cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv` at `P`
and at `P'`, precomposition by `f` on cohomology classes, and precomposition by the image of `f`
in `D(R)` commutes. Thus `Hom^•(-, L)` represents `RHom_R(-, L)` contravariantly.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv_naturality_left (P P' L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)
    (f : P' ⟶ P) (d d' n : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE d] [∀ i, CategoryTheory.Projective (P.X i)]
    [P'.IsStrictlyLE d'] [∀ i, CategoryTheory.Projective (P'.X i)]
    (c : CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass P L n) :
    cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv P' L d' n (cohomologyClassPrecomp f L n c) =
      DerivedCategory.Qh.map
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f) ≫
        cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv P L d n c

declarations.name: cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv_naturality_right
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A66**.
Naturality of the comparison isomorphism in the second variable: for `g : L ⟶ L'` the square
formed by `cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv` at `L` and at `L'`, postcomposition by `g` on cohomology
classes, and postcomposition by the image of `g⟦n⟧'` in `D(R)` commutes. Thus `Hom^•(P, -)`
represents `RHom_R(P, -)` covariantly.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv_naturality_right (P L L' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)
    (g : L ⟶ L') (d n : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE d] [∀ i, CategoryTheory.Projective (P.X i)]
    (c : CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass P L n) :
    cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv P L' d n (cohomologyClassPostcomp P g n c) =
      cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv P L d n c ≫
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map (g⟦n⟧'))

declarations.name: homComplexRHom_isKInjective_model_comm
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A66**.
Compatibility of the two routes to `RHom`: for `g : L ⟶ I` with `I` K-injective, the square whose
left edge is the comparison of [stacks 0A66] for `(P, L)`, whose right edge is the comparison of
[stacks 0A64] for `(P, I)`, whose top edge is the map on cohomology classes induced by `g`, and
whose bottom edge is postcomposition with the image of `g⟦n⟧'` in `D(R)`, commutes. No
quasi-isomorphism hypothesis is needed for commutativity.
declarations.statement:
theorem homComplexRHom_isKInjective_model_comm (P L I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)
    (g : L ⟶ I) [I.IsKInjective] (d n : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE d]
    [∀ i, CategoryTheory.Projective (P.X i)]
    (c : CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass P L n) :
    cohomologyClassRHomAddEquivOfIsKInjective P I n (cohomologyClassPostcomp P g n c) =
      cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv P L d n c ≫
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map (g⟦n⟧'))

declarations.name: homComplexRHom_eq_isKInjective_model_route
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A66**.
The comparison of [stacks 0A66] is *computed by* the comparison of [stacks 0A64] through a
K-injective model: if `g : L ⟶ I` is a quasi-isomorphism with `I` K-injective, then the bottom
edge of the square of `homComplexRHom_isKInjective_model_comm` is invertible, and the
[stacks 0A66] comparison for `(P, L)` is the [stacks 0A64] comparison for `(P, I)` applied to the
transported class, followed by that inverse. So the two representability statements agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem homComplexRHom_eq_isKInjective_model_route (P L I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)
    (g : L ⟶ I) [I.IsKInjective] [QuasiIso g] (d n : ℤ) [P.IsStrictlyLE d]
    [∀ i, CategoryTheory.Projective (P.X i)]
    (c : CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass P L n) :
    cohomologyClassRHomAddEquiv P L d n c =
      cohomologyClassRHomAddEquivOfIsKInjective P I n (cohomologyClassPostcomp P g n c) ≫
        CategoryTheory.inv (DerivedCategory.Qh.map
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map (g⟦n⟧')))

declarations.name: Dualizing.homComplexRHomologyLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[stacks 0A66] read on the derived category, `S`-linearly.**  For `P` a bounded above complex
of projective `S`-modules and `L` any complex, the degree-`n` cohomology of the `S`-linear Hom
complex `Hom^•_S(P, L)` is the module of morphisms `P ⟶ L⟦n⟧` in `D(S)`, as `S`-modules.

This is `Dualizing.homComplexRHomologyAddEquiv` with the `S`-action checked.  The comparison runs
through the cohomology classes of the Hom complex of the underlying abelian groups, where no
`S`-action is available, so the equivariance is read on representatives: a class in
`H^n(Hom^•_S(P, L))` is the class of a cocycle
(`Dualizing.LocalDuality.homComplexRHomologyAddEquiv_cyclesMk`), the `S`-action on `H^n` is the
action on cocycles, and the passage from a cocycle to a morphism in the homotopy category is
`S`-linear because `CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cocycle.equivHomShift` is and because
`HomotopyCategory.quotient` and `DerivedCategory.Qh` are `S`-linear functors.
declarations.statement:
def homComplexRHomologyLinearEquiv (P L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} S) ℤ) (d n : ℤ)
    [P.IsStrictlyLE d] [∀ i, Projective (P.X i)] :
    ((CochainComplex.HomComplexR S P L).homology n : Type u) ≃ₗ[S]
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P ⟶
        (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} S)) n).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.exists_evaluationToIteratedDerivedHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A67.** There is a canonical morphism
`RHom_R(L, M) ⊗ᴸ_R K ⟶ RHom_R(RHom_R(K, L), M)` for arbitrary objects of `D(R)`,
natural in all three objects. On K-flat and K-injective representatives it is induced by the
chain-level evaluation map of Stacks Tag 0A60 through the standard comparison isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_evaluationToIteratedDerivedHom :
    let D := derivedHomAdjunction (R := R)
    let e₀ := ChainEvaluation.chainEvaluation
    ∃ e : ∀ (K L M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)),
        D.tensor.obj (D.hom.obj (Opposite.op L, M), K) ⟶
          D.hom.obj (Opposite.op (D.hom.obj (Opposite.op K, L)), M),
      (∀ {K K' L M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : K ⟶ K'),
        D.tensor.map (𝟙 (D.hom.obj (Opposite.op L, M)), f) ≫ e K' L M =
          e K L M ≫ D.hom.map
            ((D.hom.map (f.op, 𝟙 L)).op, 𝟙 M)) ∧
      (∀ {K L L' M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : L ⟶ L'),
        D.tensor.map (D.hom.map (f.op, 𝟙 M), 𝟙 K) ≫ e K L M =
          e K L' M ≫ D.hom.map
            ((D.hom.map (𝟙 (Opposite.op K), f)).op, 𝟙 M)) ∧
      (∀ {K L M M' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : M ⟶ M'),
        D.tensor.map (D.hom.map (𝟙 (Opposite.op L), f), 𝟙 K) ≫ e K L M' =
          e K L M ≫ D.hom.map
            (𝟙 (Opposite.op (D.hom.obj (Opposite.op K, L))), f)) ∧
      (∀ (K L M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) (hK : K.KFlat)
          [L.IsKInjective] [M.IsKInjective],
        D.tensor.map ((D.homIso L M).hom, 𝟙 (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) ≫
              (D.tensorIso (HomComplexR R L M) K hK).hom ≫
              DerivedCategory.Q.map (e₀ K L M) ≫
              (D.homIso (HomComplexR R K L) M).inv ≫
              D.hom.map ((D.homIso K L).hom.op, 𝟙 (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M)) =
            e (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L)
              (DerivedCategory.Q.obj M))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.evaluationToIteratedDerivedHom_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A68.** The canonical evaluation morphism
`RHom_R(L, M) ⊗ᴸ_R K ⟶ RHom_R(RHom_R(K, L), M)` is an isomorphism if `K` is
perfect, or if `K` is pseudo-coherent, `L` is cohomologically bounded below, and `M` has
finite injective dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem evaluationToIteratedDerivedHom_isIso
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R))
    (h : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K ∨
      (StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K ∧
        DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow L ∧
        StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.HasFiniteInjectiveDimension M)) :
    let e := Classical.choose
      (exists_evaluationToIteratedDerivedHom (R := R))
    IsIso (e K L M)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.evaluationToIteratedDerivedHom_isIso_of_truncLE_pseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A69.** The canonical evaluation morphism
`RHom_R(L, M) ⊗ᴸ_R K ⟶ RHom_R(RHom_R(K, L), M)` is an isomorphism if `L` and `M`
have finite injective dimension, `RHom_R(L, M)` has finite Tor dimension, and every
truncation `τ_{≤ n} K` is pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem evaluationToIteratedDerivedHom_isIso_of_truncLE_pseudoCoherent
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R))
    (hL : StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.HasFiniteInjectiveDimension L)
    (hM : StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.HasFiniteInjectiveDimension M)
    (hTor :
      let D := derivedHomAdjunction (R := R)
      ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ (N : ModuleCat R) (i : ℤ), i ∉ Set.Icc a b →
        Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat R) i).obj
          (D.tensor.obj
            (D.hom.obj (Opposite.op L, M),
              (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat R) 0).obj N))))
    (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
      ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncLE n).obj K)) :
    let e := Classical.choose
      (exists_evaluationToIteratedDerivedHom (R := R))
    IsIso (e K L M)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedHom.BaseChangeIso.isIso_derivedHomBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6A.** The canonical derived-Hom base-change morphism
`RHom_R(K, M) ⊗ᴸ_R A ⟶ RHom_A(K ⊗ᴸ_R A, M ⊗ᴸ_R A)` of Stacks 0E1X is an isomorphism in each of
four cases: `K` is perfect; `A` is perfect as an `R`-module; the ring map is flat, `K` is
pseudo-coherent and `M` is bounded below; or `A` has finite Tor dimension over `R`, `K` is
pseudo-coherent and `M` is bounded below.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_derivedHomBaseChange
    {R : Type uR} {A : Type uA} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] (f : R →+* A) :
    letI : (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uR, uA, max uR uA uM} f).IsLeftAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj.{max uR uM, uR, uA} f).isLeftAdjoint
    letI : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max uR uA uM, uR, uA} f).IsRightAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj.{max uR uM, uR, uA} f).isRightAdjoint
    letI : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max uR uA uM, uR, uA} f).IsLeftAdjoint :=
      (ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj.{max uR uM, uR, uA} f).isLeftAdjoint
    ∀ (F : Functor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} R))
      (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} A)))
    (comparison : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ F ⟶
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{uR, uA, max uR uA uM} f).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    [F.IsLeftDerivedFunctor comparison
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    (K M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} R)),
    (StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K ∨
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} R) 0).obj
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f).obj (ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{max uR uM} A)))) ∨
      (f.Flat ∧ StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K ∧
        ∃ b : ℤ, DerivedCategory.IsGE M b) ∨
      ((let e := moduleUniverseEquiv.{uR, max uA uM} R
        letI : e.functor.Additive :=
          inferInstanceAs (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max uR uA uM, max uR uA uM, uR}
            (ULift.ringEquiv : ULift.{max uA uM} R ≃+* R).toRingHom).Additive
        ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} R) (i : ℤ), i < a →
          IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} (ULift.{max uA uM} R)) i).obj
            ((canonTensorMod
                (e.functor.obj N)).obj
              (e.functor.mapDerivedCategory.obj
                ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max uR uA uM} R) 0).obj
                  ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars f).obj
                    (ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{max uR uM} A)))))))) ∧
        StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K ∧
        ∃ b : ℤ, DerivedCategory.IsGE M b)) →
    IsIso (Stacks.DerivedHom.ExtensionOfScalars.derivedHomBaseChange.{uR, uA, uM} f F comparison K
      M)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedTensorHomCoevaluation_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6B.** The canonical morphism `K ⟶ RHom(L, K ⊗ᴸ L)` is the transpose
of the identity on `K ⊗ᴸ L`; it is covariantly natural in `K` and dinatural in `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorHomCoevaluation_natural :
    (∀ (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)),
      DerivedInternalHom.Model.homEquiv K L ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).obj (K, L))
          (DerivedInternalHom.Model.coevaluation K L) =
        𝟙 ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).obj (K, L))) ∧
    (∀ {K K' L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : K ⟶ K'),
      f ≫ DerivedInternalHom.Model.coevaluation K' L =
        DerivedInternalHom.Model.coevaluation K L ≫
          (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map
            (𝟙 (Opposite.op L), (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map (f, 𝟙 L))) ∧
    (∀ {K L L' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (g : L ⟶ L'),
      DerivedInternalHom.Model.coevaluation K L' ≫
          (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map
            ((g.op, 𝟙 ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).obj (K, L'))) :
              (Opposite.op L', (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).obj (K, L')) ⟶
                (Opposite.op L, (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).obj (K, L'))) =
        DerivedInternalHom.Model.coevaluation K L ≫
          (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map
            ((𝟙 (Opposite.op L), (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map (𝟙 K, g)) :
              (Opposite.op L, (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).obj (K, L)) ⟶
                (Opposite.op L, (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).obj (K, L'))))

declarations.name: DerivedHomLocalization.derivedHom_localization_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6C.** For `f, g ∈ A` and `K ∈ D(A)`, there is a canonical isomorphism
`RHom_A(A_f, RHom_A(A_g, K)) ≅ RHom_A(A_{fg}, K)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def derivedHom_localization_comp {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat A)] (f g : A) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat A)) :
    let D := StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := A)
    let away (a : A) := DerivedCategory.Q.obj
      ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat A) 0).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (Localization.Away a)))
    D.hom.obj (Opposite.op (away f), D.hom.obj (Opposite.op (away g), K)) ≅
      D.hom.obj (Opposite.op (away (f * g)), K)

declarations.name: CechCompletion.isZero_cechCompletion_of_isIso_smul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6D.** Let `I` be the ideal generated by a finite family `g`. If some `x ∈ I`
acts invertibly on `K ∈ D(A)`, then the derived completion of `K` with respect to `I` is zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_cechCompletion_of_isIso_smul (A : Type u) [CommRing A] {r : ℕ}
    (g : Fin r → A) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    [HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))]
    {x : A} (hx : x ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range g)) [IsIso (x • 𝟙 K)] :
    IsZero ((cechCompletionFunctor A g).obj K)

declarations.name: DerivedHomCechCompletion.derivedHom_cechCompletion
declarations.doc:
For a finite family `f` generating an ideal of `A`, derived completion commutes naturally
with derived Hom in its target: `RHom_A(K, L)^∧ ≅ RHom_A(K, L^∧)`. If `η : K ⟶ K^∧` is the
reflection unit, then precomposition with `η` is the natural isomorphism
`RHom_A(K^∧, L^∧) ≅ RHom_A(K, L^∧)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedHom_cechCompletion (A : Type u) [CommRing A] {r : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → A)
    [HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))] :
    let C := DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)
    let D := StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := A)
    let F := CechCompletion.cechCompletionFunctor A f
    ∃ η : Functor.id C ⟶ F,
      (∀ K, IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) (F.obj K)) ∧
      (∀ (K E : C), IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) E →
        Function.Bijective (fun g : F.obj K ⟶ E ↦ η.app K ≫ g)) ∧
      Nonempty
        ((D.hom ⋙ F) ≅
          (((CategoryTheory.Prod.fst Cᵒᵖ C).prod'
            (CategoryTheory.Prod.snd Cᵒᵖ C ⋙ F)) ⋙ D.hom)) ∧
      ∃ e :
          ((((CategoryTheory.Prod.fst Cᵒᵖ C ⋙ F.op).prod'
              (CategoryTheory.Prod.snd Cᵒᵖ C ⋙ F)) ⋙ D.hom) ≅
            (((CategoryTheory.Prod.fst Cᵒᵖ C).prod'
              (CategoryTheory.Prod.snd Cᵒᵖ C ⋙ F)) ⋙ D.hom)),
        ∀ (K L : C), e.hom.app (Opposite.op K, L) =
          D.hom.map
            (show (Opposite.op (F.obj K), F.obj L) ⟶ (Opposite.op K, F.obj L) from
              ((η.app K).op, 𝟙 (F.obj L)))

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.homSheaf
declarations.doc:
The functor `SheafHom_{𝒪₁}(𝒪₂, -)` from `𝒪₁`-modules to `𝒪₂`-modules. On underlying
presheaves it is the coextension of scalars `Stacks.PresheafOfModules.CoextendScalars.coextFunMap`.
declarations.comment: the internal Hom sheaf, as a functor to modules over the target ring

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.restrictScalarsHomAdjunction
declarations.doc:
Restriction of scalars along a homomorphism of sheaves of rings is left adjoint to the
internal-Hom functor `SheafHom_{𝒪₁}(𝒪₂, -)`.
declarations.comment: the bifunctorial Hom identification

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.injective_cechCohomologyToCohomology_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A6G.** For a covering family `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` of an object of a site
and an abelian sheaf `G`, the map `Ȟ¹(𝒰, G) → H¹(U, G)` of Stacks 03AX is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_cechCohomologyToCohomology_one (hE : Sieve.generate E.presieve₀ ∈ K U)
    (G : Sheaf K Ab.{max a u v w}) :
    Function.Injective ((cechCohomologyToCohomology.{a} K E hE 1).app G)
declarations.comment: variant: injectivity of the derived-category comparison; the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.locallyTrivialClassEquivCechH1
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A6G.** First Čech cohomology of a covering family, as the set of
isomorphism classes of `G|_U`-torsors which restrict to trivial torsors over each member of
the family.
declarations.comment: variant: the Čech class bijection onto Ȟ¹(𝒰,G); the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.injective_cechH1ToCohomology_and_bijective_cechClass
declarations.doc:
For a covering family `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` of an object of a site and an abelian sheaf `G`, the
map `Ȟ¹(𝒰, G) → H¹(U, G)` is injective, and `Ȟ¹(𝒰, G)` is in bijection — under the Čech class
of a family of local sections — with the isomorphism classes of `G|_U`-torsors which restrict to
trivial torsors over each `U_i`. Both assertions are about the group
`Stacks.CechSite.cechH1 E G.obj`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_cechH1ToCohomology_and_bijective_cechClass (hE : E.sieve₀ ∈ K U)
    (G : Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w}) :
    Function.Injective (cechH1ToCohomology.{a} K E hE G) ∧
      Function.Bijective (Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.cechClass E G)
declarations.comment: variant: injectivity and the Čech class bijection at the explicit Ȟ¹(𝒰,G); the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.injective_torsorCohomologyClass_and_range_eq
declarations.doc:
For a covering family `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` of an object of a site and an abelian sheaf `G`, the
map which sends an isomorphism class of `G|_U`-torsors trivial over each `U_i` to the image in
`H¹(U, G)` of its Čech class is injective, and its image is exactly the image of
`Ȟ¹(𝒰, G) → H¹(U, G)`.

So `Ȟ¹(𝒰, G)` is a subgroup of `H¹(U, G)`, and the Čech class map identifies that subgroup with
the isomorphism classes of `G|_U`-torsors which restrict to trivial torsors over each `U_i`. The
map is `Stacks.CechSite.torsorCohomologyClass`, which is the Čech class map
followed by the comparison (`Stacks.CechSite.torsorCohomologyClass_eq`); on a representative with
local sections it is the comparison applied to the class of the transition cocycle
(`Stacks.CechSite.torsorCohomologyClass_mk`), and it vanishes exactly on the trivial torsor
(`Stacks.CechSite.isTrivial_iff_torsorCohomologyClass_eq_zero`).
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_torsorCohomologyClass_and_range_eq (hE : E.sieve₀ ∈ K U)
    (G : Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w}) :
    Function.Injective (torsorCohomologyClass.{a} K E hE G) ∧
      Set.range (torsorCohomologyClass.{a} K E hE G) =
        Set.range (cechH1ToCohomology.{a} K E hE G)
declarations.comment: variant: the Čech class of a torsor read in the derived H¹(U,G); the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒰 = {U_i → U}` be a covering of a site and `G` an abelian sheaf. The map
`Ȟ¹(𝒰, G) → H¹(U, G)` of Stacks 03AX is injective and, through the bijection of Stacks 03AJ between
isomorphism classes of `G|_U`-torsors and `H¹(U, G)`, identifies `Ȟ¹(𝒰, G)` with the set of
isomorphism classes of `G|_U`-torsors which restrict to trivial torsors over each `U_i`: the class
under 03AJ of such a torsor is the image of its Čech class, and the image of `Ȟ¹(𝒰, G)` is exactly
the set of these classes.

Here `H¹(U, G)` is `Sheaf.H (G.over U) 1`, the target of the bijection of 03AJ, and the map is the
comparison of 03AX read there through the canonical identification of the two models of first
cohomology (`Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH`). Sheafification, the comparison of the sheaf
topology with local bijectivity, enough injectives and the `Ext`-groups at the coefficient
universe `max a u v w` exist on every site and are constructed in the statement. The existence
of the iterated fibre products of the members of `𝒰` is part of the definition of a covering in
the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq (hE : E.sieve₀ ∈ K U)
    (G : Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w}) :
    letI : HasSheafify K AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w} :=
      site_hasSheafify_addCommGrp.{u, v, max a w}
    letI : K.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w} :=
      site_wEqualsLocallyBijective_addCommGrp.{u, v, max a w}
    letI : EnoughInjectives (Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w}) :=
      CategoryTheory.Sheaf.enoughInjectives_addCommGrpCat_max.{max a w, v, u} K
    letI : HasSheafify (K.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w} :=
      site_hasSheafify_addCommGrp.{max u v, v, max a w}
    letI : EnoughInjectives (Sheaf (K.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w}) :=
      CategoryTheory.Sheaf.enoughInjectives_addCommGrpCat_max.{max a w, v, max u v} (K.over U)
    letI : HasExt.{max a u v w} (Sheaf (K.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{max a u v w}) :=
      hasExt_of_enoughInjectives _
    Function.Injective (cechH1ToSliceH.{a} K E hE G) ∧
      (∀ c : LocallyTrivialClass E G,
        cechH1ToSliceH.{a} K E hE G (cechClass E G c) =
          torsorIsoClassesEquivH1.{max a u v w} (G.over U) c.1) ∧
      Set.range (cechH1ToSliceH.{a} K E hE G) =
        torsorIsoClassesEquivH1.{max a u v w} (G.over U) ''
          {c | ∃ F : AbelianTorsor (G.over U),
            Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid (G.over U)) F = c ∧ IsTrivialOnMembers E G F}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.isTrivial_iff_cechClass_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**A torsor with vanishing Čech class is trivial.** For a covering family, the Čech class of
a torsor with a section over every member vanishes exactly when the torsor is trivial: the class
vanishes when the transition cocycle is a Čech coboundary, and subtracting that coboundary from
the local sections makes the transition cochain vanish on the nose.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivial_iff_cechClass_eq_zero (hE : E.sieve₀ ∈ J U) (F : AbelianTorsor (G.over U))
    (hs : ∀ i, Nonempty (F.1.presheaf.obj (op (Over.mk (E.f i))))) :
    F.1.IsTrivial ↔
      cechClass E G ⟨Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid (G.over U)) F, ⟨F, rfl, hs⟩⟩ = 0
declarations.comment: variant: the Čech class vanishes exactly on the trivial torsor; the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.cechClass_injective
declarations.doc:
**The Čech class is injective on the locally trivial isomorphism classes.** Under the
bijection of Stacks 03AJ between isomorphism classes of torsors and first cohomology, this is
the injectivity of the identification of `Ȟ¹(𝒰, G)` with the isomorphism classes of torsors
which are trivial over every member of `𝒰`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechClass_injective (hE : E.sieve₀ ∈ J U) :
    Function.Injective (cechClass E G)
declarations.comment: variant: injectivity of the Čech class map; the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.cls_transitionCocycle_congr
declarations.doc: **The Čech class of the transition cocycle does not depend on the chosen local sections.**
declarations.statement:
lemma cls_transitionCocycle_congr (F : AbelianTorsor (G.over U))
    (s s' : ∀ i, F.1.presheaf.obj (op (Over.mk (E.f i)))) :
    cls E G.obj (transitionCocycle E G F s) = cls E G.obj (transitionCocycle E G F s')
declarations.comment: variant: independence of the chosen local sections; the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.cls_transitionCocycle_eq_of_isIsomorphic
declarations.doc:
**The Čech class of the transition cocycle depends only on the isomorphism class of the
torsor.**
declarations.statement:
lemma cls_transitionCocycle_eq_of_isIsomorphic {F F' : AbelianTorsor (G.over U)}
    (hFF' : AbelianTorsor.IsIsomorphic F F')
    (s : ∀ i, F.1.presheaf.obj (op (Over.mk (E.f i))))
    (s' : ∀ i, F'.1.presheaf.obj (op (Over.mk (E.f i)))) :
    cls E G.obj (transitionCocycle E G F s) = cls E G.obj (transitionCocycle E G F' s')
declarations.comment: variant: independence of the torsor inside its isomorphism class; the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.isTrivialOnMembers_iff
declarations.doc:
**The torsors which restrict to trivial torsors over each member of the covering.** A torsor
under `G|_U` restricts to a trivial torsor over every member of the family exactly when it has a
section over every member.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivialOnMembers_iff (F : AbelianTorsor (G.over U)) :
    IsTrivialOnMembers E G F ↔
      ∀ i, Nonempty (F.1.presheaf.obj (op (Over.mk (E.f i))))
declarations.comment: variant: torsors trivial over each member have sections there; the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.cechClass_eq_zero_of_isTrivial
declarations.doc:
**A trivial torsor has vanishing Čech class.** A global section restricts to a family of
local sections all of whose differences vanish.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechClass_eq_zero_of_isTrivial (F : AbelianTorsor (G.over U))
    (hF : F.1.IsTrivial)
    (hs : ∀ i, Nonempty (F.1.presheaf.obj (op (Over.mk (E.f i))))) :
    cechClass E G ⟨Quotient.mk (torsorSetoid (G.over U)) F, ⟨F, rfl, hs⟩⟩ = 0
declarations.comment: variant: the trivial torsor has vanishing Čech class; the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.isTrivial_of_transitionCochain_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**A vanishing transition cochain makes the torsor trivial.** The local sections then agree
on every common refinement of two members of the covering, so the sheaf condition for the
covering sieve glues them to a section over the terminal object of `C/U`, and a torsor with such
a section is trivial by Stacks 03AI.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivial_of_transitionCochain_eq_zero (hE : E.sieve₀ ∈ J U)
    (F : AbelianTorsor (G.over U))
    (s : ∀ i, F.1.presheaf.obj (op (Over.mk (E.f i))))
    (hs : transitionCochain E G F s = 0) : F.1.IsTrivial
declarations.comment: variant: a torsor whose transition cocycle vanishes is trivial; the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Torsors.isTrivial_iff_exists_transitionCochain_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Triviality in terms of the transition cocycle.** For a covering family, a torsor under
`G|_U` with a section over every member of the family is trivial exactly when some family of
local sections has vanishing transition cochain, that is, exactly when the local sections can be
chosen to agree on all the fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTrivial_iff_exists_transitionCochain_eq_zero (hE : E.sieve₀ ∈ J U)
    (F : AbelianTorsor (G.over U)) :
    F.1.IsTrivial ↔
      ∃ s : ∀ i, F.1.presheaf.obj (op (Over.mk (E.f i))), transitionCochain E G F s = 0
declarations.comment: variant: triviality in terms of the transition cocycle; the tag is Stacks.CechSite.cechH1ToSliceH_injective_and_range_eq

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affineDerivedTildeHomComparison_perfect
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison agrees with clause (3)(b).** For `K` perfect it is the inverse
of the isomorphism `affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso`, hence invertible. This is what identifies
the comparison as the morphism whose invertibility clause (3)(b) asserts, rather than as some
morphism between the right two objects: the two are equal because they agree on bounded
finite-projective sources with K-injective targets, where both are the five-fold model
composite, and because both are natural.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineDerivedTildeHomComparison_perfect (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K) :
    affineDerivedTildeHomComparison R K L =
      (affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso R K L hK).inv
declarations.comment: (3)(b) K perfect and L arbitrary: the canonical comparison is the inverse of the isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6H, clause (3), case (b).** Let `R` be a commutative ring, `X = Spec R`, and let
`K`, `L` be objects of `D(R)` with `K` perfect. Then the derived internal Hom of the derived
sheafifications is the derived sheafification of the derived Hom over `R`:

`R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K̃, L̃)  ≅  (R Hom_R(K, L))~`.

The object `L` is arbitrary. The isomorphism is not an arbitrary one: it is
pinned down on bounded finite-projective representatives by
`affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso_model`, and it is natural in both arguments by
`affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_left` and `_natural_right`.
declarations.statement:
public def affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom (Spec R).sheaf).obj
        (op ((tildeDer R).obj K))).obj ((tildeDer R).obj L) ≅
      (tildeDer R).obj
        ((StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := R)).hom.obj (op K, L))
declarations.comment: (3)(b) K perfect and L arbitrary

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso_model
declarations.doc:
**The normalization of clause (3)(b).** On a bounded complex `P` of finite projective
modules the comparison is the sheafification of the ordinary Hom-complex comparison
`affineHomComplexTildeIso`, read through the [Stacks, Tag 08JH] comparison on the sheaf side and
the [Stacks, Tag 0A66] comparison on the module side. This identifies the isomorphism, not just
its source and target.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso_model (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (P L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (b : ℤ)
    [P.IsStrictlyLE b] [∀ i, Projective (P.X i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (P.X i)]
    (hP : {i : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (P.X i)}.Finite)
    (hK : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)) :
    strictlyPerfectHomComparison (specSite R) (specRHom R)
          ((tildeCx R).obj P) ((tildeCx R).obj L) ≫
        ((specRHom R).hom.map ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app P).op).app
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((tildeCx R).obj L)) ≫
        ((specRHom R).hom.obj (op ((tildeDer R).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)))).map
          ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app L) ≫
        (affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso R (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L) hK).hom ≫
        (tildeDer R).map (StacksDraft.DerivedHom.projectiveHomComparison.iso P L b).hom ≫
        (tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
          (CochainComplex.HomComplexR R P L) =
      (DerivedCategory.Q.mapIso (affineHomComplexTildeIso R P L hP)).hom
declarations.comment: (3)(b) K perfect and L arbitrary

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_right
declarations.doc: **Clause (3)(b) is natural in the target.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_right (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K)
    {L L' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)} (g : L ⟶ L') :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom (Spec R).sheaf).obj
          (op ((tildeDer R).obj K))).map ((tildeDer R).map g) ≫
        (affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso R K L' hK).hom =
      (affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso R K L hK).hom ≫
        (tildeDer R).map
          ((StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := R)).hom.map (𝟙 (op K), g))
declarations.comment: (3)(b) K perfect and L arbitrary

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_left
declarations.doc: **Clause (3)(b) is contravariantly natural in the perfect source.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_left (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)} (f : K' ⟶ K)
    (hK : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K)
    (hK' : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K')
    (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom (Spec R).sheaf).map
          ((tildeDer R).map f).op).app ((tildeDer R).obj L) ≫
        (affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso R K' L hK').hom =
      (affinePerfectDerivedSheafHomIso R K L hK).hom ≫
        (tildeDer R).map
          ((StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := R)).hom.map (f.op, 𝟙 L))
declarations.comment: (3)(b) K perfect and L arbitrary

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineExt.cohomologySheaf_isSheafification_extPresheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a commutative ring, let `K`, `L` be objects of `D(A)` and let `n` be an integer.
The `n`-th cohomology sheaf of `R𝓗om(K̃, L̃)` on `Spec A` is the sheaf of `𝒪_{Spec A}`-modules
associated to the presheaf `D(f) ↦ Ext^n_{A_f}(K ⊗_A A_f, L ⊗_A A_f)` on the principal opens of
`Spec A`: the canonical maps `Ext^n_{A_f}(K ⊗_A A_f, L ⊗_A A_f) ⟶ Γ(D(f), Hⁿ(R𝓗om(K̃, L̃)))`,
one for every `f : A`, which are `A_f`-linear
(`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineExt.extToCohomologySheafLinear`),
* commute with restriction, the restriction of `Ext` classes from `D(f)` to `D(g) ⊆ D(f)` being
  derived base change along `A_f ⟶ A_g`;
* are locally surjective: every section of `Hⁿ(R𝓗om(K̃, L̃))` over `D(f)` is, around every point of
  `D(f)`, the restriction of the image of an `Ext` class over a smaller principal open;
* are locally injective: an `Ext` class over `D(f)` with zero image restricts to zero over a
  principal open around every point of `D(f)`.

Here `A_f = Γ(Spec A, D(f))` is the localization of `A` away from `f`, which is also the ring of
sections of `𝒪_{Spec A}` over `D(f)`. The objects `K` and `L` are arbitrary.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologySheaf_isSheafification_extPresheaf (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (n : ℤ) :
    (∀ (f g : R) (h : basicOpen R g ≤ basicOpen R f) (α : localizedExt R K L f n),
