        (cohomologySheaf R K L n).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op
            (extToCohomologySheafLinear R K L n f α) =
          extToCohomologySheafLinear R K L n g (localizedExtRestrict R K L h n α)) ∧
      (∀ (f : R) (s : Γ(cohomologySheaf R K L n, basicOpen R f)) (x : Spec R),
        x ∈ basicOpen R f → ∃ (g : R) (h : basicOpen R g ≤ basicOpen R f),
          x ∈ basicOpen R g ∧ ∃ α, extToCohomologySheafLinear R K L n g α =
            (cohomologySheaf R K L n).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op s) ∧
      (∀ (f : R) (α : localizedExt R K L f n), extToCohomologySheafLinear R K L n f α = 0 →
        ∀ x : Spec R, x ∈ basicOpen R f → ∃ (g : R) (h : basicOpen R g ≤ basicOpen R f),
          x ∈ basicOpen R g ∧ localizedExtRestrict R K L h n α = 0)
declarations.comment: (4) the n-th cohomology sheaf of RHom(K~, L~) on Spec A is the sheaf of modules associated to the presheaf D(f) ↦ Ext^n_{A_f}(K ⊗ A_f, L ⊗ A_f), through the canonical A_f-linear comparison maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A6H] (3)(a).** Let `R` be a commutative ring, `X = Spec R`, and let `K`, `L`
be objects of `D(R)` with `K` pseudo-coherent and `L` bounded below. Then the derived internal
Hom of the derived sheafifications of `K` and `L` is the derived sheafification of the derived
Hom `RHom_R(K, L)`:

`RSheafHom_{𝒪_X}(K̃, L̃) ≅ (RHom_R(K, L))~`.

The comparison is not an arbitrary isomorphism. `K` is replaced by a bounded-above
representative with finite free terms and `L` by a bounded-below K-injective representative;
there the sheaf side is computed by the ordinary internal Hom complex (Stacks 08I5) and the
module side by the ordinary Hom complex (Stacks 0A66), and the comparison is the one pinned
degreewise by the affine internal-Hom isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 01I8]. The representatives
are definite choices, so the construction is a function of its arguments, and it is natural in
both of them (`affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_left` and
`affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_right`). The canonical comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.affineDerivedTildeHomComparison` in the other direction is an isomorphism under
the same hypotheses, `isIso_affineDerivedTildeHomComparison_of_isPseudoCoherent`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hL : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).plus L) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom (Spec R).sheaf).obj
        (op ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))).obj
          ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.obj L) ≅
      (tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        ((StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := R)).hom.obj (op K, L))
declarations.comment: (3)(a) K pseudo-coherent and L bounded below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_left
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A6H] (3)(a).** The affine comparison is contravariantly natural in the
pseudo-coherent argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_left (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    {K K' L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hK' : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K')
    (hL : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).plus L) (f : K' ⟶ K) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom (Spec R).sheaf).map
        ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.map f).op).app
          ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.obj L) ≫
      (affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso R K' L hK' hL).hom =
    (affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso R K L hK hL).hom ≫
      (tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := R)).hom.map
          (f.op, 𝟙 L))
declarations.comment: (3)(a) K pseudo-coherent and L bounded below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_right
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A6H] (3)(a).** The affine comparison is covariantly natural in the
bounded-below argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso_natural_right (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    {K L L' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hL : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).plus L)
    (hL' : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).plus L') (g : L ⟶ L') :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom (Spec R).sheaf).obj
        (op ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.obj K))).map
          ((tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.map g) ≫
      (affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso R K L' hK hL').hom =
    (affinePseudoCoherentDerivedSheafHomIso R K L hK hL).hom ≫
      (tilde.functor R).mapDerivedCategory.map
        ((StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := R)).hom.map
          (𝟙 (op K), g))
declarations.comment: (3)(a) K pseudo-coherent and L bounded below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_affineDerivedTildeHomComparison_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A6H] (3)(a), for the canonical comparison.** Let `R` be a commutative ring,
`X = Spec R`, and let `K`, `L` be objects of `D(R)` with `K` pseudo-coherent and `L` bounded below.
Then the canonical comparison

`(RHom_R(K, L))~ ⟶ R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K̃, L̃)`

of `AlgebraicGeometry.affineDerivedTildeHomComparison` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_affineDerivedTildeHomComparison_of_isPseudoCoherent (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hL : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).plus L) :
    IsIso (affineDerivedTildeHomComparison R K L)
declarations.comment: (3)(a) K pseudo-coherent and L bounded below: the canonical comparison is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedCategoryB_derivedSheafHom_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A6H, part (2).** Let `Y` be a scheme, let `E` be a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_Y)` and let `F` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then the derived internal Hom
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(E, F)` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`: all of its cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent.

The affine opens of `Y` cover it, so by the locality of quasi-coherence it is enough to see that
each cohomology sheaf restricts to a quasi-coherent module on every affine open `U`. Restriction
along `U.ι` commutes with the derived internal Hom by [Stacks, Tag 08DL], keeps `E` perfect by
[Stacks, Tag 09UA] and keeps `F` in `D_QCoh`, so the restriction is the derived internal Hom of
the restrictions on the affine scheme `U`, where
`derivedCategoryB_derivedSheafHom_of_isPerfect_of_isAffine` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryB_derivedSheafHom_of_isPerfect (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (E F : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Y.sheaf))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := Y.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hF : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf) F) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj (op E)).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (2) on an arbitrary scheme: the derived internal Hom out of a perfect object into an object of D_QCoh has quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyBoundedBelow_derivedSheafHom_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
Let `Y` be a scheme, let `E` be a pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_Y)` and let `F` be an
object of `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then `R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(E, F)` is locally bounded below: every point of `Y`
has an open neighbourhood over which the cohomology sheaves vanish in all sufficiently negative
degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyBoundedBelow_derivedSheafHom_of_isPseudoCoherent (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (E F : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Y.sheaf))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Y.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hF : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf) F) :
    RingedSpace.IsLocallyBoundedBelow Y.toRingedSpace
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj (op E)).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (1) on an arbitrary scheme: the derived internal Hom out of a pseudo-coherent object into an object of D⁺_QCoh is locally bounded below

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedCategoryB_derivedSheafHom_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A6H, part (1).** Let `Y` be a scheme, let `E` be a pseudo-coherent
object of `D(𝒪_Y)` and let `F` be an object of `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then the derived internal Hom
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(E, F)` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`: all of its cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent.

The affine opens of `Y` cover it, so by the locality of quasi-coherence it is enough to see that
each cohomology sheaf restricts to a quasi-coherent module on every affine open `U`. Restriction
along `U.ι` commutes with the derived internal Hom by [Stacks, Tag 08DL], keeps `E`
pseudo-coherent by [Stacks, Tag 08CC] and keeps `F` in `D⁺_QCoh`, so the restriction is the
derived internal Hom of the restrictions on the affine scheme `U`, where
`derivedCategoryB_derivedSheafHom_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_isAffine` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryB_derivedSheafHom_of_isPseudoCoherent (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (E F : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Y.sheaf))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Y.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hF : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf) F) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Y.ringCatSheaf)
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Y.sheaf).obj (op E)).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (1) on an arbitrary scheme: the derived internal Hom out of a pseudo-coherent object into an object of D⁺_QCoh has quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedSheafHom_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
Let `Z` be a scheme, let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_Z)` which is pseudo-coherent and
cohomologically bounded above, and let `F` lie in `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Z)`.  Then `R𝓗om_{𝒪_Z}(E, F)` lies
in `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Z)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedSheafHom_of_isPseudoCoherent (Z : Scheme.{u})
    (E F : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Z.sheaf))
    (hE : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Z.toRingedSpace) E)
    (hE' : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedAbove E)
    (hF : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Z.ringCatSheaf) F) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Z.ringCatSheaf)
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom Z.sheaf).obj (op E)).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (1) with the lower bound, on an arbitrary scheme, for a cohomologically bounded-above pseudo-coherent first argument

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffineExt.hasInjectiveAmplitude_extD_locMap
declarations.doc:
**Injective amplitude is preserved by localization.** Over a Noetherian ring `R`, if `L` in
`D(R)` has injective amplitude in `[a, b]`, then `L ⊗_R R_f` has injective amplitude in `[a, b]`
over `R_f`.

A bounded complex of injective `R`-modules representing `L` is carried degreewise, and in the
same degrees, to a bounded complex of injective `R_f`-modules representing `L ⊗_R R_f`: the
terms stay injective by [Stacks, Tag 0A6I], the bounds are preserved because an additive functor
carries zero objects to zero objects, and the complex still represents the localization because
extension of scalars along a localization is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasInjectiveAmplitude_extD_locMap (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (a b : ℤ) (f : R)
    (hL : StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.HasInjectiveAmplitude L a b) :
    StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.HasInjectiveAmplitude ((extD (locMap R f)).obj L) a b
declarations.comment: injective amplitude is preserved by localization

declarations.name: Module.tensorProduct_polynomial_hasInjectiveDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A6J.** Extending an injective module over a Noetherian ring to the
one-variable polynomial ring gives a module of injective dimension at most one.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorProduct_polynomial_hasInjectiveDimensionLE
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (E : Type v) [AddCommGroup E] [Module A E] [Module.Injective A E] :
    HasInjectiveDimensionLE
      (ModuleCat.of (Polynomial A) (TensorProduct A (Polynomial A) E)) 1

declarations.name: isSerreClass_isIPowerTorsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6K.** The modules annihilated elementwise by positive powers of a finitely
generated ideal form a Serre subcategory of the category of modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSerreClass_isIPowerTorsion
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG) :
    CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass
      ((fun M : ModuleCat.{v} R => IsIPowerTorsion R M I) :
        CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty (ModuleCat.{v} R))

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedInclusion_adj_derivedPowerTorsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6L.** Local cohomology `RΓ_I`, as the named total right derived functor of
the `I`-power-torsion-submodule functor, is right adjoint to the derived inclusion of the
category of `I`-power-torsion modules into `D(A)`. Its counit is induced by the underived
torsion-submodule inclusion, compatibly with the total right derived unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedInclusion_adj_derivedPowerTorsion
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    let P : ObjectProperty (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) := fun M ↦ IsIPowerTorsion A M I
    letI : P.IsSerreClass := isSerreClass_isIPowerTorsion I hI
    letI : PreservesFiniteLimits P.ι :=
      ObjectProperty.preservesFiniteLimits_ι_of_isWeakSerreClass P
    letI : PreservesFiniteColimits P.ι :=
      ObjectProperty.preservesFiniteColimits_ι_of_isWeakSerreClass P
    ∃ adj : P.ι.mapDerivedCategory ⊣ derivedPowerTorsion.{u, v} A I hI,
      IsCanonicalDerivedPowerTorsionCounit.{u, v} A I hI adj.counit

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsion_isZero_of_isIso_smul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6M.** Let `I` be a finitely generated ideal of `A` and let `K ∈ D(A)` be such that
multiplication by some `f ∈ I` is an isomorphism of `K` (e.g. `K` is a complex of
`A_f`-modules). Then `RΓ_I(K) = 0`, where `RΓ_I` is the derived functor of `H^0_I` with values
in the derived category of `I`-power-torsion modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPowerTorsion_isZero_of_isIso_smul
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (f : A) (hf : f ∈ I) (hiso : IsIso (f • 𝟙 K)) :
    IsZero ((derivedPowerTorsion.{u, v} A I hI).obj K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.powerTorsionComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6N.** The canonical functor from the derived category of `I`-power-torsion
`A`-modules to the full subcategory of `D(A)` on the objects with `I`-power-torsion cohomology.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def powerTorsionComparison
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    DerivedCategory (PowerTorsionModule A I hI) ⥤
      PowerTorsionDerivedCategory A I hI

declarations.name: Dualizing.bijective_derivedInclusion_map_singleFunctor
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of power-torsion modules induces a bijection on derived
morphisms between modules concentrated in degree zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_derivedInclusion_map_singleFunctor
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (M N : PowerTorsionModule.{u, v} A I hI) :
    let F := (powerTorsionModuleProperty A I hI).ι.mapDerivedCategory
    let X := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (PowerTorsionModule.{u, v} A I hI) 0).obj M
    let Y := (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
      (PowerTorsionModule.{u, v} A I hI) 0).obj N
    Function.Bijective (fun f : X ⟶ Y ↦ F.map f)
declarations.comment: part (1), the Hom comparison

declarations.name: Dualizing.bijective_mapExt_one_powerTorsionModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6P, Ext¹ comparison.** The exact inclusion of the category of
`I`-power-torsion modules into all `A`-modules induces a bijection on Ext¹.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_mapExt_one_powerTorsionModule
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (M N : PowerTorsionModule.{u, v} A I hI) :
    Function.Bijective
      ((powerTorsionModuleProperty A I hI).ι.mapExtAddHom M N 1)
declarations.comment: part (2), the Ext¹ comparison

declarations.name: Dualizing.exists_not_surjective_mapExt_two_powerTorsionModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6P (3).** The comparison map
`Ext²_{D(I^∞-torsion)}(M, N) ⟶ Ext²_{D(A)}(M, N)` between `I`-power-torsion modules is not
surjective in general: there is a commutative ring `A`, a finitely generated (indeed principal)
ideal `I`, and `I`-power-torsion modules `M` and `N` for which the inclusion of the torsion
category does not hit every class of `Ext²_A(M, N)`.

Parts (1) and (2) of the source, that the comparison is bijective on `Hom` and on `Ext¹`, are
`Dualizing.bijective_derivedInclusion_map_singleFunctor` and
`Dualizing.bijective_mapExt_one_powerTorsionModule`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_surjective_mapExt_two_powerTorsionModule :
    ∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
      (M N : PowerTorsionModule.{0, 0} A I hI),
      ¬ Function.Surjective
        ((powerTorsionModuleProperty A I hI).ι.mapExtAddHom M N 2)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: Dualizing.exists_not_isEquivalence_powerTorsionComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6P (4).** The comparison functor of Stacks 0A6N,
`D(I^∞-torsion) ⟶ D_{I^∞-torsion}(A)`, is not an equivalence in general.

This is part (3) together with
`Dualizing.not_isEquivalence_powerTorsionComparison_of_not_surjective_mapExt`: an equivalence
would be bijective on `Extⁿ` in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_isEquivalence_powerTorsionComparison :
    ∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG),
      ¬ (powerTorsionComparison.{0, 0} A I hI).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: Dualizing.bijective_hom_and_ext_one_and_exists_not_surjective_ext_two_and_not_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6P, all four parts.** For every ring `A`, every finitely generated ideal
`I ⊆ A` and all `I`-power-torsion `A`-modules `M` and `N`:

1. `Hom_{D(A)}(M, N) = Hom_{D(I^∞-torsion)}(M, N)`;
2. `Ext¹_{D(A)}(M, N) = Ext¹_{D(I^∞-torsion)}(M, N)`;
3. `Ext²_{D(I^∞-torsion)}(M, N) ⟶ Ext²_{D(A)}(M, N)` is not surjective in general;
4. the comparison functor `D(I^∞-torsion) ⟶ D_{I^∞-torsion}(A)` of Stacks 0A6N is not an
   equivalence in general.

Parts (1) and (2) are universally quantified and parts (3) and (4) are existential, exactly as
in the source. The four conjuncts are
`Dualizing.bijective_derivedInclusion_map_singleFunctor`,
`Dualizing.bijective_mapExt_one_powerTorsionModule`,
`Dualizing.exists_not_surjective_mapExt_two_powerTorsionModule` and
`Dualizing.exists_not_isEquivalence_powerTorsionComparison`, each of which carries the tag for
its own clause.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_hom_and_ext_one_and_exists_not_surjective_ext_two_and_not_isEquivalence :
    (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
        (M N : PowerTorsionModule.{u, v} A I hI),
        Function.Bijective fun f :
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (PowerTorsionModule.{u, v} A I hI) 0).obj M ⟶
              (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (PowerTorsionModule.{u, v} A I hI) 0).obj N ↦
          (powerTorsionModuleProperty A I hI).ι.mapDerivedCategory.map f) ∧
      (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
        (M N : PowerTorsionModule.{u, v} A I hI),
        Function.Bijective ((powerTorsionModuleProperty A I hI).ι.mapExtAddHom M N 1)) ∧
      (∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
        (M N : PowerTorsionModule.{0, 0} A I hI),
        ¬ Function.Surjective
          ((powerTorsionModuleProperty A I hI).ι.mapExtAddHom M N 2)) ∧
      (∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG),
        ¬ (powerTorsionComparison.{0, 0} A I hI).IsEquivalence)
declarations.comment: all four parts conjoined

declarations.name: Dualizing.localCohomologyFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6Q.** Local cohomology with support in `V(I)`, valued in the full subcategory of
derived objects with `I`-power-torsion cohomology.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localCohomologyFunctor
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A) ⥤
      PowerTorsionDerivedCategory A I hI
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: Dualizing.localCohomologyRightAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6R, local cohomology right adjoint.** Let `A` be a ring and `I ⊆ A` a finitely
generated ideal. The inclusion `D_{I^∞-torsion}(A) → D(A)` of the derived category of objects with
`I`-power-torsion cohomology has a right adjoint. This construction supplies the functor
`RΓ_Z : D(A) → D_{I^∞-torsion}(A)` for `Z = V(I)` of equation (47.9.0.1), the functor which
Section 47.9 of the Stacks project, [Stacks, Tag 0952], sets out to construct.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localCohomologyRightAdjoint
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    Σ F : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A) ⥤
        PowerTorsionDerivedCategory A I hI,
      (derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI).ι ⊣ F
declarations.comment: local_cohomology_right_adjoint

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.CechFormula.localCohomologyCechIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6R, the Čech formula.** For a finitely generated ideal `I = (f₁, …, f_r)` of `A`,
local cohomology `RΓ_Z` with `Z = V(I)` is, as a functor on `D(A)`, the derived tensor product
with the extended alternating Čech complex of `f`. Normalized by
`localCohomologyCechIso_comp_augmentation`.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomologyCechIso (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    Dualizing.localCohomologyFunctor A I hI ⋙
        (Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI).ι ≅
      (canonicalDerivedTensorProductFunctor A).obj (cechRegularObject.{u, u} f)
declarations.comment: the Čech formula, functorially in K ∈ D(A); module universe = ring universe

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.CechFormula.localCohomologyCechIso_comp_augmentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6R, the normalization of the Čech formula.** Composing it with the Čech comparison
map gives the counit of the adjunction that defines local cohomology, which is what makes the
isomorphism of `localCohomologyCechIso` the canonical one.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCohomologyCechIso_comp_augmentation (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) :
    (localCohomologyCechIso A I hI f hf).hom ≫ cechTensorToId A f =
      (Dualizing.localCohomologyAdjunction A I hI).counit
declarations.comment: normalization of the Čech formula against the local-cohomology counit

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomologySequence.cohomologyWithSupportTildeSpanSingletonIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6T degreewise, for a module and a principal ideal.**  Let `A` be a Noetherian
ring, `f : A`, `X = Spec A` and `Z = V(f)`.  For an `A`-module `M` the cohomology of `X` with
support in `Z` of the sheaf `M̃`, read as an `A`-module, is the algebraic local cohomology
`H^n_Z(M)` of `M`, in every degree `n`.
declarations.statement:
def cohomologyWithSupportTildeSpanSingletonIso [IsNoetherianRing A] (f : A)
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) (n : ℕ) :
    (globalToBase A).obj ((cohomologyWithSupport (Ideal.span {f}) n).obj (tildeSheaf M)) ≅
      (localCohomologySpanSingleton A f n).obj M
declarations.comment: degreewise, for a module and a principal ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomologyTilde.mem_sectionsWithSupportIn_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6T in degree zero.** An element of `M` is an algebraic section with support in a
subset `T` of the spectrum exactly when the corresponding global section of `M̃` has all its
germs outside `T` equal to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_sectionsWithSupportIn_iff (T : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) (m : M) :
    m ∈ Stacks.LocalCohomology.sectionsWithSupportIn R T M ↔
      (tilde.toOpen M ⊤) m ∈ (supportedSectionsSubmodule T (tilde M)).obj (op ⊤)
declarations.comment: degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomologyTilde.image_sectionsWithSupportIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6T in degree zero.** The canonical isomorphism from `M` to the global sections of
`M̃` carries the algebraic sections with support in `T` onto the geometric ones.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_sectionsWithSupportIn (T : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)) :
    (tilde.toOpen M ⊤).hom '' (Stacks.LocalCohomology.sectionsWithSupportIn R T M : Set M) =
      ((supportedSectionsSubmodule T (tilde M)).obj (op ⊤) :
        Set ((tilde M).val.obj (op ⊤)))
declarations.comment: degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomologyTilde.image_primaryComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6T in degree zero.** For a finitely generated ideal `I` and `Z = V(I)`, the
canonical isomorphism from `M` to the global sections of `M̃` carries the degree-zero local
cohomology `H⁰_Z(M)`, namely the `I`-power-torsion submodule, onto the global sections of `M̃`
with support in `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem image_primaryComponent :
    (tilde.toOpen M ⊤).hom '' (I.primaryComponent M : Set M) =
      ((supportedSectionsSubmodule (zeroLocus (I : Set R)) (tilde M)).obj (op ⊤) :
        Set ((tilde M).val.obj (op ⊤)))
declarations.comment: degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomologyTilde.sectionsWithSupportTildeIso
declarations.doc:
For a closed subset `T` of `Spec A`, the global sections with support in `T` of the sheaf
`M̃`, read as an `A`-module, are the algebraic sections of `M` with support in `T`, naturally in
`M`.
declarations.comment: degree zero, as a natural isomorphism of functors

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomologyTilde.localCohomologyIsoDerivedSectionsWithSupport
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a ring, let `I ⊆ A` be a finitely generated ideal and set `Z = V(I) ⊆ X = Spec A`.
For `K ∈ D(A)`, corresponding to `K̃ ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` by [Stacks, Tag 06Z0], there is an
isomorphism

`RΓ_Z(K) ≅ RΓ_Z(X, K̃)`

in `D(A)`, functorial in `K`. On the left is the local cohomology functor of
[Stacks, Tag 0A6Q], followed by the inclusion of the complexes with `I`-power-torsion cohomology
into `D(A)`. On the right is the total right derived functor
`RΓ_Z(X, -) : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_X(X))` of `F ↦ Γ_Z(X, F)` on the unbounded derived category, as in
[Stacks, Section 0G6Y], applied to `K̃` and read as a complex of `A`-modules by restriction of
scalars along the canonical isomorphism `A ≅ 𝒪_X(X)`.

The ring is arbitrary, `K` is an arbitrary object of the unbounded derived category, and the
only hypothesis on `I` is finite generation.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomologyIsoDerivedSectionsWithSupport :
    Dualizing.localCohomologyFunctor (A : Type u) I hI ⋙
        (Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsionProperty (A : Type u) I hI).ι ≅
      (tildeSheafFunctor A).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        canonicalDerivedSectionsWithSupport (Spec A).toRingedSpace (vanishingSet A I)
          (isClosed_vanishingSet A I) ⋙
        (globalToBase A).mapDerivedCategory

declarations.name: Dualizing.compareTorsionFunctors
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6U.** The canonical natural transformation from derived power torsion followed
by the comparison functor to local cohomology with support in `V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def compareTorsionFunctors
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    (derivedPowerTorsion.{u, v} A I hI ⋙
      powerTorsionComparison.{u, max u v} A I hI) ⟶
      localCohomologyFunctor.{u, max u v} A I hI

declarations.name: Dualizing.isIso_derivedCompletion_map_localCohomologyCounit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6W, completion after local cohomology.** For a finitely generated ideal `I` of a
commutative ring `A` and `Z = V(I)`, the counit `RΓ_Z(K) ⟶ K` of the adjunction defining local
cohomology becomes an isomorphism after derived `I`-completion; equivalently
`RΓ_Z(K)^∧ = K^∧` in `D(A)`, naturally in `K`.

The statement holds for every reflection `C` of `D(A)` onto the derived `I`-complete objects, so
it is independent of the chosen model of derived completion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletion_map_localCohomologyCounit
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A) ⥤ DerivedCompleteDerivedCategory A I)
    (hC : C ⊣ (derivedCompleteProperty A I).ι) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) :
    IsIso ((C ⋙ (derivedCompleteProperty A I).ι).map
      ((localCohomologyAdjunction A I hI).counit.app K))
declarations.comment: completion_after_local

declarations.name: Dualizing.isIso_localCohomology_map_derivedCompletionUnit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6W, local cohomology after completion.** For a finitely generated ideal
`I = (f₁, …, f_r)` of a commutative ring `A` and `Z = V(I)`, the derived-completion unit
`K ⟶ K^∧` induces an isomorphism `RΓ_Z(K) ⟶ RΓ_Z(K^∧)` in `D(A)`, naturally in `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_localCohomology_map_derivedCompletionUnit (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (f : Fin r → A) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :
    IsIso (((localCohomologyRightAdjoint A I hI).1 ⋙
      (derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI).ι).map
        ((DerivedCompletion.derivedCompletionUnit A f).app K))
declarations.comment: local_after_completion

declarations.name: Dualizing.torsionCompleteEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A6X.** For a finitely generated ideal `I` of a commutative ring `A` and `Z = V(I)`,
derived `I`-completion and local cohomology with support in `Z` are quasi-inverse equivalences
between the full subcategory of `D(A)` of complexes with `I`-power-torsion cohomology and the
full subcategory of derived `I`-complete complexes. The two functors of the equivalence are
identified with derived completion and local cohomology by natural isomorphisms, not merely
objectwise.
declarations.statement:
def torsionCompleteEquivalence (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    Σ E : PowerTorsionDerivedCategory.{u, v} A I hI ≌ DerivedCompleteDerivedCategory A I,
      (E.functor ≅ ((derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI).ι ⋙ derivedCompletion A I hI)) ×
      (E.inverse ≅ ((derivedCompleteProperty A I).ι ⋙ localCohomologyFunctor A I hI))

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedHomCompletionTorsionIso
declarations.doc:
For `A` a commutative ring, `I` a finitely generated ideal, `Z = V(I)`, `(-)^∧` derived
`I`-adic completion and `RΓ_Z` local cohomology, the canonical isomorphism
`RHom_A(K^∧, L^∧) ≅ RHom_A(RΓ_Z(K), RΓ_Z(L))` in `D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedHomCompletionTorsionIso (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :
    (StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := A)).hom.obj
        (Opposite.op ((DerivedCompletion.derivedCompletionFunctor A f).obj K),
          (DerivedCompletion.derivedCompletionFunctor A f).obj L) ≅
      (StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := A)).hom.obj
        (Opposite.op ((localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI).obj K),
          (localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI).obj L)

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedCompletionDerivedHomTorsionNatIso
declarations.doc:
For a finite family `f` generating an ideal `I` of a commutative ring `A`, with `Z = V(I)`,
there is an isomorphism `RHom_A(-, L)^∧ ≅ RHom_A(RΓ_Z(-), RΓ_Z(L))` of contravariant functors
on `D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCompletionDerivedHomTorsionNatIso (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (f : Fin r → A)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :
    derivedHomInto A L ⋙ DerivedCompletion.derivedCompletionFunctor A f ≅
      (localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI).op ⋙
        derivedHomInto A ((localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI).obj L)
declarations.comment: natural in the source object

declarations.name: Dualizing.AnyModel.restrictScalarsDerived_adj_derivedHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A70.** Derived coextension of scalars `RHom_A(B, -)` is right adjoint to restriction
of scalars from `D(B)` to `D(A)`, for arbitrary chosen models of the two derived categories.

This is the model-generic form of `Dualizing.restrictScalarsDerived_adj_derivedHom`, which is
silently specialised to `HasDerivedCategory.standard`; it is recovered from this by supplying that
instance.
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictScalarsDerived_adj_derivedHom (f : A →+* B) :
    Nonempty ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max v u u'} f).mapDerivedCategory ⊣
      derivedHom.{u, v, u', w, w'} f)

declarations.name: Dualizing.restrictDerivedHomIsoDerivedHomAlong
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A71**, the displayed formula, with both derived functors constructed:
`φ_* RHom(B, K) = RHom_A(B, K)`, where `φ_* : D(B) ⥤ D(A)` is restriction of scalars.

Restricting the constructed derived coextension functor `Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHom f` to
`D(A)` is the constructed `A`-valued derived Hom functor `Dualizing.derivedHomAlong f`, by the
unique isomorphism compatible with the two derived units. This is
`Dualizing.derivedCoextendScalarsCompDerivedRestrictScalarsIso` with all four of its parameters
discharged: `RH`, `β` by `Dualizing.derivedHomAlong`, `Dualizing.derivedHomAlongUnit`, and
`RF`, `α` by `Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHom`, `Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHomUnit`.
declarations.statement:
def restrictDerivedHomIsoDerivedHomAlong (f : A →+* B) :
    { e : AnyModel.derivedHom.{u, v, u, wA, wB} f ⋙
          (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max v u} f).mapDerivedCategory ≅
        derivedHomAlong.{u, v, wA} f //
      restrictedDerivedUnit f (AnyModel.derivedHom.{u, v, u, wA, wB} f)
            (AnyModel.derivedHomUnit.{u, v, wA, wB} f) ≫
          Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh e.hom =
        derivedHomAlongUnit.{u, v, wA} f }
declarations.comment: derived Hom after restriction, with both derived functors constructed: RHom(B, -) is AnyModel.derivedHom, the total right derived functor of coextension of scalars, and RHom_A(B, -) is derivedHomAlong, that of Hom_A(B, -). Both rings in one universe, modules in max v u, arbitrary models of the two derived categories

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedHomHomologyLinearEquivExt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A71**, the "in particular" clause, with the derived functor constructed:
`R^q Hom(B, K) = Ext^q_A(B, K)`.

The cohomology of the constructed derived coextension functor `Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHom f`,
restricted to `A`-modules, is `Ext^q_A(B, K)`, `A`-linearly, naturally in `K` and normalized by
the derived unit. This is `Dualizing.derivedCoextendScalarsHomologyLinearEquivExt` with its
parameters `RF`, `α` discharged by `Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHom` and
`Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHomUnit`.
declarations.comment: cohomology as Ext, with the derived functor constructed: RHom(B, -) is AnyModel.derivedHom, the total right derived functor of coextension of scalars. Both rings in one universe, modules in max v u, arbitrary models of the two derived categories

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedCoextendScalarsCompDerivedRestrictScalarsIso
declarations.doc:
Restricting derived coextension gives `RHom_A(B, -)`, with the comparison uniquely
specified by its compatibility with the derived units.

Both derived functors enter as arbitrary right derived functors presented by their universal
properties, so the statement is independent of the models chosen for them. That data is
discharged by `Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHom` with `Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHomUnit` on the
left and by `Dualizing.derivedHomAlong` with `Dualizing.derivedHomAlongUnit` on the right,
giving the unconditional `Dualizing.restrictDerivedHomIsoDerivedHomAlong`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCoextendScalarsCompDerivedRestrictScalarsIso
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) (.up ℤ))]
    (RH : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A))
    (β : homAlongToDerivedCategory f ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RH)
    [RH.IsRightDerivedFunctor β (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) (.up ℤ))] :
    { e : RF ⋙ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max v u} f).mapDerivedCategory ≅ RH //
      restrictedDerivedUnit f RF α ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh e.hom = β }
declarations.comment: derived Hom after restriction, for arbitrary right derived functors RF of coextension of scalars and RH of Hom_A(B, -); the data RF, alpha, RH, beta is discharged by AnyModel.derivedHom with AnyModel.derivedHomUnit and derivedHomAlong with derivedHomAlongUnit, giving the unconditional restrictDerivedHomIsoDerivedHomAlong

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedCoextendScalarsHomologyLinearEquivExt
declarations.doc:
The cohomology of derived coextension is Ext, naturally and compatibly with the derived
unit (and hence with the restriction comparison).

Derived coextension enters as an arbitrary right derived functor presented by its universal
property, so the statement is independent of the model chosen for it. That data is discharged by
`Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHom` with `Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHomUnit`, giving the
unconditional `Dualizing.derivedHomHomologyLinearEquivExt`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCoextendScalarsHomologyLinearEquivExt
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) (.up ℤ))] :
    HomologyExtComparison f RF α
declarations.comment: cohomology as Ext, for an arbitrary right derived functor RF of coextension of scalars; the data RF, alpha is discharged by AnyModel.derivedHom with AnyModel.derivedHomUnit, giving the unconditional derivedHomHomologyLinearEquivExt

declarations.name: Dualizing.isBoundedBelowCoherent_obj_rightDerivedCoextendScalars
declarations.doc:
Derived coextension of scalars along a finite homomorphism of Noetherian rings sends
bounded-below complexes with coherent cohomology to bounded-below complexes with coherent
cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBoundedBelowCoherent_obj_rightDerivedCoextendScalars
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A)] [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} B)]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : f.Finite)
    (RF : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} B))
    (alpha : (ModuleCat.coextendScalars f).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ RF)
    [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor alpha
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    {K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A)}
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (fun M : ModuleCat.{max v u} A ↦ Module.Finite A M) K) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (fun M : ModuleCat.{max v u} B ↦ Module.Finite B M) (RF.obj K)

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.sheafHomExactSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A75 (the functor).** The sheaf Hom from `𝒪_Z` with exact support,
regarded as a functor from `𝒪_X`-modules to `𝒪_Z`-modules.  It is the internal Hom
`SheafHom_{𝒪_X}(i_* 𝒪_Z, -)`, which is annihilated by the kernel ideal and therefore descends
to `Z`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomExactSupport :
    SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.Z)
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportIsoHomSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A75 (the internal Hom identification).** After pushforward to `X`,
sheaf Hom with exact support is naturally the internal Hom `SheafHom_{𝒪_X}(i_* 𝒪_Z, -)`,
regarded as an `𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportIsoHomSheaf :
    S.sheafHomExactSupport ⋙ modulePushforward S.i ≅
      homSheaf (structureSheafHom S.i) ⋙
        SheafOfModules.restrictScalars (structureSheafHom S.i)
declarations.comment: the internal Hom identification

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A75 (adjunction).** Pushforward from a closed quotient ringed
subspace is left adjoint to sheaf Hom with exact support.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction :
    modulePushforward S.i ⊣ S.sheafHomExactSupport
declarations.comment: the adjunction

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction_counit_app
declarations.doc:
The counit of the exact-support adjunction is, under the internal Hom identification,
evaluation of a local homomorphism at the section `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction_counit_app
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X)) (U : Opens S.X)
    (s : ((modulePushforward S.i).obj (S.sheafHomExactSupport.obj F)).val.obj (op U)) :
    (S.modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction.counit.app F).val.app (op U) s =
      Stacks.PresheafOfModules.CoextendScalars.invSecVal (structureSheafHom S.i).hom F.val (op U)
        ((S.modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportIsoHomSheaf.hom.app F).val.app (op U) s)
declarations.comment: the counit is evaluation at one

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A75 (sections).** If `V ⊆ Z` is the inverse image of `U ⊆ X`, sections
over `V` of sheaf Hom with exact support are canonically the sections of `F` over `U` annihilated
by the kernel ideal.  The map is `ψ ↦ ψ(1)|_U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv (U : Opens S.X) (V : Opens S.Z)
    (hUV : (opensMap S.i).obj U = V) :
    ((S.sheafHomExactSupport.obj F).val.obj (op V) : Type u) ≃+
      S.sectionsLocallyAnnihilatedByKernelIdeal F U
declarations.comment: the description of sections

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A75.** The section equivalence is the map induced by the adjunction
counit; equivalently, after the internal Hom identification it evaluates a local homomorphism
at `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv_apply
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X)) (U : Opens S.X) (V : Opens S.Z)
    (hUV : (opensMap S.i).obj U = V)
    (s : (S.sheafHomExactSupport.obj F).val.obj (op V)) :
    (S.sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv F U V hUV s).1 =
      (S.modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction.counit.app F).val.app (op U)
        (by
          change (S.sheafHomExactSupport.obj F).val.obj
            (op ((opensMap S.i).obj U))
          exact hUV.symm ▸ s)
declarations.comment: evaluation characterization of the description of sections

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A75.** The section identification for sheaf Hom with exact support is
natural in the `𝒪_X`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv_naturality
    {F G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X)} (f : F ⟶ G)
    (U : Opens S.X) (V : Opens S.Z) (hUV : (opensMap S.i).obj U = V)
    (s : (S.sheafHomExactSupport.obj F).val.obj (op V)) :
    ((S.sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv G U V hUV
      ((S.sheafHomExactSupport.map f).val.app (op V) s)).1) =
        f.val.app (op U) ((S.sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv F U V hUV s).1)
declarations.comment: naturality of the description of sections

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A75.** The section identification commutes with restriction to a
smaller open subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv_restrict
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X))
    (U U' : Opens S.X) (hUU' : U' ≤ U)
    (V V' : Opens S.Z) (hVV' : V' ≤ V)
    (hUV : (opensMap S.i).obj U = V) (hU'V' : (opensMap S.i).obj U' = V')
    (s : (S.sheafHomExactSupport.obj F).val.obj (op V)) :
    (S.sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv F U' V' hU'V'
      ((S.sheafHomExactSupport.obj F).val.map (homOfLE hVV').op s)).1 =
        F.val.map (homOfLE hUU').op
          ((S.sectionsSheafHomExactSupportEquiv F U V hUV s).1)
declarations.comment: restriction naturality of the description of sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.LocallySmall.derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A76, at the locally small derived categories.** Derived pushforward
along a closed immersion of schemes, read as a closed quotient morphism of ringed spaces, is left
adjoint to the right derived functor of sheaf Hom with exact support: `Ri_* ⊣ R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)`.

The abstract input `Stacks.DerivedFunctor.derivedAdjunction` is stated at a free
`[HasDerivedCategory.{w} _]` binder, so the only thing the standard model was supplying is the
model itself.
declarations.statement:
def derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction :
    (modulePushforward (closedQuotient i).i).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ derivedSheafHomExactSupport i
declarations.comment: at the locally small derived categories, the model at which the direct-sum and Brown-representability statements about D(O_X) have content; the standard-model form is RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction, which is about a different pair of categories

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A76.** Derived pushforward along a closed quotient morphism of
ringed spaces is left adjoint to the right derived functor of sheaf Hom with exact support:
`Ri_* ⊣ R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction :
    (modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategory ⊣ S.derivedSheafHomExactSupport

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction_unit_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A76.** The unit of the derived adjunction is the one induced by the
unit of the adjunction of [Stacks, Tag 0A75] and the two derived-functor comparison maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction_unit_app
    (M : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.Z)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) :
    S.derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction.unit.app
          (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj M) ≫
        S.derivedSheafHomExactSupport.map
          ((modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.hom.app M) =
      DerivedCategory.Qh.map
          ((Adjunction.mapHomotopyCategoryAdjunction
            S.modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).unit.app M) ≫
        S.derivedSheafHomExactSupportComparison.app
          (((modulePushforward S.i).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M)

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction_counit_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A76.** The counit of the derived adjunction is the one induced by
the counit of the adjunction of [Stacks, Tag 0A75] and the two derived-functor comparison
maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction_counit_app
    (K : HomotopyCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing S.X)) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) :
    (modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (S.derivedSheafHomExactSupportComparison.app K) ≫
        S.derivedModulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction.counit.app
          (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj K) =
      (modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh.hom.app
          ((S.sheafHomExactSupport.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map
          ((Adjunction.mapHomotopyCategoryAdjunction
            S.modulePushforwardSheafHomExactSupportAdjunction
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).counit.app K)

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedModulePushforwardDerivedSheafHomExactSupportIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A77.** For a closed quotient morphism `i : Z ⟶ X` of ringed spaces,
derived pushforward of the right derived sheaf Hom with exact support is the right derived
internal Hom from `i_* 𝒪_Z`:

`Ri_* R ℰom(𝒪_Z, K) ≅ R ℰom_{𝒪_X}(i_* 𝒪_Z, K)` naturally in `K ∈ D(𝒪_X)`.

Both sides are right derived functors — the left one because `i_*` is exact, so composing with
it preserves the property — of the two functors identified on the homotopy category by
`mapHomotopyCategoryPushforwardSheafHomExactSupportIso`, which is the underived identification
of [Stacks, Tag 0A75]. The isomorphism is the induced one on right derived functors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivedModulePushforwardDerivedSheafHomExactSupportIso :
    S.derivedSheafHomExactSupport ⋙ (modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategory ≅
      S.derivedHomSheafFromPushforwardStructureSheaf

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedModulePushforwardDerivedSheafHomExactSupportIso_fac
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A77.** The isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 0A77] is compatible with the
comparison maps out of the homotopy category and with the underived identification of
[Stacks, Tag 0A75].
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedModulePushforwardDerivedSheafHomExactSupportIso_fac :
    S.derivedModulePushforwardComparison ≫
        Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh
          S.derivedModulePushforwardDerivedSheafHomExactSupportIso.hom =
      S.mapHomotopyCategoryPushforwardSheafHomExactSupportIso.hom ≫
        S.derivedHomSheafFromPushforwardStructureSheafComparison
declarations.comment: compatibility of the isomorphism with the comparison maps

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedModulePushforwardDerivedSheafHomExactSupportIso_uniq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A77.** The isomorphism of [Stacks, Tag 0A77] is the unique one
compatible with the comparison maps out of the homotopy category.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedModulePushforwardDerivedSheafHomExactSupportIso_uniq
    (e : S.derivedSheafHomExactSupport ⋙ (modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategory ≅
      S.derivedHomSheafFromPushforwardStructureSheaf)
    (he : S.derivedModulePushforwardComparison ≫
        Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Qh e.hom =
      S.mapHomotopyCategoryPushforwardSheafHomExactSupportIso.hom ≫
        S.derivedHomSheafFromPushforwardStructureSheafComparison) :
    e = S.derivedModulePushforwardDerivedSheafHomExactSupportIso
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the isomorphism

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedSheafHomExactSupportPushforwardNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A77.** Derived sheaf Hom with exact support followed by derived
pushforward is the derived internal Hom out of the derived pushforward of the structure sheaf of
the closed subspace: `Ri_* R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -) ≅ R ℰom_X(Ri_* 𝒪_Z, -)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHomExactSupportPushforwardNatIso :
    S.derivedSheafHomExactSupport ⋙ (modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom S.X.sheaf).obj
        (op ((modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (RingedSite.derivedStructureSheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite S.Z.sheaf))))
declarations.comment: via the derived internal Hom bifunctor

declarations.name: RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.ClosedQuotientMorphismOfRingedSpaces.derivedHomSheafFromPushforwardStructureSheafSiteIso
declarations.doc:
**The two right-hand sides of [Stacks, Tag 0A77] agree.** For a closed quotient morphism
`i : Z ⟶ X` of ringed spaces, the right derived functor of coextension of scalars along
`𝒪_X ⟶ i_* 𝒪_Z` is the derived internal Hom of the ringed site of opens of `X` out of
`Ri_* 𝒪_Z`:

`R ℰom_{𝒪_X}(i_* 𝒪_Z, -) ≅ RSheafHom(Ri_* 𝒪_Z, -)`.

Both sides are the common value of the two formalized forms of [Stacks, Tag 0A77], whose shared
left-hand side is `R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)` followed by `i_*` on derived categories.
declarations.statement:
def derivedHomSheafFromPushforwardStructureSheafSiteIso :
    S.derivedHomSheafFromPushforwardStructureSheaf ≅
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom S.X.sheaf).obj
        (op ((modulePushforward S.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (RingedSite.derivedStructureSheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite S.Z.sheaf))))
declarations.comment: the two right-hand sides identified: coextension of scalars and the site-level derived internal Hom bifunctor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.derivedSheafHomExactSupport_mem_derivedCategoryBPlus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A78, part (1).** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a pseudo-coherent closed
immersion of schemes. Then `R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)` maps `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Z)`.

Boundedness below is `isBoundedBelow_derivedSheafHomExactSupport_obj`. For quasi-coherence, the
pushforward `Ri_* R ℰom(𝒪_Z, K)` is the derived internal Hom `R ℰom_{𝒪_X}(Ri_* 𝒪_Z, K)` by
[Stacks, Tag 0A77], and `Ri_* 𝒪_Z` is pseudo-coherent by [Stacks, Tag 0AVX]; part (1) of
[Stacks, Tag 0A6H] makes the cohomology sheaves of that
derived internal Hom quasi-coherent. Since `i_*` is exact it commutes with taking cohomology, so
each cohomology sheaf of `R ℰom(𝒪_Z, K)` has quasi-coherent pushforward, and
`isQuasicoherent_of_pushforward` descends quasi-coherence to `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomExactSupport_mem_derivedCategoryBPlus (hi : PseudoCoherent i)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) K) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Z.ringCatSheaf)
      ((Stacks.ClosedImmersion.closedQuotientOfClosedImmersion
        i).derivedSheafHomExactSupport.obj K)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.derivedSheafHomExactSupport_mem_derivedCategoryBPlus_of_noetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A78, part (1), the locally Noetherian case.** For *every* closed
immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` into a locally Noetherian scheme, `R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)` maps `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into
`D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Z)`: a closed immersion is locally of finite type, hence pseudo-coherent over a
locally Noetherian target by [Stacks, Tag 0684].
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomExactSupport_mem_derivedCategoryBPlus_of_noetherian
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) K) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent Z.ringCatSheaf)
      ((Stacks.ClosedImmersion.closedQuotientOfClosedImmersion
        i).derivedSheafHomExactSupport.obj K)
declarations.comment: part (1) for a locally Noetherian target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_affineDerivedSheafHomComparison_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A78, part (2).** Let `φ : A ⟶ B` be a ring map whose spectrum is a
pseudo-coherent closed immersion `i : Z = Spec B ⟶ X = Spec A`, and let `L` be a bounded-below
object of `D(A)`. Then the comparison map of `affineDerivedSheafHomComparison` is invertible at
`L`:

`(R Hom_A(B, L))^~  ≅  R ℰom(𝒪_Z, L^~)`.

This is the commutativity of the square of part (2): the derived sheafification functors
`D⁺(A) ⥤ D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `D⁺(B) ⥤ D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Z)` intertwine `R Hom_A(B, -)` with
`R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)`.

By the affine case of part (1), `affineDerivedSheafHomExactSupport_mem_derivedCategoryBPlus`, the
target has quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves, so it is the derived sheafification of an object
`N` of `D(B)`, and the comparison is the sheafification of a map `ψ` into `N`. For every `T` in
`D(B)`, composition with `ψ` is, by `map_comp_affineDerivedSheafHomComparison_app`, the composite
of the adjunction bijection of [Stacks, Tag 0A70], full faithfulness of derived sheafification on
`Spec A`, composition with an isomorphism, and the adjunction bijection of [Stacks, Tag 0A76]. So
`ψ` is an isomorphism by Yoneda, and hence so is the comparison.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_affineDerivedSheafHomComparison_app [IsClosedImmersion (Spec.map φ)]
    (hφ : PseudoCoherent (Spec.map φ))
    (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (hL : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow L) :
    IsIso ((affineDerivedSheafHomComparison A B φ).app L)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_affineDerivedSheafHomComparison_app_of_noetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A78, part (2), the locally Noetherian case.** For *every* closed
immersion `Spec B ⟶ Spec A` with `Spec A` locally Noetherian, the comparison map of
`affineDerivedSheafHomComparison` is invertible at every bounded-below object of `D(A)`: a closed
immersion is locally of finite type, hence pseudo-coherent over a locally Noetherian target by
[Stacks, Tag 0684].
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_affineDerivedSheafHomComparison_app_of_noetherian
    [IsLocallyNoetherian (Spec A)] [IsClosedImmersion (Spec.map φ)]
    (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (hL : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow L) :
    IsIso ((affineDerivedSheafHomComparison A B φ).app L)
declarations.comment: part (2) for a locally Noetherian target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedSheafHomExactSupport_mem_derivedCategoryBPlus_coherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A79.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of schemes with `X`
locally Noetherian. Then `R ℰom(𝒪_Z, -)` carries `D⁺_Coh(𝒪_X)` into `D⁺_Coh(𝒪_Z)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomExactSupport_mem_derivedCategoryBPlus_coherent
    {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace)))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules X.ringCatSheaf) K) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.coherentModules Z.ringCatSheaf)
      ((Stacks.ClosedImmersion.closedQuotientOfClosedImmersion
        i).derivedSheafHomExactSupport.obj K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
A dualizing complex over a Noetherian commutative ring is a derived object of finite
injective dimension whose cohomology modules are finite and whose homothety map to its derived
endomorphism complex is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
structure IsDualizingComplex {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{v} A)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) : Prop

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedBiduality
declarations.doc:
**The canonical biduality morphisms, natural in the derived object.** Each component is the
canonical morphism `K ⟶ RHom_A(RHom_A(K, ω), ω)` of
`Dualizing.dualizingBidualityMor`; naturality is `Dualizing.bidualityMor_naturality` at the
adjunction of [stacks 0A63].
declarations.statement:
def derivedBiduality (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) :
    Functor.id (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) ⟶
      opOp (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) ⋙
        (dualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, v} A ω).op ⋙
          dualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, v} A ω
declarations.comment: canonical biduality morphism

declarations.name: Dualizing.dualizingDerivedHom_biduality_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Canonical biduality is a natural isomorphism on objects with finite cohomology.** Each
component is invertible by `Dualizing.isIso_dualizingBidualityMor_of_finiteCohomology`, and a
morphism of a full subcategory is invertible as soon as the underlying morphism is.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingDerivedHom_biduality_isIso
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω) :
    IsIso (coherentDerivedBiduality.{u, v} A ω hω)
declarations.comment: canonical biduality

declarations.name: Dualizing.coherentDualizingDerivedHom_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Derived Hom into a dualizing complex is an anti-equivalence on the derived category of
objects with finite cohomology, [stacks 0A7C].**
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentDualizingDerivedHom_isEquivalence
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω) :
    (coherentDualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, v} A ω hω).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the anti-equivalence on coherent objects

declarations.name: Dualizing.dualizingDerivedHom_plus_iff_minus
declarations.doc:
**On objects with finite cohomology, derived Hom into a dualizing complex exchanges bounded
below with bounded above.** The forward implication is the bound exchange
`Dualizing.dualizingDerivedHom_isLE_of_isGE`; the converse applies the other bound exchange to
`RHom_A(K, ω)` and transports the resulting bound along canonical biduality.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingDerivedHom_plus_iff_minus
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj K)) :
    (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).plus K ↔
      (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).minus
        ((dualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, v} A ω).obj (Opposite.op K))
declarations.comment: exchange of bounded below and bounded above

declarations.name: Dualizing.dualizingDerivedHom_minus_iff_plus
declarations.doc:
**On objects with finite cohomology, derived Hom into a dualizing complex exchanges bounded
above with bounded below.** The forward implication is the bound exchange
`Dualizing.dualizingDerivedHom_isGE_of_isLE`; the converse applies the other bound exchange to
`RHom_A(K, ω)` and transports the resulting bound along canonical biduality.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingDerivedHom_minus_iff_plus
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj K)) :
    (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).minus K ↔
      (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).plus
        ((dualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, v} A ω).obj (Opposite.op K))
declarations.comment: exchange of bounded above and bounded below

declarations.name: Dualizing.boundedCoherentDualizingDerivedHom_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Derived Hom into a dualizing complex is an anti-equivalence on bounded objects with finite
cohomology, [stacks 0A7C].**
declarations.statement:
theorem boundedCoherentDualizingDerivedHom_isEquivalence
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω) :
    (boundedCoherentDualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, v} A ω hω).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the bounded anti-equivalence

declarations.name: Dualizing.nonempty_extIntoOmegaAtIso
declarations.doc:
**The Ext--cohomology comparison for derived Hom**, natural in the source module.
The `ULift` is necessary because derived morphisms live in a larger universe than the modules in
the derived category. This comparison does not require `ω` to be dualizing.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_extIntoOmegaAtIso
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (i : ℤ) :
    Nonempty (extIntoOmegaAt.{u, v} A ω i ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) 0).op ⋙
        dualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, v} A ω ⋙
          DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i ⋙
            ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{max (u + 1) (v + 1), max u v} A)
declarations.comment: Ext–cohomology comparison

declarations.name: Dualizing.dualizingDerivedHomFunctor
declarations.doc:
The contravariant functor `RHom_A(-, ω)` defined using the canonical derived
tensor--Hom adjunction.
declarations.statement:
public def dualizingDerivedHomFunctor
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) :
    (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))ᵒᵖ ⥤
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: Dualizing.dualizingDerivedHom_bounded
declarations.doc:
On objects with finite cohomology, derived Hom into a dualizing complex preserves
cohomological boundedness.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dualizingDerivedHom_bounded [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj K))
    (hK' : (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).bounded K) :
    (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t).bounded
      ((dualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, v} A ω).obj (.op K))
declarations.comment: preservation of bounded coherent objects

declarations.name: Dualizing.dualizingDerivedHom_finiteCohomology
declarations.doc:
Derived Hom into a dualizing complex has finite cohomology when its argument does.

This is Tag 0G4H specialized to a dualizing complex as target: a dualizing complex has finite
cohomology and finite injective dimension, which are exactly the two hypotheses that tag puts
on its second argument.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dualizingDerivedHom_finiteCohomology [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj K)) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) i).obj
        ((dualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, v} A ω).obj (.op K)))
declarations.comment: preservation of coherent objects

declarations.name: StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.exists_finite_module_detecting_homology_mod_ideal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A7D.** If degree-`i` cohomology of a pseudo-coherent complex over a Noetherian
ring is nonzero modulo an ideal, it is detected by a map to a finite module annihilated by a
power of that ideal, placed in degree `i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_module_detecting_homology_mod_ideal
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) (hK : IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (m : Ideal A) (i : ℤ)
    (hi : Nontrivial
      (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) i).obj K) ⧸
        (m • (⊤ : Submodule A
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) i).obj K))))) :
    ∃ (E : ModuleCat.{v} A), Module.Finite A E ∧
      (∃ n : ℕ, m ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A E) = ⊥) ∧
      ∃ f : K ⟶ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) i).obj E,
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) i).map f ≫
          (DerivedCategory.singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso
            (ModuleCat.{v} A) i).hom.app E ≠ 0

declarations.name: Dualizing.isInvertible_obj_ring_of_linear_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A7E.** An `A`-linear autoequivalence of the bounded derived category of complexes
of `A`-modules with finite cohomology, an equivalence of categories with no compatibility with
the shift or the triangulated structure assumed, sends the ring, placed in degree zero, to an
invertible object of the unbounded derived category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isInvertible_obj_ring_of_linear_isEquivalence [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (F : BoundedCoherentDerivedCategory A ⥤ BoundedCoherentDerivedCategory A)
    [F.IsEquivalence] [F.Linear A] :
    let m := (DerivedCategory.Invertible.derivedCategory_symmetricMonoidalCategory A).choose
    letI := m
    MonoidalCategory.IsInvertible (F.obj (ringObject A)).obj

declarations.name: Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex.exists_iso_derivedTensorProduct_invertible
declarations.doc:
Two dualizing complexes over a Noetherian ring differ by derived tensor product with an
invertible object.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsDualizingComplex.exists_iso_derivedTensorProduct_invertible
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)}
    (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) (hK' : IsDualizingComplex K') :
    ∃ T : CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.DerivedTensorProductGeneral.{u, v} A,
      ∃ m : MonoidalCategory (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)),
        letI := m
        (Nonempty (MonoidalCategory.curriedTensor _ ≅ T.tensor) ∧
          Nonempty
          (𝟙_ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) ≅
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) 0).obj
              (ModuleCat.of A (ULift.{v} A)))) ∧
          ∃ L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A),
            MonoidalCategory.IsInvertible L ∧
              Nonempty (K' ≅ (T.tensor.obj K).obj L)

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_localization
declarations.doc:
The derived extension of a dualizing complex along a localization is a dualizing complex
over the localized ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_localization {A : Type u} {B : Type w} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsNoetherianRing A] (S : Submonoid A) [IsLocalization S B]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A)) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    @IsDualizingComplex (A := B) inferInstance
      (IsLocalization.isNoetherianRing S B inferInstance) inferInstance
      ((StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.derivedExtensionScalars (algebraMap A B)).obj K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_of_localizations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A7H.** A complex over a Noetherian ring is dualizing as soon as its
derived localization at every member of a family of elements generating the unit ideal is a
dualizing complex over the corresponding localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_of_localizations [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {ι : Type w} (f : ι → A) (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
    (hK : ∀ i, IsDualizingComplex ((localizationAwayFunctorAux.{u, u} (f i)).obj K)) :
    IsDualizingComplex K

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_derivedHom_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AX0.** For a finite homomorphism of Noetherian rings and a dualizing
complex `ω` over the source, `RHom_A(B, ω)` is a dualizing complex over `B`.

Noetherianity of `B` follows from that of `A` and finiteness of `f`, but it is a hypothesis here
because `Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex` is only stated over a Noetherian ring, so the conclusion
cannot be written down without it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_derivedHom_of_finite [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : f.Finite) (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A))
    (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω) :
    IsDualizingComplex ((derivedHom.{u, v, u} f).obj ω)
declarations.comment: the surjective case, a surjection being a finite ring map

declarations.name: Dualizing.polynomialBaseChange_isDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
A dualizing complex over a Noetherian ring remains dualizing after tensoring with the
polynomial ring in one variable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem polynomialBaseChange_isDualizingComplex {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A))
    (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    IsDualizingComplex (polynomialBaseChange K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.exists_isDualizingComplex_of_isEssentiallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A7K.** If a Noetherian ring `A` has a dualizing complex, then every
`A`-algebra essentially of finite type over `A` has a dualizing complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isDualizingComplex_of_isEssentiallyOfFiniteType {A B : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra A B]
    (hB : IsEssentiallyOfFiniteType A B (algebraMap A B))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    ∃ (hB' : IsNoetherianRing B) (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B)),
      @IsDualizingComplex B _ hB' _ L

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedHom_residueField_iso_shift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A7L.** Derived Hom from the residue field at a maximal ideal into a
dualizing complex is isomorphic to an integral shift of the residue field.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHom_residueField_iso_shift
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A))
    (hK : IsDualizingComplex K)
    (m : Ideal A) (hm : m.IsMaximal) :
    ∃ n : ℤ, Nonempty
      ((derivedHom.{u, v, u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk m)).obj K ≅
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} (A ⧸ m)) 0).obj
          ((ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{v} (A ⧸ m)).obj
            (ModuleCat.of (A ⧸ m) (A ⧸ m))))⟦n⟧)

registrations.name: Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex
registrations.comment: the normalization convention `RHom_A(κ, ω_A^•) = κ` in degree zero

registrations.name: Dualizing.exists_isNormalizedDualizingComplex_shift
registrations.comment: every dualizing complex over a Noetherian local ring is a shift of a normalized one

registrations.name: Dualizing.isNormalizedDualizingComplex_shift_iff_eq
registrations.comment: the normalizing shift is unique

declarations.name: Dualizing.isNormalizedDualizingComplex_derivedHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AX1.** If `A → B` is a finite local homomorphism of Noetherian local
rings and `K` is a normalized dualizing complex over `A`, then `RHom_A(B, K)` is a normalized
dualizing complex over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormalizedDualizingComplex_derivedHom
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] (hf : f.Finite)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, v} K) :
    IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, v}
      ((derivedHom.{u, v} f).obj K)
declarations.comment: the surjective case, a surjection of local rings being a finite local homomorphism

declarations.name: Dualizing.linearEquivalenceFiniteLengthIsoIdentity
declarations.doc:
Every linear self-equivalence of finite-length modules over a Noetherian local ring is
naturally isomorphic to the identity functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem linearEquivalenceFiniteLengthIsoIdentity
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (F : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun M : ModuleCat.{u} A => IsFiniteLength A M) ≌
      ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun M : ModuleCat.{u} A => IsFiniteLength A M))
    [F.functor.Linear A] :
    Nonempty (F.functor ≅ 𝟭 (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
      (fun M : ModuleCat.{u} A => IsFiniteLength A M)))

declarations.name: Dualizing.derivedHomFiniteLengthIsoMatlisDual
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A7Q.** Derived Hom into a normalized dualizing complex agrees
naturally, on finite-length modules, with Matlis duality into an injective hull of the residue
field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedHomFiniteLengthIsoMatlisDual
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex K)
    (E : ModuleCat.{max v u} A)
    (i : (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{v} A).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)) ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    Nonempty
      (derivedHomFiniteLengthFunctor A K ≅ matlisDualFiniteLengthFunctor A E)

declarations.name: Dualizing.nonempty_iso_single_injectiveHull_of_ringKrullDim_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A7R.** A normalized dualizing complex over a zero-dimensional
Noetherian local ring is an injective hull of the residue field placed in degree zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_iso_single_injectiveHull_of_ringKrullDim_eq_zero
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, v} K) (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 0)
    (E : ModuleCat.{max v u} A)
    (i : (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{v} A).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)) ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    Nonempty (K ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) 0).obj E)

declarations.name: Dualizing.exists_distTriang_normalizedDualizing_quotient_finiteLengthIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A7S.** If `I` is a finite-length ideal contained in the
maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring `A`, a normalized dualizing complex of `A / I`,
restricted to `A`, fits into a distinguished triangle with the normalized dualizing complex
of `A` and the degree-zero complex on `Hom_A(I, E)`, for any injective hull `E` of the
residue field.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_distTriang_normalizedDualizing_quotient_finiteLengthIdeal
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex K)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (hIfl : IsFiniteLength A I)
    (E : ModuleCat.{max v u} A)
    (i : (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{v} A).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)) ⟶ E) [Mono i]
    (hi : Module.IsInjectiveHull i) :
    letI : Nontrivial (A ⧸ I) := Ideal.Quotient.nontrivial_iff.mpr
      (lt_of_le_of_lt hI
        (inferInstance : (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).IsMaximal).lt_top).ne
    letI : IsLocalRing (A ⧸ I) :=
      IsLocalRing.of_surjective' (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective
    ∃ (KB : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} (A ⧸ I))),
      IsNormalizedDualizingComplex KB ∧
        ∃ (f : ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapDerivedCategory).obj KB ⟶ K)
          (g : K ⟶ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) 0).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A (I →ₗ[A] E)))
          (δ : (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max v u} A) 0).obj
              (ModuleCat.of A (I →ₗ[A] E)) ⟶
            (shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A)) (1 : ℤ)).obj
              (((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
