declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_iso_preadditiveYoneda_of_compactlyGenerated
declarations.doc:
**Brown representability**: let `D` be a triangulated category with arbitrary direct sums
which is compactly generated, i.e. there is a family `E : ι → D` of compact objects (each
`preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op (E i))` preserves direct sums) whose direct sum generates `D` (the
only objects right orthogonal to all shifts of the `E i` are the zero objects). Then every
contravariant cohomological functor `H : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat` which transforms direct sums into
products is representable: `H ≅ Hom(-, X)` for some `X : D`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_preadditiveYoneda_of_compactlyGenerated
    {ι : Type v} (E : ι → D)
    [∀ (i : ι) (α : Type v),
      PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete α) (preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op (E i)))]
    (hE : ∀ Y : D, ((ofObj E).shiftClosure ℤ).rightOrthogonal Y → IsZero Y)
    (H : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v}) [H.IsHomological]
    [∀ α : Type v, PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete α) H] :
    ∃ X : D, Nonempty (H ≅ preadditiveYoneda.obj X)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_of_compactlyGenerated
declarations.doc:
Let `D` be a triangulated category with arbitrary direct sums which is compactly generated,
i.e. there is a family `E : ι → D` of compact objects (each `preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op (E i))`
preserves direct sums) whose direct sum generates `D` (the only objects right orthogonal to all
shifts of the `E i` are the zero objects). Let `F : D ⥤ D'` be an exact functor of triangulated
categories which transforms direct sums into direct sums. Then `F` has a right adjoint `G`,
which is again exact: the adjunction `F ⊣ G` is a triangulated adjunction for a (unique)
`Functor.CommShift ℤ` structure on `G`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_of_compactlyGenerated
    (F : D ⥤ D') [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    [∀ α : Type v, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete α) F]
    {ι : Type v} (E : ι → D)
    [∀ (i : ι) (α : Type v),
      PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete α) (preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op (E i)))]
    (hE : ∀ Y : D, ((ofObj E).shiftClosure ℤ).rightOrthogonal Y → IsZero Y) :
    ∃ (G : D' ⥤ D) (adj : F ⊣ G) (_ : G.CommShift ℤ), adj.IsTriangulated

declarations.name: composition_morphism_exists
declarations.doc:
There is a morphism of complexes of `R`-modules
`c : tensorObj (HomComplexR R L M) (HomComplexR R K L) ⟶ HomComplexR R K M` such that for
`β : Cochain L M p` and `γ : Cochain K L q` with `p + q = n`, the `(p, q)`-component of `c` sends
`β ⊗ₜ γ` to the composite cochain `γ.comp β`.
declarations.statement:
theorem composition_morphism_exists :
    ∃ c : HomologicalComplex.tensorObj (HomComplexR R L M) (HomComplexR R K L) ⟶ HomComplexR R K M,
      ∀ (p q n : ℤ) (h : p + q = n) (β : Cochain L M p) (γ : Cochain K L q),
        (HomologicalComplex.ιTensorObj (HomComplexR R L M) (HomComplexR R K L) p q n h ≫ c.f n).hom
            (β ⊗ₜ[R] γ)
          = γ.comp β (by rw [add_comm]; exact h)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedInternalHomComposition_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8J.** The canonical composition morphisms
`RHom(L, M) ⊗ᴸ RHom(K, L) ⟶ RHom(K, M)` in `D(R)` are contravariantly natural in
`K`, dinatural in `L`, and covariantly natural in `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedInternalHomComposition_natural
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [HasDerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)] :
    (∀ {K K' L M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : K' ⟶ K),
      (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map
            (𝟙 ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op L, M)),
              (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map (f.op, 𝟙 L)) ≫
          DerivedInternalHom.Model.composition K' L M =
        DerivedInternalHom.Model.composition K L M ≫
          (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map (f.op, 𝟙 M)) ∧
    (∀ {K L L' M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : L' ⟶ L),
      (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map
            ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map (f.op, 𝟙 M),
              𝟙 ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op K, L'))) ≫
          DerivedInternalHom.Model.composition K L' M =
        (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map
            ((𝟙 ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op L, M)),
              ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map (𝟙 (Opposite.op K), f) :
                (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op K, L') ⟶
                  (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op K, L))) :
              ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op L, M),
                (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op K, L')) ⟶
              ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op L, M),
                (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op K, L))) ≫
          DerivedInternalHom.Model.composition K L M) ∧
    (∀ {K L M M' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat R)} (f : M ⟶ M'),
      (DerivedInternalHom.Model.tensor R).map
            ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map (𝟙 (Opposite.op L), f),
              𝟙 ((DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).obj (Opposite.op K, L))) ≫
          DerivedInternalHom.Model.composition K L M' =
        DerivedInternalHom.Model.composition K L M ≫
          (DerivedInternalHom.Model.hom R).map (𝟙 (Opposite.op K), f))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHomComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8K.** The internal Hom complex `SheafHom•(K, I)` of two complexes of
`O_X`-modules on a ringed space: in degree `n` its sections over an open `U` are the degree-`n`
cochains from `K|_U` to `I|_U`, that is the product over the pairs `p + n = q` of the sections
of `SheafHom(K^p, I^q)`, with the differential `d(f) = d_I ∘ f - (-1)^n f ∘ d_K`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev sheafHomComplex (K I : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ) :
    SheafHomComplex Rc K I

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHomComplexHomologyEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8L.** The `n`-th cohomology of the sections over `U` of the internal Hom complex
`SheafHom^•(L, M)` of [Stacks, Tag 0A8K] is canonically the group of morphisms from `L|_U` to
`M|_U[n]` in the homotopy category of complexes of `O_U`-modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomComplexHomologyEquiv (U : Opens X)
    (L M : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    (sectionComplex Rc (sheafHomComplex Rc L M).obj U).homology n ≃+
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((structureSheaf Rc).over U))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (restrictComplex Rc L U) ⟶
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((structureSheaf Rc).over U))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj ((restrictComplex Rc M U)⟦n⟧))
declarations.comment:
H^n(Γ(U, SheafHom^•(L, M))) = Hom_{K(O_U)}(L|_U, M|_U[n]) for every open U of X
and every n ∈ ℤ, with SheafHom^•(L, M) the internal Hom complex constructed in Tag 0A8K.

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivHomotopyCategory
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th cohomology of the sections over `U` of the internal Hom complex from `L` to `M` is
canonically the group of morphisms from `L|_U` to `M|_U[n]` in the homotopy category of complexes
of `O_U`-modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivHomotopyCategory
    {X : TopCat.{u}} (Rc : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} X)
    (U : Opens X)
    (L M : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ)
    (H : SheafHomComplex Rc L M) (n : ℤ) :
    (sectionComplex Rc H.obj U).homology n ≃+
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((structureSheaf Rc).over U))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (restrictComplex Rc L U) ⟶
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((structureSheaf Rc).over U))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj ((restrictComplex Rc M U)⟦n⟧))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SheafHomComplexCurrying.sheafHomTensorIsoConstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8M.** For complexes `K`, `L`, `M` of `O_X`-modules on a ringed space there is an
isomorphism `SheafHom•(K, SheafHom•(L, M)) ≅ SheafHom•(Tot(K ⊗_{O_X} L), M)` of complexes of
`O_X`-modules, functorial in `K`, `L` and `M`.
declarations.statement: def sheafHomTensorIsoConstruction : SheafHomTensorIsoConstruction Rc

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.compositionConstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A91.** For complexes `K`, `L`, `M` of modules on a ringed site there is a
canonical morphism of complexes of `O`-modules

`Tot(SheafHom(L, M) ⊗_O SheafHom(K, L)) ⟶ SheafHom(K, M)`,

namely the one sending each homogeneous local pure tensor to the composite of its two factors,
with no extra sign.

A ringed space is a ringed site, namely the site of its opens with the open-cover topology, so
this also gives the composition morphism for complexes of modules on a ringed space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def compositionConstruction : CompositionConstruction X
declarations.comment: the ringed space case

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.evaluationConstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8P.** The canonical evaluation morphisms for internal Hom complexes of modules
on a ringed space, specified on homogeneous local pure tensors by the signed formula
`φ ⊗ k ↦ (-1)^(r + (-a) * r) (ψ ↦ φ (ψ k))`. It is the evaluation morphism of the ringed site
of opens of the space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def evaluationConstruction : EvaluationConstruction Rc
declarations.comment: canonical evaluation morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.evaluateAndMore_natural
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0A8P.** Evaluation is covariant in `K` and `M` and contravariant in `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem evaluateAndMore_natural
    {K K' L L' M M' : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ}
    (k : K ⟶ K') (l : L' ⟶ L) (m : M ⟶ M') :
    tensorTotalMap Rc (sheafHomComplexMap Rc l m) k ≫
        evaluateAndMore Rc K' L' M' =
      evaluateAndMore Rc K L M ≫
        sheafHomComplexMap Rc (sheafHomComplexMap Rc k l) m
declarations.comment: functoriality in all three complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.diagonalTensorHom
declarations.doc:
The diagonal morphism sends a homogeneous section `k` of `K` to the homogeneous map
`l ↦ k ⊗ l` from `L` to the total tensor product.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def diagonalTensorHom
    (K L : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ) :
    K ⟶ (sheafHomComplex Rc L (tensorTotal Rc K L)).obj
declarations.comment: canonical diagonal morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.diagonalTensorHom_apply
declarations.doc:
On local sections, the diagonal morphism is inclusion of the pure tensor in the
appropriate summand of the total complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem diagonalTensorHom_apply
    (K L : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ) (U : Opens X)
    (n p : ℤ) (k : (K.X n).val.obj (op U))
    (l : (L.X p).val.obj (op U)) :
    applyHomSection Rc (sheafHomComplex Rc L (tensorTotal Rc K L))
        U n p (n + p) (by omega)
        (((diagonalTensorHom Rc K L).f n).val.app (op U) k) l =
      tensorTotalSection Rc K L U n p k l
declarations.comment: canonical characterization

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.diagonalTensorHom_natural
declarations.doc: The diagonal morphism is natural in `K` and dinatural in `L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem diagonalTensorHom_natural
    {K K' L L' : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ}
    (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L ⟶ L') :
    diagonalTensorHom Rc K L ≫
        sheafHomComplexMap Rc (𝟙 L) (tensorTotalMap Rc f g) =
      f ≫ diagonalTensorHom Rc K' L' ≫
        sheafHomComplexMap Rc g (𝟙 (tensorTotal Rc K' L'))
declarations.comment: functoriality in both complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivDerivedCategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8R.** If `I` is K-injective, degree-zero cohomology over `U` of the internal
Hom complex from `L` to `I` is canonically the group of derived morphisms between the objects
represented by their restrictions to the open subspace `U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivDerivedCategory
    {X : TopCat.{u}} (Rc : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} X) (U : Opens X)
    (L I : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective]
    (H : SheafHomComplex Rc L I)
    (LU MU : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U (structureSheaf Rc))))
    (eL : DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj
        (restrictComplexToSubspace (structureSheaf Rc) U L)) ≅ LU)
    (eM : DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj
        ((restrictComplexToSubspace (structureSheaf Rc) U I)⟦(0 : ℤ)⟧)) ≅ MU) :
    (sectionComplex Rc H.obj U).homology 0 ≃+
      (LU ⟶ MU)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivDerivedCategory_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8R.** The canonical identification sends a section cohomology class first to its
homotopy-class morphism, transports that morphism from the slice-site model to the
open-subspace model, and then localizes it. In particular this fixes its value on the identity
class and its behaviour under changing the two representatives.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivDerivedCategory_apply
    {X : TopCat.{u}} (Rc : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} X) (U : Opens X)
    (L I : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective]
    (H : SheafHomComplex Rc L I)
    (LU MU : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (resRing U (structureSheaf Rc))))
    (eL : DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj
        (restrictComplexToSubspace (structureSheaf Rc) U L)) ≅ LU)
    (eM : DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj
        ((restrictComplexToSubspace (structureSheaf Rc) U I)⟦(0 : ℤ)⟧)) ≅ MU)
    (z : (sectionComplex Rc H.obj U).homology 0) :
    sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivDerivedCategory Rc U L I H LU MU eL eM z =
      (let E := U.sheafOfModulesEquivOver (structureSheaf Rc)
            let Fh := E.functor.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
       let K := restrictComplex Rc L U
       let J := (restrictComplex Rc I U)⟦(0 : ℤ)⟧
       let eK := (E.functor.mapHomotopyCategoryFactors (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).app K ≪≫
         (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).mapIso
           (eqToIso (mapHomologicalComplex_restrictComplex Rc U L))
       let eJ := (E.functor.mapHomotopyCategoryFactors (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).app J ≪≫
         (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).mapIso
           (eqToIso (mapHomologicalComplex_restrictComplex_shiftZero Rc U I))
       eL.inv ≫ DerivedCategory.Qh.map
         (eK.inv ≫ Fh.map
           (sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivHomotopyCategory
             Rc U L I H 0 z) ≫ eJ.hom) ≫ eM.hom)
declarations.comment: canonical comparison on section classes

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.sheafHomComplexMap_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8S.** A quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes, together with a
quasi-isomorphism in the contravariant variable, induces a quasi-isomorphism between the
corresponding canonical internal Hom complexes. This is what makes the derived internal Hom
of complexes of `O_X`-modules well defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHomComplexMap_quasiIso
    {I' I L' L : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ}
    (i : I' ⟶ I) [QuasiIso i] [I'.IsKInjective] [I.IsKInjective]
    (l : L' ⟶ L) [QuasiIso l] :
    QuasiIso (sheafHomComplexMap Rc l i)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isKInjective_sheafHomComplex_of_isKFlat
declarations.doc:
The internal Hom complex `SheafHom^•(L, I)` from a K-flat complex `L` of `O_X`-modules into a
K-injective complex `I` of `O_X`-modules is K-injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_sheafHomComplex_of_isKFlat
    (L I : CochainComplex (StructureSheafModules Rc) ℤ)
    (hL : IsKFlat Rc L) [I.IsKInjective] :
    (sheafHomComplex Rc L I).obj.IsKInjective

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomEvaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8U.** For objects `K`, `L`, `M` of `D(O_X)` on a ringed space there is a canonical
evaluation morphism

`RSheafHom(L, M) ⊗^L_{O_X} K ⟶ RSheafHom(RSheafHom(K, L), M)`

in `D(O_X)`, obtained from the evaluation morphism of internal Hom complexes after passing to a
K-flat representative of `K` and K-injective representatives of `L` and `M`.
declarations.comment: the canonical evaluation morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomEvaluation_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8U.** Derived evaluation is functorial in all three objects at once: covariant in
the object being tensored, contravariant in the source of the inner internal hom, and covariant
in its target.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomEvaluation_natural
    {K K' L L' M M' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf Rc))}
    (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L' ⟶ L) (h : M ⟶ M') :
    derivedTensorMap Rc (derivedSheafHomMap Rc g h) f ≫
        derivedSheafHomEvaluation Rc K' L' M' =
      derivedSheafHomEvaluation Rc K L M ≫
        derivedSheafHomMap Rc (derivedSheafHomMap Rc f g) h
declarations.comment: functoriality in all three objects

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomEvaluation_model
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8U.** On a K-flat representative `P` of `K` and K-injective representatives `J`
of `L` and `I` of `M`, derived evaluation is the class of the evaluation morphism of internal
Hom complexes `Tot(SheafHom^•(J, I) ⊗_{O_X} P) ⟶ SheafHom^•(SheafHom^•(P, J), I)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomEvaluation_model
    (P J I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf Rc)) ℤ)
    (hP : IsKFlat Rc P) [J.IsKInjective] [I.IsKInjective] :
    derivedSheafHomEvaluation Rc (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj J)
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I) ≫
        (RingedSite.derivedEvaluationTargetComparison (ringedSite Rc)
          (derivedInternalHom Rc) P J I).hom =
      (RingedSite.derivedEvaluationSourceComparison (ringedSite Rc)
          (canonicalDerivedTensorProduct (ringedSite Rc)) (derivedInternalHom Rc)
          P J I hP).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (RingedSite.evaluationMap (ringedSite Rc) P J I)
declarations.comment: comparison with evaluation of complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomComposition
declarations.doc:
For objects `K`, `L`, `M` of `D(O_X)` on a ringed space, the canonical composition morphism

`RSheafHom(L, M) ⊗^L_{O_X} RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M)`

in `D(O_X)`, obtained from the composition morphism of internal Hom complexes after passing to
K-injective representatives of `L` and `M` and a K-flat model of the internal Hom complex into
the representative of `L`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHomComposition
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))) :
    ((derivedTensor Rc).obj (((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op L)).obj M)).obj
        (((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op K)).obj L) ⟶
      ((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op K)).obj M
declarations.comment: the canonical composition morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomComposition_natural_source
declarations.doc: Derived composition is contravariant in the source object.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomComposition_natural_source
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))}
    (k : K' ⟶ K)
    (L M : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))) :
    derivedSheafHomComposition Rc K L M ≫ derivedSheafHomMap Rc k (𝟙 M) =
      derivedTensorMap Rc (𝟙 (((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op L)).obj M))
          (derivedSheafHomMap Rc k (𝟙 L)) ≫
        derivedSheafHomComposition Rc K' L M
declarations.comment: functoriality in the source

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomComposition_natural_target
declarations.doc: Derived composition is covariant in the target object.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomComposition_natural_target
    (K L : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc)))
    {M M' : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))}
    (m : M ⟶ M') :
    derivedSheafHomComposition Rc K L M ≫ derivedSheafHomMap Rc (𝟙 K) m =
      derivedTensorMap Rc (derivedSheafHomMap Rc (𝟙 L) m)
          (𝟙 (((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op K)).obj L)) ≫
        derivedSheafHomComposition Rc K L M'
declarations.comment: functoriality in the target

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomComposition_dinatural_middle
declarations.doc:
Derived composition is dinatural in the intermediate object: a morphism `L ⟶ L'` may be
absorbed covariantly into the left tensor factor or contravariantly into the right one, with the
same result.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomComposition_dinatural_middle
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc)))
    {L L' : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))}
    (l : L ⟶ L')
    (M : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc))) :
    derivedTensorMap Rc (𝟙 (((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op L')).obj M))
          (derivedSheafHomMap Rc (𝟙 K) l) ≫
        derivedSheafHomComposition Rc K L' M =
      derivedTensorMap Rc (derivedSheafHomMap Rc l (𝟙 M))
          (𝟙 (((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op K)).obj L)) ≫
        derivedSheafHomComposition Rc K L M
declarations.comment: functoriality in the intermediate object

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHomComposition_kFlatModel
declarations.doc:
On K-injective representatives `J` of `L` and `I` of `M` and any map `f` from a K-flat
complex `H` to the internal Hom complex `SheafHom^•(K, J)`, derived composition is the class of
the composition morphism of internal Hom complexes
`Tot(SheafHom^•(J, I) ⊗_{O_X} SheafHom^•(K, J)) ⟶ SheafHom^•(K, I)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHomComposition_kFlatModel
    (K J I H : CochainComplex (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} (Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} Rc)) ℤ)
    [hJ : J.IsKInjective] [hI : I.IsKInjective] (hH : IsKFlat Rc H)
    (f : H ⟶ (sheafHomComplex Rc K J).obj) :
    ((derivedTensor Rc).obj
            (((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj J))).obj
              (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I))).map
          (DerivedCategory.Q.map f ≫
            (@RingedSite.derivedSheafHomComparison (ringedSite Rc) _ K J hJ).inv) ≫
        derivedSheafHomComposition Rc (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj J)
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I) ≫
        (@RingedSite.derivedSheafHomComparison (ringedSite Rc) _ K I hI).hom =
      (RingedSite.derivedEvaluationSourceComparison (ringedSite Rc)
            (canonicalDerivedTensorProduct (ringedSite Rc)) (derivedInternalHom Rc)
            H J I hH).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (tensorTotalMap Rc (𝟙 (sheafHomComplex Rc J I).obj) f) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (RingedSite.compositionMap (ringedSite Rc) K J I)
declarations.comment: comparison with composition of complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorHomUnit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8W.** For objects `K`, `L` of `D(O_X)` on a ringed space, the canonical morphism

`K ⟶ RSheafHom(L, K ⊗^L_{O_X} L)`

in `D(O_X)`: the morphism corresponding to the identity of `K ⊗^L_{O_X} L` under the
tensor–internal-Hom bijection of Stacks 08DI.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorHomUnit (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    K ⟶ ((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op L)).obj (((derivedTensor Rc).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism, as the unit of Stacks 08DI

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8W.** For objects `K`, `L` of `D(O_X)` on a ringed space, the canonical morphism

`K ⟶ RSheafHom(L, K ⊗^L_{O_X} L)`

in `D(O_X)`, built the way the source builds it: on the chosen K-flat representative `A` of `K`
and the chosen K-injective representative `B` of `L` it is the diagonal morphism of complexes of
Stacks 0A93, `A ⟶ SheafHom(B, Tot(A ⊗_{O_X} B))`, followed by the augmentation of
`Tot(A ⊗_{O_X} B)` into its chosen K-injective resolution, read through the comparisons
identifying source and target with classes of complexes.

A ringed space is a ringed site, so this is the morphism of Stacks 0A99 read off along
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite`. It is the construction that carries the functoriality of the
tag, in `canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit_natural_left` and
`canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit_natural_right` below.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    K ⟶ ((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op L)).obj (((derivedTensor Rc).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism, built as the source builds it

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8W.** The canonical morphism built the source's way is the class of the diagonal
morphism of complexes of Stacks 0A93 followed by the K-injective resolution augmentation, read
through the comparisons of its source and target with classes of complexes. This is the equation
that pins the morphism down; in particular it is not an arbitrary morphism between the two
objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit_eq (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)) :
    (RingedSite.kFlatModelIso (ringedSite Rc) K).hom ≫
        canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit Rc K L ≫
        (RingedSite.diagonalTargetIso (ringedSite Rc) K L L).hom =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (RingedSite.diagonalComplexMap (ringedSite Rc)
        (RingedSite.kFlatModel (ringedSite Rc) K)
        (RingedSite.kInjectiveModel (ringedSite Rc) L))
declarations.comment: the characterisation on representatives

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit_natural_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8W: the canonical morphism is functorial in `K`.** For a morphism `k : K ⟶ K'` of
`D(O_X)` the square

`k ≫ u_{K',L} = u_{K,L} ≫ RSheafHom(𝟙_L, k ⊗ 𝟙_L)`

commutes in `D(O_X)`: the first variable of the morphism acts covariantly, both on the source
and inside the derived tensor product.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit_natural_left
    (L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)} (k : K ⟶ K') :
    k ≫ canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit Rc K' L =
      canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit Rc K L ≫
        ((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op L)).map (((derivedTensor Rc).map k).app L)
declarations.comment: functoriality in K

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit_natural_right
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A8W: the canonical morphism is functorial in `L`.** For a morphism `l : L' ⟶ L` of
`D(O_X)` the square

`u_{K,L} ≫ RSheafHom(l, 𝟙) = u_{K,L'} ≫ RSheafHom(𝟙_{L'}, 𝟙_K ⊗ l)`

commutes in `D(O_X)`: the second variable acts contravariantly in the source of the internal Hom
and covariantly inside the derived tensor product, which is the dinaturality that the statement
of the tag asserts.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit_natural_right
    (K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc))
    {L L' : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules Rc)} (l : L' ⟶ L) :
    canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit Rc K L ≫
        ((derivedSheafHom Rc).map l.op).app (((derivedTensor Rc).obj K).obj L) =
      canonicalDerivedTensorHomUnit Rc K L' ≫
        ((derivedSheafHom Rc).obj (op L')).map (((derivedTensor Rc).obj K).map l)
declarations.comment: functoriality in L

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomComplex
declarations.doc:
The canonical internal sheaf Hom complex `SheafHom•(L, M)`: in degree `n` its sections over
an object `U` are the degree-`n` cochains from `L|_U` to `M|_U`, that is the product over the
pairs `p + n = q` of the sections of `SheafHom(L^p, M^q)`, with the differential
`d(f) = d_M ∘ f - (-1)^n f ∘ d_L`, together with its description on every slice site and the
compatibility of these descriptions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomComplex (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    (L M : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) :
        SheafHomComplex X L M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomComplexSectionHomologyEquivHomotopyCategory
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th cohomology of the sections over `U` of the internal Hom complex from `L` to `M`
is the group of morphisms `L|_U ⟶ M|_U[n]` in the homotopy category of `O|_U`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def sheafHomComplexSectionHomologyEquivHomotopyCategory
    (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (L M : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (U : X.C) (n : ℤ) :
    (sectionComplex X (sheafHomComplex X L M).obj U).homology n ≃+
    ((HomotopyCategory.quotient
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
            (restrictComplex X L U) ⟶
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient
          (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
            ((restrictComplex X M U)⟦n⟧))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivHomotopyCategory
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th cohomology of the global sections of the internal sheaf Hom complex from `L` to
`M` is canonically the group of morphisms from `L` to `M[n]` in the homotopy category.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomComplexHomologyEquivHomotopyCategory
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, w})
    (L M : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (n : ℤ) :
    (globalSectionsComplex X (sheafHomComplex X L M).obj).homology n ≃+
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj L ⟶
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient (SheafOfModules.{m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj (M⟦n⟧))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomTensorIsoConstruction
declarations.doc:
For complexes `K`, `L`, `M` of `O`-modules on a ringed site `(C, O)` there is an isomorphism
`SheafHom•(K, SheafHom•(L, M)) ≅ SheafHom•(Tot(K ⊗_O L), M)` of complexes of `O`-modules,
functorial in `K`, `L` and `M`.
declarations.statement: def sheafHomTensorIsoConstruction : SheafHomTensorIsoConstruction X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomTensorCurryIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A90.** The canonical currying isomorphism of internal Hom complexes on a ringed
site: `SheafHom(K, SheafHom(L, M)) ≅ SheafHom(Tot(K ⊗_O L), M)`.
declarations.comment: the currying isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.compositionConstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A91.** For complexes `K`, `L`, `M` of modules on a ringed site there is a
canonical morphism of complexes of `O`-modules

`Tot(SheafHom(L, M) ⊗_O SheafHom(K, L)) ⟶ SheafHom(K, M)`,

namely the one sending each homogeneous local pure tensor to the composite of its two factors,
with no extra sign.

A ringed space is a ringed site, namely the site of its opens with the open-cover topology, so
this also gives the composition morphism for complexes of modules on a ringed space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def compositionConstruction : CompositionConstruction X

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.compositionConstruction
declarations.doc: The canonical composition of internal Hom complexes of module sheaves.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def compositionConstruction : CompositionConstruction X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.evaluationConstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A92.** For complexes `K`, `L`, `M` of modules on a ringed site there is a
canonical morphism of complexes of `O`-modules

`Tot(SheafHom(L, M) ⊗_O K) ⟶ SheafHom(SheafHom(K, L), M)`,

namely the one sending each homogeneous local pure tensor `φ ⊗ k` to the local section taking
`ψ` to `φ(ψ(k))`, with the Koszul sign.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def evaluationConstruction : EvaluationConstruction X
declarations.comment: canonical evaluation morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.evaluationMap_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A92.** The evaluation morphism is natural in `K`, contranatural in `L` and
natural in `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem evaluationMap_natural (k : K ⟶ K') (l : L' ⟶ L) (m : M ⟶ M') :
    tensorTotalMap X (homMap X l m) k ≫ evaluationMap X K' L' M' =
      evaluationMap X K L M ≫ homMap X (homMap X k l) m
declarations.comment: functoriality in all three complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.evaluationConstruction
declarations.doc: The canonical evaluation morphism for every three complexes of modules.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def evaluationConstruction : EvaluationConstruction X
declarations.comment: canonical evaluation morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.evaluation_natural
declarations.doc: Evaluation is natural in `K`, contranatural in `L`, and natural in `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem evaluation_natural
    {K K' L L' M M' : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ}
    (k : K ⟶ K') (l : L' ⟶ L) (m : M ⟶ M') :
    tensorTotalMap X (sheafHomComplexMap X l m) k ≫
        evaluation X K' L' M' =
      evaluation X K L M ≫
        sheafHomComplexMap X (sheafHomComplexMap X k l) m
declarations.comment: functoriality in all three complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.diagonalConstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A93.** For complexes `K`, `L` of modules on a ringed site there is a canonical
morphism of complexes of `O`-modules

`K ⟶ SheafHom(L, Tot(K ⊗_O L))`,

namely the one sending each homogeneous local section `k` of `K` to the local section
`l ↦ k ⊗ l` of the internal Hom complex.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diagonalConstruction : DiagonalConstruction X
declarations.comment: canonical diagonal morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.diagonalMap_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A93.** The diagonal morphism is natural in `K` and dinatural in `L`: a morphism
`g : L ⟶ L'` acts covariantly inside the tensor product and contravariantly in the source of
the internal Hom.
declarations.statement:
theorem diagonalMap_natural (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L ⟶ L') :
    diagonalMap X K L ≫ homMap X (𝟙 L) (tensorTotalMap X f g) =
      f ≫ diagonalMap X K' L' ≫ homMap X g (𝟙 (tensorTotal X K' L'))
declarations.comment: functoriality in both complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomGlobalHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A94, global sections, naturality.** The identification of the degree-zero
cohomology of the global sections of `SheafHom(L, I)` with `Hom_{D(O)}(L, I)` is natural in both
variables: `homMap k m`, for `k : L' ⟶ L` and `m : I ⟶ I'`, acts on it by precomposition with `k`
and postcomposition with `m` in the derived category.

This is the global companion of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomSectionHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom_naturality`, and it
is what a consumer identifying two such bijections of morphism groups needs.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHomGlobalHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom_naturality
    {L L' I I' : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ}
    [I.IsKInjective] [I'.IsKInjective] (k : L' ⟶ L) (m : I ⟶ I')
    (η : (globalSectionsComplex X (sheafHomComplex X L I).obj).homology 0) :
    sheafHomGlobalHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom X L' I'
        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (globalSectionsComplexMap X (homMap X k m)) 0 η) =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map k ≫ sheafHomGlobalHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom X L I η ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map m
declarations.comment: global sections, naturality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomSectionHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A94, sections over an object.** If `I` is K-injective then the degree-zero
cohomology of the sections over `U` of the internal Hom complex from `L` to `I` is the group of
morphisms `L|_U ⟶ I|_U` in the derived category of `O|_U`-modules.

This is Stacks 0A8Y in degree `0` followed by the identification of homotopy-category with
derived-category morphisms into a K-injective target; the restriction `I|_U` is K-injective by
Stacks 08FI.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomSectionHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom
    (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (L I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] (U : X.C) :
    (sectionComplex X (sheafHomComplex X L I).obj U).homology 0 ≃+
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (restrictComplex X L U) ⟶
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (restrictComplex X I U))
declarations.comment: sections over an object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomGlobalHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A94, global sections.** If `I` is K-injective then the degree-zero cohomology of
the global sections of the internal Hom complex from `L` to `I` is the group of morphisms
`L ⟶ I` in the derived category of `O`-modules.

This is Stacks 0A8Z in degree `0` followed by the same identification of homotopy-category with
derived-category morphisms into a K-injective target.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafHomGlobalHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, r})
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}]
    (L I : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] :
    (globalSectionsComplex X (sheafHomComplex X L I).obj).homology 0 ≃+
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj I)
declarations.comment: global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomSectionHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom_naturality
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A94, sections over an object, naturality.** The identification of the degree-zero
cohomology of the sections over `U` of `SheafHom(L, I)` with `Hom_{D(O|_U)}(L|_U, I|_U)` is
natural in both variables: `homMap k m`, for `k : L' ⟶ L` and `m : I ⟶ I'`, acts on it by
precomposition with `k|_U` and postcomposition with `m|_U` in the derived category.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHomSectionHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom_naturality
    {L L' I I' : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ}
    [I.IsKInjective] [I'.IsKInjective] (k : L' ⟶ L) (m : I ⟶ I') (U : X.C)
    (η : (sectionComplex X (sheafHomComplex X L I).obj U).homology 0) :
    sheafHomSectionHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom X L' I' U
        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (sectionComplexMap X U (homMap X k m)) 0 η) =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (restrictComplexMap X U k) ≫
        sheafHomSectionHomologyEquivDerivedCategoryHom X L I U η ≫
          DerivedCategory.Q.map (restrictComplexMap X U m)
declarations.comment: sections over an object, naturality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.homMap_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A95.** A quasi-isomorphism `l : L' ⟶ L` and a quasi-isomorphism `i : I' ⟶ I`
between K-injective complexes of `O`-modules induce a quasi-isomorphism
`SheafHom(L, I') ⟶ SheafHom(L', I)` of internal Hom complexes.

This is what makes the derived internal Hom well defined. The objects of the site need not lie
in the universe of its morphisms; at `c = u` the extra size conditions above the tag's are
automatic, which
is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.homMap_quasiIso_of_collapsed`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homMap_quasiIso (i : I' ⟶ I) [QuasiIso i] [I'.IsKInjective] [I.IsKInjective]
    (l : L' ⟶ L) [QuasiIso l] : QuasiIso (homMap X l i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.InternalHom.sheafHomComplexMap_quasiIso
declarations.doc:
Quasi-isomorphisms in both variables, with K-injective complexes in the
second variable, induce a quasi-isomorphism of internal Hom complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHomComplexMap_quasiIso
    (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    {I' I L' L : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ}
    (i : I' ⟶ I) [QuasiIso i] [I'.IsKInjective] [I.IsKInjective]
    (l : L' ⟶ L) [QuasiIso l] :
    QuasiIso (sheafHomComplexMap X l i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isKInjective_sheafHomComplex_of_isKFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A96.** The internal Hom complex `SheafHom(L, I)` from a K-flat complex `L` of
`O`-modules into a K-injective complex `I` of `O`-modules is K-injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_sheafHomComplex_of_isKFlat
    (L I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O L) [I.IsKInjective] :
    (sheafHomComplex X L I).obj.IsKInjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedEvaluation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A97: the canonical evaluation morphism of derived internal Homs.** For arbitrary
objects `K`, `L`, `M` of `D(Mod(O))` there is a canonical morphism

`RSheafHom(L, M) ⊗^L_O K ⟶ RSheafHom(RSheafHom(K, L), M)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedEvaluation
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor.{u, u, d} X).obj
        (((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).obj (op L)).obj M)).obj K ⟶
      ((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).obj
        (op (((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).obj (op K)).obj L))).obj M
declarations.comment: the canonical evaluation morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedEvaluation_model
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A97.** On a K-flat source and K-injective targets, the canonical evaluation
morphism is the class of the evaluation morphism of internal Hom complexes of Stacks 0A92.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedEvaluation_model
    (A B C : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    (hA : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsKFlat X.O A) [B.IsKInjective] [C.IsKInjective] :
    derivedEvaluation X (DerivedCategory.Q.obj A) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj B)
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj C) ≫
        (derivedEvaluationTargetComparison X (canonicalDerivedInternalHom.{u, d} X)
          A B C).hom =
      (derivedEvaluationSourceComparison X
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct.{u, u, d} X)
          (canonicalDerivedInternalHom.{u, d} X) A B C hA).hom ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map (evaluationMap X A B C)
declarations.comment: comparison with evaluation of complexes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedEvaluation_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A97.** The canonical evaluation morphism is natural in the source object and in
the target object, and contranatural in the intermediate object.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedEvaluation_natural
    {K K' L L' M M' :
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L' ⟶ L) (h : M ⟶ M') :
    derivedEvaluation X K L M ≫
        ((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).map
          ((((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).obj (op K')).map g ≫
            ((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).map f.op).app L).op)).app M ≫
        ((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).obj
          (op (((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).obj (op K')).obj L'))).map h =
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor.{u, u, d} X).map
          (((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).map g.op).app M ≫
            ((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).obj (op L')).map h)).app K ≫
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor.{u, u, d} X).obj
          (((derivedInternalHomFunctor.{u, d} X).obj (op L')).obj M')).map f ≫
        derivedEvaluation X K' L' M'
declarations.comment: functoriality in all three objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHomCompositionConstruction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A98: the composition morphism of derived internal Homs.** For arbitrary objects
`K`, `L`, `M` of `D(Mod(O))` there is a canonical morphism

`RSheafHom(L, M) ⊗^L_O RSheafHom(K, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(K, M)`,

which on a K-flat model of the second internal Hom complex is the composition morphism of
internal Hom complexes of Stacks 0A91, and which is contravariant in the source, covariant in
the target and dinatural in the intermediate object.
declarations.statement: def derivedSheafHomCompositionConstruction : DerivedSheafHomComposition X T Hd

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A99.** For objects `K`, `L` of `D(O)` the canonical morphism

`K ⟶ RSheafHom(L, K ⊗_O^L L)`

in `D(O)`: on the chosen K-flat representative `A` of `K` and the chosen K-injective
representative `B` of `L` it is the diagonal morphism of complexes of Stacks 0A93, followed by
the augmentation of `Tot(A ⊗_O B)` into its chosen K-injective resolution.
declarations.statement:
def canonicalDerivedDiagonal
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    K ⟶ ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).obj
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: the canonical morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedDiagonal_eq
declarations.doc:
**The canonical morphism of Stacks 0A99 is the class of the resolved diagonal of complexes**,
read through the comparisons of its source and target with classes of complexes.  In particular
it is not an arbitrary morphism between the two objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalDerivedDiagonal_eq
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    (kFlatModelIso X K).hom ≫ canonicalDerivedDiagonal X K L ≫
        (diagonalTargetIso X K L L).hom =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (diagonalComplexMap X (kFlatModel X K) (kInjectiveModel X L))
declarations.comment: the characterisation on representatives

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedDiagonal_natural_right
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A99: the canonical morphism is functorial in `L`.** For a morphism `l : L' ⟶ L` of
`D(O)` the square

`u_{K,L} ≫ RSheafHom(l, 𝟙) = u_{K,L'} ≫ RSheafHom(𝟙, 𝟙_K ⊗ l)`

commutes in `D(O)`: the second variable of the diagonal acts contravariantly in the source of
the internal Hom and covariantly inside the derived tensor product, which is the dinaturality
that the statement of the tag asserts.

The chosen representative of `L` is K-injective, so `l` is the class of a morphism of the chosen
representatives and the square is the dinaturality of Stacks 0A93 at the level of complexes,
conjugated by the target comparisons.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalDerivedDiagonal_natural_right
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    {L L' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (l : L' ⟶ L) :
    canonicalDerivedDiagonal X K L ≫
        ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).map l.op).app
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).obj L) =
      canonicalDerivedDiagonal X K L' ≫
        ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L')).map
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).obj K).map l)
declarations.comment: functoriality in L

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.canonicalDerivedDiagonal_natural_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A99: the canonical morphism is functorial in `K`.** For a morphism `f : K ⟶ K'` of
`D(O)` the square

`f ≫ u_{K',L} = u_{K,L} ≫ RSheafHom(𝟙_L, f ⊗ 𝟙_L)`

commutes in `D(O)`: the first variable of the diagonal acts covariantly.

A morphism of `D(O)` does not lift to the chosen K-flat representatives, which are not
K-injective.  It is instead written as a right fraction `inv (Q s₀) ≫ Q g₀`
(`DerivedCategory.right_fac`) and the apex of that roof is replaced by a K-flat resolution of it
(Stacks 06YS), giving a roof `A ⟵ P ⟶ A'` with all three complexes K-flat and the left leg
invertible in `D(O)`.  The one-sided K-flat comparison of Stacks 06YU is then available at all
three vertices, which makes the tensored left leg invertible with no K-flatness of the other
factor, and the square closes from the complex-level functoriality of Stacks 0A93.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalDerivedDiagonal_natural_left
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    {K K' : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (f : K ⟶ K') :
    f ≫ canonicalDerivedDiagonal X K' L =
      canonicalDerivedDiagonal X K L ≫
        ((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op L)).map
          (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor X).map f).app L)
declarations.comment: functoriality in K

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.SupportedGeneration.exists_isPerfect_quasiCoherentSupported_isWeakGenerator_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A9A]** (Rouquier, Theorem 6.8). Let `X` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme and let `T ⊆ X` be a closed subset such that `X ∖ T` is quasi-compact.
Then `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` is generated by a single perfect object: there is a perfect object `P` of
`D(𝒪_X)` lying in `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` such that every object `E` of `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` with
`Hom(P[n], E) = 0` for all `n ∈ ℤ` is zero.

Generation is [Stacks, Tag 09SJ] for `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)`, written out; morphisms of the full
subcategory are morphisms of `D(𝒪_X)`. The generator is the compact one of
`Stacks.Duality.SupportedGeneration.hasCompactSupportedGenerators`, built by the induction of the
source, and it is perfect by
`Stacks.Duality.SupportedGeneration.isPerfect_of_isCompactObject`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_quasiCoherentSupported_isWeakGenerator_of_qcqs (X : Scheme.{u})
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ) :
    ∃ P : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
      AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) P ∧
        quasiCoherentSupported X T P ∧
        ∀ E : DerivedCategory X.Modules, quasiCoherentSupported X T E →
          (∀ (n : ℤ) (g : P⟦n⟧ ⟶ E), g = 0) → IsZero E

declarations.name: Stacks.Rouquier.exists_isPerfect_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_supported
declarations.doc:
**The theorem of Rouquier.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated
scheme and let `T ⊆ X` be closed with quasi-compact complement. Then `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` has a weak
triangulated generator which is perfect as an object of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_supported (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ) :
    ∃ G : Stacks.Duality.QuasiCoherentSupportedDerivedCategory X T,
      IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) G.obj ∧
        (ObjectProperty.singleton G).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.comment: the generator is an object of D_{QCoh,T}(O_X), perfect in D(O_X); generation in the sense of 09SJ, as ObjectProperty.IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Supported.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**An object of `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` is compact if and only if it is perfect as an object of
`D(𝒪_X)`**, for `X` quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `T` closed with quasi-compact
complement. The derived category is taken at the locally small model.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ)
    (K : QuasiCoherentSupportedDerivedCategory X T) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} K ↔ IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K.obj
declarations.comment: compactness in `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` is perfectness in `D(𝒪_X)`, with nothing carried. Both results the source cites are proved in this library and discharged in the proof: Tag 09M1, that a perfect object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is a compact object of it, as `AlgebraicGeometry.isCompactObject_of_isPerfect`, and Tag 0A9A, that `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` is generated by a perfect object, as `Stacks.Rouquier.exists_isPerfect_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_supported`. They are discharged at the cost of the source's own hypotheses that `X` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated and that `T` be closed with quasi-compact complement, which are Tag 0A9B's hypotheses too and are used for nothing else. The source's step (d), that a direct summand of a perfect object is perfect, is Tag 08CS and is proved in this library, so it is not a hypothesis. The derived category is the locally small model rather than a binder, Tag 0A9A being available at no other; the two directions at an arbitrary model are `Stacks.Duality.Supported.isCompactObject_of_isPerfect` and, with the generator given, `Stacks.Duality.Supported.isPerfect_of_isCompactObject`

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Supported.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_of_isClosed
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A9B].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let
`T ⊆ X` be a closed subset such that `X ∖ T` is quasi-compact. An object of `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` is
compact (in `D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)`) if and only if it is perfect as an object of `D(𝒪_X)`.

Perfect objects are compact in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` by [Stacks, Tag 09M1]
(`Stacks.Duality.PerfectCompact.isCompactObject_of_isPerfect`), hence in the full subcategory
`D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)`, which is closed under direct sums
(`Stacks.Duality.Supported.isCompactObject_of_isCompactObject_obj`). Conversely
`D_{QCoh,T}(𝒪_X)` has a compact perfect generator ([Stacks, Tag 0A9A],
`Stacks.Duality.Supported.exists_isCompactObject_isPerfect_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator`), so
every compact object is built from it by shifts, cones, finite direct sums and summands
([Stacks, Tag 09SR]), and is perfect
(`Stacks.Duality.Supported.isPerfect_of_isCompactObject_of_generator`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_of_isClosed (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsCompact Tᶜ)
    (K : Stacks.Duality.QuasiCoherentSupportedDerivedCategory X T) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} K ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K.obj

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_isPerfect_whiskerRight_comp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A9C].** Let `X` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, `U ⊆ X` a quasi-compact
open and `α : P ⟶ E` a morphism of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with `E` supported on `X \ U`, where either `P`
is perfect, or `P` is pseudo-coherent and `E` is bounded below. Then there is a perfect complex
`I` and a map `u : I ⟶ 𝒪_X` invertible on `U` such that `I ⊗ᴸ P ⟶ P ⟶ E` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_whiskerRight_comp_eq_zero {X U : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact j]
    {P E : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X} (α : P ⟶ E)
    (hE : IsZero ((derivedRestrict j).obj E.obj))
    (hP : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) P.obj ∨
      (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := X.toRingedSpace) P.obj ∧
        DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow E.obj)) :
    ∃ (I : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) (u : I ⟶ 𝟙_ (quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)),
      Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) I.obj ∧
        IsIso ((derivedRestrict j).map ((ObjectProperty.ι _).map u)) ∧
          (u ▷ P) ≫ (λ_ P).hom ≫ α = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLeftAdjoint_qcqsQuasiCoherentDerivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A9E].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of
schemes with `Y` quasi-compact. Then `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` has a right adjoint, the
twisted inverse image `f^×`.

The source assumes `X` and `Y` quasi-compact and quasi-separated, which gives these hypotheses:
`Y` is quasi-compact; `f` is quasi-compact because `X` is and `Y` is quasi-separated; and `f` is
quasi-separated because `X` is.

The generating family of [Stacks, Tag 0GYG] is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_generating_family_quasiCoherentDerivedCategory`, and
`Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.isLeftAdjoint_qcqsQuasiCoherentDerivedPushforward_of_generating`
supplies the rest of the source's argument: part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 08D5], that `Rf_*` preserves
quasi-coherence of cohomology, and [Stacks, Tag 08DZ], that the restricted functor commutes with
direct sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftAdjoint_qcqsQuasiCoherentDerivedPushforward {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [CompactSpace Y] :
    (Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f
      (Stacks.Duality.isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).IsLeftAdjoint
declarations.comment: for a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism with quasi-compact target

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.AnyModel.isLeftAdjoint_restrictedDerivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A9E] at an arbitrary chosen model of the two derived categories.** Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism between quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes. Then
`Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` has a right adjoint — the twisted inverse image `f^×` — at
every chosen model of `D(𝒪_X)` and `D(𝒪_Y)`, and not only at the locally small model at which the
Brown representability argument of the source can be run.

The functor is the canonical `Stacks.Duality.AnyModel.restrictedDerivedPushforward`: that `Rf_*`
carries `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` at all is part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 08D5] and is
discharged, at any model.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftAdjoint_restrictedDerivedPushforward (hX : HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules)
    (hY : HasDerivedCategory.{w} Y.Modules) :
    (restrictedDerivedPushforward f hX hY).IsLeftAdjoint
declarations.comment: at an arbitrary chosen model of the two derived categories, the Brown representability argument of the source being available only at a locally small one

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.isLeftAdjoint_qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A9E.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism between quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes. The functor `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` has a right adjoint.

The proof is the source's: Brown representability ([Stacks, Tag 0A8G]) applies because
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` has direct sums ([Stacks, Tag 08DT]) and is compactly generated
([Stacks, Tag 09IS],
`Stacks.Duality.QcqsGeneration.isCompactlyGenerated_quasiCoherentDerivedCategory`), and because
`f`, a morphism between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated, so that `Rf_*` carries `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into `D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` ([Stacks, Tag 08D5])
and commutes with direct sums ([Stacks, Tag 08DZ]); those two facts about `f` are found by
instance search (`AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_compactSpace`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated.of_quasiSeparatedSpace`).

The derived categories are the locally small models
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasDerivedCategory`, whose morphisms live in the universe `u`
of the schemes. This is the only model at which the statement has content: Brown representability
asks for direct sums indexed by the morphism universe, and at
`CategoryTheory.HasDerivedCategory.standard`, whose morphisms live in `Type (u + 1)`, those direct
sums do not exist in the category of `𝒪_X`-modules. The functor is the canonical
`Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLeftAdjoint_qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward_of_qcqs :
    (qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward f).IsLeftAdjoint

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A9E, with the adjoint exhibited as exact.** For a morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` between quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes there is a functor
`a : D_QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, an adjunction `Rf_* ⊣ a`, and a shift structure on `a` for which
the adjunction is triangulated: Brown representability returns the right adjoint as an exact
functor.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTriangulated_rightAdjoint_qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward_of_qcqs :
    ∃ (a : _) (adj : qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward f ⊣ a) (_ : a.CommShift ℤ),
      adj.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the adjoint is exact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTilde_comp_rightAdjoint_derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardIsoDerivedHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A9F.** Let `φ : R ⟶ S` be a homomorphism of commutative rings, `Y = Spec R`,
`X = Spec S` and `f = Spec φ : X ⟶ Y`. Let `a` be a right adjoint of
`Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then `a` corresponds to `RHom_R(S, -)` under derived
sheafification.

This is the second assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0A9F]; the first — that `Rf_*` corresponds to
restriction of scalars — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTildeCompDerivedQuasicoherentPushforwardIso`, which is also
[Stacks, Tag 0DJK] and is what discharges the hypothesis `hP` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTilde_comp_rightAdjointIsoDerivedHom` here. The other two hypotheses of
that statement, that the comparison functor of [Stacks, Tag 06VT] is an equivalence on the two
affine schemes, are `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.derivedQuasicoherentComparison_isEquivalence`.

`a` is arbitrary, so this says more than the corresponding statement about the particular right
adjoint `AlgebraicGeometry.affineTwistedInverseImage` constructed below; its existence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_adj_affineTwistedInverseImage`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_adj_derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_isoDerivedHom` combines the two into
the tag with no hypothesis. The adjunction `adjP` is therefore **not** hypothetical: it is
constructed, and this statement is kept in the general form only because quantifying over `a`
says more.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTilde_comp_rightAdjoint_derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardIsoDerivedHom
    {R S : CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ S)
    {a : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec S).Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec S).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory}
    (adjP : derivedQuasicoherentPushforward (Spec.map φ) ⊣ a) :
    Nonempty (derivedTilde R ⋙ a ≅
      Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHom.{u, u, u, u, u} φ.hom ⋙ derivedTilde S)
declarations.comment: the right adjoint is derived Hom; the general form, which takes the adjunction adjP for an arbitrary right adjoint a of Rf_* as data. THAT DATA IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: it is constructed by AlgebraicGeometry.derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_adj_affineTwistedInverseImage below, at the functor AlgebraicGeometry.affineTwistedInverseImage, by conjugating the adjunction of Tag 0A70 (Dualizing.AnyModel.restrictScalarsDerived_adj_derivedHom) along the derived sheafification equivalences of Tag 06Z0; the two combine into AlgebraicGeometry.exists_adj_derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_isoDerivedHom below, which assumes nothing beyond the ring map. This form is kept because quantifying over an arbitrary right adjoint says more, a right adjoint being unique up to canonical isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_adj_affineTwistedInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A9F, the existence of the right adjoint in the affine case.** Let `φ : R ⟶ S` be a
homomorphism of commutative rings and `f = Spec φ`. Then
`Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec S}) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})` *has* a right adjoint, namely
`AlgebraicGeometry.affineTwistedInverseImage φ`.

No hypothesis is assumed: the source cites [Stacks, Tag 0A9E] for existence, whose proof goes
through Brown representability and compact generation of `D_QCoh` ([Stacks, Tag 09IS]), but over
an affine base the adjoint can be produced directly. Derived sheafification is an equivalence on
either side ([Stacks, Tag 06Z0], `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTilde_isEquivalence`) and carries
derived restriction of scalars to `Rf_*` ([Stacks, Tag 0DJK],
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTildeCompDerivedQuasicoherentPushforwardIso`), so `Rf_*` is conjugate to
a functor which already has a right adjoint, `RHom_R(S, -)` ([Stacks, Tag 0A70],
`Dualizing.AnyModel.restrictScalarsDerived_adj_derivedHom`); the conjugate of that right adjoint
is a right adjoint of `Rf_*`, which is
`CategoryTheory.Adjunction.ofSquare`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_adj_affineTwistedInverseImage
    {R S : CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ S) :
    Nonempty (derivedQuasicoherentPushforward (Spec.map φ) ⊣ affineTwistedInverseImage φ)
declarations.comment: the right adjoint exists, affine case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_adj_derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_isoDerivedHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0A9F in full, with nothing assumed.** Let `φ : R ⟶ S` be a homomorphism of
commutative rings, `Y = Spec R`, `X = Spec S` and `f = Spec φ : X ⟶ Y`. Then
`Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` has a right adjoint `a`, and `a` corresponds to `RHom_R(S, -)`
under derived sheafification.

This packages the two halves of the tag that the declarations above prove separately — existence,
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_adj_affineTwistedInverseImage`, and the
identification, `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTilde_comp_affineTwistedInverseImageIsoDerivedHom` —
into the single unconditional statement. The first assertion of the tag, that `Rf_*` itself is
derived restriction of scalars, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTildeCompDerivedQuasicoherentPushforwardIso`, which is also
[Stacks, Tag 0DJK].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_adj_derivedQuasicoherentPushforward_isoDerivedHom
    {R S : CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ S) :
    ∃ a : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec R).Modules)
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec R).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory ⥤
        (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec S).Modules)
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec S).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
      Nonempty (derivedQuasicoherentPushforward (Spec.map φ) ⊣ a) ∧
        Nonempty (derivedTilde R ⋙ a ≅
          Dualizing.AnyModel.derivedHom.{u, u, u, u, u} φ.hom ⋙ derivedTilde S)
declarations.comment: existence and identification of the right adjoint, affine case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTildeCompDerivedQuasicoherentPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0DJK.** Let `φ : R ⟶ S` and let `f = Spec φ : Spec S ⟶ Spec R`. Then the square
`D(S) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec S}) ⟶^{Rf_*} D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`,
`D(S) ⟶^{restriction of scalars} D(R) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`
commutes: derived direct image along a morphism of affine schemes corresponds, under derived
sheafification, to derived restriction of scalars.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedTildeCompIso_of_comparisonSquare` with its hypothesis `hsq`
discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedQuasicoherentComparisonSquare`, the commuting square of
[Stacks, Tag 08D7]. It is also the first assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0A9F].
declarations.comment: Rf_* is derived restriction of scalars

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.polynomialRightAdjoint_homologyZero_not_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A9G.** Let `k` be a field and `f : 𝔸¹_k ⟶ Spec k` the structure
morphism of the affine line, which is a separated morphism of finite type between Noetherian
schemes (`AlgebraicGeometry.affineLine_isSeparated`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.affineLine_locallyOfFiniteType`, `AlgebraicGeometry.affineLine_quasiCompact`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.affineLine_isLocallyNoetherian` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_Spec_of_field`). Let `a` be a right adjoint of
`Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_{𝔸¹_k}) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec k})`. Then the degree-zero cohomology sheaf of
`a(𝒪_{Spec k})` is not coherent, so `a` does not carry `D_Coh(𝒪_{Spec k})` into
`D_Coh(𝒪_{𝔸¹_k})`.

The input is coherent: it is `𝒪_{Spec k}` in degree zero by
`AlgebraicGeometry.homologyZeroDerivedTildeSelfIso`, and lies in `D_Coh` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_homologyDerivedTildeSingle`. By [Stacks, Tag 0A9F] the output is
`RHom_k(k[X], k)^~`, whose degree-zero cohomology module is the linear dual `Hom_k(k[X], k)`; that
module is the product of countably many copies of `k`, and multiplication by `X` on it is a
surjective endomorphism with nonzero kernel, so it is not finite over the Noetherian ring `k[X]`
(`Dualizing.AnyModel.polynomialDerivedHom_not_finite`, resting on
`Dualizing.polynomialDerivedHom_not_finite`). The passage from that to non-coherence of the sheaf
is `AlgebraicGeometry.finite_of_isFiniteType_homologyDerivedTilde`.

The existence of `a` is not asserted, exactly as the source does not assert it: it comes from
[Stacks, Tag 0A9E] and enters as the hypothesis `adjP`.
declarations.statement:
theorem polynomialRightAdjoint_homologyZero_not_isCoherent (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {a : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent
          (Spec (CommRingCat.of (Polynomial k))).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory}
    (adjP : derivedQuasicoherentPushforward (Spec.map
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (Polynomial.C : k →+* Polynomial k))) ⊣ a) :
    ¬ ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor

          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent
            (Spec (CommRingCat.of (Polynomial k))).ringCatSheaf)).ι.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dualNumberRightAdjoint_not_minus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A9H.** Let `k` be a field, `Y = Spec(k[ε])` the spectrum of the dual
numbers, `X = Spec(k)` and `f : X ⟶ Y` the closed immersion of the closed point, a finite
morphism of Noetherian schemes (`AlgebraicGeometry.dualNumberSpecMap_isFinite`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_Spec_dualNumber`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_Spec_of_field`). Let `a` be a right adjoint of
`Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then the image under `a` of the sheafification of the residue
field `k[ε]/(ε)` in degree zero is not bounded above. That object is itself bounded above
(`AlgebraicGeometry.minus_derivedTildeSingle`), so `a` does not map `D^-_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` into
`D^-_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.dualNumberRightAdjoint_not_preserves_minus`.

By [Stacks, Tag 0A9F] that image is `RHom_{k[ε]}(k, k[ε]/(ε))^~`, which is unbounded above
because `Ext^i_{k[ε]}(k, k)` is nonzero for every `i ≥ 0`
(`Dualizing.dualNumberDerivedHom_not_minus`, resting on
`Dualizing.dualNumberResidue_zExt_nontrivial`); sheafification reflects the vanishing of a
cohomology module, being faithful. The existence of `a` is not asserted: it comes from
[Stacks, Tag 0A9E] and enters as the hypothesis `adjP`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualNumberRightAdjoint_not_minus (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {a : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent
          (Spec (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k))).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory}
    (adjP : derivedQuasicoherentPushforward
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Dualizing.dualNumberFst k))) ⊣ a) :
    ¬ (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).Modules)).minus
      ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).ringCatSheaf)).ι.obj
          (a.obj ((derivedTilde (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k))).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (DualNumber k)) 0).obj
              (Dualizing.dualNumberResidue k)))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.dualNumberRightAdjoint_not_preserves_minus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0A9H.** For `f : Spec(k) ⟶ Spec(k[ε])` the closed immersion of the
closed point of the spectrum of the dual numbers over a field, a finite morphism of Noetherian
schemes, a right adjoint `a` of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` does not map
`D^-_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` into `D^-_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

The residue field `k[ε]/(ε)`, in degree zero and sheafified, is a bounded-above object
(`AlgebraicGeometry.minus_derivedTildeSingle`) whose image under `a` is not
(`AlgebraicGeometry.dualNumberRightAdjoint_not_minus`).
declarations.statement:
theorem dualNumberRightAdjoint_not_preserves_minus (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {a : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent
          (Spec (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k))).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory}
    (adjP : derivedQuasicoherentPushforward
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Dualizing.dualNumberFst k))) ⊣ a) :
    ¬ ∀ K : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent
          (Spec (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k))).ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
      (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t
          (C := (Spec (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k))).Modules)).minus
        ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent
            (Spec (CommRingCat.of (DualNumber k))).ringCatSheaf)).ι.obj K) →
        (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t (C := (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).Modules)).minus
          ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent
              (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).ringCatSheaf)).ι.obj (a.obj K))

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isBoundedBelow_twistedInverseImage_obj_and_exists_bound
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A9I].** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated
schemes and let `a = f^× : D_QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` be the right adjoint of `Rf_*` of
[Stacks, Tag 0A9E]. Then `a` maps `D^+_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` into `D^+_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. In fact, there exists an
integer `N` such that `H^i(K) = 0` for `i ≤ c` implies `H^i(a(K)) = 0` for `i ≤ c - N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBoundedBelow_twistedInverseImage_obj_and_exists_bound :
    (∀ K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y, DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj →
      DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow
        ((twistedInverseImage f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).obj
          K).obj) ∧
    ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y) (c : ℤ),
      (∀ i ≤ c, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor Y.Modules i).obj K.obj)) →
      ∀ i ≤ c - N, IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj
        ((twistedInverseImage f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).obj
          K).obj)
