declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulay_iff_of_surjective
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing S] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ)
    (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module.Finite S N] :
    IsCohenMacaulayPropForm S N ↔
      (letI : Module R N := Module.compHom N φ; IsCohenMacaulayPropForm R N)

declarations.name: isCohenMacaulay_iff_of_surjective'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 10.103.6 (tag 0AAD).**
Let `φ : R →+* S` be a surjective homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, and let `N`
be a finite `S`-module.  Then `N` is Cohen-Macaulay as an `S`-module if and only if `N`
is Cohen-Macaulay as an `R`-module, where the `R`-module structure on `N` is obtained by
restriction of scalars along `φ` (`Module.compHom N φ`).

Here Noetherianity of `R` is encoded by `IsNoetherianRing R` (and `S` is then automatically
Noetherian as a quotient, but we also assume it for convenience).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulay_iff_of_surjective'
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing S] [IsNoetherianRing S]
    (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : Function.Surjective φ)
    (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module.Finite S N] :
    IsCohenMacaulayModule S N ↔
      (letI : Algebra R S := φ.toAlgebra
       letI : Module R N := Module.compHom N φ
       haveI : IsScalarTower R S N := ⟨fun r s n => mul_smul (φ r) s n⟩
       haveI : Module.Finite R S := Module.Finite.of_surjective (Algebra.linearMap R S) hφ
       haveI : Module.Finite R N := Module.Finite.trans S N
       IsCohenMacaulayModule R N)

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_support_eq_univ
declarations.doc:
**Maximal chains of primes in a local ring with a Cohen–Macaulay module of full support.**
Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring and let `M` be a finite `R`-module which is Cohen–Macaulay
with `Supp(M) = Spec(R)`, that is `depth_𝔪(M) = dim(R)` and `Supp(M) = Spec(R)`. Then every
maximal chain of primes of `R` — one whose steps are covering pairs `𝔭_i ⋖ 𝔭_{i + 1}`, starting
at a minimal prime and ending at a maximal ideal — has length `dim(R)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_support_eq_univ
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (hM : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R M)
    (hsupp : Module.support R M = Set.univ)
    (s : RelSeries {(p, q) : PrimeSpectrum R × PrimeSpectrum R | p ⋖ q})
    (hmin : IsMin s.head) (hmax : IsMax s.last) :
    (s.length : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R
declarations.comment:
The source's `M` Cohen-Macaulay with `Spec(R) = Supp(M)` is the conjunction of
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R M` (Definition 00NF, i.e. `depth_𝔪(M) = dim R`) and
`Module.support R M = Set.univ`, the two being equivalent to it as the source itself remarks; a
maximal chain of primes is a `RelSeries` for the covering relation `⋖` on `PrimeSpectrum R` whose
head is minimal and whose last is maximal. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay.ringKrullDim_eq_height_add_ringKrullDim_quotient_of_support_eq_univ
declarations.doc:
**The dimension formula in a local ring with a Cohen–Macaulay module of full support.** Let
`R` be a Noetherian local ring and let `M` be a finite `R`-module which is Cohen–Macaulay with
`Supp(M) = Spec(R)`, that is `depth_𝔪(M) = dim(R)` and `Supp(M) = Spec(R)`. Then every prime `𝔭`
of `R` satisfies `dim(R) = dim(R_𝔭) + dim(R/𝔭)`, the dimension of the localisation `R_𝔭` being
written as the height of `𝔭`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_eq_height_add_ringKrullDim_quotient_of_support_eq_univ
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (hM : Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R M)
    (hsupp : Module.support R M = Set.univ) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    ringKrullDim R = p.height + ringKrullDim (R ⧸ p)
declarations.comment:
The source's `M` Cohen-Macaulay with `Spec(R) = Supp(M)` is the conjunction of
`Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay R M` (Definition 00NF, i.e. `depth_𝔪(M) = dim R`) and
`Module.support R M = Set.univ`, the two being equivalent to it as the source itself remarks;
`dim(R_𝔭)` is written `𝔭.height`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.depth_eq_supportDim_of_isLocalizedModule
declarations.doc:
**Cohen–Macaulayness localizes.** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring and `M` a finite
`R`-module which is Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. `depth_𝔪(M) = dim Supp(M)` (Definition 00N3). Let
`𝔭 ⊆ R` be a prime in the support of `M`, presented by a localization `Rₚ` of `R` at `𝔭` and a
localization `f : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ` of `M` at `𝔭`. Then `M_𝔭` is Cohen–Macaulay over `R_𝔭`, that is
`depth_{𝔭R_𝔭}(M_𝔭) = dim Supp(M_𝔭)`. Both equations are read in `WithBot ℕ∞`, where
`Module.supportDim` lives.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_eq_supportDim_of_isLocalizedModule {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M]
    (hM : (depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) M : WithBot ℕ∞) = supportDim R M)
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (Rₚ : Type*) [CommRing Rₚ] [Algebra R Rₚ]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime Rₚ p] [IsLocalRing Rₚ] (Mₚ : Type*) [AddCommGroup Mₚ] [Nontrivial Mₚ]
    [Module R Mₚ] [Module Rₚ Mₚ] [IsScalarTower R Rₚ Mₚ] (f : M →ₗ[R] Mₚ)
    [IsLocalizedModule p.primeCompl f] :
    (depth Rₚ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal Rₚ) Mₚ : WithBot ℕ∞) = supportDim Rₚ Mₚ
declarations.comment: Cohen–Macaulayness is spelled out as `depth_𝔪(N) = dim Supp(N)`, the equation Definition 00N3 unfolds to, there being no predicate for it in this library yet; the localization is presented by `IsLocalization.AtPrime` and `IsLocalizedModule`; and `𝔭` is required to lie in `Supp(M)`, spelled `Nontrivial Mₚ`, without which the conclusion is false for the source's own conventions. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.IsCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Cohen–Macaulay module.** An `R`-module `M` is *Cohen–Macaulay* if for every prime `𝔭` in
the support of `M` the localisation `M_𝔭` is a Cohen–Macaulay module over the local ring `R_𝔭`,
that is `depth_{𝔭R_𝔭}(M_𝔭) = dim Supp(M_𝔭)`, the equation being read in `WithBot ℕ∞`.
declarations.statement:
public def IsCohenMacaulay (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] : Prop
declarations.comment: The condition is imposed at the primes of `Supp(M)` rather than at all primes of `R`, the literal reading being vacuous for the source's own conventions on the zero module; Cohen–Macaulayness at a prime is spelled out as the equation `depth_{𝔭R_𝔭}(M_𝔭) = dim Supp(M_𝔭)` of Definition 00N3, there being no predicate for it in this library; the localisations are the canonical models; and the Noetherian and finiteness hypotheses are dropped, as in tags 00LI and 00NF. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsLocallyCohenMacaulayModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AAH.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, not necessarily local, and let `M` be a finite
`R`-module. Then `M` is *Cohen-Macaulay* if `M_p` is a Cohen-Macaulay `R_p`-module for every prime
`p` in the support of `M`. The name records that this is a condition imposed at the points of
`Spec R`; the Stacks project calls it simply "Cohen-Macaulay", which in this repository is already
the name of the local notion `IsCohenMacaulayModule`.

**Erratum in the source.** Stacks 0AAH literally reads "for all primes `p` of `R`". Taken
literally that wording is mathematically inconsistent, because at a prime `p ∉ Supp M` the
localization `M_p` is the zero module, and the zero module is *not* Cohen-Macaulay: with

  `IsCohenMacaulayModule R M ↔ depthSup R 𝔪 M = (krullDim (Module.support R M) : WithBot ℕ∞)`,

the right-hand side is `⊥` for the zero module (its support is empty) while the left-hand side is
a coercion from `ℕ∞` and so is never `⊥`. A literal all-primes reading would therefore be
satisfied by no module except those of full support, which is plainly not the notion 0AAH intends.

This definition quantifies over `Module.support R M` deliberately, which is the intended content
of 0AAH. The restriction is a correction of the source's wording, not a narrowing of the
formalization: the class of modules defined here is exactly the class 0AAH describes.
declarations.statement:
def IsLocallyCohenMacaulayModule (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] : Prop
declarations.comment: Quantified over Supp M. The source's literal all-primes wording is inconsistent when M_p = 0, since the zero module is not Cohen-Macaulay here; this is a source erratum, and the definition captures 0AAH in full.

declarations.name: Module.IsCohenMacaulay.mvPolynomial_of_isBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Cohen–Macaulayness ascends along a polynomial extension.** Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, let
`M` be a finite Cohen–Macaulay `R`-module, and let `N`, together with an `R`-linear map
`f : M →ₗ[R] N`, be the base change of `M` to the polynomial ring `S = MvPolynomial σ R` in
finitely many variables. Then `N` is a Cohen–Macaulay `S`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsCohenMacaulay.mvPolynomial_of_isBaseChange {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] {σ : Type*} [Finite σ] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module (MvPolynomial σ R) N]
    [IsScalarTower R (MvPolynomial σ R) N] {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (hf : IsBaseChange (MvPolynomial σ R) f)
    (hM : IsCohenMacaulay R M) : IsCohenMacaulay (MvPolynomial σ R) N
declarations.comment: The base change `M ⊗_R R[x_1, …, x_n]` is presented abstractly, as an `S`-module `N` with an `R`-linear `f : M →ₗ[R] N` satisfying `IsBaseChange S f` for `S = MvPolynomial σ R`, as in tag 0AAG and in Mathlib's `RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular.of_flat_of_isBaseChange`; the variables are indexed by an arbitrary finite type rather than by `Fin n`; and the finiteness of `M`, which the source keeps inside Definition 0AAH, is assumed explicitly. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: CompletionAdjunction.derivedCompletion_finiteCohomologicalDimension
declarations.doc:
Derived completion along an ideal generated by `r` elements has cohomological amplitude
contained in `[-r, 0]`: it preserves isomorphisms in positive cohomological degrees and
epimorphisms in degree zero, and it sends isomorphisms in negative degrees together with a
monomorphism in degree zero to isomorphisms below degree `-r` and a monomorphism in degree `-r`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedCompletion_finiteCohomologicalDimension
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))]
    {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      fun K ↦ IsDerivedComplete (Ideal.span (Set.range f)) K
    ∀ (C : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory),
      (C ⊣ P.ι) →
      ∀ {K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)} (φ : K ⟶ L),
        (((∀ i : ℤ, 1 ≤ i →
              IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).map φ)) ∧
            Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).map φ)) →
          ((∀ i : ℤ, 1 ≤ i →
              IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).map
                ((C ⋙ P.ι).map φ))) ∧
            Epi ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).map
              ((C ⋙ P.ι).map φ)))) ∧
        (((∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ -1 →
              IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).map φ)) ∧
            Mono ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).map φ)) →
          ((∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ -(r : ℤ) - 1 →
              IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).map
                ((C ⋙ P.ι).map φ))) ∧
            Mono ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-(r : ℤ))).map
              ((C ⋙ P.ι).map φ))))

declarations.name: Dualizing.LocalDuality.nonempty_adicCompletion_ext_linearEquiv_linearMap_localCohomology
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a Noetherian local ring, let `ω` be a normalized dualizing complex, let
`ι : κ ⟶ E` be an injective hull of the residue field, and let `K` be an object of `D_Coh(A)`,
that is, a complex all of whose cohomology modules are finite. Then the `𝔪`-adic completion of
`Ext^{-i}_A(K, ω)` is isomorphic to the module of `A`-linear maps from `H^i_𝔪(K)` to `E`.
Local cohomology is `RΓ_Z` for `Z = V(𝔪)`, and `Ext^{-i}_A(K, ω)` is `Hom_{D(A)}(K, ω⟦-i⟧)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_adicCompletion_ext_linearEquiv_linearMap_localCohomology
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hω : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} ω)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj K))
    {E : ModuleCat.{u} A}
    (ι : (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{u} A).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)) ⟶ E)
    [Mono ι] (hι : Module.IsInjectiveHull ι) (i : ℤ) :
    Nonempty
      (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
          (DerivedCategory.Ext K ω (-i)) ≃ₗ[A]
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj
            ((derivedPowerTorsionProperty A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
                (IsNoetherian.noetherian _)).ι.obj
              ((localCohomologyFunctor A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
                (IsNoetherian.noetherian _)).obj K)) →ₗ[A] E))

declarations.name: Dualizing.LocalDuality.exists_localDualityExtNatEquiv
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a Noetherian local ring, let `ω` be a normalized dualizing complex, let
`ι : κ ⟶ E` be an injective hull of the residue field, and let `Z = V(𝔪)`. For every integer
`i` there is a family of `A`-linear isomorphisms

`H^0(RHom_A(K, ω⟦-i⟧)^∧) ≅ Hom_A(H^i_Z(K), E)`

indexed by the objects `K` of `D(A)`, compatible with the maps induced by every morphism of
`D(A)`: local duality in its module form, natural in `K`.

The left-hand side is the degree-zero cohomology of the derived `𝔪`-adic completion of
`RHom_A(K, ω⟦-i⟧)`, whose degree-zero cohomology is `Ext^{-i}_A(K, ω)`; the right-hand side is
the Matlis dual of the degree-`i` local cohomology module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_localDualityExtNatEquiv
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → A) (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hω : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} ω)
    {E : ModuleCat.{u} A}
    (ι : (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{u} A).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)) ⟶ E)
    [Mono ι] (hι : Module.IsInjectiveHull ι) (i : ℤ) :
    ∃ θ : ∀ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A),
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
            ((DerivedCompletion.derivedCompletionFunctor A f).obj
              ((StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := A)).hom.obj
                (Opposite.op K,
                  (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor
                    (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (-i)).obj ω))) : Type u) ≃ₗ[A]
          (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj
              ((localCohomologyEndofunctor A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
                (IsNoetherian.noetherian _)).obj K) : Type u) →ₗ[A] (E : Type u)),
      ∀ (K K' : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (g : K' ⟶ K)
        (x : ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj
          ((DerivedCompletion.derivedCompletionFunctor A f).obj
            ((StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := A)).hom.obj
              (Opposite.op K,
                (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor
                  (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (-i)).obj ω))) : Type u)),
        θ K' (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).map
              ((DerivedCompletion.derivedCompletionFunctor A f).map
                ((StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedHomAdjunction (R := A)).hom.map
                  (show (Opposite.op K, (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor
                        (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (-i)).obj ω) ⟶
                      (Opposite.op K', (CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor
                        (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (-i)).obj ω) from
                    (g.op, 𝟙 _))))).hom x) =
          (θ K x).comp
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).map
              ((localCohomologyEndofunctor A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
                (IsNoetherian.noetherian _)).map g)).hom
declarations.comment: natural in K

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.nonempty_adicCompletion_ext_linearEquiv_matlisDual_localCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AAK** in the spelling of local cohomology with support in `V(𝔪)`.
Over a Noetherian local ring with a normalized dualizing complex, the `𝔪`-adic completion of
`Ext^{-i}(K, ω)` is the Matlis dual of `H^i_{V(𝔪)}(K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_adicCompletion_ext_linearEquiv_matlisDual_localCohomology
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (K ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj K))
    (hω : Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex ω)
    (E : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (e : (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{u} A).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)) ⟶ E)
    [Mono e] (he : Module.IsInjectiveHull e) (i : ℤ) :
    Nonempty
      (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) (DerivedCategory.Ext K ω (-i)) ≃ₗ[A]
        (localCohomologyWithSupportIn
          A (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (maximalIdeal A : Set A)) K i →ₗ[A] E))
declarations.comment: the module form, with the support-closed-subset model of local cohomology in place of the torsion-complex model

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.nonempty_adicCompletion_ext_linearEquiv_matlisDual_localCohomologyPlus
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 0AAK** for a bounded-below complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_adicCompletion_ext_linearEquiv_matlisDual_localCohomologyPlus
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) j).obj K))
    (hω : Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex ω)
    (E : ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (e : (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{u} A).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)) ⟶ E)
    [Mono e] (he : Module.IsInjectiveHull e) (i : ℤ) :
    Nonempty
      (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) (DerivedCategory.Ext K.obj ω (-i)) ≃ₗ[A]
        (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus
          A (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (maximalIdeal A : Set A)) K i →ₗ[A] E))
declarations.comment: the module form for a bounded-below complex, with the support-closed-subset model of local cohomology

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.nonempty_adicCompletion_localizedDualCohomology_linearEquiv_matlisDual
declarations.doc:
**Local duality at an arbitrary prime.** Let `A` be Noetherian with dualizing complex `ω`
and dimension function `δ`, let `q` be a prime, and let `E` be an injective hull of the residue
field of `A_q`. For `K` in `D⁺_{Coh}(A)` and `n + i = -δ(q)`, the `qA_q`-adic completion of
`H^n(RHom_A(K, ω))_q` is the Matlis dual of `H^i_{qA_q}(K_q)`.

This is [Stacks, Tag 0AAK] at a general prime: the localization `ω_q⟦-δ(q)⟧` is a normalized
dualizing complex over `A_q` by [Stacks, Tag 0A7Z], and flat base change identifies
`H^n(RHom_A(K, ω))_q` with `Ext^n_{A_q}(K_q, ω_q)`. It is the local-duality input to the proof
of [Stacks, Tag 0EFX]. The two sides are isomorphic as `A_q`-modules for each `K` separately;
no naturality in `K` is claimed, and 0AAK provides none.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_adicCompletion_localizedDualCohomology_linearEquiv_matlisDual
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (q : PrimeSpectrum A) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) i).obj K))
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (hω : Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex ω)
    (E : ModuleCat.{u} (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
    (e : (ModuleCat.uliftFunctor.{u} (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)).obj
      (ModuleCat.of (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
        (ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))) ⟶ E)
    [Mono e] (he : Module.IsInjectiveHull e)
    (n i : ℤ) (hni : n + i = -Dualizing.dualizingDimension ω q) :
    Nonempty
      (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal))
          (LocalizedModule q.asIdeal.primeCompl
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) n).obj
              ((Dualizing.dualizingDerivedHomFunctor.{u, u} A ω).obj (.op K.obj))))
          ≃ₗ[Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal]
        (localCohomologyWithSupportInPlus (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)
          (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) : Set _))
          (localizedComplex.{u, u} q K) i →ₗ[Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal] E))
declarations.comment: local duality at an arbitrary prime of a Noetherian ring with a dualizing complex, reached from the local case through the normalizing shift of 0A7Z and flat base change of Ext; objectwise, with no naturality in the complex

declarations.name: acyclic_limit_of_acyclic_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
Let `α` be an ordinal and `K` an inverse system of cochain complexes of
abelian groups over `α`. If every `K_β` is acyclic and the comparison map
`K^n_β → lim_{γ < β} K^n_γ` is surjective for every `β` and `n`, then the
limit complex `lim_{β < α} K_β` is acyclic.
declarations.statement:
theorem acyclic_limit_of_acyclic_of_surjective (α : Ordinal.{u})
    (K : (α.ToType)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u} ℤ)
    (hAcyclic : ∀ β : α.ToType, (K.obj (op β)).Acyclic)
    (hSurj : ∀ (β : α.ToType) (n : ℤ),
      Function.Surjective
        (ConcreteCategory.hom (comparisonMap α K β n))) :
    (limit K).Acyclic

declarations.name: IsClosedMap.image_closure_preimage_eq_closure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AAU** (part 1). A closed continuous map carries the closure of the preimage of
a subset of its range onto the closure of that subset.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsClosedMap.image_closure_preimage_eq_closure
    (hf_closed : IsClosedMap f) (hf_cont : Continuous f) {T : Set Y}
    (hT : T ⊆ range f) :
    f '' closure (f ⁻¹' T) = closure T

declarations.name: isLocallyClosed_iff_preimage_isLocallyClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AAU** (part 4). For a surjective closed continuous map `f : X → Y` and any `T ⊆ Y`,
`T` is locally closed iff `f ⁻¹' T` is locally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyClosed_iff_preimage_isLocallyClosed
    (hf_surj : Function.Surjective f) (hf_cont : Continuous f)
    (hf_closed : IsClosedMap f) (T : Set Y) :
    IsLocallyClosed T ↔ IsLocallyClosed (f ⁻¹' T)

registrations.name: IsClosedMap.isQuotientMap
registrations.comment: submersive

declarations.name: intersectionSubring_ne_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AAV.** Let `L / K` be an algebraic extension of fields and let
`B` be a valuation subring of `L` (so `B` is a valuation ring with `Frac B = L`)
which is not a field (`B ≠ ⊤`). Then `A = K ∩ B = B.comap (algebraMap K L)` is a
valuation subring of `K` (so a valuation ring with fraction field `K`, by its type)
which is not a field (`A ≠ ⊤`).
declarations.statement:
theorem intersectionSubring_ne_top
    {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    (halg : Algebra.IsAlgebraic K L)
    (B : ValuationSubring L) (hB : B ≠ ⊤) :
    intersectionSubring B ≠ (⊤ : ValuationSubring K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.compl_mem_nhds_of_isLocallyConstructible_of_mem_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
A generic point of an irreducible component which is not in a
locally constructible subset has an open neighbourhood disjoint from that subset.
declarations.statement:
public theorem compl_mem_nhds_of_isLocallyConstructible_of_mem_genericPoints
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {E : Set X} {ξ : X} (hE : IsLocallyConstructible E)
    (hξ : ξ ∈ genericPoints X) (hξE : ξ ∉ E) :
    Eᶜ ∈ 𝓝 ξ
declarations.comment: neighborhood_disjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_nhds_of_isLocallyConstructible_of_mem_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
A locally constructible set containing the generic point of an irreducible component
contains an open neighbourhood of that point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mem_nhds_of_isLocallyConstructible_of_mem_genericPoints
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {E : Set X} {ξ : X} (hE : IsLocallyConstructible E)
    (hξ : ξ ∈ genericPoints X) (hξE : ξ ∈ E) :
    E ∈ 𝓝 ξ
declarations.comment: neighborhood_contained

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isArtinianRing_stalk_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_zero
declarations.doc: The local rings of a locally Noetherian scheme of dimension at most zero are Artinian.
declarations.statement:
lemma isArtinianRing_stalk_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_zero
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 0) (x : X) :
    IsArtinianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)
declarations.comment: the summands are spectra of Artinian local rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_sigmaFromSpecStalk_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_zero
declarations.doc:
A locally Noetherian scheme of dimension at most zero is the coproduct of the spectra of its
local rings.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIso_sigmaFromSpecStalk_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_zero
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 0) :
    IsIso (sigmaFromSpecStalk X)
declarations.comment: the disjoint-union decomposition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finite_setOf_mapsTo_and_quasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
For a finite-type morphism of schemes, the set of points over a fixed point at which the
morphism is quasi-finite is finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_setOf_mapsTo_and_quasiFiniteAt
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (s : S) :
    {x : X | f x = s ∧ quasiFiniteAt f x}.Finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsModification
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` to an integral scheme is a **modification** if `X'` is
integral and `f` is birational and proper.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsModification {X X' : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] (f : X' ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlteration
declarations.doc:
A morphism to an integral scheme is an alteration if it is proper and dominant, its
source is integral, and its restriction over some nonempty open of the target is finite.
declarations.statement: public abbrev IsAlteration {Y X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] (f : Y ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_isIntegralHom_of_isBirational_of_isNormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AB1.** An integral birational morphism of integral schemes whose
target is normal is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_of_isIntegralHom_of_isBirational_of_isNormal
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y]
    [IsIntegralHom f] [IsNormal Y] (hf : IsBirational f) :
    IsIso f

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_pow_eq_pow_of_eq_at_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
Two elements of a Noetherian local ring of dimension at most one which
agree at every minimal prime have equal positive powers if one lies in the
maximal ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pow_eq_pow_of_eq_at_minimalPrimes
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A ≤ 1) (a₁ a₂ : A)
    (ha₂ : a₂ ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)
    (heq : ∀ p : minimalPrimes A,
      (algebraMap A (@Localization.AtPrime A _ p.1 p.2.isPrime)) a₁ =
        (algebraMap A (@Localization.AtPrime A _ p.1 p.2.isPrime)) a₂) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ a₁ ^ n = a₂ ^ n

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_pow_mem_range_of_sub_mem_nilradical_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AB3.** An element of the product of the minimal-prime localizations that is
congruent, modulo the extended nilradical, to an element of the maximal ideal has a positive
power in the image of the original ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pow_mem_range_of_sub_mem_nilradical_map
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) :
    let L := ∀ p : {q : PrimeSpectrum A // q.asIdeal ∈ minimalPrimes A},
      Localization.AtPrime p.1.asIdeal
    let I : Ideal A := sInf (minimalPrimes A)
      ∀ (f : L) (a : A), a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A →
      f - algebraMap A L a ∈ I.map (algebraMap A L) →
        ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ f ^ n ∈ Set.range (algebraMap A L)

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_mem_maximalIdeal_radical_span_eq_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AB4.** An integral subring of the product of the minimal-prime
localizations contains the image of a parameter of a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_mem_maximalIdeal_radical_span_eq_of_isIntegral
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 1) :
    let L := ∀ p : {q : PrimeSpectrum A // q.asIdeal ∈ minimalPrimes A},
      Localization.AtPrime p.1.asIdeal
    ∀ (K : Type v) [CommRing K] (f : K →+* L), f.IsIntegral →
      ∃ a : A, a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∧
        (∃ x : K, f x = algebraMap A L a) ∧
        (Ideal.span {a}).radical = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt_of_target_stalk_dimension_le_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AB6.** A locally finite type morphism which is generically
quasi-finite is quasi-finite above a point with Noetherian local ring of dimension at most
one. It suffices to impose the generic condition only on components whose generic points
specialize to the chosen point, or alternatively to assume quasi-finiteness at every generic
point or on a dense set over a locally Noetherian target.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiFiniteAt_of_target_stalk_dimension_le_one
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (y : Y)
    (hyNoetherian : IsNoetherianRing (Y.presheaf.stalk y))
    (hyDimension : ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk y) ≤ 1)
    (hgeneric :
      (∀ η : X, η ∈ genericPoints X →
        letI := (f.residueFieldMap η).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.IsAlgebraic (Y.residueField (f η)) (X.residueField η)) ∨
      (∀ η : X, η ∈ genericPoints X → Specializes (f η) y →
        letI := (f.residueFieldMap η).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.IsAlgebraic (Y.residueField (f η)) (X.residueField η)) ∨
      (∀ η : X, η ∈ genericPoints X → quasiFiniteAt f η) ∨
      (IsLocallyNoetherian Y ∧ Dense {x : X | quasiFiniteAt f x})) :
    ∀ x : X, f x = y → quasiFiniteAt f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_ringKrullDim_stalk_le_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AB7.** A proper morphism which is generically quasi-finite is finite
over a neighbourhood of a point whose local ring is Noetherian of dimension at most one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFinite_morphismRestrict_of_ringKrullDim_stalk_le_one
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (y : Y)
    [IsNoetherianRing (Y.presheaf.stalk y)] (hy : ringKrullDim (Y.presheaf.stalk y) ≤ 1)
    (h : (∀ (η : X), η ∈ genericPoints X → letI := (f.residueFieldMap η).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.IsAlgebraic (Y.residueField (f η)) (X.residueField η)) ∨
      ((∀ (η : X), η ∈ genericPoints X → Specializes (f η) y →
          letI := (f.residueFieldMap η).hom.toAlgebra
          Algebra.IsAlgebraic (Y.residueField (f η)) (X.residueField η)) ∨
        ((∀ (η : X), η ∈ genericPoints X → quasiFiniteAt f η) ∨
          (IsLocallyNoetherian Y ∧ Dense {x : X | quasiFiniteAt f x})))) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, y ∈ V ∧ IsFinite (f ∣_ V)

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.finiteStratification
declarations.doc: The canonical Fitting stratification associated to source of a groupoid scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finiteStratification {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) (n : ℕ) :
    G.objects.left.IdealSheafData
declarations.comment: the Fitting stratification

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.finiteStratification_zero
declarations.doc: The identity arrows force the zeroth Fitting closed subscheme to be all objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteStratification_zero {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left] :
    finiteStratification G 0 = ⊥
declarations.comment: the first closed subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.finiteStratification_mono
declarations.doc: The Fitting closed subschemes form a decreasing sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteStratification_mono {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left] (n : ℕ) :
    finiteStratification G n ≤ finiteStratification G (n + 1)
declarations.comment: decreasing closed subschemes

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.finiteStratification_exhaustive
declarations.doc: No point lies in all Fitting closed subschemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteStratification_exhaustive {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left] (x : G.objects.left) :
    ∃ n, x ∉ (finiteStratification G n).support
declarations.comment: empty intersection

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.finiteStratification_invariant
declarations.doc:
Every member of the Fitting stratification is invariant under the groupoid.

The second projection of the scheme of composable pairs is simultaneously the base change of
source along target and the base change of source along source, by the two cartesian lower
squares of the diagram of Stacks Tag 04LF. So both inverse images of a member of the
stratification are the Fitting ideal sheaf of the pushforward of the structure sheaf along that
single projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteStratification_invariant {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left] (n : ℕ) :
    IsInvariantClosedSubscheme G (finiteStratification G n)
declarations.comment: invariance

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.finiteStratification_rank
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AB9: the rank of each stratum.** For a groupoid scheme with finite
source and target there is an open subscheme `W` of the closed subscheme cut out by the
`(r-1)`st Fitting ideal sheaf of `s_* 𝒪_R` whose image in the object scheme is the difference of
the supports of the `(r-1)`st and `r`th Fitting ideal sheaves, and the base change of source to
`W` is finite locally free of rank `r`.

The open subscheme is `Stacks.Groupoids.exists_opens_finiteStratification_stratum`. Finite local
freeness is checked affine-locally by
`Stacks.Groupoids.module_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_finiteStratification_stratum` and assembled
into the sheaf-level statement by
`Stacks.Modules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_of_module_affineOpens` and
`Stacks.Modules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_iff_localGenerators`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteStratification_rank {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left] (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) :
    ∃ W : (finiteStratification G (r - 1)).subscheme.Opens,
      Set.range (W.ι ≫ (finiteStratification G (r - 1)).subschemeι) =
          ((finiteStratification G (r - 1)).support : Set G.objects.left) \
            ((finiteStratification G r).support : Set G.objects.left) ∧
        IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank
          (pullback.snd G.source.left
            (W.ι ≫ (finiteStratification G (r - 1)).subschemeι)) r
declarations.comment: rank of each stratum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invariant_thickening_finiteLocallyFree_restriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ABA.** A groupoid scheme with finite source and target has an
invariant open subscheme `W` carrying an invariant closed thickening `W'` such that the source
and target maps of the restriction of the groupoid to `W'` are finite locally free, and such
that the saturation of the closure of `W` is the whole object scheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_invariant_thickening_finiteLocallyFree_restriction {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left] :
    ∃ (W : G.objects.left.Opens) (W' : Scheme.{u}) (i : W' ⟶ W.toScheme)
      (hmono : Mono (i ≫ W.ι)),
      letI : Mono (i ≫ W.ι) := hmono
      IsInvariantOpen G W ∧
      IsInvariantMonomorphism G (i ≫ W.ι) ∧
      (G.target.left.base ''
        (G.source.left.base ⁻¹' closure (W : Set G.objects.left)) = Set.univ) ∧
      IsThickening i ∧
      (let g : Over.mk (i ≫ W.ι ≫ G.objects.hom) ⟶ G.objects := Over.homMk (i ≫ W.ι)
       IsFiniteLocallyFree (restrictionSource G g).left ∧
       IsFiniteLocallyFree (restrictionTarget G g).left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finitePresentation_layerThickeningInclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ABB (1).** For a groupoid scheme with finite source and target whose
source map is of finite presentation, the inclusion of the invariant closed thickening into the
invariant open is of finite presentation: on each stage it is the base change of one member of
the Fitting stratification along the inclusion of the open chosen there.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_layerThickeningInclusion {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left]
    (hs : FinitePresentation G.source.left) :
    FinitePresentation (layerThickeningInclusion G)
declarations.comment: finite_presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_layerUnionOpen_of_orbit_subset_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ABB (2).** For a groupoid scheme with finite source and target whose
source map is of finite presentation, a point whose orbit consists of generic points of
irreducible components of the object scheme lies in the invariant open constructed for the
groupoid.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_layerUnionOpen_of_orbit_subset_genericPoints {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left]
    (hs : FinitePresentation G.source.left) (x : G.objects.left)
    (hx : ∀ y : G.objects.left,
      (∃ r : G.arrows.left, G.source.left r = x ∧ G.target.left r = y) →
        y ∈ genericPoints G.objects.left) :
    x ∈ layerUnionOpen G
declarations.comment: generic_orbit_mem

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invariant_affine_open_with_finiteLocallyFree_thickening'
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ABC].** Let `G` be a groupoid scheme whose source and target are finite and
of finite presentation, with quasi-separated object scheme, and let `x : ι → U` be finitely many
points whose orbits consist of generic points of irreducible components of the object scheme.
Then there is an invariant affine open `V` of the object scheme and an ideal sheaf `Z` on it such
that the closed subscheme `V(Z)` is an affine invariant thickening of finite presentation inside
`V` containing the images of the `x i`, over which the source and target of the restricted
groupoid are finite locally free.

Nothing is assumed beyond the hypotheses of the tag. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invariant_affine_open_with_finiteLocallyFree_thickening`, which carries
[Stacks, Tag 06AD] as the hypothesis `H06AD`, with that hypothesis discharged by
`Stacks.Thickenings.forall_isAffine_of_isThickening`, the library's 06AD.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_invariant_affine_open_with_finiteLocallyFree_thickening'
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left]
    (hs : FinitePresentation G.source.left)
    (ht : FinitePresentation G.target.left)
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace G.objects.left]
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (x : ι → G.objects.left)
    (hx : ∀ i y, (∃ r : G.arrows.left,
      G.source.left r = x i ∧ G.target.left r = y) →
        ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents G.objects.left, IsGenericPoint y Z) :
    ∃ (V : G.objects.left.Opens) (Z : V.toScheme.IdealSheafData),
      (∀ i, x i ∈ Set.range (Z.subschemeι ≫ V.ι)) ∧
      Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantOpen G V ∧
      IsAffineOpen V ∧
      Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantMonomorphism G (Z.subschemeι ≫ V.ι) ∧
      IsAffine Z.subscheme ∧
      IsThickening Z.subschemeι ∧
      FinitePresentation Z.subschemeι ∧
      (let U' : Over S := Over.mk (Z.subschemeι ≫ V.ι ≫ G.objects.hom)
       let g : U' ⟶ G.objects := Over.homMk (Z.subschemeι ≫ V.ι) (by rfl)
       Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree
          (AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.restrict G g).groupoid.source.left ∧
       Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree
          (AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.restrict G g).groupoid.target.left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invariant_affine_finiteLocallyFree_thickening_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ABD].** Let `G` be a groupoid scheme whose source and target are finite, with
locally Noetherian object scheme, and let `x : ι → U` be finitely many points whose orbits consist
of generic points of irreducible components of the object scheme. Then there is an invariant
affine open `V` of the object scheme and an ideal sheaf `Z` on it such that the closed subscheme
`V(Z)` is an affine invariant thickening inside `V` containing the images of the `x i`, over which
the source and target of the restricted groupoid are finite locally free.

Nothing is assumed beyond the hypotheses: the affineness of `V` comes from [Stacks, Tag 01YQ]
through
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_preimage_eq_of_isThickening_of_isLocallyNoetherian`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_invariant_affine_finiteLocallyFree_thickening_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian G.objects.left]
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (x : ι → G.objects.left)
    (hx : ∀ i y, (∃ r : G.arrows.left,
      G.source.left r = x i ∧ G.target.left r = y) →
        ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents G.objects.left, IsGenericPoint y Z) :
    ∃ (V : G.objects.left.Opens) (Z : V.toScheme.IdealSheafData),
      (∀ i, x i ∈ Set.range (Z.subschemeι ≫ V.ι)) ∧
      Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantOpen G V ∧
      IsAffineOpen V ∧
      Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantMonomorphism G (Z.subschemeι ≫ V.ι) ∧
      IsAffine Z.subscheme ∧
      IsThickening Z.subschemeι ∧
      (let U' : Over S := Over.mk (Z.subschemeι ≫ V.ι ≫ G.objects.hom)
       let g : U' ⟶ G.objects := Over.homMk (Z.subschemeι ≫ V.ι) (by rfl)
       Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree
          (AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.restrict G g).groupoid.source.left ∧
       Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFree
          (AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.restrict G g).groupoid.target.left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invariant_affine_open_of_restriction_integral
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ABE]**.  Let `G` be a groupoid scheme over `S` whose source and target maps
are integral, let `g : U' ⟶ G.objects` be integral with image meeting every orbit of `G`, and
let `R` be the restriction of `G` along `g`.  A point of the object scheme of `R` contained in
an invariant affine open has its image in `G.objects` contained in an invariant affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_invariant_affine_open_of_restriction_integral
    (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S) [IsIntegralHom G.source.left]
    [IsIntegralHom G.target.left] {U' : Over S} {g : U' ⟶ G.objects} [IsIntegralHom g.left]
    (R : GroupoidScheme.Restriction G g)
    (horbit : ∀ u : G.objects.left, ∃ u' : U'.left, ∃ r : G.arrows.left,
      G.source.left r = u ∧ G.target.left r = g.left u')
    (u' : R.groupoid.objects.left) (W' : R.groupoid.objects.left.Opens)
    (hW'inv : Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantOpen R.groupoid W') (hW'aff : IsAffineOpen W')
    (hu' : u' ∈ W') :
    ∃ W : G.objects.left.Opens, Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantOpen G W ∧ IsAffineOpen W ∧
      R.hom.mapObjects.left u' ∈ W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_ideal_invariant_affine_preimage_basicOpen'
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ABF].** Let `G` be a groupoid scheme whose source and target are finite and
of finite presentation, let `x : ι → U` be finitely many points whose orbits consist of generic
points of irreducible components of the object scheme, let `j : U ⟶ Spec A` be an immersion, and
let `I` be an ideal of `A` whose vanishing locus misses the image of `j` and whose union with
that image is closed. Then some `h ∈ I` has `j ⁻¹ D(h)` an invariant affine open of the object
scheme containing all the `x i`.

Nothing is assumed beyond the hypotheses of the tag. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mem_ideal_invariant_affine_preimage_basicOpen`, which carries
[Stacks, Tag 06AD] as the hypothesis `H06AD`, with that hypothesis discharged by
`Stacks.Thickenings.forall_isAffine_of_isThickening`, which is Tag 06AD.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mem_ideal_invariant_affine_preimage_basicOpen'
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left]
    (hs : FinitePresentation G.source.left)
    (ht : FinitePresentation G.target.left)
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (x : ι → G.objects.left)
    (hx : ∀ i y, (∃ r : G.arrows.left,
      G.source.left r = x i ∧ G.target.left r = y) →
        ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents G.objects.left, IsGenericPoint y Z)
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (j : G.objects.left ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [IsImmersion j]
    (I : Ideal A)
    (hdisj : Disjoint (Set.range (j : G.objects.left → Spec (CommRingCat.of A)))
      (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A)))
    (hclosed : IsClosed (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) ∪
      Set.range (j : G.objects.left → Spec (CommRingCat.of A)))) :
    ∃ h : A, h ∈ I ∧
      (let W := j ⁻¹ᵁ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen h
       Stacks.Groupoids.IsInvariantOpen G W ∧ IsAffineOpen W ∧ ∀ i, x i ∈ W)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.not_specialization_of_exists_arrow
declarations.doc:
Distinct points joined by an arrow of a groupoid scheme with finite source and target cannot
be related by specialization.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_specialization_of_exists_arrow {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left]
    {u u' : G.objects.left} (hne : u ≠ u')
    (horbit : ∃ r : G.arrows.left, G.source.left r = u ∧ G.target.left r = u') :
    ¬ (u ⤳ u')

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffine_of_isImmersion_of_isAffineOpen_preimage_basicOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ABH.** A quasi-compact immersion into an affine scheme whose
restriction over a standard open is affine and the remainder of whose image is closed has an
affine source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_isImmersion_of_isAffineOpen_preimage_basicOpen {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {V : Scheme.{u}} (j : V ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [IsImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (f : A) (hD : IsAffineOpen (j ⁻¹ᵁ PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f))
    (hclosed : IsClosed (Set.range (j : V → Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) ∩
      ((Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).basicOpen
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv f) :
          Set (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)))ᶜ)) : IsAffine V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_isInvariantOpen_isAffineOpen_mem_of_krullDimLE_one
declarations.doc:
Let `G` be a groupoid scheme whose source and target maps are finite and whose object scheme
is separated and locally Noetherian, and let `u` be a point of the object scheme such that every
point of the orbit of `u` has a stalk of Krull dimension at most one. Then `u` lies in an
invariant affine open of the object scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvariantOpen_isAffineOpen_mem_of_krullDimLE_one
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) [IsFinite G.source.left] [IsFinite G.target.left]
    [G.objects.left.IsSeparated] [IsLocallyNoetherian G.objects.left]
    (u : G.objects.left)
    (hdim : ∀ u' : G.objects.left,
      (∃ r : G.arrows.left, G.source.left.base r = u ∧ G.target.left.base r = u') →
        Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (G.objects.left.presheaf.stalk u')) :
    ∃ W : G.objects.left.Opens, IsInvariantOpen G W ∧ IsAffineOpen W ∧ u ∈ W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEmbedding_pointsMap_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABJ, part one.** The map on points of an immersion of algebraic spaces over `S`
is a topological embedding: a homeomorphism onto its image.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEmbedding_pointsMap_of_isImmersion (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    Topology.IsEmbedding (pointsMap B S hS Z i)
declarations.comment: homeomorphism onto the image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyClosed_range_pointsMap_of_isImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABJ, part two.** The image on points of an immersion of algebraic spaces over
`S` is a locally closed subset of the point space of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyClosed_range_pointsMap_of_isImmersion (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsLocallyClosed (Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z i))
declarations.comment: locally closed image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsDominant
declarations.doc:
A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` is *dominant* when the image of its map on points is
dense in the point space of the target.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsDominant (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsLocallyQuasiFinite.of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The base change of a locally quasi-finite morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` along an
arbitrary morphism of algebraic spaces is locally quasi-finite.

The square is the one with `p` over `f`, so `p : W ⟶ Z` is the base change of
`f : X ⟶ Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyQuasiFinite.of_isPullback
    {W X Z Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS p
declarations.comment: part (3): locally quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiFinite.of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
The base change of a quasi-finite morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` along an arbitrary
morphism of algebraic spaces is quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiFinite.of_isPullback
    {W X Z Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiFinite B S hS p
declarations.comment: part (4): quasi-finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isOpen_setOf_isQuasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABM, part (1).** The set of points at which a morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` is quasi-finite is open in the point space of Tag 03BU. Applied to a base change `f'` of
`f` this is the second clause of part (1), that the quasi-finite locus of `f'` is open.

The source assumes `f` locally of finite type; that is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_setOf_isQuasiFiniteAt (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsOpen {x | IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: part (1): the quasi-finite locus is open

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.setOf_isQuasiFiniteAt_eq_preimage_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABM, part (2).** For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of
finite type, the locus of quasi-finiteness of a base change is the inverse image of the locus
of quasi-finiteness of the morphism.

Compatible surjective étale charts of the cartesian square
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_compatible_etale_charts`) give a chart `V` of the target, a
chart `U ⟶ V` of `f`, a chart `V' ⟶ V` of `g` and the induced chart `U' = U ×_V V' ⟶ V'` of
the base change, with `U'` an atlas of the fibre product. A field-valued point of `U'` lying
over the given point of `|X'|` turns the two squares into pointed étale charts of `f'` at that
point and of `f` at its image, whose selected scheme points correspond under `U' ⟶ U`. Local
quasi-finiteness of morphisms of schemes being étale local on the source and target
(Stacks 04R3), quasi-finiteness at a point is the induced germ condition read in any one
pointed chart (Stacks 04NC), so each side becomes quasi-finiteness of a morphism of schemes at
corresponding points of a cartesian square of schemes, which is **Stacks 01TM**.
declarations.comment: part (2): the locus commutes with base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.setOf_isQuasiFiniteAt_eq_preimage_of_isPullback'
declarations.doc:
In a cartesian square of presheaves over `S` whose corners `X`, `Y` and `Z` are algebraic
spaces, with `f` locally of finite type, the locus in the source of the base change of `f` where
that base change is quasi-finite is the preimage, under the projection on points, of the locus in
the source of `f` where `f` is quasi-finite.

The square is the one with `p` over `f` and `q` over `g`, so `p : W ⟶ Z` is the base change of
`f : X ⟶ Y` and `q : W ⟶ X` is the projection.
declarations.statement:
theorem setOf_isQuasiFiniteAt_eq_preimage_of_isPullback'
    {W X Z Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    {x' | IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS p x'} =
      pointsMap B S hS W q ⁻¹' {x | IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: part (2): the quasi-finite locus commutes with base change

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_setOf_mapsTo_and_isQuasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABN.** For a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` of finite type, only finitely
many points of the source lying over a fixed point of the target are points at which the
morphism is quasi-finite.

Represent the point of the target by a field-valued point `Spec k ⟶ Y` and base change twice:
once along it, and once more along the identity of `Spec k`. The second base change is a
finite-type morphism out of an algebraic space with quasi-compact source, so it has an
*affine* surjective étale chart `U` (Stacks 03H6), and the morphism of schemes `U ⟶ Spec k`
it induces is of finite type with compact source, hence quasi-compact: Stacks 0AAY bounds the
set of its quasi-finite points over the closed point of `Spec k`, and that is all of `U`
because `Spec k` is a one-point space.

A point of `|X|` over the given point at which `f` is quasi-finite lifts through both
cartesian squares (Stacks 03H4), and quasi-finiteness travels with it because forming the
quasi-finite locus commutes with base change
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.setOf_isQuasiFiniteAt_eq_preimage_of_isPullback`). A field-valued
representative of the lift on the chart then exhibits the point as the image of a member of
that finite set.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_setOf_mapsTo_and_isQuasiFiniteAt
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (y : points B S hS Y) :
    {x : points B S hS X |
      pointsMap B S hS X f x = y ∧ IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x}.Finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleAlgebraRestrictionIntegralClosureIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABP, part (1), at the level of algebras.**  The integral closure of the structure
sheaf in an algebra commutes with restriction along an étale morphism `g : W ⟶ X`.

This is the whole of the source's reason for part (1): the normalization of `X` in `Y` is the
relative spectrum of the integral closure of `𝒪_X` in `f_* 𝒪_Y`, and that construction is
étale-local, hence "commutes with étale base change".
declarations.statement:
def etaleAlgebraRestrictionIntegralClosureIso (g : W ⟶ X) (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom)
    (A : AlgebraSheaf.{u, m} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    (etaleAlgebraRestriction B S hS g hg).obj (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf A) ≅
      AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf ((etaleAlgebraRestriction B S hS g hg).obj A)
declarations.comment:
part (1), étale base change: the integral closure of the structure sheaf in an
  algebra is unchanged by restriction along an étale morphism, which is the construction of the
  normalization commuting with étale base change. The geometric form, for the relative spectra,
  is `normalizationInBaseChangeIso`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationInBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABP, part (1).**  For an étale morphism `g : W ⟶ X` the fibre product
`W ×_X X'` is the normalization of `W` in `W ×_X Y`.

The identification of the two algebras is étale-locality of the integral closure,
`etaleAlgebraRestrictionIntegralClosureIso`, together with `halg` and `hbc`; the identification
of the two relative spectra is the base-change clause of Stacks 081V.
declarations.statement:
def normalizationInBaseChangeIso {Y YW : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (g : W ⟶ X) (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom) (f : Y ⟶ X) (p : YW ⟶ Y) (fW : YW ⟶ W)
    (_sq : IsPullback p fW f g)
    (hqc' : (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
      (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hqcW' : (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
      (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk fW))).IsQuasicoherent)
    (halg : C.algebraPullback g ≅ etaleAlgebraRestriction.{u, u} B S hS g hg)
    (hbc : (etaleAlgebraRestriction.{u, u} B S hS g hg).obj
        (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f)) ≅
      pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk fW)) :
    (C.affineBaseChange g).obj (normalizationIn B S hS E f hqc') ≅
      normalizationIn B S hS E fW hqcW'
declarations.comment:
part (1), étale base change, in its geometric form. `halg` is the identification
  of the algebra pullback of Stacks 081V along an étale morphism with étale restriction and `hbc`
  is Stacks 03LX for the direct image of the structure sheaf, read as algebras; neither is part
  (1), and the module docstring records why each is carried. The content of part (1) is
  `etaleAlgebraRestrictionIntegralClosureIso`, which is unconditional.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.normalizationInRepresentableIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABP, part (2).**  Let `X` and `Y` be representable, by `X₀` and `Y₀`, and let
`N₀` represent the normalization of the scheme `X₀` in the scheme `Y₀` of Stacks 035E.  Then the
normalization `X'` of `X` in `Y` is representable by `N₀`.
declarations.statement:
def normalizationInRepresentableIso {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hqc' : (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
      (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))).IsQuasicoherent)
    {X₀ Y₀ N₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS} (_eX : X.1 ≅ yoneda.obj X₀) (_eY : Y.1 ≅ yoneda.obj Y₀)
    (f₀ : Y₀ ⟶ X₀) (_hf₀ : yoneda.map f₀ = _eY.inv ≫ f.hom ≫ _eX.hom)
    [QuasiCompact ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀)]
    [QuasiSeparated ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀)]
    (_hN : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj N₀ ≅
      ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀).normalization)
    (Z : AffineOver B S hS X) (eZ : Z.obj.left.1 ≅ yoneda.obj N₀)
    (hcmp : pushforwardAlgebra B S hS Z.obj ≅
      AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))) :
    (normalizationIn B S hS E f hqc').obj.left.1 ≅ yoneda.obj N₀
declarations.comment:
part (2), comparison with the normalization of schemes. `Z` is the scheme
  normalization `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalization` of Stacks 035E, read inside the site
  as an algebraic space affine over `X`, and `hcmp` identifies its direct image of the structure
  sheaf with the integral closure of `𝒪_X` in `f_* 𝒪_Y`. That identification is the source's
  computation of `ν⁻¹(U)`. It is *not* Descent, Proposition 03DX(2): that proposition for the
  small étale site of an algebraic space is available here, unconditionally, as
  `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff_isCartesianOnAffineCharts`, and it compares
  the sections over two affine charts rather than computing the sections of the integral closure.
  The module docstring lists what `hcmp` still needs.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_normalizationIn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABP, part (2), representability.**  In the representable case the normalization
`X'` of `X` in `Y` is representable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_normalizationIn {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hqc' : (AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf
      (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))).IsQuasicoherent)
    {X₀ Y₀ N₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS} (eX : X.1 ≅ yoneda.obj X₀) (eY : Y.1 ≅ yoneda.obj Y₀)
    (f₀ : Y₀ ⟶ X₀) (hf₀ : yoneda.map f₀ = eY.inv ≫ f.hom ≫ eX.hom)
    [QuasiCompact ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀)]
    [QuasiSeparated ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀)]
    (hN : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj N₀ ≅
      ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀).normalization)
    (Z : AffineOver B S hS X) (eZ : Z.obj.left.1 ≅ yoneda.obj N₀)
    (hcmp : pushforwardAlgebra B S hS Z.obj ≅
      AlgebraSheaf.integralClosureSheaf (pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (Over.mk f))) :
    (normalizationIn B S hS E f hqc').obj.left.1.IsRepresentable
declarations.comment:
part (2), representability of the normalization. The hypotheses are those of
  `normalizationInRepresentableIso`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRelativeNormalization_normalizationInQcqs_etaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABP, part (1).**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S`, with normalization `Y ⟶ X' ⟶ X` (Definition 0822), and let
`g : W ⟶ X` be étale.  Let `P = W ×_X X'` and `Y' = W ×_X Y`, with `f'_P : Y' ⟶ P` the base
change of `f' : Y ⟶ X'`.  Then `Y' ⟶ P ⟶ W` is the normalization of `W` in `Y'`: it has the
universal property of Stacks 0823, and it is joined to the normalization of `W` in `Y'` of
Definition 0822 by a unique isomorphism compatible with both factorizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativeNormalization_normalizationInQcqs_etaleBaseChange
    {W P Y' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (g : W ⟶ X) (hg : IsEtale B S hS g.hom)
    (i : P ⟶ normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs) (νP : P ⟶ W)
    (hP : IsPullback i νP (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs) g)
    (j : Y' ⟶ Y) (fW : Y' ⟶ W) (hY : IsPullback j fW f g) (f'P : Y' ⟶ P)
    (h₁ : f'P ≫ i = j ≫ toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs) (h₂ : f'P ≫ νP = fW) :
    IsRelativeNormalization B S hS fW.hom νP.hom f'P.hom ∧
      ∃ (hWqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS fW.hom) (hWqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS fW.hom),
        ∃! e : (normalizationInQcqs B S hS fW hWqc hWqs).1 ≅ P.1,
          (toNormalizationInQcqs fW hWqc hWqs).hom ≫ e.hom = f'P.hom ∧
            e.hom ≫ νP.hom = (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS fW hWqc hWqs).hom
declarations.comment: part (1): for W ⟶ X étale, W ×_X X' is the normalization of W in W ×_X Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentable_normalizationInQcqs_and_iso_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABP, part (2).**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X` and `Y` representable, by objects `X₀` and `Y₀` of the
site, and let `f₀ : Y₀ ⟶ X₀` be the induced morphism.  Then the normalization `X'` of `X` in `Y`
(Definition 0822) is representable, and canonically isomorphic to the normalization of the scheme
`X₀` in the scheme `Y₀` (Morphisms, Section 035E): there is an object `N₀` of the site whose
underlying scheme is that normalization, compatibly with both of its legs, and a unique
isomorphism `X' ≅ N₀` compatible with both factorizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_normalizationInQcqs_and_iso_normalization {X₀ Y₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (eX : X.1 ≅ yoneda.obj X₀) (eY : Y.1 ≅ yoneda.obj Y₀) (f₀ : Y₀ ⟶ X₀)
    (hf₀ : yoneda.map f₀ = eY.inv ≫ f.hom ≫ eX.hom) :
    (normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs).1.IsRepresentable ∧
      ∃ (_ : QuasiCompact ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀))
        (_ : QuasiSeparated ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀))
        (N₀ : BigFppfOver B S hS) (t : Y₀ ⟶ N₀) (ν₀ : N₀ ⟶ X₀)
        (e : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj N₀ ≅
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀).normalization),
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map t ≫ e.hom =
            ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀).toNormalization ∧
          e.hom ≫ ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f₀).fromNormalization =
            (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map ν₀ ∧
          ∃! φ : (normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs).1 ≅ yoneda.obj N₀,
            (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom ≫ φ.hom = eY.hom ≫ yoneda.map t ∧
              φ.hom ≫ yoneda.map ν₀ = (normalizationInQcqsHom B S hS f hfqc hfqs).hom ≫ eX.hom
declarations.comment:
part (2): for X and Y representable, X' is representable and canonically
  isomorphic to the normalization of the scheme X in the scheme Y of 035E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationInData.isOpenSubspace_quasiFiniteImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABR, the open subspace.** For a representable morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
which is of finite type and separated, the image in the normalization of `Y` in `X` of the
quasi-finite locus of `f` is an open subspace of that normalization.

Over a surjective étale scheme chart `W ⟶ Y` the quasi-finite locus base changes to the
quasi-finite locus of the induced morphism of schemes (part (2) of Tag 0ABM), and Zariski's main
theorem for schemes — Tag 03GW, Mathlib's
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.exists_isIso_morphismRestrict_toNormalization` — says that locus
maps by an open immersion into the relative normalization of the chart, which by the chart
description of the normalization datum is the base change of `ν`. So the restriction of `f'` to
the quasi-finite locus is an open immersion after base change along one surjective étale chart
of `Y'`, hence an open immersion, by Tag 03M4 for open immersions; its image is therefore an
open subspace.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpenSubspace_quasiFiniteImage (N : NormalizationInData B S hS f)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS N.quasiFiniteImage
declarations.comment: the open subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationInData.isIso_fromPreimage_quasiFiniteImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABR, part (1).** The inverse image of the open subspace under `f'` maps
isomorphically onto it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_fromPreimage_quasiFiniteImage (N : NormalizationInData B S hS f)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsIso (N.quasiFiniteImage.fromPreimage N.toNorm)
declarations.comment: part (1): the inverse image of the open subspace maps isomorphically onto it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationInData.preimage_quasiFiniteImage_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABR, part (2).** The inverse image of the open subspace under `f'` is the
quasi-finite locus of `f`, as a subspace of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preimage_quasiFiniteImage_eq (N : NormalizationInData B S hS f)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    N.quasiFiniteImage.preimage N.toNorm = quasiFiniteLocusSubspace B S hS f
declarations.comment: part (2): the inverse image is the quasi-finite locus, as a subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationInData.range_pointsMap_preimage_quasiFiniteImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABR, part (2), on points.** The point set of the inverse image of the open subspace
under `f'` is the set of points of `X` at which `f` is quasi-finite. This is the form in which
the source states part (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pointsMap_preimage_quasiFiniteImage (N : NormalizationInData B S hS f)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (N.quasiFiniteImage.preimage N.toNorm).toFunctor
        (N.quasiFiniteImage.preimage N.toNorm).ι) =
      {x : points B S hS X | IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: part (2): the inverse image is the set of points of quasi-finiteness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isIso_fromPreimage_and_range_pointsMap_preimage_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABR.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
representable, of finite type and separated, and let `X ⟶ Y' ⟶ Y` be the normalization of `Y`
in `X`. Then there is an open subspace `U' ⊆ Y'` such that `(f')⁻¹(U') ⟶ U'` is an isomorphism
and `(f')⁻¹(U') ⊆ X` is the set of points at which `f` is quasi-finite.

The open subspace is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationInData.quasiFiniteImage`, the image of
the quasi-finite locus.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isIso_fromPreimage_and_range_pointsMap_preimage_eq
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {f : X ⟶ Y} (N : NormalizationInData B S hS f)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hrep : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f)
    (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    ∃ U' : Subfunctor N.space, IsOpenSubspace B S hS U' ∧
      IsIso (U'.fromPreimage N.toNorm) ∧
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (U'.preimage N.toNorm).toFunctor
          (U'.preimage N.toNorm).ι) =
        {x : points B S hS X | IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x}
declarations.comment: the existence statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.zariskiMainTheorem
declarations.doc:
**Zariski's main theorem for algebraic spaces.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-finite
separated morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`. Then `f` is quasi-affine, and the
normalization of `Y` in `X` exists: there is a factorization `X --f'--> Y' --ν--> Y` of `f`
whose base change along every étale scheme chart of `Y` is the relative normalization of that
chart, in which `f'` is a quasi-compact open immersion and `ν` is integral.

Neither side is required to be representable and no bound on sizes is assumed: the datum is
glued along a surjective étale chart of the target in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationGluing.nonempty_normalizationInData`, and the four
assertions about it are the theorems of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.ZariskiMainTheoremQuasiFinite`.
declarations.statement:
theorem zariskiMainTheorem (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hqf : IsQuasiFinite B S hS f) (hsep : IsSeparated B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiAffineHom B S hS f ∧
      ∃ N : NormalizationInData B S hS f,
        N.toNorm ≫ N.fromNorm = f ∧
        IsOpenImmersion B S hS N.toNorm ∧
        IsQuasiCompact B S hS N.toNorm ∧
        IsIntegralHom B S hS N.fromNorm

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecentSpace_relocalizeRestrict
declarations.doc:
Decency of an algebraic space over an affine scheme `S` is preserved by restriction along a
morphism `g : S' ⟶ S` of affine schemes of the site: every point of the restricted space is
presented by a quasi-compact monomorphism from the spectrum of a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecentSpace_relocalizeRestrict (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S S' : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (hS' : B.Contains S')
    [IsAffine S] [IsAffine S']
    (g : B.obj hS' ⟶ B.obj hS)
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    IsDecentSpace B S' hS' ((CategoryTheory.OverShriek.relocalizeRestrict g).obj X)
declarations.comment: decency under change of affine base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative_of_relativelyRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABT, the decent case in the form of condition (4) of Stacks 03JU.** Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a representable morphism of presheaves on the big fppf site over `S`. If every
point of `Y` is the class of a field-valued point presenting it by a monomorphism, then so is
every point of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative_of_relativelyRepresentable (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hY : ∀ y : points B S hS Y, HasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative B S hS Y y)
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    HasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative B S hS X x
declarations.comment: decent, as condition (4) of Stacks 03JU at every point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint_of_relativelyRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABT, the decent case as property `(β)` of Stacks 03JX.** The source of a
representable morphism into a presheaf all of whose points have a monomorphic field-valued
representative has property `(β)`: every point of it has a finite relation fibre in some
étale chart.

This is the reading of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative_of_relativelyRepresentable`
through the equivalences of Stacks 03JU, which need the source to be an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint_of_relativelyRepresentable
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hY : ∀ y : points B S hS Y, HasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative B S hS Y y) :
    HasFiniteRelationFibersAtEveryPoint B S hS X
declarations.comment: decent, as property (β) of Stacks 03JX

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecentSpace_of_relativelyRepresentable
registrations.comment: decent

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonableSpace_of_relativelyRepresentable
registrations.comment: reasonable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecentSpace_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABU, the decent case.** An algebraic space over `S` étale over a decent
algebraic space over `S` is decent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecentSpace_of_isEtale (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y) :
    IsDecentSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: decent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isReasonableSpace_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABU, the reasonable case.** An algebraic space over `S` étale over a reasonable
algebraic space over `S` is reasonable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReasonableSpace_of_isEtale (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f)
    (hreas : IsReasonableSpace B S hS Y) :
    IsReasonableSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: reasonable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_genericPoints_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABV.** For a point `x` of a decent algebraic space `X` over `S` the following
are equivalent: `x` is a generic point of an irreducible component of `|X|`; for every étale
morphism of algebraic spaces onto `X`, every point above `x` is a generic point of an
irreducible component of the source; for some étale morphism onto `X` some point above `x`
is; and the local ring of `X` at `x` has dimension zero, which is to say that `x` is a point
of codimension `0` on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_genericPoints_tfae (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (x : points B S hS X) :
    List.TFAE
      [ x ∈ genericPoints (points B S hS X),
        ∀ (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y → ∀ f : Y ⟶ X,
          IsEtale B S hS f → ∀ y : points B S hS Y, pointsMap B S hS Y f y = x →
            y ∈ genericPoints (points B S hS Y),
        ∃ (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (_ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : Y ⟶ X)
          (y : points B S hS Y), IsEtale B S hS f ∧ pointsMap B S hS Y f y = x ∧
            y ∈ genericPoints (points B S hS Y),
        localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 ]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_le_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
A locally quasi-finite morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` does not increase the dimension
of the local ring: for a point `x` of the source, the dimension of the local ring there is at
most the dimension of the local ring of the target at the image of `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingDimension_le_of_isLocallyQuasiFinite
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS f)
    (x : points B S hS X) :
    localRingDimension B S hS x ≤
      localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS X f x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDecent_of_isDecentSpace_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABX, the decent case.** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` whose source is
a decent algebraic space is a decent morphism.

A morphism `g : h_T ⟶ Y` out of a representable presheaf into an algebraic space is
representable, because the diagonal of `Y` is; hence so is the projection
`T ×_Y X ⟶ X` of its base change, and decency passes from the target of a representable
morphism to its source by Stacks 0ABT.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDecent_of_isDecentSpace_source (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) :
    IsDecent B S hS f
declarations.comment: decent: a morphism whose source is decent is decent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative_pullback_of_source
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ABX, the decent case in the form of condition (4) of Stacks 03JU.** Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of presheaves on the big fppf site over `S` with `Y` an algebraic
space. If every point of `X` is the class of a field-valued point presenting it by a
monomorphism, then so is every point of every base change of `f` along a morphism from a
representable presheaf into `Y`: that base change is representable over `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasMonomorphicFieldRepresentative_pullback_of_source
