declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDiscreteFieldFibrePoints_iff_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACK, conditions (5) and (6).** For a morphism locally of finite type and a
field-valued point of its target with nonempty field fibre whose point space is `T₀`, the point
space `|X_k|` is discrete exactly when it has Krull dimension zero.

The nonemptiness hypothesis is carried by the direction from condition (5) alone, and it cannot
be dropped there: `topologicalKrullDim` lands in `WithBot ℕ∞`, so the empty fibre is discrete
while having dimension `⊥` rather than `0`. The `T₀` hypothesis is carried by the other
direction, is not in the source, and cannot be dropped either; it holds in particular when `f`

declarations.statement:
theorem isDiscreteFieldFibrePoints_iff_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints

    IsDiscreteFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p ↔ IsZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZeroDimensionalFieldFibre_iff_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints

locally of finite type and a field-valued point of its target, the point space `|X_k|` of the
field fibre has Krull dimension zero exactly when `X_k` has dimension zero as an algebraic
space.

Neither direction needs a nonemptiness hypothesis: each of the two conditions is an equation
`… = 0` in `WithBot ℕ∞` for a dimension whose value on the empty fibre is `⊥`, so each already
forces the fibre to have a point. The `T₀` hypothesis is carried by the direction out of
condition (6) alone, is not in the source, and cannot be dropped; it holds in particular when
`f` is a decent morphism, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.t0Space_points_fieldFibre_of_isDecent`.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDiscreteSetFibre_of_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACK, condition (3) implies condition (2), for a decent target and a Kolmogorov
`F`.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces locally of finite type, let `p` be a
field-valued point of a decent `Y`, and suppose the set-theoretic fibre `F = f^{-1}({y})` is
`T₀` and has Krull dimension zero. Then `F` is discrete.

Decency of `Y` supplies a field-valued point `q` representing the same point of `|Y|` whose
presenting morphism is a quasi-compact monomorphism, which is condition (4) of Stacks 03JV. For
that representative Lemma 0AC8 identifies `|X_q|` with `F` as topological spaces
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.homeomorphSetFibre`), and `F` is the same set for `q` as for `p` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.setFibre_eq_of_class_eq`. The Krull dimension of a topological space is
a homeomorphism invariant, so condition (3) for `p` is condition (6) for `q`, and both the `T₀`
hypothesis and the resulting discreteness travel across that same homeomorphism.

**The `T₀` hypothesis on `F` is not in the source and cannot be dropped**, so the source's
claim that conditions (2) and (3) are equivalent for a decent target is false; see the
implementation notes of this file. It is weaker than decency of `f`, which gives it through the
homeomorphism above, and it holds in particular when `X` is a decent algebraic space — a
hypothesis the source itself makes, in its last clause — by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.t0Space_setFibre_of_isDecentSpace_source`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDiscreteSetFibre_of_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)
    (ht0 : T0Space (setFibre B S hS f p)) (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (h : IsZeroDimensionalSetFibre B S hS f p) :
    IsDiscreteSetFibre B S hS f p
declarations.comment: decent target: (3) implies (2), corrected: F must be Kolmogorov

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDiscreteFieldFibrePoints_of_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACK, condition (3) implies condition (5), for a decent target and a Kolmogorov
`F`.** If the set-theoretic fibre `F` is `T₀` and has Krull dimension zero, `Y` is decent and
`f` is locally of finite type, then the point space `|X_k|` of the field fibre is discrete.

Condition (3) gives condition (2), and conditions (2) and (5) are equivalent for a decent
target by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.discreteTopology_setFibre_iff_discreteTopology_points_fieldFibre`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDiscreteFieldFibrePoints_of_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)

    (h : IsZeroDimensionalSetFibre B S hS f p) :
    IsDiscreteFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p
declarations.comment: decent target: (3) implies (5), corrected: F must be Kolmogorov

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDiscreteSetFibre_iff_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACK, conditions (2) and (3) for a decent target and a Kolmogorov `F`.** For a
morphism locally of finite type into a decent algebraic space, and a field-valued point of the
target whose set-theoretic fibre `F` is nonempty and `T₀`, the fibre `F` is discrete exactly
when it has Krull dimension zero.

The nonemptiness hypothesis is carried by the direction from condition (2) alone, where it
cannot be dropped: the empty fibre is discrete while having Krull dimension `⊥`. The `T₀`
hypothesis is carried by the other direction, is not in the source, and cannot be dropped
either.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDiscreteSetFibre_iff_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)
    (ht0 : T0Space (setFibre B S hS f p)) (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hne : (setFibre B S hS f p).Nonempty) :
    IsDiscreteSetFibre B S hS f p ↔ IsZeroDimensionalSetFibre B S hS f p
declarations.comment: decent target: conditions (2) and (3), corrected: F must be Kolmogorov

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_fibre_conditions_of_isDecentSpace_target
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACK, conditions (2), (5), (7) and (8) for a decent target.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of algebraic spaces locally of finite type, let `Y` be a decent algebraic space and let
`p` be a field-valued point of `Y` with nonempty set-theoretic fibre `F`. Then the following are
equivalent: `F` is discrete; `|X_k|` is discrete; `dim(X_k) = 0`; and `f` is quasi-finite at
every point of `|X|` above the point `p` represents.

These are the four conditions of the source's decent-target clause whose equivalence holds at
the hypotheses the source states, with no decency hypothesis on `f`. The two it omits are the
Krull-dimension conditions (3) and (6), whose arrows to the others are false in that
generality.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_fibre_conditions_of_isDecentSpace_target
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)
    (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y) (hne : (setFibre B S hS f p).Nonempty) :
    [IsDiscreteSetFibre B S hS f p, IsDiscreteFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p,
      IsZeroDimensionalFieldFibre B S hS f p (isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre hX hY f p),
      IsQuasiFiniteAboveFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p].TFAE
declarations.comment: decent target: conditions (2), (5), (7) and (8)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_fibre_conditions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACK, conditions (2), (3), (5), (6), (7) and (8) for a decent target and
Kolmogorov fibres.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces locally of finite type,
let `Y` be a decent algebraic space and let `p` be a field-valued point of `Y` whose
set-theoretic fibre `F` is nonempty, with `F` and `|X_k|` both `T₀`. Then the following are
equivalent: `F` is discrete; `dim(F) = 0`; `|X_k|` is discrete; `dim(|X_k|) = 0`;
`dim(X_k) = 0`; and `f` is quasi-finite at every point of `|X|` above the point `p` represents.

This is the source's clause "if `Y` is decent, then conditions (2) and (3) are equivalent to
each other and to conditions (5), (6), (7) and (8)", with the two Kolmogorov hypotheses that
the clause needs and does not state, and with the nonemptiness that the `= 0` form of the two
dimension conditions needs; see the implementation notes of this file. The `T₀` hypothesis on
`F` is used only by the arrow out of condition (3) and the one on `|X_k|` only by the arrow out
of condition (6), which are exactly the two arrows the counterexample kills. Both are weaker
than decency of `f`, which gives them by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.t0Space_points_fieldFibre_of_isDecent` and the homeomorphism of
Lemma 0AC8.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_fibre_conditions
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)
    (ht0F : T0Space (setFibre B S hS f p))
    (ht0k : T0Space (points B S hS (fieldFibre B S hS f p)))
    (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y) (hne : (setFibre B S hS f p).Nonempty) :
    [IsDiscreteSetFibre B S hS f p, IsZeroDimensionalSetFibre B S hS f p,
      IsDiscreteFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p, IsZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p,
      IsZeroDimensionalFieldFibre B S hS f p (isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre hX hY f p),
      IsQuasiFiniteAboveFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p].TFAE
declarations.comment: decent target: conditions (2), (3), (5), (6), (7) and (8), Kolmogorov fibres

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fibre_conditions_of_finite_setFibre_of_isDecent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACK, condition (1) implies all the other conditions, for decent spaces.** Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces locally of finite type with `X` and `Y` both
decent, and let `p` be a field-valued point of `Y` whose set-theoretic fibre `F` is finite and
nonempty. Then `|X_k|` is finite, `F` is discrete, `dim(F) = 0`, `|X_k|` is discrete,
`dim(|X_k|) = 0`, `dim(X_k) = 0`, and `f` is quasi-finite at every point of `|X|` above the
point `p` represents — conditions (4), (2), (3), (5), (6), (7) and (8) of the tag.

Condition (4) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_univ_points_fieldFibre_of_finite_setFibre_of_isDecent`. A
morphism out of a decent algebraic space is a decent morphism by the decent case of Stacks
0ABX, so condition (4) gives condition (5) by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.discreteTopology_points_fieldFibre_of_finite_of_isDecent`, and the
remaining five conditions are condition (5) read through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_fibre_conditions`.

The nonemptiness hypothesis is the one the two Krull-dimension conditions and condition (7)
need: the empty fibre is finite and discrete while every `… = 0` among the conditions reads
`⊥ = 0` on it. It cannot be dropped, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre_of_finite_setFibre`, which
refutes this clause in the form the source states it, with both `X` and `Y` decent and no
hypothesis on the fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem fibre_conditions_of_finite_setFibre_of_isDecent
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)
    (hXdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS X) (hYdec : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hne : (setFibre B S hS f p).Nonempty) (hfinite : (setFibre B S hS f p).Finite) :
    (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS (fieldFibre B S hS f p))).Finite ∧
      IsDiscreteSetFibre B S hS f p ∧ IsZeroDimensionalSetFibre B S hS f p ∧
      IsDiscreteFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p ∧
      IsZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p ∧
      IsZeroDimensionalFieldFibre B S hS f p (isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre hX hY f p) ∧
      IsQuasiFiniteAboveFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p
declarations.comment: decent spaces: condition (1) implies the other seven conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre_of_isDiscreteSetFibre
declarations.doc:
**The source's implication from condition (2) to condition (3) is false.** There is a
decent algebraic space locally of finite type over a decent algebraic space, and a field-valued
point of the target, whose set-theoretic fibre is empty: that fibre is discrete and has Krull
dimension `-∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre_of_isDiscreteSetFibre :
    ¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
        (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X →

        IsDiscreteSetFibre B S hS f p → IsZeroDimensionalSetFibre B S hS f p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints_of_isDiscreteFieldFibrePoints
declarations.doc:
**The source's implication from condition (5) to condition (6) is false.** The field fibre
over a field-valued point outside the image has no points, so its point set is discrete and has
Krull dimension `-∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints_of_isDiscreteFieldFibrePoints :
    ¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
        (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X →
        IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y → IsDecentSpace B S hS X → IsDecentSpace B S hS Y →
        ∀ f : X ⟶ Y, IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f → ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y,
        IsDiscreteFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p →
          IsZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints B S hS f p
declarations.comment: (5) => (6) is false: an empty field fibre is discrete of dimension -infinity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibre_of_isQuasiFiniteAboveFieldValuedPoint
declarations.doc:
**The source's implication from condition (8) to condition (7) is false.** A morphism is
quasi-finite above every point outside its image, while the field fibre there has no points and
so has dimension `-∞` in the sense of Stacks 04N6.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibre_of_isQuasiFiniteAboveFieldValuedPoint :
    ¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
        (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
        (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y), IsDecentSpace B S hS X → IsDecentSpace B S hS Y →
        ∀ f : X ⟶ Y, IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f → ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y,
        IsQuasiFiniteAboveFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p →
          IsZeroDimensionalFieldFibre B S hS f p (isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre hX hY f p)
declarations.comment: (8) => (7) is false: an empty field fibre has dimension -infinity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre_of_finite_setFibre
declarations.doc:

decent, condition (1) implies all the other conditions; the empty fibre is finite while failing

This is the clause `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fibre_conditions_of_finite_setFibre_of_isDecent`

declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre_of_finite_setFibre :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isDiscreteFieldFibrePoints_of_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibre_of_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isQuasiFiniteAboveFieldValuedPoint_of_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints
declarations.doc:

declarations.statement:

          IsQuasiFiniteAboveFieldValuedPoint B S hS f p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isDiscreteFieldFibrePoints_iff_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints
declarations.doc:
**The source's equivalence of conditions (5) and (6) is false.** This is the negation of
that equivalence, in the source's own vocabulary.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isDiscreteFieldFibrePoints_iff_isZeroDimensionalFieldFibrePoints :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isDiscreteSetFibre_of_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre
declarations.doc:

false.** There is a morphism of algebraic spaces locally of finite type into a decent algebraic
space, and a field-valued point of the target, whose set-theoretic fibre has Krull dimension

declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isDiscreteSetFibre_of_isZeroDimensionalSetFibre :

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACV.** A morphism of decent algebraic spaces with finitely many irreducible
components is birational when it bijects the generic points of the irreducible components and
induces isomorphisms on their schematic-locus local rings.
declarations.statement:
def IsBirational
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hdecX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isDominant_of_isBirational
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACW.** A birational morphism of decent algebraic spaces over `S` with finitely
many irreducible components is dominant: it maps the generic points of the irreducible
components of the source onto those of the target, and those are dense in a quasi-sober
space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDominant_of_isBirational (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hdecX : IsDecentSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecY : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfiniteX : (letI := pointTopology B S hS X
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS X)).Finite))
    (hfiniteY : (letI := pointTopology B S hS Y
      (irreducibleComponents (points B S hS Y)).Finite))
    {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (hf : IsBirational B S hS hX hY hdecX hdecY hfiniteX hfiniteY f) :
    IsDominant B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_fieldFiber_iff_quasiFiniteAt_fiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACZ, conditions (1) and (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-separated morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` of finite type and let `p` be a field-valued representative of a
point `y` of `|Y|`. The field fibre `X_k` has finitely many points exactly when `f` is
quasi-finite at every point of `|X|` above `y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_fieldFiber_iff_quasiFiniteAt_fiber (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (y : points B S hS Y)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y) (hp : p.class B S hS Y = y) :
    Set.Finite (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS
        (pullback f (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value)))) ↔
      ∀ x : points B S hS X, pointsMap B S hS X f x = y →
        IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_fieldFiber_iff_finite_setFiber_of_decent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACZ, condition (4) for a decent target.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-separated
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` of finite type with `Y` a decent algebraic space, and
let `p` be a field-valued representative of a point `y` of `|Y|`. The field fibre `X_k` has
finitely many points exactly when the set-theoretic fibre `f^{-1}({y}) ⊂ |X|` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_fieldFiber_iff_finite_setFiber_of_decent (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hdecent : IsDecentSpace B S hS Y)
    (y : points B S hS Y) (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)
    (hp : p.class B S hS Y = y) :
    Set.Finite (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS
        (pullback f (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value)))) ↔
      Set.Finite {x : points B S hS X | pointsMap B S hS X f x = y}
declarations.comment: condition (4) for a decent target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isFinite_pullback_snd_of_finite_fieldFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACZ, conditions (1) and (2) imply condition (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` of finite type, let `y` be a point of
`|Y|` whose local ring has dimension zero and let `p` be a field-valued representative of `y`
with field of definition `k`. If the field fibre `X_k = X ×_Y Spec(k)` has finitely many
points then there is an open subspace `V ⊂ Y` with `y ∈ |V|` whose base change
`V ×_Y X ⟶ V` is finite.

An affine étale chart `V ⟶ Y` at `y` may be chosen so that `y` comes from a generic point `v`
of `V` (Stacks 0BAQ). Over an affine étale atlas `U` of `V ×_Y X` the two morphisms
`U ⟶ V` and `U ×_{V ×_Y X} U ⟶ V` are quasi-finite above `v` (Stacks 0BBB), so both become
finite after shrinking `V` to an affine open neighbourhood of `v` (Stacks 02NW). The relation
being finite over the atlas makes the atlas finite over the shrunk chart, and the chart being
affine with a finite surjective atlas makes `V ×_Y X` an affine scheme (Stacks 01ZT), over
which finiteness is properness together with affineness. Descending along the étale chart
produces the open subspace of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isFinite_pullback_snd_of_finite_fieldFiber
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (y : points B S hS Y)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)
    (hp : p.class B S hS Y = y)
    (hy : localRingDimension B S hS y = 0) :
    Set.Finite (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS
      (pullback f (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value)))) →
    ∃ V : Subfunctor Y,
        IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
        y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
        IsFinite B S hS (pullback.snd f V.ι)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2) imply condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiFiniteAt_of_isFinite_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACZ, condition (3) implies condition (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type and let `V ⊂ Y` be an open subspace
containing a point `y` of `|Y|` in its point set. If the base change `V ×_Y X ⟶ V` is finite
then `f` is quasi-finite at every point of `|X|` above `y`.

A finite morphism is quasi-finite (Stacks 04NY), so `V ×_Y X ⟶ V` is quasi-finite at every
point of its source; a point of `|X|` above `y` lifts to `|V ×_Y X|` (Stacks 03H4), and
quasi-finiteness at a point passes to and from a base change (Stacks 0ABM).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiFiniteAt_of_isFinite_pullback_snd
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (y : points B S hS Y)
    (V : Subfunctor Y)
    (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hyV : y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι))
    (hfin : IsFinite B S hS (pullback.snd f V.ι))
    (x : points B S hS X)
    (hxy : pointsMap B S hS X f x = y) :
    IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_fieldFiber_iff_exists_isOpenSubspace_isFinite_pullback_snd
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ACZ, conditions (1) and (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-separated morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` of finite type, let `y` be a point of `|Y|` whose local ring has
dimension zero and let `p` be a field-valued representative of `y`. The field fibre `X_k` has
finitely many points exactly when there is an open subspace `V ⊂ Y` with `y ∈ |V|` whose base
change `V ×_Y X ⟶ V` is finite.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_fieldFiber_iff_quasiFiniteAt_fiber` this closes
the equivalence of the source's conditions (1), (2) and (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_fieldFiber_iff_exists_isOpenSubspace_isFinite_pullback_snd
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hft : IsFiniteType B S hS f)
    (y : points B S hS Y)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y)
    (hp : p.class B S hS Y = y)
    (hy : localRingDimension B S hS y = 0) :
    Set.Finite (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS
        (pullback f (yonedaEquiv.symm p.value)))) ↔
      ∃ V : Subfunctor Y,
        IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
        y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
        IsFinite B S hS (pullback.snd f V.ι)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_setFibre_iff_finite_fieldFibre_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD0, the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type, let `Y`
be a quasi-separated algebraic space, let `y` be a point of `|Y|` of codimension zero and let
`p` be a field-valued representative of `y`, with field of definition `k`. Then the
set-theoretic fibre `f^{-1}({y}) ⊂ |X|` is finite exactly when the point set of the field
fibre `X_k = X ×_Y Spec(k)` is finite.

Quasi-separatedness of `Y` makes `Y` decent (Stacks 03JX) and quasi-separatedness of `f` then
makes `X` decent (Stacks 03M5 and Stacks 0ABY), so both implications are instances of the
comparison of conditions (1) and (4) of Stacks 0ACK for decent source and target: condition (4)
implies condition (1) because the comparison map `|X_k| → |X|` has image the set-theoretic
fibre, and the converse is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_univ_points_fieldFibre_of_finite_setFibre_of_isDecent` once the
fibre is nonempty, an empty fibre leaving `|X_k|` without points by the same surjectivity.

The codimension-zero hypothesis on `y` is the source's; this implication does not use it.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_setFibre_iff_finite_fieldFibre_of_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    (y : points B S hS Y) (_hy : localRingDimension B S hS y = 0)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y) (hp : p.class B S hS Y = y) :
    {x : points B S hS X | pointsMap B S hS X f x = y}.Finite ↔
      (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS (fieldFibre B S hS f p))).Finite
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_setFibre_of_isFinite_openRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD0, condition (3) implies condition (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`, let `y` be a point of `|Y|`, let `U ⊂ X` and `V ⊂ Y`
be open subspaces and let `g : U ⟶ V` be a morphism whose square with the two inclusions and
`f` commutes, so that `f` carries `U` into `V` and `g` restricts `f`. If `y` lies in `|V|`, if
the set-theoretic fibre `f^{-1}({y}) ⊂ |X|` is contained in `|U|` and if `g` is finite, then
`f^{-1}({y})` is finite.

A finite morphism of algebraic spaces is universally closed with discrete fibres (Stacks 0A4X),
so each of its set-theoretic fibres is finite. The inclusion `|V| → |Y|` is injective because
the inclusion of an open subspace is a monomorphism, so the point `v` of `|V|` above `y` is the
only one, and a point of `|U|` lands on `y` under `f` exactly when it lands on `v` under `g`.
The fibre `f^{-1}({y})` is therefore the image under `|U| → |X|` of a fibre of `g`.

No hypothesis on `f`, on `Y` or on `y` is needed: the quasi-separatedness, finite type and
codimension-zero hypotheses of the tag are used only for the other implications.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_setFibre_of_isFinite_openRestriction (f : X ⟶ Y) (y : points B S hS Y)
    (U : Subfunctor X) (V : Subfunctor Y) (g : U.toFunctor ⟶ V.toFunctor)
    (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U) (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hcomm : g ≫ V.ι = U.ι ≫ f)
    (hy : y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι))
    (hfib : {x : points B S hS X | pointsMap B S hS X f x = y} ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι))
    (hg : IsFinite B S hS g) :
    {x : points B S hS X | pointsMap B S hS X f x = y}.Finite
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_fieldFibre_of_isFinite_openRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD0, condition (3) implies condition (2).** In the situation of condition (3) of
the tag, with `f` in addition quasi-separated and locally of finite type and `Y` a
quasi-separated algebraic space, the point set of the field fibre `X_k` over a field-valued
representative `p` of `y` is finite.

The source omits the proof of this implication. It is obtained here by composing
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_setFibre_of_isFinite_openRestriction` with the equivalence of
conditions (1) and (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_fieldFibre_of_isFinite_openRestriction (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f) (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    (y : points B S hS Y) (hy0 : localRingDimension B S hS y = 0)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y) (hp : p.class B S hS Y = y)
    (U : Subfunctor X) (V : Subfunctor Y) (g : U.toFunctor ⟶ V.toFunctor)
    (hU : IsOpenSubspace B S hS U) (hV : IsOpenSubspace B S hS V)
    (hcomm : g ≫ V.ι = U.ι ≫ f)
    (hy : y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι))
    (hfib : {x : points B S hS X | pointsMap B S hS X f x = y} ⊆
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι))
    (hg : IsFinite B S hS g) :
    (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS (fieldFibre B S hS f p))).Finite
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isFinite_openRestriction_of_finite_setFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD0, conditions (1) and (2) imply condition (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
quasi-separated morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type, let `Y`
be a quasi-separated algebraic space and let `y` be a point of `|Y|` whose local ring has
dimension zero. If the set-theoretic fibre `f^{-1}({y}) ⊂ |X|` is finite then there are open
subspaces `U ⊂ X` and `V ⊂ Y` and a morphism `g : U ⟶ V` restricting `f`, with `y ∈ |V|`,
with `f^{-1}({y}) ⊂ |U|`, and with `g` finite.

A finite set of points of an algebraic space is covered by a quasi-compact open subspace, so
`X` may be shrunk to a quasi-compact open `U₀` containing the fibre. Quasi-separatedness of
`Y` makes the restriction `U₀ ⟶ Y` quasi-compact (Stacks 073B) and hence of finite type, and
its fibre over `y` is still finite, so the field fibre is finite as well. Condition (3) of
Stacks 0ACZ then supplies an open `V ⊂ Y` containing `y` over which `U₀` becomes finite, and
the base change `U₀ ×_Y V` is an open subspace of `X` because `U₀` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isFinite_openRestriction_of_finite_setFibre
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y)
    (y : points B S hS Y)
    (hy : localRingDimension B S hS y = 0) :
    Set.Finite {x : points B S hS X |
      pointsMap B S hS X f x = y} →
      ∃ (U : Subfunctor X) (V : Subfunctor Y)
        (g : U.toFunctor ⟶ V.toFunctor),
        IsOpenSubspace B S hS U ∧
        IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
        g ≫ V.ι = U.ι ≫ f ∧
        y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
        {x : points B S hS X |
          pointsMap B S hS X f x = y} ⊆
          Set.range (pointsMap B S hS U.toFunctor U.ι) ∧
        IsFinite B S hS g
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2) imply condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiFiniteAt_of_localRingDimension_le_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AD1.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
which is locally of finite type, with `Y` locally Noetherian, and let `y` be a point of `|Y|`
whose local ring has dimension at most one. Write `X⁰` for the points of `|X|` whose local
ring has dimension zero. If one of the following holds — the transcendence degree of `x` over
`f(x)` is zero for every `x` of `X⁰`; the same for every `x` of `X⁰` whose image specializes
to `y`; `f` is quasi-finite at every point of `X⁰`; `f` is quasi-finite at a dense set of
points of `|X|` — then `f` is quasi-finite at every point of `|X|` above `y`.

The proof reduces to the corresponding statement for morphisms of schemes, Stacks 0AB6, which
is `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiFiniteAt_of_target_stalk_dimension_le_one`, applied in an étale
chart of the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiFiniteAt_of_localRingDimension_le_one
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (y : points B S hS Y) (hy : localRingDimension B S hS y ≤ 1)
    (hgeneric :
      (∀ x : points B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x 0) ∨
      (∀ x : points B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        pointsMap B S hS X f x ⤳ y → HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x 0) ∨
      (∀ x : points B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x) ∨
      Dense {x : points B S hS X | IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x}) :
    ∀ x : points B S hS X, pointsMap B S hS X f x = y → IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isFinite_pullback_snd_of_localRingDimension_le_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AD2.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` with `Y` locally Noetherian, and let `y` be a point of `|Y|` whose local ring has dimension
at most one. If one of the four generic quasi-finiteness conditions of Stacks 0AD1 holds, then
`y` has an open neighbourhood `V ⊆ Y` over which the base change `f^{-1}(V) ⟶ V` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isFinite_pullback_snd_of_localRingDimension_le_one
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hp : IsProper B S hS f)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (y : points B S hS Y) (hy : localRingDimension B S hS y ≤ 1)
    (hgeneric :
      (∀ x : points B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x 0) ∨
      (∀ x : points B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        pointsMap B S hS X f x ⤳ y → HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x 0) ∨
      (∀ x : points B S hS X, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x) ∨
      Dense {x : points B S hS X | IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x}) :
    ∃ V : Subfunctor Y, IsOpenSubspace B S hS V ∧
      y ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS V.toFunctor V.ι) ∧
      IsFinite B S hS (pullback.snd f V.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsIntegralSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD4.** An algebraic space over `S` is *integral* when it is reduced, decent,
and its space of points is irreducible.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsIntegralSpace : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_residueFieldHom_genericPoint_of_hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_zero
declarations.doc:
**Spaces over Fields, Lemma 0AD5, (1) implies (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a dominant
morphism of integral algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite type. If the
transcendence degree of the generic point of `X` over the generic point of `Y` is zero, then
the induced extension of residue fields at the generic point is finite.

Both residue fields are read on a pair of representable open charts through the generic point,
which exist by Stacks 086U and Stacks 03IE.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_residueFieldHom_genericPoint_of_hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_zero
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) (hYInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hdom : IsDominant B S hS f)
    (htr : HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f (genericPoint B S hS hX hXInt) 0) :
    letI := (residueFieldHom B S hS X Y hY hXInt.2.1 hYInt.2.1 f
      (genericPoint B S hS hX hXInt)).toAlgebra
    Module.Finite
      (residueField B S hS Y hYInt.2.1
        (pointsMap B S hS X f (genericPoint B S hS hX hXInt)))
      (residueField B S hS X hXInt.2.1 (genericPoint B S hS hX hXInt))
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies condition (2): finiteness of the residue field extension at the generic point, from vanishing of the relative transcendence degree there

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiFiniteAt_iff_forall_eq_of_pointsMap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD5, conditions (4) and (5).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a dominant morphism locally of
finite type of algebraic spaces over `S` with `Y` integral, and let `x` and `y` be generic
points of `|X|` and `|Y|`. Then `f` is quasi-finite at `x` exactly when `x` is the only point
of `|X|` mapping to `y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiFiniteAt_iff_forall_eq_of_pointsMap_eq
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hdom : IsDominant B S hS f)
    {x : points B S hS X} (hx : IsGenericPoint x (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS X)))
    {y : points B S hS Y} (hy : IsGenericPoint y (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS Y))) :
    IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x ↔
      ∀ x' : points B S hS X, pointsMap B S hS X f x' = y → x' = x
declarations.comment: conditions (4) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_zero_of_isQuasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD5, condition (4) implies condition (1).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over
`S` which is quasi-finite at a point of its source has transcendence degree zero there: on an
open subspace containing the point the morphism is locally quasi-finite, so contributes a
finite residue field extension in every étale chart, and an open immersion does not change the
transcendence degree (Stacks 06RX).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_zero_of_isQuasiFiniteAt
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    {x : points B S hS X} (h : IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x) :
    HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x 0
declarations.comment: condition (4) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_eq_zero_and_isFiniteOverAffineOpen
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_hasTranscendenceDegreeAt_eq_zero_and_isFiniteOverAffineOpen
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) (hYInt : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hlft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hdom : IsDominant B S hS f)
    {x : points B S hS X} (hx : IsGenericPoint x (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS X)))
    {y : points B S hS Y} (hy : IsGenericPoint y (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS Y))) :
    List.TFAE
        [HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x 0,
          HasFiniteResidueFieldExtensionAt B S hS hY hXInt.2.1 hYInt.2.1 f x,
          ExistsAffineOpenFiniteRestriction B S hS f,
          IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x,
          ∀ x' : points B S hS X, pointsMap B S hS X f x' = y → x' = x] ∧
      ((IsSeparated B S hS f ∨ IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) →
        List.TFAE
          [HasTranscendenceDegreeAt B S hS f x 0,
            HasFiniteResidueFieldExtensionAt B S hS hY hXInt.2.1 hYInt.2.1 f x,
            ExistsAffineOpenFiniteRestriction B S hS f,
            IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f x,
            (∀ x' : points B S hS X, pointsMap B S hS X f x' = y → x' = x),
            IsFiniteOverAffineOpen B S hS f])

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.degree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD6.** The degree of `X` over `Y` for a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of integral
algebraic spaces over `S`: the degree `[κ(x) : κ(y)]` of the extension of residue fields at
the generic point `x` of `|X|` and its image `y`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def degree (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) (hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) : ℕ
declarations.comment: the degree of X over Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.degree_pos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD6.** The degree of `X` over `Y` is a positive integer once the extension of
residue fields at the generic point is finite, which is condition (2) of Stacks 0AD5.
declarations.statement:
theorem degree_pos (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) (hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    {x : points B S hS X}
    (hx : IsGenericPoint x (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS X)))
    (hfin : HasFiniteResidueFieldExtensionAt B S hS hY hXint.isDecentSpace
      hYint.isDecentSpace f x) :
    0 < degree B S hS hX hY hXint hYint f
declarations.comment: positivity of the degree, under condition (2) of Stacks 0AD5, which this development cannot yet deduce from the other four

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsIntegralModification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD8.** A *modification* of an integral algebraic space `X` over `S` is a
birational proper morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` with `X'` integral.

No decency hypotheses are needed: an integral algebraic space is decent, so the decency of the
target is `hXint.isDecentSpace` and that of the source comes with its integrality.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsIntegralModification.exists_isIso_fromPreimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AD9.** A modification of an integral algebraic space over `S` is an isomorphism
over a nonempty open subspace of its target.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAlteration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ADA.** An *alteration* of an integral algebraic space `X` over `S` is a proper
dominant morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` with `Y` integral such that the
inverse image of some nonempty open subspace `U ⊆ X` is finite over `U`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAlteration (f : Y ⟶ X) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlteration_iff_isQuasiFiniteAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ADB.** A proper dominant morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of integral algebraic spaces over
`S` is an alteration exactly when it is quasi-finite at the generic point of `|Y|`, which is
condition (4) of Stacks 0AD5 and hence equivalent to the other conditions compared there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlteration_iff_isQuasiFiniteAt (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) (f : Y ⟶ X) (hp : IsProper B S hS f)
    (hdom : IsDominant B S hS f)
    {y : points B S hS Y} (hy : IsGenericPoint y (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS Y)))
    {x : points B S hS X} (hx : IsGenericPoint x (Set.univ : Set (points B S hS X))) :
    IsAlteration B S hS f ↔ IsQuasiFiniteAt B S hS f y
declarations.comment: against condition (4) of Stacks 0AD5

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_localRingDimension_eq_zero_and_exists_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace
declarations.doc:
Let `x` be a point of a quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`. The
following are equivalent:
1. `x` is a point of codimension `0` on the space, that is, by Tag 04NA, the dimension of the
   local ring there is `0`;
2. the local ring of the space at `x` has dimension `0`, in the chart-wise form of Tag 0BAM:
   every étale scheme chart has a local ring of Krull dimension `0` at each point above `x`;
3. `x` is a generic point of an irreducible component of the space of points.

If these hold, then some open subspace of the space containing `x` is a scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_localRingDimension_eq_zero_and_exists_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ F) (x : points B S hS F) :
    [localRingDimension B S hS x = 0, AllChartsLocalRingDimension B S hS x 0,
        x ∈ genericPoints (points B S hS F)].TFAE ∧
      (localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        ∃ G : Subfunctor F, IsOpenSubspace B S hS G ∧ G.toFunctor.IsRepresentable ∧
          x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_mem_range_of_mem_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ADC, the final statement.** A generic point of an irreducible component of the
space of points of a quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` lies in an open subspace which
is a scheme, namely in the schematic locus of Tag 03JH.

The equivalence of the tag's conditions (1), (2) and (3) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_zero_iff_mem_genericPoints_of_quasiSeparated`;
the codimension-zero clause of Tag 06NH which carries such a generic point into the schematic
locus is `codimensionZero_mem_schematicLocus_of_isZariskiLocallyQuasiSeparated` above.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRepresentable_isOpenSubspace_mem_range_of_mem_genericPoints
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ F)
    (x : points B S hS F) (hx : x ∈ genericPoints (points B S hS F)) :
    ∃ G : Subfunctor F, IsOpenSubspace B S hS G ∧ G.toFunctor.IsRepresentable ∧
      x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι)
declarations.comment: the final statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.localRingDimension_eq_zero_iff_mem_genericPoints_of_quasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
A point of a quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` has a local ring of dimension zero —
equivalently, is a point of codimension `0` — exactly when it is a generic point of an
irreducible component of the space of points.
declarations.statement:
theorem localRingDimension_eq_zero_iff_mem_genericPoints_of_quasiSeparated
    (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ F) (x : points B S hS F) :
    localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 ↔ x ∈ genericPoints (points B S hS F)
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1), (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isRepresentable_of_localRingDimension_le_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ADD.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` which is separated and locally
Noetherian, and let `x ∈ |X|` be a point whose local ring has dimension at most one
(Stacks 04NA). Then there is an open subspace of `X` containing `x` which is a scheme, that
is, whose functor of points is representable.

An affine étale chart `V ⟶ X` through `x` has open image `Z₀`, which is quasi-compact,
separated and locally Noetherian; `V` is immersed over `Z₀` in a proper representable morphism,
the fibres of `V ⟶ Z₀` at field-valued points have bounded degree, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isRepresentable_of_chart_rank_le` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isRepresentable_of_localRingDimension_le_one
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hsep : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X)
    (hnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (x : points B S hS X) (hdim : localRingDimension B S hS x ≤ 1) :
    ∃ G : Subfunctor X, IsOpenSubspace B S hS G ∧ G.toFunctor.IsRepresentable ∧
      x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpenSubspace_isRepresentable_of_localRingDimension_le_one_of_fittingBlowups
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ADE.**  Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` which is separated and locally
Noetherian, and let `x ∈ |X|` be a point whose local ring has dimension at most one
(Stacks 04NA).  Then there is an open subspace of `X` containing `x` which is a scheme, that is,
whose functor of points is representable; the route of the remark makes it an affine scheme,
which is recorded as well.

This is the statement of Stacks 0ADD, proved along the route of the remark Stacks 0ADE, which
avoids More on Groupoids, Lemma 0ABI: the finite surjective cover by a scheme near `x` comes
from the induction on the degree of an affine étale chart through `x`
(`exists_isOpenSubspace_isRepresentable_of_chart_rank_le_of_fittingBlowups`), and the
remark's Steps 1 to 5 — reduction, flattening by blowing up Fitting ideals (Stacks 0D0Q), the
finite flat quotient of Stacks 07S6 with Stacks 09NN, the affine open with saturated principal
trace via Stacks 0ADC and 09NN, and Stacks 07VP — turn it into an open subspace which is a scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenSubspace_isRepresentable_of_localRingDimension_le_one_of_fittingBlowups
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hsep : IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X)
    (hnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (x : points B S hS X) (hdim : localRingDimension B S hS x ≤ 1) :
    ∃ G : Subfunctor X, IsOpenSubspace B S hS G ∧ G.toFunctor.IsRepresentable ∧
      IsAffineSpace B S hS G.toFunctor ∧ x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS G.toFunctor G.ι)
declarations.comment: Lemma 0ADD proved along the route of the remark, avoiding Stacks 0ABI

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.DescentData
declarations.doc: A descent datum relative to a family of morphisms of algebraic spaces over a scheme.
declarations.statement:
public structure DescentData
    (hT : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS T)
    (hX : ∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (X i))
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2): a descent datum relative to one morphism Y → X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.DescentData.Hom
declarations.doc: A morphism of descent data is a compatible family of maps over the family members.
declarations.statement: public structure Hom (D E : DescentData f hT hX)
declarations.comment: parts (1) and (2): a descent datum relative to one morphism Y → X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.gluingProjEquiv
declarations.doc:
Over the pairwise fibre product `X i ×_T X j`, an isomorphism `V_i ×_T X_j ≅ X_i ×_T V_j`
is the same thing as an isomorphism `pr₀^* V_i ≅ pr₁^* V_j` of the two base changes along the
projections.
declarations.statement:
def gluingProjEquiv (i j : ι) (Vi : Over (X i)) (Vj : Over (X j)) :
    (Over.mk (prod.map (structureMap (f i) Vi) (𝟙 (Over.mk (f j)))) ≅
        Over.mk (prod.map (𝟙 (Over.mk (f i))) (structureMap (f j) Vj))) ≃
      (projFstObj f i j Vi ≅ projSndObj f i j Vj)
declarations.comment: the two presentations of the gluing isomorphism of a descent datum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.DescentData.projGluing
declarations.doc:
The gluing isomorphism of a descent datum, read as an isomorphism `pr₀^* V_i ≅ pr₁^* V_j`
of algebraic spaces over the pairwise fibre product `X i ×_T X j`.
declarations.statement:
def projGluing (D : DescentData f hT hX) (i j : ι) :
    projFstObj f i j (D.obj i) ≅ projSndObj f i j (D.obj j)
declarations.comment: the gluing isomorphism read as a map pr₀^* V ⟶ pr₁^* V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.DescentData.projGluing01_comp_projGluing12
declarations.doc:
The cocycle condition of a descent datum, read on base changes along the projections of
the triple fibre product: `pr₀₂^* φ_ik = pr₁₂^* φ_jk ∘ pr₀₁^* φ_ij`.
declarations.statement:
theorem projGluing01_comp_projGluing12 (D : DescentData f hT hX) (i j k : ι) :
    D.projGluing01 i j k ≫ D.projGluing12 i j k = D.projGluing02 i j k
declarations.comment: the cocycle condition in the form pr₀₂^* φ = pr₁₂^* φ ∘ pr₀₁^* φ

declarations.doc: A descent datum relative to a family of morphisms of algebraic spaces over a scheme.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.familyCoproductEquivalenceOfAdmitsCoproductIndex
declarations.doc:
Let `{f i : X i → T}` be a family of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with fixed
target, and let `Y = ∐ X i` be the coproduct of the sources in sheaves on the big fppf site, an
algebraic space over `S` by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.sigmaAlgebraicSheafCoproduct`. There
is a canonical equivalence from the category of descent data relative to the family to the
category of descent data relative to `Y → T`, which sends `(V i, φ i j)` to `(V, φ)` with
`V = ∐ V i` and `φ` restricting to `φ i j` on each pair of summands, and a morphism `(ψ i)` to
`∐ ψ i`.

The index type is `u`-small and of cardinality below the cofinality of the site's size cutoff,
as is every countable index type.
declarations.statement:
public def familyCoproductEquivalenceOfAdmitsCoproductIndex :
    FullFamilyCoproductEquivalence.{u, v, w} f hT hX (sigmaAlgebraicSheafCoproduct X hX)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.pullbackDescentDataFunctor
declarations.doc:
The pullback functor on descent data, with the canonical natural comparison of its
underlying space over `Y'` with ordinary pullback along `f`.
declarations.statement:
public def pullbackDescentDataFunctor
    {X X' Y Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a : Y ⟶ X) (a' : Y' ⟶ X') (h : X' ⟶ X) (f : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (ha : f ≫ a = a' ≫ h)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X')
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') :
    { F : HomDescentData.{u, v} a hX hY ⥤ HomDescentData.{u, w} a' hX' hY' //
      ∃ α : ∀ D : HomDescentData.{u, v} a hX hY,
          (F.obj D).obj PUnit.unit ≅ (Over.pullback f).obj (D.obj PUnit.unit),
        (∀ {D E : HomDescentData.{u, v} a hX hY} (φ : D ⟶ E),
          (F.map φ).hom PUnit.unit ≫ (α E).hom =
            (α D).hom ≫ (Over.pullback f).map (φ.hom PUnit.unit)) ∧
        (∀ D : HomDescentData.{u, v} a hX hY,
          let A' := (Over.map a').obj ((F.obj D).obj PUnit.unit)
          let B' := Over.mk a'
          let A := (Over.map a).obj (D.obj PUnit.unit)
          let B := Over.mk a
          ∃ (q : (Over.map h).obj A' ⟶ A)
            (r : (Over.map h).obj B' ⟶ B),
            q.left = (α D).hom.left ≫ pullback.fst (D.obj PUnit.unit).hom f ∧
            r.left = f ∧
            (let s : (Over.map h).obj (A' ⨯ B') ⟶ A ⨯ B :=
                prod.lift ((Over.map h).map (prod.fst : A' ⨯ B' ⟶ A') ≫ q)
                  ((Over.map h).map (prod.snd : A' ⨯ B' ⟶ B') ≫ r)
             let t : (Over.map h).obj (B' ⨯ A') ⟶ B ⨯ A :=
                prod.lift ((Over.map h).map (prod.fst : B' ⨯ A' ⟶ B') ≫ r)
                  ((Over.map h).map (prod.snd : B' ⨯ A' ⟶ A') ≫ q)
             (Over.map h).map ((F.obj D).gluing PUnit.unit PUnit.unit).hom.left ≫ t =
               s ≫ (D.gluing PUnit.unit PUnit.unit).hom.left)) }
declarations.comment: part (1), pullback functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.pullbackDescentDataFunctor_canonicalIso
declarations.doc:
Pullback along two maps completing the same square is canonically and naturally
isomorphic, by the gluing isomorphism of the descent datum.
declarations.statement:
public def pullbackDescentDataFunctor_canonicalIso :
    let F₀ := pullbackDescentDataFunctor.{u, v, w} a a' h f₀ ha₀ hX hX' hY hY'
    let F₁ := pullbackDescentDataFunctor.{u, v, w} a a' h f₁ ha₁ hX hX' hY hY'
    let α₀ := Classical.choose F₀.property
    let α₁ := Classical.choose F₁.property
    { η : F₀.val ≅ F₁.val //
      ∀ D : HomDescentData.{u, v} a hX hY,
        let V₀ := (F₀.val.obj D).obj PUnit.unit
        let V₁ := (F₁.val.obj D).obj PUnit.unit
        let A := (Over.map a).obj (D.obj PUnit.unit)
        let B₀ := Over.mk a
        ∃ (q₀ : (Over.map (a' ≫ h)).obj V₀ ⟶ A)
          (q₁ : (Over.map (a' ≫ h)).obj V₁ ⟶ A)
          (y₁ : (Over.map (a' ≫ h)).obj V₀ ⟶ B₀)
          (y₀ : (Over.map (a' ≫ h)).obj V₁ ⟶ B₀),
          q₀.left = (α₀ D).hom.left ≫ pullback.fst (D.obj PUnit.unit).hom f₀ ∧
          q₁.left = (α₁ D).hom.left ≫ pullback.fst (D.obj PUnit.unit).hom f₁ ∧
          y₁.left = V₀.hom ≫ f₁ ∧ y₀.left = V₁.hom ≫ f₀ ∧
          prod.lift q₀ y₁ ≫ (D.gluing PUnit.unit PUnit.unit).hom.left =
            (Over.map (a' ≫ h)).map ((η.hom.app D).hom PUnit.unit) ≫
              prod.lift y₀ q₁ }
declarations.comment: part (2), canonical isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.pullbackDescentDataFunctor
declarations.doc:
The pullback functor on descent data, with the canonical natural comparison of its
underlying space over `Y'` with ordinary pullback along `f`.
declarations.statement:
public def pullbackDescentDataFunctor
    {X X' Y Y' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (a : Y ⟶ X) (a' : Y' ⟶ X') (h : X' ⟶ X) (f : Y' ⟶ Y)
    (ha : f ≫ a = a' ≫ h)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X')
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hY' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y') :
    { F : HomDescentData.{u, v} a hX hY ⥤ HomDescentData.{u, w} a' hX' hY' //
      ∃ α : ∀ D : HomDescentData.{u, v} a hX hY,
          (F.obj D).obj PUnit.unit ≅ (Over.pullback f).obj (D.obj PUnit.unit),
        (∀ {D E : HomDescentData.{u, v} a hX hY} (φ : D ⟶ E),
          (F.map φ).hom PUnit.unit ≫ (α E).hom =
            (α D).hom ≫ (Over.pullback f).map (φ.hom PUnit.unit)) ∧
        (∀ D : HomDescentData.{u, v} a hX hY,
          let A' := (Over.map a').obj ((F.obj D).obj PUnit.unit)
          let B' := Over.mk a'
          let A := (Over.map a).obj (D.obj PUnit.unit)
          let B := Over.mk a
          ∃ (q : (Over.map h).obj A' ⟶ A)
            (r : (Over.map h).obj B' ⟶ B),
            q.left = (α D).hom.left ≫ pullback.fst (D.obj PUnit.unit).hom f ∧
            r.left = f ∧
            (let s : (Over.map h).obj (A' ⨯ B') ⟶ A ⨯ B :=
                prod.lift ((Over.map h).map (prod.fst : A' ⨯ B' ⟶ A') ≫ q)
                  ((Over.map h).map (prod.snd : A' ⨯ B' ⟶ B') ≫ r)
             let t : (Over.map h).obj (B' ⨯ A') ⟶ B ⨯ A :=
                prod.lift ((Over.map h).map (prod.fst : B' ⨯ A' ⟶ B') ≫ r)
                  ((Over.map h).map (prod.snd : B' ⨯ A' ⟶ A') ≫ q)
             (Over.map h).map ((F.obj D).gluing PUnit.unit PUnit.unit).hom.left ≫ t =
               s ≫ (D.gluing PUnit.unit PUnit.unit).hom.left)) }
declarations.comment: the functor so constructed is the pullback functor on descent data

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.pullbackDatum
declarations.doc: Pullback of a descent datum along a morphism of families of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
public def pullbackDatum (g : T' ⟶ T) (comm : ∀ i, gᵢ i ≫ f (α i) = f' i ≫ g) :
    PulledBackDatum f f' hT hX hT' hX' α gᵢ D
declarations.comment: family_pullback_datum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.pullbackFunctorCoproductComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ADN part (4).** Let `U = {X j → T}` and `U' = {X' i → T'}` be
families of morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S` with fixed target, and let
`α : I' → I`, `g : T' → T`, `gᵢ : X' i → X (α i)` be a morphism of families with fixed
target. The pullback functor on descent data along that morphism of families, Tag 0ADN
part (2), agrees — through the canonical equivalences of Tag 0ADK between descent data for a
family and descent data for the coproduct of its sources — with the pullback functor of
Tag 0ADL for the induced commutative square
`∐ X' i → ∐ X j`, `T' → T` of single morphisms.

The isomorphism is pinned on each summand: on the `i`-th summand of the coproduct of the
pulled-back components it is the projection of `X' i ×_{X (α i)} V (α i)` onto `V (α i)`,
followed by the inclusion of the `α i`-th summand of the coproduct of the original
components.

The index types are `u`-small and of cardinality below the cofinality of the site's size
cutoff, as is every countable index type. This is the same size condition that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Descent.familyCoproductEquivalenceOfAdmitsCoproductIndex` carries,
and it is what makes the coproducts exist at all.
declarations.statement:
public def pullbackFunctorCoproductComparison :
    let Ycop := sigmaAlgebraicSheafCoproduct X hX
    let Y'cop := sigmaAlgebraicSheafCoproduct X' hX'
    let E := familyCoproductEquivalenceOfAdmitsCoproductIndex.{u, v, w} f hT hX
    let E' := familyCoproductEquivalenceOfAdmitsCoproductIndex.{u, v', w} f' hT' hX'
    let P := pullbackFunctor f f' hT hX hT' hX' α g gᵢ comm
    let F := pullbackDescentDataFunctor.{u, w, w} (Ycop.desc (spaceSheaf T hT) f)
      (Y'cop.desc (spaceSheaf T' hT') f') g (coproductMap hX hX' α gᵢ Ycop Y'cop)
      (coproductMap_comm f f' hT hX hT' hX' α g gᵢ comm Ycop Y'cop) hT hT'
      Ycop.isAlgebraicSpace Y'cop.isAlgebraicSpace
    let αF := Classical.choose F.property
    { η : P.functor ⋙ E'.equivalence.functor ≅ E.equivalence.functor ⋙ F.val //
      ∀ (D : DescentData f hT hX) (i : ι'),
        ((fullTotalCoproduct f' hT' hX' (P.functor.obj D)).ι i).hom ≫
            (E'.objIso (P.functor.obj D)).inv.left ≫
            ((η.hom.app D).hom PUnit.unit).left ≫
            (αF (E.equivalence.functor.obj D)).hom.left ≫
            pullback.fst ((E.equivalence.functor.obj D).obj PUnit.unit).hom
              (coproductMap hX hX' α gᵢ Ycop Y'cop) =
          ((eqToHom (P.obj_eq D)).hom i).left ≫
            (pullbackDatum f f' hT hX hT' hX' α gᵢ D g comm).objMap i ≫
            ((fullTotalCoproduct f hT hX D).ι (α i)).hom ≫ (E.objIso D).inv.left }
declarations.comment: part (4), agreement with the pullback functors of 0ADL through 0ADK
