declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_spfLTRSMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AHZ**, injectivity of the comparison map. In the identification
`Mor_{LTRS}((Spf B, 𝒪_{Spf B}), (Spf A, 𝒪_{Spf A})) = Hom_cont(A, B)` the map from continuous
ring homomorphisms to morphisms of formal spectra is injective as soon as `B` is separated and
linearly topologized: a morphism determines the map it induces on global sections, that map is
the homomorphism read through the canonical maps into global sections, and the canonical map of
`B` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_spfLTRSMap [IsLinearTopology B B] [T2Space B] :
    Function.Injective (spfLTRSMap A B hA I₀ hB)
declarations.comment: injectivity of the comparison map Hom_cont(A, B) → Mor_LTRS(Spf B, Spf A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_spfLTRSMap
declarations.doc:
**Morphisms of formal spectra come from continuous ring maps.** Every morphism
`g : Spf B → Spf A` of locally topologically ringed spaces between the formal spectra of admissible
topological rings comes from a continuous ring homomorphism `A → B`, namely from
`AlgebraicGeometry.ltrsGlobalSectionsRingHom g`, the map `g` induces on global sections read
through the identifications `Γ(Spf A, 𝒪_{Spf A}) = A` and `Γ(Spf B, 𝒪_{Spf B}) = B` of Stacks 0AHY.
declarations.statement: theorem surjective_spfLTRSMap : Function.Surjective (spfLTRSMap A B hA.1 I₀ hB.1)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the comparison map Hom_cont(A, B) → Mor_LTRS(Spf B, Spf A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_spfLTRSMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AHZ.** For admissible topological rings `A` and `B` the comparison map taking a
continuous ring homomorphism `A → B` to the induced morphism `Spf B → Spf A` of locally
topologically ringed spaces is a bijection: it is injective by
`AlgebraicGeometry.injective_spfLTRSMap`, separatedness of `B` making the canonical map
`B → Γ(Spf B, 𝒪_{Spf B})` injective, and surjective by
`AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_spfLTRSMap`.
declarations.statement: theorem bijective_spfLTRSMap : Function.Bijective (spfLTRSMap A B hA.1 I₀ hB.1)
declarations.comment: the full bijection Hom_cont(A, B) = Mor_LTRS(Spf B, Spf A) for admissible A, B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.schemeToFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI0.** The functor `Schemes ⟶ Formal Schemes`: pseudo-discretisation, a scheme
being a formal scheme by `AlgebraicGeometry.isFormalScheme_schemeToLTRSObj`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def schemeToFormalScheme : Scheme.{u} ⥤ FormalScheme.{u}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.full_schemeToFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI0.** The functor from schemes to formal schemes is full: a morphism of the
pseudo-discretised spaces has an automatically continuous comparison map, so it is the image of
the morphism of schemes with the same data.
declarations.statement: instance full_schemeToFormalScheme : schemeToFormalScheme.{u}.Full
declarations.comment: full faithfulness: fullness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.faithful_schemeToFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI0.** The functor from schemes to formal schemes is faithful: a morphism of
schemes is recovered from its pseudo-discretisation by forgetting the topologies.
declarations.statement: instance faithful_schemeToFormalScheme : schemeToFormalScheme.{u}.Faithful
declarations.comment: full faithfulness: faithfulness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_formalSchemeFunctorOfPoints_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI1**, injectivity. A morphism of formal schemes whose source satisfies the size
condition is determined by the natural transformation it induces on functors of points on the
schemes of size below `κ`.

The morphisms `Spec (A/I_λ) → Spf A ≅ 𝔛|_𝔘 → 𝔛` attached to the affine formal charts of `𝔛` are
jointly epimorphic, and the size condition is exactly what makes them morphisms out of objects
of `Sch_κ`, hence points of `𝔛` seen by the functor of points. Their underlying maps cover `𝔛`
because each `Spec (A/I_λ) → Spf A` is a homeomorphism; and they separate the sections of
`𝒪_𝔛`, because `𝒪_𝔛` is a sheaf and the sections of `𝒪_{Spf A} = lim 𝒪_λ` are a limit.
declarations.comment: injectivity: a morphism of formal schemes is determined by the induced transformation of functors of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_formalSchemeFunctorOfPoints_map
declarations.doc:
**Morphisms of formal schemes are transformations of functors of points.** For a formal scheme
`𝔛` whose size is not too large — the schemes `Spec (A/I_λ)` cut out of its affine formal charts
being objects of `Sch_κ` — and any formal scheme `𝔜`,

`Mor_{Formal Schemes}(𝔛, 𝔜) = Mor_{PSh(Sch_κ)}(h_𝔛, h_𝔜)`.
declarations.comment: the bijection Mor(𝔛, 𝔜) = Mor(h_𝔛, h_𝔜) for a formal scheme 𝔛 whose size is bounded by the cutoff

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_formalSchemePointsFunctor_map_eq
declarations.doc:
Every transformation `h_𝔛 → h_𝔜` of functors of points on the category of all schemes is
induced by a morphism of formal schemes `𝔛 → 𝔜`, with no size hypothesis.
declarations.comment: surjectivity on all schemes: every transformation of functors of points is induced by a morphism of formal schemes, with no size hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_formalSchemePointsFunctor_map
declarations.doc:
For formal schemes `𝔛` and `𝔜`, the functor of points on the category of all schemes induces
a bijection

`Mor_{Formal Schemes}(𝔛, 𝔜) = Mor_{PSh(Sch)}(h_𝔛, h_𝔜)`,

with no size hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_formalSchemePointsFunctor_map {X Y : FormalScheme.{u}} :
    Function.Bijective fun f : X ⟶ Y => formalSchemePointsFunctor.map f
declarations.comment: the bijection Mor(𝔛, 𝔜) = Mor(h_𝔛, h_𝔜) on all schemes, with no size hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.full_formalSchemePointsFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor of points of formal schemes on the category of all schemes is full, with no size
hypothesis.
declarations.statement: instance full_formalSchemePointsFunctor : formalSchemePointsFunctor.{u}.Full
declarations.comment: fullness of the functor of points on morphisms, with no size hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_formalSchemePointsFunctor_map
declarations.doc:
A morphism of formal schemes is determined by the natural transformation it induces on
functors of points on the category of all schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_formalSchemePointsFunctor_map {X Y : FormalScheme.{u}} :
    Function.Injective fun f : X ⟶ Y => formalSchemePointsFunctor.map f
declarations.comment: injectivity of the functor of points on morphisms, with no size hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheafFor_formalSchemeFunctorOfPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI2** for the functor of points of Stacks 0AI1, on the schemes of size below `κ`:
it satisfies the sheaf condition for every family of morphisms of `Sch_κ` which is an fpqc
covering.

Members of `Sch_κ` have their fibre products in `Sch_κ`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_pullback_lt`), so a family of points compatible on `Sch_κ` is
compatible on all schemes, and `AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_formalSchemePoints`
applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafFor_formalSchemeFunctorOfPoints {κ : Cardinal.{u}} (X : FormalScheme.{u})
    {T : (schemeCutoff κ).FullSubcategory} {R : Presieve T}
    (covering : R ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.{u}.comap (schemeCutoff κ).ι T) :
    Presieve.IsSheafFor ((formalSchemeFunctorOfPoints κ).obj X) R

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_formalSchemePoints_of_isoSpf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI2**, the gluing clause included, for an affine formal scheme: the functor of
points of a formal scheme isomorphic to a formal spectrum is an fpqc sheaf.

Transporting along the isomorphism reduces this to
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_formalSchemePoints_spfFormalScheme`.
declarations.comment: sheaf condition with gluing, for a formal scheme isomorphic to a formal spectrum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_formalSchemePoints_schemeToFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
The functor of points of a scheme seen as a formal scheme satisfies the sheaf condition,
gluing included, for fpqc coverings of schemes.
declarations.comment: sheaf condition with gluing, for a scheme seen as a formal scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_formalSchemePoints_of_iso
declarations.doc:
The functor of points of a formal scheme isomorphic to a scheme satisfies the sheaf
condition, gluing included, for fpqc coverings of schemes.
declarations.comment: sheaf condition with gluing, for a formal scheme isomorphic to a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_zariskiTopology_formalSchemePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI2**, the Zariski case in full. The functor of points of a formal scheme, on the
category of all schemes, is a sheaf for the big Zariski topology: a matching family of points on
the members of any Zariski covering of a scheme has a unique amalgamation.

Zariski coverings are the jointly surjective families of open immersions, so this follows from
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheafFor_ofArrows_formalSchemePoints` once the sheaf condition for a
Grothendieck topology generated by a precoverage is reduced to its covering families, which is
`CategoryTheory.Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_zariskiTopology_formalSchemePoints (X : FormalScheme.{u}) :
    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (formalSchemePoints X)
declarations.comment: Zariski case in full, separatedness and gluing: the functor of points is a sheaf for the big Zariski topology on all schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints_formalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIR**, the sheaf clause, for an *arbitrary* formal scheme: the functor of points
of a formal scheme à la EGA satisfies the fppf sheaf condition on the big fppf site of `S`, with
no hypothesis assumed.

This is the first sentence of the source's remark, "by Lemma 87.2.2 the functor of points
`h_𝔛` associated to a formal scheme `𝔛` is a sheaf in the fppf topology". It is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_formalSchemePoints`, the full statement of Stacks 0AI2,
read on the big fppf site of `S` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints_of_isSheaf_fpqcTopology`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints_formalScheme (X : FormalScheme.{u}) :
    IsFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints B S hS X
declarations.comment: the fpqc sheaf condition read on the big fppf site of a base scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_spfwGammaHom
declarations.doc:
**The counterpart for McQuillan's weakening of the identification
`Γ(Spf A, 𝒪_{Spf A}) = A`.** For a weakly admissible topological ring `A` the canonical map
`A → Γ(Spfw A, 𝒪)` into the global sections of the formal spectrum taken along the *weak* ideals
of definition of `A` is an isomorphism of topological rings.

The proof is the one for an admissible ring, run over the whole family of weak ideals of
definition instead of over the powers of a single ideal of definition. What it needs of the
family is exactly that its members are open, that it is closed under intersection, and that it is
a fundamental system of open neighbourhoods of zero — the last two being the intersection clause
and the fundamental-system clause of Stacks 0AI3 — together with completeness and separatedness
of `A`. The cofinality of the powers `Iⁿ` of a single `I`, which an ideal of definition has and a
weak ideal of definition need not, is used nowhere.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_spfwGammaHom [IsLinearTopology A A] (hA : IsWeaklyAdmissible A) :
    IsIso (spfGammaHomOn A IsWeakIdealOfDefinition)
declarations.comment: the identification the counterparts of Lemmas 87.2.1 and 87.2.2 consume: Γ(Spfw A, 𝒪) = A for a weakly admissible ring, over the whole system of weak ideals of definition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spfwGammaIso
declarations.doc:
**The identification `A = Γ(Spfw A, 𝒪)` of topological rings** for a weakly admissible
topological ring: McQuillan's counterpart of the identification `Γ(Spf A, 𝒪_{Spf A}) = A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spfwGammaIso [IsLinearTopology A A] (hA : IsWeaklyAdmissible A) :
    TopCommRingCat.of A ≅ (spfPresheafOn A IsWeakIdealOfDefinition).obj (op ⊤)
declarations.comment: the identification the counterparts of Lemmas 87.2.1 and 87.2.2 consume: A = Γ(Spfw A, 𝒪) as topological rings, for a weakly admissible ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsMcQuillanFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
An object of `LTRS` is a *formal scheme in the sense of McQuillan* when every point has an
open neighbourhood isomorphic to the formal spectrum, taken along the weak ideals of definition,
of a weakly admissible topological ring. As for `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFormalScheme`, the
isomorphism is asked for as one of presheafed spaces of topological rings, which for objects of
`LTRS` is the same as an isomorphism in `LTRS`.
declarations.statement: def IsMcQuillanFormalScheme : ObjectProperty LTRS.{u}
declarations.comment: the larger category of formal schemes based on weak admissibility: its objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.McQuillanFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
The category of *McQuillan formal schemes*: the full subcategory of `LTRS` on the objects
locally isomorphic to a formal spectrum taken along the weak ideals of definition of a weakly
admissible topological ring. A morphism is a morphism of `LTRS`.
declarations.statement: abbrev McQuillanFormalScheme
declarations.comment: the larger category of formal schemes based on weak admissibility: the category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_mcQuillanFormalSchemeFunctorOfPoints_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI3**, the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.1 in McQuillan's setting. A morphism of
McQuillan formal schemes whose source satisfies the size condition is determined by the natural
transformation it induces on functors of points on the schemes of size below `κ`.

The proof is the source's: the morphisms `Spec (A/I_λ) → 𝔛|_𝔘 → 𝔛` attached to the charts of
`𝔛` are jointly epimorphic, and the size condition makes them points of `𝔛` seen by the functor
of points. Their underlying maps cover `𝔛` because each `Spec (A/I_λ)` is carried
homeomorphically onto the space of open primes of `A`, a prime being open exactly when it
contains the weak ideal of definition `I_λ`; and they separate the sections of `𝒪_𝔛` because
`𝒪_𝔛` is a sheaf and the sections of the structure presheaf of the chart are the limit over the
weak ideals of definition.
declarations.comment: the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.1: a morphism of McQuillan formal schemes is determined by the induced transformation of functors of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_mcQuillanFormalSchemePointsFunctor_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI3**, the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.1 in McQuillan's setting, with no size
hypothesis: a morphism of McQuillan formal schemes is determined by the transformation it
induces on functors of points on all schemes. Every McQuillan formal scheme satisfies the size
condition for some cutoff, and the functor of points on `Sch_κ` is the restriction of the
functor of points on all schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_mcQuillanFormalSchemePointsFunctor_map {X Y : McQuillanFormalScheme.{u}} :
    Function.Injective fun f : X ⟶ Y => mcQuillanFormalSchemePointsFunctor.map f
declarations.comment: the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.1: injectivity of the functor of points on morphisms of McQuillan formal schemes, with no size hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_fpqcTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI3**, the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2 in McQuillan's setting. The functor of
points of a McQuillan formal scheme, on the category of all schemes, is separated for the fpqc
topology: a point of `𝔛` over a scheme `T` is determined by its restrictions along any fpqc
covering sieve of `T`.

The proof is the source's: an fpqc covering sieve contains an fpqc covering family, whose
members are flat and jointly surjective, and a morphism from a scheme to a locally topologically
ringed space is determined by its restrictions along such a family.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparated_fpqcTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints (X : McQuillanFormalScheme.{u}) :
    Presieve.IsSeparated Scheme.fpqcTopology.{u} (mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints X)
declarations.comment: the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2: the functor of points of a McQuillan formal scheme on all schemes is separated for the fpqc topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparatedFor_mcQuillanFormalSchemeFunctorOfPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI3**, the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2 in McQuillan's setting, for the functor of
points on the schemes of size below `κ`: a point of `𝔛` over a scheme `T` of `Sch_κ` is
determined by its restrictions along a family of morphisms of `Sch_κ` which is an fpqc covering
of `T`.
declarations.comment: the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2: the functor of points of a McQuillan formal scheme on the schemes of size below the cutoff is separated for the fpqc topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_zariskiTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI3**, the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2 in McQuillan's setting, for the big Zariski
topology. The functor of points of a McQuillan formal scheme, on the category of all schemes, is
a sheaf for the big Zariski topology: a matching family of points on the members of any Zariski
covering of a scheme has a unique amalgamation.

The proof is the source's: Zariski coverings are the jointly surjective families of open
immersions, and a matching family of morphisms into a locally topologically ringed space on the
members of an open covering glues uniquely.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_zariskiTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints (X : McQuillanFormalScheme.{u}) :
    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints X)
declarations.comment: the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2: the functor of points of a McQuillan formal scheme on all schemes is a sheaf for the big Zariski topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_comp_eq_of_flat_surjective_spfwLTRS
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI3**, the existence half of the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2 at an affine test
scheme. For a weakly admissible topological ring `A`, a point `Spec S ⟶ Spfw A` of McQuillan's
formal spectrum whose two pullbacks along any pair of morphisms agreeing over `Spec R` agree
descends along a faithfully flat morphism `Spec S → Spec R` of affine schemes.

This is the affine descent step the source's proof of Lemma 87.2.2 reduces to, and it is that
proof unchanged: the weak ideals of definition of `A` form a weak ideal system, and the
identification `Γ(Spfw A, 𝒪) = A` it consumes is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_spfwGammaHom`. The separatedness half, which together with this one is
the sheaf condition for the covering `{Spec S → Spec R}`, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_fpqcTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_comp_eq_of_flat_surjective_spfwLTRS (hA : IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    {R S : CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ S) (hflat : Flat (Spec.map φ))
    (hsurj : Surjective (Spec.map φ)) (u : schemeToLTRSObj (Spec S) ⟶ spfwLTRS A hA.1)
    (hu : ∀ {Z : Scheme.{u}} (p₁ p₂ : Z ⟶ Spec S), p₁ ≫ Spec.map φ = p₂ ≫ Spec.map φ →
      schemeToLTRS.map p₁ ≫ u = schemeToLTRS.map p₂ ≫ u) :
    ∃ t : schemeToLTRSObj (Spec R) ⟶ spfwLTRS A hA.1,
      schemeToLTRS.map (Spec.map φ) ≫ t = u
declarations.comment: the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2: existence of an amalgamation at an affine test scheme, for a point of McQuillan's formal spectrum of a weakly admissible ring along a faithfully flat morphism of affine schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI3**, the existence half of the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2 in McQuillan's setting,
and so the full sheaf condition. The functor of points of a McQuillan formal scheme `𝔛`, on the
category of all schemes, satisfies the sheaf condition for fpqc coverings.

The proof is the source's, and is the one already carried out for admissible rings in
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_formalSchemePoints`. Uniqueness of amalgamations is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_fpqcTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints`. For existence, a
compatible family of points first descends on underlying spaces to a continuous map `g : T → 𝔛`,
continuous maps into a fixed space forming an fpqc sheaf. Around each point `p` of `T` choose a
weak affine formal chart `𝔘 ≅ Spfw A` of `𝔛` containing `g p`; over the open `g⁻¹ 𝔘` every member
of the pulled-back family lands in `𝔘`, so it has an amalgamation by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAmalgamation_of_range_subset_weakChart`. These local amalgamations
glue because the functor of points is a Zariski sheaf
(`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_zariskiTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_fpqcTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints (X : McQuillanFormalScheme.{u}) :
    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.fpqcTopology.{u} (mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints X)
declarations.comment: the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2: the functor of points of a McQuillan formal scheme on all schemes is a sheaf for the fpqc topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSheafFor_mcQuillanFormalSchemeFunctorOfPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI3**, the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2 in McQuillan's setting for the functor of
points on the schemes of size below `κ`: it satisfies the sheaf condition for every family of
morphisms of `Sch_κ` which is an fpqc covering.

Members of `Sch_κ` have their fibre products in `Sch_κ`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.size_pullback_lt`), so a family of points compatible on `Sch_κ` is
compatible on all schemes, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_mcQuillanFormalSchemePoints` applies.
declarations.comment: the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.2: the functor of points of a McQuillan formal scheme on the schemes of size below the cutoff is a sheaf for the fpqc topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bijective_mcQuillanFormalSchemeFunctorOfPoints_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI3**, the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.1 in McQuillan's setting, in full. For a
McQuillan formal scheme `𝔛` whose size is not too large — the schemes `Spec (A/I_λ)` cut out of
its weak affine formal charts being objects of `Sch_κ` — and any McQuillan formal scheme `𝔜`,

`Mor_{McQuillan Formal Schemes}(𝔛, 𝔜) = Mor_{PSh(Sch_κ)}(h_𝔛, h_𝔜)`.

Injectivity is `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_mcQuillanFormalSchemeFunctorOfPoints_map` and
surjectivity is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_mcQuillanFormalSchemeFunctorOfPoints_map_eq`.
declarations.comment: the counterpart of Lemma 87.2.1: the bijection Mor(𝔛, 𝔜) = Mor(h_𝔛, h_𝔜) for a McQuillan formal scheme 𝔛 whose size is bounded by the cutoff

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isWeakIdealOfDefinition_inf_of_isOpen_right
declarations.doc:
The intersection of a weak ideal of definition with an open ideal is a weak ideal of
definition.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isWeakIdealOfDefinition_inf_of_isOpen_right {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [TopologicalSpace A] {I J : Ideal A} (hI : TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I)
    (hJ : IsOpen (J : Set A)) : TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (I ⊓ J)
declarations.comment: intersection

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.hasBasis_nhds_zero_isWeakIdealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
In a weakly admissible linearly topologized ring, its weak ideals of definition form a
fundamental system of neighborhoods of zero.
declarations.statement:
public lemma hasBasis_nhds_zero_isWeakIdealOfDefinition
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) :
    (nhds (0 : A)).HasBasis
      (fun I : Ideal A ↦ TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I)
      (fun I : Ideal A ↦ (I : Set A))
declarations.comment: weak_basis

registrations.comment: admissible_recall

registrations.comment: weak_admissibility

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TopologicalSheaf.hasLimits_sheaf_topModuleCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI4** (limits), for sheaves of topological modules over a topological ring `R`:
`Sh(C, TopMod_R)` has limits, the inclusion into presheaves preserves them, and limits of
presheaves are computed sectionwise.
declarations.comment: limits (topological modules)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TopologicalSheaf.hasLimits_sheaf_topAddCommGrpCat
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0AI4** (limits), for sheaves of topological abelian groups.
declarations.comment: limits (topological abelian groups)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TopologicalSheaf.hasLimits_sheaf_topCommRingCat
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0AI4** (limits), for sheaves of topological rings.
declarations.comment: limits (topological rings)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TopologicalSheaf.exists_bounded_subsheaf_factorization_topModuleCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI4** (bounded subsheaf), for sheaves of topological modules over a topological
ring `R`: any map from a fixed presheaf to a sheaf factors through a subsheaf whose values have
cardinality bounded by a cardinal depending only on the site and the presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bounded_subsheaf_factorization_topModuleCat
    (R : Type (max u v w)) [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ TopModuleCat.{max u v w} R) :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{max u v w}, ∀ (G : Sheaf J (TopModuleCat.{max u v w} R)) (f : F ⟶ G.obj),
      ∃ (G' : Sheaf J (TopModuleCat.{max u v w} R)) (i : G' ⟶ G), Mono i ∧
        (∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Cardinal.mk (G'.obj.obj U) ≤ κ) ∧ ∃ f' : F ⟶ G'.obj, f' ≫ i.hom = f
declarations.comment: bounded_subsheaf (topological modules)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TopologicalSheaf.exists_bounded_subsheaf_factorization_topAddCommGrpCat
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0AI4** (bounded subsheaf), for sheaves of topological abelian groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bounded_subsheaf_factorization_topAddCommGrpCat
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ TopAddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{max u v w}, ∀ (G : Sheaf J TopAddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) (f : F ⟶ G.obj),
      ∃ (G' : Sheaf J TopAddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}) (i : G' ⟶ G), Mono i ∧
        (∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, Cardinal.mk (G'.obj.obj U) ≤ κ) ∧ ∃ f' : F ⟶ G'.obj, f' ≫ i.hom = f
declarations.comment: bounded_subsheaf (topological abelian groups)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TopologicalSheaf.isSheaf_skyscraperPresheaf_topModuleCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI4** (the sheaf `U ↦ Map(u(U), M)`), for topological modules over a topological
ring `R`, topological abelian groups (`R = ℤ`) and, by
`isSheaf_skyscraperPresheaf_topCommRingCat`, topological rings: for a point of the site given by
`u : C ⥤ Sets` satisfying conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 00Y5 and a topological module `M`, the
presheaf `U ↦ ∏_{x ∈ u(U)} M` (the product in `TopModuleCat R`, i.e. with the product topology) is
a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_skyscraperPresheaf_topModuleCat (R : Type w) [Ring R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    (h₁ : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (P : Presieve X), P ∈ K X → ∀ x : u.obj X,
      ∃ (Y : C) (f : Y ⟶ X) (_ : P f) (y : u.obj Y), u.map f y = x)
    (h₂ : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (P : Presieve X), P ∈ K X → ∀ ⦃Y Z : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X), P f →
      ∀ (g : Z ⟶ X) [HasPullback f g], Function.Bijective (pullbackComparison u f g))
    (M : TopModuleCat.{w} R) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf K.toGrothendieck (ElementColimit.skyscraperPresheaf u M)
declarations.comment: point_mapping_sheaf (topological modules and abelian groups)

theorem isSheaf_skyscraperPresheaf_topCommRingCat

theorem isIso_elementColimit_map_toSheafify_topModuleCat (R : Type w) [Ring R]

declarations.comment: size

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TopologicalSheaf.exists_bounded_subsheaf_factorization
declarations.doc:
Any map from a fixed presheaf of topological spaces to a sheaf factors through a
subsheaf of uniformly bounded size.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_bounded_subsheaf_factorization (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ TopCat.{w}) :
    ∃ κ : Cardinal.{max u v w}, ∀ (G : Sheaf J TopCat.{w}) (f : F ⟶ G.obj),
      ∃ (G' : Sheaf J TopCat.{w}) (i : G' ⟶ G),
        Mono i ∧ Cardinal.lift.{v} (sheafSize G') ≤ κ ∧
          ∃ f' : F ⟶ G'.obj, f' ≫ i.hom = f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TopologicalSheaf.isSheaf_mappingPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI4** (the sheaf `U ↦ Map(u(U), M)`). Let `p` be a point of the site `C` given by
a functor `u : C ⥤ Sets` (Stacks 00Y5). For a topological space `M`, the presheaf
`U ↦ Map(u(U), M) = ∏_{x ∈ u(U)} M`, with the product topology, is a sheaf of topological
spaces.

The site is the small category `C` with the topology generated by a precoverage `K` that has
the fibre products of its coverings and is stable under base change, and `h₁`, `h₂` are
conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 00Y5 for `u`; condition (3) is not needed. The general form,
for any category with products, is `CategoryTheory.ElementColimit.isSheaf_skyscraperPresheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_mappingPresheaf
    (h₁ : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (R : Presieve X), R ∈ K X → ∀ x : u.obj X,
      ∃ (Y : C) (f : Y ⟶ X) (_ : R f) (y : u.obj Y), u.map f y = x)
    (h₂ : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (R : Presieve X), R ∈ K X → ∀ ⦃Y Z : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X), R f →
      ∀ (g : Z ⟶ X) [HasPullback f g], Function.Bijective (pullbackComparison u f g))
    (M : TopCat.{w}) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf K.toGrothendieck (mappingPresheaf u M)
declarations.comment: point_mapping_sheaf

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.TopologicalSheaf.isIso_elementColimit_map_toSheafify_topCat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI4** (sheafification commutes with taking stalks at a point). Let `p` be a point
of the site `C` given by a functor `u : C ⥤ Sets` (Stacks 00Y5), and let `F` be a presheaf of
topological spaces on `C`. Then the canonical map `F_p ⟶ (F^#)_p` is an isomorphism of
topological spaces, where `F_p = colim_{(U, x) ∈ Nbh(p)ᵒᵖ} F(U)` is the colimit in `TopCat`
(`CategoryTheory.elementColimit`) and `F^#` is the sheafification of `hasWeakSheafify_topCat`.

The site is the small category `C` with the topology generated by a precoverage `K` that has
the fibre products of its coverings and is stable under base change, and `h₁`, `h₂` are
conditions (1) and (2) of Stacks 00Y5 for `u`; condition (3) is not needed. No cofilteredness
of the category of neighbourhoods is assumed, so this does not go through Mathlib's
`GrothendieckTopology.Point`. The general form, for any category with products, colimits and
sheafification, is `CategoryTheory.ElementColimit.isIso_elementColimit_map_toSheafify`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_elementColimit_map_toSheafify_topCat
    (h₁ : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (R : Presieve X), R ∈ K X → ∀ x : u.obj X,
      ∃ (Y : C) (f : Y ⟶ X) (_ : R f) (y : u.obj Y), u.map f y = x)
    (h₂ : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄ (R : Presieve X), R ∈ K X → ∀ ⦃Y Z : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X), R f →
      ∀ (g : Z ⟶ X) [HasPullback f g], Function.Bijective (pullbackComparison u f g))
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ TopCat.{w}) :
    IsIso ((elementColimit u TopCat.{w}).map (toSheafify K.toGrothendieck F))
declarations.comment: stalk_preservation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
An *affine formal algebraic space* over `S` is an fppf sheaf on the big fppf site of `S`
which satisfies the set-theoretic condition
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition` and which is the colimit of a
directed diagram of affine schemes over `S` all of whose transition morphisms are thickenings.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
An *affine formal algebraic space* over `S` is a sheaf on the big fppf site of `S` which
satisfies the set-theoretic condition and is a directed colimit of sheaves represented by affine
schemes whose transition morphisms are thickenings.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.diagonal_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
The diagonal of an affine formal algebraic space is representable and a
closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem diagonal_isClosedImmersion
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type (u + 1)} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS)
    (hD : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
      Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening
        ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f)))
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (e : colimit
      (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
        Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
          (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) ≅ X) :
    (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) (diag X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relativelyRepresentable_colimitι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI9.** A stage of a directed presentation of an affine formal algebraic space by
affine schemes with thickening transition morphisms maps representably to the colimit: every
base change of `X_i ⟶ X` along a morphism from a represented sheaf is again represented by an
object of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyRepresentable_colimitι (i : I) :
    (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable
      (colimit.ι
        (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
          Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) i ≫ e.hom)
declarations.comment: representability

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isThickening_colimitι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AI9.** A stage of a directed presentation of an affine formal algebraic space by
affine schemes with thickening transition morphisms maps to the colimit by a thickening: the
map `X_i ⟶ X` is representable, and each of its base changes along a represented sheaf is a
thickening of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_colimitι (i : I) :
    (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (colimit.ι
        (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
          Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) i ≫ e.hom)
declarations.comment: thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_factor_through_thickening'
declarations.doc:
A morphism from a quasi-compact algebraic space to a presented affine formal
algebraic space factors through one of its affine stages.

Two of the hypotheses of Stacks 0AIA are not asked for, because the argument does not use them.
Of the target, only the presentation `D`, `hD`, `e` is used, so the set-theoretic condition of
Stacks 0AIS -- the other half of being an affine formal algebraic space, and for a formal
spectrum a condition on the size of the site -- is not assumed. Of the transition morphisms of
the presentation, only that they are closed immersions is used, not that they are thickenings:
surjectivity plays no part. The index of the presentation may lie in any universe, provided it
is `u + 1`-small, the colimit being taken in sheaves of `Type (u + 1)`. Of the source, only the
surjective étale cover by a quasi-compact scheme that quasi-compactness provides is used, so `Y`
is not assumed to be an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factor_through_thickening'
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (I : Type w₁) [Preorder I] [Small.{u + 1} I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS)
    (hD : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (g : i ⟶ j),
      IsClosedImmersion ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map g)))
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (e : X ≅ colimit
      (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
        Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)))
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hYqc : Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : (presheafToSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
      (Type (u + 1))).obj (Y ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}) ⟶ X) :
    ∃ i : I, ∃ g : (presheafToSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
        (Type (u + 1))).obj (Y ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}) ⟶
        (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
          ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (D.obj i)),
      g ≫ colimit.ι
      (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
        Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) i ≫
        e.inv = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIB.** A sheaf on the big fppf site of `S` is an affine formal algebraic space if
and only if every morphism to it from a sheaf represented by an affine scheme over `S` factors
through a morphism from an affine scheme over `S` which is representable and a thickening, and
the sheaf satisfies the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_iff
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X ↔
      ((∀ U : BigAffineFppf B S hS,
          ∀ f : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
            (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
              ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj U) ⟶ X,
          ∃ T : BigAffineFppf B S hS,
            ∃ g : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
              (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
                ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj U) ⟶
              (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
                  ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj T),
            ∃ h : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
              (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
                ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj T) ⟶ X,
              (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable h ∧
              (MorphismProperty.relative
                (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                  (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
                (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
                  (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
                  (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) h ∧
              g ≫ h = f) ∧
        SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isPresentingRing_of_hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (2) implies condition (1).** If some morphism from an affine formal
algebraic space `X` to an affine scheme turns every closed immersion of an affine scheme
into `X` into a closed immersion, then `X` is presented by a weakly admissible topological ring:
the inverse limit of the section rings of any presentation of `X` by affine thickenings.

The stage rings are quotients of the sections of the given affine scheme, so that inverse limit
is a ring in the universe of the schemes; its projections to the stage rings are surjective, and
their kernels are weak ideals of definition forming a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of
`0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPresentingRing_of_hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A)
      (_ : IsLinearTopology A A), IsPresentingRing B S hS A X
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isPresentingRing_of_hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (3) implies condition (1).** The criterion for closed immersions of
arbitrary schemes restricts to affine schemes, and then condition (2) gives condition (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPresentingRing_of_hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A)
      (_ : IsLinearTopology A A), IsPresentingRing B S hS A X
declarations.comment: (3) implies (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion.hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (2) implies condition (3).** If some morphism from `X` to an affine
scheme over `S` turns every closed immersion of an *affine* scheme into `X` into a closed
immersion of schemes, then it does so for every *scheme* of the site: a scheme closed-immersed in
an affine formal algebraic space is already affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion.hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion B S hS X) :
    HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion B S hS X
declarations.comment: part (2) implies part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion.hasAllSurjectivePresentations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (2) implies condition (5).** Condition (2) is read on every
presentation of `X` by affine thickenings at once, which is condition (5).
declarations.statement:
theorem HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion.hasAllSurjectivePresentations
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion B S hS X) :
    HasAllSurjectivePresentations B S hS X
declarations.comment: part (2) implies part (5), and with it part (2) implies part (4). No hypothesis beyond condition (2) is carried. What remains open in this tag is the implication (4) implies (1) for a presentation indexed by an arbitrary directed type in Type (u + 1): the ring it asks for is the limit of the section rings of the presentation, which then lies in Type (u + 1) rather than Type u, so a smallness argument on the index is needed that this development does not have. The sequential case is exists_quotientSystem_formalSpectrum_iso and the countably indexed case is isPresentingRing_of_isCountablyIndexed. The implication (1) implies (2) is open for the reason recorded in the implementation notes above: conditions (2) and (3) ask for an affine scheme over S, and the ring of a presentation carries structure morphisms only on its quotients

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (2) implies condition (4).** The presentation by affine thickenings
that affineness of `X` supplies has surjective section-ring projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion B S hS X) :
    HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X
declarations.comment: part (2) implies part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (3) implies condition (4).** The criterion for all schemes
of the site restricts to the affine ones, which is already enough.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion B S hS X) :
    HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X
declarations.comment: part (3) implies part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasAllSurjectivePresentations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (2) implies condition (5).** If some morphism from `X` to an affine
scheme turns every closed immersion of an affine scheme into `X` into a closed immersion, then
every presentation of `X` by affine thickenings has surjective section-ring projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasAllSurjectivePresentations
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X) :
    HasAllSurjectivePresentations B S hS X
declarations.comment: (2) implies (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasAllSurjectivePresentations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (3) implies condition (5).** The criterion for closed immersions of
arbitrary schemes restricts to affine schemes, and then condition (2) gives condition (5).
declarations.statement:
theorem HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasAllSurjectivePresentations
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X) :
    HasAllSurjectivePresentations B S hS X
declarations.comment: (3) implies (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (3) implies condition (4).** Every presentation of `X` by affine
thickenings has surjective section-ring projections, and `X` has one.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X) :
    HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X
declarations.comment: (3) implies (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (2) implies condition (3)**, for the conditions with the morphism
to `Spec A` recorded as a `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.MapToScheme`. If some morphism from `X`
to an affine scheme turns every closed immersion of an *affine* scheme into `X` into a closed
immersion of schemes, then it does so for every *scheme* of the site: a scheme closed-immersed in
an affine formal algebraic space is already affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X) :
    HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X
declarations.comment: part (2) implies part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (3) implies condition (2)**, for the conditions with the morphism
to `Spec A` recorded as a `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.MapToScheme`. The affine schemes of the
site are among its schemes, so the criterion for all schemes restricts to them.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec.hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X) :
    HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X
declarations.comment: (3) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_continuous_ringEquiv_sections_of_weakIdealColimitPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, the concluding clause.** If `X` is the colimit of the spectra of the
quotients of a weakly admissible topological ring `A` by its weak ideals of definition, then for
*any* presentation `X = colim Xᵢ` of `X` by affine thickenings the ring `A` is the inverse limit
`lim Γ(Xᵢ, 𝒪)` of the section rings of that presentation, *as a topological ring*: the comparison
map is an isomorphism of rings which is a homeomorphism for the limit topology of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.topologicalSpaceSections`.

Reduction modulo the weak ideals of definition `Jᵢ` cut out by the stages is the comparison
homomorphism; it is injective because those ideals are cofinal and `A` is separated, surjective
because `A` is complete, continuous because each `Jᵢ` is open, and open because the `Jᵢ` are
cofinal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_continuous_ringEquiv_sections_of_weakIdealColimitPresentation
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (P : WeakIdealColimitPresentation B S hS A X)
    (I : Type (u + 1)) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS)
    (hD : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
      Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f)))
    (eD : X ≅ colimit (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
      Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))) :
    ∃ e : A ≃+* (sectionDiagram B S hS D ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}).sections,
      Continuous e ∧ Continuous e.symm
declarations.comment: the associated ring is A = lim Γ(X_λ, 𝒪), with its limit topology, for an arbitrary presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_continuous_ringEquiv_of_isPresentingRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC: the presenting ring of a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space is unique
up to isomorphism of topological rings.** If the weakly admissible topological rings `A` and
`C` over `S` both present the affine formal algebraic space `X` — each exhibiting `X` as the
colimit of the spectra of its quotients by weak ideals of definition — then `A` and `C` are
isomorphic as topological rings.
declarations.comment: the associated ring of a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space is well defined: two rings presenting one affine formal algebraic space are isomorphic as topological rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.SequentialQuotients.exists_quotientSystem_formalSpectrum_iso
declarations.doc:
A sheaf presented as the colimit of a sequence of affine thickenings whose section rings are
the quotients of a linearly topologized ring `A` by a fundamental system of weak ideals of
definition is the formal spectrum of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quotientSystem_formalSpectrum_iso :
    ∃ Q : QuotientSystem B S hS A, Nonempty (X ≅ formalSpectrum Q)
declarations.comment: (4) implies (1), for a sequential presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.SequentialQuotients.exists_quotientSystem_formalSpectrum_iso'
declarations.doc:
A sheaf presented as the colimit of a sequence of affine thickenings whose section rings are
the quotients of a linearly topologized ring `A` by a fundamental system of weak ideals of
definition is the formal spectrum of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quotientSystem_formalSpectrum_iso' (P : SequentialQuotients B S hS X A) :
    ∃ Q : QuotientSystem B S hS A, Nonempty (X ≅ formalSpectrum Q)
declarations.comment: (4) implies (1), for a sequential presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasSomeSurjectivePresentation.hasAllSurjectivePresentations
declarations.doc:
If *some* presentation of an affine formal algebraic space by affine thickenings has all its
section-ring projections surjective, then *every* such presentation does.
declarations.statement:
public theorem HasSomeSurjectivePresentation.hasAllSurjectivePresentations
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X) :
    HasAllSurjectivePresentations B S hS X
declarations.comment: part (4) implies part (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isPresentingRing_of_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (4) implies condition (1).** An affine formal algebraic space with a
presentation by affine thickenings whose section-ring projections are surjective is presented by
a weakly admissible topological ring, namely the inverse limit of the section rings of that
presentation.

The presentation has only `u`-many stages up to isomorphism over `X`, so a polynomial ring on the
sections of a `u`-small cofinal family of stages surjects compatibly onto every stage ring; the
weakly admissible completion of that polynomial ring is the presenting ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPresentingRing_of_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A)
      (_ : IsLinearTopology A A), IsPresentingRing B S hS A X
declarations.comment: (4) implies (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isPresentingRing_of_hasAllSurjectivePresentations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (5) implies condition (1).** A presentation whose section-ring
projections are all surjective exists as soon as every presentation has that property.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPresentingRing_of_hasAllSurjectivePresentations
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasAllSurjectivePresentations B S hS X) :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A)
      (_ : IsLinearTopology A A), IsPresentingRing B S hS A X
declarations.comment: (5) implies (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_iff_exists_isPresentingRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, conditions (1), (4) and (5) are equivalent.** For an fppf sheaf satisfying the
set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS, being presented by a weakly admissible topological ring
is the same as having one presentation by affine thickenings with surjective section-ring
projections, and the same as having that property for every presentation. This is the form a
consumer wants: McQuillan's condition and the existence of the presenting ring may be exchanged
freely, with no ring and no structure morphism given in advance.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_iff_exists_isPresentingRing
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X) :
    HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X ↔
      ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A)
        (_ : IsLinearTopology A A), IsPresentingRing B S hS A X
declarations.comment: (1), (4) and (5) are equivalent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAllSurjectivePresentations_iff_exists_isPresentingRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, conditions (4) and (5) are equivalent to condition (1).** The statement above
for the "every presentation" form of McQuillan's condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAllSurjectivePresentations_iff_exists_isPresentingRing
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X) :
    HasAllSurjectivePresentations B S hS X ↔
      ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A)
        (_ : IsLinearTopology A A), IsPresentingRing B S hS A X
declarations.comment: (1), (4) and (5) are equivalent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isThickening_quotient
declarations.doc: Every weak ideal of definition gives a thickening of the formal space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isThickening_quotient
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (J : WeakIdeals A) :
    (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (quotientMap B S hS A X P J)
declarations.comment: thickening_classification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relativelyRepresentable_quotient
declarations.doc:
Every weak ideal of definition gives a representable morphism from its
quotient scheme to the formal space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativelyRepresentable_quotient
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (J : WeakIdeals A) :
    (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable
      (quotientMap B S hS A X P J)
declarations.comment: thickening_classification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.existsUnique_weakIdeal_quotient
declarations.doc:
Any representable thickening from a scheme into the formal space is,
uniquely up to its weak ideal, a quotient stage of the canonical presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_weakIdeal_quotient
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj T ⟶ X)
    (_hf_repr : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hf_thick : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f) :
    ∃! J : WeakIdeals A,
      ∃ e : T ≅ (BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (P.diagram.obj J),
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
          (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map e.hom ≫
          quotientMap B S hS A X P J = f
declarations.comment: thickening_classification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.inducedSectionHom
declarations.doc:
The homomorphism on global sections induced by a representable thickening
into the formal space. The uniqueness and compatibility statements below show
that this construction does not depend on the chosen quotient description.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def inducedSectionHom
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj T ⟶ X)
    (hf_repr : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hf_thick : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f) :
    A →+* Γ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T, ⊤)
declarations.comment: thickening_classification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.inducedSectionHom_quotient
declarations.doc:
At every quotient description compatible with the morphism to the formal
space, the induced map on sections is the canonical quotient map followed by
the affine global-sections isomorphism and transport to `T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem inducedSectionHom_quotient
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj T ⟶ X)
    (hf_repr : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hf_thick : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (J : WeakIdeals A)
    (e : T ≅ (BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (P.diagram.obj J))
    (he : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map e.hom ≫
        quotientMap B S hS A X P J = f) :
    inducedSectionHom B S hS A X P hA T f hf_repr hf_thick =
      sectionHomOfQuotientIso B S hS A X P J T e
declarations.comment: thickening_classification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.quotient_ker_sections
declarations.doc:
The classifying ideal of a representable thickening is the kernel of the
homomorphism from the associated ring to its global sections.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quotient_ker_sections
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (T : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj T ⟶ X)
    (hf_repr : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable f)
    (hf_thick : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (J : WeakIdeals A)
    (e : T ≅ (BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (P.diagram.obj J))
    (he : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
      (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map e.hom ≫
        quotientMap B S hS A X P J = f) :
    RingHom.ker (inducedSectionHom B S hS A X P hA T f hf_repr hf_thick) = J.1
declarations.comment: thickening_classification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_toSpec_of_weakIdealColimitPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (1) implies condition (2).** Let `A` be a weakly admissible
topological ring and let the fppf sheaf `X`, satisfying the set-theoretic condition of
Stacks 0AIS, be the colimit of the spectra of the quotients of `A` by its weak ideals of
definition. Then `X` is an affine formal algebraic space, and every closed immersion of an
affine scheme `T` of the site into `X` factors through the spectrum of a quotient `A ⧸ K` in
such a way that the resulting morphism `T ⟶ Spec A` — which is the composition of `T ⟶ X` with
the canonical `X ⟶ Spec A` — is a closed immersion of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_toSpec_of_weakIdealColimitPresentation
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X)
    (P : WeakIdealColimitPresentation B S hS A X) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X ∧
      ∀ (T : BigAffineFppf B S hS)
        (g : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
            ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj T) ⟶ X),
        IsClosedImmersionInto B S hS g →
        ∃ (K : WeakIdeals A) (c : T ⟶ P.diagram.obj K),
          (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map
              ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).map c) ≫
            colimit.ι (P.diagram ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
              Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) K ≫ P.colimitIso.inv = g ∧
          IsClosedImmersion ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map c ≫
            (P.quotientIso K).hom ≫
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk K.1)))
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion_of_weakIdealColimitPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (1) implies condition (2).** Let `A` be a weakly admissible
topological ring and let the fppf sheaf `X`, satisfying the set-theoretic condition of
Stacks 0AIS, be the colimit of the spectra of the quotients of `A` by its weak ideals of
definition. Then `X` is an affine formal algebraic space, and there are a ring and a morphism of
sheaves from `X` to its spectrum such that every closed immersion of an affine scheme of the
site into `X` composes to a closed immersion of schemes; the witnesses are `A` itself and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.weakIdealToSpecPoints`.

This is the library's `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec`:
the morphism to `Spec A` is given at every object of the site, not only at those carrying a closed
immersion into `X`. The implication is unconditional — no morphism `Spec A ⟶ S` and no
compatibility with the structure morphisms of the stages is assumed — because condition (2),
like the source's, asks for none.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion_of_weakIdealColimitPresentation
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X)
    (P : WeakIdealColimitPresentation B S hS A X) :
    HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion_of_weakIdealColimitPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (1) implies condition (3).** Condition (1) gives condition (2), and
a scheme closed-immersed in an affine formal algebraic space is affine, so the criterion extends
from the affine schemes of the site to all of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion_of_weakIdealColimitPresentation
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X)
    (P : WeakIdealColimitPresentation B S hS A X) :
    HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X
declarations.comment: (1) implies (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion_of_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (4) implies condition (2).** An affine formal algebraic space with
*some* presentation by affine thickenings whose section-ring projections are surjective admits a
ring `A` and a morphism `X ⟶ Spec A` through which every closed immersion of an affine scheme of
the site into `X` composes to a closed immersion of schemes.

The ring is the one condition (4) produces, namely the inverse limit of the section rings of the
presentation, and the morphism is the global family built above. No structure morphism
`Spec A ⟶ S` is involved anywhere, which is what makes this arrow available: that limit carries
none, so a condition (2) demanding one would have no arrow out of condition (4).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion_of_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X) :
    HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X
declarations.comment: (4) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion_of_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (4) implies condition (3).** Condition (4) gives condition (2), and
a scheme closed-immersed in an affine formal algebraic space is affine, so the criterion extends
from the affine schemes of the site to all of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterion_of_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X) :
    HasSchemeClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X
declarations.comment: (4) implies (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion_of_hasAllSurjectivePresentations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, condition (5) implies condition (2).** Condition (5) gives condition (4) by
instantiating its quantifier at the presentation an affine formal algebraic space comes with,
and condition (4) gives condition (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffineClosedImmersionCriterion_of_hasAllSurjectivePresentations
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : HasAllSurjectivePresentations B S hS X) :
    HasAffineClosedImmersionCriterionMapToSpec B S hS X
declarations.comment: (5) implies (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAllSurjectivePresentations_of_exists_weaklyAdmissible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIC, (1) ⇒ (5).** Condition (1) of Stacks 0AIC — the existence of a weakly
admissible topological ring over `S` presenting `X` as the colimit of the spectra of its
quotients by weak ideals of definition — implies condition (5): `X` is an affine formal
algebraic space and *every* presentation of it by affine thickenings has surjective section-ring
projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAllSurjectivePresentations_of_exists_weaklyAdmissible
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X)
    (h : ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A)
        (_ : IsTopologicalRing A) (_ : IsLinearTopology A A),
      letI : CommRing A := ‹CommRing A›
      letI : TopologicalSpace A := ‹TopologicalSpace A›
      letI : IsTopologicalRing A := ‹IsTopologicalRing A›
      letI : IsLinearTopology A A := ‹IsLinearTopology A A›
      TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A ∧
        Nonempty (WeakIdealColimitPresentation B S hS A X)) :
    HasAllSurjectivePresentations B S hS X
declarations.comment: (1) implies (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsClassical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AID (1).** A McQuillan affine formal algebraic space is *classical* when its
associated weakly admissible topological ring is admissible, that is has an ideal of
definition and is complete.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsClassical (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: classical

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsWeaklyAdic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AID (2).** A McQuillan affine formal algebraic space is *weakly adic* when its
associated weakly admissible topological ring is weakly adic, that is the closed powers of a
single ideal form a fundamental system of open ideals.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsWeaklyAdic (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: weakly adic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsAdic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AID (3).** A McQuillan affine formal algebraic space is *adic* when its
associated weakly admissible topological ring is adic, that is its topology is the adic
topology of an ideal of definition and it is complete.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdic (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: adic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsAdicStar
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AID (4).** A McQuillan affine formal algebraic space is *adic\** when its
associated weakly admissible topological ring is adic and moreover has a finitely generated
ideal of definition.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdicStar (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: adic star

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AID (5).** A McQuillan affine formal algebraic space is *Noetherian* when its
associated weakly admissible topological ring is both a Noetherian ring and adic.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsNoetherian (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: Noetherian

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasSomeSurjectivePresentation
registrations.comment: McQuillan

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap_app_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE**, the affine case of the colimit formula. The comparison map
`colim h_{Spec (A/I)} → h_{Spf A}` is surjective on the points over an affine scheme: such a
point factors through one of the quotients by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_factor_spfQuotientPointOn`.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap_app_of_isAffine (hA : IsAdmissible A)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine T] :
    Function.Surjective ((spfQuotientPointsColimitMap A hA).app (op T))
declarations.comment: the comparison map of the colimit formula is surjective at an affine test scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap_of_isAdmissible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE**, the colimit formula, with no hypothesis beyond admissibility: the
comparison map `colim h_{Spec (A/I)} → h_{Spf A}` is locally surjective for the Zariski
topology. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyInjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap` this is the source's
`h_{Spf A} = colim h_{Spec (A/I)}`, read — as it must be — as an isomorphism of the associated
sheaves.

This discharges the hypothesis of
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap`, which was the affine case,
i.e. the surjectivity half of Stacks 0AHZ.
declarations.comment: the comparison map of the colimit formula is locally surjective, with no hypothesis beyond admissibility

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.spfQuotientPointsColimitMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE.** The comparison map of the source's colimit formula
`h_{Spf A} = colim h_{Spec (A/I)}`: the morphism out of the colimit of the functors of points of
the quotient spectra determined by the morphisms `Spec (A/I) → Spf A`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spfQuotientPointsColimitMap [IsLinearTopology A A] (hA : IsAdmissible A) :
    colimit (spfQuotientPointsDiagram A) ⟶ formalSchemePoints (spfFormalScheme A hA)
declarations.comment: the comparison map h_colim → h_Spf A of the colimit formula

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap_app
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE.** The comparison map of the colimit formula is injective on the points over
every scheme: two morphisms `T → Spec (A/I)` and `T → Spec (A/J)` inducing the same point of
`Spf A` already agree over `Spec (A/(I ∩ J))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap_app [IsLinearTopology A A] (hA : IsAdmissible A)
    (T : Scheme.{u}) :
    Function.Injective ((spfQuotientPointsColimitMap A hA).app (op T))
declarations.comment: the comparison map of the colimit formula is injective at every test scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mono_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE.** The colimit of the functors of points of the quotient spectra is a
subfunctor of the functor of points of `Spf A`: the comparison map is a monomorphism of
presheaves, being injective on the points over every scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap [IsLinearTopology A A] (hA : IsAdmissible A) :
    Mono (spfQuotientPointsColimitMap A hA)
declarations.comment: the comparison map of the colimit formula is a monomorphism of presheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyInjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE.** The comparison map of the colimit formula is locally injective for the
Zariski topology on schemes, being injective on the points over every scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyInjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : IsAdmissible A) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u}
      (spfQuotientPointsColimitMap A hA)
declarations.comment: the comparison map of the colimit formula is locally injective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE.** The reduction of the colimit formula to the affine case. If every point of
`Spf A` over an affine scheme factors through one of the quotients `Spec (A/I)`, then the
comparison map of the colimit formula is locally surjective for the Zariski topology, because
every scheme has an affine open cover.

The hypothesis is the surjectivity half of the identification
`Mor(Spec B, Spf A) = Hom_cont(A, Γ(Spec B, 𝒪))` of Stacks 0AHZ. It is proved in
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_factor_spfQuotientPointOn`, so the conclusion holds with no hypothesis
beyond admissibility; that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap_of_isAdmissible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallySurjective_spfQuotientPointsColimitMap [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : IsAdmissible A)
    (haff : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}, IsAffine T →
      Function.Surjective ((spfQuotientPointsColimitMap A hA).app (op T))) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u}
      (spfQuotientPointsColimitMap A hA)
declarations.comment: the colimit formula is locally surjective, assuming its affine case (the surjectivity half of Stacks 0AHZ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClassical_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf_of_contains
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE.** Over a terminal base, the functor of points of an affine formal scheme
`Spf A` is a classical affine formal algebraic space as soon as the coproduct of the schemes
`Spec (A/I)`, over the ideals of definition of `A`, belongs to the big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClassical_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf_of_contains (hterm : IsTerminal S)
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdmissible A) {X : FormalScheme.{u}} (e : X ≅ spfFormalScheme A hA)
    (hB : B.Contains (∐ fun I : IdealsOfDefinition A => Spec (spfQuotient A I))) :
    IsClassical B S hS (formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf B S hS X)
declarations.comment: if the coproduct of the Spec(A/I) over the ideals of definition belongs to the site, then h_X is a classical affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf_of_contains
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE.** Over a terminal base, the functor of points of an affine formal scheme
`Spf A` is an affine formal algebraic space as soon as the coproduct of the schemes
`Spec (A/I)`, over the ideals of definition of `A`, belongs to the big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf_of_contains
    (hterm : IsTerminal S) (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdmissible A) {X : FormalScheme.{u}}
    (e : X ≅ spfFormalScheme A hA)
    (hB : B.Contains (∐ fun I : IdealsOfDefinition A => Spec (spfQuotient A I))) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf B S hS X)
declarations.comment: if the coproduct of the Spec(A/I) over the ideals of definition belongs to the site, then h_X is an affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isEquivalence_smallAffineFormalSchemePointsFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE**, the equivalence. Over a terminal base `S` (the source's `Spec(ℤ)`), the
functor of points `𝔛 ↦ h_𝔛` is an equivalence from the category of affine formal schemes
`Spf A` whose coproduct `∐_I Spec (A/I)` belongs to the big fppf site `B` (the source's
"compatible choices of big site") to the category of classical affine formal algebraic spaces
over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_smallAffineFormalSchemePointsFunctor (hterm : IsTerminal S) :
    (smallAffineFormalSchemePointsFunctor B S hS hterm).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the category of affine formal schemes is equivalent to the category of classical affine formal algebraic spaces, by the functor of points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClassical_iff_exists_admissible_quotientSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE, the objects.** An fppf sheaf over `S` satisfying the set-theoretic condition
of Stacks 0AIS is a *classical* affine formal algebraic space in the sense of Stacks 0AID (1)
exactly when it is isomorphic to the formal spectrum of Stacks 0AIF of an admissible topological
ring over `S`.

This is the object half of the correspondence the source's remark describes, read on the
formal-space side of the bridge: the classical affine formal algebraic spaces are the `Spf A`
