for `A` admissible, and nothing else. Both directions hold, with no hypothesis beyond the
set-theoretic condition, which the left-hand side implies.

The correspondence with affine formal *schemes*, and the equivalence of categories the source
concludes with, need in addition the identification of the formal spectrum with the functor of
points of `Spf A` and the full faithfulness of Stacks 0AI1; see the implementation notes of
this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClassical_iff_exists_admissible_quotientSystem {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X) :
    IsClassical B S hS X ↔
      ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A)
        (_ : IsLinearTopology A A),
        TopologicalRing.IsAdmissible A ∧
          ∃ D : QuotientSystem B S hS A, Nonempty (X ≅ formalSpectrum D)
declarations.comment: the objects: a sheaf is a classical affine formal algebraic space exactly when it is the formal spectrum of an admissible topological ring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.final_idealOfDefinitionIndex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE**, the index reconciliation. In a pre-admissible topological ring the ideals of
definition are cofinal below the weak ideals of definition — the intersection of a weak ideal of
definition with an ideal of definition is an ideal of definition — so the functor they induce on
index categories is final, and colimits may be computed over either index.

This is what reconciles the colimit of Stacks 0AIE, taken over the ideals of definition of an
admissible ring, with the formal spectrum of Stacks 0AIF, taken over the weak ideals of
definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem final_idealOfDefinitionIndex (hA : TopologicalRing.IsPreAdmissible A) :
    (idealOfDefinitionIndex A).monotone.functor.Final
declarations.comment: the ideals of definition are cofinal among the weak ideals of definition, so the colimit of the remark and the formal spectrum of Stacks 0AIF have the same index

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.QuotientSystem.formalSpectrumIsoIdealOfDefinitionColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE**, the colimit of the remark. The colimit of the represented quotient spectra
over the *ideals of definition* of a pre-admissible topological ring is the formal spectrum of
Stacks 0AIF, whose colimit runs over the *weak* ideals of definition. The two indices have the
same colimit by `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.final_idealOfDefinitionIndex`.
declarations.statement:
def QuotientSystem.formalSpectrumIsoIdealOfDefinitionColimit
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsPreAdmissible A) (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) :
    colimit D.idealOfDefinitionDiagram ≅ formalSpectrum D
declarations.comment: the colimit over the ideals of definition is the formal spectrum of Stacks 0AIF

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isIso_spfFormalSchemeFppfComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE, the colimit formula.** The comparison morphism from the formal spectrum of an
admissible topological ring `A` over a terminal base to the functor of points of the affine
formal scheme `Spf A` is an isomorphism of fppf sheaves over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_spfFormalSchemeFppfComparison (hterm : IsTerminal S)
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdmissible A) (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) :
    IsIso (spfFormalSchemeFppfComparison hA D)
declarations.comment: h_{Spf A} = colim h_{Spec (A/I)} as fppf sheaves: the comparison morphism from the formal spectrum to the functor of points of the affine formal scheme is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClassical_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE, the type of the functor of points.** The functor of points of the affine
formal scheme `Spf A` of an admissible topological ring `A` over a terminal base is a
*classical* affine formal algebraic space over `S` in the sense of Stacks 0AID (1).

Nothing is assumed beyond admissibility of `A` and the source's own size conditions: that the
quotient spectra lie in the chosen big fppf site, which is part of the datum of a quotient
system, and that their coproduct does, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.QuotientSystem.HasLargeSite`. The fppf sheaf condition on the
functor of points is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints_formalScheme`
and the identification with the formal spectrum is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isIso_spfFormalSchemeFppfComparison`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClassical_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf (hterm : IsTerminal S)
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdmissible A) (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A)
    (hB : D.HasLargeSite) :
    IsClassical B S hS (formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf B S hS (spfFormalScheme A hA))
declarations.comment: the functor of points of an affine formal scheme over a terminal base is a classical affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE.** The functor of points of an affine formal scheme over a terminal base is an
affine formal algebraic space over `S`; it is the affineness half of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClassical_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf (hterm : IsTerminal S)
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdmissible A) (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A)
    (hB : D.HasLargeSite) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf B S hS (spfFormalScheme A hA))
declarations.comment: the functor of points of an affine formal scheme over a terminal base is an affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClassical_formalSpectrum
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIE.** Let `A` be an admissible topological ring over `S`. If the coproduct of the
spectra of the quotients of `A` by its weak ideals of definition lies in the chosen big fppf
site, then the formal spectrum `Spf A` is a *classical* affine formal algebraic space over `S`
in the sense of Stacks 0AID (1).

This is the second conclusion of the source's remark, for the object its colimit formula
produces. The size hypothesis is the source's own: the source needs the coproduct of the
quotient spectra to lie in the chosen big fppf site, which is what supplies the representable
atlas demanded by the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS. The source's colimit runs over the
ideals of definition of `A` and this one over its weak ideals of definition; the two agree,
because in a pre-admissible ring the ideals of definition are cofinal below the weak ideals of
definition (`TopologicalRing.exists_isIdealOfDefinition_le_of_isWeakIdealOfDefinition`).

Only this direction holds: see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClassical_formalSpectrum (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdmissible A)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (hB : D.HasLargeSite) :
    IsClassical B S hS (formalSpectrum D)
declarations.comment: the formal spectrum of an admissible topological ring is a classical affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalSpectrum
declarations.doc:
The formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological ring over `S`: the
fppf-sheaf colimit of its quotient spectra by weak ideals of definition.
declarations.statement:
public def formalSpectrum (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) :
    Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSpectrum
declarations.doc: The formal spectrum is affine as a formal algebraic space over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSpectrum
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (hB : D.HasLargeSite) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (formalSpectrum D)
declarations.comment: affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.existsUnique_formalSpectrumMap
declarations.doc:
The map of formal spectra is uniquely characterized by its effect on every
quotient stage. This is the universal-property construction of `Spf(f)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_formalSpectrumMap
    {D : QuotientSystem B S hS A} {E : QuotientSystem B S hS C}
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (f : ContinuousHom D E) :
    ∃! φ : formalSpectrum E ⟶ formalSpectrum D,
      ∀ (J : { I : Ideal A // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I })
        (K : { I : Ideal C // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I })
        (h : J.1 ≤ Ideal.comap f.toRingHom K.1),
        formalSpectrumInclusion E (OrderDual.toDual K) ≫ φ =
          (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
            (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map
              ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).map
                (f.stageMap J K h)) ≫
        formalSpectrumInclusion D (OrderDual.toDual J)
declarations.comment: quotient-stage characterization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalSpectrumMap
declarations.doc: The canonical contravariant map on formal spectra.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def formalSpectrumMap
    {D : QuotientSystem B S hS A} {E : QuotientSystem B S hS C}
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (f : ContinuousHom D E) : formalSpectrum E ⟶ formalSpectrum D
declarations.comment: functorial map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalSpectrumMap_id
declarations.doc: The formal-spectrum map of the identity homomorphism is the identity.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formalSpectrumMap_id
    {D : QuotientSystem B S hS A}
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (f : ContinuousHom D D) (hf : f.toRingHom = RingHom.id A) :
    formalSpectrumMap hA f = 𝟙 (formalSpectrum D)
declarations.comment: identity law

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalSpectrumMap_comp
declarations.doc: Formal spectrum reverses composition of continuous maps over the base.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formalSpectrumMap_comp
    {D : QuotientSystem B S hS A} {E : QuotientSystem B S hS C}
    {G : Type u} [CommRing G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    {F : QuotientSystem B S hS G}
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [IsTopologicalRing C] [IsLinearTopology C C]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
    (f : ContinuousHom D E) (g : ContinuousHom E F)
    (gf : ContinuousHom D F)
    (hgf : gf.toRingHom = g.toRingHom.comp f.toRingHom) :
    formalSpectrumMap hC g ≫ formalSpectrumMap hA f =
      formalSpectrumMap hA gf
declarations.comment: composition law

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalSpectrumMap_comp_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIF.** The formal spectrum turns `ContinuousHom.comp` into composition of
morphisms of formal spectra, in the direction that reverses the order.
declarations.statement:
theorem formalSpectrumMap_comp_eq (hw₂ : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A₂)
    (hw₃ : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A₃)
    (q : ContinuousHom D₂ D₁) (r : ContinuousHom D₃ D₂) :
    formalSpectrumMap hw₂ q ≫ formalSpectrumMap hw₃ r =
      formalSpectrumMap hw₃ (ContinuousHom.comp hw₂ hw₃ q r)
declarations.comment: composition law for the composite continuous hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relativelyRepresentable_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B` and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`. If `X` is an affine
formal algebraic space and `f` is representable by algebraic spaces and locally quasi-finite,
then `f` is representable by schemes.

`X` is a sheaf of `Type u`, the universe of the schemes, and the hypothesis that it is an
affine formal algebraic space is imposed on the sheaf obtained from it by lifting its values
one universe up. Local quasi-finiteness of a morphism which is only representable by
algebraic spaces is the assertion that each of its base changes along a scheme-valued point
of the target, an algebraic space over `S`, is locally quasi-finite over that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyRepresentable_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type u))
    (Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (f : X.1 ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      ((presheafToSheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))).obj
        (X.1 ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u})))
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f)
    (hlqf : ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ξ : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y),
      Space.IsLocallyQuasiFinite B S hS (pullback.fst ξ f)) :
    yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relativelyRepresentable_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpaceULift
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B`, let `X` be an affine formal algebraic
space over `S` and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism to a presheaf of `Type (u + 1)` on the big fppf
site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces and whose represented base changes are
locally quasi-finite. Then `f` is representable by objects of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyRepresentable_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpaceULift
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} {Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1)} (f : X.obj ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f)
    (hlqf : ∀ (T : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ξ : uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj T ⟶ Y),
      Space.HoldsOnEveryEtaleChartULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        ((@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊓
          (@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}))
        (pullback.fst ξ f)) :
    uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.relativelyRepresentable f
declarations.comment: the tag read at the value universe Type (u+1), where a formal algebraic space and the affine formal algebraic spaces of its atlas of Definition 0AIM live, so that the tag applies to an atlas member. Nothing is assumed beyond the Type u reading: the smallness that one asks of its affine formal algebraic space is supplied by the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS, which an affine formal algebraic space carries, and the smallness of the base change by its being an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relativelyRepresentable_of_isEtale_of_isAffineFormal
declarations.doc:
A morphism `g : X ⟶ Y` of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` whose source is an affine
formal algebraic space, which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale, is representable by
objects of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyRepresentable_of_isEtale_of_isAffineFormal {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (g : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom)
    (het : Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (fun _ _ k ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS k.hom) g.hom hrep) :
    uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.relativelyRepresentable g.hom
declarations.comment: the case of an etale morphism, at the value universe Type (u+1) where a formal algebraic space and the affine formal algebraic spaces of its atlas of Definition 0AIM live. Nothing is assumed beyond the tag: an etale morphism of schemes is locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite by Stacks 03WS, which is the tag's hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_sequential_presentation_iff_exists_countable_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AII.** A sequential affine presentation by thickenings exists exactly when a
countably indexed directed affine presentation by thickenings exists.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sequential_presentation_iff_exists_countable_presentation
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))) :
    (∃ D : ℕ ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS,
      (∀ ⦃i j : ℕ⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
        Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening
          ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f))) ∧
        Nonempty (X ≅ colimit
          (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
            Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
              (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)))) ↔
    (∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (pre : Preorder I),
      letI : Preorder I := pre
      Nonempty I ∧ IsDirected I (· ≤ ·) ∧ Countable I ∧
        ∃ D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS,
          (∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
            Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening
              ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f))) ∧
            Nonempty (X ≅ colimit
              (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
                Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
                  (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_iff_exists_countable_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AII.** An fppf sheaf has a sequential presentation by affine
schemes and thickenings if and only if it has one indexed by a countable nonempty directed
preorder.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexed_iff_exists_countable_presentation (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X ↔
      ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (pre : Preorder I),
        letI : Preorder I := pre
        Nonempty I ∧ IsDirected I (· ≤ ·) ∧ Countable I ∧
          ∃ D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS,
            (∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
              Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening
                ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f))) ∧
              Nonempty (X ≅ colimit
                (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
                  Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsCountablyIndexed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIJ.** A sheaf on the big fppf site of `S` is *countably indexed* when it is
the colimit of a sequence of sheaves represented by affine schemes whose transition
morphisms are thickenings.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsCountablyIndexed (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsCountablyIndexed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIJ.** An fppf sheaf is *countably indexed* when it admits a presentation indexed
by `ℕ` by affine schemes whose transition maps are thickenings. For an affine formal algebraic
space this is the countably indexed property.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCountablyIndexed (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicStar_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIK, item (1).** A Noetherian affine formal algebraic space is adic\*: its
presenting ring is adic, and an ideal of definition of a Noetherian ring is finitely
generated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicStar_of_isNoetherian {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS X) :
    IsAdicStar B S hS X
declarations.comment: noetherian_adic_star

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdic_of_isAdicStar
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIK, item (2).** An adic\* affine formal algebraic space is adic: adic\* is
adicness of the presenting ring together with the extra demand that some ideal of definition
be finitely generated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdic_of_isAdicStar {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsAdicStar B S hS X) :
    IsAdic B S hS X
declarations.comment: adic_star_adic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isWeaklyAdic_of_isAdic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIK, item (3).** An adic affine formal algebraic space is weakly adic, because
an adic linearly topologized ring is weakly adic.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAdic_of_isAdic {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsAdic B S hS X) :
    IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X
declarations.comment: adic_weakly_adic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClassical_of_isWeaklyAdic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIK, item (4).** A weakly adic affine formal algebraic space is classical,
because a weakly adic linearly topologized ring is admissible (Stacks 0GXF).
declarations.statement:
theorem isClassical_of_isWeaklyAdic {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X) :
    IsClassical B S hS X
declarations.comment: weakly_adic_classical

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_of_isWeaklyAdic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIK, item (5).** A weakly adic affine formal algebraic space is countably
indexed.

Let `A` be the presenting ring, `W` one of its weak ideals of definition, and `I` an ideal
whose closed powers are open and form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of `0`, which is
what weak adicness of `A` provides. The ideals `W ⊓ (I ^ n)‾` are then weak ideals of
definition, they decrease in `n`, and every weak ideal of definition contains one of them,
being open. So the sequence they form is a final functor into the index of the canonical
weak-ideal presentation of `X`, and restricting that presentation along it exhibits `X` as the
colimit of a sequence of affine schemes whose transition morphisms are thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexed_of_isWeaklyAdic {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X) : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X
declarations.comment: weakly_adic_countable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_of_isCountablyIndexed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AIK**, item (6). A countably indexed affine formal algebraic space
is McQuillan: it has a presentation by affine thickenings all of whose section-ring projections
are surjective, which is condition (4) of Stacks 0AIC.
declarations.comment: countable_mcquillan

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isPresentingRing_of_isCountablyIndexed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AIK**, item (6). A countably indexed affine formal algebraic space
is McQuillan: it has a presentation by affine thickenings all of whose section-ring projections
are surjective, which is condition (4) of Stacks 0AIC, and it is the formal spectrum of a
weakly admissible topological ring, which is condition (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isPresentingRing_of_isCountablyIndexed {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hc : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X) :
    HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X ∧
      ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : TopologicalSpace A) (_ : IsTopologicalRing A)
        (_ : IsLinearTopology A A), IsPresentingRing B S hS A X
declarations.comment: (6), countably indexed implies McQuillan

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalAlgebraicSpaces_discussion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIL**, the discussion following Definition 0AIM in Section 87.11, "Formal algebraic
spaces". Over a scheme `S` contained in a big fppf site:

1. *(sanity check)* every affine formal algebraic space is a formal algebraic space;
2. in the situation of Definition 0AIM — a family of maps `fᵢ : Xᵢ ⟶ X` of fppf sheaves whose
   sources are affine formal algebraic spaces and which are representable by algebraic spaces
   and étale — every `fᵢ` is representable by schemes, that is, by objects of the site
   (Lemma 0AIG);
3. *(Bootstrap, Lemma 04S1)* Definition 0AIM is unchanged if the requirement that `∐ Xᵢ ⟶ X` be
   surjective as a map of sheaves is replaced by the requirement that it be surjective, meaning
   that each of its base changes along a scheme of the site mapping to `X` is surjective.

The last conjunct records that an affine formal algebraic space is moreover a quasi-compact
formal algebraic space (Definition 0AJA, through condition (3) of Lemma 0AJ9), its identity being
a surjective representable étale chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem formalAlgebraicSpaces_discussion :
    letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) := Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
    (∀ X : FppfSheaf B S hS,
      IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X → IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) ∧
    (∀ (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (I : Type (u + 1)) (Xi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS)
      (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X), (∀ i, IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Xi i)) →
      (∀ i, ∃ hfi : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (f i).hom,
        Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
          (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) (f i).hom hfi) →
      ∀ i, uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.relativelyRepresentable (f i).hom) ∧
    (∀ X : FppfSheaf B S hS,
      IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X ↔
        SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X ∧
          ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (Xi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS) (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X),
            (∀ i, IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Xi i)) ∧
            (∀ i, ∃ hfi : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (f i).hom,
              Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
                (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) (f i).hom hfi) ∧
            IsSurjectiveOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS (Sigma.desc f)) ∧
    (∀ X : FppfSheaf B S hS,
      IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X → IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
declarations.comment: the unnumbered discussion of Definition 0AIM in the section: an affine formal algebraic space is a formal algebraic space; the members of a family as in Definition 0AIM are representable by schemes; surjectivity of the map from the coproduct as a map of sheaves may be replaced by surjectivity (Bootstrap, Lemma 04S1). Also records that an affine formal algebraic space is quasi-compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
An fppf sheaf on the big fppf site of `S` is a *formal algebraic space* over `S` when it
satisfies the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS and admits an atlas by affine formal
algebraic spaces: a family of maps into it whose sources are affine formal algebraic spaces,
each of which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale, and whose induced map from the
coproduct is a surjection of sheaves.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsFormalAlgebraicSpace (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIN** for an affine formal algebraic space. Let `X` be an affine formal algebraic
space over `S`. There is a reduced algebraic space `Xred` and a representable morphism
`Xred ⟶ X` which is a thickening and through which every morphism to `X` from a reduced
algebraic space factors uniquely.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isReduction_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃ (Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS) (i : Xred ⟶ X), IsReduction B S hS X Xred i
declarations.comment: affine formal algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIN for a general formal algebraic space, as a construction.** The chosen
reduction of a formal algebraic space over `S`, in the bundled shape the étale sites of
Stacks 0DEA consume.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def reduction (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    Reduction B S hS X
declarations.comment: general formal algebraic spaces, as a chosen datum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S`. There exists a reduced algebraic space `X_red`
and a representable morphism `X_red ⟶ X` which is a thickening, and a morphism `U ⟶ X` with `U`
a reduced algebraic space factors uniquely through `X_red`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isReduction_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃ (Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS) (i : Xred ⟶ X), IsReduction B S hS X Xred i
declarations.comment: a general formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relativelyRepresentable_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIP, representability, for an arbitrary formal algebraic space:** the absolute
diagonal of a formal algebraic space over `S` is representable by objects of the big fppf site
of `S`.

The diagonal is representable exactly when every morphism into the space from a sheaf
represented by an object of the site is, and that is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasRepresentableRelativeProducts_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativelyRepresentable_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable
      (diag X)
declarations.comment: representable by schemes, for an arbitrary formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_locallyOfFiniteType_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIP, local finite type, for an arbitrary formal algebraic space:** every
represented base change of the absolute diagonal of a formal algebraic space over `S` is a
locally of finite type morphism of objects of the big fppf site of `S`.

This is the assertion on underlying presheaves,
`…relative_locallyOfFiniteType_diag_hom_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace`, transported to the sheaf
category, which is where Stacks 0AIP and Stacks 0AN2 are stated.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_locallyOfFiniteType_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) (diag X)
declarations.comment: locally of finite type, for an arbitrary formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_locallyQuasiFinite_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIP, local quasi-finiteness, for an arbitrary formal algebraic space:** every
represented base change of the absolute diagonal of a formal algebraic space over `S` is a
locally quasi-finite, locally of finite type morphism of schemes.

The base change is locally of finite type by
`…relative_locallyOfFiniteType_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace` and a monomorphism because the
diagonal is, and a monomorphism of schemes locally of finite type is locally quasi-finite, which
is **Stacks 0CT8**.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_locallyQuasiFinite_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      ((@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) ⊓
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}))
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) (diag X)
declarations.comment: locally quasi-finite, for an arbitrary formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_isSeparated_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIP, separatedness, for an arbitrary formal algebraic space:** every represented
base change of the absolute diagonal of a formal algebraic space over `S` is a separated
morphism of schemes.

This one needs only the representability assertion: the base change is a monomorphism because
the diagonal is, and a monomorphism of schemes is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_isSeparated_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) (diag X)
declarations.comment: separated, for an arbitrary formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relativelyRepresentable_diag_of_isAffineFormal
declarations.doc:
The absolute diagonal of an affine formal algebraic space is representable by objects of the
site.
declarations.comment: representable by schemes, for an affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_locallyQuasiFinite_diag_of_isAffineFormal

Every represented base change of the absolute diagonal of an affine formal algebraic space is

theorem relative_locallyQuasiFinite_diag_of_isAffineFormal {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_locallyOfFiniteType_diag_of_isAffineFormal
declarations.doc:
Every represented base change of the absolute diagonal of an affine formal algebraic space is
a locally of finite type morphism of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_locallyOfFiniteType_diag_of_isAffineFormal {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_isSeparated_diag_of_isAffineFormal
declarations.doc:
Every represented base change of the absolute diagonal of an affine formal algebraic space is
a separated morphism of schemes.

    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.mono_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
The absolute diagonal of a formal algebraic space over `S` is a monomorphism of fppf sheaves,
which by **Stacks 0AQB** is what it is for a morphism of formal algebraic spaces to be a
monomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_diag_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (_hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) : Mono (diag X)
declarations.comment: monomorphism, for an arbitrary formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_isAlgebraicSpaceULift_of_isFormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIQ for an arbitrary formal algebraic space target.** A morphism of fppf sheaves
whose source is an algebraic space over `S` and whose target is a formal algebraic space over `S`
is representable by algebraic spaces.

This carries nothing. `isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_isAlgebraicSpaceULift`
(`MapsFromAlgebraicSpace`) states the implication with the target's representable relative
products as a hypothesis, and that hypothesis is the theorem above -- the representability
assertion of **Stacks 0AIP**. It is stated here rather than beside that theorem because
`MapsFromAlgebraicSpace` lies in this module's import closure and not conversely, so the
discharge can only be written downstream.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_isAlgebraicSpaceULift_of_isFormal
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : Space.IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS X.obj)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary formal algebraic space target, carrying nothing: the representable-relative-products hypothesis is discharged by this module's own Stacks 0AIP

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_isAlgebraicSpaceULift_of_isAffineFormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIQ** when the target is an affine formal algebraic space. A morphism of fppf
sheaves from an algebraic space over `S` to an affine formal algebraic space over `S` is
representable by algebraic spaces, the relative products of the target being representable by
**Stacks 0AI8**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_isAlgebraicSpaceULift_of_isAffineFormal
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : Space.IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS X.obj)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom
declarations.comment: for a target which is an affine formal algebraic space, that being the case in which this library has Stacks 0AIP

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.full_formalSchemePointsFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor of points of formal schemes on the category of all schemes is full, with no size
hypothesis.
declarations.statement: instance full_formalSchemePointsFunctor : formalSchemePointsFunctor.{u}.Full
declarations.comment: fullness of the embedding by the functor of points, on all schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithfulFormalSchemePointsFunctor
declarations.doc:
Taking the functor of points on the category of all schemes is a fully faithful embedding of
the category of formal schemes into presheaves of sets on schemes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fullyFaithfulFormalSchemePointsFunctor :
    formalSchemePointsFunctor.{u}.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: the assignment 𝔛 ↦ h_𝔛 is a fully faithful embedding of formal schemes into presheaves on schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.faithful_formalSchemePointsFunctor
declarations.doc: The functor of points of formal schemes on the category of all schemes is faithful.
declarations.statement: instance faithful_formalSchemePointsFunctor : formalSchemePointsFunctor.{u}.Faithful
declarations.comment: faithfulness of the embedding by the functor of points, on all schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_isOpenImmersion_openFormalSubschemePresheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIR, clause (4).** The morphism `h_{𝔛|_𝔘} ⟶ h_𝔛` of fppf sheaves on the big fppf
site of `S` is representable and an open immersion: it is representable by morphisms of the
site, and every morphism of the site representing a base change of it is an open immersion of
schemes. Nothing is assumed of `𝔛`, of `𝔘` or of the base scheme `S`.

The base change along a point `g` of `𝔛` over `T` is the inclusion of the open subscheme
`g⁻¹(𝔘)` of `T`, which is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isPullback_chart`; any other morphism
of the site representing the same base change differs from it by an isomorphism, the
universe-lifted Yoneda embedding being fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_isOpenImmersion_openFormalSubschemePresheafHom :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion.{u} :
        MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative
      (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}) (openFormalSubschemePresheafHom B S hS X V hV)
declarations.comment: the morphisms h_{𝔛ᵢ} ⟶ h_𝔛 of an open covering are representable and open immersions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_openFormalSubschemePoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIR, clause (3).** For a member `𝔛|_𝔘` of an affine open covering of `𝔛` — an open
of `𝔛` whose restriction is isomorphic to the formal spectrum of an admissible topological ring
`A` — the functor of points `h_{𝔛|_𝔘}` is an affine formal algebraic space over `S`.

This is Stacks 0AIE,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf`,
transported along the chart isomorphism, the functor of points being a functor of the formal
scheme. The source's own hypotheses are kept: the base is terminal, as the source assumes it is
`Spec(ℤ)`, and the quotient spectra of `A` and their coproduct belong to the chosen big fppf
site, which is the datum `D` and the condition `hB`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_openFormalSubschemePoints (hterm : IsTerminal S)
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsAdmissible A) (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (hB : D.HasLargeSite)
    (e : (X.obj.restrict V).toPresheafedSpace ≅ (spfLTRS A hA.1).toPresheafedSpace) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf B S hS (openFormalSubscheme X V hV))
declarations.comment: the charts h_{𝔛ᵢ} of an affine open covering are affine formal algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.fullyFaithfulFormalSchemePointsFppfSheafFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIR, clause (2).** The assignment `𝔛 ↦ h_𝔛` is a fully faithful embedding of the
category of formal schemes into the category `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.FppfSheaf B S hS`
of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` — the category in which formal algebraic spaces over
`S` live, and the one the comparison of Stacks 0AIR is about.

The source's "modulo set theoretic issues" is the restriction of the source category to the
formal schemes whose affine chart quotients belong to the big fppf site, which is the size
condition of Stacks 0AI1 for the site's cutoff, and the source's assumption that the base is
`Spec(ℤ)` is the hypothesis `hterm`. Both halves are Stacks 0AI1 read on the site:
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.injective_map_formalSchemePointsFppfSheafFunctor` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_map_eq_formalSchemePointsFppfSheafFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
def fullyFaithfulFormalSchemePointsFppfSheafFunctor (hterm : IsTerminal S) :
    (sizeBoundedFormalSchemePointsFppfSheafFunctor B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: the assignment 𝔛 ↦ h_𝔛 is a fully faithful embedding of formal schemes into the fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of the base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpaceFormalSchemePoints_of_affineCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIR, clause (5).** The functor of points of a formal scheme à la EGA is a formal
algebraic space over `S`, for a formal scheme admitting an open covering `𝔛 = ⋃ 𝔘_i` whose
charts have affine formal algebraic space functors of points and whose own functor of points
satisfies the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS.

This is the last sentence of the source's remark. The family `{h_{𝔛|_{𝔘_i}} ⟶ h_𝔛}` is a family
as in Definition 0AIM: the sources are affine formal algebraic spaces, which is the hypothesis
`haff` supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_openFormalSubschemePoints`; the
arrows are representable open immersions, hence representable étale, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableEtale_openFormalSubschemeSheafHom`; and the
family is jointly surjective, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_openFormalSubschemeSheafHom`. The
conclusion is then Stacks 0AJ1,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover`.

The hypothesis `hset` is the source's "modulo set theoretic issues" in the precise form of
Stacks 0AIS, and it is the only thing the source leaves to the reader here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpaceFormalSchemePoints_of_affineCover
    (hcov : ∀ p : X.obj, ∃ i, p ∈ U i)
    (haff : ∀ i, IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS
      (formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf B S hS (openFormalSubscheme X (U i) (hU i))))
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (formalSchemePointsFppfSheaf B S hS X)) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpaceFormalSchemePoints B S hS X
declarations.comment: the functor of points of a formal scheme with an affine open covering is a formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.fullyFaithfulComparableFormalSchemePointsFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIR, the comparison.** The category of formal schemes à la EGA is equivalent to a
full subcategory of the category of formal algebraic spaces over `S`: the functor `𝔛 ↦ h_𝔛`
from the formal schemes the comparison applies to into the formal algebraic spaces over `S` is
fully faithful, so it is an equivalence onto the full subcategory on its image.

This is the opening sentence of the source's remark. Its "modulo set theoretic issues" is the
restriction of the source category to
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.comparableFormalSchemes`, and the source's assumption that the
base is `Spec(ℤ)` is the hypothesis `hterm`. Full faithfulness is clause (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.fullyFaithfulFormalSchemePointsFppfSheafFunctor`, and the
functor lands in formal algebraic spaces by clause (5).
declarations.statement:
def fullyFaithfulComparableFormalSchemePointsFunctor (hterm : IsTerminal S) :
    (comparableFormalSchemePointsFunctor B S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: the category of formal schemes is equivalent to a full subcategory of the category of formal algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIR**, the sheaf clause, for a formal scheme isomorphic to a scheme: its functor
of points satisfies the fppf sheaf condition on the big fppf site of `S`, with no hypothesis
assumed.

The functor of points of a scheme seen as a formal scheme is the presheaf it represents and the
fpqc topology is subcanonical, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_formalSchemePoints_of_iso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints_of_iso {X : FormalScheme.{u}} {Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (e : X ≅ schemeToFormalScheme.obj Z) : IsFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints B S hS X
declarations.comment: the functor of points is an fppf sheaf, for a formal scheme that is a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints_formalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIR**, the sheaf clause, for an *arbitrary* formal scheme: the functor of points
of a formal scheme à la EGA satisfies the fppf sheaf condition on the big fppf site of `S`, with
no hypothesis assumed.

This is the first sentence of the source's remark, "by Lemma 87.2.2 the functor of points
`h_𝔛` associated to a formal scheme `𝔛` is a sheaf in the fppf topology". It is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqcTopology_formalSchemePoints`, the full statement of Stacks 0AI2,
read on the big fppf site of `S` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints_of_isSheaf_fpqcTopology`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints_formalScheme (X : FormalScheme.{u}) :
    IsFppfSheafFormalSchemePoints B S hS X
declarations.comment: the functor of points of an arbitrary formal scheme is an fppf sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition
declarations.doc:
An fppf sheaf satisfies the *set-theoretic condition* when there is a representable sheaf
surjecting onto it and a representable sheaf surjecting onto the kernel pair of that surjection.
Representability is recorded by an isomorphism of underlying presheaves with a universe-lifted
Yoneda presheaf.
declarations.statement: abbrev SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: the set-theoretic condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_bounded_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIS, bounded colimit.** A directed colimit of affine fppf sheaves along
thickenings satisfies the set-theoretic condition as soon as one cardinal `μ` below the size
cutoff of the site bounds both the index and the size of every stage.

The coproduct of the stages is then an object of the site — a coproduct of at most `μ` schemes
of size at most `μ` has size at most `μ`, by `AlgebraicGeometry.schemeSize_coproduct_le` — and
its universe-lifted representable sheaf is the coproduct of those of the stages, which is the
hypothesis of `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_colimit`.

Nothing is asked of the cofinality of the cutoff, and the index may be uncountable: the uniform
bound dominates the supremum of the stage sizes outright.
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_bounded_colimit
    {I : Type (u + 1)} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS)
    (hD : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
      Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f)))
    {μ : Cardinal.{u}} (hμ : μ < B.cutoff) (hI : #I ≤ Cardinal.lift.{u + 1, u} μ)
    (hstage : ∀ i : I, ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).obj (D.obj i)).size ≤ μ)
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hX : Nonempty (X ≅ colimit
      (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
        Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)))) :
    SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X
declarations.comment: bounded_colimit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_representable_epi_of_countable_atlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIS, observation (3), first half.** Let `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` be a family of maps of fppf
sheaves over `S` satisfying conditions (1), (2) and (3) of Definition 0AIM, with a *countable*
index. Then there is an object `U` of the big fppf site of `S` and a surjection of fppf sheaves
from the sheaf it represents onto `X`.

The surjection `Uᵢ ⟶ Xᵢ` from an object of the site onto each member of the family is the
first half of the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS, which the hypothesis that `Xᵢ` is an
affine formal algebraic space carries; countability makes the coproduct `U = ∐ Uᵢ` an object of
the site, the size cutoff of a big fppf site having uncountable cofinality.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_representable_epi_of_countable_atlas (X : FppfSheaf B S hS)
    {I : Type (u + 1)} [Countable I] (Xi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS) (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hatlas : IsFormalAtlas B S hS X Xi f) :
    ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (t : (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS).uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj U ⟶ X), Epi t
declarations.comment: observation (3), countable atlas

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_countable_atlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIS, observation (3).** Let `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` be a family of maps of fppf sheaves over
`S` satisfying conditions (1), (2) and (3) of Definition 0AIM with a *countable* index. Then
`X` satisfies the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS.

Countability provides the object `U` of the site surjecting onto `X`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_representable_epi_of_countable_atlas`). For the relation
it provides the second half as well. The kernel pair `U ×_X U` is covered by the family of
fibre products `(U ×_X Xᵢ) ×_{Xᵢ} (U ×_X Xᵢ)`, one for each member of the atlas: that family
is the base change of `U ×_X U` along the surjection `∐ Xᵢ ⟶ X` of condition (3), decomposed
along the coproduct, coproducts of sheaves of sets being stable under base change. Each member
is an algebraic space over `S` — this is the step of Stacks 0AIP available unconditionally in
this library, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAlgebraicSpaceULift_pullback_snd_pullback_snd` —
and an algebraic space over `S` receives a surjection of sheaves from an *object of the site*,
that being what its étale scheme atlas is by Definition 025Y. The coproduct of those atlases,
one for each index, is an object of the site because the index is countable and the size cutoff
of a big fppf site has uncountable cofinality; it is the required `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_countable_atlas (X : FppfSheaf B S hS)
    {I : Type (u + 1)} [Countable I] (Xi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS) (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hatlas : IsFormalAtlas B S hS X Xi f) :
    SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X
declarations.comment: observation (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_countable_atlas_of_hasQuasiCompactDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIS, observation (3), without the source's diagonal hypothesis.** Let
`{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` be a family of maps of fppf sheaves over `S` satisfying conditions (1), (2) and
(3) of Definition 0AIM with a *countable* index. Then `X` satisfies the set-theoretic
condition of Stacks 0AIS. The source also asks the diagonal of `X` to be quasi-compact, that
is, `X` to be quasi-separated over `S`; that hypothesis is unused and is not taken here.

Quasi-separatedness of `X` over `S` is quasi-compactness of the relative diagonal of its
structure morphism in the sense of Stacks 0ARN part (2), the structure morphism being the
morphism to the terminal object of the category of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`,
whose relative self-product is therefore `X ×_S X`. It is the source's hypothesis, and the
source is right that it suffices; it is not needed, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_countable_atlas` proves the
same conclusion from the countable atlas alone. The reason is that the source bounds the size
of the relation `R` by that of `U ×_S U`, for which it needs the diagonal to be tame, whereas
the argument here never leaves the site: the relation is assembled from the étale scheme
atlases of the members of a countable cover of `U ×_X U`, and those are objects of the site by
the definition of an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_countable_atlas_of_hasQuasiCompactDiagonal
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) {I : Type (u + 1)} [Countable I] (Xi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS)
    (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X) (hatlas : IsFormalAtlas B S hS X Xi f) :
    SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X
declarations.comment: observation (3), the source's quasi-compact diagonal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_countable_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIS, countable colimit.** A countable directed colimit of affine fppf sheaves
along thickenings satisfies the set-theoretic condition.

Countability replaces the representability hypothesis on the coproduct of the stages in
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_colimit`: a countable
coproduct is itself represented by an object of the big fppf site. What the argument uses is
only that a countable index is admissible for coproducts in the site, so this is the countable
case of `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_admissible_colimit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_countable_colimit (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {I : Type (u + 1)} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Countable I] (D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS)
    (hD : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
      Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f)))
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hX : Nonempty (X ≅ colimit
      (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
        Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)))) :
    SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X
declarations.comment: countable_colimit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_representable_over_affineFormal
declarations.doc:
**The set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS for the source of a morphism to an affine
formal algebraic space representable by algebraic spaces.** This is the first conjunct of the
conclusion of **Stacks 0AJH**, discharged.

The condition on `Y` supplies one object `U` of the site with `h_U ⟶ Y` a surjection of
sheaves. The fibre product `W = h_U ×_Y X` is then an algebraic space over `S`, and `W ⟶ X` is
a surjection of sheaves, so the étale scheme atlas `h_V ⟶ W` of `W` composes to a surjection
`a : h_V ⟶ X` from a representable. That atlas is representable by objects of the site and
`W ⟶ X` is a base change of `h_U ⟶ Y`, which is representable by objects of the site because an
affine formal algebraic space has representable relative products (Stacks 0AI8); so `a` is
representable by algebraic spaces, `h_V ×_X h_V` is an algebraic space by Stacks 03XY, and the
étale scheme atlas of `h_V ×_X h_V` is the second half of the condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_representable_over_affineFormal
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom) :
    SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X
declarations.comment: the condition for the source of a morphism to an affine formal algebraic space which is representable by algebraic spaces, which is the first conjunct of the conclusion of Stacks 0AJH

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAlgebraicSpace_of_affineSchemeAtlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIS, observation (2), the sanity check.** A family `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` as in
Definition 0AIM — the set-theoretic condition included — in which every `Xᵢ` is an affine
scheme makes `X` an algebraic space.

The affine schemes of the family need not be objects of the chosen site; each is presented by
its restricted functor of points, sheafified. The scheme atlas of the conclusion is assembled
inside the chosen site rather than by descent from a larger one: the set-theoretic condition
gives an object `U` of the site surjecting onto `X`, each `Xᵢ` is then represented by an affine
object of the site of size at most that of `U`, and the coproduct of one such for each point of
`U` is an object of the site because the size cutoff is a strong prelimit.

The diagonal is not a hypothesis: the atlas assembled here is representable by objects of the
site, so Stacks 0BGR gives the algebraic-space condition outright.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_affineSchemeAtlas
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (X : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hAtlas :
      let J := AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS
      letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (Sheaf J (Type (u + 1))) :=
        Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
      ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (Xi : I → Sheaf J (Type (u + 1)))
        (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X),
        (∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Xi i)) ∧
        (∀ i, ∃ (U : Over S), IsAffine U.left ∧
          Nonempty (Xi i ≅
            (presheafToSheaf J (Type (u + 1))).obj
              (Stacks.Groupoids.points (Over.post B.inclusion) U ⋙
                uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}))) ∧
        (∀ i, ∃ hfi : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1}
            B S hS (f i).hom,
          AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
            (fun _ _ g ↦ AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom)
            (f i).hom hfi) ∧
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc f)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS X.obj
declarations.comment: observation (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
A directed colimit of affine fppf sheaves along thickenings satisfies the set-theoretic
condition if the coproduct of its stages is representable in the big site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_colimit
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type (u + 1)} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : I ⥤ BigAffineFppf B S hS)
    (hD : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (f : i ⟶ j),
      Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening
        ((BigAffineFppf.toScheme B S hS).map (D.map f)))
    (X : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hX : Nonempty (X ≅ colimit
      (D ⋙ BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS ⋙
        Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))))
    (hU : ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (F : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))),
      Nonempty (F.obj ≅ (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).obj U) ∧
        Nonempty (F ≅ ∐ fun i : I ↦
          (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
            (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
              ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (D.obj i)))) :
    SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X
declarations.comment: colimit_condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_colimit_isRepresentableThickeningULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIU, corrected.** Let `E` be a directed system of algebraic spaces over `S` whose
transition morphisms are representable thickenings. A sheaf `Z` isomorphic to `colim E` which
satisfies the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS is a formal algebraic space over `S`.

The set-theoretic condition cannot be dropped: without it the statement is false
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit_thickenings`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_colimit_isRepresentableThickeningULift
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [Preorder Λ] [Nonempty Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)]
    (E : Λ ⥤ FppfSheaf B S hS)
    (halg : ∀ i : Λ, Space.IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS (E.obj i).obj)
    (hthick : ∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (g : i ⟶ j),
      Space.IsRepresentableThickeningULift.{u + 1} B S hS (E.map g).hom)
    (Z : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hZset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS Z)
    (hZ : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
        Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
      Nonempty (Z ≅ colimit E)) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z
declarations.comment: corrected form (errata.md, 2026-10-27, entry 0GVM, 0AIU): the printed statement is false, since for an index set large compared with the site the colimit admits no surjection from an object of the site, so it fails the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS that Definition 0AIM includes in being a formal algebraic space (AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_colimit_thickenings). The correction adds exactly that clause of the conclusion to the hypotheses, for a sheaf isomorphic to the colimit; the source's other hypotheses are unchanged and its charts are constructed in the proof

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.McQuillanFormalScheme.not_forall_isFppfColimitOfThickenings_of_exists
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIV, the "if" direction as printed, is false.** There is a formal scheme `𝔛` in the
sense of McQuillan (the twisted double `AlgebraicGeometry.TwistedDouble.𝔛`, a formal scheme à la
EGA) which has a fundamental system of weak ideals of definition, in the source's sectionwise
sense, but whose functor of points `h_𝔛` is not a colimit of schemes along thickenings in fppf
sheaves, as in Stacks 0AIU. On a formal scheme à la EGA the weak affine formal opens are the
affine formal opens, and a fundamental system of ideals of definition is one of weak ideals of
definition, so the fundamental system of
`AlgebraicGeometry.TwistedDouble.exists_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn` serves.

The corrected form is
`McQuillanFormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff_exists_isFundamentalSystem`,
where the weak ideals of definition are cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens.
declarations.statement:
theorem McQuillanFormalScheme.not_forall_isFppfColimitOfThickenings_of_exists :
    ¬ ∀ 𝔛 : McQuillanFormalScheme.{0},
      (∃ 𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf 𝔛.obj),
        IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen 𝔛.obj)) →
        𝔛.IsFppfColimitOfThickenings
declarations.comment: the statement as printed is false: the if direction, for sectionwise weak ideals of definition, fails for the twisted double, a formal scheme with a fundamental system of (weak) ideals of definition whose functor of points h_𝔛 is not a colimit of schemes as in Lemma 0AIU (colimit in fppf sheaves); the corrected form is McQuillanFormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff_exists_isFundamentalSystem

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IdealSheaf.IsWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn
declarations.doc:
An ideal sheaf on `X` is a *weak ideal of definition* over a class `𝒜` of opens — the
affine formal open subschemes — when its ideal of sections over every open of `𝒜` is a weak
ideal of definition of the topological ring of sections there.
declarations.statement: def IsWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn (I : IdealSheaf X) (𝒜 : Opens X → Prop) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition, over a class `𝒜` of affine formal opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn
declarations.doc:
A family of ideal sheaves on `X` is a *fundamental system of weak ideals of definition* over
a class `𝒜` of opens — the affine formal open subschemes — when each member is a weak ideal of
definition and, over every open of `𝒜`, their ideals of sections form a neighbourhood basis of
zero in the topological ring of sections.
declarations.statement:
def IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn {X : LTRS.{u}} (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X))
    (𝒜 : Opens X → Prop) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition, over a class `𝒜` of affine formal opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.McQuillanFormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff_exists_isFundamentalSystem
declarations.doc:
The functor of points `h_𝔛` of a McQuillan formal scheme is a colimit of schemes along
thickenings, as in Stacks 0AIU, in fppf sheaves if and only if `𝔛` has a fundamental system of
weak ideals of definition cut out by their sections over the weakly affine formal opens.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff_exists_isFundamentalSystem (𝔛 : McQuillanFormalScheme.{u}) :
    𝔛.IsFppfColimitOfThickenings ↔ ∃ 𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf 𝔛.obj),
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, I.IsCutOutOn (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen 𝔛.obj)) ∧
        IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen 𝔛.obj)
declarations.comment: h_𝔛 is a colimit of schemes along thickenings as in Lemma 0AIU (colimit in fppf sheaves) exactly when there exists a fundamental system of weak ideals of definition, CORRECTED: the weak ideals of definition are those cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens, the ones to which the correspondence ℐ ↦ (𝔛, 𝒪_𝔛/ℐ) applies (it fails for an arbitrary ideal sheaf)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.McQuillanFormalScheme.exists_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFppfColimitOfThickenings
declarations.doc:
If the functor of points `h_𝔛` of a formal scheme `𝔛` in the sense of McQuillan is a colimit
of schemes along thickenings, then there exists a fundamental system of weak ideals of definition
for `𝔛`: a family of ideal sheaves each of which is a weak ideal of definition over every affine
formal open, whose ideals of sections form a neighbourhood basis of zero over every affine formal
open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFppfColimitOfThickenings
    (𝔛 : McQuillanFormalScheme.{u}) (h : 𝔛.IsFppfColimitOfThickenings) :
    ∃ 𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf 𝔛.obj),
      IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen 𝔛.obj)
declarations.comment: the forward direction of the last sentence, as printed, with no extra hypothesis: if h_𝔛 is a colimit of schemes along thickenings as in Lemma 0AIU (colimit in fppf sheaves), then there exists a fundamental system of weak ideals of definition for 𝔛, in the sectionwise sense the source defines, with no condition on its members. The converse fails as printed (not_forall_isFppfColimitOfThickenings_of_exists) and needs the members to be cut out by their sections (isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff_exists_isFundamentalSystem)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.McQuillanFormalScheme.weakIdealOfDefinitionEquivThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIV, the one-to-one correspondence between weak ideals of definition and thickenings
`Z → h_𝔛`.** A weak ideal of definition `ℐ` (cut out by its sections over the weak affine formal
opens) goes to the thickening `(𝔛, 𝒪_𝔛/ℐ) → h_𝔛`, and a thickening goes to its kernel ideal sheaf;
the thickenings are taken up to isomorphism over `h_𝔛`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def weakIdealOfDefinitionEquivThickening :
    𝔛.WeakIdealOfDefinition ≃ Quotient (Thickening.setoid (𝔛 := 𝔛))
declarations.comment: the one-to-one correspondence between weak ideals of definition and thickenings Z → h_𝔛, CORRECTED: the weak ideals of definition are those cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens (`IdealSheaf.IsCutOutOn`, the formal analogue of quasi-coherence), the printed statement for an arbitrary ideal sheaf being false (`exists_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_forall_thickening_ideal_ne`); a thickening is a scheme Z with a relatively representable morphism h_Z → h_𝔛 whose base changes are thickenings of schemes, the functors of points being presheaves on all schemes, and thickenings are taken up to isomorphism over h_𝔛

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.McQuillanFormalScheme.ker_quotientPoint_and_existsUnique_factor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIV: the thickening attached to `ℐ` is `(𝔛, 𝒪_𝔛/ℐ)` with its obvious morphism to
`𝔛`.** The morphism `Z → 𝔛` of locally topologically ringed spaces underlying the thickening has
kernel ideal sheaf `ℐ`, and a point `T → 𝔛` of a scheme factors through it, uniquely, exactly when
it kills `ℐ`: `Z` is the closed subspace of `𝔛` cut out by `ℐ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_quotientPoint_and_existsUnique_factor (I : 𝔛.WeakIdealOfDefinition) :
    IdealSheaf.ker I.thickening.point = I.1 ∧
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (f : schemeToLTRSObj T ⟶ 𝔛.obj),
        I.1.Kills f ↔ ∃! k : T ⟶ I.thickening.scheme, schemeToLTRS.map k ≫ I.thickening.point = f
declarations.comment: the correspondence associates to ℐ the scheme Z = (𝔛, 𝒪_𝔛/ℐ) with the obvious morphism to 𝔛: its kernel is ℐ and the points of 𝔛 killing ℐ are those factoring through it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.McQuillanFormalScheme.exists_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_forall_thickening_ideal_ne
declarations.doc:
**Without the cut-out condition the correspondence of Stacks 0AIV fails.** There is a McQuillan
formal scheme — the pseudo-discretisation of the spectrum of the dual numbers over the `2`-adic
integers — with a weak ideal of definition which is the kernel ideal sheaf of no thickening
`Z → h_𝔛`: kernels of thickenings are cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens, and
this ideal sheaf is not.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_forall_thickening_ideal_ne :
    ∃ (𝔛 : McQuillanFormalScheme.{0}) (I : IdealSheaf 𝔛.obj),
      I.IsWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen 𝔛.obj) ∧
        ∀ Z : 𝔛.Thickening, Z.ideal ≠ I
declarations.comment: the printed correspondence, for an arbitrary ideal sheaf, is false: a weak ideal of definition which is the kernel of no thickening

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IdealSheaf.exists_not_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIV is false as printed: the weak ideal of definition condition cannot be checked on
the members of an affine open covering.** There is a McQuillan formal scheme `X` whose whole space
is a weak affine formal open, with an ideal sheaf `ℐ` such that `ℐ(X)` is a weak ideal of
definition, while `ℐ` is not a weak ideal of definition over every weak affine formal open. The
witness is the spectrum of the dual numbers `ℤ₂[ε]` over the `2`-adic integers, pseudo-discretised,
with the ideal sheaf of sections vanishing at the closed point; here `t = 2` lies in the maximal
ideal and `2ⁿ ε ≠ 0` for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover :
    ∃ (X : LTRS.{0}) (_ : IsMcQuillanFormalScheme X) (I : IdealSheaf X),
      IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X ⊤ ∧ TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal ⊤) ∧
        ¬ I.IsWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: the statement as printed is false: checking the weak ideal-of-definition condition on the members of an affine open covering does not suffice, already for Spec of the dual numbers over the 2-adic integers covered by itself, with the ideal sheaf of sections vanishing at the closed point; the corrected form is IdealSheaf.isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIV, the locality of the fundamental-system condition, is false as printed.** It is
not true that a family of ideal sheaves on a formal scheme in the sense of McQuillan is a
fundamental system of weak ideals of definition as soon as, over the members of an affine open
covering, its members are weak ideals of definition whose ideals of sections form a
neighbourhood basis of zero, even for a nonempty family directed by inclusion. The witness is
the one-member family `{ℐ}` of `IdealSheaf.exists_not_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover`, on
the pseudo-discretised spectrum of the dual numbers `ℤ₂[ε]` covered by itself: `ℐ(X) = 0` is a
weak ideal of definition and a neighbourhood of zero of the discrete ring `𝒪_X(X)`, but `ℐ` is
not a weak ideal of definition over the affine open `D(2)`.

The corrected statement checks the condition on the affine formal opens contained in the members
of the covering:
`isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover :
    ¬ ∀ (X : LTRS.{0}), IsMcQuillanFormalScheme X → ∀ (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X))
      (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)), 𝒮.Nonempty →
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
        K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W) →
      (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X V) → sSup 𝒰 = ⊤ →
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal V)) →
      (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, (nhds (0 : (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)).HasBasis (· ∈ 𝒮)
        fun I : IdealSheaf X => (I.ideal V : Set (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)) →
      IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: the statement as printed is false: checking the fundamental-system condition on the members of an affine open covering does not suffice, already for a one-member family on Spec of the dual numbers over the 2-adic integers covered by itself, with the ideal sheaf of sections vanishing at the closed point; the corrected form is isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIV, the locality of the fundamental-system condition, is false as printed, also when
only the neighbourhood-basis half is checked on the covering.** It is not true that a family of
weak ideals of definition (over every affine formal open) on a formal scheme in the sense of
McQuillan is a fundamental system as soon as its ideals of sections form a neighbourhood basis of
zero over the members of an affine open covering, even for a nonempty family directed by
inclusion. The witness is that of
`not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover` for Stacks 0AIW: on the
pseudo-discretisation of `Spec (ℤ[X₀, X₁, …] / (X_k ^ (k + 1)))`, a McQuillan formal scheme, the
sections whose germs are multiples of the germ of `X₁`, vanishing outside `D(n!)`, form an ideal
of definition, hence a weak one, over every quasi-compact open; it is zero over the whole space,
which is affine and has discrete sections, but its sections over `D(n!)`, which are discrete,
contain `X₁ ≠ 0`.

The corrected statement checks the condition on the affine formal opens contained in the members
of the covering:
`isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover :
    ¬ ∀ (X : LTRS.{0}), IsMcQuillanFormalScheme X → ∀ (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X))
      (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)), 𝒮.Nonempty →
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
        K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W) →
      (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X V) → sSup 𝒰 = ⊤ →
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, I.IsWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)) →
      (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, (nhds (0 : (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)).HasBasis (· ∈ 𝒮)
        fun I : IdealSheaf X => (I.ideal V : Set (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)) →
      IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: the statement as printed is false, also on the reading where the members are weak ideals of definition everywhere and the neighbourhood-basis property alone is checked on the members of an affine open covering: already for one weak ideal of definition on the pseudo-discretised Spec(Z[X_0, X_1, ...]/(X_k^(k+1))) covered by itself; the corrected form is isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IdealSheaf.isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isCutOutOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIV, the weak ideal-of-definition condition may be checked on the members of an
affine open covering, for ideal sheaves cut out by their sections.** Let `𝔛` be a formal scheme
in the sense of McQuillan and `ℐ` an ideal sheaf cut out by its sections over the affine formal
opens (`IdealSheaf.IsCutOutOn`). If `ℐ(𝔙)` is a weak ideal of definition for the members `𝔙` of a
covering of `𝔛` by affine formal opens, then `ℐ` is a weak ideal of definition.

These are the ideal sheaves of the correspondence of Stacks 0AIV with thickenings
(`McQuillanFormalScheme.weakIdealOfDefinitionEquivThickening`) and of its colimit criterion
(`McQuillanFormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff_exists_isFundamentalSystem`). For an
arbitrary ideal sheaf checking the covering members is not enough
(`IdealSheaf.exists_not_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover`), and the condition must then be
checked on the affine formal opens inside the covering members
(`IdealSheaf.isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme`). Over an affine formal
open `𝔚` inside a covering member `𝔙 ≅ Spfw A`, the ideal `ℐ(𝔚)` is the kernel of the quotient
point `Spec (A/ℐ(𝔙)) → 𝔛` (`IdealSheaf.isWeakIdealOfDefinition_of_le_of_isCutOutOn`).
declarations.statement:
theorem IdealSheaf.isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isCutOutOn
    (hX : IsMcQuillanFormalScheme X) (I : IdealSheaf X)
    (hC : I.IsCutOutOn (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)) (𝒰 : Set (Opens X))
    (h𝒰 : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X V) (hcover : sSup 𝒰 = ⊤)
    (hI : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal V)) :
    I.IsWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the weak ideal-of-definition condition on the members of an affine open covering: for ideal sheaves cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens (IdealSheaf.IsCutOutOn), the class of the correspondence with thickenings and of the colimit criterion; for an arbitrary ideal sheaf it is false (IdealSheaf.exists_not_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isCutOutOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIV, the fundamental-system condition may be checked on the members of an affine
open covering, for ideal sheaves cut out by their sections.** Let `𝔛` be a formal scheme in the
sense of McQuillan and `{ℐ_λ}` a nonempty family of ideal sheaves, directed by inclusion, each cut
out by its sections over the affine formal opens. If over the members `𝔙` of a covering of `𝔛` by
affine formal opens the `ℐ_λ(𝔙)` are weak ideals of definition forming a neighbourhood basis of
zero, then `{ℐ_λ}` is a fundamental system of weak ideals of definition.
