The family is indexed, as in the source, by a directed set (nonempty, by Stacks' definition of a
directed set), with `ℐ_μ ⊆ ℐ_λ` for `μ ≥ λ`; this is the directedness asked here. Over an affine
formal open inside a single covering member no directedness is used
(`hasBasis_of_le_of_isCutOutOn`); it serves to pass to affine formal opens meeting several members.
These are the families of the colimit criterion
`McQuillanFormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff_exists_isFundamentalSystem`. For arbitrary
ideal sheaves checking the covering members is not enough
(`not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover`,
`not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isCutOutOn
    (hX : IsMcQuillanFormalScheme X) (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X))
    (hC : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, I.IsCutOutOn (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)) (hne : 𝒮.Nonempty)
    (hdir : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
      K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W)
    (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)) (h𝒰 : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X V) (hcover : sSup 𝒰 = ⊤)
    (h𝒮 : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal V))
    (hbasis : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, (nhds (0 : (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)).HasBasis (· ∈ 𝒮)
      fun I : IdealSheaf X => (I.ideal V : Set (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)) :
    IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the fundamental-system condition on the members of an affine open covering: for a family indexed by a directed set, as in the source, of ideal sheaves cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens (IdealSheaf.IsCutOutOn), the class of the colimit criterion; for arbitrary ideal sheaves it is false (not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IdealSheaf.isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
An ideal sheaf on a formal scheme `𝔛` in the sense of McQuillan is a weak ideal of definition
as soon as its ideals of sections over the affine formal opens contained in the members of an open
covering are weak ideals of definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem IdealSheaf.isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme
    (hX : IsMcQuillanFormalScheme X) (I : IdealSheaf X) (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)) (hcover : sSup 𝒰 = ⊤)
    (hI : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, ∀ U : Opens X, U ≤ V → IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X U →
      TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal U)) :
    I.IsWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the weak ideal-of-definition condition on an affine open covering, CORRECTED: on the affine formal opens contained in a covering member, checking the covering members alone being insufficient (`exists_not_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover`)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
A nonempty family of ideal sheaves on a formal scheme `𝔛` in the sense of McQuillan, directed
by inclusion, is a fundamental system of weak ideals of definition as soon as, over every affine
formal open contained in a member of an open covering, its members are weak ideals of definition
whose ideals of sections form a neighbourhood basis of zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isMcQuillanFormalScheme
    (hX : IsMcQuillanFormalScheme X) (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X)) (hne : 𝒮.Nonempty)
    (hdir : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
      K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W)
    (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)) (hcover : sSup 𝒰 = ⊤)
    (h𝒮 : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, ∀ U : Opens X, U ≤ V → IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X U →
      TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal U))
    (hbasis : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, ∀ U : Opens X, U ≤ V → IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X U →
      (nhds (0 : (X.presheaf.obj (op U)).α)).HasBasis (· ∈ 𝒮)
        fun I : IdealSheaf X => (I.ideal U : Set (X.presheaf.obj (op U)).α)) :
    IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsWeakAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the fundamental-system condition on an affine open covering, CORRECTED: on the affine formal opens contained in a covering member, checking the covering members alone being insufficient (`exists_not_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover`), for a nonempty system directed by inclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IdealSheaf.IsIdealOfDefinitionOn
declarations.doc:
An ideal sheaf on `X` is an *ideal of definition* over a class `𝒜` of opens — the affine
formal open subschemes — when its ideal of sections over every open of `𝒜` is an ideal of
definition of the topological ring of sections there.
declarations.statement: def IsIdealOfDefinitionOn (I : IdealSheaf X) (𝒜 : Opens X → Prop) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition, over a class `𝒜` of affine formal opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn
declarations.doc:
A family of ideal sheaves on `X` is a *fundamental system of ideals of definition* over a
class `𝒜` of opens — the affine formal open subschemes — when each member is an ideal of
definition and, over every open of `𝒜`, their ideals of sections form a neighbourhood basis of
zero in the topological ring of sections.
declarations.statement:
def IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn {X : LTRS.{u}} (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X))
    (𝒜 : Opens X → Prop) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition, over a class `𝒜` of affine formal opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.exists_isIdealOfDefinition_of_isFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW**, the eventual ideals of definition on a quasi-compact formal scheme à la EGA.
Here the class of opens is the class of affine formal open subschemes, so the two geometric
inputs of
`exists_isIdealOfDefinition_of_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn` are discharged: the
affine formal opens cover `X` because `X` is a formal scheme, and the ring of sections over one of
them is pre-admissible by Stacks 0AHY.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isIdealOfDefinition_of_isFormalScheme {X : LTRS.{u}} [CompactSpace ↥X]
    (hX : IsFormalScheme X) (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X)) (hne : 𝒮.Nonempty)
    (hdir : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
      K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W)
    (hfund : IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X)) :
    ∃ 𝒰 : Set (Opens X), 𝒰.Finite ∧ (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsAffineFormalOpen X V) ∧ sSup 𝒰 = ⊤ ∧
      ∃ I₀ ∈ 𝒮, ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, (∀ W : Opens X, I.ideal W ≤ I₀.ideal W) →
        ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal V)
declarations.comment: `ℐ_λ` is an ideal of definition for `λ` large, on a quasi-compact formal scheme à la EGA, over the members of a finite affine open covering, which is what the source's argument proves; `hdir` and `hne` are the source's directed index set `Λ`. Over every affine formal open the step is false for arbitrary ideal sheaves (erratum in errata.md, `not_forall_exists_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn`) and holds for systems cut out by their sections, `exists_forall_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_isCutOutOn`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.exists_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_not_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_nilradical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW**, the separation of the ideal-of-definition condition from the weak one of
Stacks 0AIV, at the level of ideal sheaves on a formal scheme à la EGA. Let `R` be a nontrivial
commutative ring with exactly one prime ideal whose nilradical is not nilpotent. Then the
pseudo-discretisation of `Spec R` is a formal scheme à la EGA carrying an ideal sheaf — the
nilradical — which is a weak ideal of definition over its affine formal open subschemes and is
*not* an ideal of definition over them. This is why the correspondence of Stacks 0AIV between
weak ideals of definition and thickenings cannot restrict to a correspondence between ideals of
definition and thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_not_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_nilradical
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Nontrivial R] [Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum R)]
    (hnil : ∀ n : ℕ, (nilradical R) ^ n ≠ ⊥) :
    ∃ (X : LTRS.{u}) (_ : IsFormalScheme X) (I : IdealSheaf X),
      I.IsWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X) ∧
        ¬ I.IsIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: we do NOT get the same correspondence as in Stacks 0AIV: already on a formal scheme à la EGA the ideal-of-definition condition is strictly stronger than the weak one, witnessed by the nilradical of the pseudo-discretisation of a one-prime scheme whose nilradical is not nilpotent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalScheme.exists_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFppfColimitOfThickenings
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW, the "only if" direction, for arbitrary ideal sheaves.** If the functor of points
`h_𝔛` of a quasi-compact formal scheme `𝔛` à la EGA is a colimit of schemes along thickenings in
fppf sheaves, as in Stacks 0AIU, then `𝔛` has a fundamental system of ideals of definition, with
the definitions of the source: ideal sheaves whose ideals of sections over every affine formal open
are ideals of definition, and a neighbourhood basis of zero there.
declarations.statement:
theorem FormalScheme.exists_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFppfColimitOfThickenings
    (X : FormalScheme.{u}) [CompactSpace ↥X.obj]
    (h : X.toMcQuillanFormalScheme.IsFppfColimitOfThickenings) :
    ∃ 𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X.obj),
      IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X.obj)
declarations.comment: the direction from colimit to fundamental system: for 𝔛 quasi-compact, if h_𝔛 is a colimit of schemes as in Lemma 0AIU (colimit in fppf sheaves) then there exists a fundamental system of ideals of definition for 𝔛, for ideal sheaves in the source's generality

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW.** The functor of points `h_𝔛` of a quasi-compact formal scheme `𝔛` à la EGA is a
colimit of schemes along thickenings in fppf sheaves, as in Stacks 0AIU, if and only if `𝔛` has a
fundamental system of ideals of definition cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens.

This is the corrected form of the remark. The "only if" direction holds without the cut-out
condition
(`FormalScheme.exists_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFppfColimitOfThickenings`).
The source's definition of an ideal of definition is sectionwise and does not ask for the cut-out
condition (the analogue of `ℐ|_𝔘 = ℐ(𝔘)^Δ` in EGA), and with it the "if" direction is false
(`FormalScheme.not_forall_isFppfColimitOfThickenings_of_exists`).
declarations.statement:
theorem FormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff (X : FormalScheme.{u}) [CompactSpace ↥X.obj] :
    X.toMcQuillanFormalScheme.IsFppfColimitOfThickenings ↔ ∃ 𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X.obj),
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, I.IsCutOutOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X.obj)) ∧
        IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X.obj)
declarations.comment: corrected form: for 𝔛 quasi-compact, h_𝔛 is a colimit of schemes as in Lemma 0AIU (colimit in fppf sheaves) iff there exists a fundamental system of ideals of definition for 𝔛 cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens (erratum in errata.md); the direction from fundamental system to colimit as printed is false: see FormalScheme.not_forall_isFppfColimitOfThickenings_of_exists; the direction from colimit to fundamental system holds for arbitrary ideal sheaves, exists_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFppfColimitOfThickenings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.not_forall_exists_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW, the eventual ideals of definition, is false as printed.** It is not true that on
every quasi-compact formal scheme à la EGA a fundamental system `{ℐ_λ}` of weak ideals of
definition consists of ideals of definition for `λ` sufficiently large, even for a nonempty
system directed by inclusion: in the system of
`exists_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn_forall_not_isIdealOfDefinitionOn` no member
at all is an ideal of definition over the affine formal opens.

The source's argument shows that `ℐ_λ(𝔘)` is an ideal of definition for `λ` large on the finitely
many members `𝔘` of an affine open covering, which is true
(`exists_isIdealOfDefinition_of_isFormalScheme`), and concludes by the locality claim refuted in
`not_forall_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_exists_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn :
    ¬ ∀ (X : LTRS.{0}), IsFormalScheme X → CompactSpace X → ∀ 𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X),
      𝒮.Nonempty →
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
        K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W) →
      IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X) →
      ∃ I₀ ∈ 𝒮, ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, (∀ W : Opens X, I.ideal W ≤ I₀.ideal W) →
        I.IsIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: `ℐ_λ` is an ideal of definition for `λ` large: FALSE as printed, for ideal sheaves in the source's generality, on a quasi-compact (even affine) formal scheme à la EGA and for a nonempty directed system; the true statement is over the members of a finite affine open covering, `exists_isIdealOfDefinition_of_isFormalScheme`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.not_forall_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW, the locality of the ideal-of-definition condition, is false as printed.** It is
not true that an ideal sheaf on a formal scheme à la EGA is an ideal of definition as soon as its
ideals of sections over the members of an affine open covering are ideals of definition: on the
pseudo-discretisation of `Spec (ℤ[X₀, X₁, …] / (X_k ^ (k + 1)))` the sections with nilpotent germs
vanishing outside `D(n!)` are zero over the whole space, which is affine, and are not an ideal of
definition over `D(n!)`.

The corrected statement checks the condition on the affine formal opens contained in the members
of the covering: `IdealSheaf.isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover :
    ¬ ∀ (X : LTRS.{0}), IsFormalScheme X → ∀ (I : IdealSheaf X) (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)),
      (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsAffineFormalOpen X V) → sSup 𝒰 = ⊤ →
      (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal V)) →
      I.IsIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the ideal-of-definition condition on an affine open covering: FALSE as printed, for ideal sheaves in the source's generality, already for the covering of an affine formal scheme by itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW, the locality of the fundamental-system condition, is false as printed.** It is
not true that a family of ideals of definition on a formal scheme à la EGA is a fundamental system
as soon as its ideals of sections form a neighbourhood basis of zero over the members of an affine
open covering, even for a nonempty directed family whose members are ideals of definition over
every affine formal open: on the pseudo-discretisation of `Spec (ℤ[X₀, X₁, …] / (X_k ^ (k + 1)))`
the sections whose germs are multiples of the germ of `X₁`, vanishing outside `D(n!)`, form an
ideal of definition which is zero over the whole space, which is affine, but whose sections over
`D(n!)`, which are discrete, contain `X₁ ≠ 0`.

The corrected statement checks the condition on the affine formal opens contained in the members
of the covering: `isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_directed`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover :
    ¬ ∀ (X : LTRS.{0}), IsFormalScheme X → ∀ (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X)) (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)),
      𝒮.Nonempty →
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
        K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W) →
      (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsAffineFormalOpen X V) → sSup 𝒰 = ⊤ →
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, I.IsIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)) →
      (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, (nhds (0 : (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)).HasBasis (· ∈ 𝒮)
        fun I : IdealSheaf X => (I.ideal V : Set (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)) →
      IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the fundamental-system condition on an affine open covering: FALSE as printed, for ideal sheaves in the source's generality, already for a single ideal of definition and the covering of an affine formal scheme by itself

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.exists_forall_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_isCutOutOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW, the eventual ideals of definition, for a system cut out by its sections.** On a
quasi-compact formal scheme à la EGA, let `𝒮` be a nonempty, directed fundamental system of weak
ideals of definition over the affine formal opens, each member cut out by its sections over the
affine formal opens. Then there is a member `I₀` such that every member below it is an ideal of
definition over every affine formal open.

The finite affine covering produced by quasi-compactness gives `I₀` with ideals of definition over
the members of the covering (`exists_isIdealOfDefinition_of_isFormalScheme`), and
`IdealSheaf.pow_ideal_le_of_isCutOutOn` carries the comparison of powers from the covering to an
arbitrary affine formal open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_forall_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_isCutOutOn {X : LTRS.{u}} [CompactSpace ↥X]
    (hX : IsFormalScheme X) (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X)) (hne : 𝒮.Nonempty)
    (hdir : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
      K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W)
    (hfund : IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X))
    (hcut : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, I.IsCutOutOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)) :
    ∃ I₀ ∈ 𝒮, ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, (∀ W : Opens X, I.ideal W ≤ I₀.ideal W) →
      I.IsIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: `ℐ_λ` is an ideal of definition for `λ` large, over EVERY affine formal open, for a directed system whose members are cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens (the condition of Stacks 0AIV singling out the ideal sheaves of thickenings); for arbitrary ideal sheaves the statement is false, `not_forall_exists_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_isFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IdealSheaf.isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isCutOutOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW, the ideal-of-definition condition may be checked on the members of an affine
open covering, for ideal sheaves cut out by their sections.** Let `𝔛` be a formal scheme à la EGA
and `ℐ` an ideal sheaf cut out by its sections over the affine formal opens
(`IdealSheaf.IsCutOutOn`). If `ℐ(𝔙)` is an ideal of definition for the members `𝔙` of a covering
of `𝔛` by affine formal opens, then `ℐ` is an ideal of definition.

These are the ideal sheaves of the colimit criterion of Stacks 0AIW,
`FormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff`. For an arbitrary ideal sheaf checking the covering
members is not enough (`not_forall_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover`), and the condition must then be
checked on the affine formal opens inside the covering members
(`IdealSheaf.isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isFormalScheme`). Over an affine formal open inside
a covering member the condition is `IdealSheaf.isIdealOfDefinition_of_le_of_isCutOutOn`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IdealSheaf.isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isCutOutOn
    (hX : IsFormalScheme X) (I : IdealSheaf X)
    (hC : I.IsCutOutOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)) (𝒰 : Set (Opens X))
    (h𝒰 : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsAffineFormalOpen X V) (hcover : sSup 𝒰 = ⊤)
    (hI : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal V)) :
    I.IsIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the ideal-of-definition condition on the members of an affine open covering: for ideal sheaves cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens (IdealSheaf.IsCutOutOn), the class of the colimit criterion FormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff; for an arbitrary ideal sheaf it is false (not_forall_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isCutOutOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW, the fundamental-system condition may be checked on the members of an affine
open covering, for ideal sheaves cut out by their sections.** Let `𝔛` be a formal scheme à la EGA
and `{ℐ_λ}` a nonempty family of ideal sheaves, directed by inclusion, each cut out by its sections
over the affine formal opens. If over the members `𝔙` of a covering of `𝔛` by affine formal opens
the `ℐ_λ(𝔙)` are ideals of definition forming a neighbourhood basis of zero, then `{ℐ_λ}` is a
fundamental system of ideals of definition.

The family is indexed, as in the source, by a directed set (nonempty, by Stacks' definition of a
directed set), with `ℐ_μ ⊆ ℐ_λ` for `μ ≥ λ`; over an affine formal open inside a single covering
member no directedness is used (`hasBasis_of_le_of_isCutOutOn`). These are the families of the
colimit criterion `FormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff`. For arbitrary ideal sheaves
checking the covering members is not enough
(`not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isCutOutOn
    (hX : IsFormalScheme X) (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X))
    (hC : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, I.IsCutOutOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)) (hne : 𝒮.Nonempty)
    (hdir : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
      K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W)
    (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)) (h𝒰 : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsAffineFormalOpen X V) (hcover : sSup 𝒰 = ⊤)
    (h𝒮 : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal V))
    (hbasis : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, (nhds (0 : (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)).HasBasis (· ∈ 𝒮)
      fun I : IdealSheaf X => (I.ideal V : Set (X.presheaf.obj (op V)).α)) :
    IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the fundamental-system condition on the members of an affine open covering: for a family indexed by a directed set, as in the source, of ideal sheaves cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens (IdealSheaf.IsCutOutOn), the class of the colimit criterion FormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff; for arbitrary ideal sheaves it is false (not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IdealSheaf.isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW**, the locality of the ideal-of-definition condition on a formal scheme à la EGA.
An ideal sheaf is an ideal of definition as soon as its ideals of sections over the affine formal
open subschemes contained in the members of some covering are ideals of definition. The
affine formal open subschemes are quasi-compact and form a basis, which are the two hypotheses
`IdealSheaf.isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover` asks of the class of opens.
declarations.statement:
theorem IdealSheaf.isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isFormalScheme {X : LTRS.{u}}
    (hX : IsFormalScheme X) (I : IdealSheaf X) (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)) (hcover : sSup 𝒰 = ⊤)
    (hI : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, ∀ U : Opens X, U ≤ V → IsAffineFormalOpen X U →
      TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal U)) :
    I.IsIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the ideal-of-definition condition on an affine open covering, CORRECTED, on a formal scheme à la EGA with no further hypothesis: the condition is checked on the affine formal opens contained in a covering member, not on the covering members themselves, which is false as the source states it (`not_forall_isIdealOfDefinitionOn_of_cover`)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW**, the locality of the fundamental-system condition on a formal scheme à la EGA,
with no hypothesis on the class of opens: for a nonempty family directed by inclusion, both halves
of the condition may be checked on the affine formal open subschemes contained in the members of a
covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_cover_of_isFormalScheme {X : LTRS.{u}}
    (hX : IsFormalScheme X) (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X)) (hne : 𝒮.Nonempty)
    (hdir : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
      K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W)
    (𝒰 : Set (Opens X)) (hcover : sSup 𝒰 = ⊤)
    (h𝒮 : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, ∀ U : Opens X, U ≤ V → IsAffineFormalOpen X U →
      TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition (I.ideal U))
    (hbasis : ∀ V ∈ 𝒰, ∀ U : Opens X, U ≤ V → IsAffineFormalOpen X U →
      (nhds (0 : (X.presheaf.obj (op U)).α)).HasBasis (· ∈ 𝒮)
        fun I : IdealSheaf X => (I.ideal U : Set (X.presheaf.obj (op U)).α)) :
    IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: it suffices to check the fundamental-system condition on an affine open covering, CORRECTED, on a formal scheme à la EGA with no further hypothesis: both halves are checked on the affine formal opens contained in a covering member, not on the covering members themselves, which is false as the source states it (`not_forall_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_hasBasis_cover`), for a nonempty system directed by inclusion (`hne`, `hdir`), the source's directed index set `Λ`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalScheme.not_forall_isFppfColimitOfThickenings_of_exists
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW, the "if" direction as printed, is false.** There is a quasi-compact formal
scheme `𝔛` à la EGA (the twisted double `AlgebraicGeometry.TwistedDouble.𝔛`) which has a
fundamental system of ideals of definition, in the source's sectionwise sense, but whose functor
of points `h_𝔛` is not a colimit of schemes along thickenings in fppf sheaves, as in Stacks 0AIU.

The corrected form is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff`, where the
ideals of definition are cut out by their sections over the affine formal opens.
declarations.statement:
theorem FormalScheme.not_forall_isFppfColimitOfThickenings_of_exists :
    ¬ ∀ (X : FormalScheme.{0}) [CompactSpace X.obj],
      (∃ 𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X.obj),
        IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X.obj)) →
        X.toMcQuillanFormalScheme.IsFppfColimitOfThickenings
declarations.comment: the if direction as printed (sectionwise ideals of definition) is false: a quasi-compact formal scheme with a fundamental system of ideals of definition whose functor of points h_𝔛 is not a colimit of schemes as in Lemma 0AIU (colimit in fppf sheaves); corrected form: FormalScheme.isFppfColimitOfThickenings_iff

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.WeakIdealOfDefinitionExample.isThickening_residueField_and_not_isIdealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW**, the failure of the correspondence of Stacks 0AIV for ideals of definition.
For a valuation ring `(A, 𝔪, κ)` which is `(π)`-adically complete for a nonzero `π ∈ 𝔪` whose
radical is `𝔪`, and whose maximal ideal is not finitely generated, the residue-field stage
`Spec κ ⟶ Spf A` of the formal spectrum is a thickening, while the weak ideal of definition `𝔪`
to which the correspondence of Stacks 0AIV attaches it is *not* an ideal of definition. So the
correspondence between weak ideals of definition and thickenings does not restrict to a
correspondence between ideals of definition and thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_residueField_and_not_isIdealOfDefinition [IsDomain A]
    (hval : IsValuationRing A) (hπm : π ∈ maximalIdeal A)
    (hadic : IsAdic (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)))
    (hrad : (Ideal.span ({π} : Set A)).radical = maximalIdeal A)
    (hnotfg : ¬ (maximalIdeal A).FG)
    {B : BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : B.Contains S}
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) :
    let J : { I : Ideal A // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I } :=
      ⟨maximalIdeal A, isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal π hadic hrad⟩
    (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (formalSpectrumInclusion D (OrderDual.toDual J)) ∧
      ¬ TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition J.1
declarations.comment: we do NOT get the same correspondence between ideals of definition and thickenings as in Stacks 0AIV: the residue-field stage of Spf A is a thickening while the weak ideal of definition it corresponds to is not an ideal of definition (Stacks 0CB8); the formal spectrum is taken over a big fppf site through its presentation `D` (site membership and structure morphisms to `S`), as in the statements of Stacks 0CB8 combined here

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal_and_not_isIdealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW**, the negative clause on the example of Stacks 0CB8. The maximal ideal of the
ring of integers of the field `ℂ_[p]` of `p`-adic complex numbers is a weak ideal of definition
of that admissible topological ring, and it is not an ideal of definition. So the two notions
differ, and the correspondence of Stacks 0AIV between weak ideals of definition and thickenings
cannot restrict to one between ideals of definition and thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal_and_not_isIdealOfDefinition :
    TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (maximalIdeal (PadicComplexInt p)) ∧
      ¬ TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition (maximalIdeal (PadicComplexInt p))
declarations.comment: the negative clause is not vacuous: in the ring of integers of ℂ_[p] the maximal ideal is a weak ideal of definition and is not an ideal of definition

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.isThickening_residueField_not_from_idealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW**, the negative clause on the example of Stacks 0CB8, geometrically: the
residue-field stage `Spec ℂ_[p]^- ⟶ Spf 𝒪_{ℂ_p}` of the formal spectrum of the ring of integers
of `ℂ_[p]` is a thickening whose weak ideal of definition, the maximal ideal, is not an ideal of
definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isThickening_residueField_not_from_idealOfDefinition
    {B : BigFppfSite.{0}} {S : Scheme.{0}} {hS : B.Contains S}
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS (PadicComplexInt p)) :
    let J : { I : Ideal (PadicComplexInt p) // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I } :=
      ⟨maximalIdeal (PadicComplexInt p),
        (isWeakIdealOfDefinition_maximalIdeal_and_not_isIdealOfDefinition p).1⟩
    (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening : MorphismProperty Scheme.{0})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)))
      (formalSpectrumInclusion D (OrderDual.toDual J)) ∧
      ¬ TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition J.1
declarations.comment: the negative clause on the example of Stacks 0CB8: a thickening of the formal spectrum of the ring of integers of ℂ_[p] whose weak ideal of definition is not an ideal of definition; the formal spectrum is taken over a big fppf site through its presentation `D`

declarations.name: PadicComplexInt.exists_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_not_isIdealOfDefinitionOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW**, the negative clause at the level of ideal sheaves, unconditionally. The
pseudo-discretisation of `Spec (𝒪_{ℂ_p}/(p))` is a formal scheme à la EGA whose nilradical is a
weak ideal of definition over its affine formal open subschemes and is not an ideal of definition
over them: the ring has the single prime `𝔪/(p)`, and no power of its nilradical vanishes because
no power of `𝔪` lies inside `(p)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn_not_isIdealOfDefinitionOn
    (q : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime q)] :
    ∃ (X : LTRS.{0}) (_ : IsFormalScheme X) (I : LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.IdealSheaf X),
      I.IsWeakIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X) ∧
        ¬ I.IsIdealOfDefinitionOn (IsAffineFormalOpen X)
declarations.comment: the negative clause is not vacuous at the level of ideal sheaves: an explicit formal scheme à la EGA with a weak ideal of definition that is not an ideal of definition

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.isIdealOfDefinition_of_le_of_isOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIW.** An open ideal contained in an ideal of definition is an ideal of definition:
its powers lie inside the corresponding powers of the larger ideal, and those are cofinal among
the neighbourhoods of zero. Since in an admissible topological ring the open ideals form a basis
of neighbourhoods of zero, this is the source's observation that all sufficiently small open
ideals of such a ring are ideals of definition.
declarations.comment: in an admissible topological ring all sufficiently small open ideals are ideals of definition: any open ideal contained in an ideal of definition is one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completionSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIY.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X = Spec A` be an affine scheme over `S` lying
in the big fppf site and let `T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset. The completion of `X` along `T` —
the fppf sheaf attached to the functor sending `U` to the set of morphisms `f : U ⟶ X` with
`f(|U|) ⊆ T` — is a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space: it is the directed colimit of the
affine thickenings `Spec (A ⧸ J)` over the ideals `J` with `V(J) = T`, and the projections from
the inverse limit of the section rings of that presentation onto each stage are surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completionSheaf
    (T : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (affineOver B S hS hA f))) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hatlas : HasStageAtlas B S hS hA f (PrimeSpectrum.vanishingIdeal T)) :
    HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS
      (Space.completionSheaf B S hS (yoneda.obj (affineOver B S hS hA f))
        (supportedPoints B S hS (affineOver B S hS hA f) T))
declarations.comment: McQuillan affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completionSheaf_of_isClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIY.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X = Spec A` be an affine scheme over `S` lying
in the big fppf site and let `T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset. The completion of `X` along `T` —
the fppf sheaf attached to the functor sending `U` to the set of morphisms `f : U ⟶ X` with
`f(|U|) ⊆ T` — is a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completionSheaf` with its
atlas hypothesis discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasStageAtlas`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completionSheaf_of_isClosed
    (T : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (affineOver B S hS hA f))) (hT : IsClosed T) :
    HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS
      (Space.completionSheaf B S hS (yoneda.obj (affineOver B S hS hA f))
        (supportedPoints B S hS (affineOver B S hS hA f) T))
declarations.comment: McQuillan affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isIso_toSheafify_completionSubfunctor_affineOver
declarations.doc:
Let `X = Spec A` be an affine scheme over `S` lying in the site and `T ⊆ |X|` a subset. The
functor sending an object `U` of the big fppf site of `S` to the morphisms `f : U ⟶ X` with
`f(|U|) ⊆ T` is an fppf sheaf: the map to its sheafification, the completion of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionSheaf`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_toSheafify_completionSubfunctor_affineOver {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (f : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
    (T : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (affineOver B S hS hA f))) :
    IsIso (toSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
      (Space.completionSubfunctor B S hS (yoneda.obj (affineOver B S hS hA f))
        (supportedPoints B S hS (affineOver B S hS hA f) T)).toFunctor)
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheaf_of_isClosed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIZ.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset. The completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T` — the fppf sheaf attached
to the functor sending `U` to the morphisms `f : U ⟶ X` with `f(|U|) ⊆ T` — is a formal
algebraic space over `S`.

The affine étale charts of `X` are those of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_affine_etale_charts`, the inverse image of `T` on each is
the set of points supported in a closed subset
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isClosed_preimage_eq_supportedPoints`), the stage atlas
of each chart completion is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasStageAtlas`, and the set-theoretic
condition is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionSheaf`;
with these the atlas argument of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheaf` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheaf_of_isClosed
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AIZ.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset. The completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T` — the fppf sheaf attached
to the functor sending `U` to the morphisms `f : U ⟶ X` with `f(|U|) ⊆ T` — is a formal
algebraic space over `S`: the completions of the affine charts of `X` along the inverse images
of `T` form an atlas of `X_{/T}`, and each of them is an affine formal algebraic space by the
affine case, Stacks 0AIY.

The affine étale charts of `X`, the description of the inverse image of `T` on each of them as
the points supported in a closed subset, the per-chart hypothesis `HasStageAtlas` of the
affine case and the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS are carried as hypotheses; see the
section "What is assumed" of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheaf
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    {Ix : Type (u + 1)} {A : Ix → Type u} [∀ i, CommRing (A i)]
    (hA : ∀ i, B.Contains (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of (A i))))
    (str : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of (A i)) ⟶ S)
    (a : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (affineOver B S hS (hA i) (str i)) ⟶ X)
    (ha : ∀ i, ∃ hai : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (a i)).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ q ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS q.hom)
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (a i)).hom hai)
    (hcov : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
          Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Sigma.desc fun i ↦ Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (a i)))
    (Ti : ∀ i, Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (affineOver B S hS (hA i) (str i))))
    (hTi : ∀ i, IsClosed (Ti i))
    (hTpts : ∀ i, Space.pointsMap B S hS _ (a i) ⁻¹' T =
      supportedPoints B S hS (affineOver B S hS (hA i) (str i)) (Ti i))
    (hstage : ∀ i, HasStageAtlas B S hS (hA i) (str i)
      (PrimeSpectrum.vanishingIdeal (Ti i)))
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)
declarations.comment: assumes the affine étale charts of X as hA, str, a, ha, hcov, their closed point sets as hTi and hTpts, the affine case's HasStageAtlas as hstage, and the 0AIS condition as hset

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isIso_toSheafify_completionSubfunctor
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and `T` a set of points of `X`. The functor sending
an object `U` of the big fppf site of `S` to the morphisms `f : U ⟶ X` with `f(|U|) ⊆ T` is an
fppf sheaf: the map to its sheafification, the completion `X_{/T}` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionSheaf`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_toSheafify_completionSubfunctor
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) :
    IsIso (toSheafify (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)
      (Space.completionSubfunctor B S hS X T).toFunctor)
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ1.** A jointly surjective family of representable étale maps from formal
algebraic spaces makes its target a formal algebraic space, provided the target satisfies the
set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover {I : Type (u + 1)}
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (Xi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS) (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hXi : ∀ i, IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Xi i))
    (hf : ∀ i, ∃ hfi : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (f i).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) (f i).hom hfi)
    (hsurj : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
        Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
      Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc f))
    (hXset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS X) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ1 is false without a bound on the index.** Over a nonempty scheme `S` of a big
fppf site, it is not the case that every fppf sheaf `X` with a family `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` satisfying
conditions (a), (b) and (c) of Stacks 0AJ1 is a formal algebraic space: the sheaf of locally
constant functions with values in a discrete set as large as the cutoff of the site, with its
family of constant functions out of `h_S`, satisfies (a)–(c) but not the set-theoretic
condition of Stacks 0AIS that Definition 0AIM asks of a formal algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover [Nonempty S] :
    letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) := Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
    ¬ ∀ (I : Type (u + 1)) (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (Xi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS)
      (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X),
      (∀ i, IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Xi i)) →
      (∀ i, ∃ hfi : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (f i).hom,
        Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
          (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) (f i).hom hfi) →
      Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc f) →
      IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: the statement as printed is false: over any nonempty S, the sheaf of locally constant functions to a discrete set as large as the size cutoff of the site, with the family of its constant sections out of h_S, satisfies (a)-(c) but fails the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS; the corrected form is AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover_of_admitsCoproductIndex

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover_of_admitsCoproductIndex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ1, for an index which is not too large.** Let `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}_{i ∈ I}` be a family of
maps of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`, indexed by a type admissible for coproducts in
the site (of cardinality below the cofinality of its size cutoff; for instance a countable one),
such that (a) each `Xᵢ` is a formal algebraic space over `S`, (b) each `Xᵢ ⟶ X` is
representable by algebraic spaces and étale, and (c) `∐ Xᵢ ⟶ X` is a surjection of sheaves.
Then `X` is a formal algebraic space over `S`.

The atlas is the source's: the atlases of the `Xᵢ` composed with the maps `Xᵢ ⟶ X`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover`). The set-theoretic
condition of Stacks 0AIS, which Definition 0AIM asks of `X` as well, is not assumed: it is
derived from (a)–(c) by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_etaleCover`, which is where
the size of the index enters, as observation (3) of Remark 0AIS says it must. Without a bound
on the index the statement is false
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover_of_admitsCoproductIndex
    {I : Type (u + 1)} [Small.{u} I] [B.AdmitsCoproductIndex I]
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (Xi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS) (f : ∀ i, Xi i ⟶ X)
    (hXi : ∀ i, IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Xi i))
    (hf : ∀ i, ∃ hfi : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (f i).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom) (f i).hom hfi)
    (hsurj : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
        Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
      Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc f)) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: corrected form: the printed statement is false for an index set as large as the size cutoff of the site, the target then failing the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS that Definition 0AIM asks of a formal algebraic space (AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_forall_isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_etaleCover); stated, under the source's hypotheses (a)-(c), for an index admissible for coproducts in the site, the proviso 'I not too large' of Stacks 0AIS observation (3), and with that condition derived, not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_isSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ2** for a base which is separated in the sense of clause (2) of Stacks 0AJ6.
The fibre product of two formal algebraic spaces over such a base, whose relative products of
representables are representable, is a formal algebraic space.

Separatedness enters only through Stacks 0AN3 clause (1): it makes the fibre product of two
affine formal algebraic spaces over `Z` again an affine formal algebraic space, which is the
hypothesis `hstage` of `isFormalAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_affineStages`. The set-theoretic
condition of Stacks 0AIS on `X ×_Z Y` and on the intermediate fibre products follows from
`hZrep` alone, by `satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_pullback_of_hasRepresentableRelativeProducts`
over `Z` and, after the pasting isomorphism, over `Z` again.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_isSeparated
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hZrep : HasRepresentableRelativeProducts B S hS Z)
    (hZsep : IsSeparated B S hS Z)
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (pullback p q)
declarations.comment: the case of a base separated in the sense of clause (2) of Stacks 0AJ6, where Stacks 0AN3 clause (1) makes every fibre product of two affine formal algebraic spaces over the base an affine formal algebraic space, in place of the directed colimit argument of Stacks 0AIU that the general case needs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_isAffineFormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ2** for a separated base, on two affine formal algebraic spaces: an affine
formal algebraic space is a formal algebraic space, so this is a special case of
`isFormalAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_isSeparated`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_isAffineFormal
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hZrep : HasRepresentableRelativeProducts B S hS Z)
    (hZsep : IsSeparated B S hS Z)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (pullback p q)
declarations.comment: the case of two affine formal algebraic spaces over a base separated in the sense of clause (2) of Stacks 0AJ6, where Stacks 0AN3 clause (1) makes the fibre product of the two an affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_representableDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ2.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` and `Y` be formal algebraic spaces over `S` and
let `Z` be a sheaf on `(Sch/S)_fppf` whose diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces. For
maps of sheaves `p : X ⟶ Z` and `q : Y ⟶ Z`, the fibre product `X ×_Z Y` is a formal algebraic
space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_representableDiagonal
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (p : X ⟶ Z) (q : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hZ : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (diag Z.obj))
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (pullback p q)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasPullbacks_formalAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ3.** The category of formal algebraic spaces over a scheme `S` has fibre
products.

The fibre product is the fibre product of the underlying fppf sheaves: that is again a formal
algebraic space by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_pullback_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace`, so the
full inclusion into fppf sheaves creates fibre products and the subcategory inherits them.
declarations.statement: instance hasPullbacks_formalAlgebraicSpaces : HasPullbacks (FormalAlgebraicSpaces B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_reduction_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ5.** Let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S` and let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a
reduction of `X`, presented by a presheaf `Xred` of `Type u` together with an isomorphism from
its universe lift. The following are equivalent: `Xred` is a quasi-separated algebraic space;
for every pair of objects of the big fppf site of `S` with quasi-compact underlying scheme and
every pair of morphisms from their universe-lifted Yoneda presheaves into `X`, every object of
the site representing the fibre product has quasi-compact underlying scheme; and the same for
every pair of objects with affine underlying scheme.

Condition (1) is equivalent to the intersection condition for `Xred`, with quasi-compact or
with affine test objects, by Stacks 0AHR. The intersection condition for `X` implies the one
for `Xred` because the inclusion of a reduction is a monomorphism, and conversely it follows
from the one for `Xred` by the thickening comparison of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasQuasiCompactIntersectionsULift_of_isReduction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_reduction_tfae
    {X Xr : FppfSheaf B S hS} (_hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {i : Xr ⟶ X} (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xr i)
    {Xred : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (e : Xred ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ Xr.obj) :
    List.TFAE
      [ Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Xred,
        HasQuasiCompactIntersectionsULift B S hS
          (fun Z : Scheme.{u} ↦ CompactSpace (Z : Type u)) X.obj,
        HasQuasiCompactIntersectionsULift B S hS (fun Z : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsAffine Z) X.obj ]
declarations.comment: the reduction of X is a given, in the sense of AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsReduction and supplied by Stacks 0AIN, and is presented by a presheaf of Type u together with an isomorphism from its universe lift, since an algebraic space over S is a presheaf of Type u while a formal algebraic space is a sheaf of Type (u + 1); clauses (2) and (3) quantify over the objects of the site representing the fibre product, as the carriers of Stacks 0AHR do for the identical clauses, rather than asserting that it is representable, which is Stacks 0AIP

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_reduction_tfae_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ5, with clauses (2) and (3) asserting representability.** Let `X` be a formal
algebraic space over `S` and let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X`, presented by a presheaf
`Xred` of `Type u` together with an isomorphism from its universe lift. The following are
equivalent: `Xred` is a quasi-separated algebraic space; for every pair of objects of the big
fppf site of `S` with quasi-compact underlying scheme and every pair of morphisms from their
universe-lifted Yoneda presheaves into `X`, the fibre product is represented by an object of
the site with quasi-compact underlying scheme; and the same for every pair of objects with
affine underlying scheme.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_reduction_tfae` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasRepresentableQuasiCompactIntersectionsULift_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_reduction_tfae_representable
    {X Xr : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {i : Xr ⟶ X} (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xr i)
    {Xred : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (e : Xred ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ Xr.obj) :
    List.TFAE
      [ Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Xred,
        HasRepresentableQuasiCompactIntersectionsULift B S hS
          (fun Z : Scheme.{u} ↦ CompactSpace (Z : Type u)) X.obj,
        HasRepresentableQuasiCompactIntersectionsULift B S hS
          (fun Z : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsAffine Z) X.obj ]
declarations.comment: with clauses (2) and (3) in the source's own form, asserting that the fibre product U ×_X V is representable by an object of the site with quasi-compact underlying scheme; read against a reduction of X, in the sense of AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsReduction and supplied by Stacks 0AIN, presented by a presheaf of Type u together with an isomorphism from its universe lift

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_of_hasAffineIntersectionsULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ6, the implication (2) ⟹ (1).** Let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S`
and let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X`, presented by a presheaf `Xred` of `Type u`
together with an isomorphism from its universe lift. If for every pair of objects of the big
fppf site of `S` with affine underlying scheme and every pair of morphisms from their
universe-lifted Yoneda presheaves into `X` every object of the site representing the fibre
product has affine underlying scheme and the canonical map from the tensor product over `ℤ` of
the two rings of global sections to its ring of global sections is surjective, then `Xred` is a
separated algebraic space.

The inclusion of a reduction is a monomorphism, so a cartesian square exhibiting a fibre
product over `Xred` also exhibits it over `X`; the condition therefore restricts from `X` to
`Xred`, where it is separatedness by Stacks 0AHS.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_of_hasAffineIntersectionsULift
    {X Xr : FppfSheaf B S hS} (_hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {i : Xr ⟶ X} (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xr i)
    {Xred : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (e : Xred ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ Xr.obj)
    (h : HasAffineIntersectionsULift B S hS X.obj) :
    Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ Xred
declarations.comment: (2) implies (1): the affine-intersection and surjectivity condition for X gives that the reduction of X is a separated algebraic space. The reduction is a given, in the sense of AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsReduction and supplied by Stacks 0AIN, and is presented by a presheaf of Type u together with an isomorphism from its universe lift, since an algebraic space over S is a presheaf of Type u while a formal algebraic space is a sheaf of Type (u + 1). Clause (2) quantifies over the objects of the site representing the fibre product, as the carrier of Stacks 0AHS does for the identical clause, rather than asserting that it is representable, which is Stacks 0AIP. The converse implication (1) implies (2), the equivalence read against an arbitrary reduction, and the tag itself, whose reduction is produced from Stacks 0AIN, are AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineIntersectionsULift_of_isReduction, AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift and AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift in StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.ReductionSeparatedConverse

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ6.** Let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S` and let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a
reduction of `X`, presented by a presheaf `Xred` of `Type u` together with an isomorphism from
its universe lift. Then `Xred` is a separated algebraic space if and only if for every pair of
objects of the big fppf site of `S` with affine underlying scheme and every pair of morphisms
from their universe-lifted Yoneda presheaves into `X` every object of the site representing the
fibre product has affine underlying scheme and the canonical map from the tensor product over
`ℤ` of the two rings of global sections to its ring of global sections is surjective.

The implication from the condition to separatedness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_of_hasAffineIntersectionsULift`:
the inclusion of a reduction is a monomorphism, so the condition restricts from `X` to the
reduction, where it is separatedness by Stacks 0AHS. The converse is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineIntersectionsULift_of_isReduction`, the argument of the
source through the thickening comparison of the two fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift
    {X Xr : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {i : Xr ⟶ X} (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xr i)
    {Xred : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (e : Xred ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ Xr.obj) :
    Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ Xred ↔
      HasAffineIntersectionsULift B S hS X.obj
declarations.comment: both implications, read against a reduction of X, in the sense of AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsReduction, and a presentation of it by a presheaf of Type u together with an isomorphism from its universe lift -- an algebraic space over S being a presheaf of Type u while a formal algebraic space is a sheaf of Type (u + 1). Clause (2) quantifies over the objects of the site representing the fibre product, as the carrier of Stacks 0AHS does for the identical clause, rather than asserting that it is representable, which is Stacks 0AIP. The tag itself, which produces the reduction and its presentation, is AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ6.** Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B` and let `X` be a
formal algebraic space over `S`. The reduction of `X` exists — a reduced algebraic space
`X_red` and a representable thickening `i : X_red ⟶ X` through which every morphism to `X`
from a reduced algebraic space factors uniquely — it is presented by a presheaf `Xred` of
`Type u` together with an isomorphism from its universe lift, and the following are
equivalent:

1. `Xred` is a separated algebraic space;
2. for every pair of objects of the big fppf site of `S` with affine underlying scheme and
   every pair of morphisms from their universe-lifted Yoneda presheaves into `X`, every
   object of the site representing the fibre product has affine underlying scheme and the
   canonical map from the tensor product over `ℤ` of the two rings of global sections to its
   ring of global sections is surjective.

The reduction comes from Stacks 0AIN,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace`; its presentation
by a presheaf of `Type u` from the pointwise `u`-smallness of an algebraic space,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_comp_uliftFunctor_iso_of_isAlgebraicSpaceULift`; and the
equivalence from
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift`,
which reads it against any reduction and any presentation of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isReduction_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃ (Xr : FppfSheaf B S hS) (i : Xr ⟶ X) (Xred : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (_ : Xred ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ Xr.obj),
      IsReduction B S hS X Xr i ∧
        (Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ Xred ↔
          HasAffineIntersectionsULift B S hS X.obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_iff_hasRepresentableAffineIntersectionsULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ6, with clause (2) asserting representability.** Let `X` be a formal algebraic
space over `S` and let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X`, presented by a presheaf `Xred` of
`Type u` together with an isomorphism from its universe lift. Then `Xred` is a separated
algebraic space if and only if for every pair of objects of the big fppf site of `S` with affine
underlying scheme and every pair of morphisms from their universe-lifted Yoneda presheaves into
`X` the fibre product is represented by an object of the site with affine underlying scheme and
the canonical map from the tensor product over `ℤ` of the two rings of global sections to its
ring of global sections is surjective.

This is `…isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift` composed with
`…hasRepresentableAffineIntersectionsULift_iff`, which identifies clause (2) in the source's
form with the form that quantifies over the representing objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAbsolutelySeparated_reduction_iff_hasRepresentableAffineIntersectionsULift
    {X Xr : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {i : Xr ⟶ X} (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xr i)
    {Xred : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (e : Xred ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ Xr.obj) :
    Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ Xred ↔
      HasRepresentableAffineIntersectionsULift B S hS X.obj
declarations.comment: both implications, with clause (2) in the source's own form, which asserts that the fibre product U ×_X V is representable by an object of the site and that its underlying scheme is affine, rather than quantifying over the objects of the site representing it. The two readings agree on a formal algebraic space, by AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasRepresentableAffineIntersectionsULift_iff, whose nontrivial direction is the representability assertion of Stacks 0AIP for an arbitrary formal algebraic space. Read against a reduction of X, in the sense of AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsReduction, and a presentation of it by a presheaf of Type u together with an isomorphism from its universe lift -- an algebraic space over S being a presheaf of Type u while a formal algebraic space is a sheaf of Type (u + 1). The tag with the reduction and its presentation produced is AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_iff_hasRepresentableAffineIntersectionsULift

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_iff_hasRepresentableAffineIntersectionsULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ6, with clause (2) asserting representability.** Let `S` be a scheme contained
in a big fppf site `B` and let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S`. The reduction of `X`
exists — a reduced algebraic space `X_red` and a representable thickening `i : X_red ⟶ X`
through which every morphism to `X` from a reduced algebraic space factors uniquely — it is
presented by a presheaf `Xred` of `Type u` together with an isomorphism from its universe lift,
and the following are equivalent:

1. `Xred` is a separated algebraic space;
2. for every pair of objects of the big fppf site of `S` with affine underlying scheme and
   every pair of morphisms from their universe-lifted Yoneda presheaves into `X`, the fibre
   product is represented by an object of the site with affine underlying scheme and the
   canonical map from the tensor product over `ℤ` of the two rings of global sections to its
   ring of global sections is surjective.

Clause (2) is here the source's own, asserting that `U ×_X V` is a scheme. The reduction comes
from Stacks 0AIN for an arbitrary formal algebraic space,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isReduction_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_iff_hasRepresentableAffineIntersectionsULift
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    ∃ (Xr : FppfSheaf B S hS) (i : Xr ⟶ X) (Xred : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
      (_ : Xred ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ Xr.obj),
      IsReduction B S hS X Xr i ∧
        (Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ Xred ↔
          HasRepresentableAffineIntersectionsULift B S hS X.obj)
declarations.comment: the reduction and its presentation by a presheaf of Type u produced, from Stacks 0AIN for an arbitrary formal algebraic space and from the pointwise u-smallness of an algebraic space, with clause (2) in the source's own form, which asserts that the fibre product U ×_X V is representable by an object of the site and that its underlying scheme is affine. The variant whose clause (2) quantifies over the objects of the site representing the fibre product instead is AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_and_isAbsolutelySeparated_iff_hasAffineIntersectionsULift in StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.ReductionSeparatedConverse

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsSeparated
declarations.doc:
An fppf sheaf `X` on the big fppf site of `S` is *separated* when, for every pair of morphisms
to `X` from sheaves represented by affine schemes over `S`, every object of the site representing
their fibre product is affine and the canonical map from the tensor product over `ℤ` of the two
coordinate rings to its coordinate ring is surjective.

The condition quantifies over the objects of the site representing the fibre product, so on an
fppf sheaf whose fibre products are not representable it holds vacuously. On a formal algebraic
space it agrees with `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_iff_isSeparated`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSeparated (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (2): separated, in the form of clause (2) of Stacks 0AJ6

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
An fppf sheaf `X` on the big fppf site of `S` is *quasi-separated* when, for every pair of
morphisms to `X` from sheaves represented by affine schemes over `S`, every object of the site
representing their fibre product has quasi-compact underlying scheme.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiSeparated (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (1): quasi-separated, in the form of clause (3) of Stacks 0AJ5, whose equivalence with clause (2) of Stacks 0AJ5 and with quasi-separatedness of the reduction is not proved in this library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace.isSeparated
declarations.doc:
Every affine formal algebraic space over `S` is separated, in the form of clause (2) of
Stacks 0AJ6.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace.isSeparated {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) : IsSeparated B S hS X
declarations.comment: clause (2): an affine formal algebraic space is separated, in the form of clause (2) of Stacks 0AJ6, whose equivalence with clause (1) is not proved in this library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiSeparated_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
Every affine formal algebraic space over `S` is quasi-separated, in the form of clause (3)
of Stacks 0AJ5.
declarations.comment: clause (1): an affine formal algebraic space is quasi-separated, in the form of clause (3) of Stacks 0AJ5

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ7, clause (1): quasi-separated formal algebraic spaces.** A formal algebraic
space `X` over `S` is *quasi-separated* when the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0AJ5 hold.
The condition recorded is clause (3) of Stacks 0AJ5: for every pair of objects `U`, `V` of the
big fppf site of `S` with affine underlying scheme and every pair of morphisms `U ⟶ X`,
`V ⟶ X` (morphisms `h_U ⟶ X`, `h_V ⟶ X` of presheaves out of the universe-lifted Yoneda
presheaves), the fibre product `U ×_X V` is a scheme — represented by an object of the site
with a cartesian square over the two morphisms — and that scheme is quasi-compact.

The fibre product is the genuine one, and it is always representable, by Stacks 0AIP; so the
condition is never vacuous. Its equivalence with the other conditions of Stacks 0AJ5 —
quasi-separatedness of the reduction of `X`, and clause (2) with quasi-compact test objects —
is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_tfae`. On a formal
algebraic space it agrees with `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiSeparated`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_iff_isQuasiSeparated`.
declarations.statement: def IsQuasiSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (1): a formal algebraic space is quasi-separated when the conditions of Stacks 0AJ5 hold, recorded as clause (3) of Stacks 0AJ5 with the fibre product asserted to be a scheme; equivalent to every condition of Stacks 0AJ5 by isQuasiSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_tfae

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ7, clause (2): separated formal algebraic spaces.** A formal algebraic space
`X` over `S` is *separated* when the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0AJ6 hold. The condition
recorded is clause (2) of Stacks 0AJ6: for every pair of objects `U`, `V` of the big fppf site
of `S` with affine underlying scheme and every pair of morphisms `U ⟶ X`, `V ⟶ X` (morphisms
`h_U ⟶ X`, `h_V ⟶ X` of presheaves out of the universe-lifted Yoneda presheaves), the fibre
product `U ×_X V` is a scheme — represented by an object of the site with a cartesian square
over the two morphisms — that scheme is affine, and the canonical map
`𝒪(U) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪(V) ⟶ 𝒪(U ×_X V)` is surjective.

The fibre product is the genuine one, and it is always representable, by Stacks 0AIP; so the
condition is never vacuous. Its equivalence with clause (1) of Stacks 0AJ6, separatedness of
the reduction of `X`, is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_tfae`.
On a formal algebraic space it agrees with `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsSeparated`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_iff_isSeparated`.
declarations.statement: def IsSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: clause (2): a formal algebraic space is separated when the conditions of Stacks 0AJ6 hold, recorded as clause (2) of Stacks 0AJ6 with the fibre product asserted to be a scheme; equivalent to clause (1) of Stacks 0AJ6 by isSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_tfae

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ7, clause (1), is the class of the conditions of Stacks 0AJ5.** Let `X` be a
formal algebraic space over `S` and let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X`, presented by a
presheaf `Xred` of `Type u` together with an isomorphism from its universe lift. The following
are equivalent: `X` is quasi-separated in the sense of Stacks 0AJ7; `Xred` is a quasi-separated
algebraic space (clause (1) of Stacks 0AJ5); for every pair of quasi-compact test objects over
`X` the fibre product is a quasi-compact scheme (clause (2)); and the same for every pair of
affine test objects (clause (3)).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_tfae
    {X Xr : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {i : Xr ⟶ X} (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xr i)
    {Xred : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (e : Xred ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ Xr.obj) :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsQuasiSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X,
        Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Xred,
        HasRepresentableQuasiCompactIntersectionsULift B S hS
          (fun Z : Scheme.{u} ↦ CompactSpace (Z : Type u)) X.obj,
        HasRepresentableQuasiCompactIntersectionsULift B S hS
          (fun Z : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsAffine Z) X.obj ]
declarations.comment: clause (1): the definition is equivalent to each of the conditions of Stacks 0AJ5, read against a reduction of X presented by a presheaf of Type u, which exists by Stacks 0AIN

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJ7, clause (2), is the class of the conditions of Stacks 0AJ6.** Let `X` be a
formal algebraic space over `S` and let `i : X_red ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X`, presented by a
presheaf `Xred` of `Type u` together with an isomorphism from its universe lift. Then `X` is
separated in the sense of Stacks 0AJ7 if and only if `Xred` is a separated algebraic space
(clause (1) of Stacks 0AJ6).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace_tfae
    {X Xr : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    {i : Xr ⟶ X} (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xr i)
    {Xred : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (e : Xred ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1} ≅ Xr.obj) :
    IsSeparatedFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X ↔ Space.IsAbsolutelySeparated B S hS hZ Xred
declarations.comment: clause (2): the definition is equivalent to clause (1) of Stacks 0AJ6, read against a reduction of X presented by a presheaf of Type u, which exists by Stacks 0AIN

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.tfae_isQuasiCompactSpace_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S` and let `i : Xred ⟶ X` be a reduction of `X`.
Then quasi-compactness of `Xred`, the existence of an atlas as in Definition 0AIM indexed by a
finite type, and the existence of a morphism from an affine formal algebraic space which is
representable by algebraic spaces, étale and a surjection of sheaves are equivalent.

A reduction of `X` exists by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isReduction_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isQuasiCompactSpace_unconditional
    {X Xred : FppfSheaf B S hS} {i : Xred ⟶ X}
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hi : IsReduction B S hS X Xred i) :
    [Space.IsQuasiCompactSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS Xred.obj,
      HasFiniteFormalAtlas B S hS X,
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X].TFAE
declarations.comment: the equivalence of the three conditions, for every reduction i : Xred ⟶ X of X; a reduction exists by Stacks 0AIN (exists_isReduction_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.tfae_isQuasiCompactSpace_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S`. The following are equivalent:

1. the reduction `reduction` of `X` is a quasi-compact algebraic space,
2. `X` admits an atlas as in Definition 0AIM indexed by a finite type,
3. `X` receives a morphism from an affine formal algebraic space which is representable by
   algebraic spaces, étale and a surjection of sheaves.

Condition (1) is read at the reduction `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reduction` that
Stacks 0AIN produces; by `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.Reduction.iso` any two reductions of
`X` are canonically isomorphic, so the condition does not depend on the choice, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.tfae_isQuasiCompactSpace_of_isReduction_unconditional` is the same
equivalence at an arbitrary reduction.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isQuasiCompactSpace_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    [Space.IsQuasiCompactSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (liftSheaf B S hS (reduction B S hS X hX).space).obj,
      HasFiniteFormalAtlas' B S hS X,
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X].TFAE
declarations.comment: the equivalence of the three conditions

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompactSpace
registrations.comment: the definition, realized by condition (3) of Stacks 0AJ9, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompactSpace`; the equivalence with conditions (1) and (2) that makes the choice of condition immaterial is `tfae_isQuasiCompactSpace`, which carries the two hypotheses standing for the steps of the omitted proof of Stacks 0AJ9

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (2) implies condition (3).** The fibre product condition over the
quasi-compact schemes over `S` in the site restricts to the affine ones, an affine scheme
being quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.isQuasiCompact {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (h : IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f) : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (3); no other implication among the four conditions is proved here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiCompactOnReductions_iff_isQuasiCompactULift_chosenReductionMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over
`S`. The morphism `f_red : X_red ⟶ Y_red` of the chosen reductions is a quasi-compact morphism of
algebraic spaces if and only if every morphism between reductions of `X` and of `Y` compatible
with `f` is one. The second condition is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompactOnReductions`, the phrasing of condition (1) which
quantifies over the reductions instead of choosing them.

Given reductions `iX : Xred ⟶ X` and `iY : Yred ⟶ Y` and a compatible `fred`, the universal
properties of the chosen reductions supply comparison morphisms `a : Xred ⟶ X_red` and
`b : Yred ⟶ Y_red` over `X` and over `Y`, and these are isomorphisms because two reductions of
