one sheaf are isomorphic over it. The inclusion of the reduction of `Y` is a monomorphism, so
`a ≫ f_red = fred ≫ b`, and `fred` is `f_red` conjugated by the two isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompactOnReductions_iff_isQuasiCompactULift_chosenReductionMap
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsQuasiCompactOnReductions B S hS f ↔
      Space.IsQuasiCompactULift.{u + 1} B S hS (chosenReductionMap B S hS hX hY f).hom
declarations.comment: condition (1), in the source's own form — quasi-compactness of the morphism f_red of the chosen reductions — identified with the phrasing of the condition that quantifies over the reductions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompact.isQuasiCompactULift_chosenReductionMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (3) implies condition (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal
algebraic spaces over `S` such that every fibre product of `f` with an affine scheme over `S` in
the site mapping to `Y` is a quasi-compact formal algebraic space — that is, let `f` be
quasi-compact in the sense of Stacks 0AJC. Then the morphism `f_red : X_red ⟶ Y_red` of the
chosen reductions is a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces.
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (1), for the morphism f_red of the chosen reductions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.isQuasiCompactULift_chosenReductionMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (2) implies condition (1).** The fibre product condition over the
quasi-compact schemes over `S` in the site restricts to the affine ones, which already makes the
morphism `f_red` of the chosen reductions a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.isQuasiCompactULift_chosenReductionMap
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (h : IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f) :
    Space.IsQuasiCompactULift.{u + 1} B S hS (chosenReductionMap B S hS hX hY f).hom
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1), for the morphism f_red of the chosen reductions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompact.isQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (3) implies condition (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of fppf
sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` every one of whose fibre products with an affine scheme over
`S` in the site mapping to `Y` is a quasi-compact formal algebraic space over `S`. Then the same
holds over every *quasi-compact* scheme over `S` in the site.

Let `T` be such a scheme and let `W` be a fibre product of `f` with a point `T ⟶ Y`. A finite
affine open covering `{U_i ⟶ T}` of `T` inside the site exists because `T` is quasi-compact
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.exists_finite_affine_open_cover`). Each `W ×_T U_i` is, by
pasting the two cartesian squares, a fibre product of `f` with the affine point `U_i ⟶ Y`, hence
a quasi-compact formal algebraic space by the hypothesis; each projection `W ×_T U_i ⟶ W` is a
base change of `U_i ⟶ T`, hence representable étale, an open immersion being étale; and the
family of projections is jointly surjective because `{U_i ⟶ T}` generates a covering sieve and
coproducts of sheaves of types are stable under base change. So
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiCompactSpace_of_finite_isRepresentableEtale_cover`
applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiCompact.isQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (h : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) : IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiCompact_iff_isQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, the equivalence of conditions (2) and (3).** For a morphism of fppf sheaves
on the big fppf site of `S`, the fibre product condition over the quasi-compact schemes over `S`
in the site and the fibre product condition over the affine ones are equivalent.

One implication restricts the quantifier, an affine scheme being quasi-compact, and is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.isQuasiCompact`; the other is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompact.isQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges`. This is the
first cycle closed among the four conditions of Stacks 0AJB.
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompactOnReductions.hasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (1) implies condition (4).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
formal algebraic spaces over `S` such that every morphism between reductions of `X` and of `Y`
compatible with `f` is a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces. Then there is a covering
`{Yⱼ ⟶ Y}` as in Definition 0AIM all of whose fibre products with `f` are quasi-compact formal
algebraic spaces over `S`.

The covering is the atlas of `Y` that the hypothesis `IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y` supplies,
which is the covering Definition 0AIM provides and the one the source's hypothesis on `Y` names.
Its members are affine formal algebraic spaces, hence quasi-compact formal algebraic spaces, and
representable by algebraic spaces and étale, so
`IsQuasiCompactOnReductions.isQuasiCompactSpace_of_isRepresentableEtale` applies to each fibre
product.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiCompactOnReductions.hasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} (h : IsQuasiCompactOnReductions B S hS f)
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    HasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies condition (4), with the reductions quantified over in place of Stacks 0AIN and with the source's own hypothesis that X and Y be formal algebraic spaces, which is what supplies the covering of Y that condition (4) asks for

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompact.hasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (3) implies condition (4).** A morphism of formal algebraic spaces
over `S` which is quasi-compact in the sense of Stacks 0AJC — every fibre product of it with an
affine scheme over `S` in the site mapping to its target is a quasi-compact formal algebraic
space — admits a covering of its target as in Definition 0AIM all of whose fibre products with
it are quasi-compact formal algebraic spaces.

Condition (3) implies condition (1) by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompact.isQuasiCompactOnReductions`, and condition (1)
implies condition (4).
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (4), with the source's own hypothesis that X and Y be formal algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.hasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (2) implies condition (4).** A morphism of formal algebraic spaces
over `S` every one of whose fibre products with a quasi-compact scheme over `S` in the site
mapping to its target is a quasi-compact formal algebraic space admits a covering of its target
as in Definition 0AIM all of whose fibre products with it are quasi-compact formal algebraic
spaces: condition (2) restricts to the affine schemes, which is condition (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.hasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} (h : IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f)
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    HasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (4), with the source's own hypothesis that X and Y be formal algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompact.isQuasiCompactOnReductions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (3) implies condition (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` such that every fibre product of `f` with an affine
scheme over `S` in the site mapping to `Y` is a quasi-compact formal algebraic space — that is,
let `f` be quasi-compact in the sense of Stacks 0AJC. Then every morphism between reductions of
`X` and of `Y` compatible with `f` is a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces.

Quasi-compactness of the morphism of reductions is tested against the quasi-compact algebraic
spaces mapping to the reduction of `Y`; such a space has, by Stacks 03H6, a surjective étale
chart by an *affine* scheme of the site, along which the test descends, so it suffices to treat
an affine scheme of the site, which is `isQuasiCompactSpaceULift_pullback_of_affine`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiCompact.isQuasiCompactOnReductions (hf : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiCompactOnReductions B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (1), with the reductions quantified over in place of Stacks 0AIN

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.isQuasiCompactOnReductions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (2) implies condition (1).** The fibre product condition over the
quasi-compact schemes over `S` in the site restricts to the affine ones, which already implies
quasi-compactness of every induced morphism of reductions.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.isQuasiCompactOnReductions
    (hf : IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f) :
    IsQuasiCompactOnReductions B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1), with the reductions quantified over in place of Stacks 0AIN

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas.isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB, condition (4) implies condition (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of fppf
sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` admitting a covering `{cⱼ : Yⱼ ⟶ Y}` as in Definition 0AIM
all of whose fibre products with `f` are quasi-compact formal algebraic spaces. Then every fibre
product of `f` with an affine scheme over `S` in the site mapping to `Y` is a quasi-compact formal
algebraic space; that is, `f` is quasi-compact in the sense of Stacks 0AJC.

Let `g : T ⟶ Y` with `T` affine. The base changes `Yⱼ ×_Y T` are objects `Vⱼ` of the site étale
over `T` (Stacks 0AIG); an affine open of some `Vⱼ` through each point of `T`, and
quasi-compactness of `T`, give finitely many affine objects `Uₖ` étale over `T`, covering it, each
mapping to a member `Yⱼ` compatibly with `g`. The fibre product `W = X ×_Y T` is covered along
representable étale morphisms by the finitely many `W ×_T Uₖ = X ×_Y Uₖ`, each of which is
quasi-compact by
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiCompactSpace_of_isPullback_comp`, so `W` is quasi-compact
by `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiCompactSpace_of_finite_isRepresentableEtale_cover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem HasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas.isQuasiCompact {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (h : HasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas B S hS f) : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f
declarations.comment: condition (4) implies condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.tfae_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJB.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S`. The
following are equivalent:

1. the morphism `f_red : X_red ⟶ Y_red` induced between the reductions (Stacks 0AIN) is a
   quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces;
2. for every quasi-compact scheme `T` over `S` in the site and morphism `T ⟶ Y`, the fibre product
   `X ×_Y T` is a quasi-compact formal algebraic space;
3. the same for every affine scheme `T` over `S` in the site;
4. there is a covering `{Yⱼ ⟶ Y}` as in Definition 0AIM such that every `X ×_Y Yⱼ` is a
   quasi-compact formal algebraic space.

The reductions in condition (1) are the chosen ones,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.reduction`, and `f_red` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.chosenReductionMap`. The cycle of implications is
(1) ⇒ (4) (`IsQuasiCompactOnReductions.hasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas`),
(4) ⇒ (3) (`HasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas.isQuasiCompact`),
(3) ⇒ (2) (`IsQuasiCompact.isQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges`)
and (2) ⇒ (1) (`IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges.isQuasiCompactULift_chosenReductionMap`).
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isQuasiCompact {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [Space.IsQuasiCompactULift.{u + 1} B S hS (chosenReductionMap B S hS hX hY f).hom,
        IsQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges B S hS f,
        IsQuasiCompact B S hS f,
        HasQuasiCompactFormalAtlas B S hS f]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of the four conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJC**, in the form of **Stacks 0AJB, condition (3)**. A morphism of formal
algebraic spaces over `S` is *quasi-compact* when every fibre product of it with an affine
scheme over `S` in the site mapping to its target is a quasi-compact formal algebraic space
over `S`. The condition makes sense, and is stated, for an arbitrary morphism of fppf sheaves
on the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsQuasiCompact {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: condition (3) of Stacks 0AJB taken as the definition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_colimit_presentation_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
An affine formal algebraic space over `S` is a directed colimit of algebraic spaces over `S`
along thickenings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_colimit_presentation_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) := Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
    ∃ (Λ : Type (u + 1)) (pre : Preorder Λ),
      letI : Preorder Λ := pre
      Nonempty Λ ∧ IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·) ∧
        ∃ D : Λ ⥤ AlgebraicSpaces B S hS,
          (∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (f : i ⟶ j), Space.IsThickeningHom B S hS (D.map f)) ∧
          Nonempty (X ≅ colimit (D ⋙ liftSheafFunctor B S hS))
declarations.comment: the conclusion for an AFFINE formal algebraic space only; the general quasi-compact quasi-separated case is not proved here, see the implementation notes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_colimit_presentation_of_quasiCompact_quasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B` and let `X` be a formal algebraic space
over `S` which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then `X` is a directed colimit of algebraic
spaces over `S` all of whose transition morphisms are thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_colimit_presentation_of_quasiCompact_quasiSeparated
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (_hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS X) :
    letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) := Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
    ∃ (Λ : Type (u + 1)) (pre : Preorder Λ),
      letI : Preorder Λ := pre
      Nonempty Λ ∧ IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·) ∧
        ∃ D : Λ ⥤ AlgebraicSpaces B S hS,
          (∀ ⦃i j : Λ⦄ (f : i ⟶ j), Space.IsThickeningHom B S hS (D.map f)) ∧
          Nonempty (X ≅ colimit (D ⋙ liftSheafFunctor B S hS))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyTopologicallyRingedSpace.exists_subfamily_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJF.** A quasi-compact formal scheme à la EGA carrying a fundamental system of weak
ideals of definition carries a fundamental system of genuine ideals of definition, over a finite
covering by affine formal open subschemes.

This is the remark's conclusion. Its hypothesis — the fundamental system of weak ideals of
definition — is what the translation of Stacks 0AJE supplies, and that *translation* is not
carried by this library, although Stacks 0AJE itself is; see the implementation notes of this
file. Here the class of opens is the class of
affine formal open subschemes, so the two geometric inputs of
`exists_subfamily_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn`
are discharged: the affine formal opens cover `X` because `X` is a formal scheme, and the ring of
sections over one of them is pre-admissible by Stacks 0AHY.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_subfamily_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFormalScheme
    {X : LTRS.{u}} [CompactSpace ↥X] (hX : IsFormalScheme X) (𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X))
    (hne : 𝒮.Nonempty)
    (hdir : ∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
      K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W)
    (hfund : IsFundamentalSystemOfWeakIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X)) :
    ∃ 𝒰 : Set (Opens X), 𝒰.Finite ∧ (∀ V ∈ 𝒰, IsAffineFormalOpen X V) ∧ sSup 𝒰 = ⊤ ∧
      ∃ 𝒮' : Set (IdealSheaf X), 𝒮' ⊆ 𝒮 ∧ 𝒮'.Nonempty ∧
        IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮' (· ∈ 𝒰)
declarations.comment: the shrinking of a fundamental system of WEAK ideals of definition to one of ideals of definition; the weak system is a hypothesis, see the implementation notes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFormalScheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJF.** Every quasi-compact and quasi-separated formal scheme à la EGA has a
fundamental system of ideals of definition: a nonempty family of ideal sheaves, sectionwise
directed, each of which is an ideal of definition over every affine formal open subscheme, and
whose ideals of sections over every affine formal open subscheme form a neighbourhood basis of
zero.

The members are the intersections `⋂ᵢ ker(Spec (Aᵢ/Jᵢ) ⟶ X)` over a finite covering by affine
formal charts `Spf Aᵢ`, which is the ideal of the scheme-theoretic image that the source's
induction produces; see the implementation notes. Quasi-separatedness is that of the underlying
space, which for a formal scheme à la EGA is quasi-separatedness of the formal scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn_of_isFormalScheme
    {X : LTRS.{u}} [CompactSpace ↥X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ↥X] (hX : IsFormalScheme X) :
    ∃ 𝒮 : Set (IdealSheaf X), 𝒮.Nonempty ∧
      (∀ I ∈ 𝒮, ∀ J ∈ 𝒮, ∃ K ∈ 𝒮, ∀ W : Opens X,
        K.ideal W ≤ I.ideal W ∧ K.ideal W ≤ J.ideal W) ∧
      IsFundamentalSystemOfIdealsOfDefinitionOn 𝒮 (IsAffineFormalOpen X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsLocallyOfFiniteType.of_isRepresentableEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJG.** A morphism of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces and étale is locally of finite type in the sense of
Stacks 0AM4. This is the instance of the theory of morphisms representable by algebraic spaces
that the rig-surjectivity theory of Stacks 0AQS and Stacks 0AQV asks for: étaleness of the
morphism of algebraic spaces cut out by a represented base change already makes it locally of
finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyOfFiniteType.of_isRepresentableEtale {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsRepresentableEtale B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f
declarations.comment: the theory of morphisms of algebraic spaces available to a morphism representable by algebraic spaces, in the instance this library uses it: a representable etale morphism is locally of finite type in the sense of Definition 0AM4

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_representable_over_isAffineFormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJH.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `Y` be an affine formal algebraic space over `S`,
and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` which is representable
by algebraic spaces. Then `X` is a formal algebraic space over `S`.

The affine étale charts of one stage `X₀ = Y₀ ×_Y X` are transported to `X` along the
representable thickening `X₀ ⟶ X`; the stages of a transported chart over the stages `Y_μ` of
`Y` are algebraic spaces over the affine `Y_μ` whose base change to `Y₀` is affine, hence affine
by the thickening case of Stacks 07VT
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineSpace_of_isClosedSubspace_of_isSurjective_terminal`), so each
transported chart is an affine formal algebraic space, and the charts cover `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_representable_over_isAffineFormal
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X
declarations.comment: the full statement, with no hypothesis beyond the source's: the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS on the source is proved, not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJI.** If `Y` is a formal algebraic space over `S` and `f : X ⟶ Y` is a morphism
of fppf sheaves representable by algebraic spaces, then `X` is a formal algebraic space over
`S`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_representable_over_formal`
with its hypotheses proved: the set-theoretic condition of `X` and of the base changed atlas
members by
`satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_of_isRepresentableByAlgSpacesULift_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace`
and Stacks 0AIU by its corrected form
`isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_colimit_isRepresentableThickeningULift`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom) :
    IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is *of finite type* when it is representable
by algebraic spaces and every base change of it along a scheme-valued point of its target is a
morphism of algebraic spaces which is of finite type. The condition is stated for an arbitrary
morphism of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFiniteType {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: representable plus Bootstrap finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsBootstrapFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is representable by algebraic spaces and of
finite type in the bootstrap sense of Stacks 03XZ when every base change of it along a
scheme-valued point of its target is a morphism of algebraic spaces which is of finite type. The
condition is stated for an arbitrary morphism of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsBootstrapFiniteType {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: condition (2): representable by algebraic spaces plus of finite type in the Bootstrap sense of Stacks 03XZ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFiniteType'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AM4, part (2)**, which is **Stacks 0AJJ, condition (1)**. A morphism of formal
algebraic spaces over `S` is *of finite type* when it is locally of finite type, in the sense
of Definition 0AM4, part (1), and quasi-compact, in the sense of Definition 0AJC. The
condition makes sense, and is stated, for an arbitrary morphism of fppf sheaves on the big
fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFiniteType' {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: condition (1): of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFiniteType_iff_isBootstrapFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJJ.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S`. Then
`f` is of finite type — locally of finite type and quasi-compact in the sense of Definition
0AJC — exactly when it is representable by algebraic spaces and of finite type in the
Bootstrap sense of Stacks 03XZ.

Both conditions contain being locally of finite type: the Bootstrap condition for being of
finite type is the conjunction of the Bootstrap condition for being locally of finite type
with the Bootstrap condition for being quasi-compact, which is the content of Stacks 03XF,
part (3), in the universe-lifted form of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.LargeValuedFiniteType`. What is left is the comparison
of Definition 0AJC with the Bootstrap condition for being quasi-compact, which is Stacks 0AM2
above. The witnesses that the source and the
target are formal algebraic spaces are not used, so the statement is for an arbitrary
morphism of fppf sheaves; each condition carries its own representability witness, so
representability is not a hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_iff_isBootstrapFiniteType {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsFiniteType' B S hS f ↔ IsBootstrapFiniteType B S hS f
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2), for an arbitrary morphism of fppf sheaves, representability by algebraic spaces being part of both conditions rather than a hypothesis

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.FiniteTypeAlgebraSystem.exists_uniform_generatedBy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJK, part (3): the uniform generator bound.** For an inverse system `(B_λ)` of
finite type algebras over the quotients of `A` by a fundamental system of weak ideals of
definition — the system Stacks 0AL1 attaches to a finite type morphism `Y → Spf(A)` of affine
formal algebraic spaces — there is a single integer `r`, independent of `λ`, such that `B_λ` is
generated by `r` elements over `A / I_λ` for every `λ`.

The index `r` is produced from one member of the system, chosen using nonemptiness of the index,
and transported to an arbitrary member through a common upper bound.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_generatedBy [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (P : FiniteTypeAlgebraSystem A I J) :
    ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ i : I, P.GeneratedBy r i
declarations.comment: part (3), the asserted sentence: for the inverse system `(B_λ)` of finite type `A / I_λ`-algebras that Stacks 0AL1 attaches to a finite type morphism `Y → X = Spf(A)` of affine formal algebraic spaces, there is a fixed integer `r` such that `B_λ` is generated by `r` elements over `A / I_λ` for all `λ`. The clause of part (3) citing Stacks 0AL1 for the presentation `Y = colim Spec(B_λ)` is covered by the anti-equivalence itself; the question part (3) goes on to ask, whether there is an example in which `Y` is not McQuillan, is a question and is not asserted anywhere.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_taut_formalSpectrumMap_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJK, part (1).** Let `A` be a weakly admissible topological ring over `S` whose
formal spectrum `X = Spf(A)` is an affine formal algebraic space, and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a
closed immersion. Then `Y` is a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space, and `f` corresponds to
a continuous homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ B` of weakly admissible topological rings — `Y` is
identified with `Spf(B)` and `f` with `Spf(φ)` — which is taut, whose kernel is a closed ideal
of `A`, and whose image is dense in `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_taut_formalSpectrumMap_of_isClosedImmersion
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A)
    (hX : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (formalSpectrum D))
    {Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : Y ⟶ formalSpectrum D) (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS Y ∧
      ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : TopologicalSpace C) (_ : IsTopologicalRing C)
        (_ : IsLinearTopology C C) (E : QuotientSystem B S hS C),
        TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C ∧
          ∃ (e : Y ≅ formalSpectrum E) (g : ContinuousHom D E),
            f = e.hom ≫ formalSpectrumMap hA g ∧ RingHom.IsTaut g.toRingHom ∧
              IsClosed (RingHom.ker g.toRingHom : Set A) ∧ DenseRange g.toRingHom
declarations.comment: part (1), every assertion of the item: for a closed immersion `f : Y → X` into `X = Spf(A)`, the source `Y` is McQuillan (condition (4) of Stacks 0AIC) and `f` corresponds to a continuous homomorphism `φ : A → B` of weakly admissible topological rings, `Y ≅ Spf(B)` with `f = Spf(φ)` through that isomorphism, which is taut, has closed kernel `K` and has dense image. The source `Y` is an arbitrary fppf sheaf here, which generalizes the item's affine formal algebraic space. The question the item ends with, which conditions on `A` force `B = (A/K)^∧`, is a question and is asserted nowhere. Part (2) of the remark is a question in its entirety and asserts nothing.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_finiteTypeAlgebraSystem_uniform_generatedBy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJK, part (3).** Let `A` be a weakly admissible topological ring over `S` whose
formal spectrum `X = Spf(A)` is an affine formal algebraic space, let `(I_λ)` be a fundamental
system of weak ideals of definition of `A`, and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a morphism of finite type
from an affine formal algebraic space. Then `Y = colim Spec(B_λ)` for an object `(B_λ)` of the
category `𝒞` of Stacks 0AL1 — the inverse system which the anti-equivalence of Stacks 0AL1
sends to `f` — and there is a single integer `r` such that `B_λ` is generated by `r` elements
over `A/I_λ` for every `λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteTypeAlgebraSystem_uniform_generatedBy
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A)
    (hX : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (formalSpectrum D))
    (I : Type v) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (J : IdealBasis A I)
    {Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hY : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (f : Y ⟶ formalSpectrum D) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) :
    ∃ P : FiniteTypeAlgebraSystem A I J,
      Nonempty ((finiteTypeAlgebraSystemAntiEquivalence B S hS A hA (formalSpectrum D)
          (hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_formalSpectrum_of_isAffine B S hS hA D hX)
          D.weakIdealColimitPresentation I J).functor.obj (Opposite.op P) ≅
            ⟨Over.mk f, hY, hf⟩) ∧
        ∃ r : ℕ, ∀ i : I, P.GeneratedBy r i
declarations.comment: part (3), every assertion of the item: a finite type morphism `f : Y → X` of affine formal algebraic spaces with `X = Spf(A)` gives `Y = colim Spec(B_λ)` for an object `(B_λ)` of the category `𝒞` of Stacks 0AL1, namely the object the anti-equivalence of Stacks 0AL1 sends to `f` (that functor is the colimit of the spectra of the terms), and one integer `r` generates every `B_λ` over `A/I_λ`. The question the item ends with, whether there is an example in which `Y` is not McQuillan, is a question and is asserted nowhere.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_taut_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_affineSpace_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJK, part (4).** Let `A` be a weakly admissible topological ring over `S` whose
formal spectrum `X = Spf(A)` is an affine formal algebraic space, and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a
morphism of finite type with `Y` a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space. Then `f`
corresponds to a continuous homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ B` of weakly admissible topological rings —
`Y` is identified with `Spf(B)` and `f` with `Spf(φ)` — which is taut and makes `B`
topologically of finite type over `A`. In other words `f` factors as
`Y ⟶ 𝔸ʳ_X ⟶ X`, where `𝔸ʳ_X = Spf A{x₁, …, xᵣ}` maps to `X` by `Spf` of the canonical
homomorphism and the first arrow is a closed immersion of McQuillan affine formal algebraic
spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_taut_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_affineSpace_factorization
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A)
    (hX : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (formalSpectrum D))
    {Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hYM : HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS Y)
    (f : Y ⟶ formalSpectrum D) (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) :
    ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : TopologicalSpace C) (_ : IsTopologicalRing C)
      (_ : IsLinearTopology C C) (E : QuotientSystem B S hS C),
      TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C ∧
        ∃ (e : Y ≅ formalSpectrum E) (g : ContinuousHom D E),
          f = e.hom ≫ formalSpectrumMap hA g ∧ RingHom.IsTaut g.toRingHom ∧
            TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType g.toRingHom ∧
            ∃ (r : ℕ) (E' : QuotientSystem B S hS
                (TopologicalRing.CompletionOver (MvPolynomial.C : A →+* MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)))
              (π : ContinuousHom D E') (ι : ContinuousHom E' E),
              π.toRingHom = TopologicalRing.CompletionOver.canonicalMap MvPolynomial.C ∧
                HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS (formalSpectrum E') ∧
                IsClosedImmersion B S hS (formalSpectrumMap
                  (TopologicalRing.completionOver_isWeaklyAdmissible MvPolynomial.C hA) ι) ∧
                f = e.hom ≫ formalSpectrumMap
                  (TopologicalRing.completionOver_isWeaklyAdmissible MvPolynomial.C hA) ι ≫
                    formalSpectrumMap hA π
declarations.comment: part (4), every assertion of the item: for a finite type `f : Y → X = Spf(A)` with `Y` McQuillan, `f` corresponds to a continuous homomorphism `φ : A → B` of weakly admissible topological rings, `Y ≅ Spf(B)` with `f = Spf(φ)` through that isomorphism; `φ` is taut, which is derived from `f` being of finite type through Stacks 0AN5 and 0AKN; `B` is topologically of finite type over `A`; and `f` factors as `Y → 𝔸ʳ_X → X` with `𝔸ʳ_X = Spf A{x_1, ..., x_r}` the formal spectrum of the completion of `A[x_1, ..., x_r]` over the weak ideals of definition of `A`, the second arrow `Spf` of the canonical map and the first a closed immersion, both its source and its target being McQuillan affine formal algebraic spaces. The item's closing remark that questions (1) and (2) are then in force for `Y → 𝔸ʳ_X` asserts nothing further.

registrations.name: finiteTypeAlgebraSystemAntiEquivalence
registrations.comment: part (3), the clause citing Stacks 0AL1: a morphism `f : Y → X = Spf(A)` of affine formal algebraic spaces which is of finite type corresponds to an object `(B_λ)` of the category `𝒞`, so that `Y = colim Spec(B_λ)`. The uniform bound part (3) asserts next, that one integer `r` generates every `B_λ` over `A/I_λ`, is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.FiniteTypeAlgebraSystem.exists_uniform_generatedBy` in this file. The question part (3) closes with, whether there is an example in which `Y` is not McQuillan, is a question and is asserted nowhere.

registrations.name: hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_of_isClosedImmersion
registrations.comment: part (1), the conclusion that `Y` is McQuillan: the source of a closed immersion of formal algebraic spaces whose target is a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space is again a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space. Part (1)'s conclusions about the presenting homomorphism `φ : A → B` are tagged separately. The question part (1) raises, which conditions on `A` force `B = (A/K)^∧`, is a question and is asserted nowhere.

registrations.name: isClosed_ker_toRingHom
registrations.comment: part (1), the conclusion that the kernel `K ⊂ A` of the homomorphism `φ : A → B` presenting a closed immersion is a closed ideal. It is proved here in the stronger form that needs only continuity of the homomorphism and separatedness of its target, so no closed-immersion hypothesis appears.

registrations.name: denseRange_of_isClosedImmersion_formalSpectrumMap
registrations.comment: part (1), the conclusion that the image `φ(A)` of the homomorphism `φ : A → B` presenting a closed immersion is dense in `B`. Whether `φ` is moreover surjective and open, equivalently whether `B` is the quotient `A/K` itself, is the question part (2) of the remark raises and is asserted nowhere.

registrations.name: isTaut_of_isClosedImmersion_formalSpectrumMap
registrations.comment: part (1), the conclusion that the homomorphism `φ : A → B` presenting a closed immersion is taut.

registrations.name: exists_formalSpectrumMap_of_isClosedImmersion
registrations.comment: part (1), the conclusion that `f` corresponds to a continuous homomorphism `φ : A → B` of weakly admissible topological rings: a closed immersion `f` into `X = Spf(A)` whose source `Y` is a formal algebraic space is `Spf(φ)` for a weakly admissible `B` presenting `Y`, read through the identification of `Y` with `Spf(B)`. The three conclusions part (1) draws about `φ` are tagged on `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isTaut_of_isClosedImmersion_formalSpectrumMap`, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosed_ker_toRingHom` and `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.denseRange_of_isClosedImmersion_formalSpectrumMap`, and that `Y` is McQuillan on `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_of_isClosedImmersion`.

registrations.name: isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_of_isFiniteType_formalSpectrumMap
registrations.comment: part (4), the conclusion that `B` is topologically of finite type over `A` for a finite type `f : Y → X` with `Y` McQuillan, and with it part (4)'s restatement that `f` factors as `Y → A^r_X → X` with the first arrow a closed immersion: the conclusion `TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType` produces the integer `r` together with a homomorphism `A[x_1, ..., x_r] → B` restricting to `φ` on constants and having dense image, which is that factorization and the dense image of its first arrow. Tautness of `φ`, part (4)'s other conclusion, is carried here as a hypothesis rather than deduced. Part (4) closes by observing that questions (1) and (2) are then in force for `Y → A^r_X`; those are questions and are asserted nowhere.

registrations.name: isTaut_and_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_of_isFiniteType_formalSpectrumMap'
registrations.comment: part (4), both of its conclusions, for a finite type `f : Y → X` with `Y` McQuillan: the homomorphism `f` comes from is taut, and its target is topologically of finite type over its source -- `φ : A → B` in the source's letters, `φ : A ⟶ C` here, the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological ring being McQuillan by construction. With the second goes part (4)'s restatement that `f` factors as `Y → A^r_X → X` with the first arrow a closed immersion: the conclusion `TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType` produces the integer `r` together with a homomorphism `A[x_1, ..., x_r] → C` restricting to `φ` on constants and having dense image, which is that factorization and the dense image of its first arrow. Neither conclusion is carried as a hypothesis: tautness is deduced from finite type, by the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 0AN5. Part (4) closes by observing that questions (1) and (2) are then in force for `Y → A^r_X`; those are questions and are asserted nowhere.

registrations.name: isTaut_and_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_of_isFiniteType_formalSpectrumMap
registrations.comment: part (4) in full. For a finite type `f : Y → X` with `Y` McQuillan, the homomorphism `φ : A → B` presenting `f` is taut and `B` is topologically of finite type over `A`, which are part (4)'s two conclusions; and with the second comes part (4)'s restatement that `f` factors as `Y → A^r_X → X` with the first arrow a closed immersion of McQuillan affine formal algebraic spaces, since `TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType` produces the integer `r` together with a homomorphism `A[x_1, ..., x_r] → B` restricting to `φ` on constants and having dense image, which is that factorization and the dense image of its first arrow. Part (4) closes by observing that questions (1) and (2) are then in force for `Y → A^r_X`; those are questions and are asserted nowhere.

declarations.name: RestrictedPowerSeries.existsUnique_continuousAlgHom_extends
declarations.doc:
The universal property of restricted power series: every polynomial algebra map into a
complete linearly topologized algebra extends by a unique continuous algebra map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_continuousAlgHom_extends
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    {C : Type x} [CommRing C] [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C]
    [IsLinearTopology C C] [Algebra A C]
    {ι : Type w} [Preorder ι] [Nonempty ι] [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)]
    (J : ι → Ideal A) (hJ : Antitone J)
    (_ : ∀ i, IsOpen (J i : Set A))
    (hfund : ∀ U ∈ nhds (0 : A), ∃ i, (J i : Set A) ⊆ U)
    (hAC : Continuous (algebraMap A C))
    (hC : TopologicalRing.IsComplete C)
    {σ : Type v} (f : MvPolynomial σ A →ₐ[A] C) :
    ∃! g : RestrictedPowerSeriesOfIdeals J hJ σ →ₐ[A] C,
      Continuous g ∧ g.comp (idealSystemPolynomialAlgHom J hJ σ) = f

declarations.name: Rig.adicQuotientFunctor
declarations.doc:
The functor which associates to an adically complete algebra `B` its inverse system
of quotients
`B ⧸ (I.map (algebraMap A B)) ^ (n + 1)`.

Its transition maps are the canonical quotient maps, and its action on morphisms is induced
by the underlying `A`-algebra maps.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def adicQuotientFunctor (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) :
    AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I ⥤
      AdicAlgebraSystem.{u, v} A I

declarations.name: Rig.exists_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial_quotient_equiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AJP.** An adically complete algebra of finite type modulo a
finitely generated ideal is a quotient of a completed polynomial algebra in finitely many
variables.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial_quotient_equiv
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) :
    ∃ r : ℕ,
      let P := AdicCompletion
        (I.map (MvPolynomial.C : A →+* MvPolynomial (Fin r) A))
        (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)
    ∃ J : Ideal P, Nonempty ((P ⧸ J) ≃ₐ[A] B.carrier)
declarations.comment: completed_polynomial_presentation

declarations.name: Rig.iAdicallyCompleteRing_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
The completion of a polynomial algebra is complete for the ideal extended
from the coefficient ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem iAdicallyCompleteRing_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial (hI : I.FG) :
    IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A
        (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)))
          (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A))))
      (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)))
        (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A))
declarations.comment: polynomial_completions

declarations.name: Rig.finiteType_quotient_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
The reduction modulo `I` of a completed polynomial algebra is of finite
type over `A ⧸ I`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteType_quotient_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial (hI : I.FG) :
    Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ I)
      ((AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)))
          (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)) ⧸
        I.map (algebraMap A
          (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)))
            (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A))))
declarations.comment: polynomial_completions

declarations.name: Rig.adicQuotientEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AJP.** The functor `(Bₙ) ↦ lim Bₙ` from systems of finite type
algebras over the quotients `A ⧸ Iⁿ` to adically complete algebras of finite type modulo `I` is
quasi-inverse to the functor `B ↦ (B ⧸ Iⁿ⁺¹B)` of [StacksProject 0AJN]: the two categories are
equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def adicQuotientEquivalence (hI : I.FG) :
    AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I ≌ AdicAlgebraSystem.{u, v} A I
declarations.comment: the functor (Bₙ) ↦ lim Bₙ is a quasi-inverse of the functor of 0AJN, so the two categories are equivalent

declarations.name: Rig.isNoetherianRing
declarations.doc:
Every adically complete algebra of finite type modulo an ideal over a Noetherian
commutative ring has a Noetherian underlying ring.
declarations.statement:
public instance isNoetherianRing {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {I : Ideal A} (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) :
    IsNoetherianRing B.carrier
declarations.comment: noetherian_objects

declarations.name: Rig.quotient_isAdicFiniteType
declarations.doc:
Every quotient of an adically complete algebra of finite type modulo an ideal over a
Noetherian ring is again an adically complete algebra of finite type modulo that ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quotient_isAdicFiniteType {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {I : Ideal A} (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I)
    (J : Ideal B.carrier) :
    IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A (B.carrier ⧸ J))) (B.carrier ⧸ J) ∧
      Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ I)
        ((B.carrier ⧸ J) ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A (B.carrier ⧸ J)))
declarations.comment: quotients_remain_objects

declarations.name: Rig.iAdicallyCompleteRing_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial_of_isNoetherianRing
declarations.doc:
The completion of the polynomial ring in `r` variables over a Noetherian ring is
complete for the ideal extended from the coefficient ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem iAdicallyCompleteRing_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial_of_isNoetherianRing :
    IsAdicComplete
      (I.map (algebraMap A
        (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)))
          (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A))))
      (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)))
        (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A))
declarations.comment: polynomial_completions

declarations.name: Rig.finiteType_quotient_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial_of_isNoetherianRing
declarations.doc:
The reduction modulo `I` of the completed polynomial ring in `r` variables is of
finite type over `A ⧸ I`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteType_quotient_adicCompletion_mvPolynomial_of_isNoetherianRing :
    Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ I)
      ((AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)))
          (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)) ⧸
        I.map (algebraMap A
          (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A)))
            (MvPolynomial (Fin r) A))))
declarations.comment: polynomial_completions

declarations.name: Rig.adicCompletion_isAdicallyComplete
declarations.doc:
The completion of a finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring is complete for the ideal
extended directly from the base ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_isAdicallyComplete
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (C : Type v) [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [Algebra.FiniteType A C] :
    IsAdicComplete
      (I.map (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)))
      (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)
declarations.comment: finite_type_completions

declarations.name: Rig.adicCompletion_finiteType_quotient
declarations.doc:
The quotient modulo the ideal from the base ring of the completion of a finite type algebra
is of finite type over the quotient of the base ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_finiteType_quotient
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (C : Type v) [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [Algebra.FiniteType A C] :
    Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ I)
      ((AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C) ⧸
        I.map (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)))
declarations.comment: finite_type_completions

declarations.name: Rig.completedNaiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
For a supplied presentation `B = A[x₁, …, xᵣ]̂ / J`, construct its completed naive
cotangent complex `J / J² → ⨁ i, B dxᵢ`. Its differential sends the class of a power
series `g ∈ J` to the tuple of its formal partial derivatives.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def completedNaiveCotangentComplex
    [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I)
    (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) : CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex P

declarations.name: Rig.CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex.isDerivedLimit_reductionTower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJS (2).**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `B` an object of
the category of Stacks 0AL4, presented as `B = A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩ / J`.  Then the completed naive
cotangent complex is the derived inverse limit of the naive cotangent complexes of the
reductions, `NL^∧_{B/A} = R lim NL_{Bₙ/Aₙ}` in `D(B)`: the inverse system `{NL_{Bₙ/Aₙ}}` has
surjective transition maps and `NL^∧_{B/A}` is its ordinary inverse limit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDerivedLimit_reductionTower [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (K : CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex P) :
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} B.carrier)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    IsDerivedLimit ((K.reductionTower ⋙ cochainComplexFunctor B.carrier) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Q) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K.cochainComplex)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Rig.CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex.nonempty_iso_reductionTower
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJS (1).**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `B` an object of
the category of Stacks 0AL4, presented as `B = A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩ / J`.  Then the pro-objects
`{NL^∧_{B/A} ⊗_B Bₙ}` and `{NL_{Bₙ/Aₙ}}` are *strictly* isomorphic: there is one shift making
the two systems isomorphic in the strict pro-category, and at every level the second system is
the naive cotangent complex of the induced presentation `Bₙ = Aₙ[x₁, …, x_r] / Jₙ` — the
conormal modules and the degree-`0` terms agree and the two differentials correspond.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_iso_reductionTower [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (K : CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex P) :
    Nonempty (proObj K.completedReductionTower ≅ proObj K.reductionTower) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (e₁ : (K.reductionTower.obj (op n)).X₁ ≃ₗ[B.carrier]
            (P.reductionGenerators n).toExtension.Cotangent)
          (e₀ : (K.reductionTower.obj (op n)).X₀ ≃ₗ[B.carrier]
            (P.reductionGenerators n).toExtension.CotangentSpace),
          ∀ x, e₀ ((K.reductionTower.obj (op n)).d x) =
            (P.reductionGenerators n).toExtension.cotangentComplex (e₁ x)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: TwoTermComplex.comp_eq_zero_of_two_term_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJT.** Let `K₁, K₂, K₃` be objects of `D(R)` with cohomology in degrees `-1` and
`0`, and let `φ : K₁ ⟶ K₂`, `ψ : K₂ ⟶ K₃`. If `H⁰(φ) = 0` and `H⁻¹(ψ) = 0`, then `φ ≫ ψ = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem comp_eq_zero_of_two_term_homology
    {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    (K₁ K₂ K₃ : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))
    (hK₁ : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj K₁))
    (_hK₂ : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj K₂))
    (hK₃ : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 →
      Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj K₃))
    (φ : K₁ ⟶ K₂) (ψ : K₂ ⟶ K₃)
    (hφ : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).map φ = 0)
    (hψ : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) (-1)).map ψ = 0) :
    φ ≫ ψ = 0

declarations.name: Rig.CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex.exists_annihilator_twoTerm_iff_forall_reducedComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJU, the equivalence of (0AJW) and (0AJX).**  For a completed polynomial
presentation `B = A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩ / J` of an object `B` of the category (Stacks 0AL4) over a
Noetherian ring `A`, the following are equivalent:

* some power of `I` annihilates `H^i(NL^∧_{B/A})` for `i = -1, 0`;
* some power of `I` annihilates `H^i(NL_{Bₙ/Aₙ})` for `i = -1, 0` and all `n ≥ 1`.

Here `NL_{Bₙ/Aₙ}` is `Rig.CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex.reducedComplex`, the object the
strict pro-isomorphism of Stacks 0AJS (1) produces: the quotient of `NL^∧_{B/A}` by the image
of `J ∩ Iⁿ A⟨x⟩` in degree `-1` and by `IⁿB · (⨁ B dxᵢ)` in degree `0`.  The forward
implication doubles the exponent and the backward one preserves it; see
`annihilatesCohomology_reducedComplex` and `annihilatesCohomology_twoTerm`.  Annihilation by
the ideal `IᶜB` is the source's elementwise condition by
`annihilatesCohomology_adicIdeal_pow_iff`, and the left-hand side is condition (3) on the
nose: `H⁻¹` is `LinearMap.ker K.differential` and `H⁰` is
`(Fin r → B) ⧸ LinearMap.range K.differential`.

The sublabel records that `NL_{Bₙ/Aₙ}` is taken in the shape Stacks 0AJS (1) produces; see
the implementation notes for the identifications that would be needed to read condition (4)
through `Algebra.naiveCotangentComplex Aₙ Bₙ` instead.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_annihilator_twoTerm_iff_forall_reducedComplex [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (K : CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex P) :
    (∃ c : ℕ, NaiveCotangent.AnnihilatesCohomology (B.adicIdeal ^ c) K.twoTerm) ↔
      ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ 1, NaiveCotangent.AnnihilatesCohomology (B.adicIdeal ^ c)
        (K.reducedComplex n)
declarations.comment: (3) iff (4) for the reduced complexes

declarations.name: Rig.isCohomologyAnnihilated_iff_isReductionCohomologyAnnihilated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJU, the equivalence of conditions (3) and (4).**  For a completed polynomial
presentation `B = A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩ / J` of an object `B` of the category (Stacks 0AL4) over a
Noetherian ring `A`, the following are equivalent:

* (3) some power `I^c` of `I` annihilates `H^{-1}` and `H^0` of `NL^∧_{B/A}`, that is, the
  kernel and the cokernel of the differential of `Rig.completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P`;
* (4) some power `I^c` of `I` annihilates, for every `n ≥ 1`, the degree-`1` and degree-`0`
  homology of `Algebra.naiveCotangentComplex Aₙ Bₙ`, where `Aₙ = A / Iⁿ` and `Bₙ = B / IⁿB`.

Condition (4) is the source's, and is *presentation-free*: `NL_{Bₙ/Aₙ}` is the naive cotangent
complex of the tautological presentation `Aₙ[Bₙ] → Bₙ` and its cohomology is the categorical
homology of a `HomologicalComplex.double`.  Three identifications turn it into a statement
about the presentation `Bₙ = Aₙ[x₁, …, x_r] / Jₙ` of Stacks 0AJS, through which the source's
argument runs: the homology of a `double` is the kernel and the cokernel of its differential;
those are independent of the presentation; and `reducedComplex n`, the quotient of
`NL^∧_{B/A}` by the image of `J ∩ Iⁿ A⟨x⟩` and by `IⁿB · (⨁ B dxᵢ)`, *is*
`NL(Bₙ = Aₙ[x] / Jₙ)`.  The transport of the annihilation statement across those is then
`Rig.CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex.exists_annihilator_twoTerm_iff_forall_reducedComplex`,
whose forward direction doubles the exponent and whose backward direction spends the shift of
Stacks 0AJS (1) and preserves it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohomologyAnnihilated_iff_isReductionCohomologyAnnihilated
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) :
    (∃ c : ℕ,
        (I ^ c).map (algebraMap A B.carrier) ≤
          Module.annihilator B.carrier
            (LinearMap.ker (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).differential) ∧
        (I ^ c).map (algebraMap A B.carrier) ≤
          Module.annihilator B.carrier
            ((Fin P.variableCount → B.carrier) ⧸
              LinearMap.range (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).differential)) ↔
      ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
        ∀ a : A, a ∈ I ^ c →
          ((Ideal.Quotient.mk ((I ^ n).map (algebraMap A B.carrier))
                (algebraMap A B.carrier a)) ∈
              Module.annihilator (B.carrier ⧸ (I ^ n).map (algebraMap A B.carrier))
                ((Algebra.naiveCotangentComplex (A ⧸ I ^ n)
                  (B.carrier ⧸ (I ^ n).map (algebraMap A B.carrier))).homology 1) ∧
            (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((I ^ n).map (algebraMap A B.carrier))
                (algebraMap A B.carrier a)) ∈
              Module.annihilator (B.carrier ⧸ (I ^ n).map (algebraMap A B.carrier))
                ((Algebra.naiveCotangentComplex (A ⧸ I ^ n)
                  (B.carrier ⧸ (I ^ n).map (algebraMap A B.carrier))).homology 0))

declarations.name: Rig.isRigEtale_iff_exists_annihilator_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJU, (1) ⇔ (3).**  For an `I`-adically complete `A`-algebra `B` of finite type
modulo `I` over a Noetherian ring `A`, and any completed polynomial presentation
`B = A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩ / J`, rig-étaleness of `B` over `(A, I)` is equivalent to the existence of a
`c` with `IᶜB` annihilating both cohomology modules `H⁻¹(NL^∧_{B/A}) = ker d` and
`H⁰(NL^∧_{B/A}) = coker d`.

Condition (1) is annihilation of the complex *in the derived category* and condition (3) is
annihilation of its cohomology, which is weaker for a general complex; the two agree here
because `NL^∧_{B/A}` has two terms and its degree-`0` term is free, so the annihilating scalar
is realised by an honest two-sided splitting of the differential.  Passing from (3) to (1) costs
a squaring of the ideal and passing back costs nothing, which is why the statement is an
equivalence of the *existence* of an exponent rather than of a fixed one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigEtale_iff_exists_annihilator_cohomology
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) :
    IsRigEtale B ↔
      ∃ c : ℕ,
        (I ^ c).map (algebraMap A B.carrier) ≤
          Module.annihilator B.carrier
            (LinearMap.ker (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).differential) ∧
        (I ^ c).map (algebraMap A B.carrier) ≤
          Module.annihilator B.carrier
            ((Fin P.variableCount → B.carrier) ⧸
              LinearMap.range (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).differential)

declarations.name: Rig.isArtinJacobian_of_isRigEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJU, (1) implies (6).**  A rig-étale adic algebra satisfies the elementwise
Jacobian criterion: for every `a ∈ I` there are an exponent `c` and elements
`f₁, …, f_r` of the kernel `J` of a completed polynomial presentation such that the Jacobian
determinant `det(∂fⱼ/∂xᵢ)` divides `a ^ c` in `B` and `a ^ c · J ⊆ (f₁, …, f_r) + J²`.

The proof is the one in the source.  Rig-étaleness gives an exponent `c₀` with
`a ^ c₀ · 𝟙 NL^∧_{B/A} = 0` in `D(B)`, hence by Stacks 0ALN(1) a two-sided retraction
`H : ⨁ i, B dxᵢ → J / J²` of the differential up to `a ^ c₀`
(`Rig.exists_linearMap_twoSided_of_smul_id_eq_zero`).  Taking `fᵢ ∈ J` representing `H(dxᵢ)`,
the identity `d ∘ H = a ^ c₀` says that the Jacobian matrix `(∂fⱼ/∂xᵢ)` is exactly
`a ^ c₀` times the identity, so its determinant is `a ^ (c₀ r)`; and `H ∘ d = a ^ c₀` is the
conormal Cramer relation.  The exponent is taken to be `c₀ (r + 1)`, which dominates both
`c₀ r` and `c₀`, the latter being needed when `r = 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isArtinJacobian_of_isRigEtale (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I)
    (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) (hB : IsRigEtale B) :
    ∀ a : A, a ∈ I →
      ∃ (c : ℕ) (f : Fin P.variableCount → P.ker),
        Matrix.det (fun i j : Fin P.variableCount =>
          P.toAlgHom ((completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).partialDeriv i
            (f j : P.completedPolynomialRing))) ∣ (algebraMap A B.carrier a) ^ c ∧
        ∀ g : P.ker,
          algebraMap A P.completedPolynomialRing (a ^ c) * (g : P.completedPolynomialRing) ∈
            Ideal.span (Set.range fun i => (f i : P.completedPolynomialRing)) + P.ker ^ 2
declarations.comment: (1) implies (6)

declarations.name: Rig.isArtinPreliminary_of_isArtinJacobian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJU, (6) ⇒ (5).**  If the Jacobian determinant of `f₁, …, f_r ∈ J` divides
`a ^ c`, then `a ^ c` annihilates `H⁰(NL^∧_{B/A})`.

Cramer's rule `M · adj(M) = det(M) · 1` puts `det(M) · eᵢ` in the image of the Jacobian matrix,
whose columns are images of the differential; so `det(M)`, and with it every multiple of it,
carries `⨁ i, B dxᵢ` into the image of the differential.  The second half of the two
conditions is literally the same sentence, so the exponent and the family carry over.
declarations.comment: (6) implies (5)

declarations.name: Rig.isCohomologyAnnihilated_of_isArtinPreliminary
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJU, (5) ⇒ (3).**  Condition (5) gives, for each `a ∈ I`, a power of `a`
annihilating both cohomology modules of `NL^∧_{B/A}`: for `H⁰` this is its first half and for
`H⁻¹` it is `Rig.pow_mem_annihilator_ker_differential_of_artinPreliminary`.  The scalars
annihilating both form an ideal of the Noetherian ring `B`, and every element of `IB` has a
power in it, so a single power of `IB` lies in it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohomologyAnnihilated_of_isArtinPreliminary
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B)
    (h : IsArtinPreliminary B P) : IsCohomologyAnnihilated B P
declarations.comment: (5) implies (3)

declarations.name: Rig.isRigEtale_iff_isJacobianCramerBounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJU, (1) ⇔ (7).**  Rig-étaleness of `B` over `(A, I)` is equivalent to the
Jacobian ideal and the Cramer ideal of *every* finite generating family of `J` each containing
a power of `IB`.

For a single family this is Stacks 0AJY,
`Rig.isRigEtale_iff_exists_pow_le_completedJacobianIdeal_and_completedCramerIdeal`; the
quantified form follows because `J` is a finitely generated ideal of the Noetherian ring
`A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩`, so at least one such family exists.

declarations.name: Rig.tfae_isRigEtale
declarations.statement:
public theorem tfae_isRigEtale (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I)
    (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) :
    List.TFAE [IsRigEtale B, IsDerivedAnnihilated B P, IsCohomologyAnnihilated B P,
      IsReductionCohomologyAnnihilated B, IsArtinPreliminary B P, IsArtinJacobian B P,
      IsJacobianCramerBounded B P]

declarations.name: Rig.isRigEtale_iff_exists_pow_le_completedJacobianIdeal_and_completedCramerIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AJY**, part (7) of Stacks 0AJU.  For an `I`-adically complete `A`-algebra `B` of
finite type modulo `I` over a Noetherian ring `A`, a completed polynomial presentation
`B = A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩ / J` and generators `f₁, …, f_t` of `J`, rig-étaleness of `B` over `(A, I)`
is equivalent to the Jacobian ideal and the Cramer ideal of `B` over `A` each containing a
power of `IB`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigEtale_iff_exists_pow_le_completedJacobianIdeal_and_completedCramerIdeal
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B) {t : ℕ}
    (f : Fin t → P.completedPolynomialRing) (hf : P.ker = Ideal.span (Set.range f)) :
    IsRigEtale B ↔
      ((∃ c : ℕ, (I ^ c).map (algebraMap A B.carrier) ≤ completedJacobianIdeal B P f) ∧
        ∃ c : ℕ, (I ^ c).map (algebraMap A B.carrier) ≤ completedCramerIdeal B P)
declarations.comment: (7) of 0AJU, as an equivalence with rig-étaleness

declarations.name: Rig.completedBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AK0.** If a positive power of `I₁` maps into the finitely generated
ideal `I₂`, then `B ↦ (B ⊗[A₁] A₂)⁁` is a functor between the categories of adically complete
algebras of finite type modulo `I₁` and `I₂`.

declarations.name: Rig.smul_id_of_completedBaseChangeFunctor
declarations.doc:
With `(A₁, I₁) → (A₂, I₂)` as in Stacks Remark 0AL5, witnessed by `hc` and `hmap`, a scalar
`f₁ ∈ B₁` acting by zero on `NL^∧_{B₁/A₁}` in `D(B₁)` has its image
`Rig.CompletedBaseChange.scalar` in the base change `B₂ = C.functor.obj B₁` acting by zero on
`NL^∧_{B₂/A₂}` in `D(B₂)`, for any completed polynomial presentations of the two algebras.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smul_id_of_completedBaseChangeFunctor
    (C : CompletedBaseChange (A₁ := A₁) (A₂ := A₂) (I₁ := I₁) (I₂ := I₂))
    (hc : 0 < c) (hmap : (I₁ ^ c).map (algebraMap A₁ A₂) ≤ I₂)
    (B₁ : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u₁, v} A₁ I₁)
    (P₁ : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I₁ B₁)
    (P₂ : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I₂ (C.functor.obj B₁)) (f₁ : B₁.carrier)
    (h : f₁ • 𝟙 (derivedCompletedNaiveCotangentComplex B₁ P₁) = 0) :
    C.scalar B₁ f₁ •
      𝟙 (derivedCompletedNaiveCotangentComplex (C.functor.obj B₁) P₂) = 0

declarations.name: Rig.exists_continuousAlgHom_add_variables
declarations.doc:
A continuous algebra map on restricted series can be perturbed by arbitrary increments
in the images of its finitely many variables.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_continuousAlgHom_add_variables
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    {C : Type w} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C]
    {σ : Type v}
    (ψ : RestrictedPowerSeries I σ →ₐ[A] C)
    (hψ : @Continuous _ _ (limitTopology I σ)
      ((I.map (algebraMap A C)).adicTopology) ψ)
    (δ : σ → C) :
    ∃! ψ' : RestrictedPowerSeries I σ →ₐ[A] C,
      @Continuous _ _ (limitTopology I σ)
        ((I.map (algebraMap A C)).adicTopology) ψ' ∧
      ∀ i, ψ' (polynomialAlgHom I σ (MvPolynomial.X i)) =
        ψ (polynomialAlgHom I σ (MvPolynomial.X i)) + δ i
declarations.comment: existence of the perturbed map

declarations.name: Rig.eval_add_variables_eq_linear_add_error
declarations.doc:
The evaluation of a perturbed restricted series is its original evaluation plus the
formal linear term, up to the ideal generated by pairwise products of increments.
declarations.statement:
public theorem eval_add_variables_eq_linear_add_error
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    {C : Type w} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C]
    {σ : Type v} [Fintype σ]
    (ψ ψ' : RestrictedPowerSeries I σ →ₐ[A] C)
    (hψ : @Continuous _ _ (limitTopology I σ)
      ((I.map (algebraMap A C)).adicTopology) ψ)
    (hψ' : @Continuous _ _ (limitTopology I σ)
      ((I.map (algebraMap A C)).adicTopology) ψ')
    (δ : σ → C)
    (hδ : ∀ i, ψ' (polynomialAlgHom I σ (MvPolynomial.X i)) =
      ψ (polynomialAlgHom I σ (MvPolynomial.X i)) + δ i)
    (g : RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) :
    ∃ ξ : C,
      ξ ∈ Ideal.span (Set.range (fun ij : σ × σ ↦ δ ij.1 * δ ij.2)) ∧
      ψ' g = ψ g + (∑ i, ψ (partialDerivative I i g) * δ i) + ξ
declarations.comment: linear approximation and quadratic error

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_etale_neighbourhood_algHom_approximation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AK4.** Let `A` be a Noetherian G-ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `B`, `C` finite type
`A`-algebras. Every `A`-algebra map `ψ` between the `I`-adic completions of `B` and `C` is
approximated, to every positive order `N`, by an `A`-algebra map `φ : B → C'` into an étale
`C`-algebra `C'` whose closed fibre agrees with that of `C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etale_neighbourhood_algHom_approximation
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (C : Type w)
    [CommRing A] (hA : IsGRing A)
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [Algebra.FiniteType A C]
    (I : Ideal A)
    (ψ : AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A B)) B →ₐ[A]
      AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)
    (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) :
    ∃ (C' : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing C') (_ : Algebra C C')
      (_ : Algebra A C') (_ : IsScalarTower A C C') (_ : Algebra.Etale C C')
      (φ : B →ₐ[A] C'),
      (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Bijective
          (Ideal.quotientMap (((I.map (algebraMap A C)) ^ n).map (algebraMap C C'))
            (algebraMap C C') Ideal.le_comap_map)) ∧
      Function.Bijective
          (Ideal.quotientMap ((I.map (algebraMap A C)).map (algebraMap C C'))
            (algebraMap C C') Ideal.le_comap_map) ∧
      ∀ b : B,
        Ideal.quotientMap (((I.map (algebraMap A C)) ^ N).map (algebraMap C C'))
            (algebraMap C C') Ideal.le_comap_map
            (AdicCompletion.evalₐ (I.map (algebraMap A C)) N
              (ψ (algebraMap B (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A B)) B) b))) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (((I.map (algebraMap A C)) ^ N).map (algebraMap C C')) (φ b)
declarations.comment: the full conclusion with NO carried hypotheses, for every `N ≥ 1`: an étale `C`-algebra `C'` inducing an isomorphism `C / IC ≅ C' / IC'` (indeed `C / (IC)^n ≅ C' / (IC)^n C'` for every `n`), and an `A`-algebra map `B → C'` agreeing modulo `I ^ N` with the given map of `I`-adic completions. Stacks 0AH5 is used, not assumed, and the `IsIndSmoothAdicCompletion` hypothesis it carries in place of the source's G-ring is discharged by Popescu's Theorem 07GC (`indSmooth_of_isRegularRingMap`) through `isIndSmoothAdicCompletion_of_isGRing`, applied once to the henselization of (C, IC), which is a G-ring by 0AH3 and whose completion map is regular by 0AH2. Stacks 0AKJ supplies the single étale stage.

declarations.name: Rig.exists_algHom_lift_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AK6.** Let `I = (a)` be a principal ideal of a Noetherian ring `A`, let `B` be an
`I`-adically complete `A`-algebra of finite type modulo `I`, and suppose `a ^ c` annihilates
`Ext¹_B(NL^∧_{B/A}, N)` for every `B`-module `N`. Let `C` be an `I`-adically complete
`A`-algebra on which `a` is a nonzerodivisor and let `n > 2c`. Then every `A`-algebra map
`B → C / aⁿC` agrees modulo `a ^ (n - c)` with the reduction of an `A`-algebra map `B → C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_algHom_lift_of_isRegular
    (a : A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I = Ideal.span {a})
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I)
    (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B)
    (c : ℕ)
    (hExt : ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{max u v} B.carrier)
      (ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).cochainComplex)
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} B.carrier) 0).obj N) 1),
      (algebraMap A B.carrier a) ^ c • ξ = 0)
    {C : Type w} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C]
    (ha : IsRegular (algebraMap A C a))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 * c < n)
    (ψn : B.carrier →ₐ[A] C ⧸ (I.map (algebraMap A C)) ^ n) :
    ∃ φ : B.carrier →ₐ[A] C,
      (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ A
        (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.sub_le n c))).comp ψn =
      (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A ((I.map (algebraMap A C)) ^ (n - c))).comp φ

declarations.name: Rig.exists_algHom_lift_of_torsion_disjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AK7.** Let `I = (a)` be a principal ideal of a Noetherian ring `A`, let `B` be
an `I`-adically complete `A`-algebra of finite type modulo `I`, and suppose `a ^ c`
annihilates `Ext¹_B(NL^∧_{B/A}, N)` for every `B`-module `N`. Let `C` be an `I`-adically
complete `A`-algebra whose `a`-power torsion `C[a^∞]` meets `a^d C` in `0`, and let
`n > max (2c) (c + d)`. Then every `A`-algebra map `B → C / aⁿC` agrees modulo `a ^ (n - c)`
with the reduction of an `A`-algebra map `B → C`.

This drops the regularity hypothesis of Stacks 0AK6: the torsion is killed, 0AK6 is applied
to `C / C[a^∞]`, and the resulting map is glued with the reduction of `ψₙ` along the
cartesian square of quotients of `C` by `C[a^∞]` and `a^{n-c}C`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_algHom_lift_of_torsion_disjoint
    (a : A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I = Ideal.span {a})
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I)
    (P : CompletedPolynomialPresentation I B)
    (c : ℕ)
    (hExt : ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{max u v} B.carrier)
      (ξ : DerivedCategory.Ext
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (completedNaiveCotangentComplex B P).cochainComplex)
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} B.carrier) 0).obj N) 1),
      (algebraMap A B.carrier a) ^ c • ξ = 0)
    {C : Type w} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C]
    (d : ℕ)
    (htorsion : Disjoint (torsionIdeal C (algebraMap A C a))
      ((I.map (algebraMap A C)) ^ d))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : max (2 * c) (c + d) < n)
    (ψn : B.carrier →ₐ[A] C ⧸ (I.map (algebraMap A C)) ^ n) :
    ∃ φ : B.carrier →ₐ[A] C,
      (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ A
        (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.sub_le n c))).comp ψn =
      (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A ((I.map (algebraMap A C)) ^ (n - c))).comp φ

declarations.name: Rig.exists_finiteType_algEquiv_adicCompletion_of_isRigEtale
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and `I ⊆ A` an ideal. If `B` is an object of
`Rig.AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra A I` which is rig-étale over `(A, I)`, then there is a finite type
`A`-algebra `C` and an isomorphism `B ≅ C^∧` with its `I`-adic completion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteType_algEquiv_adicCompletion_of_isRigEtale
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (hB : IsRigEtale B) :
    ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C),
      Algebra.FiniteType A C ∧
        Nonempty (B.carrier ≃ₐ[A] AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)

declarations.name: Rig.exists_isEtaleOutside_finiteType_algEquiv_of_isRigEtale_principal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKG, the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0AJU imply condition (8), over a
principal ideal.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and `I = (a)` a principal ideal. Let `B` be an
object of the category of `I`-adically complete `A`-algebras of finite type modulo `I` (Stacks
0AL4) which is rig-étale over `(A, I)`. Then there is a finite type `A`-algebra `C` with
`Spec(C) → Spec(A)` étale over `Spec(A) ∖ V(I)` and an isomorphism `B ≅ C^∧`.

Stacks 0ALS (`Rig.exists_finiteType_algEquiv_of_isRigEtale_principal`) algebraizes `B` over a
principal ideal, and
`Rig.exists_isEtaleOutside_finiteType_algEquiv_of_algEquiv_adicCompletion` improves the
algebraization to one étale off `V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isEtaleOutside_finiteType_algEquiv_of_isRigEtale_principal
    (hI : I.IsPrincipal) (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (hB : IsRigEtale B) :
    ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C),
      Algebra.FiniteType A C ∧ IsEtaleOutside I C ∧
        Nonempty (B.carrier ≃ₐ[A] AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)
declarations.comment: the converse implication, over a PRINCIPAL ideal: the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0AJU imply condition (8). Stacks 0ALS algebraizes a rig-étale object over a principal ideal and the improvement step above makes the algebraization étale over the complement of V(I); that improvement step, `Rig.exists_isEtaleOutside_finiteType_algEquiv_of_algEquiv_adicCompletion`, is proved for an arbitrary ideal

declarations.name: Rig.isRigEtale_iff_exists_isEtaleOutside_algEquiv
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `B` an `I`-adically complete `A`-algebra
with `A ⧸ I → B ⧸ IB` of finite type. Then `B` is rig-étale if and only if there is a finite type
`A`-algebra `C` with `Spec(C) → Spec(A)` étale over `Spec(A) ∖ V(I)` and an isomorphism
`B ≅ C^∧` of `A`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigEtale_iff_exists_isEtaleOutside_algEquiv
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] {I : Ideal A}
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) :
    IsRigEtale B ↔
      ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C),
        Algebra.FiniteType A C ∧ IsEtaleOutside I C ∧
          Nonempty (B.carrier ≃ₐ[A] AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)

declarations.name: Rig.isRigEtale_of_isEtaleOutside_of_algEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKG, condition (8) implies the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0AJU.**  Let `A`
be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `B` an `I`-adically complete `A`-algebra of finite
type modulo `I`.  If `B` is isomorphic as an `A`-algebra to the `I`-adic completion `C^∧` of a
finite type `A`-algebra `C` with `Spec(C) → Spec(A)` étale over `Spec(A) ∖ V(I)`, then `B` is
rig-étale over `(A, I)`.

This is Stacks 0ALQ, part (1) applied to `C`, followed by the invariance of rig-étaleness
under isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigEtale_of_isEtaleOutside_of_algEquiv
    {B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, w} A I} {C : Type v} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [Algebra.FiniteType A C] (hC : IsEtaleOutside I C)
    (e : B.carrier ≃ₐ[A] (adicCompletionObj I (B := C)).carrier) :
    IsRigEtale B
declarations.comment: condition (8) implies the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0AJU; the converse implication is not covered, since it rests on the algebraization lemma — that a rig-étale object of this category is the completion of a finite type algebra — which this library does not carry

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Unramified.finite_morphisms_over_of_unramified
declarations.doc:
There are finitely many morphisms over a Noetherian base from a Noetherian scheme to a
quasi-compact unramified scheme.

declarations.name: Rig.exists_etale_factorization_algHom_henselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AKJ (étale factorization).** Every map from a
finite type algebra to the henselization of `(C, IC)` factors through an
étale `C`-algebra whose closed fibre is canonically isomorphic to that of
`C`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_etale_factorization_algHom_henselization
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (C : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (I : Ideal A)
    [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] :
    let H := (henselization C (I.map (algebraMap A C)) : Type w)
    letI : Algebra A H :=
      ((algebraMap C H).comp (algebraMap A C)).toAlgebra
    letI : IsScalarTower A C H :=
      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
    ∀ f : B →ₐ[A] H,
    ∃ (Cp : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing Cp) (_ : Algebra C Cp)
      (_ : Algebra A Cp) (_ : IsScalarTower A C Cp) (_ : Algebra.Etale C Cp)
      (g : B →ₐ[A] Cp)
      (k : Cp →ₐ[C] H),
      Function.Bijective
        (Ideal.quotientMap ((I.map (algebraMap A C)).map (algebraMap C Cp))
          (algebraMap C Cp) Ideal.le_comap_map) ∧
        (k.restrictScalars A).comp g = f
declarations.comment: étale factorization

declarations.name: Rig.exists_unique_algHom_henselization_of_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AKJ (descent and uniqueness).**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring,
`I ⊆ A` an ideal and `B` a finite type `A`-algebra such that `Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is étale over
`Spec(A) ∖ V(I)`, and let `C` be a Noetherian `A`-algebra.  Then every `A`-algebra map
`B^∧ → C^∧` of `I`-adic completions comes from a *unique* `A`-algebra map `B → Cʰ` into the
henselization of the pair `(C, IC)`.

Uniqueness is `Rig.eq_of_henselizationToAdicCompletion_comp_eq`, which rests on the fact that
`Cʰ` is a subring of `C^∧`.  For existence, follow the source and replace `(A, I, B, C)` by
`(C, IC, C ⊗_A B, C)`: the given map makes `D = C ⊗_A B` a `C`-algebra over `C^∧`, and the
étaleness hypothesis, which annihilates `Ω_{B/A}` by a power of `I`, annihilates `Ω_{D/C}` by
the same power after base change.  `exists_algHom_henselization_of_annihilator_kaehlerDifferential`
then lifts `D → C^∧` to `D → Cʰ`, and restricting along `B → D` gives the map sought.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_unique_algHom_henselization_of_adicCompletion
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (C : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (I : Ideal A) (hEtale : IsEtaleOutside I B)
    [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [IsNoetherianRing C] :
    let H := (henselization C (I.map (algebraMap A C)) : Type w)
    letI : Algebra A H :=
      ((algebraMap C H).comp (algebraMap A C)).toAlgebra
    letI : IsScalarTower A C H :=
      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
    ∀ φ : AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A B)) B →ₐ[A]
          AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C,
        ∃! ψ : B →ₐ[A] H,
          ((henselizationToAdicCompletion C
            (I.map (algebraMap A C))).val.restrictScalars A).comp ψ =
            φ.comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom A B
