              (AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A B)) B))
declarations.comment: descent and uniqueness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isAlgebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**The analogue of [Stacks, Tag 0A0I] for morphisms of algebraic stacks, [HL-P, Theorem 6.5],
which is the content of the last sentence of [Stacks, Tag 0AKL].** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a
1-morphism of algebraic stacks over `S`, let `τ` be a topology coarser than the fppf one (any of
the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf topologies), and consider the morphism of ringed
topoi `(Sh(𝒳_τ), 𝒪_𝒳) ⟶ (Sh(𝒴_τ), 𝒪_𝒴)` that `f` induces (Stacks 06TW). Let `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪_𝒴` be a sheaf
of ideals of finite type and let `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_𝒳`. Then the canonical comparison map

`(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`

is invertible for every object `K` of `D(𝒪_𝒳)`, the completion on `𝒴` being taken along `ℐ` and
the one on `𝒳` along `ℐ'`. In particular `Rf_*(ℱ^∧) = (Rf_*ℱ)^∧` for every complex of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-modules `ℱ`, which is the form in which the remark states it, and every
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type is an admissible `ℐ`.

The ideal `ℐ'` is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.inverseImageIdealSheaf`, the sheaf of ideals
generated by `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ)`; the relation between `ℐ` and `ℐ'` that the comparison map needs, and
finite type of `ℐ'`, are theorems about that construction. The two algebraic stacks are taken
with objects and morphisms in `Type (u + 1)` and the structure sheaves with sections in
`Type (u + 1)`; see the module documentation for why.

It is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_fullRingedToposHom`,
which needs only that `𝒳` and `𝒴` are fibred in groupoids — the first clause of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAlgebraicStack`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isAlgebraicStack
    {𝒳 𝒴 : BasedCategory.{u + 1, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS)}
    (h𝒳 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (h𝒴 : IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)
    (f : 𝒳 ⥤ᵇ 𝒴)
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
      (fullRingedTopos.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS 𝒴.p τ
        (liftedStructureSheaf.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS 𝒴.p τ h𝒴.fst hτ)).toRingedSite.O)))
    [I.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType]
    (K : letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard; DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (fullRingedTopos.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.p τ
          (liftedStructureSheaf.{u, u + 1, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳.p τ h𝒳.fst hτ)).toRingedSite.O))) :
    IsIso ((RingedToposHom.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison
      (fullRingedToposHom B S hS 𝒳.p 𝒴.p f.toFunctor h𝒳.fst h𝒴.fst τ hτ
        (.of_isFiberedInGroupoids h𝒴.fst f.w)) I
      (RingedToposHom.inverseImageIdealSheaf.{u + 1}
        (fullRingedToposHom B S hS 𝒳.p 𝒴.p f.toFunctor h𝒳.fst h𝒴.fst τ hτ
          (.of_isFiberedInGroupoids h𝒴.fst f.w)) I)
      (RingedToposHom.idealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf.{u + 1}
        (fullRingedToposHom B S hS 𝒳.p 𝒴.p f.toFunctor h𝒳.fst h𝒴.fst τ hτ
          (.of_isFiberedInGroupoids h𝒴.fst f.w)) I)).app K)
declarations.comment: the mathematical content of Remark 52.7.4, which is its fifth and last sentence: the analogue of Equation 52.7.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0A0I] for complexes of quasi-coherent modules, [HL-P, Theorem 6.5], here for a 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of **algebraic stacks** over `S`. For the morphism of ringed topoi `(Sh(𝒳_τ), 𝒪_𝒳) ⟶ (Sh(𝒴_τ), 𝒪_𝒴)` that `f` induces, at any topology `τ` coarser than the fppf one, a sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪_𝒴` of finite type and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_𝒳`, the canonical comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible for **every** object `K` of `D(𝒪_𝒳)`, so in particular for every complex of quasi-coherent modules, and every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type is an admissible `ℐ`. The proof is [Stacks, Tag 0A0G] for an arbitrary morphism of ringed topoi, `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType`, at the morphism of ringed topoi of [Stacks, Tag 06TW], `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fullRingedToposHom`; it holds for every 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_fullRingedToposHom`. The stacks have objects and morphisms in `Type (u + 1)` and the structure sheaves sections in `Type (u + 1)`, the seating at which the library's derived completion on a ringed topos is defined. The remark's first four sentences are bibliography — pointers to [lurie-thesis, Theorem 6.3.1] for a derived formal functions theorem for proper maps, to [dag12, Chapter 4] with the cross-reference to More on Algebra, Section 091N for the affine story, and to [G-R, Section 2.9] for proper base change and derived completion via (ind) coherent modules — and carry no formalizable statement. [HL-P, Theorem 6.5] is also stated for morphisms of **derived** algebraic stacks; derived algebraic stacks are not defined in this library, so that part of the reference's setting is outside it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isFiniteType_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**Equation 52.7.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0A0I] in the display's own setting and at the source's
own data, for a derived-complete object.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let
`ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_S` be a sheaf of ideals of finite type and let `ℐ' ⊆ 𝒪_X` be a sheaf of ideals of finite
type with `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ) ⊆ ℐ'` — which the display's `f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` is. Then
`(Rf_*ℱ)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(ℱ^∧)` is invertible for every `ℱ ∈ D(𝒪_X)` derived complete along `ℐ'`.

This is the display at the hypotheses Section 52.7 writes it under. The source asks `ℐ` to be a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type and `ℱ` to be quasi-coherent, and uses those
hypotheses only through [Stacks, Tag 099F], to know the two derived completion functors exist;
here finite type alone produces them, by
`Stacks.RingedSpace.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_of_isFiniteType`, so quasi-coherence is
not needed and the statement applies in particular to every quasi-coherent `ℐ` of finite type
and every complex of quasi-coherent modules derived complete along `ℐ'`.

Because `ℱ` ranges over all the objects of `D(𝒪_X)` derived complete along `ℐ'`, this is also
the analogue of the display *for complexes of quasi-coherent modules* that the fifth and last
sentence of [Stacks, Tag 0AKL] attributes to [HL-P, Theorem 6.5], at a morphism of schemes. At
a morphism of algebraic stacks, for an arbitrary object, that analogue is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isAlgebraicStack` of
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionAlgebraicStacks.lean`; derived algebraic stacks, the other half of
the setting of that reference, are not defined in this library.

The restriction to a derived-complete `ℱ` is on the object, not on the data: the invertibility
for an arbitrary `ℱ` is the assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0A0G], and it is proved — at a morphism of
ringed *sites* and at the constructed `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` rather than at an independent
parameter `ℐ'` — by
`RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType`,
and at a morphism of schemes and a quasi-coherent `ℐ` of finite type by
`Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf`.
declarations.comment: the mathematical content of Remark 52.7.4, which is its fifth and last sentence: the analogue of Equation 52.7.0.1 for complexes of quasi-coherent modules, [HL-P, Theorem 6.5]. What is proved here is that analogue at a morphism of **schemes**, at the source's own data — two sheaves of ideals of finite type, `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_S` and `ℐ' ⊆ 𝒪_X` with `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ) ⊆ ℐ'` — for every object of `D(𝒪_X)` derived complete along `ℐ'`, hence for every complex of quasi-coherent modules derived complete along `ℐ'`, with both derived completion functors produced from the finite-type hypotheses by [Stacks, Tag 099F]. The remark's first four sentences are bibliography — pointers to [lurie-thesis, Theorem 6.3.1] for a derived formal functions theorem for proper maps, to [dag12, Chapter 4] with the cross-reference to More on Algebra, Section 091N for the affine story, and to [G-R, Section 2.9] for proper base change and derived completion via (ind) coherent modules — and carry no formalizable statement. At a morphism of algebraic stacks the analogue is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isAlgebraicStack`; derived algebraic stacks, the other half of the setting of [HL-P, Theorem 6.5], are not defined in this library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**Equation 52.7.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0A0I] at Section 52.7's own data, for a derived-complete
object.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_S` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of
ideals of finite type and let `ℐ' ⊆ 𝒪_X` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type with
`f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ) ⊆ ℐ'` — which the display's `f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` is. Then `(Rf_*ℱ)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(ℱ^∧)` is
invertible for every `ℱ ∈ D(𝒪_X)` derived complete along `ℐ'`, in particular for every such
complex of quasi-coherent modules.

This is the display written at the hypotheses Section 52.7 states it under, in the library's own
scheme-theoretic vocabulary: `ℐ` and `ℐ'` are `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData`, so
quasi-coherent, and the finite-type hypothesis is `SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType` — locally
generated by finitely many sections. It is
`isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isFiniteType_of_isDerivedComplete` above at
those sheaves of ideals, and the only thing the hypotheses are used for is [Stacks, Tag 099F],
which is what produces the two derived completion functors.

Because `ℱ` ranges over the objects of `D(𝒪_X)` derived complete along `ℐ'` and not over
quasi-coherent sheaves alone, this is also the analogue of the display *for complexes of
quasi-coherent modules* that the fifth and last sentence of [Stacks, Tag 0AKL] attributes to
[HL-P, Theorem 6.5], at a morphism of schemes.

The restriction to a derived-complete `ℱ` is on the object, not on the data: the invertibility
for an arbitrary `ℱ` is the assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0A0G], and it is proved — at a morphism of
ringed *sites* and at the constructed `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` rather than at an independent
parameter `ℐ'` — by
`RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType`,
and at a morphism of schemes and a quasi-coherent `ℐ` of finite type by
`Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf`.
declarations.comment: the mathematical content of Remark 52.7.4, which is its fifth and last sentence: the analogue of Equation 52.7.0.1 for complexes of quasi-coherent modules, [HL-P, Theorem 6.5]. What is proved here is that analogue at a morphism of **schemes** and at Section 52.7's own data — two **quasi-coherent** sheaves of ideals **of finite type**, `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_S` and `ℐ' ⊆ 𝒪_X` with `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ) ⊆ ℐ'` — for every object of `D(𝒪_X)` derived complete along `ℐ'`, hence for every complex of quasi-coherent modules derived complete along `ℐ'`. Both derived completion functors are produced from the finite-type hypothesis by [Stacks, Tag 099F]. The remark's first four sentences are bibliography — pointers to [lurie-thesis, Theorem 6.3.1] for a derived formal functions theorem for proper maps, to [dag12, Chapter 4] with the cross-reference to More on Algebra, Section 091N for the affine story, and to [G-R, Section 2.9] for proper base change and derived completion via (ind) coherent modules — and carry no formalizable statement. At a morphism of algebraic stacks the analogue is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isAlgebraicStack`; derived algebraic stacks, the other half of the setting of [HL-P, Theorem 6.5], are not defined in this library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Equation 52.7.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0A0I] at Section 52.7's own data, for an arbitrary
object — and so the analogue for complexes of quasi-coherent modules of [Stacks, Tag 0AKL].** Let
`f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_S` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite
type and let `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` be the sheaf of ideals Section 52.7 builds out of it. Then the
canonical comparison map

`(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`

is invertible for **every** object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)`, the completion on `S` being taken along `ℐ`
and the one on `X` along `ℐ'`. In particular it is invertible for every complex of
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules, with no derived-completeness or nilpotence restriction.

`ℐ` is an `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData`, read on the small Zariski ringed site by
`Stacks.Algebraization.idealSheafSiteSubmodule`, and "of finite type" is
`SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType` (automatic on a locally Noetherian scheme, by
`Stacks.Algebraization.isFiniteType_idealSheafSiteSubmodule`). The sheaf of ideals `ℐ'` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.inverseImageIdealSheaf`, the image of `f^*ℐ ⟶ 𝒪_X`; that `f^♯`
carries `f^{-1}ℐ` into it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.pushforwardIdealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf`, and that it is of
finite type — so that the derived completion along it exists, by [Stacks, Tag 099F] — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isFiniteType_inverseImageIdealSheaf`. Neither is a hypothesis.

This is
`RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_inverseImageIdealSheaf_of_isFiniteType`,
the ringed-sites case of [Stacks, Tag 0A0G], at the morphism of ringed sites
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.toRingedSiteHom f` underlying `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf
    [(idealSheafSiteSubmodule I).toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType]
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (Stacks.RingedSpace.toRingedSite X.toRingedSpace).O)))) :
    IsIso ((RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison (toRingedSiteHom f)
      (idealSheafSiteSubmodule I)
      (RingedSite.inverseImageIdealSheaf.{u} (toRingedSiteHom f) (idealSheafSiteSubmodule I))
      (RingedSite.pushforwardIdealCompatible_inverseImageIdealSheaf.{u} (toRingedSiteHom f)
        (idealSheafSiteSubmodule I))).app K)
declarations.comment: the mathematical content of Remark 52.7.4, which is its fifth and last sentence: the analogue of Equation 52.7.0.1 for complexes of quasi-coherent modules, [HL-P, Theorem 6.5]. Proved here at a morphism of **schemes** `f : X ⟶ S` and at Section 52.7's own data — a **quasi-coherent** sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_S` **of finite type** and the sheaf of ideals `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` built out of it — for an **arbitrary** object of `D(𝒪_X)`, hence for every complex of quasi-coherent modules, with no derived-completeness or nilpotence restriction: the canonical comparison map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible. That `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ) ⊆ ℐ'` and that `ℐ'` is of finite type are theorems about the construction, not hypotheses. The remark's first four sentences are bibliography — pointers to [lurie-thesis, Theorem 6.3.1] for a derived formal functions theorem for proper maps, to [dag12, Chapter 4] with the cross-reference to More on Algebra, Section 091N for the affine story, and to [G-R, Section 2.9] for proper base change and derived completion via (ind) coherent modules — and carry no formalizable statement. At a morphism of algebraic stacks the analogue is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isAlgebraicStack`; derived algebraic stacks, the other half of the setting of [HL-P, Theorem 6.5], are not defined in this library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0I] in the display's own setting, for a derived-complete object, with
nothing assumed.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes, let `ℐ = (t_1, …, t_s) ⊆ 𝒪_S` and
`ℐ' = (g_1, …, g_r) ⊆ 𝒪_X` be the sheaves of ideals generated by finitely many global sections
of the two structure sheaves, with `f^♯(f^{-1}ℐ) ⊆ ℐ'` — which the display's `f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`
satisfies. Then `(Rf_*ℱ)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(ℱ^∧)` is invertible for every `ℱ ∈ D(𝒪_X)` derived complete
along `ℐ'`.

Both derived completion functors are produced from the generators, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf`, so
[Stacks, Tag 099F] is nowhere a hypothesis; neither quasi-coherence nor finite type nor
quasi-coherence of `ℱ` is assumed either, those entering the source only through that tag. The
restriction to a derived-complete `ℱ` is the tag's own content and remains; the invertibility
for an arbitrary `ℱ` is the assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0A0G]. The descent from a globally
generated `ℐ` to a finite-type one is carried out in
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionFiniteType.lean`, where the derived completion functors come from
[Stacks, Tag 099F] at a sheaf of ideals of finite type; this statement is the case of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`
`.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isFiniteType_of_isDerivedComplete` there in
which the two sheaves of ideals are generated by global sections.

Because `ℱ` ranges over the derived-complete objects of `D(𝒪_X)` and not over quasi-coherent
sheaves alone, this is also the analogue of the display *for complexes of quasi-coherent
modules* that the fifth and last sentence of [Stacks, Tag 0AKL] attributes to
[HL-P, Theorem 6.5]; related statements are
`isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isFiniteType_of_isDerivedComplete` of
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionFiniteType.lean`, the same statement at two sheaves of ideals of
finite type, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_forall_isNilpotent` of
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionSpaces.lean`, which takes an arbitrary object in the nilpotent
regime and whose module documentation accounts for the remark sentence by sentence.
declarations.comment: the mathematical content of Remark 52.7.4 — its fifth and last sentence, the analogue of Equation 52.7.0.1 for complexes of quasi-coherent modules, [HL-P, Theorem 6.5] — in the second of the two regimes this library reaches for it. Proved here: that analogue at a morphism of **schemes**, for an object of `D(𝒪_X)` that is **derived complete** along `ℐ'`, with `ℐ` and `ℐ'` generated by finitely many global sections of the two structure sheaves, out of which both derived completion functors are built. The objects covered are therefore the derived-complete complexes of quasi-coherent modules, at ideal sheaves on which the only demand is those generators. The same analogue at two sheaves of ideals of finite type, which is the source's own hypothesis on the data, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme``.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isFiniteType_of_isDerivedComplete` of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionFiniteType.lean`, and for an arbitrary complex, at a quasi-coherent `ℐ` of finite type and `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`, it is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme``.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf` of the same file. At a morphism of algebraic stacks the analogue is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isAlgebraicStack` of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionAlgebraicStacks.lean`; derived algebraic stacks, the other half of the setting of [HL-P, Theorem 6.5], are not defined in this library. The remark's first four sentences are bibliography — pointers to [lurie-thesis, Theorem 6.3.1] for a derived formal functions theorem for proper maps, to [dag12, Chapter 4] with the cross-reference to More on Algebra, Section 091N for the affine story, and to [G-R, Section 2.9] for proper base change and derived completion via (ind) coherent modules — and carry no formalizable statement. A further registration, which takes an **arbitrary** object in the regime where the local sections of both ideal sheaves are nilpotent, is in `PushforwardCommutesCompletionSpaces.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_forall_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**Equation 52.7.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0A0I] in the display's own setting, for an arbitrary
object**, when the local sections of `ℐ` and of `ℐ'` are nilpotent: the comparison
`(Rf_*ℱ)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(ℱ^∧)` is invertible for every `ℱ ∈ D(𝒪_X)`, in particular for every
quasi-coherent `ℱ`, with no hypothesis on `ℱ`.

The restriction is on the two sheaves of ideals, not on `ℱ`, and it *discharges* the conclusion
of [Stacks, Tag 099F] on `X` and on `S` rather than assuming it: this statement has no instance
hypothesis. It is not the general case of the display — nilpotence is not the source's
hypothesis, and in that regime both derived completion functors are the identity. The display at
the source's own data, two sheaves of ideals of finite type, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`
`.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isFiniteType_of_isDerivedComplete` of
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionFiniteType.lean`, for an object derived complete along `ℐ'`.
An arbitrary object, at a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ` of finite type and
`ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X`, is
`Scheme.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf` of
the same file.

Because `ℱ` ranges over all of `D(𝒪_X)`, this is also the analogue of the display *for complexes
of quasi-coherent modules* that the fifth and last sentence of [Stacks, Tag 0AKL] attributes to
[HL-P, Theorem 6.5], in the nilpotent regime. The derived-complete case of that remark is, at two
sheaves of ideals of finite type, `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`
`.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isFiniteType_of_isDerivedComplete` of
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionFiniteType.lean`, and at ideal sheaves generated by finitely many
global sections, `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`
`.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_generatedIdealSheaf_of_isDerivedComplete` of
`PushforwardCommutesCompletionGenerated.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_forall_isNilpotent
    (hnil : ∀ (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X.toRingedSpace.carrier)
      (g : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (Stacks.RingedSpace.toRingedSite X.toRingedSpace).O)).obj.obj (op V)),
      g ∈ I'.toSubmodule.obj (op V) → IsNilpotent g)
    (hnil' : ∀ (W : TopologicalSpace.Opens S.toRingedSpace.carrier)
      (s : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (Stacks.RingedSpace.toRingedSite S.toRingedSpace).O)).obj.obj (op W)),
      s ∈ I.toSubmodule.obj (op W) → IsNilpotent s)
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
        (Stacks.RingedSpace.toRingedSite X.toRingedSpace).O)))) :
    letI : (ObjectProperty.ι (RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u}
        (Stacks.RingedSpace.toRingedSite X.toRingedSpace) I')).IsRightAdjoint :=
      RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_of_forall_isNilpotent
        (Stacks.RingedSpace.toRingedSite X.toRingedSpace) I' hnil
    letI : (ObjectProperty.ι (RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u}
        (Stacks.RingedSpace.toRingedSite S.toRingedSpace) I)).IsRightAdjoint :=
      RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_of_forall_isNilpotent
        (Stacks.RingedSpace.toRingedSite S.toRingedSpace) I hnil'
    IsIso ((RingedSite.derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison
      (toRingedSiteHom f) I I' hI).app K)

  the analogue of Equation 52.7.0.1 for complexes of quasi-coherent modules, [HL-P,

  An arbitrary complex at a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of finite type and
  `ℐ' = f^{-1}ℐ · 𝒪_X` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme`
  `.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_idealSheafData_inverseImageIdealSheaf` of
  `PushforwardCommutesCompletionFiniteType.lean`. At a morphism of algebraic stacks it is

  of `PushforwardCommutesCompletionAlgebraicStacks.lean`; derived algebraic stacks, the other
  half of the setting of [HL-P, Theorem 6.5], are not defined in this library. The remark's first
  four sentences are
  bibliography — pointers to [lurie-thesis, Theorem 6.3.1] for a derived formal functions
  theorem for proper maps, to [dag12, Chapter 4] with the cross-reference to More on Algebra,
  Section 091N for the affine story, and to [G-R, Section 2.9] for proper base change and
  derived completion via (ind) coherent modules — and carry no formalizable statement. A third
  registration, at a derived-complete object and ideal sheaves generated by finitely many global

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_derivedPushforward_derivedSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**The pushed-forward completion is derived complete.** Let `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be
a morphism of ringed sites and let `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪`, `ℐ' ⊂ 𝒪'` be sheaves of ideals such that `f^♯` sends
`f^{-1}ℐ` into `ℐ'`. If `K` in `D(𝒪')` is derived complete along `ℐ'`, then for every `M` in
`D(𝒪')` the object `Rf_*(R𝑆heafHom_{𝒪'}(M, K))` is derived complete along `ℐ`.

Taking `M` to be the extended alternating Čech complex of a finite family of global sections
generating `ℐ'`, so that `R𝑆heafHom_{𝒪'}(M, K)` is the derived completion `K^∧` of
[Stacks, Tag 099B], this says that the left-hand side `Rf_*(K^∧)` of the displayed equation of
[Stacks, Tag 0A0I] is derived complete.

[Stacks, Tag 099A] puts `R𝑆heafHom_{𝒪'}(M, K)` in `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')`, and [Stacks, Tag 099J]
carries it from there into `D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_derivedPushforward_derivedSheafHom
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))))
    (I' : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (hI : ∀ (W : Y.C) (s : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)).obj.obj (op W)),
      s ∈ I.toSubmodule.obj (op W) →
        fSharpSection f W s ∈ I'.toSubmodule.obj (op (f.u.obj W)))
    (M K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (hK : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I' K) :
    IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} Y I
      ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj
        (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op M)).obj K))
declarations.comment:
the mathematical content of the remark, which is its fifth and last sentence:
  the analogue of the displayed equation (0A0I) for complexes of quasi-coherent modules,
  [HL-P, Theorem 6.5]. The first four sentences are bibliography and carry no mathematical
  statement — a pointer to [lurie-thesis, Theorem 6.3.1] for a derived formal functions theorem
  for proper maps, one to [dag12, Chapter 4] together with the cross-reference to More on
  Algebra, Section 091N for the affine story, and one to [G-R, Section 2.9] for proper base
  change and derived completion via (ind) coherent modules. Covered here and in
  `isDerivedComplete_derivedSheafHom_derivedPushforward`: that both sides of (0A0I) are derived
  complete, for an arbitrary coefficient object of the derived category of modules, which
  subsumes the complexes of quasi-coherent modules the sentence speaks of. This is the step of
  the proof of Tag 0A0G that makes the comparison between the two sides canonical. NOT covered:
  the comparison isomorphism itself, which cannot be stated while Tag 099B and Tag 099F leave
  the derived completion without the universal property that pins the map down, nor proved
  while Tag 0944 and Tag 0A0E are unavailable; and not the setting of (derived) algebraic
  stacks in which [HL-P, Theorem 6.5] is stated. See the module documentation.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_derivedSheafHom_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**The completion of a pushforward is derived complete.** In the situation of
`isDerivedComplete_derivedPushforward_derivedSheafHom`, for every `N` in `D(𝒪)` the object
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(N, Rf_*K)` is derived complete along `ℐ`.

Taking `N` to be the extended alternating Čech complex of a finite family of global sections
generating `ℐ`, this says that the right-hand side `(Rf_*K)^∧` of the displayed equation of
[Stacks, Tag 0A0I] is derived complete.

The two inputs are used in the opposite order to the companion result: [Stacks, Tag 099J] puts
`Rf_*K` in `D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)` and [Stacks, Tag 099A] keeps the derived internal Hom into it there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_derivedSheafHom_derivedPushforward
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))))
    (I' : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (hI : ∀ (W : Y.C) (s : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)).obj.obj (op W)),
      s ∈ I.toSubmodule.obj (op W) →
        fSharpSection f W s ∈ I'.toSubmodule.obj (op (f.u.obj W)))
    (N : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O))))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (hK : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I' K) :
    IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} Y I
      (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor Y).obj (op N)).obj
        ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj K))
declarations.comment:
the second half of the covered statement; see
  `isDerivedComplete_derivedPushforward_derivedSheafHom` for the full accounting of which
  sentences of the remark carry mathematical content and of what is and is not covered.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasNoetherianClosedSubschemes_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKM, (1) ⇒ (2).** Every scheme of the site admitting a closed immersion into a
Noetherian affine formal algebraic space `X` is a Noetherian scheme.

By the implication (1) ⇒ (3) of the same tag, `X` has a presentation by Noetherian affine
schemes. A closed immersion `T ⟶ X` in the sense of Stacks 0ANP is one in the sense of
Stacks 0AIC, so the geometric step of Stacks 0AIC factors it through a stage of that
presentation by a closed immersion of schemes `T ⟶ X_λ`. As `X_λ` is Noetherian, so is `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNoetherianClosedSubschemes_of_isNoetherian {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS X) : HasNoetherianClosedSubschemes B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_tfae'
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherian_tfae' (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsNoetherian B S hS X,
        IsAdicStar B S hS X ∧ HasNoetherianClosedSubschemes B S hS X,
        IsAdicStar B S hS X ∧ HasNoetherianAffinePresentation B S hS X,
        IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X ∧ HasNoetherianAffinePresentation B S hS X]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicStar_and_hasNoetherianAffinePresentation_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKM, (1) ⇒ (3).** A Noetherian affine formal algebraic space is adic\* and every
presentation of it by affine thickenings has Noetherian stages. Indeed an ideal of definition
of a Noetherian ring is finitely generated, and every stage of a presentation is the spectrum
of a quotient of the presenting ring, hence of a Noetherian ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicStar_and_hasNoetherianAffinePresentation_of_isNoetherian
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsNoetherian B S hS X) :
    IsAdicStar B S hS X ∧ HasNoetherianAffinePresentation B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_of_isAdicStar
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKM, (3) ⇒ (1).** An adic\* affine formal algebraic space with a presentation by
Noetherian affine schemes is Noetherian. Let `I` be a finitely generated ideal of definition of
the presenting ring `A`. The weak ideals of definition cutting out the stages are cofinal, so
one of them is contained in `I`; the corresponding stage being Noetherian makes `A ⧸ I` a
quotient of a Noetherian ring, and `A` is `I`-adically complete, so Stacks 05GH makes `A`
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherian_of_isAdicStar {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsAdicStar B S hS X)
    (hpres : HasNoetherianAffinePresentation B S hS X) : IsNoetherian B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isWeaklyAdic_of_isAdicStar
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKM, (3) ⇒ (4).** An adic\* affine formal algebraic space is weakly adic, because
an adic topological ring is weakly adic.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAdic_of_isAdicStar {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsAdicStar B S hS X) :
    IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicStar_of_isWeaklyAdic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKM, (4) ⇒ (3).** A weakly adic affine formal algebraic space with a
presentation by Noetherian affine schemes is adic\*.

Let `A` be the presenting ring and `I` an ideal of definition, which exists because a weakly
adic ring is admissible. By Stacks 0GXF the closure `I₂` of `I ^ 2` is open, so it is a weak
ideal of definition; cofinality of the weak ideals cutting out the stages produces a stage
contained in `I₂`, whence `A ⧸ I₂` is Noetherian. The image of `I` in `A ⧸ I₂` is then a
finitely generated module, that is `I / I₂` is a finite `A`-module, and Stacks 0GXH produces a
finitely generated ideal defining the topology of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicStar_of_isWeaklyAdic {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X)
    (hpres : HasNoetherianAffinePresentation B S hS X) : IsAdicStar B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasNoetherianAffinePresentation_of_hasNoetherianClosedSubschemes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKM, (2) ⇒ (3).** If every scheme closed-immersed in an affine formal algebraic
space `X` is Noetherian, then every presentation of `X` by affine thickenings has Noetherian
stages: by Stacks 0AI9 each stage inclusion `X_λ → X` is a thickening, in particular a closed
immersion of formal algebraic spaces, so the hypothesis applies to its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNoetherianAffinePresentation_of_hasNoetherianClosedSubschemes
    {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hclosed : HasNoetherianClosedSubschemes B S hS X) :
    HasNoetherianAffinePresentation B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_of_hasNoetherianClosedSubschemes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKM, (2) ⇒ (1).** An adic\* affine formal algebraic space all of whose
closed subschemes that are schemes are Noetherian is itself Noetherian: the stages of any
presentation are such closed subschemes, so condition (3) holds and (3) ⇒ (1) applies.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKM, conditions (1), (3) and (4).** For an fppf sheaf `X` on the big fppf site of
`S` the following are equivalent: `X` is a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space; `X` is
adic\* and has a presentation by Noetherian affine schemes; `X` is weakly adic and has a
presentation by Noetherian affine schemes. Each condition already contains the requirement that
`X` be a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherian_tfae (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsNoetherian B S hS X,
        IsAdicStar B S hS X ∧ HasNoetherianAffinePresentation B S hS X,
        IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X ∧ HasNoetherianAffinePresentation B S hS X]
declarations.comment: clauses (1), (3) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_isAffineHom_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKN.** Let `S` be a scheme contained in a big fppf site `B` and let `f : X ⟶ Y`
be a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by algebraic
spaces. Then `f` is representable by schemes and affine: every base change of `f` along a
morphism to `Y` from a sheaf represented by an object of the site is represented by an object of
the site, and the induced morphism of underlying schemes is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_isAffineHom_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
    {X Y : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_affine_baseChange_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKN** over the test objects with affine underlying scheme. Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces,
and let `g` be a morphism to `Y` from a sheaf represented by an object `U` of the site with
affine underlying scheme. Then the fibre product of `f` and `g` is represented by an object of
the site with affine underlying scheme, and the induced morphism to `U` is an affine morphism of
schemes: `f` is representable by schemes and affine over `U`.

Of the two sheaves only the presentations by affine thickenings are used, not the set-theoretic
condition of Stacks 0AIS which together with them makes them affine formal algebraic spaces; so
the conclusion is available for the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological ring over
any site containing its quotient spectra, with no condition on the size of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_baseChange_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces'
    {X Y : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : HasThickeningPresentation B S hS X)
    (hY : HasThickeningPresentation B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (hU : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U))
    (g : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj U ⟶ Y) :
    ∃ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
      (p : (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj V ⟶ X) (q : V ⟶ U),
      IsPullback p ((Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map q) f g ∧
        IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj V) ∧
        IsAffineHom ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map q)
declarations.comment: representability by schemes together with affineness, over every test object of the site whose underlying scheme is affine

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_isAffineHom_of_hasThickeningPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKN.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is
representable by algebraic spaces is representable by schemes, and the morphism of schemes
underlying each of its represented base changes is affine. Nothing is assumed of the test
objects: this is the source's assertion over every object of the site.

Over a test object with affine underlying scheme the conclusion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_affine_baseChange_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`,
and it carries in addition that the representing object is affine, which an arbitrary test
object cannot have. The passage to an arbitrary test object `U` is affine-locality on the
target, carried out in the value universe of the site: the fibre product `X ×_Y U` is an
algebraic space over `S`, because `f` is representable by algebraic spaces and `U` is
representable, hence pointwise `u`-small, so it is the universe lift of an algebraic space `Z₀`
in the value universe of the site and the projection to `U` descends with it. The affine form
above, read over each morphism of the site into `U` with affine source, is exactly the
affine-base-change condition of that descended projection, which relative Tag 03JH for a
morphism out of an algebraic space —
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_representing_over_of_holdsOnAffineBaseChange_of_isAlgebraicSpace`
— glues into a single object of the site with affine projection to `U`, affineness of a
morphism of schemes being Zariski-local at the target.

As in the affine form, of the two sheaves only the presentations by affine thickenings are used
and not the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS.
declarations.statement:
theorem relative_isAffineHom_of_hasThickeningPresentation
    {X Y : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1))} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : HasThickeningPresentation B S hS X)
    (hY : HasThickeningPresentation B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom) :
    (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
      (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).relative
        (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)) f
declarations.comment: both assertions of the source -- representability by schemes and affineness -- over an arbitrary test object of the site

declarations.doc:
The source of a representable affine map of fppf sheaves to an affine

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKP, part (1).** The source of a representable affine morphism of fppf sheaves
whose target is an affine formal algebraic space is itself an affine formal algebraic space.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_of_relative_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKP, part (3).** The source of a representable affine morphism of fppf sheaves
whose target is a countably indexed and classical affine formal algebraic space is itself
countably indexed and classical.

Countable indexing of the source is part (2) of the same tag. For the classical half the
morphism is the formal spectrum of a continuous taut homomorphism of presenting rings, and
pre-admissibility ascends along such a homomorphism by Stacks 0GX8; the presenting ring of the
source is complete and separated, being weakly admissible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_of_relative_isAffineHom
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hY : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS Y ∧ IsClassical B S hS Y) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X ∧ IsClassical B S hS X
declarations.comment: classical_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isWeaklyAdic_of_relative_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKP, part (4).** The source of a representable affine morphism of fppf sheaves
whose target is a weakly adic affine formal algebraic space is itself weakly adic.

A weakly adic affine formal algebraic space is countably indexed by item (5) of Stacks 0AIK, so
the morphism is the formal spectrum of a continuous taut homomorphism of presenting rings; weak
pre-adicness ascends along such a homomorphism by Stacks 0GXI, and the presenting ring of the
source is complete and separated, being weakly admissible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAdic_of_relative_isAffineHom
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hY : IsWeaklyAdic B S hS Y) :
    IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X
declarations.comment: weakly_adic_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicStar_of_relative_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKP, part (5).** The source of a representable affine morphism of fppf sheaves
whose target is an adic\* affine formal algebraic space is itself adic\*.

An adic\* affine formal algebraic space is countably indexed by items (2) and (3) and (5) of
Stacks 0AIK, so the morphism is the formal spectrum of a continuous taut homomorphism of
presenting rings; Stacks 0APU makes the target of such a homomorphism adic with a finitely
generated ideal of definition as soon as its source is and the target is complete and
separated, which the presenting ring of the source is, being weakly admissible. The finitely
generated ideal of definition the hypothesis supplies defines the topology adically because the
ring is pre-adic.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicStar_of_relative_isAffineHom
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hY : IsAdicStar B S hS Y) :
    IsAdicStar B S hS X
declarations.comment: adic_star_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_of_relative_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKP, part (6).** The source of a representable affine morphism of fppf sheaves
which is locally of finite type and whose target is a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space
is itself Noetherian.

A Noetherian affine formal algebraic space is countably indexed by items (1), (2), (3) and (5)
of Stacks 0AIK, so the morphism is the formal spectrum of a continuous taut homomorphism
`φ : A → C` of presenting rings. An ideal of definition of the Noetherian ring `A` is finitely
generated, so Stacks 0APU produces a finitely generated ideal `J ⊆ C` defining the topology of
`C` adically; `C` is then `J`-adically complete, and Stacks 05GH reduces Noetherianness of `C`
to that of `C ⧸ J`. The closed extended ideals form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of
zero by tautness, so `J` contains the closure `J(I)` of `I C` for a weak ideal of definition
`I ⊆ A`; the stage half of Stacks 0ANT makes `A ⧸ I → C ⧸ J(I)` of finite type, hence
`C ⧸ J(I)` Noetherian, and `C ⧸ J` is a quotient of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherian_of_relative_isAffineHom
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hY : IsNoetherian B S hS Y) :
    IsNoetherian B S hS X
declarations.comment: noetherian_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_and_isClassical_of_relative_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKP, part (3).** The source of a representable affine morphism of fppf sheaves
whose target is a countably indexed classical affine formal algebraic space is itself countably
indexed and classical.

Countable indexing passes to the source by part (2) of Stacks 0AKP, and admissibility of the
presenting ring ascends along the taut homomorphism inducing the morphism, by Stacks 0GX8.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexed_and_isClassical_of_relative_isAffineHom
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hYc : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS Y) (hYcl : IsClassical B S hS Y) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X ∧ IsClassical B S hS X
declarations.comment: classical_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_of_relative_isAffineHom'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKP, part (6).** The source of a representable affine morphism of fppf sheaves
which is locally of finite type and whose target is a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space
is itself Noetherian.

By the equivalence of conditions (1) and (3) of Stacks 0AKM a Noetherian affine formal
algebraic space is an adic\* one with a presentation by Noetherian affine schemes. Part (5)
above gives the first half for the source, and the presentation pulls back to a Noetherian one
because each stage of the source is of finite type over the corresponding Noetherian stage of
the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNoetherian_of_relative_isAffineHom'
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYn : IsNoetherian B S hS Y) :
    IsNoetherian B S hS X
declarations.comment: noetherian_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicStar_of_relative_isAffineHom'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKP, part (5).** The source of a representable affine morphism of fppf sheaves
whose target is an adic\* affine formal algebraic space is itself adic\*.

The powers of an ideal of definition of an adic ring are a fundamental system of open ideals,
so the target is countably indexed and part (2) of Stacks 0AKP carries that to the source. The
presenting ring of the source is complete and separated, so by Stacks 0APU the taut
homomorphism inducing the morphism makes it adic with a finitely generated ideal of
definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicStar_of_relative_isAffineHom'
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hYa : IsAdicStar B S hS Y) :
    IsAdicStar B S hS X
declarations.comment: adic_star_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isWeaklyAdic_of_relative_isAffineHom'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKP, part (4).** The source of a representable affine morphism of fppf sheaves
whose target is a weakly adic affine formal algebraic space is itself weakly adic.

A weakly adic ring has the closed powers of a single ideal as a fundamental system of open
ideals, so the target is countably indexed and part (2) of Stacks 0AKP carries that to the
source; weak pre-adicness of the presenting ring then ascends along the taut homomorphism
inducing the morphism, by Stacks 0GXI.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyAdic_of_relative_isAffineHom'
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : (MorphismProperty.relative
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS))
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@IsAffineHom.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) f)
    (hYw : IsWeaklyAdic B S hS Y) :
    IsWeaklyAdic B S hS X
declarations.comment: weakly_adic_source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_of_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKQ, clause (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal algebraic
spaces over `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces. If `Y` is countably indexed then
so is `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexed_of_isRepresentable {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)

    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X
declarations.comment: clause (1); Stacks 0AKN is the library's `relative_isAffineHom_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces` and parts (1) and (2) of Stacks 0AKP are the library's `isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_of_relative_isAffineHom` and `isCountablyIndexed_of_relative_isAffineHom`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_of_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKQ, clause (2).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal algebraic
spaces over `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces. If `Y` is countably indexed and
classical then so is `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_of_isRepresentable {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (hYc : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS Y ∧ IsClassical B S hS Y) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X ∧ IsClassical B S hS X
declarations.comment: clause (2); Stacks 0AKN is the library's `relative_isAffineHom_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces` and clause (3) of Stacks 0AKP is the library's `isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_of_relative_isAffineHom`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isWeaklyAdic_of_isRepresentable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKQ, clause (3).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal algebraic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_of_isCountablyIndexed_of_surjective_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKS, the forward implication.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal
algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and flat. If
`X` is countably indexed then so is `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexed_of_isCountablyIndexed_of_surjective_flat
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f)
    (hflat : ∃ hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ g ↦ Space.HoldsOnEveryEtaleChartULift.{u + 1} B S hS
          (@AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u}) g.hom) f.hom hf)
    (hXc : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS Y
declarations.comment: the implication from the source being countably indexed to the target being countably indexed, which is the content of the source's proof; the converse is clause (1) of Stacks 0AKQ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_iff_of_surjective_flat
declarations.doc:

which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective and flat. Then `X` is countably indexed
if and only if `Y` is.

theorem isCountablyIndexed_iff_of_surjective_flat {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) (hflat : IsRepresentableFlat B S hS f) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X ↔ IsCountablyIndexed B S hS Y
declarations.comment: the equivalence, at the source's own hypotheses. The forward implication is the source's cofinality argument, `isCountablyIndexed_target_of_surjective_flat`, which rests on Stacks 0AIA, on Stacks 0AKN — the library's `relative_isAffineHom_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces` — and on faithful flatness of a represented base change; the reverse implication is part (2) of Stacks 0AKP, the library's `isCountablyIndexed_of_relative_isAffineHom`

The forward implication is the library's Stacks 0GXQ and the reverse one is clause (5) of Stacks 0AKP, the library's `isAdicStar_of_relative_isAffineHom`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isNoetherian_iff_of_isSurjective_of_isRepresentableFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKW.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S`
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and locally of finite type. Then
`X` is Noetherian if and only if `Y` is.

The reverse implication is clause (5) of Stacks 0AKQ. For the forward one, let `C` be a
Noetherian adic ring presenting `X`. A presenting ring `A` of `Y` with a continuous taut
homomorphism `φ : A → C` whose maps on quotients by open ideals are faithfully flat is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isTaut_faithfullyFlat_presentingRing_of_surjective_flat`.
By Stacks 0GXQ the ring `A` has a finitely generated ideal of definition `J` defining its
topology; `A ⧸ J` is Noetherian by Stacks 033E, its faithfully flat extension
`C ⧸ (J C)‾` being a quotient of the Noetherian ring `C`; and `A`, complete for the `J`-adic
topology, is Noetherian by Stacks 05GH.
declarations.statement: alias isNoetherian_iff_of_isSurjective_of_isRepresentableFlat

declarations.comment: the equivalence, at the source's own hypotheses. The presenting ring of the target with its continuous taut homomorphism to that of the source is `exists_isTaut_faithfullyFlat_presentingRing_of_surjective_flat`; its finitely generated ideal of definition is the library's Stacks 0GXQ, the descent of the Noetherian property to the quotient by it is Stacks 033E, `descent_noetherian`, and the passage to the complete ring is Stacks 05GH, `noetherian_of_isAdicComplete_fg`; Stacks 0AKN is the library's `relative_isAffineHom_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces`. The reverse implication is clause (6) of Stacks 0AKP, the library's `isNoetherian_of_relative_isAffineHom`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineEtaleChartProperty_iff_hasAffineEtaleAtlasWithProperty_of_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKX.** Let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S` and let `P` be one of the
properties of affine formal algebraic spaces *countably indexed*, *countably indexed and
classical*, *weakly adic*, *adic\** and *Noetherian*. The following are equivalent:

1. if `Y` is an affine formal algebraic space and `Y ⟶ X` is representable by algebraic spaces
   and étale, then `Y` has property `P`;
2. for some covering `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` as in Definition 0AIM each `Xᵢ` has property `P`.

For (2) ⟹ (1) the atlas is refined against the chart and cut down to a finite subfamily by
quasi-compactness; its members have `P` by Stacks 0AKQ, their disjoint union has `P`, and `P`
passes to the chart along the surjective flat morphism from that disjoint union by Stacks 0AKS,
0GXR, 0GXS, 0AKT or 0AKW.
declarations.statement: alias hasAffineEtaleChartProperty_iff_hasAffineEtaleAtlasWithProperty_of_mem

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineEtaleChartProperty_iff_hasAffineEtaleAtlasWithProperty_isCountablyIndexed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKX at countable indexing.** Let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S`. Then
every affine formal algebraic space representable étale over `X` is countably indexed if and
only if `X` admits an atlas as in Definition **Stacks 0AIM** all of whose members are countably
indexed.

The implication (1) ⟹ (2) is the atlas of `X`. For (2) ⟹ (1), a chart `g : Z ⟶ X` receives a
surjective flat morphism, representable by algebraic spaces, from a countably indexed affine
formal algebraic space — the coproduct of a finite jointly surjective subfamily of the atlas
refined against `Z` — and **Stacks 0AKS** transfers countable indexing along it.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffineEtaleChartProperty_iff_hasAffineEtaleAtlasWithProperty_isCountablyIndexed
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    HasAffineEtaleChartProperty B S hS X (IsCountablyIndexed B S hS) ↔
      HasAffineEtaleAtlasWithProperty B S hS X (IsCountablyIndexed B S hS)
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2) at the property of being countably indexed, with nothing assumed. The refinement of the atlas against a chart is the library's `exists_countablyIndexed_surjective_flat_over_chart` (Stacks 0AJ3 in its chart form, clause (1) of Stacks 0AKQ, the implication (1) ⟹ (2) of Stacks 0AJ9 and the coproduct stability of countable indexing), and the transfer of countable indexing along the surjective flat morphism it produces is Stacks 0AKS. The equivalence is registered at this property rather than at an arbitrary one because the refinement is false at an arbitrary property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineEtaleChartProperty_iff_hasAffineEtaleAtlasWithProperty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKX.** Let `X` be a formal algebraic space over `S` and let `P` be one of the
properties of affine formal algebraic spaces *countably indexed*, *countably indexed and
classical*, *weakly adic*, *adic\** and *Noetherian*. The following are equivalent:

1. if `Y` is an affine formal algebraic space and `Y ⟶ X` is representable by algebraic spaces
   and étale, then `Y` has property `P`;

declarations.statement:
theorem hasAffineEtaleChartProperty_iff_hasAffineEtaleAtlasWithProperty
    (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (P : FppfSheaf B S hS → Prop)
    (hP : P = IsCountablyIndexed B S hS ∨
      P = (fun Z ↦ IsCountablyIndexed B S hS Z ∧ IsClassical B S hS Z) ∨
      P = IsWeaklyAdic B S hS ∨ P = IsAdicStar B S hS ∨ P = IsNoetherian B S hS) :
    HasAffineEtaleChartProperty B S hS X P ↔ HasAffineEtaleAtlasWithProperty B S hS X P
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2), at the source's own hypotheses and for each of the five properties of its list. For (2) ⟹ (1) the refinement of the atlas against a chart is `exists_surjective_flat_over_chart_of_hasAffineEtaleAtlasWithProperty`: Stacks 0AJ3 for the fibre products, the coverings of Definition 0AIM, quasi-compactness of the chart, Stacks 0AKQ along the étale maps and the finite disjoint union of the members; the property then passes to the chart by Stacks 0AKS, 0GXR, 0GXS, 0AKT or 0AKW

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasAffineEtaleChartProperty_iff_atlas_isCountablyIndexedAndClassical_unconditional

when it admits an atlas as in Definition 0AIM by adic\* affine formal algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyAdicStar (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: locally adic star

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AKY, locally Noetherian.** A formal algebraic space over `S` is *locally
Noetherian* when it admits an atlas as in Definition 0AIM by Noetherian affine formal
algebraic spaces, that is by affine formal algebraic spaces whose associated weakly admissible
topological ring is Noetherian and adic.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyNoetherian (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) : Prop
declarations.comment: locally Noetherian

declarations.name: RestrictedPowerSeries.limitCompleteSpace
declarations.doc: Restricted power series are complete for their inverse-limit topology.
declarations.statement:
public instance limitCompleteSpace {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (σ : Type v) :
    let _ : UniformSpace (RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) :=
      limitUniformSpace I σ
    CompleteSpace (RestrictedPowerSeries I σ)
declarations.comment: limit_completeness

declarations.name: RestrictedPowerSeries.isHomeomorph_adicCompletionEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical completion equivalence is an isomorphism of topological rings when the
coefficient ideal is finitely generated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isHomeomorph_adicCompletionEquiv {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (σ : Type v) (hI : I.FG) :
    let _ : TopologicalSpace (RestrictedPowerSeries I σ) :=
      limitTopology I σ
    let _ : TopologicalSpace
      (AdicCompletion (I.map (MvPolynomial.C : A →+* MvPolynomial σ A))
        (MvPolynomial σ A)) := polynomialCompletionAdicTopology I σ
    IsHomeomorph (adicCompletionEquiv I σ)
declarations.comment: finite_generation_topology

registrations.name: RestrictedPowerSeries.adicCompletionEquiv
registrations.comment: ring_identification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.finiteTypeAlgebraSystemAntiEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AL1.** Let `X` be a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space over `S` presented as
the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological ring `A`, and let `J` be a fundamental
system of weak ideals of definition of `A`. The category of inverse systems of finite type
algebras over the quotients of `J` is anti-equivalent to the category of finite type morphisms
to `X` from affine formal algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finiteTypeAlgebraSystemAntiEquivalence
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (_hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (X : Sheaf (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hX : HasSomeSurjectivePresentation B S hS X)
    (P : WeakIdealColimitPresentation B S hS A X)
    (I : Type v) [Preorder I] [Nonempty I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (J : IdealBasis A I) :
    (FiniteTypeAlgebraSystem A I J)ᵒᵖ ≌ AffineFiniteTypeOver B S hS X
declarations.comment: anti-equivalence

declarations.name: Rig.AdicAlgebraSystem
declarations.doc:
The category of inverse systems `… → B₃ → B₂ → B₁` in which `Bₙ` is a finite
type `A ⧸ I ^ n`-algebra and each transition identifies its target with reduction of its
source modulo `I ^ n`.  The Lean index `n` represents the mathematical index `n + 1`.
declarations.statement: structure AdicAlgebraSystem (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)

declarations.name: Rig.AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The category of `I`-adically complete `A`-algebras whose reduction modulo `I` is of
finite type over `A ⧸ I`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)

declarations.name: Rig.adicBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AL5.** Let `A₁ → A₂` be a ring map and `I₁ ⊆ A₁`, `I₂ ⊆ A₂` ideals
with `I₁ ^ c` mapping into `I₂` for some `c ≥ 1`. This induces ring maps
`A₁ ⧸ I₁ ^ (cn) → A₂ ⧸ I₂ ^ n`, and there is a base change functor `(Bₙ) ↦ (B_{cn} ⊗ A₂ ⧸ I₂ ^ n)`
between the categories of systems. If `I₂` is finitely generated there is a base change functor
`B ↦ (B ⊗[A₁] A₂)^` between the categories of complete algebras, and if both ideals are
finitely generated the two base change functors agree via the equivalences `B ↦ (B ⧸ IⁿB)ₙ`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def adicBaseChange :
    AdicBaseChange.{v, u₁, u₂} A₁ A₂ I₁ I₂ hc hmap

declarations.name: Rig.quotient_isAdicallyComplete
declarations.doc:
The quotient of an adically finite type algebra by an ideal from the base is
complete for every ideal defining the induced adic topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quotient_isAdicallyComplete
    (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hI : (I ^ c).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) ≤ barI)
    (hbarI : barI ^ d ≤ I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a))
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) :
    IsAdicComplete (barI.map (algebraMap (A ⧸ a)
        (B.carrier ⧸ a.map (algebraMap A B.carrier))))
      (B.carrier ⧸ a.map (algebraMap A B.carrier))
declarations.comment: the quotient is complete

declarations.name: Rig.tensor_quotient_completion_bijective
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the tensor-product presentation of the quotient algebra
to its `barI`-adic completion is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensor_quotient_completion_bijective
    (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hI : (I ^ c).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) ≤ barI)
    (hbarI : barI ^ d ≤ I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a))
    (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) :
    Function.Bijective
      (AdicCompletion.of
        (baseChangedIdeal (A₂ := A ⧸ a) (I₂ := barI) B)
        (baseChangedAlgebra (A₂ := A ⧸ a) B))
declarations.comment: completed base change is the quotient

declarations.name: Rig.quotientBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Base change to a closed subscheme is the quotient functor. The isomorphism to
completed base change is the canonical completion map, and quotienting a morphism
acts by quotienting its underlying algebra homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quotientBaseChange
    (hc : 0 < c) (hd : 0 < d)
    (hI : (I ^ c).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a) ≤ barI)
    (hbarI : barI ^ d ≤ I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a)) :
    ∃ (Q : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I ⥤
        AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, max v u} (A ⧸ a) barI),
      ∃ (η : Q ≅
          (completedBaseChange (A₁ := A) (A₂ := A ⧸ a)
            I barI c hc hI (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing barI)).functor),
        ∃ (e : ∀ B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I,
            (Q.obj B).carrier ≃+* (B.carrier ⧸ a.map (algebraMap A B.carrier))),
          (∀ (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (x : B.carrier),
            ((completedBaseChange (A₁ := A) (A₂ := A ⧸ a)
              I barI c hc hI (Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing barI)).completedTensorProductEquiv B)
                (AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.hom (η.hom.app B)
                  ((e B).symm (Ideal.Quotient.mk (a.map (algebraMap A B.carrier)) x))) =
              AdicCompletion.of
                (baseChangedIdeal (A₂ := A ⧸ a) (I₂ := barI) B)
                (baseChangedAlgebra (A₂ := A ⧸ a) B)
                ((Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivTensorQuot B.carrier a)
                  (Ideal.Quotient.mk (a.map (algebraMap A B.carrier)) x))) ∧
          (∀ {B C : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I} (f : B ⟶ C) (x : B.carrier),
            e C (AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.hom (Q.map f)
              ((e B).symm (Ideal.Quotient.mk (a.map (algebraMap A B.carrier)) x))) =
              Ideal.Quotient.mk (a.map (algebraMap A C.carrier))
                  (AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.hom f x))
declarations.comment: the quotient functor and its natural comparison

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.finite_iff_piScalarRightHom_nat_surjective
declarations.doc:
A countable module is finitely generated if and only if the canonical map
`M ⊗[R] (ℕ → R) → (ℕ → M)` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_iff_piScalarRightHom_nat_surjective :
    Module.Finite R M ↔
      Function.Surjective (TensorProduct.piScalarRightHom R R M ℕ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.finitePresentation_iff_piScalarRightHom_nat_bijective
declarations.doc:
A countable module over a countable ring is finitely presented if and only if the canonical
map `M ⊗[R] (ℕ → R) → (ℕ → M)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_iff_piScalarRightHom_nat_bijective :

      Function.Bijective (TensorProduct.piScalarRightHom R R M ℕ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.isCoherentRing_iff_flat_pi_nat
declarations.doc:
A countable commutative ring is coherent if and only if its countable product, as a module
over itself, is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentRing_iff_flat_pi_nat (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Countable R] :
    IsCoherentRing R ↔ Module.Flat R (ℕ → R)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_powerSeries_not_flat
declarations.doc:
For some commutative ring, its formal power series ring is flat over neither the
coefficient ring nor the polynomial ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_powerSeries_not_flat :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (hR : CommRing R),
      letI : CommRing R := hR
      (¬ Module.Flat R (PowerSeries R)) ∧
        (¬ Module.Flat (Polynomial R) (PowerSeries R))

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.not_flat_powerSeries_map_localizationAway
declarations.doc:
The coefficientwise localization map from the power series ring of
`k[y, z, aᵢ]/(y aᵢ, aᵢ aⱼ)` to the power series ring of its localization at `z`
is not flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_flat_powerSeries_map_localizationAway
    (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    ¬ (PowerSeries.map
      (algebraMap (nonflatPowerSeriesRing k)
        (Localization.Away (nonflatPowerSeriesElement k)))).Flat

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_nonflat_completed_localization
declarations.doc:
There is a ring complete for a principal ideal whose completed principal
localization is not flat over the ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nonflat_completed_localization :
    ∃ (A : Type*) (_ : CommRing A) (x f : A),
      IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {x}) A ∧
        ¬ Module.Flat A
          (AdicCompletion
            ((Ideal.span {x}).map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f)))
            (Localization.Away f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.not_nonempty_abelian_quasicoherentModules_padicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALG, the source's example.** For a prime `p`, the formal spectrum
`X = Spf(ℤ_p)` over `Spec ℤ` is a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space whose category of
quasi-coherent modules (Stacks 06WG) admits no abelian structure: by Examples, Section 0ALF, it
is the category of `p`-adically complete abelian groups, which is not abelian (Stacks 07JR).
declarations.statement:
theorem not_nonempty_abelian_quasicoherentModules_padicCompletion (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hZ : B.Contains (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (hZp : B.Contains (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ_[p])))) :
    IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B _ hZ (padicCompletion p B hZ hZp) ∧
      IsNoetherian B _ hZ (padicCompletion p B hZ hZp) ∧
      ¬ Nonempty (Abelian (FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} B _ hZ
        (completionFibred B _ hZ (specULiftZIsTerminal.from _) hZp
          (Ideal.span {(p : ULift.{u} ℤ_[p])})).p
        (isFiberedInGroupoids_completionFibred B _ hZ _ hZp _)))
declarations.comment: the source's example `Spf(ℤ_p)`, for every prime `p`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isNoetherian_not_nonempty_abelian_quasicoherentModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALG.** The category of quasi-coherent modules on a formal algebraic space is not
abelian in general, even for a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space: there is a big fppf
site with a base scheme and a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space `X` over it — `Spf(ℤ_2)`
over `Spec ℤ` — whose category of quasi-coherent modules (Stacks 06WG, on the category fibred in
groupoids of `X`) admits no abelian structure.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isNoetherian_not_nonempty_abelian_quasicoherentModules :
    ∃ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (X : FppfSheaf B S hS),
      IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X ∧ IsNoetherian B S hS X ∧
      ¬ Nonempty (Abelian (FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} B S hS
        (presheafOfGroupoids (X.obj ⋙ typeToGrpd)).p
        (isFiberedInGroupoids_presheafOfGroupoids _)))

declarations.name: exists_etale_lift_of_isCoprime_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALH.** A factorization of a monic polynomial into coprime monic factors modulo an
ideal lifts to a factorization into monic polynomials over an étale algebra which induces an
isomorphism modulo the extended ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_lift_of_isCoprime_factorization
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (f : Polynomial A)
    (gbar hbar : Polynomial (A ⧸ I)) (hf : f.Monic) (hgbar : gbar.Monic)
    (hhbar : hbar.Monic) (hfac : f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = gbar * hbar)
    (hcoprime : IsCoprime gbar hbar) :
    ∃ (A' : Type u) (_ : CommRing A') (_ : Algebra A A') (g' h' : Polynomial A'),
      Algebra.Etale A A' ∧
      Function.Bijective
        (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap A A')) (algebraMap A A')
          Ideal.le_comap_map) ∧
      g'.Monic ∧ h'.Monic ∧ IsCoprime g' h' ∧
      f.map (algebraMap A A') = g' * h' ∧
      gbar.map
          (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap A A')) (algebraMap A A')
            Ideal.le_comap_map) =
        g'.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A A'))) ∧
      hbar.map
          (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap A A')) (algebraMap A A')
            Ideal.le_comap_map) =
        h'.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A A')))

declarations.name: etaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_and_henselianRing_of_le_nilradical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALI.** If every element of `I` is nilpotent, reduction modulo `I` induces an
equivalence from étale `A`-algebras to étale `(A ⧸ I)`-algebras, and `(A, I)` is a henselian
pair.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_and_henselianRing_of_le_nilradical {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
  (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : I ≤ nilradical A) :
    (etaleBaseChange I).IsEquivalence ∧ HenselianRing A I

declarations.name: etaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_and_henselianPair_of_le_nilradical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALI.** If every element of `I` is nilpotent, reduction modulo `I` induces an
equivalence from étale `A`-algebras to étale `(A ⧸ I)`-algebras, and `(A, I)` is a henselian pair
in the sense that coprime monic factorizations modulo `I` lift to `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleBaseChange_isEquivalence_and_henselianPair_of_le_nilradical
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I ≤ nilradical A) :
    (etaleBaseChange I).IsEquivalence ∧ HenselianPair A I
declarations.comment: henselianness in the monic-factorization sense of Definition 09XE

An `I`-adically complete ring is henselian at `I`; this is Mathlib's
