declarations.name: FormalGlueing.exists_descent_of_idealPowerTorsion_kernel_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALK.** A map to or from an extended module whose kernel and cokernel are
ideal-power torsion descends at the level of its source or target module, with the
given map recovered by extension of scalars and with the same kernel and cokernel after
restriction of scalars.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_descent_of_idealPowerTorsion_kernel_cokernel
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG) (hflat : Module.Flat R S)
    (hq : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap R S)) (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map)) :
    let E := ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, v, max u v w} (algebraMap R S)
    let U := ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v w} (algebraMap R S)
    (∀ (N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (M' : ModuleCat.{max u v w} S)
      (φ : M' ⟶ E.obj N),
      IsIPowerTorsion S
        (↥(kernel φ : ModuleCat.{max u v w} S)) (I.map (algebraMap R S)) →
      IsIPowerTorsion S
        (↥(cokernel φ : ModuleCat.{max u v w} S)) (I.map (algebraMap R S)) →
      ∃ (M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (ψ : M ⟶ N) (e : E.obj M ≅ M')
          (_eKer : U.obj (kernel φ) ≅ kernel ψ)
          (_eCoker : U.obj (cokernel φ) ≅ cokernel ψ),
        e.hom ≫ φ = E.map ψ) ∧
    (∀ (M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (N' : ModuleCat.{max u v w} S)
      (φ : E.obj M ⟶ N'),
      IsIPowerTorsion S
        (↥(kernel φ : ModuleCat.{max u v w} S)) (I.map (algebraMap R S)) →
      IsIPowerTorsion S
        (↥(cokernel φ : ModuleCat.{max u v w} S)) (I.map (algebraMap R S)) →
      ∃ (N : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R) (ψ : M ⟶ N) (e : E.obj N ≅ N')
          (_eKer : U.obj (kernel φ) ≅ kernel ψ)
          (_eCoker : U.obj (cokernel φ) ≅ cokernel ψ),
        E.map ψ ≫ e.hom = φ)

declarations.name: Rig.CompletedPolynomialPresentation.exists_sixTerm_exact_combined
declarations.doc:
**The six-term exact sequence of Stacks 0ALM.**

Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal, `B` an object of (Stacks 0AL4) with a completed
polynomial presentation `B = A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩/J`, and `C` an object of (0AL4) over `B` presented
over `B` by `ψ : B⟨y₁, …, y_s⟩ ↠ C`, so that `C = A⟨x, y⟩/K` by the combined presentation.
Then there is an exact sequence

```
H⁻¹(NL^∧_{B/A} ⊗_B C) → H⁻¹(NL^∧_{C/A}) → H⁻¹(NL^∧_{C/B}) --δ-->
  H⁰(NL^∧_{B/A} ⊗_B C) → H⁰(NL^∧_{C/A}) → H⁰(NL^∧_{C/B}) → 0.
```

Every input of `NaiveCotangent.exists_sixTerm_exact_of_finAppend` is now discharged: the
degree-`0` row is the split row `⨁_{i<r} C → ⨁_{i<r+s} C → ⨁_{j<s} C` of that file, the
degree-`1` row is `Rig.CompletedPolynomialPresentation.exact_cotangentMap_combined` together
with `..._surjective_cotangentMap_combined`, and the two squares are the two lemmas above.

This theorem alone is the content of the tag: the combined presentation, the two commuting
squares and the right exactness of the degree-`1` row are steps of the source's *proof*, not
part of its statement.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sixTerm_exact_combined
    (hFc : ∀ j, @Continuous _ _
      (RestrictedPowerSeries.polynomialCompletionLimitTopology B.adicIdeal (Fin s))
      (RestrictedPowerSeries.polynomialCompletionLimitTopology B.adicIdeal (Fin s)) (F j))
    (hFp : ∀ (j : Fin s) (q : MvPolynomial (Fin s) B.carrier),
      F j (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin s) B.carrier)
          (AdicCompletion.completedMvPolynomial B.adicIdeal (Fin s)) q) =
        algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin s) B.carrier)
          (AdicCompletion.completedMvPolynomial B.adicIdeal (Fin s))
          (MvPolynomial.pderiv j q)) :
    ∃ δ : NaiveCotangent.H₁
          (NaiveCotangent.TwoTerm.ofFree (outerDifferential s ψ hψ F)) →ₗ[C.carrier]
        NaiveCotangent.H₀
          (NaiveCotangent.TwoTerm.ofFree (P.innerBaseChangeDifferential (C := C) KB)),
      Function.Exact
          (NaiveCotangent.chainMapInl _
            (P.combinedDifferential_comp_innerCotangentMap s ψ hψ KB KC)).onH₁
          (NaiveCotangent.chainMapProj _
            (P.outerDifferential_comp_outerCotangentMap s ψ hψ KC F hFc hFp)).onH₁ ∧
        Function.Exact
            (NaiveCotangent.chainMapProj _
              (P.outerDifferential_comp_outerCotangentMap s ψ hψ KC F hFc hFp)).onH₁ δ ∧
          Function.Exact δ
              (NaiveCotangent.chainMapInl _
                (P.combinedDifferential_comp_innerCotangentMap s ψ hψ KB KC)).onH₀ ∧
            Function.Exact
                (NaiveCotangent.chainMapInl _
                  (P.combinedDifferential_comp_innerCotangentMap s ψ hψ KB KC)).onH₀
                (NaiveCotangent.chainMapProj _
                  (P.outerDifferential_comp_outerCotangentMap s ψ hψ KC F hFc hFp)).onH₀ ∧
              Function.Surjective
                (NaiveCotangent.chainMapProj _
                  (P.outerDifferential_comp_outerCotangentMap s ψ hψ KC F hFc hFp)).onH₀

declarations.name: TwoTermComplexExt.exists_hom_Q_map_eq_of_comp_canonical
declarations.doc:
**(3)** Assume `K^i = 0` for `i ≤ -3`. Let `α ∈ Hom_{D(R)}(M, K)`. Suppose the
composite of `α` with the canonical map `K → K^{-2}[2]`, viewed in
`Hom_{D(R)}(M, K^{-2}[2]) = Ext^2(M, K^{-2})`, comes from an `R`-module
homomorphism `a : M^{-2} → K^{-2}` with `a ∘ d_M^{-3} = 0` (i.e. equals the
`D(R)`-morphism induced by the chain map `M → (single (-2)).obj (K^{-2})`
determined by `a`). Then `α` is represented by a morphism of complexes
`a^• : M → K` with `a^{-2} = a`.

PROOF SKETCH (Stacks 0ALN, proof of (3)): take `P := exists_projRes`, lift `α`
to `b : F → K` with `b^{-2} = a ∘ p^{-2}` (`exists_hom_from_projRes_Q_map_eq`),
descend `b` through `p` to `ab : M → K` with `p ≫ ab = b` and `ab^{-2} = a`
(`exists_hom_comp_projRes_eq`). Then
`Q.map p ≫ Q.map ab = Q.map b = Q.map p ≫ α`, and `Q.map p` is an iso, so
`Q.map ab = α`. This `ab` is the required representative.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hom_Q_map_eq_of_comp_canonical
    (hM_pos : ∀ i, 0 < i → IsZero (M.X i)) (hM0 : Projective (M.X 0))
    (hK : ∀ i ≤ (-3 : ℤ), IsZero (K.X i))
    (α : HomD M K)
    (a : M.X (-2) ⟶ K.X (-2))
    (ha : M.d (-3) (-2) ≫ a = 0)
    (hα : α ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (canonicalToSingleNegTwo K hK)
        = DerivedCategory.Q.map (HomologicalComplex.mkHomToSingle a (by
            intro i hi
            simp only [ComplexShape.up_Rel] at hi
            have hi3 : i = -3 := by omega
            subst hi3
            exact ha))) :
    ∃ (ab : M ⟶ K),
      DerivedCategory.Q.map ab = α ∧ HomologicalComplex.Hom.f ab (-2) = a

declarations.name: TwoTermComplexExt.toHomD_bijective
declarations.doc:
**(1)** Assume `K^i = 0` for `i ≤ -2`. Then the canonical map
`Hom_{K(R)}(M, K) → Hom_{D(R)}(M, K)` is an isomorphism (bijective).

PROOF SKETCH (Stacks 0ALN, proof of (1)): Pick a termwise-surjective projective
resolution `p : F → M` (`exists_projRes`); then `F` is K-projective. By
`CochainComplex.IsKProjective.Qh_map_bijective`, the localization map
`Qh.map : Hom_{K(R)}(F, K) → Hom_{D(R)}(F, K)` is bijective. Since `Q.map p` is an
isomorphism in `D(R)` (`p` a quasi-iso), postcomposition identifies
`Hom_{D(R)}(F, K) ≅ Hom_{D(R)}(M, K)`. By `precomp_quotient_map_projRes_bijective`, precomposition
with `[p]` is a bijection `Hom_{K(R)}(M, K) → Hom_{K(R)}(F, K)`. Chasing the square
(`Qh.map` is natural and `toHomD = Qh.map`), `toHomD : Hom_{K(R)}(M, K) →
Hom_{D(R)}(M, K)` is the composite of these three bijections, hence bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem toHomD_bijective
    (hM_pos : ∀ i, 0 < i → IsZero (M.X i)) (hM0 : Projective (M.X 0))
    (hK : ∀ i ≤ (-2 : ℤ), IsZero (K.X i)) :
    Function.Bijective (fun f : HomK M K => (toHomD f : HomD M K))

declarations.name: TwoTermComplexExt.forall_Q_map_comp_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
**(2)** Assume `K^i = 0` for `i ∉ {-1, 0}` and that `K^0` is projective.
For a morphism of complexes `a : M → K`, condition (2a) — that for every module
`N` the induced map `Ext^1(a, N) : Ext^1(K, N) → Ext^1(M, N)`, given by
pre-composition with `Q.map a`, is the zero map — is equivalent to (2b) — the
existence of an `R`-module homomorphism `h^0 : M^0 → K^{-1}` with
`a^{-1} + h^0 ∘ d_M^{-1} = 0`.

PROOF SKETCH: the two implications are `Q_map_comp_eq_zero_of_nullHomotopy`
((2b)⇒(2a)) and `exists_nullHomotopy_of_Q_map_comp_eq_zero` ((2a)⇒(2b)); assemble
with `Iff.intro`.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_Q_map_comp_eq_zero_iff
    (hM_pos : ∀ i, 0 < i → IsZero (M.X i)) (hM0 : Projective (M.X 0))
    (hK : ∀ i, i ≠ -1 → i ≠ 0 → IsZero (K.X i)) (hK0 : Projective (K.X 0))
    (a : M ⟶ K) :
    (∀ (N : ModuleCat.{v} R) (ξ : ExtMod K N 1),
        DerivedCategory.Q.map a ≫ ξ = 0)
      ↔
    (∃ h0 : M.X 0 ⟶ K.X (-1),
        HomologicalComplex.Hom.f a (-1) + M.d (-1) 0 ≫ h0 = 0)

declarations.name: TwoTermComplexExt.exists_homotopy_components_of_Q_map_eq
declarations.doc:
**(4)** In the situation of (3): given `α` and a representing morphism of complexes
`a^•` with `a^{-2} = a` (as produced in (3)), for any second representing morphism
of complexes `(a')^•` with `(a')^{-2} = a`, there exist `R`-module homomorphisms
`h^0 : M^0 → K^{-1}` and `h^{-1} : M^{-1} → K^{-2}` such that
`h^{-1} ∘ d_M^{-2} = 0`, `(a')^{-1} = a^{-1} + d_K^{-2} ∘ h^{-1} + h^0 ∘ d_M^{-1}`,
and `(a')^0 = a^0 + d_K^{-1} ∘ h^0`.

PROOF SKETCH (Stacks 0ALN, proof of (4)): `ab` and `ab'` both represent `α`, so by
`nonempty_homotopy_of_Q_map_eq` they are chain-homotopic; pick a homotopy `H`.
Feed `H` (and the degree-`-2` agreement) to
`exists_homotopy_components_of_homotopy` to obtain `h^0, h^{-1}` and the three
relations.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopy_components_of_Q_map_eq
    (hM_pos : ∀ i, 0 < i → IsZero (M.X i)) (hM0 : Projective (M.X 0))
    (hK : ∀ i ≤ (-3 : ℤ), IsZero (K.X i))
    (α : HomD M K)
    (a : M.X (-2) ⟶ K.X (-2))
    (ab ab' : M ⟶ K)
    (hab : DerivedCategory.Q.map ab = α) (hab' : DerivedCategory.Q.map ab' = α)
    (hab_2 : HomologicalComplex.Hom.f ab (-2) = a)
    (hab'_2 : HomologicalComplex.Hom.f ab' (-2) = a) :
    ∃ (h0 : M.X 0 ⟶ K.X (-1)) (hm1 : M.X (-1) ⟶ K.X (-2)),
      M.d (-2) (-1) ≫ hm1 = 0 ∧
      HomologicalComplex.Hom.f ab' (-1) =
        HomologicalComplex.Hom.f ab (-1) + hm1 ≫ K.d (-2) (-1) + M.d (-1) 0 ≫ h0 ∧
      HomologicalComplex.Hom.f ab' 0 =
        HomologicalComplex.Hom.f ab 0 + h0 ≫ K.d (-1) 0

declarations.name: Rig.isRigEtale_adicCompletionObj_of_isEtaleOutside
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALQ, part (1).**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `B` a finite
type `A`-algebra.  If `Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is étale over `Spec(A) ∖ V(I)`, then the `I`-adic
completion `B^` satisfies the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0AJU, that is, `B^` is rig-étale
over `(A, I)`.

Étaleness off `V(I)` says that `H¹(L_{B/A})` and `Ω_{B/A}` are supported in `V(IB)`, so — both
being finite modules over the Noetherian ring `B` — a power of `IB` annihilates them, hence
also their base changes to `B^`.  The pivot
`Rig.isRigEtale_adicCompletionObj_iff` turns that into rig-étaleness.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRigEtale_adicCompletionObj_of_isEtaleOutside (h : IsEtaleOutside I B) :
    IsRigEtale (adicCompletionObj I (B := B))
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Rig.exists_isEtaleOutside_localization_of_isRigEtale_adicCompletionObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALQ, part (2).**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `B` a finite
type `A`-algebra.  If the `I`-adic completion `B^` satisfies the equivalent conditions of
Stacks 0AJU — that is, if `B^` is rig-étale over `(A, I)` — then there is `g ∈ 1 + IB` such that
`Spec(B_g) → Spec(A)` is étale over `Spec(A) ∖ V(I)`.

The element `g` is produced by Nakayama's lemma: rig-étaleness gives a `c` with `Iᶜ B^`
annihilating `B^ ⊗_B H¹(L_{B/A})` and `B^ ⊗_B Ω_{B/A}`, so `Iᶜ B` annihilates both finite
`B`-modules only modulo `⋂ₙ (IB)ⁿ`, and one element of `1 + IB` kills that intersection.  After
inverting it, every prime of `B` off `V(IB)` contains no element of `Iᶜ B` and so lies outside
the supports of the two modules, which is étaleness there.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isEtaleOutside_localization_of_isRigEtale_adicCompletionObj
    (h : IsRigEtale (adicCompletionObj I (B := B))) :
    ∃ g : B, g - 1 ∈ I.map (algebraMap A B) ∧ IsEtaleOutside I (Localization.Away g)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Rig.isEtaleOutside_and_isRigEtale_adicCompletionObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALQ.**  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `B` a finite type
`A`-algebra, and write `B^` for the `I`-adic completion of `B`.

1. If `Spec(B) → Spec(A)` is étale over `Spec(A) ∖ V(I)`, then `B^` satisfies the equivalent
   conditions of Stacks 0AJU, in the form of their first condition `Rig.IsRigEtale`.
2. If `B^` satisfies those conditions, then there exists `g ∈ 1 + IB` such that
   `Spec(B_g) → Spec(A)` is étale over `Spec(A) ∖ V(I)`.

The two implications are `Rig.isRigEtale_adicCompletionObj_of_isEtaleOutside` and
`Rig.exists_isEtaleOutside_localization_of_isRigEtale_adicCompletionObj`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isEtaleOutside_and_isRigEtale_adicCompletionObj :
    (IsEtaleOutside I B → IsRigEtale (adicCompletionObj I (B := B))) ∧
      (IsRigEtale (adicCompletionObj I (B := B)) →
        ∃ g : B, g - 1 ∈ I.map (algebraMap A B) ∧ IsEtaleOutside I (Localization.Away g))

declarations.name: exists_finiteType_algEquiv_adicCompletion_of_cotangent_annihilated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0ALR.** A quotient of the adic completion of a finite-type algebra is itself
the adic completion of a finite-type algebra if its conormal module is annihilated by a power of
the defining ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_algEquiv_adicCompletion_of_cotangent_annihilated
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (C : Type w) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] (I : Ideal A)
    (φ : AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A B)) B →ₐ[A] C)
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) (c : ℕ)
    (hJ : I ^ c • (⊤ : Submodule A (RingHom.ker φ.toRingHom).Cotangent) = ⊥) :
    ∃ (D : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing D) (_ : Algebra A D),
      Algebra.FiniteType A D ∧
        Nonempty (C ≃ₐ[A] AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A D)) D)

declarations.name: Rig.exists_finiteType_algEquiv_of_isRigEtale_principal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALS**, the rig-étale case of [Elkik, III Theorem 7], with no restriction on the
universe of `B`.  Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and `I = (a)` a principal ideal.  Let `B` be an
object of the category of `I`-adically complete `A`-algebras of finite type modulo `I`
(Stacks 0AL4) which is rig-étale over `(A, I)`.  Then there is a finite type `A`-algebra `C`
and an isomorphism `B ≅ C^∧`.

The carrier of `B` is replaced by the quotient `A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩/J` of a presentation of `B`
(`Rig.quotientObj`), which lives in the universe of `A` and is `A`-algebra isomorphic to
`B.carrier` by `Rig.CompletedPolynomialPresentation.quotientEquiv`; rig-étaleness transports
across that isomorphism by `Rig.isRigEtale_of_algEquiv` (Stacks 0GB2), and
`Rig.exists_finiteType_algEquiv_of_isRigEtale_principal_sameUniverse` applies to it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteType_algEquiv_of_isRigEtale_principal
    (hI : I.IsPrincipal) (B : AdicFiniteTypeAlgebra.{u, v} A I) (hB : IsRigEtale B) :
    ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C),
      Algebra.FiniteType A C ∧
        Nonempty (B.carrier ≃ₐ[A] AdicCompletion (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)
declarations.comment: the rig-étale case of Elkik III Theorem 7, over a principal ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.exists_finiteType_etale_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ALT.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `J ⊆ A` a nilpotent
ideal, and consider a commutative diagram of finite type ring maps

```
C  --->  C ⧸ JC
          ^
         B₀
          ^
A  --->  A ⧸ J
```

such that `Spec C → Spec A` is étale over `Spec A \ V(I)`, such that `Spec B₀ → Spec (A ⧸ J)` is
étale over `Spec (A ⧸ J) \ V(I (A ⧸ J))`, and such that `B₀ → C ⧸ JC` is étale and induces an
isomorphism `B₀ ⧸ I B₀ = (C ⧸ JC) ⧸ I (C ⧸ JC)`. Then the diagram can be filled in: there are a
finite type `A`-algebra `B`, an `A`-algebra map `B → C` which is étale, and an isomorphism
`B ⧸ JB ≅ B₀` compatible with the maps to `C ⧸ JC`, such that `Spec B → Spec A` is étale over
`Spec A \ V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_etale_lift
    (A C B₀ : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [CommRing B₀]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra A C] [Algebra.FiniteType A C]
    (I J : Ideal A) (hJ : IsNilpotent J)
    [Algebra A B₀] [Algebra (A ⧸ J) B₀] [IsScalarTower A (A ⧸ J) B₀]
    [Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ J) B₀]
    [Algebra (A ⧸ J) (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [IsScalarTower A (A ⧸ J) (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [Algebra B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [IsScalarTower (A ⧸ J) B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [Algebra.Etale B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    (hC : ∀ q : Ideal C, ∀ _ : q.IsPrime, ¬ I ≤ q.comap (algebraMap A C) →
      Algebra.IsEtaleAt A q)
    (hB₀ : ∀ q : Ideal B₀, ∀ _ : q.IsPrime,
      ¬ I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) ≤ q.comap (algebraMap (A ⧸ J) B₀) →
        Algebra.IsEtaleAt (A ⧸ J) q)
    (hmod : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap
      (((I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)).map (algebraMap (A ⧸ J) B₀)).map
        (algebraMap B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))))
      (algebraMap B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))) Ideal.le_comap_map)) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B) (_ : Algebra.FiniteType A B)
      (_ : Algebra B C) (_ : IsScalarTower A B C) (_ : Algebra.Etale B C)
      (e : (B ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A B)) ≃ₐ[A] B₀),
      (∀ q : Ideal B, ∀ _ : q.IsPrime, ¬ I ≤ q.comap (algebraMap A B) →
        Algebra.IsEtaleAt A q) ∧
      ∀ b : B, algebraMap B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))
            (e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J.map (algebraMap A B)) b)) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (J.map (algebraMap A C)) (algebraMap B C b)

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.exists_finiteType_etale_lift_of_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and `J ⊆ A` a nilpotent ideal, and consider a
commutative diagram of finite type ring maps

```
C  --->  C ⧸ JC
          ^
         B₀
          ^
A  --->  A ⧸ J
```

such that `Spec C → Spec A` is étale over `Spec A \ V(I)`, such that `Spec B₀ → Spec (A ⧸ J)` is
étale over `Spec (A ⧸ J) \ V(I (A ⧸ J))`, and such that `B₀ → C ⧸ JC` is étale and induces an
isomorphism `B₀ ⧸ I B₀ = (C ⧸ JC) ⧸ I (C ⧸ JC)`.  Then the diagram can be filled in: there are a
finite type `A`-algebra `B`, an `A`-algebra map `B → C` which is étale, and an isomorphism
`B ⧸ JB ≅ B₀` compatible with the maps to `C ⧸ JC`, such that `Spec B → Spec A` is étale over
`Spec A \ V(I)`.

This takes the extra hypothesis `hnil` that `I B₀` is nilpotent, equivalently that the open set
`Spec B₀ \ V(I B₀)` is empty.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_etale_lift_of_isNilpotent
    (A C B₀ : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [CommRing B₀]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra A C] [Algebra.FiniteType A C]
    (I J : Ideal A) (_hJ : IsNilpotent J)
    [Algebra A B₀] [Algebra (A ⧸ J) B₀] [IsScalarTower A (A ⧸ J) B₀]
    [Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ J) B₀]
    [Algebra (A ⧸ J) (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [IsScalarTower A (A ⧸ J) (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [Algebra B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [IsScalarTower (A ⧸ J) B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [Algebra.Etale B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    (hC : ∀ q : Ideal C, ∀ _ : q.IsPrime, ¬ I ≤ q.comap (algebraMap A C) →
      Algebra.IsEtaleAt A q)
    (_hB₀ : ∀ q : Ideal B₀, ∀ _ : q.IsPrime,
      ¬ I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) ≤ q.comap (algebraMap (A ⧸ J) B₀) →
        Algebra.IsEtaleAt (A ⧸ J) q)
    (hmod : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap
      (((I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)).map (algebraMap (A ⧸ J) B₀)).map
        (algebraMap B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))))
      (algebraMap B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))) Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (hnil : IsNilpotent ((I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)).map (algebraMap (A ⧸ J) B₀))) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B) (_ : Algebra.FiniteType A B)
      (_ : Algebra B C) (_ : IsScalarTower A B C) (_ : Algebra.Etale B C)
      (e : (B ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A B)) ≃ₐ[A] B₀),
      (∀ q : Ideal B, ∀ _ : q.IsPrime, ¬ I ≤ q.comap (algebraMap A B) →
        Algebra.IsEtaleAt A q) ∧
      ∀ b : B, algebraMap B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))
            (e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J.map (algebraMap A B)) b)) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (J.map (algebraMap A C)) (algebraMap B C b)
declarations.comment: extra hypothesis: the ideal I·B₀ is nilpotent, equivalently the open set Spec(B₀) minus V(I·B₀) along which the source glues is empty; the conclusion is delivered in full

declarations.name: Stacks.Etale.exists_finiteType_etale_lift_of_eq_top
declarations.doc:
The data and the conclusion are those of `exists_finiteType_etale_lift_of_isNilpotent`, with
the extra hypothesis `htop` that `I B₀` is the unit ideal, equivalently that the closed set
`V(I B₀) ⊆ Spec B₀` is empty, in place of `hnil`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_etale_lift_of_eq_top
    (A C B₀ : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [CommRing B₀]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Algebra A C] [Algebra.FiniteType A C]
    (I J : Ideal A) (hJ : IsNilpotent J)
    [Algebra A B₀] [Algebra (A ⧸ J) B₀] [IsScalarTower A (A ⧸ J) B₀]
    [Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ J) B₀]
    [Algebra (A ⧸ J) (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [IsScalarTower A (A ⧸ J) (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [Algebra B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [IsScalarTower (A ⧸ J) B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    [Algebra.Etale B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))]
    (hC : ∀ q : Ideal C, ∀ _ : q.IsPrime, ¬ I ≤ q.comap (algebraMap A C) →
      Algebra.IsEtaleAt A q)
    (hB₀ : ∀ q : Ideal B₀, ∀ _ : q.IsPrime,
      ¬ I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J) ≤ q.comap (algebraMap (A ⧸ J) B₀) →
        Algebra.IsEtaleAt (A ⧸ J) q)
    (_hmod : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap
      (((I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)).map (algebraMap (A ⧸ J) B₀)).map
        (algebraMap B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))))
      (algebraMap B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))) Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (htop : (I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)).map (algebraMap (A ⧸ J) B₀) = ⊤) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B) (_ : Algebra.FiniteType A B)
      (_ : Algebra B C) (_ : IsScalarTower A B C) (_ : Algebra.Etale B C)
      (e : (B ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A B)) ≃ₐ[A] B₀),
      (∀ q : Ideal B, ∀ _ : q.IsPrime, ¬ I ≤ q.comap (algebraMap A B) →
        Algebra.IsEtaleAt A q) ∧
      ∀ b : B, algebraMap B₀ (C ⧸ J.map (algebraMap A C))
            (e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (J.map (algebraMap A B)) b)) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (J.map (algebraMap A C)) (algebraMap B C b)
declarations.comment: extra hypothesis: I·B₀ is the unit ideal of B₀, equivalently the closed set V(I·B₀) in Spec(B₀) along which the source glues is empty; the conclusion is delivered in full

declarations.name: Ring.krullDimLE_one_of_finite_primeSpectrum
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian ring with finitely many primes has dimension at most `1`: every prime ideal is
either minimal or maximal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem krullDimLE_one_of_finite_primeSpectrum (R : Type*) [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Finite (PrimeSpectrum R)] :
    KrullDimLE 1 R

declarations.name: Algebra.FiniteType.krullDimLE_zero_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Zero-dimensional finite type algebras.** For an algebra `S` of finite type over an
Artinian ring `R` the following are equivalent: `S` has Krull dimension at most `0`; `S` has
finitely many prime ideals; `S` has finitely many maximal ideals; `Spec S` is Hausdorff; `S` is
finite as an `R`-module; `S` is Artinian; `Spec S` is discrete; and `Spec S` is totally
disconnected. Over a field `R = k` the fifth condition says that `S` is finite dimensional
as a `k`-vector space.
declarations.statement:
public theorem krullDimLE_zero_tfae (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsArtinianRing R] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] :
    List.TFAE
      [ Ring.KrullDimLE 0 S,
        Finite (PrimeSpectrum S),
        Finite (MaximalSpectrum S),
        T2Space (PrimeSpectrum S),
        Module.Finite R S,
        IsArtinianRing S,
        DiscreteTopology (PrimeSpectrum S),
        TotallyDisconnectedSpace (PrimeSpectrum S) ]
declarations.comment: Items (1)-(8); (4) via 04MG's Hausdorff and totally disconnected conditions.

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.CechFormula.localCohomology_derivedTensorProduct_right
declarations.doc:
Local cohomology of a derived tensor product is naturally the tensor product
with local cohomology in the right variable.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomology_derivedTensorProduct_right
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    derivedTensorProductBifunctor A ⋙ localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI ≅
      (Functor.prod (𝟭 _) (localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI)) ⋙
        derivedTensorProductBifunctor A
declarations.comment: local cohomology on the right

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.CechFormula.localCohomology_derivedTensorProduct_left
declarations.doc:
Tensoring local cohomology in the right variable is naturally isomorphic to
tensoring it in the left variable.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomology_derivedTensorProduct_left
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    (Functor.prod (𝟭 _) (localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI)) ⋙
        derivedTensorProductBifunctor A ≅
      (Functor.prod (localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI) (𝟭 _)) ⋙
        derivedTensorProductBifunctor A
declarations.comment: local cohomology on the left

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.CechFormula.localCohomology_derivedTensorProduct_both
declarations.doc:
Applying local cohomology in both tensor factors is naturally equivalent to
applying it in just the left factor.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomology_derivedTensorProduct_both
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) :
    (Functor.prod (localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI) (𝟭 _)) ⋙
        derivedTensorProductBifunctor A ≅
      (Functor.prod (localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI)
        (localCohomologyEndofunctor A I hI)) ⋙
        derivedTensorProductBifunctor A
declarations.comment: local cohomology in both factors

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.CechFormula.derivedTensorProduct_mem_powerTorsion_left
declarations.doc:
Tensoring on the right preserves a complex with `I`-power-torsion
cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorProduct_mem_powerTorsion_left
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI K) :
    Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI
      ((derivedTensorProductBifunctor A).obj (K, L))
declarations.comment: torsion in the left factor

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.CechFormula.derivedTensorProduct_mem_powerTorsion_right
declarations.doc:
Tensoring on the left preserves a complex with `I`-power-torsion
cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorProduct_mem_powerTorsion_right
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hL : Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI L) :
    Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI
      ((derivedTensorProductBifunctor A).obj (K, L))
declarations.comment: torsion in the right factor

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
Local cohomology with support in a finitely generated ideal
commutes naturally with arbitrary derived extension of scalars.
declarations.statement:
def localCohomologyBaseChangeIso :
    Dualizing.localCohomologyFunctor A I hI ⋙
          (Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI).ι ⋙
          (derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral f).functor ≅
      (derivedExtensionScalarsGeneral f).functor ⋙
          Dualizing.localCohomologyFunctor B (I.map f) (hI.map f) ⋙
          (Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsionProperty B (I.map f) (hI.map f)).ι

declarations.name: Dualizing.powerTorsionDerivedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AM0.** Flat base change and restriction of scalars are quasi-inverse on
the derived categories of objects with power-torsion cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem powerTorsionDerivedEquivalence
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (hflat : Module.Flat A B)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap A B)) (algebraMap A B)
        Ideal.le_comap_map)) :
    ∃ e : PowerTorsionDerivedCategory.{u, max u v w} A I hI ≌
        PowerTorsionDerivedCategory.{v, max u v w} B
          (I.map (algebraMap A B)) (Ideal.FG.map hI (algebraMap A B)),
      Nonempty (e.functor ⋙
          (derivedPowerTorsionProperty B (I.map (algebraMap A B))
            (Ideal.FG.map hI (algebraMap A B))).ι ≅
        (derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI).ι ⋙
          (CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, v, w}
            (algebraMap A B)).functor) ∧
      Nonempty (e.inverse ⋙ (derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI).ι ≅
        (derivedPowerTorsionProperty B (I.map (algebraMap A B))
          (Ideal.FG.map hI (algebraMap A B))).ι ⋙
          (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v w} (algebraMap A B)).mapDerivedCategory)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasProperty.mono
declarations.doc:
The property tested by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasProperty` may be enlarged: if `P` implies
`Q` for every morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, then a morphism of presheaves representable
by algebraic spaces having `P` also has `Q`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isQuasiCompact_iff_hasPropertyULift'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AM2.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which
is representable by algebraic spaces. Then `f` is quasi-compact in the sense of Stacks 0AJC —
every fibre product of it with an affine scheme over `S` in the site is a quasi-compact formal
algebraic space — exactly when it is quasi-compact in the sense of Bootstrap, Definition
03XZ: every fibre product of it with a scheme over `S` in the site is quasi-compact over that
scheme as a morphism of algebraic spaces.

Both directions pass through the agreement of the two notions of quasi-compactness of a space
on an algebraic space, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.quasiCompactSpaceAgreesOnAlgebraicSpaces`. For the remaining
direction the bootstrap condition must be tested against the quasi-compact, not only the
affine, schemes over `S` in the site, which is the implication (3) ⇒ (2) of Stacks 0AJB,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsQuasiCompact.isQuasiCompactOnSchemeBaseChanges`. The witnesses
that the source and the target are formal algebraic spaces are not used, so the statement is
for an arbitrary morphism of fppf sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiCompact_iff_hasPropertyULift' {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom) :
    IsQuasiCompact B S hS f ↔
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.quasiCompactPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS) f.hom hf
declarations.comment: both directions, for an arbitrary morphism of fppf sheaves representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is *locally of finite type* when it is
representable by algebraic spaces and every base change of it along a scheme-valued point of its
target is a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite type. The condition is stated
for an arbitrary morphism of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsLocallyOfFiniteType {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1): locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is *of finite type* when it is representable
by algebraic spaces and every base change of it along a scheme-valued point of its target is a
morphism of algebraic spaces which is of finite type. The condition is stated for an arbitrary
morphism of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFiniteType {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2): finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFiniteType'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AM4, part (2)**, which is **Stacks 0AJJ, condition (1)**. A morphism of formal
algebraic spaces over `S` is *of finite type* when it is locally of finite type, in the sense
of Definition 0AM4, part (1), and quasi-compact, in the sense of Definition 0AJC. The
condition makes sense, and is stated, for an arbitrary morphism of fppf sheaves on the big
fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFiniteType' {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2): finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AM6.** A morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is *proper* when it is
representable by algebraic spaces and every base change of it along a scheme-valued point of
its target is a morphism of algebraic spaces which is proper, that is, separated, of finite
type and universally closed. The condition makes sense, and is stated, for an arbitrary
morphism of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsProper {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isProper_of_forall_surjective_etale_cover
declarations.doc:
**Properness of morphisms of formal algebraic spaces is local on the target.** A morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` is proper in the sense of
**Stacks 0AM6** as soon as every scheme-valued point `ξ : U ⟶ Y` of its target admits a
morphism `q : U' ⟶ U` of the site, surjective and étale on underlying schemes, such that the
base change of `f` along `U' ⟶ U ⟶ Y` is an algebraic space over `S` proper over `U'`.

Being an algebraic space descends along `q` by **Stacks 0BGR** and properness by
**Stacks 0422**, both applied to the base change of the universe-lifted Yoneda image of `q`
along the projection of the base change of `f` along `ξ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_forall_surjective_etale_cover {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (h : ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ξ : (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).obj U ⟶ Y.obj),
      ∃ (U' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : U' ⟶ U),
        Surjective ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map q) ∧
        Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map q) ∧
        Space.IsAlgebraicSpaceULift.{u + 1} B S hS
          (pullback ((uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).map q ≫ ξ) f.hom) ∧
        Space.IsProperULift.{u + 1} B S hS
          (pullback.fst ((uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).map q ≫ ξ) f.hom)) :
    IsProper B S hS f
declarations.comment: local on the target

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isProper_of_isRepresentable_of_forall_fppfFamily
declarations.doc:
**Properness of a morphism representable by algebraic spaces is local on the target for a
covering family of the site.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of fppf sheaves on the big fppf
site of `S` which is representable by algebraic spaces, and suppose every scheme-valued point
`ξ : U ⟶ Y` of its target admits a family `{qᵢ : Vᵢ ⟶ U}` of morphisms of the site whose Yoneda
images form an fppf covering family of `U`, such that the base change of `f` along each
`Vᵢ ⟶ U ⟶ Y` is proper as a morphism of algebraic spaces. Then `f` is proper in the sense of
**Stacks 0AM6**.

Unlike `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isProper_of_forall_surjective_etale_cover` this takes a
*family* and not one morphism, so it needs no coproduct of the members inside the site; what it
asks instead is that `f` be representable by algebraic spaces, since being an algebraic space is
the half of properness which the family form of **Stacks 0422** does not descend. The base
change of `f` along `Vᵢ ⟶ U ⟶ Y` is compared with the base change along `qᵢ` of the base change
along `ξ` by `CategoryTheory.Limits.pullbackRightPullbackFstIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProper_of_isRepresentable_of_forall_fppfFamily {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom)
    (h : ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (ξ : (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).obj U ⟶ Y.obj),
      ∃ (Idx : Type (u + 1)) (V : Idx → BigFppfOver B S hS) (q : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U),
        Space.IsFppfCovering B S hS (fun i => yoneda.obj (V i))
          (fun i => yoneda.map (q i)) ∧
        ∀ i, Space.IsProperULift.{u + 1} B S hS
          (pullback.fst ((uliftYoneda.{u + 1}).map (q i) ≫ ξ) f.hom)) :
    IsProper B S hS f
declarations.comment: local on the target for a covering family, given representability

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.exists_rightAdjoint_truncation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AMA**.
If `C` has finite limits then for every `m` the skeleton functor `sk_m : Simp(C) ⥤ Simp_m(C)` has
a right adjoint, so that the coskeleton functor `cosk_m` exists: morphisms `U ⟶ cosk_m V` of
simplicial objects correspond naturally to morphisms `sk_m U ⟶ V` of `m`-truncated ones.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_rightAdjoint_truncation [HasFiniteLimits C] (m : ℕ) :
    ∃ G : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m ⥤ SimplicialObject C,
      Nonempty (SimplicialObject.truncation (C := C) m ⊣ G)
declarations.comment: the section's assertion that `cosk_m` exists for every `m` over a category with finite limits, which is Lemma 0183 inside the section; the degreewise limit formula is `coskConeIsLimit` below

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.existsUnique_iso_rightAdjoint_truncation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AMA**.
A right adjoint of `sk_m` is unique up to unique isomorphism: if `G` and `G'` are both right
adjoint to `sk_m`, there is exactly one isomorphism `G ≅ G'` compatible with the two counits.
declarations.comment: the section's uniqueness assertion, that a representing object `cosk_m V` is unique up to unique isomorphism by the Yoneda lemma; `compatible with the counits` is the form the uniqueness takes for the adjunctions themselves

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.coskConeIsLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AMA**.
The degreewise limit formula for the coskeleton: for an `m`-truncated simplicial object `U` of a
category with finite limits the canonical cone over `U(n)` with apex `(cosk_m U)_n` is a limit
cone, so `(cosk_m U)_n` is the limit of `U(n)` over `((Δ/[n])_{≤ m})ᵒᵖ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coskConeIsLimit (m : ℕ) (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) (n : ℕ) :
    IsLimit (coskCone m U n)
declarations.comment: the degreewise limit formula

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.map_eq_coskConeIsLimit_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AMA**.
The naturality half of the degreewise limit formula: `cosk_m U(φ)` is the morphism of limits
induced by postcomposition with `φ : [n] → [n']`, the canonical cone in degree `n'` restricted
along that functor being a cone over `U(n)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem map_eq_coskConeIsLimit_lift {m : ℕ} (U : SimplicialObject.Truncated C m) {n n' : ℕ}
    (φ : SimplexCategory.mk n ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n') :
    ((Truncated.cosk m).obj U).map φ.op =
      (coskConeIsLimit m U n).lift
        ((coskCone m U n').whisker (CostructuredArrow.map φ).op)
declarations.comment: the second clause of the degreewise limit formula, that for `φ : [n] → [n']` the map `cosk_m U(φ)` comes from the identification of `U(n')` restricted along `φ` with `U(n)`

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod_rootsOfUnityRestriction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AMB].**  Let `k` be an algebraically closed field, let `π : X ⟶ Y` be a
nonconstant morphism of smooth proper curves over `k`, and let `n` be invertible in `k`.  In the
coordinates of `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod`, which identify both
`H²_étale(Y, μ_n)` and `H²_étale(X, μ_n)` with `𝐙/n𝐙`, the pullback

`π^* : H²_étale(Y, μ_n) ⟶ H²_étale(X, μ_n)`

is multiplication by the degree `deg(X/Y) = [R(X) : R(Y)]` of the extension of function fields
([Stacks, Tag 02NY]).

The proof is the source's.  Every class of `H²_étale(Y, μ_n)` is the Kummer coboundary of a class
`a` of `H¹_étale(Y, 𝐆_m)` ([Stacks, Tag 03RM]), and the coordinate of that coboundary is the
degree of `a` modulo `n`.  Restriction along `π` commutes with the Kummer coboundary
(`Stacks.Kummer.etaleCohomologyRestrictionMap_kummerExtClass`), so the coordinate of the
restricted class is the degree of the restriction of `a`, which is `deg(X/Y)` times the degree of
`a` by `Stacks.EtaleCohomology.sheafHOneMultiplicativeDegreeMod_multiplicativeRestriction` —
and that is where nonconstancy of `π` is used, through the rank-one case of [Stacks, Tag 0AYZ].
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod_rootsOfUnityRestriction
    (x : Sheaf.H.{u + 1} (Stacks.Kummer.rootsOfUnitySheaf.{u, u + 1} Y n) 2) :
    sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod gX hn
        (rootsOfUnityRestriction.{u, u + 1, u + 1} π n 2 x) =
      ((@degreeOver X Y π _ _ (locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k gX gY π hπ)
            (isDominant_of_not_constant k gX gY π hnc) : ℕ) : ZMod n) *
        sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod gY hn x
declarations.comment: for a nonconstant morphism pi : X -> Y of smooth proper curves over an algebraically closed field k and n invertible in k, the pullback pi^* : H^2_etale(Y, mu_n) -> H^2_etale(X, mu_n) is multiplication by the degree of pi, under the canonical identifications H^2_etale(-, mu_n) = Z/nZ of Stacks 03RQ (sheafHTwoRootsOfUnityAddEquivZMod), given by the Kummer coboundary of H^1_etale(-, G_m) = Cl(-) = Pic(-) followed by the degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionAlongClosedSubset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AMC.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and let
`T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset. The *completion of `X` along `T`* is the formal algebraic space
`X_{/T}` of Stacks 0AIZ: the fppf sheaf `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionSheaf` attached to the
functor sending `U` to the morphisms `f : U ⟶ X` with `f(|U|) ⊆ T`, as an object of the full
subcategory of formal algebraic spaces over `S`, the membership being
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheaf_of_isClosed`.
declarations.statement:
def completionAlongClosedSubset {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T) :
    ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS)

declarations.name: Ideal.le_ringJacobson_iff_isUnit_one_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AME**, (1) ⇔ (2): an ideal is contained in the Jacobson radical if and only if
every element of `1 + I` is a unit.

Forwards is `Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot` at `y = 1`. Backwards uses that `I` is an ideal: to place
`x ∈ I` in the radical one must invert `1 + x * y` for every `y`, and `x * y` is again in `I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem le_ringJacobson_iff_isUnit_one_add (I : Ideal R) :
    I ≤ Ring.jacobson R ↔ ∀ x ∈ I, IsUnit (1 + x)

declarations.name: Ideal.isUnit_of_isUnit_quotient_mk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AME**, the closing clause: if `I` is contained in the Jacobson radical, then an
element of `R` whose image in `R ⧸ I` is a unit is itself a unit.

Given a right inverse `y` mod `I`, the difference `x * y - 1` lies in `I` and hence in the
radical, so `x * y` is a unit by `Ideal.isUnit_of_sub_one_mem_jacobson_bot`; a factor of a unit
in a commutative ring is a unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnit_of_isUnit_quotient_mk (I : Ideal R) (h : I ≤ Ring.jacobson R) (x : R)
    (hx : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk I x)) : IsUnit x
declarations.comment: in this case a unit mod I is a unit

declarations.name: Stacks.NilpotentIdeal.PowerMap.isUnit_quotient_mk_iff
declarations.doc: Units are detected modulo a locally nilpotent ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUnit_quotient_mk_iff (hI : ∀ x ∈ I, IsNilpotent x) {x : R} :
    IsUnit x ↔ IsUnit ((Ideal.Quotient.mk I) x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_isStableUnderComposition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AML.** A property of morphisms of schemes which is étale local on the source and
target and stable under composition induces a composition stable property of morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S`, namely the condition that it hold on every commuting square of
étale charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_isStableUnderComposition
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hP : IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget P)
    [P.IsStableUnderComposition] :
    MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderComposition
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) =>
        HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS P f.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_isStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc:
A property of morphisms of schemes which is étale local on the source and
target and stable under base change induces a base-change stable property of morphisms of
algebraic spaces over `S`, namely the condition that it hold on every commuting square of etale
charts.
declarations.statement:
theorem holdsOnEveryEtaleChart_isStableUnderBaseChange
    (P : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
    (hP : IsEtaleLocalOnSourceAndTarget P)
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange] :
    MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
      (fun ⦃F G : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS⦄ (f : F ⟶ G) =>
        HoldsOnEveryEtaleChart B S hS P f.hom)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_comp
declarations.doc:
If the relative diagonal of `b` and the composite `a ≫ b` are
representable by algebraic spaces, then so is `a`, for presheaves on the big fppf site of `S`
with values in `Type (max w u)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_comp
    {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w u)} (a : F ⟶ G) (b : G ⟶ H)
    (hdiag : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS (pullback.diagonal b))
    (hcomp : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS (a ≫ b)) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS a
declarations.comment: representable by algebraic spaces in an arbitrary value universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AMN.** If the relative diagonal of `b` and the composite `a ≫ b` are
representable by algebraic spaces, then so is `a`.

The base change of `a` along `ξ` is the base change of the relative diagonal of `b` along
the canonical morphism from the base change of `a ≫ b` along `ξ ≫ b` to `pullback b b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_comp
    {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (a : F ⟶ G) (b : G ⟶ H)
    (hdiag : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (pullback.diagonal b))
    (hcomp : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS (a ≫ b)) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_comp_of_flat_surjective_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AMP.** Let `a : F ⟶ G` and `b : G ⟶ H` be morphisms of presheaves on the big fppf
site of `S`, with `G` and `H` sheaves.  If `a` is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective,
flat and locally of finite presentation and the composite `a ≫ b` is representable by algebraic
spaces, then `b` is representable by algebraic spaces.

At a scheme-valued point `ξ` of `H` the fibre product `U ×_H F` is an algebraic space, being a
base change of `a ≫ b`, and `U ×_H G` is a sheaf.  The morphism `U ×_H F ⟶ U ×_H G` is the base
change of `a` along `U ×_H G ⟶ G`, so Stacks 046F gives it the three properties of `a`, and
Stacks 04S6 condition (3) makes `U ×_H G` an algebraic space; that deduction is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_of_comp_of_flat_surjective`, whose
bootstrap input is discharged here by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isBootstrapAlgebraicSpaceAlongFlatSurjection`.

Sheafness of `F` is assumed in the source and is not needed here: representability of `a ≫ b`
already makes the base changes of `F` that the argument uses algebraic spaces.

This is the complete statement of Stacks 0AMP and its only registration; nothing is assumed.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: TopologicalModule.Nonuniform.exists_pow_X_smul_mem
declarations.doc:
The pointwise condition of the source: for every `m` and every `x ∈ ⨁_{n ∈ ℕ} k[[t]]` there
is a `j` with `t ^ j • x ∈ M m`. It holds because `x` has only finitely many nonzero
coordinates.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_X_smul_mem (m : ℕ) (x : ℕ →₀ PowerSeries k) :
    ∃ j : ℕ, (X : PowerSeries k) ^ j • x ∈ coordinateSubmodule k m
declarations.comment: nonuniform_module_example

declarations.name: TopologicalModule.Nonuniform.not_exists_forall_pow_X_smul_mem
declarations.doc: The uniform condition fails: for `m ≥ 1` there is no `j` with `t ^ j • M ⊆ M m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_exists_forall_pow_X_smul_mem {m : ℕ} (hm : 1 ≤ m) :
    ¬ ∃ j : ℕ, ∀ x : ℕ →₀ PowerSeries k,
      (X : PowerSeries k) ^ j • x ∈ coordinateSubmodule k m
declarations.comment: nonuniform_module_example

declarations.name: TopologicalModule.Nonuniform.exists_isLinearTopology_not_exists_isOpen_ideal_smul_mem
declarations.doc:
The source's example, as an existence statement: over `R = k[[t]]` with the `t`-adic
topology there is a linearly topologized `R`-module `M`, with a fundamental system `N` of open
submodules, for which no open ideal `I` of `R` satisfies `I • M ⊆ N 1`.
declarations.comment: nonuniform_module_example

declarations.name: TopologicalModule.continuousSMul_iff_forall_exists_smul_mem
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0AMR.** Let `I` be a fundamental system of open ideals of a topological ring `R` and
let `N` be a fundamental system of open submodules of an `R`-module `M`. Then scalar
multiplication `R × M → M` is continuous exactly when `I λ • x ⊆ N μ` for some `λ`, for every
`x : M` and every `μ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuousSMul_iff_forall_exists_smul_mem
    (hI : (𝓝 (0 : R)).HasBasis (fun _ : ι ↦ True) fun l ↦ (I l : Set R))
    (hN : (𝓝 (0 : M)).HasBasis (fun _ : κ ↦ True) fun m ↦ (N m : Set M)) :
    ContinuousSMul R M ↔ ∀ (x : M) (μ : κ), ∃ l : ι, ∀ f ∈ I l, f • x ∈ N μ
declarations.comment: scalar_continuity_criterion

declarations.name: TopologicalModule.continuousSMul_iff_forall_exists_coset_smul_coset
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0AMR.** The displayed form of the continuity of `R × M → M`: for all `f`, `x` and `μ`
there are `λ` and `ν` with `(f + I λ) • (x + N ν) ⊆ f • x + N μ`. The source deduces it from
`TopologicalModule.continuousSMul_iff_forall_exists_smul_mem` using that `f • N ν + I λ • N ν ⊆
N μ` whenever `N ν ⊆ N μ`; here `ν = μ` always works.
declarations.statement:
theorem continuousSMul_iff_forall_exists_coset_smul_coset
    (hI : (𝓝 (0 : R)).HasBasis (fun _ : ι ↦ True) fun l ↦ (I l : Set R))
    (hN : (𝓝 (0 : M)).HasBasis (fun _ : κ ↦ True) fun m ↦ (N m : Set M)) :
    ContinuousSMul R M ↔ ∀ (f : R) (x : M) (μ : κ), ∃ (l : ι) (ν : κ),
      ∀ g ∈ I l, ∀ y ∈ N ν, (f + g) • (x + y) - f • x ∈ N μ
declarations.comment: scalar_continuity_criterion

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.continuous_add_of_hasBasis_addSubgroup
declarations.doc: Addition is continuous when translates of additive subgroups form a neighborhood basis.
declarations.statement:
public theorem continuous_add_of_hasBasis_addSubgroup
    {M ι : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (Mμ : ι → AddSubgroup M)
    (hbasis : ∀ x : M, (nhds x).HasBasis (fun _ : ι => True)
      (fun μ => (fun y : M => x + y) '' (Mμ μ : Set M))) :
    Continuous (fun p : M × M => p.1 + p.2)
declarations.comment: addition_continuous

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.exists_isOpen_ideal_map_le
declarations.doc:
Every open ideal in the target of a continuous ring homomorphism contains the extension
of an open ideal from the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_ideal_map_le {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]

declarations.comment: continuous_ring_map_open_ideal

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.closure_eq_iInter_sup_of_hasBasis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AMS.** Let `M` be a linearly topologized `R`-module and let
`L i`, `i : ι`, be a fundamental system of open submodules of `M`. The closure of a submodule
`N ⊆ M` is the intersection of the submodules `N + L i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem closure_eq_iInter_sup_of_hasBasis {ι : Sort*} (L : ι → Submodule R M)
    (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen ((L i : Set M)))
    (hbasis : (𝓝 (0 : M)).HasBasis (fun _ : ι ↦ True) fun i ↦ ((L i : Set M)))
    (N : Submodule R M) :
    closure (N : Set M) = ⋂ i, ((N ⊔ L i : Submodule R M) : Set M)

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.topologicalClosure_eq_iInf_sup_of_hasBasis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AMS**, as an equality of submodules: the topological closure of a
submodule `N` is the infimum of the submodules `N + L i` over a fundamental system `L i` of open
submodules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem topologicalClosure_eq_iInf_sup_of_hasBasis [ContinuousConstSMul R M]
    {ι : Sort*} (L : ι → Submodule R M)
    (hopen : ∀ i, IsOpen ((L i : Set M)))
    (hbasis : (𝓝 (0 : M)).HasBasis (fun _ : ι ↦ True) fun i ↦ ((L i : Set M)))
    (N : Submodule R M) :
    N.topologicalClosure = ⨅ i, (N ⊔ L i : Submodule R M)
declarations.comment: the same identity read as an equality of submodules

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.t2Space_quotient_of_isClosed

**Stacks Project, Tag 0AMT.** The quotient of a linearly topologized module by a closed
submodule is separated; this is the Hausdorff half of the completeness of `M ⧸ N`.

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.completeSpace_quotient_of_isCountablyGenerated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AMT.** The quotient of a complete, linearly topologized module with a
countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero by a submodule is itself complete for the
canonical uniformity of a topological additive group.
declarations.statement:
public lemma completeSpace_quotient_of_isCountablyGenerated {R : Type u} {M : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalRing R]

The topology on the usual tensor product whose fundamental open

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.quotientTensorProductLimitIdentification
declarations.doc:
The componentwise quotient-tensor-quotient equivalences identify the two
inverse limits in Tag 0AMU.  The specification records that the map is exactly
`TensorProduct.quotientTensorQuotientEquiv` in every component.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quotientTensorProductLimitIdentification :
    { e : QuotientTensorProductLimit (R := R) (M := M) (N := N) ≃L[R]
        TensorProductQuotientLimit (R := R) (M := M) (N := N) //
      ∀ x : QuotientTensorProductLimit (R := R) (M := M) (N := N),
        ∀ i : TensorProductSubmoduleIndex (R := R) (M := M) (N := N),
          ((e x : TensorProductQuotientLimit (R := R) (M := M) (N := N)) :
              ∀ j : TensorProductSubmoduleIndex (R := R) (M := M) (N := N),
                TensorProductQuotient j) i =
            TensorProduct.quotientTensorQuotientEquiv i.1.1 i.2.1
              (((x : QuotientTensorProductLimit (R := R) (M := M) (N := N)) :
                  ∀ j : TensorProductSubmoduleIndex (R := R) (M := M) (N := N),
                    QuotientTensorProduct j) i) }
declarations.comment: second inverse-limit identification

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.exists_completedTensorProductEquivQuotientLimit
declarations.doc:
The completion is canonically topologically linearly isomorphic to the
inverse limit of its discrete quotients. Every component of the identification
extends the usual quotient map.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_completedTensorProductEquivQuotientLimit :
    ∃ e : CompletedTensorProduct (R := R) (M := M) (N := N) ≃L[R]
        TensorProductQuotientLimit (R := R) (M := M) (N := N),
      ∀ z : M ⊗[R] N,
        ∀ i : TensorProductSubmoduleIndex (R := R) (M := M) (N := N),
          ((e (↑z : CompletedTensorProduct (R := R) (M := M) (N := N)) :
              TensorProductQuotientLimit (R := R) (M := M) (N := N)) :
              ∀ j : TensorProductSubmoduleIndex (R := R) (M := M) (N := N),
                TensorProductQuotient j) i = Submodule.Quotient.mk z
declarations.comment: first inverse-limit identification

Extending an ideal consisting of topologically nilpotent elements along a continuous

declarations.name: RingHom.IsTaut
declarations.doc:
A ring homomorphism is *taut* if the closure of the extension of each open source ideal is
open, and the resulting closed extended ideals form a neighbourhood basis of zero in the target.

For the Stacks definition, the source and target are linearly topologized rings and the
homomorphism is continuous; those ambient hypotheses are imposed by statements using this
predicate.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsTaut {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] (φ : A →+* B) : Prop

declarations.name: RingHom.isTaut_iff_hasBasis_isWeakIdealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
A continuous homomorphism of weakly admissible topological rings is taut exactly when the
closed extensions of the weak ideals of definition are weak ideals of definition and form a
neighbourhood basis of zero in the target.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTaut_iff_hasBasis_isWeakIdealOfDefinition
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B] (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) :
    RingHom.IsTaut φ ↔
      (∀ I : Ideal A, TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I →
        TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition (Ideal.closure (I.map φ))) ∧
      (nhds (0 : B)).HasBasis
        (fun I : Ideal A ↦ TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I)
        (fun I : Ideal A ↦ (Ideal.closure (I.map φ) : Set B))

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.closure_map_eq_ker_completedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
The closure of the extension of `I` to `B` is the kernel of the canonical map
`B → B ⊗̂[A] (A ⧸ I)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem closure_map_eq_ker_completedTensorProduct
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [TopologicalSpace B]
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [IsLinearTopology B B]
    (h : Continuous (algebraMap A B)) (I : Ideal A) :
    (Ideal.closure (I.map (algebraMap A B)) : Set B) =
      {b : B | (↑(b ⊗ₜ[A] (1 : A ⧸ I)) :
        TopologicalRing.CompletedTensorProduct (R := A) (M := B) (N := A ⧸ I)) = 0}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_continuous_ringEquiv_of_formalSpectrum_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN0, applied in both directions.** An isomorphism of the formal spectra of two
weakly admissible topological rings over `S` is the formal spectrum of a ring equivalence
which is continuous in both directions. Each direction of the isomorphism is `Spf` of a unique
continuous ring map over `S`, and each composite is a continuous ring map over `S` whose formal
spectrum is the identity, hence by uniqueness is the identity ring map. The equivalence is the
one those two ring maps make: its two directions are `g` and `g'`, whose formal spectra are the
two directions of the given isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_continuous_ringEquiv_of_formalSpectrum_iso
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
    {D : QuotientSystem B S hS A} {E : QuotientSystem B S hS C}
    (e : formalSpectrum E ≅ formalSpectrum D) :
    ∃ (g : ContinuousHom D E) (g' : ContinuousHom E D) (φ : A ≃+* C),
      formalSpectrumMap hA g = e.hom ∧ formalSpectrumMap hC g' = e.inv ∧
        ⇑φ = ⇑g.toRingHom ∧ ⇑φ.symm = ⇑g'.toRingHom ∧
          Continuous φ ∧ Continuous φ.symm
declarations.comment: the isomorphism of topological rings underlying an isomorphism of formal spectra, from the existence and uniqueness of the two continuous homomorphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.existsUnique_continuousHom_formalSpectrumMap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN0.** Let `A` and `C` be weakly admissible topological rings over `S`. Every
morphism `f : Spf C ⟶ Spf A` of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S` is `Spf (f^♯)` for a
unique continuous ring map `f^♯ : A → C` over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_continuousHom_formalSpectrumMap_eq
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
    {D : QuotientSystem B S hS A} {E : QuotientSystem B S hS C}
    (f : formalSpectrum E ⟶ formalSpectrum D) :
    ∃! g : ContinuousHom D E, formalSpectrumMap hA g = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_countable_isPresentingRing_of_isCountablyIndexed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN1, condition (1) implies condition (2)**, in the `IsPresentingRing` shape. A
countably indexed affine formal algebraic space over `S` has a presenting weakly admissible
topological ring whose neighbourhood filter of zero is countably generated.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_countable_isPresentingRing_of_isCountablyIndexed (X : FppfSheaf B S hS)
    (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hXc : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X) :
    ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : TopologicalSpace C) (_ : IsTopologicalRing C)
      (_ : IsLinearTopology C C), IsPresentingRing B S hS C X ∧
        (nhds (0 : C)).IsCountablyGenerated
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies condition (2), with `X = Spf A` read as the weak-ideal colimit presentation of Stacks 0AIC rather than as an isomorphism with a formal spectrum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_of_isPresentingRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN1, condition (2) implies condition (1)**, in the `IsPresentingRing` shape. If a
weakly admissible topological ring with countably generated neighbourhood filter of zero
presents `X`, then `X` is countably indexed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexed_of_isPresentingRing (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : IsPresentingRing B S hS A X) (hc : (nhds (0 : A)).IsCountablyGenerated) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1), with `X = Spf A` read as the weak-ideal colimit presentation of Stacks 0AIC rather than as an isomorphism with a formal spectrum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasCountableWeakPresentation_iff_hasWeakIdealChain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN1**, conditions (2) and (3) are equivalent. A countably generated filter of
neighbourhoods of `0` in a weakly admissible ring is based on a descending chain of weak ideals
of definition, and such a chain is in particular a countable fundamental system.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCountableWeakPresentation_iff_hasWeakIdealChain (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) :
    HasCountableWeakPresentation B S hS X ↔ HasWeakIdealChain B S hS X
declarations.comment: conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasWeakIdealChain_iff_hasNilpotentIdealChain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN1**, conditions (3) and (4) are equivalent. A chain of weak ideals of definition
has locally nilpotent successive quotients because its members consist of topologically
nilpotent elements; conversely, if the successive quotients are locally nilpotent then every
element of a member of the chain is topologically nilpotent, so each member is a weak ideal of
definition and the ring is weakly pre-admissible.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasWeakIdealChain_iff_hasNilpotentIdealChain (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) :
    HasWeakIdealChain B S hS X ↔ HasNilpotentIdealChain B S hS X
declarations.comment: conditions (3) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLimitOfNilpotentQuotients_of_hasWeakIdealChain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN1**, condition (3) implies condition (5). A chain of weak ideals of definition
basing the topology of a weakly admissible `A` exhibits `A` itself as the inverse limit
`lim A/Iₙ` with the limit topology, and the `S`-algebra of condition (5) can be taken to be `A`:
the successive quotients `Iₙ/Iₙ₊₁` are locally nilpotent, the kernels of the quotient maps are
the `Iₙ`, and the structure morphisms of the quotient system are already indexed by weak ideals
of definition, each of which contains some `Iₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimitOfNilpotentQuotients_of_hasWeakIdealChain (X : FppfSheaf B S hS)
    (hX : HasWeakIdealChain B S hS X) : IsLimitOfNilpotentQuotients B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasCountableWeakPresentation_of_isLimitOfNilpotentQuotients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN1**, condition (5) implies condition (2). The presenting ring of an inverse
limit presentation is weakly admissible, and the kernels of the projections are a countable
fundamental system of neighbourhoods of `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCountableWeakPresentation_of_isLimitOfNilpotentQuotients (X : FppfSheaf B S hS)
    (hX : IsLimitOfNilpotentQuotients B S hS X) : HasCountableWeakPresentation B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (5) implies condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexedAffine_of_hasCountableWeakPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN1**, condition (2) implies condition (1). The formal spectrum of a weakly
admissible ring over `S` is an affine formal algebraic space (**Stacks 0AIF**) once the site is
large enough, which a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of `0` guarantees, and it
is countably indexed because such a system is cofinal in the weak ideals of definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexedAffine_of_hasCountableWeakPresentation (X : FppfSheaf B S hS)
    (hX : HasCountableWeakPresentation B S hS X) : IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasCountableWeakPresentation_of_isCountablyIndexedAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN1**, condition (1) implies condition (2). A countably indexed affine formal
algebraic space is the formal spectrum of the limit of the section rings of a sequential
presentation (**Stacks 0AIK**, item (6)); that ring is weakly admissible and the kernels of
its projections are a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCountableWeakPresentation_of_isCountablyIndexedAffine (X : FppfSheaf B S hS)
    (hX : IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS X) : HasCountableWeakPresentation B S hS X
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies condition (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexedAffine_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexedAffine_tfae (X : FppfSheaf B S hS) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS X,
        HasCountableWeakPresentation B S hS X,
        HasWeakIdealChain B S hS X,
        HasNilpotentIdealChain B S hS X,

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.pullback_isAffine_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN3.** Let `X ⟶ Z` and `Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site
of `S` with `Z` a separated formal algebraic space.

1. If `X` and `Y` are affine formal algebraic spaces, then so is `X ×_Z Y`.
2. If `X` and `Y` are McQuillan affine formal algebraic spaces, then so is `X ×_Z Y`.
3. If `X`, `Y` and `Z` are McQuillan affine formal algebraic spaces corresponding to the weakly
  admissible topological rings `A`, `B` and `C` over `S`, then the two morphisms are induced by
  continuous ring maps `C → A` and `C → B` over `S`, and `X ×_Z Y` corresponds to the completed
  tensor product `A ⊗̂_C B`, compatibly with both projections and with the canonical maps of `A`
  and `B` into the completed tensor product.

McQuillanness is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.HasSomeSurjectivePresentation`, the predicate
**Stacks 0AID** names McQuillan in this library. The source's hypothesis that `X` and `Y` are
formal algebraic spaces is not needed: in each clause they are affine formal algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullback_isAffine_hasSomeSurjectivePresentation_completedTensorProduct
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf 𝔅 S hS} (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hZ : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace 𝔅 S hS Z) (hZsep : IsSeparated 𝔅 S hS Z) :
    (IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace 𝔅 S hS X → IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace 𝔅 S hS Y →
        IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace 𝔅 S hS (pullback f g)) ∧
      (HasSomeSurjectivePresentation 𝔅 S hS X → HasSomeSurjectivePresentation 𝔅 S hS Y →
        HasSomeSurjectivePresentation 𝔅 S hS (pullback f g)) ∧
      (HasSomeSurjectivePresentation 𝔅 S hS X → HasSomeSurjectivePresentation 𝔅 S hS Y →
        HasSomeSurjectivePresentation 𝔅 S hS Z →
        ∀ {A B C : Type u}
          [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
          [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B] [IsLinearTopology B B]
          [CommRing C] [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C] [IsLinearTopology C C]
          (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
          (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
          (hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
          (DA : QuotientSystem 𝔅 S hS A) (DB : QuotientSystem 𝔅 S hS B)
          (DC : QuotientSystem 𝔅 S hS C)
          (eX : X ≅ formalSpectrum DA) (eY : Y ≅ formalSpectrum DB)
          (eZ : Z ≅ formalSpectrum DC),
          ∃ (cToA : ContinuousHom DC DA) (cToB : ContinuousHom DC DB),
            formalSpectrumMap hC cToA = eX.inv ≫ f ≫ eZ.hom ∧
            formalSpectrumMap hC cToB = eY.inv ≫ g ≫ eZ.hom ∧
            letI : Algebra C A := cToA.toRingHom.toAlgebra
            letI : Algebra C B := cToB.toRingHom.toAlgebra
            letI : TopologicalSpace (A ⊗[C] B) :=
              TopologicalRing.tensorProductTopology (R := C) (M := A) (N := B)
            letI : UniformSpace (A ⊗[C] B) :=
              TopologicalRing.tensorProductUniformSpace (R := C) (M := A) (N := B)
            ∃ (DT : QuotientSystem 𝔅 S hS
                (TopologicalRing.CompletedTensorProduct (R := C) (M := A) (N := B)))
              (aToT : ContinuousHom DA DT) (bToT : ContinuousHom DB DT)
              (e : pullback f g ≅ formalSpectrum DT),
              TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible
                  (TopologicalRing.CompletedTensorProduct (R := C) (M := A) (N := B)) ∧
                aToT.toRingHom = (UniformSpace.Completion.coeRingHom).comp
                    (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom : A →+* A ⊗[C] B) ∧
                bToT.toRingHom = (UniformSpace.Completion.coeRingHom).comp
                    ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : B →ₐ[C] A ⊗[C] B).toRingHom) ∧
                e.hom ≫ formalSpectrumMap hA aToT = pullback.fst f g ≫ eX.hom ∧
                e.hom ≫ formalSpectrumMap hB bToT = pullback.snd f g ≫ eY.hom)
declarations.comment: all three clauses: over a separated formal algebraic space, the fibre product of affine formal algebraic spaces is affine, that of McQuillan ones is McQuillan, and over a McQuillan base it corresponds to the completed tensor product of the three weakly admissible topological rings, compatibly with both projections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentable_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN4.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of formal algebraic spaces over `S` the
following are equivalent:
1. `f` is representable by algebraic spaces;
2. there is a commutative square `U ⟶ V` over `f` with `U`, `V` formal algebraic spaces,
   vertical arrows representable by algebraic spaces, `U ⟶ X` surjective étale and `U ⟶ V`
   representable by algebraic spaces;
3. every commutative square `U ⟶ V` over `f` with `U`, `V` formal algebraic spaces and
   vertical arrows representable by algebraic spaces has `U ⟶ V` representable by algebraic
   spaces;
4. there is a covering `{Yⱼ ⟶ Y}` as in Definition 0AIM and for each `j` a covering
   `{Xⱼᵢ ⟶ Yⱼ ×_Y X}` as in Definition 0AIM with every `Xⱼᵢ ⟶ Yⱼ` representable by algebraic
   spaces;
5. there is a covering `{Xᵢ ⟶ X}` as in Definition 0AIM and for each `i` a factorization
   `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ ⟶ Y` with `Yᵢ` an affine formal algebraic space, `Yᵢ ⟶ Y` and `Xᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ`
   representable by algebraic spaces.

The source's sixth item, *add more here*, is a placeholder and not a condition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_tfae {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE [Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom,
      IsRepresentableOnSomeSquare B S hS f,
      IsRepresentableOnEverySquare B S hS f,
      IsRepresentableAfterTargetCover B S hS f,
      IsRepresentableOnFactoredAtlas B S hS f]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) to (5); the sixth item of the source, add more here, is a placeholder

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalSpectrumMap_tfae_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AN5.** Let `S` be a scheme and `φ : A ⟶ C` a continuous homomorphism of weakly
admissible topological rings over `S`, the formal spectrum `Spf C` being an affine formal
algebraic space as in Definition 0AIF. The following are equivalent:

1. `Spf φ : Spf C ⟶ Spf A` is representable by algebraic spaces;
2. `Spf φ` is representable (by objects of the site);
3. `φ` is taut.

*The hypothesis `hE`.* Definition 0AIF of the source defines `Spf(B)` to be "the affine formal
algebraic space `colim Spec(B/I)`", and an affine formal algebraic space satisfies, by
Definition 0AI7, the set-theoretic condition of Remark 0AIS; the source's proof of (1) ⟺ (2)
is Lemma 0AKN, a statement about morphisms of affine formal algebraic spaces. In this library
`formalSpectrum E` is the colimit alone, and `hE` records that it is an affine formal algebraic
space in the sense of Definition 0AI7 (`AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace`). This
is the source's own notion of `Spf(B)`, not an extra condition: for weakly admissible `C` it is
equivalent to the coproduct of the stages lying in the site
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSpectrum_iff_hasLargeSite`),
the proviso of Remark 0AIE. Nothing is asked of `Spf A`, of the cutoff of the site, or of the
stages of either ring.

*Why it cannot be dropped.* Over a site whose cutoff is singular there are taut homomorphisms
with `Spf φ` not representable
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_isTaut_not_relativelyRepresentable_of_cof_lt`), and the
formal spectrum of the target of such a homomorphism is not an affine formal algebraic space
(`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_not_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace_formalSpectrum_of_cof_lt`).

*Proof.* (1) ⟹ (3) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isTaut_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_formalSpectrumMap` and
(2) ⟹ (1) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_formalSpectrumMap`, both
with no set-theoretic input. (3) ⟹ (2) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.relative_isAffineHom_formalSpectrumMap_of_isTaut`: a point of
`Spf A` out of an affine object factors through a stage `Spec(A/I)` (Stacks 0AIA), over which the
base change is `Spec(C/J(I))` with `J(I)` the closure of `φ(I)C`, open by tautness; the charts
over the affine opens of an arbitrary test object glue inside the site because each stage of
`Spf C` is bounded by the coproduct of all of them, an object of the site by `hE`.
declarations.statement:
theorem formalSpectrumMap_tfae_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (E : QuotientSystem B S hS C)
    (hE : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (formalSpectrum E)) (f : ContinuousHom D E) :
    List.TFAE
      [Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA f).hom,
        (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).relativelyRepresentable
          (formalSpectrumMap hA f),
        RingHom.IsTaut f.toRingHom]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1), (2) and (3), with Spf(B) an affine formal algebraic space as in Definition 0AIF
