`A → (A/K)^∧` is a closed immersion of formal algebraic spaces over `S`, in the sense of
Stacks 0ANP.

The stage inclusions `Spec (A/I) ⟶ Spf A` are jointly surjective with each base change of it
along them the closed immersion `Spec (A/(K + I)) ⟶ Spec (A/I)`; the descent step of
Stacks 0GHY concludes, representability by algebraic spaces being part of what that step
returns rather than a hypothesis of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_formalSpectrumMap_quotientCompletion :
    AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsClosedImmersion B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA φ)
declarations.comment: closed immersion

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.ker_canonicalMap_eq
declarations.doc:
The kernel of the canonical map to the completion of a quotient by a closed ideal
is that ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ker_canonicalMap_eq {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (K : Ideal A)
    (hK : IsClosed (K : Set A)) :
    RingHom.ker
      (TopologicalRing.CompletionOver.canonicalMap (Ideal.Quotient.mk K)) = K
declarations.comment: kernel

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.exists_not_surjective_canonicalMap
declarations.doc:
For some weakly admissible ring and closed ideal, the map to the completed quotient
is not surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_surjective_canonicalMap :
    ∃ D : TopologicalRing.ClosedIdealQuotientCompletionSituation.{u},
      ¬ Function.Surjective D.canonicalMap
declarations.comment: nonsurjectivity

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A ring homomorphism `φ : A →+* B` is *topologically of finite type* if there is an
`A`-algebra map from a polynomial algebra in finitely many variables to `B` with dense image.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [TopologicalSpace B] (φ : A →+* B) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFiniteType_formalSpectrumMap_iff_isTaut_and_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ANT, the equivalence**, with both conditions read verbatim. Let `φ : A ⟶ C` be a
continuous homomorphism of weakly admissible topological rings over `S`. Then `Spf (φ)` is of
finite type — Definition 0AM4, part (2) — exactly when `φ` is taut and topologically of finite
type.

The forward implication is
`isTaut_and_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_of_isFiniteType_formalSpectrumMap'` and uses only the
locally-of-finite-type half of condition (1). The backward implication
passes through condition (a) of Stacks 0ANU by
`TopologicalRing.finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal_of_topologicallyOfFiniteType` and then
produces condition (2) of Stacks 0AJJ, reaching Definition 0AM4, part (2), through
Stacks 0AJJ, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFiniteType_iff_isBootstrapFiniteType`, which is
unconditional.

Condition (2) and condition (a) of Stacks 0ANU are interchangeable here with no countability
assumption, in both directions: condition (a) implies condition (2) by
`TopologicalRing.isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_of_finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal`, for which
weak pre-admissibility of the source suffices, and condition (2) implies condition (a) by
`TopologicalRing.finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal_of_topologicallyOfFiniteType`. Condition (2)
*is* condition (c) of Stacks 0ANU, so this identification is the half of that lemma which
needs no countability; what the countable generation in the hypothesis of Stacks 0ANU —
a morphism of `WAdm^count` — is spent on in `TopologicalRing.finiteType_tfae` are its
conditions (b), the cofinal form of condition (a), and (d), the restricted power series
presentation, and neither appears here. Both of those uses are of the source's filter, so
`TopologicalRing.finiteType_tfae` assumes countable generation of that filter only.

Nothing beyond the source's hypotheses is assumed. The forward implication needs the
implication (1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 0AN5, which carries no side condition because the library's
Stacks 0AKN consumes of a formal spectrum only its presentation by affine thickenings,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasThickeningPresentation_formalSpectrum`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteType_formalSpectrumMap_iff_isTaut_and_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (E : QuotientSystem B S hS C) (f : ContinuousHom D E) :
    IsFiniteType' B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA f) ↔
      RingHom.IsTaut f.toRingHom ∧
        TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType f.toRingHom
declarations.comment: the equivalence, with condition (1) read as Definition 0AM4, part (2), verbatim — locally of finite type and quasi-compact — and condition (2) read verbatim as tautness together with being topologically of finite type, Definition 0ANS. Both directions are proved and tautness is deduced from condition (1), by the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 0AN5. No countability assumption and no hypothesis beyond the source's is made.

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.finiteType_tfae'
declarations.doc:
The four finite-type conditions for a morphism of countably indexed weakly admissible rings
are equivalent.

Stacks 0ANU states this for an arrow of `WAdm^count`, both rings weakly admissible with a
countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero. Countable generation is assumed here
of the source only, which is strictly weaker and so covers every arrow of `WAdm^count`. The
hypothesis is spent twice and both times on the source: on condition (b), the cofinal form, by
`finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal_to_cofinal`, and on condition (d), the restricted power series
presentation, by `restrictedPowerSeriesPresentation_of_taut_dense`. Condition (c) costs no
countability at all — it is condition (2) of Stacks 0ANT verbatim, and
`isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_of_finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal` gets it from condition (a) for
any weakly pre-admissible source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteType_tfae' (φ : B →+* A)
    (hB : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible B)
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hBcount : (nhds (0 : B)).IsCountablyGenerated) :
    List.TFAE [
      FiniteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal φ,
      FiniteTypeModuloCofinalWeakIdeals φ,
      RingHom.IsTaut φ ∧ TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType φ,
      HasRestrictedPowerSeriesPresentation φ]
declarations.comment: equivalent_conditions

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.topologicallyFiniteType_localizationPreserves
declarations.doc:
Tautness together with topological finite type ascends along a completed étale localization
diagram of countably indexed weakly admissible rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem topologicallyFiniteType_localizationPreserves :
    LocalizationPreserves.{u} IsCountablyWeaklyAdmissible
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
        (f : B →+* A) ↦ RingHom.IsTaut f ∧ IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType f)
declarations.comment: local_property

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.topologicallyFiniteType_faithfullyFlatDescent
declarations.doc:
Tautness together with topological finite type descends along a completed étale localization
diagram whose upper horizontal ring map is faithfully flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem topologicallyFiniteType_faithfullyFlatDescent :
    FaithfullyFlatDescent.{u} IsCountablyWeaklyAdmissible
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
        (f : B →+* A) ↦ RingHom.IsTaut f ∧ IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType f)
declarations.comment: local_property

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.topologicallyFiniteType_finiteProductPreserves
declarations.doc:
Tautness together with topological finite type is preserved by finite products of
targets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem topologicallyFiniteType_finiteProductPreserves :
    FiniteProductPreserves.{u} IsCountablyWeaklyAdmissible
      (fun {B A : Type u} [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
        [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
        (f : B →+* A) ↦ RingHom.IsTaut f ∧ IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType f)
declarations.comment: local_property

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.topologicallyFiniteType_propertyIsLocal
declarations.doc:
Tautness together with topological finite type is a local property of morphisms of
countably indexed weakly admissible topological rings.
declarations.comment: local_property

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.topologicallyFiniteType_isomorphismInvariant
declarations.doc:
Tautness together with topological finite type is independent of the presentations of the
source and the target.
declarations.comment: local_property

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.topologicallyFiniteType_propertyIsLocal'
declarations.doc:
Tautness together with topological finite type is a local property of morphisms of countably
indexed weakly admissible topological rings.
declarations.comment: local_property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyOfFiniteType_tfae_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ANV.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces over `S`
with `Y` countably indexed. Then `f` being locally of finite type, `f` being of finite type in
the sense of Definition 0AM4, part (2), and `f` corresponding to a morphism `B → A` of
`WAdm^{count}` satisfying the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0ANU — taken in the two forms
(a), of finite type modulo every weak ideal of definition, and (c), taut and topologically of
finite type — are all equivalent.

As in the source, the source `X` is not assumed countably indexed. If `f` is locally of finite
type it is representable by algebraic spaces, hence affine by **Stacks 0AKN**, and `X` is then
countably indexed by **Stacks 0AKP**; the two steps together are clause (1) of Stacks 0AKQ,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_of_isRepresentable'`. Both spaces are then
formal spectra of rings of `WAdm^{count}` by **Stacks 0AN1**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_quotientSystem_of_isCountablyIndexed`, and `f` is the
formal spectrum map of a continuous homomorphism by **Stacks 0AN0**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.existsUnique_continuousHom_formalSpectrumMap_eq`. The equivalence
for that homomorphism is **Stacks 0ANT** together with Stacks 0ANU, in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalSpectrumMap_finiteType_tfae_countablyWeaklyAdmissible`.
Being locally of finite type upgrades to being of finite type by Stacks 0AKN,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsLocallyOfFiniteType.isFiniteType_of_isAffineFormal`, and
Stacks 0AJJ.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_tfae_of_isAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hYc : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f,
        IsFiniteType' B S hS f,
        CorrespondsToCountablyWeaklyAdmissibleMap B S hS
          (fun φ ↦ TopologicalRing.FiniteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal φ) f,
        CorrespondsToCountablyWeaklyAdmissibleMap B S hS
          TopologicalRing.IsTautTopologicallyOfFiniteTypeHom f]
declarations.comment: the equivalence at the source's hypotheses: `f` an arbitrary morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces with countably indexed target. Countable indexing of the source is derived from condition (1) by Stacks 0AKN and Stacks 0AKP, the presentations as formal spectra by Stacks 0AN1 and the presenting homomorphism by Stacks 0AN0. Condition (3) is the existence of such presentations of `X` and `Y` by rings of `WAdm^count` and of a continuous homomorphism with formal spectrum map `f` satisfying the conditions of Stacks 0ANU, in the forms (a) and (c)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.chartPropertyIsLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
A map of countably indexed affine formal algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of finite
type exactly when every morphism of `WAdm^{count}` presenting it is taut and topologically of
finite type.

A countably indexed affine formal algebraic space is the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible
topological ring with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero — item (6) of
Stacks 0AIK — and a map of formal spectra comes from a unique continuous homomorphism by Stacks
0AN0, so the chart condition is never vacuous here and both directions are the corresponding
implications of Stacks 0ANV for that homomorphism. The implication out of being locally of
finite type is Stacks 0AN5 (1) ⟹ (3) for tautness together with the implication (1) ⟹ (2) of
Stacks 0ANT, the two being combined in
`isTaut_and_isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_of_isFiniteType_formalSpectrumMap` once Stacks 0AKN has
upgraded locally of finite type to of finite type; the implication back is the implication
(2) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0ANT, `isFiniteType_formalSpectrumMap_of_isTaut`. Being locally of finite
type is carried across the two comparison isomorphisms by Stacks 0AQ4, an isomorphism being
representable étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem chartPropertyIsLocallyOfFiniteType :
    ChartPropertyIsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS
declarations.comment: the equivalence, read on countably indexed affine charts rather than on formal spectra: a map of countably indexed affine formal algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of finite type exactly when every morphism of `WAdm^{count}` presenting it is taut and topologically of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.formalSpectrumMap_finiteType_tfae_countablyWeaklyAdmissible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ANV.** Let `φ : A ⟶ C` be a continuous homomorphism of weakly admissible
topological rings over `S` and assume the neighbourhood filter of zero of `A` — the target
`Spf A` — countably generated. Then `Spf (φ) : Spf C → Spf A` being locally of finite type,
`Spf (φ)` being of finite type in the sense of Definition 0AM4, part (2), `φ` being a
morphism of `WAdm^{count}` of finite type modulo every weak ideal of definition, and `φ`
being a morphism of `WAdm^{count}` which is taut and topologically of finite type are all
equivalent.

Only the target is assumed countably indexed, as in the source. That the source `Spf C` is
countably indexed is part of what condition (3) asserts — membership of `φ` in
`WAdm^{count}` — and so is a conclusion of conditions (1) and (2), not a hypothesis; the
target's own membership is the standing hypothesis `hAcount` together with `hA`. The step
that produces it is Stacks 0GX6,
`RingHom.isCountablyGenerated_nhds_zero_of_isTaut`: a taut continuous homomorphism carries a
countable fundamental system of open ideals from source ring to target ring, and every one of
the four conditions supplies tautness. This replaces the appeal to Stacks 0AKN and Stacks
0AKP that the source makes, and like them it needs no affineness of the two formal spectra.

The last two conditions are conditions (a) and (c) of Stacks 0ANU, each conjoined with
membership in `WAdm^{count}`. They are identified here without any countability assumption,
by `TopologicalRing.isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_of_finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal` — for
which weak pre-admissibility of `A` suffices — and
`TopologicalRing.finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal_of_topologicallyOfFiniteType`, so Stacks
0ANU's own countability hypotheses are not needed. With `hAcount` and the `WAdm^{count}`
conjunct in hand, Stacks 0ANU identifies these two with its remaining conditions (b) and (d)
as well, which is why reading condition (3) off either form is faithful.

The implication from locally of finite type to condition (a) splits into tautness, which is
the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 0AN5, and finite type of the stage quotient maps, which
is the ring-theoretic half of Stacks 0ANT; the implication from condition (a) back is the
implication (2) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0ANT, and being locally of finite type is the first half of
the conjunction that being of finite type is.

The quasi-compactness of Definition 0AJC that the second condition contains is not
established directly anywhere in the cycle: the implication (2) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0ANT
produces condition (2) of Stacks 0AJJ,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsBootstrapFiniteType`, whose quasi-compactness assertion is
the Bootstrap one, and Stacks 0AJJ identifies that condition with Definition 0AM4, part (2),
unconditionally; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFiniteType_iff_isBootstrapFiniteType`.

Nothing beyond the source's hypotheses is assumed. The tautness step is the implication
(1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 0AN5,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isTaut_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_formalSpectrumMap`,
which carries no side condition of its own.
declarations.statement:
theorem formalSpectrumMap_finiteType_tfae_countablyWeaklyAdmissible {A C : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing C]
    [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C] [IsLinearTopology C C]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A) (hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
    (hAcount : (nhds (0 : A)).IsCountablyGenerated)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (E : QuotientSystem B S hS C) (g : ContinuousHom D E) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA g),
        IsFiniteType' B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA g),
        TopologicalRing.IsCountablyWeaklyAdmissible C ∧
          TopologicalRing.FiniteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal g.toRingHom,
        TopologicalRing.IsCountablyWeaklyAdmissible C ∧
          RingHom.IsTaut g.toRingHom ∧
            TopologicalRing.IsTopologicallyOfFiniteType g.toRingHom]
declarations.comment: the equivalence, under the source's hypotheses exactly: only the target `Spf A` is assumed countably indexed, by `hAcount`. Condition (3) is taken in the two forms (a) and (c) of Stacks 0ANU, each conjoined with membership of the source ring in `WAdm^count`, which is what `f corresponds to a morphism of WAdm^count` still asserts once the target ring's membership is the standing hypothesis. That membership is a conclusion of conditions (1) and (2) rather than an assumption: every one of the four conditions supplies tautness, and a taut continuous homomorphism carries a countable fundamental system of open ideals from source ring to target ring by Stacks 0GX6, `RingHom.isCountablyGenerated_nhds_zero_of_isTaut` — which replaces the source's appeal to Stacks 0AKN and Stacks 0AKP and, like the library's Stacks 0AKN, needs no affineness of the two formal spectra. The finite type condition is Definition 0AM4, part (2), verbatim; the implication (2) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0ANT concludes it through condition (2) of Stacks 0AJJ — representable by algebraic spaces plus of finite type in the Bootstrap sense of Stacks 03XZ — which Stacks 0AJJ, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFiniteType_iff_isBootstrapFiniteType`, identifies with Definition 0AM4, part (2), unconditionally. The two forms of condition (3) are identified with no countability assumption, by `TopologicalRing.isTopologicallyOfFiniteType_of_finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal` and `TopologicalRing.finiteTypeModuloEveryWeakIdeal_of_topologicallyOfFiniteType`, so Stacks 0ANU's own countability hypotheses are not needed here; the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of Stacks 0AN5 that supplies tautness, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isTaut_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces_formalSpectrumMap`, carries no side condition either

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyOfFiniteType_tfae'
declarations.doc:
For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of locally countably indexed formal algebraic spaces over `S`,
the condition that every affine representable étale square over `f` carry a taut, topologically
of finite type morphism of `WAdm^{count}`, the existence of an affine étale covering of `Y`
together with affine étale coverings of the fibre products of its members with `X` on which
that condition holds, the existence of an affine étale covering of `X` whose members factor
through affine representable étale charts of `Y` by such morphisms, and `f` being locally of
finite type, are all equivalent.

The first three are the three conditions of Stacks 0ANG for the class of countably indexed
weakly admissible topological rings and the property of being taut and topologically of finite
type, which Stacks 0ANU makes a local property of such arrows; the comparison with the fourth is
Stacks 0ANV on charts together with the implications (1) ⟹ (3) and (4) ⟹ (5) ⟹ (1) of Stacks
0ANL.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_tfae' {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyCountablyIndexed B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyCountablyIndexed B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [HasPropertyOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS
          TopologicalRing.IsCountablyWeaklyAdmissible
          TopologicalRing.IsTautTopologicallyOfFiniteTypeHom f,
        HasPropertyAfterTargetCover B S hS
          TopologicalRing.IsCountablyWeaklyAdmissible
          TopologicalRing.IsTautTopologicallyOfFiniteTypeHom f,
        HasPropertyAfterSourceCover B S hS
          TopologicalRing.IsCountablyWeaklyAdmissible
          TopologicalRing.IsTautTopologicallyOfFiniteTypeHom f,
        IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of its four conditions, at the source's own hypotheses. The presented refinement of a covering of the source is the library's `hasEtaleRefinementOfSourceCover_isCountablyWeaklyAdmissible` (Stacks 0AJ2, quasi-compactness of an affine formal algebraic space and Stacks 0AN8) and the implication (2) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0AKX is the library's `isCountablyIndexed_of_isRepresentableEtale_of_isLocallyCountablyIndexed`

declarations.name: isLimit_diffLimitCone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AP0**.
For a spectral space `X`, a monotone family `U` indexed by a nonempty codirected order and
`specGen E = ⋂ i, U i`, the cone `diffLimitCone` with apex `specGen E \ E` is a limit cone of
the diagram `(U i \ E)_i`: the canonical map `specGen E \ E ⟶ lim_i (U i \ E)` is a
homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimit_diffLimitCone [SpectralSpace X] [Nonempty I] [IsCodirectedOrder I]
    {E : Set X}
    (hmono : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄, i ≤ j → U i ⊆ U j)
    (hWeq : specGen E = ⋂ i, U i) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit (diffLimitCone U E hmono (fun i => hWeq ▸ Set.iInter_subset U i)))

declarations.name: isSpectral_specGen_diff_constructible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AP0**.
If `X` is a spectral space and `E ⊆ X` is a constructible subset, then the set
`specGen E \ E` of points specializing into `E` but not lying in `E`, equipped with the
subspace topology, is a spectral space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSpectral_specGen_diff_constructible [SpectralSpace X] {E : Set X}
    (hE : Topology.IsConstructible E) : SpectralSpace ↥(specGen E \ E)

declarations.name: isDiscreteValuationRing_iff_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AP1.** A Noetherian local ring is a discrete valuation ring if and only if its
completion at the maximal ideal is a discrete valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_iff_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] :
    (∃ _ : IsDomain A, IsDiscreteValuationRing A) ↔
      ∃ _ : IsDomain (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A),
        IsDiscreteValuationRing (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)

declarations.name: exists_ringEquiv_pi_isDedekindDomain_and_isDiscreteValuationRing_atPrime_of_etale
declarations.doc:
An étale algebra over a Dedekind domain is a finite product of Dedekind domains, and its
localizations at maximal ideals with nonzero contraction to the base are discrete valuation
rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ringEquiv_pi_isDedekindDomain_and_isDiscreteValuationRing_atPrime_of_etale
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
    [IsDedekindDomain A] :
    (∃ (n : ℕ) (D : Fin n → Type v) (_ : ∀ i, CommRing (D i)),
      (∀ i, IsDedekindDomain (D i)) ∧ Nonempty (B ≃+* ∀ i, D i)) ∧
      ∀ q : MaximalSpectrum B, q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A B) ≠ ⊥ →
        ∃ _ : IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal),
          IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)

declarations.name: isDiscreteValuationRing_iff_henselizations
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian local ring is a discrete valuation ring if and only if its henselization is a
discrete valuation ring, and if and only if its strict henselization is a discrete valuation
ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDiscreteValuationRing_iff_henselizations
    (R Rh Rsh : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh]
    (κsep : Type v) [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    [IsHenselization R κsep Rsh] :
    ((∃ _ : IsDomain R, IsDiscreteValuationRing R) ↔
      ∃ _ : IsDomain Rh, IsDiscreteValuationRing Rh) ∧
      ((∃ _ : IsDomain R, IsDiscreteValuationRing R) ↔
        ∃ _ : IsDomain Rsh, IsDiscreteValuationRing Rsh)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_forall_exists_restrictOpen
declarations.doc:
**Effectivity of a descent datum is local on the scheme it is carried by.** Let
`f : X ⟶ S` be a surjective, quasi-compact, flat morphism of schemes and let `(V, φ)` be a
descent datum relative to `X/S`. If every point of `V` has an invariant open neighbourhood
`W ⊆ V` such that the restricted datum `(W, φ|_{W ×_S X})` is effective, then `(V, φ)` is
effective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_of_forall_exists_restrictOpen {S X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    [Surjective f] [Flat f] [QuasiCompact f] (D : DescentDatum f)
    (h : ∀ v : D.over.left, ∃ (W : D.over.left.Opens) (hW : D.IsTransitionInvariant W),
      v ∈ W ∧ DescentData.IsEffective (D.restrictOpen W hW)) :
    DescentData.IsEffective D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_forall_exists_restrictOpen_le
declarations.doc:
**Effectivity of a descent datum is local on the scheme it is carried by.** Let
`f : X ⟶ S` be a surjective, quasi-compact, flat morphism of schemes and let `(V, φ)` be a
descent datum relative to `X/S`. Suppose that for every `v ∈ V` there is an open subscheme
`v ∈ W ⊆ V` with `φ(W ×_S X) ⊆ X ×_S W` and such that the descent datum
`(W, φ|_{W ×_S X})` is effective. Then `(V, φ)` is effective.

Only the inclusion `φ(W ×_S X) ⊆ X ×_S W` is asked for. The reverse inclusion, which makes
`φ|_{W ×_S X}` an isomorphism onto `X ×_S W` and so the gluing isomorphism of the restricted
datum, follows from the cocycle condition by
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isTransitionInvariant_of_le`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffective_of_forall_exists_restrictOpen_le {S X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S}
    [Surjective f] [Flat f] [QuasiCompact f] (D : DescentDatum f)
    (h : ∀ v : D.over.left, ∃ (W : D.over.left.Opens)
      (hW : D.transitionPullbackIso.hom ''ᵁ (pullback.fst (D.over.hom ≫ f) f ⁻¹ᵁ W) ≤
        pullback.snd f (D.over.hom ≫ f) ⁻¹ᵁ W),
      v ∈ W ∧
        DescentData.IsEffective (D.restrictOpen W (D.isTransitionInvariant_of_le W hW))) :
    DescentData.IsEffective D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsIndQuasiAffine
declarations.doc: A scheme is ind-quasi-affine if each quasi-compact open subscheme is quasi-affine.
declarations.statement: class IsIndQuasiAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsIndQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is ind-quasi-affine if the inverse image of every affine open subscheme
of its target is an ind-quasi-affine scheme.
declarations.statement: class IsIndQuasiAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop
declarations.comment: morphisms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIndQuasiAffineHom_isStableUnderBaseChange
declarations.doc: Ind-quasi-affine morphisms of schemes are stable under arbitrary base change.
declarations.statement:
instance isIndQuasiAffineHom_isStableUnderBaseChange :
    MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange
      (@IsIndQuasiAffineHom : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIndQuasiAffineHom_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc
declarations.doc: Being an ind-quasi-affine morphism of schemes is fpqc local on the base.
declarations.statement:
instance isIndQuasiAffineHom_isLocalAtTarget_fpqc :
    MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtTarget (@IsIndQuasiAffineHom : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
      Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIndQuasiAffineHom_of_isSeparated_of_locallyQuasiFinite
declarations.doc:
A separated morphism of schemes which is locally quasi-finite and locally of finite type is
ind-quasi-affine.
declarations.statement:
instance isIndQuasiAffineHom_of_isSeparated_of_locallyQuasiFinite {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyQuasiFinite f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] :
    IsIndQuasiAffineHom f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.target_image_source_preimage_eq_iInter_compact_open
declarations.doc:
The target-image of the source-preimage of a quasi-compact open in the object scheme of a
flat quasi-compact groupoid is an intersection of a nonempty family of quasi-compact opens.
declarations.statement:
theorem target_image_source_preimage_eq_iInter_compact_open
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme S)
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left] [Flat G.source.left]
    [QuasiCompact G.target.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace G.objects.left]
    (W : G.objects.left.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set G.objects.left)) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Nonempty I) (V : I → Set G.objects.left),
      (∀ i, IsOpen (V i) ∧ IsCompact (V i)) ∧
        G.target.left.base '' (G.source.left.base ⁻¹' (W : Set G.objects.left)) = ⋂ i, V i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_invariant_open_between_compact_opens
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0APB.** A quasi-compact open in the object scheme of a quasi-compact
flat groupoid scheme has an invariant open neighbourhood contained in a quasi-compact open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_invariant_open_between_compact_opens
    (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left] [Flat G.source.left]
    [QuasiCompact G.target.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace G.objects.left]
    (W : G.objects.left.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set G.objects.left)) :
    ∃ (V W' : G.objects.left.Opens),
      IsInvariantOpen G V ∧ IsCompact (W' : Set G.objects.left) ∧
        W ≤ V ∧ V ≤ W'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_isInvariantOpen_isCompact_between
declarations.doc:
Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid scheme with `s` and `t`
quasi-compact and flat and with `U` quasi-separated, and let `W ⊆ U` be a quasi-compact open.
Then there is an invariant open `V` and a quasi-compact open `W'` with `W ⊆ V ⊆ W' ⊆ U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvariantOpen_isCompact_between
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left] [Flat G.source.left]
    [QuasiCompact G.target.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace G.objects.left]
    (W : G.objects.left.Opens) (hW : IsCompact (W : Set G.objects.left)) :
    ∃ V W' : G.objects.left.Opens,
      IsInvariantOpen G V ∧ IsCompact (W' : Set G.objects.left) ∧
        (W : Set G.objects.left) ⊆ (V : Set G.objects.left) ∧
        (V : Set G.objects.left) ⊆ (W' : Set G.objects.left)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsCartesian
declarations.doc: A morphism of groupoid schemes is cartesian if its square of source maps is a pullback.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsCartesian {S : Scheme.{u}} {G H : GroupoidScheme S}
    (F : GroupoidScheme.Hom G H) : Prop
declarations.comment: the cartesian condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CartesianOver
declarations.doc: A groupoid scheme cartesian over a fixed groupoid scheme `H`.
declarations.statement: structure CartesianOver {S : Scheme.{u}} (H : GroupoidScheme S)
declarations.comment: groupoid schemes cartesian over a fixed groupoid scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.CartesianOver.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of groupoid schemes cartesian over `H` is a morphism compatible with both
components of the structure morphisms to `H`.
declarations.statement:
structure CartesianOver.Hom {S : Scheme.{u}} {H : GroupoidScheme S}
    (X Y : CartesianOver H)
declarations.comment: morphisms cartesian over a fixed groupoid scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_cartesianOverEquivariantEquivalenceData
declarations.doc:
There is an equivalence between groupoid schemes cartesian over `G` and equivariant schemes
for `G` satisfying the equations of `CartesianOverEquivariantEquivalenceData` on objects, descent
isomorphisms, and morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_cartesianOverEquivariantEquivalenceData
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    Nonempty (CartesianOverEquivariantEquivalenceData G)
declarations.comment: the equivalence with the forward construction in the proof

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianOverEquivalenceEquivariantScheme
declarations.doc:
Cartesian groupoid schemes over `G` are equivalent to schemes over the
object scheme of `G` endowed with a normalized cocyclic pullback isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cartesianOverEquivalenceEquivariantScheme
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S) :
    CartesianOver G ≌ EquivariantScheme G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianOverEquivDescentDatum
declarations.doc:
Groupoid schemes cartesian over the pair groupoid `(X, X ×_S X, s, t, c)`, as a groupoid
scheme over `S`, are the same thing as descent data relative to `X/S`.
declarations.statement:
def cartesianOverEquivDescentDatum (f : X ⟶ S) :
    CartesianOver (pairGroupoid f) ≌ DescentDatum f
declarations.comment: the equivalence for the base scheme equal to the target of `f`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cartesianOverPairGroupoidEquivDescentDatum
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0APF.**  Let `S` be a scheme and let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes over `S`,
the structure morphism of `Y` being `g : Y ⟶ S`.  Groupoid schemes over `S` cartesian over the
pair groupoid `(X, X ×_Y X, \mathrm{pr}_1, \mathrm{pr}_0, \mathrm{pr}_{02})` are the same thing
as descent data relative to `X/Y`.
declarations.statement:
def cartesianOverPairGroupoidEquivDescentDatum {S Y X : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ S) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    CartesianOver ((pairGroupoid f).pushforward g) ≌ DescentDatum f
declarations.comment: the equivalence for a morphism of schemes over a base `S`, the general case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.colimit_sections_equiv_sections_iInter
declarations.doc:
Sections on the intersection of a nonempty directed family of
quasi-compact opens of a quasi-separated scheme are the filtered colimit of
the sections on those opens.  The equivalence commutes with every canonical
map from a stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem colimit_sections_equiv_sections_iInter
    {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} {I : Type u}
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [Nonempty I]
    (F : X.toTopCat.Sheaf (Type u)) (U : I → Opens X)
    (hqc : ∀ i, IsCompact (U i : Set X))
    (hdir : ∀ i j, ∃ k, (U k : Set X) ⊆ U i ∩ U j) (E : Set X)
    (hE : E = ⋂ i, (U i : Set X)) :
    ∃ e : colimit (sectionsDiagram F U) ≃ sectionsOnSubset E F,
      ∀ (i : intersectionIndex U) (s : (sectionsDiagram F U).obj i),
        e (colimit.ι (sectionsDiagram F U) i s) =
          stageToSubset F U E
            (fun j ↦ by rw [hE]; exact Set.iInter_subset _ j) i s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_iInter_iso_iInter_in_specΓ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0API.** The canonical map from a nonempty intersection
of quasi-compact opens in an ind-quasi-affine scheme to the spectrum of its ring
of sections identifies it, as a locally ringed space, with an intersection of
quasi-compact opens in that spectrum.  Each comparison map to the spectrum of a
stage is the spectrum of the restriction map of functions from that stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iInter_iso_iInter_in_specΓ
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIndQuasiAffine X]
    {I : Type v} [Nonempty I] (U : I → X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ i, IsCompact (U i : Set X)) :
    let E : Set X := ⋂ i, (U i : Set X)
    let Z := subsetLocallyRingedSpace X.toLocallyRingedSpace E
    let Y := Spec.toLocallyRingedSpace.obj (op (LocallyRingedSpace.Γ.obj (op Z)))
    ∃ (p : ∀ i, Y ⟶ Spec.toLocallyRingedSpace.obj (op Γ(X, U i)))
      (V : I → Opens Y),
      (∀ i, IsCompact (V i : Set Y)) ∧
      (∀ i, (V i : Set Y) = (p i).base ⁻¹' Set.range (U i).toSpecΓ.base) ∧
      (∀ i (x : E), (p i).base (Z.toΓSpec.base x) =
        (U i).toSpecΓ.base ⟨x.1, Set.mem_iInter.mp x.2 i⟩) ∧
      (∀ i (W : Set X), IsOpen W → W ⊆ E →
        (p i).base ⁻¹' ((U i).toSpecΓ.base ''
          {x : U i | (x : X) ∈ W}) =
        Z.toΓSpec.base '' {x : E | (x : X) ∈ W}) ∧
      (∀ i, p i = (Scheme.Spec.map (X.openToSubset (U i) E
        (Set.iInter_subset (fun k ↦ (U k : Set X)) i)).op).toLRSHom) ∧
      ∃ e : Z ≅ subsetLocallyRingedSpace Y (⋂ i, (V i : Set Y)),
          e.hom.toHom ≫ ofSubset Y (⋂ i, (V i : Set Y)) =
            (identityToΓSpec.app Z).toHom
declarations.comment: intersection_embedding

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpen_image_toΓSpec_of_isOpen
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0API (open image).** The canonical map from an intersection of a
nonempty family of quasi-compact opens in an ind-quasi-affine scheme to the spectrum of its
global sections sends subsets which are open in the ambient scheme to open subsets.
declarations.statement:
theorem isOpen_image_toΓSpec_of_isOpen
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsIndQuasiAffine X]
    {I : Type v} [Nonempty I] (U : I → X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ i, IsCompact (U i : Set X))
    (E W : Set X) (hE : E = ⋂ i, (U i : Set X))
    (hWE : W ⊆ E) (hW : IsOpen W) :
    IsOpen
      ((subsetLocallyRingedSpace
          X.toLocallyRingedSpace E).toΓSpec.base ''
        { x : E | (x : X) ∈ W })
declarations.comment: open_image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sectionsRingOnSubset_preimage_iInter_iso_pushout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0APJ.** In a cartesian square of schemes over the affine schemes
`Spec B ⟶ Spec A`, where `A ⟶ B` is flat, formation of sections over a nonempty intersection of
quasi-compact opens commutes with base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem sectionsRingOnSubset_preimage_iInter_iso_pushout
    {A B : CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : A ⟶ B) {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : X ⟶ Scheme.Spec.obj (op B)) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (h : Y ⟶ Scheme.Spec.obj (op A))
    (H : IsPullback g f (Scheme.Spec.map φ.op) h)
    {ι : Type v} [Nonempty ι] (V : ι → Y.Opens)
    (hV : ∀ i, IsCompact (V i : Set Y)) [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    (hφ : φ.hom.Flat) :
    ∃ e : pushout (toSectionsOnSubset h (⋂ i, (V i : Set Y))) φ ≅
        X.sectionsRingOnSubset (f ⁻¹' (⋂ i, (V i : Set Y))),
      (pushout.inr _ _ ≫ e.hom =
        toSectionsOnSubset g (f ⁻¹' (⋂ i, (V i : Set Y)))) ∧
      (∀ (U : Y.Opens) (hU : (⋂ i, (V i : Set Y)) ⊆ U),
        Y.restrictOpenToSubset (⋂ i, (V i : Set Y)) U hU ≫
            pushout.inl _ _ ≫ e.hom =
          f.appLE U (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl ≫
            X.restrictOpenToSubset (f ⁻¹' (⋂ i, (V i : Set Y))) (f ⁻¹ᵁ U) (by
              intro x hx
              exact Set.mem_preimage.mpr (hU (Set.mem_preimage.mp hx))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPushout_sectionsRingOnSubset_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let
```
  X ---k---→ Spec R
  |            |
  p            g
  ↓            ↓
  Y ---πY--→ Spec A
```
be a Cartesian diagram of schemes, let `E ⊆ Y` be an intersection of a nonempty family of
quasi-compact opens of `Y`, and suppose that `Y` is quasi-separated and that `g` is flat. Then
```
Γ(p⁻¹E, 𝒪_X|_{p⁻¹E}) = Γ(E, 𝒪_Y|_E) ⊗_{Γ(Spec A, ⊤)} Γ(Spec R, ⊤) :
```
the square formed by the restrictions of the global functions of `Spec A` and of `Spec R` to `E`
and to `p⁻¹E` is a pushout of rings.

The comparison morphism `Γ(E, 𝒪_Y|_E) ⟶ Γ(p⁻¹E, 𝒪_X|_{p⁻¹E})` is produced by the statement and
characterized by the second conjunct: it agrees with the restriction along `p` on each member of
the given family.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPushout_sectionsRingOnSubset_of_flat {A R : CommRingCat.{u}} {Y X : Scheme.{u}}
    {πY : Y ⟶ Spec A} {g : Spec R ⟶ Spec A} {p : X ⟶ Y} {k : X ⟶ Spec R}
    (H : IsPullback p k πY g) [Flat g] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y] {I : Type u} [Nonempty I]
    (V : I → Y.Opens) (hV : ∀ i, IsCompact (V i : Set Y))
    (E : Set Y) (hE : E = ⋂ i, (V i : Set Y)) :
    ∃ w : Y.sectionsRingOnSubset E ⟶ X.sectionsRingOnSubset (p.base ⁻¹' E),
      IsPushout (πY.appTop ≫ Y.topToSubset E) g.appTop w
          (k.appTop ≫ X.topToSubset (p.base ⁻¹' E)) ∧
        ∀ i : I,
          Y.stageToSubset V E (fun j ↦ hE ▸ Set.iInter_subset _ j) ⟨i⟩ ≫ w =
            p.appLE (V i) (p ⁻¹ᵁ V i) le_rfl ≫
              X.stageToSubset (fun j ↦ p ⁻¹ᵁ V j) (p.base ⁻¹' E)
                (fun j ↦ hE ▸ Set.preimage_mono (Set.iInter_subset _ j)) ⟨i⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isIndQuasiAffineHom_of_anyIndex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0APK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0APK), Gabber's theorem.** Let `S`
be a scheme, let `{X i ⟶ S}` be an fpqc covering family, indexed by a type in an arbitrary
universe, and let `D` be a descent datum relative to it each of whose component morphisms
`V i ⟶ X i` is ind-quasi-affine. Then `D` is effective: it is isomorphic to the canonical descent
datum of a scheme over `S`.

Ind-quasi-affineness is stable under base change, Stacks 0AP7, and closed under finite disjoint
unions, so the general-base fpqc reduction of Stacks 02W3,
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_fpqc_of_affineSingleton_of_anyIndex`, reduces
the statement to the case of a surjective flat morphism of affine schemes, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_isIndQuasiAffineHom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isIndQuasiAffineHom_of_anyIndex {ι : Type v} {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {X : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S)
    (D : DescentData f) (hP : ∀ i, IsIndQuasiAffineHom (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isIndQuasiAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0APK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0APK) over an affine base.** Let `S`
be an affine scheme, let `{X i ⟶ S}` be an fpqc covering family and let `D` be a descent datum
relative to it each of whose component morphisms is ind-quasi-affine. Then `D` is effective: it is
isomorphic to the canonical descent datum of a scheme over `S`.

This is the special case of
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentData.isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isIndQuasiAffineHom_of_anyIndex` kept
for the consumers taking this shape.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFamilyEffective_of_forall_isIndQuasiAffineHom {ι : Type u} {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
    {X : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ S)
    (hf : Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage S)
    (D : DescentData f) (hP : ∀ i, IsIndQuasiAffineHom (D.obj i).hom) :
    D.IsFamilyEffective
declarations.comment: the case of an affine base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentDatum.isEffective_of_isIndQuasiAffineHom_of_quasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Gabber's effectivity for ind-quasi-affine descent data along a single quasi-compact fpqc
covering.** A descent datum relative to a surjective, flat, quasi-compact morphism `f : X ⟶ S`
whose structure morphism `V ⟶ X` is ind-quasi-affine is effective.

This is [Stacks, Tag 0APK](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0APK) for a one-member covering,
over an arbitrary base.
declarations.comment: the case of a one-member covering by a surjective flat quasi-compact morphism, over an arbitrary base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace.isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**An algebraic space is a sheaf for the fpqc topology**, which is
[Stacks, Tag 0APL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0APL).
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_fpqc (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf
      ((Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.comap (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).toGrothendieck) F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.LiftsAt.mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APN, (2) implies (3).** The lifting property at a point against a class of
extensions implies the lifting property against any subclass.
declarations.comment: condition (2) implies condition (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothAt_of_liftsAt_isSmallExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APN, (3) implies (1).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally
of finite type, whose target is locally Noetherian, and which has the lifting property at a
point of its source against small extensions, is smooth at that point.

A pointed étale chart at the point with locally Noetherian target chart receives every lifting
problem for its morphism of charts along a residually trivial small extension, so Stacks 02HX
makes that morphism of charts smooth at the chart point; smoothness at a point being an
étale-local property of germs, Stacks 04NC reads that back as smoothness of the morphism at the
point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothAt_of_liftsAt_isSmallExtension
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Z))
    (hFiniteType : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hlift : LiftsAt B S hS f x fun ⦃_ _⦄ φ => InfinitesimalLifting.IsSmallExtension φ) :
    IsSmoothAt B S hS f x
declarations.comment: condition (3) implies condition (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSmoothAt.liftsAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APN, (1) implies (2) and (3).** A morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
smooth at a point of its source has the lifting property at that point against every class of
square-zero surjections of local rings.

Smoothness at the point gives an open subspace of the source containing it on which the
morphism is smooth, hence formally smooth by Stacks 04AM
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.formallySmooth_of_isSmooth'`); the spectrum of a local ring whose
closed point lies over the given point factors through that open subspace, because the closed
point specializes from every point, so the lifting problem is a lifting problem for the
restricted morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsSmoothAt.liftsAt
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) {f : X ⟶ Y} {x : points B S hS X}
    (hsm : IsSmoothAt B S hS f x)
    (extension : ∀ ⦃R' R : CommRingCat.{u}⦄, (R' ⟶ R) → Prop)
    (hextension : ∀ ⦃R' R : CommRingCat.{u}⦄ (φ : R' ⟶ R),
      extension φ → InfinitesimalLifting.IsSquareZeroSurjection φ) :
    LiftsAt B S hS f x extension
declarations.comment: condition (1) implies conditions (2) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tfae_isSmoothAt_liftsAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APN.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite type, with `Y` locally Noetherian, and let `x` be a point of `X`. Then the
following are equivalent: `f` is smooth at `x`; every lifting problem at `x` along a surjection
of local rings with square-zero kernel has a solution; every lifting problem at `x` along a
small extension has a solution.

The implication from (1) to (2) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSmoothAt.liftsAt`, from (2) to
(3) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.LiftsAt.mono` and from (3) to (1) is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothAt_of_liftsAt_isSmallExtension`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isSmoothAt_liftsAt
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : points B S hS X)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Z))
    (hFiniteType : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    [IsSmoothAt B S hS f x,
      LiftsAt B S hS f x fun ⦃_ _⦄ φ => InfinitesimalLifting.IsSquareZeroSurjection φ,
      LiftsAt B S hS f x fun ⦃_ _⦄ φ =>
        InfinitesimalLifting.IsSmallExtension φ].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isSmooth_iff_liftsAgainstFiniteTypeSmallExtensions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APP, as stated, is false.** The equivalence of smoothness with condition (2) of
Stacks 0APP, in which the test morphism `Spec B' ⟶ Y` is required to be of finite type, fails for
some morphism of algebraic spaces locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian target: the
point `Spec ℚ ⟶ 𝔸¹_ℚ/ℤ` of `exists_not_isSmooth_liftsAgainstFiniteTypeSmallExtensions` satisfies
condition (2) and is not smooth.

The implication from smoothness does hold, and is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSmooth.liftsAgainstFiniteTypeSmallExtensions`; the corrected
equivalence, with the test morphism required only to be locally of finite type, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmooth_iff_forall_exists_lift_isSmallExtension`.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_isSmooth_iff_liftsAgainstFiniteTypeSmallExtensions :
    ¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
      (X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X →
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y → ∀ f : X ⟶ Y,
      HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Z) →
      IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f →
      (IsSmooth B S hS f ↔ LiftsAgainstFiniteTypeSmallExtensions B S hS f)
declarations.comment:
the statement with the test morphism Spec B' ⟶ Y of finite type is false: the
point Spec ℚ ⟶ 𝔸¹_ℚ/ℤ of the zero section satisfies that condition (2) and is not smooth. The
corrected form, with Spec B' ⟶ Y locally of finite type, is
isSmooth_iff_forall_exists_lift_isSmallExtension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsSmooth.liftsAgainstFiniteTypeSmallExtensions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APP, (1) implies (2), as stated.** A smooth morphism of algebraic spaces
satisfies condition (2) of Stacks 0APP with the test morphism of finite type. No hypothesis on
the target is needed.
declarations.comment: (1) implies (2) as stated, with the test morphism Spec B' ⟶ Y of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmooth_iff_forall_exists_lift_isSmallExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APP.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which is
locally of finite type, with `Y` locally Noetherian. Then `f` is smooth if and only if every
solid square whose vertical map is induced by a small extension `φ : R' ⟶ R` of Artinian local
rings and whose map `Spec R' ⟶ Y` is locally of finite type admits a dotted arrow making the
diagram commute.

The implication towards the lifting property is the formal smoothness of a smooth morphism
(Stacks 04AM). The converse runs the scheme-level criterion of Stacks 02HY on each commuting
square of étale charts, pushing each scheme-level lifting problem into the algebraic spaces and
pulling its solution back along the formally étale charts.

The source asks the map `Spec R' ⟶ Y` to be of finite type; with that condition the
equivalence is false, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.not_forall_isSmooth_iff_liftsAgainstFiniteTypeSmallExtensions`, so
here the map is asked only to be locally of finite type. See the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmooth_iff_forall_exists_lift_isSmallExtension
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun Z : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian Z))
    (hFiniteType : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsSmooth B S hS f ↔
      ∀ ⦃R' R : CommRingCat.{u}⦄ (φ : R' ⟶ R),
        InfinitesimalLifting.IsSmallExtension φ →
        ∀ (T T' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (i : T ⟶ T')
          (e : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T ≅ Spec R)
          (e' : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T' ≅ Spec R'),
          (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map i = e.hom ≫ Spec.map φ ≫ e'.inv →
          ∀ (α : yoneda.obj T ⟶ X) (β : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ Y),
            IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS β →
            α ≫ f = yoneda.map i ≫ β →
            ∃ γ : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ X, yoneda.map i ≫ γ = α ∧ γ ≫ f = β
declarations.comment:
corrected form: the test morphism Spec R' ⟶ Y is required to be locally of finite
type. With it of finite type, as in the source, the statement is false:
not_forall_isSmooth_iff_liftsAgainstFiniteTypeSmallExtensions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothAt_of_isSmooth_nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APQ, part (1).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` which
is locally of finite type, with `Y` locally Noetherian. Let `Z ⊆ Y` be a closed subspace, cut out
on a surjective étale chart `φ : U ⟶ Y` by the invariant sheaf of ideals `J`, so that its `n`th
infinitesimal neighbourhood is `Zₙ = nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood φ J n`, and let
`Xₙ = Zₙ ×_Y X`. If `Xₙ ⟶ Zₙ` is smooth for every `n`, then `f` is smooth at every point of
`f⁻¹(Z)`.

Every closed subspace is cut out on every surjective étale chart by exactly one invariant sheaf
of ideals (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isInvariantIdealSheaf_invariantSubspace_eq`), so this
applies to every closed subspace of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmoothAt_of_isSmooth_nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y.1)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 (fun W : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian W))
    (hFiniteType : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1)
    {J : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).IdealSheafData}
    (hJ : IsInvariantIdealSheaf B S hS hs J)
    (hZJ : invariantSubspace B S hS φ (Subobject.mk J.subschemeι) = Z.1)
    (Xn : ℕ → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (fn : ∀ n, Xn n ⟶ (nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood B S hS φ J n).toFunctor)
    (pn : ∀ n, Xn n ⟶ X)
    (hcart : ∀ n, IsPullback (pn n) (fn n) f (nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood B S hS φ J n).ι)
    (hsmooth : ∀ n, IsSmooth B S hS (fn n))
    (x : points B S hS X)
    (hx : pointsMap B S hS X f x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z.1.toFunctor Z.1.ι)) :
    IsSmoothAt B S hS f x
declarations.comment:
part (1): smooth. Z is an arbitrary closed subspace and Zₙ its nth
infinitesimal neighbourhood (Tag 05ZV), built on a surjective étale chart from the invariant
ideal sheaf cutting out Z, which exists and is unique by
exists_isInvariantIdealSheaf_invariantSubspace_eq and ker_rep_snd_eq_of_invariantSubspace_eq;
Xₙ is any fibre product Zₙ ×_Y X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEtaleAt_of_isEtale_nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APQ, part (2).** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSmoothAt_of_isSmooth_nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood`, if
`Xₙ = Zₙ ×_Y X ⟶ Zₙ` is étale for every `n`, then `f` is étale at every point of `f⁻¹(Z)`.

Étaleness of every base change gives smoothness of every base change, hence smoothness of `f`
at the point by part (1). It also gives unramifiedness of the zeroth base change, hence
unramifiedness of `f` at the point, which lies in the image of `X₀` because the zeroth square
is cartesian. Stacks 02GK for algebraic spaces assembles the two.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleAt_of_isEtale_nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X ⟶ Y.1)
    (hNoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 (fun W : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian W))
    (hFiniteType : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS Y.1)
    {J : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U).IdealSheafData}
    (hJ : IsInvariantIdealSheaf B S hS hs J)
    (hZJ : invariantSubspace B S hS φ (Subobject.mk J.subschemeι) = Z.1)
    (Xn : ℕ → (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (fn : ∀ n, Xn n ⟶ (nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood B S hS φ J n).toFunctor)
    (pn : ∀ n, Xn n ⟶ X)
    (hcart : ∀ n, IsPullback (pn n) (fn n) f (nthOrderInfinitesimalNeighbourhood B S hS φ J n).ι)
    (hetale : ∀ n, IsEtale B S hS (fn n))
    (x : points B S hS X)
    (hx : pointsMap B S hS X f x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Z.1.toFunctor Z.1.ι)) :
    IsEtaleAt B S hS f x
declarations.comment:
part (2): étale. Z is an arbitrary closed subspace and Zₙ its nth
infinitesimal neighbourhood (Tag 05ZV), built on a surjective étale chart from the invariant
ideal sheaf cutting out Z, which exists and is unique by
exists_isInvariantIdealSheaf_invariantSubspace_eq and ker_rep_snd_eq_of_invariantSubspace_eq;
Xₙ is any fibre product Zₙ ×_Y X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_and_isFlatOnFibre_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APR.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
with `X`, `Y`, `Z` locally Noetherian, let `F` be an `𝒪_X`-module and let `x̄` be a geometric
point of `X` whose geometric stalk `F_{x̄}` is a nonzero finite `𝒪_{X, x̄}`-module.  Then `F` is
flat over `Z` at `x̄` and flat on the fibre over `z̄` relative to the fibre of `Y` exactly when
`Y` is flat over `Z` at `ȳ` and `F` is flat over `Y` at `x̄`.

Over the étale local rings `𝒪_{Z, z̄} → 𝒪_{Y, ȳ} → 𝒪_{X, x̄}` this is Stacks 00MP in one
direction, and transitivity of flatness together with base change along
`𝒪_{Y, ȳ} → 𝒪_{Y, ȳ}/𝔪_{z̄}𝒪_{Y, ȳ}` in the other.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtGeometricPoint_and_isFlatOnFibre_iff {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (F : Modules.{u, m} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hY : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hZ : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Z.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (hfin : Module.Finite (etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 xbar)
      (geometricModuleStalk B S hS X xbar F))
    (hne : Nontrivial (geometricModuleStalk B S hS X xbar F)) :
    (IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS (f ≫ g) F xbar ∧
        IsFlatOnFibreAtGeometricPoint B S hS f g F xbar) ↔
      (IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (geometricPointMap f.hom xbar).image ∧
        IsFlatOverAtGeometricPoint B S hS f F xbar)
declarations.comment:
The full equivalence, at a geometric point `x̄` of `X`: condition (1) is
  flatness of `F` over `Z` at `x̄` (condition (2) of Stacks 05VU for `X ⟶ Z`) together with the
  fibre condition read on geometric stalks as in part (1) of Stacks 05WY, and condition (2) is
  flatness of `Y` over `Z` at the image point of `ȳ` together with flatness of `F` over `Y` at
  `x̄`.  Local Noetherianity of `X`, `Y`, `Z` is the étale-local scheme property; coherence of
  `F` is used only through finiteness of `F_{x̄}` over `𝒪_{X, x̄}`, which is hypothesised, so
  quasi-coherence of `F` is not assumed.  NOT covered: the identification of the fibre
  condition with flatness of a pullback of `F` to a genuine fibre product over a field-valued
  representative of `z̄`, which is Stacks 05WY.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlatOverAtPoint_comp_and_isFlatOnFibreAtFieldValuedPoint_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APR.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of locally Noetherian
algebraic spaces over `S`, let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `x ∈ |X|`, with image
`y ∈ |Y|`.  Suppose `F_{x̄} ≠ 0` for a geometric point `x̄` of `X` over `x`.  Then for every
field-valued point `Spec(K) ⟶ X` in the class of `x` the following are equivalent:

1. `F` is flat over `Z` at `x`, and the pullback of `F` to the fibre `X_z = Spec(K) ×_Z X` over
   the image `z` of the point is flat over `Y_z = Spec(K) ×_Z Y` at the `K`-rational point of
   `X_z`;
2. `Y` is flat over `Z` at `y`, and `F` is flat over `Y` at `x`.

Flatness at a point is the definition of Stacks 05VV for modules and of Stacks 03ML for
morphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlatOverAtPoint_comp_and_isFlatOnFibreAtFieldValuedPoint_iff
    {X Y Z : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F]
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hY : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (hZ : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Z.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (x : points B S hS X.1) (xbar : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) (hxbar : xbar.LiesOver x)
    (hne : Nontrivial (geometricModuleStalk B S hS X xbar F))
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X.1) (hp : p.class B S hS X.1 = x) :
    (IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 (f ≫ g).hom F x ∧
        IsFlatOnFibreAtFieldValuedPoint B S hS f g p F) ↔
      (IsFlatAt B S hS g.hom (pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x) ∧
        IsFlatOverAtPoint B S hS X.2 f.hom F x)
declarations.comment:
The full statement: flatness of F over Z and over Y at x is the definition of
  Stacks 05VV (IsFlatOverAtPoint), flatness of Y over Z at y is that of Stacks 03ML, and the
  fibre clause is flatness of the pullback of F to the fibre product Spec(K) x_Z X over
  Spec(K) x_Z Y at the K-point, for every field-valued representative of x (condition (2) of
  Stacks 05WY); F is coherent and X, Y, Z are locally Noetherian.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0APS, conclusion (A).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms
of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`. If `X`, `Y`, `Z` are locally Noetherian, `X` is flat
over `Z`, and the fibres of `X` over the points of `Z` are flat over the corresponding fibres
of `Y` in the chart sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasFlatFibreCharts`, then `f` is
flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hXn : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X
      (fun A : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian A))
    (hYn : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y
      (fun A : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian A))
    (hZn : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Z
      (fun A : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian A))
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hfib : HasFlatFibreCharts B S hS f g) :
    IsFlat B S hS f
declarations.comment:
conclusion (A): flatness of the morphism; hypothesis (3) in its every-étale-chart
reading `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasFlatFibreCharts`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts_of_isSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0APS, conclusion (B).** In the situation of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts`, if `f` is in addition surjective then `Y`
is flat over `Z`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_of_flatFibreCharts_of_isSurjective
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hXn : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X
      (fun A : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian A))
    (hYn : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y
      (fun A : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian A))
    (hZn : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Z
      (fun A : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian A))
    (hflat : IsFlat B S hS (f ≫ g)) (hfib : HasFlatFibreCharts B S hS f g)
    (hfs : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    IsFlat B S hS g

declarations.name: RingHom.isOpenMap_of_isTaut_of_denseRange
declarations.doc:
A continuous taut map with dense image from a complete countably based linearly
topologized ring to a separated linearly topologized ring is open.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isOpenMap_of_isTaut_of_denseRange (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hA : @CompleteSpace A (IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace A))
    (hcount : (nhds (0 : A)).IsCountablyGenerated) (htaut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (hdense : DenseRange φ) : IsOpenMap φ
declarations.comment: openness

declarations.name: RingHom.surjective_of_isTaut_of_denseRange
declarations.doc:
A continuous taut map with dense image under the completeness and countability hypotheses
is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public lemma surjective_of_isTaut_of_denseRange (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hA : @CompleteSpace A (IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace A))
    (hcount : (nhds (0 : A)).IsCountablyGenerated) (htaut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (hdense : DenseRange φ) : Function.Surjective φ
declarations.comment: surjectivity

declarations.name: RingHom.completeSpace_of_isTaut_of_denseRange
declarations.doc:
The separated target of a continuous taut dense map from a complete countably based
linearly topologized ring is complete.
declarations.comment: completeness of the target

declarations.name: RingHom.isClosed_ker_of_continuous
declarations.doc: The kernel of a continuous ring homomorphism into a space with closed points is closed.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isClosed_ker_of_continuous {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [CommRing S] [TopologicalSpace S] [T1Space S] (φ : R →+* S) (hφ : Continuous φ) :
    IsClosed (RingHom.ker φ : Set R)
declarations.comment: closed kernel

declarations.name: RingHom.quotientKerEquiv_of_isTaut_of_denseRange
declarations.doc:
The canonical map from the quotient by the kernel to the target is a homeomorphic ring
equivalence.
declarations.statement:
public lemma quotientKerEquiv_of_isTaut_of_denseRange (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hA : @CompleteSpace A (IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace A))
    (hcount : (nhds (0 : A)).IsCountablyGenerated) (htaut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (hdense : DenseRange φ) :
    ∃ e : (A ⧸ RingHom.ker φ) ≃+* B,
      (∀ a : A, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (RingHom.ker φ) a) = φ a) ∧ IsHomeomorph e
declarations.comment: quotient presentation

declarations.name: RingHom.exists_fg_ideal_isAdic_of_isTaut
declarations.doc:
The target of a taut continuous homomorphism from a pre-adic ring with a finitely generated
ideal of definition is itself adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition, provided that
the target is complete.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_fg_ideal_isAdic_of_isTaut
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (hTaut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (hA : ∃ I : Ideal A, I.FG ∧ _root_.IsAdic I)
    [@CompleteSpace B (IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace B)] [T2Space B] :
    ∃ J : Ideal B, J.FG ∧ _root_.IsAdic J
declarations.comment: the target is adic with a finitely generated ideal of definition

declarations.name: RingHom.isAdic_of_isTaut
declarations.doc:
A taut continuous homomorphism from a pre-adic ring with a finitely generated ideal of
definition to a complete linearly topologized ring is adic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isAdic_of_isTaut
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing B] [TopologicalSpace B] [IsTopologicalRing B]
    [IsLinearTopology B B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (hTaut : RingHom.IsTaut φ)
    (hA : ∃ I : Ideal A, I.FG ∧ _root_.IsAdic I)
    [@CompleteSpace B (IsTopologicalAddGroup.rightUniformSpace B)] [T2Space B] :
    RingHom.IsAdic φ
declarations.comment: the homomorphism is adic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APV.** Completion is compatible with base change: for a morphism `f : X' ⟶ X`
of presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` and a set `T` of points of `X`, the square formed
by the completion of `X'` along `|f|⁻¹ T`, the completion of `X` along `T` and the two
ambient sheaves is a cartesian square of fppf sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_completionSheafMap
    {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (T : Set (points B S hS X)) :
    IsPullback
      (completionSheafInclusion B S hS X' (pointsMap B S hS X' f ⁻¹' T))
      (completionSheafMap B S hS f T)
      (sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS f)
      (completionSheafInclusion B S hS X T)
declarations.comment: cartesian square

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_completionMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APV.** For a morphism `f : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` and a set `T`
of points of `X`, the induced morphism of completions `X'_{/|f|⁻¹ T} ⟶ X_{/T}` is
representable by algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_completionMap
    {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (points B S hS X)) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
      (completionSheafMap B S hS f T).hom
declarations.comment: representable by algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicStar_zeroLocusCompletion_of_isCountablyIndexed
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APW (1).** Let `X = Spec A` be an affine scheme over `S` and `T = V(I)` a closed
subset. If the formal completion `X_{/T}` is countably indexed and `T = V(e 0, e 1, …)` is cut
out by countably many elements of `A`, then `X_{/T}` is adic\*.

By `exists_isCofinalVanishingSequence_of_isCountablyIndexed` the countable indexedness gives a
cofinal sequence `J` of ideals cutting out `T`; by `countableCompletionIsoZeroLocusCompletion`
the completion is the colimit of the `Spec (A ⧸ J n)`, which is adic\* by
`isAdicStar_countableCompletion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicStar_zeroLocusCompletion_of_isCountablyIndexed (I : Ideal A) (e : ℕ → A)
    (heI : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (Set.range e))
    (hX : IsCountablyIndexed B S hS (zeroLocusCompletion B S hS hA f I)) :
    IsAdicStar B S hS (zeroLocusCompletion B S hS hA f I)
declarations.comment: clause (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexed_not_isAdicStar_zeroLocusCompletion_gabber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0APW (2).** The conclusion of clause (1) fails without the countability of the
equations: for Gabber's ring `A` and `T = V(x_α : α ∈ ω₁)`, the formal completion `X_{/T}` of
`X = Spec A` is countably indexed but not adic\*, and so `T` is not cut out by countably many
elements of `A`.

The completion is identified with `gabberCompletionSheaf`, the colimit along the cofinal
sequence `J_n = (x_α^(n+1))`, by `countableCompletionIsoZeroLocusCompletion`, and
`isCountablyIndexed_not_isAdicStar_gabberCompletionSheaf` is the statement for that sheaf. The
last conjunct follows from clause (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexed_not_isAdicStar_zeroLocusCompletion_gabber (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of GabberRing.{u})))
    (f : Spec (.of GabberRing.{u}) ⟶ S) :
    IsCountablyIndexed B S hS (zeroLocusCompletion B S hS hA f gabberVanishingIdeal.{u}) ∧
      ¬ IsAdicStar B S hS (zeroLocusCompletion B S hS hA f gabberVanishingIdeal.{u}) ∧
      ¬ ∃ e : ℕ → GabberRing.{u},
        PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (gabberVanishingIdeal.{u} : Set GabberRing.{u}) =
          PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (Set.range e)
declarations.comment: clause (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSeparatedMorphism_of_isClosedImmersion_diag
declarations.doc:
A morphism `f : U ⟶ X` of fppf sheaves over `S` whose source is separated over `S`, that is
whose diagonal `U ⟶ U ⨯ U` is a closed immersion, is separated.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_comp
declarations.doc:
A composition of morphisms representable by algebraic spaces is
representable by algebraic spaces, for presheaves on the big fppf site of `S` with values in
`Type (max w u)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_comp
    {F G H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w u)} (a : F ⟶ G) (b : G ⟶ H)
    (ha : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS a)
    (hb : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS b) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS (a ≫ b)
declarations.comment: representable by algebraic spaces in an arbitrary value universe

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.relativelyRepresentable.isMultiplicative
registrations.comment: representable by schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
A base change of a morphism representable by algebraic spaces is
representable by algebraic spaces: in a cartesian square of presheaves on the big fppf site
of `S` with values in `Type (max w u)` whose right-hand column `a` is representable by
algebraic spaces, the left-hand column `a'` is representable by algebraic spaces too.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_isPullback
    {F G G' H : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max w u)}
    (p : H ⟶ F) (a' : H ⟶ G') (a : F ⟶ G) (g : G' ⟶ G) (h : IsPullback p a' a g)
    (ha : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS a) :
    IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{w} B S hS a'
declarations.comment: representable by algebraic spaces

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.relativelyRepresentable.isStableUnderBaseChange
registrations.comment: representable by schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_comp_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`
with `Y` a formal algebraic space. If `f ≫ g` is representable by algebraic spaces then so is
`f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_comp_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hcomp : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (f.hom ≫ g.hom)) :
    Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom
declarations.comment: for a second morphism whose source is an arbitrary formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_comp_of_isAffineFormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ0** when the intermediate sheaf is an affine formal algebraic space. Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` with `Y`
an affine formal algebraic space. If `f ≫ g` is representable by algebraic spaces then so is
`f`, the relative diagonal of `g` being representable by Stacks 0AN2.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_comp_of_isAffineFormal
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hcomp : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (f.hom ≫ g.hom)) :
    Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom
declarations.comment: for a second morphism whose source is an affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_comp_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ0** when the second morphism is a monomorphism. Its relative diagonal is then
an isomorphism, hence representable by objects of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_of_comp_of_mono {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Mono g]
    (hcomp : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (f.hom ≫ g.hom)) :
    Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS f.hom
declarations.comment: for a second morphism which is a monomorphism of fppf sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_completionSheaf_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ1, part (2).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic
space over `S` and let `T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset. The completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T` is
locally Noetherian.

The affine étale charts `Spec A_k ⟶ X` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_affine_etale_charts` are étale over the locally Noetherian
`X`, so each `Spec A_k` is locally Noetherian and each `A_k` is a Noetherian ring; the
set-theoretic condition is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionSheaf`. With these the
atlas argument of `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_completionSheaf`
applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_completionSheaf_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXN : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T) :
    IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyAdicStar_completionSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ1, part (1).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and
let `T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset such that `X \ T ⟶ X` is quasi-compact. The completion `X_{/T}`
of `X` along `T` is *locally adic\**: the completions of the affine charts of `X` along the
inverse images of `T` form an atlas of `X_{/T}`, and each of them is an adic\* affine formal
algebraic space by the affine case, Stacks 0GBA (1), the complement of the inverse image of `T`
on a chart being quasi-compact.

The affine étale charts of `X` and the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS are carried as
hypotheses, as in `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheaf`
(Stacks 0AIZ); quasi-compactness of `X \ T ⟶ X` is carried in the form it is used in, namely
chartwise quasi-compactness of the complement `hqc`, which is the source's step transferring
the hypothesis from `X` to the charts. The hypothesis `HasStageAtlas` of Stacks 0AIY is *not*
needed here: being adic\* already contains being an affine formal algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAdicStar_completionSheaf
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T)
    {Ix : Type (u + 1)} {A : Ix → Type u} [∀ i, CommRing (A i)]
    (hA : ∀ i, B.Contains (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of (A i))))
    (str : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of (A i)) ⟶ S)
    (a : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (affineOver B S hS (hA i) (str i)) ⟶ X)
    (ha : ∀ i, ∃ hai : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (a i)).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ q ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS q.hom)
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (a i)).hom hai)
    (hcov : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
          Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
