          (Sigma.desc fun i ↦ Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (a i)))
    (hqc : ∀ i, @IsCompact _
      (Space.pointTopology B S hS (yoneda.obj (affineOver B S hS (hA i) (str i))))
      (Space.pointsMap B S hS _ (a i) ⁻¹' T)ᶜ)
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)) :
    IsLocallyAdicStar B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)
declarations.comment: part (1): locally adic star; assumes the affine étale charts of X as hA, str, a, ha, hcov, chartwise quasi-compactness of the complement as hqc, and the 0AIS condition as hset

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_completionSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ1, part (2).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic
space over `S` and let `T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset. The completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T` is
*locally Noetherian*: the completions of the affine charts of `X` along the inverse images of
`T` form an atlas of `X_{/T}`, and each of them is a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space by
the affine case, Stacks 0GBA (3), the chart rings being Noetherian.

The affine étale charts of `X` and the set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS are carried as
hypotheses, as in `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFormalAlgebraicSpace_completionSheaf`
(Stacks 0AIZ); local Noetherianness of `X` is carried in the form it is used in, namely
Noetherianness of the chart rings `hNoeth`, which is the source's step transferring the
hypothesis from `X` to the charts. The hypothesis `HasStageAtlas` of Stacks 0AIY is *not* needed
here: being Noetherian already contains being an affine formal algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_completionSheaf
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T)
    {Ix : Type (u + 1)} {A : Ix → Type u} [∀ i, CommRing (A i)]
    (hNoeth : ∀ i, IsNoetherianRing (A i))
    (hA : ∀ i, B.Contains (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of (A i))))
    (str : ∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of (A i)) ⟶ S)
    (a : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (affineOver B S hS (hA i) (str i)) ⟶ X)
    (ha : ∀ i, ∃ hai : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (a i)).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun _ _ q ↦ Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS q.hom)
        (Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (a i)).hom hai)
    (hcov : letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{u + 1, u + 1} (FppfSheaf B S hS) :=
          Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
        Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective
          (Sigma.desc fun i ↦ Space.sheafifiedULiftMap B S hS (a i)))
    (hset : SatisfiesSetTheoreticCondition B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)) :
    IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)
declarations.comment: part (2): locally Noetherian; assumes the affine étale charts of X as hA, str, a, ha, hcov, Noetherianness of the chart rings as hNoeth, and the 0AIS condition as hset

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyAdicStar_completionSheaf_of_isQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ1, part (1).** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S` and
let `T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset such that the inclusion `X ∖ T ⟶ X` of the open complement is
quasi-compact. Then the completion `X_{/T}` of `X` along `T` is locally adic*.

The affine étale charts `Spec A_k ⟶ X` are those of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_affine_etale_charts`; on each, the complement of the
inverse image of `T` is quasi-compact
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCompact_compl_preimage_pointsMap_of_isQuasiCompact_ι`), and the
set-theoretic condition of Stacks 0AIS is
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.satisfiesSetTheoreticCondition_completionSheaf`. With these the
atlas argument of `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyAdicStar_completionSheaf` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAdicStar_completionSheaf_of_isQuasiCompact
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T)
    (hqc : Space.IsQuasiCompact B S hS (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι) :
    IsLocallyAdicStar B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyAdicStar_completionSheaf_and_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ1.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `T ⊆ |X|`
be a closed subset and let `X_{/T}` be the completion of `X` along `T`.

1. If `X ∖ T ⟶ X` is quasi-compact, then `X_{/T}` is locally adic*.
2. If `X` is locally Noetherian, then `X_{/T}` is locally Noetherian.

The two parts are
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyAdicStar_completionSheaf_of_isQuasiCompact` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_completionSheaf_of_isLocallyNoetherian`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyAdicStar_completionSheaf_and_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T) :
    (Space.IsQuasiCompact B S hS (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι →
        IsLocallyAdicStar B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T)) ∧
      (Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X →
        IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS (Space.completionSheaf B S hS X T))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram_iff_isTautAdicStar
declarations.doc:
**Section 0AQ2, the footnote.** On `WAdm^{adic*}` the chart condition of the section may be
read with "adic" or with "taut": the two readings agree, by Stacks 0GBS.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram_iff_isTautAdicStar {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsAdicOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS f ↔
      IsTautOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagramAdicStar B S hS f
declarations.comment: the footnote of the section: on WAdm^{adic*} the adic and the taut reading of the chart condition agree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isAdicMorphism_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Section 0AQ2.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of locally adic\* formal algebraic spaces
over `S`. The following are equivalent:

1. `f` is representable by algebraic spaces, that is, `f` is an adic morphism in the sense of
   Definition 0AQ3;
2. for every commutative square
   ```
   U ⟶ V
   ↓     ↓
   X ⟶ Y
   ```
   with `U` and `V` affine formal algebraic spaces and `U ⟶ X`, `V ⟶ Y` representable by
   algebraic spaces and étale, the morphism `U ⟶ V` corresponds to an adic map in
   `WAdm^{adic*}`;
3. the same with "adic" replaced by "taut", which is the footnote of the section.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicMorphism_tfae {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyAdicStar B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyAdicStar B S hS Y) :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsAdicMorphism B S hS f,
        IsAdicOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagram B S hS f,
        IsTautOnEveryAffineEtaleDiagramAdicStar B S hS f ]
declarations.comment: the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2) of the section for a morphism of locally adic* formal algebraic spaces, together with the footnote reading (2) with taut maps

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsAdicMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ3.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` with
`X` and `Y` locally adic\*. Then `f` is an *adic morphism* when `f` is representable by
algebraic spaces.

The locally adic\* hypotheses on `X` and `Y` are the standing assumptions under which the
source introduces the terminology; as for Stacks 0AQM they are imposed by the results that use
the predicate rather than built into it, so that the predicate is the defining condition and
nothing more.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdicMorphism {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 02YQ.** A morphism of presheaves is representable by algebraic
spaces if its pullback to every scheme over the base is an algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (a : F ⟶ G) : Prop
declarations.comment: the defining condition of an adic morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsLocallyOfFiniteType.comp
declarations.doc:
A composition of morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which are locally of finite
type is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyOfFiniteType.comp {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFiniteType.comp
declarations.doc:
A composition of morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which are of finite type is
of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiniteType.comp {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsFiniteType B S hS g) :
    IsFiniteType B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsBootstrapFiniteType.comp
declarations.doc:
A composition of morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which are representable by
algebraic spaces and of finite type in the bootstrap sense of Stacks 03XZ is again such.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsBootstrapFiniteType.comp {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : IsBootstrapFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsBootstrapFiniteType B S hS g) :
    IsBootstrapFiniteType B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: finite type, proved for condition (2) of Stacks 0AJJ — representable by algebraic spaces plus of finite type in the Bootstrap sense of Stacks 03XZ — rather than for Definition 0AM4, part (2), verbatim, which is defined further up the import order: the two are identified unconditionally by Stacks 0AJJ, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isFiniteType_iff_isBootstrapFiniteType`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsLocallyOfFiniteType.of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
A base change of a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of finite
type is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyOfFiniteType.of_isPullback {W X Z Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS p
declarations.comment: locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFiniteType.of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
A base change of a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is of finite type is
of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiniteType.of_isPullback {W X Z Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hf : IsFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsFiniteType B S hS p
declarations.comment: finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsFiniteType.of_isPullback'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ5, the global half.** A base change of a morphism of formal algebraic spaces
over `S` which is of finite type is of finite type: both halves of the condition are stable
under base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiniteType.of_isPullback' {W X Z Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hf : IsFiniteType' B S hS f) :
    IsFiniteType' B S hS p
declarations.comment: finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsLocallyOfFiniteType.of_comp
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`
with `Y` a formal algebraic space. If `f ≫ g` is locally of finite type then so is `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyOfFiniteType.of_comp {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f
declarations.comment: stated for arbitrary fppf sheaves, only the source of the second morphism being assumed a formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsLocallyOfFiniteType.of_comp_of_isAffineFormal
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S`
with `Y` an affine formal algebraic space. If `f ≫ g` is locally of finite type then so is
`f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsLocallyOfFiniteType.of_comp_of_isAffineFormal {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hY : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hfg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f
declarations.comment: for a second morphism whose source is an affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_source_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ7.** If `Y` is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space
over `S` and `f : X ⟶ Y` is a morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is locally of
finite type, then `X` is locally Noetherian.

The atlas of `Y` by Noetherian affine formal algebraic spaces base changes to a family of
fibre products covering `X`, and the atlases of those fibre products assemble into an atlas of
`X`. Its members are locally of finite type over the members of the atlas of `Y` by Stacks
0ANL, condition (1) implies condition (3), hence Noetherian by clause (5) of Stacks 0AKQ,
which Stacks 0AKN makes unconditional.

The fibre products `Vⱼ ×_Y X` are formal algebraic spaces by **Stacks 0AJ3**, which this
library proves outright for a base which is a formal algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_source_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType'
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_of_isPullback'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ8.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of formal
algebraic spaces over `S`. If `Z` is locally Noetherian and `f` is locally of finite type, then
`Z ×_Y X` is locally Noetherian.

The projection `p : Z ×_Y X ⟶ Z` is a base change of `f`, so it is locally of finite type by
Stacks 0AQ5, and `Z ×_Y X` is a formal algebraic space by Stacks 0AJ3; Stacks 0AQ7 applies to
`p`. The fibre product is presented as an arbitrary cartesian square, so the statement covers
either order of its two legs.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_of_isPullback'
    {W X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS W
declarations.comment: stated for an arbitrary cartesian square over `Y` rather than for the chosen fibre product `Z ×_Y X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyNoetherian_of_isPullback_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ8.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of fppf sheaves over `S`.
If `Z` is a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space and `f` is locally of finite type, then
`Z ×_Y X` is locally Noetherian.

The projection `p : Z ×_Y X ⟶ Z` is a base change of `f`, so it is locally of finite type by
Stacks 0AQ5; being representable by algebraic spaces it makes `Z ×_Y X` a formal algebraic space
by Stacks 0AJI, and Stacks 0AQ7 applies to `p`. The fibre product is presented as an arbitrary
cartesian square, so the statement covers either order of its two legs; `X` and `Y` need not be
formal algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyNoetherian_of_isPullback_of_isLocallyOfFiniteType
    {W X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hZ : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Z)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyOfFiniteType_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQ9.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `T`
be a set of points of `X`. If `f` is locally of finite type, then the induced morphism of
completions `X'_{/|f|⁻¹ T} ⟶ X_{/T}` is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_completionSheafMap
    {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hf : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Mono
registrations.comment: monomorphism of the underlying sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQD.** A formal algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S` contained in a big fppf site
`B` satisfies the sheaf property for the fpqc topology of the big fppf site of `S`.

By `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSheaf_fpqc_of_isSheafFor_singleton_affine_of_formal` it is
enough to check the sheaf condition for one surjective, flat, quasi-compact morphism of the
site, which is `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSheafFor_singleton_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_fpqc {X : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf
      ((Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.comap (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).toGrothendieck) X.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_formalSpectrumToSpec
declarations.doc:
The canonical formal-to-ordinary-spectrum map exists and restricts to the
quotient-spectrum map at every stage.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_formalSpectrumToSpec
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A)
    (hAS : B.Contains (Spec (.of A))) (fA : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
    (hcompat : ∀ J : { I : Ideal A // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J.1)) ≫ fA = D.overS J) :
    ∃ q : formalSpectrum D ⟶
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
        ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (specOver hAS fA)),
      ∀ J : { I : Ideal A // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
        formalSpectrumInclusion D (OrderDual.toDual J) ≫ q =
          (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map
            ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).map
              (stageToSpec D hAS fA J (hcompat J)))
declarations.comment: canonical map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.bijective_map_into_affine
declarations.doc:
For an affine target over `S`, restriction to the quotient spectra is a
bijection on morphisms over `S`. The ordinary spectrum need not belong to the
chosen big fppf site.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_map_into_affine
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A)
    (fA : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
    (hcompat : ∀ J : { I : Ideal A // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J.1)) ≫ fA = D.overS J)
    (X : BigAffineFppf B S hS) :
    Function.Bijective (restrictToFormalSpectrum D fA hcompat
      ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj X))
declarations.comment: bijectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.existsUnique_equiv_specHom_formalSpectrumHom
declarations.doc:
The canonical bijection between maps from a spectrum and from its formal
spectrum to an `S`-scheme, characterized by restriction to every weak quotient.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_equiv_specHom_formalSpectrumHom
    {B : BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}} {hS : B.Contains S}
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A]
    [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A)
    (p : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S)
    (hp : ∀ J : { I : Ideal A // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J.1)) ≫ p = D.overS J)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I)
    [IsLocalRing (A ⧸ I)]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : B.Contains X) (xS : X ⟶ S) :
    let Xo : BigFppfOver B S hS :=
      Over.mk (ObjectProperty.homMk xS : B.obj hX ⟶ B.obj hS)
    ∃! e : ((Over.mk p : Over S) ⟶ (Over.mk xS : Over S)) ≃
        (formalSpectrum D ⟶
          (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj Xo),
      ∀ (f : (Over.mk p : Over S) ⟶ (Over.mk xS : Over S))
    (J : { I : Ideal A // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I }),
        ∃ g : (BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (D.stage J) ⟶ Xo,
          B.inclusion.map g.left =
              Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J.1)) ≫ f.left ∧
            formalSpectrumInclusion D (OrderDual.toDual J) ≫ e f =
              (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).map g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.injective_map_into_algebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**The injectivity half of Stacks 0AQH**, in the shape of the bijectivity statement:
restriction along the canonical map `Spf R ⟶ Spec R` is injective on morphisms to an
algebraic space over `S`.

Only the second cofinality condition on the weak ideals of definition is used — that every
power of the maximal ideal contains one — and the Noetherian hypothesis on `R` enters only
through locality and completeness.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_map_into_algebraicSpace
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    (hR : IsNoetherianCompleteLocalRing R)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS R)
    (hD : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ J : { I : Ideal R // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      J.1 ≤ (@IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R _ hR.isLocal) ^ n)
    (hRS : B.Contains (Spec (.of R))) (p : Spec (.of R) ⟶ S)
    (hp : ∀ J : { I : Ideal R // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J.1)) ≫ p = D.overS J)
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    Function.Injective (fun f :
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
        ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (specOver hRS p)) ⟶ upliftedSheaf X hX =>
      formalSpectrumToSpec D hRS p hp ≫ f)
declarations.comment: injectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.surjective_map_into_algebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**The surjectivity half of Stacks 0AQH.** Restriction along the canonical map
`Spf R ⟶ Spec R` hits every morphism from the formal spectrum of a Noetherian complete local
`S`-algebra `R` to an algebraic space over `S`.

Both cofinality conditions on the weak ideals of definition are used, so that the formal
spectrum of the quotient system is the `𝔪`-adic one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem surjective_map_into_algebraicSpace
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    (hR : IsNoetherianCompleteLocalRing R)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS R)
    (hD₁ : ∀ J : { I : Ideal R // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      ∃ n : ℕ, (@IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R _ hR.isLocal) ^ n ≤ J.1)
    (hD : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ J : { I : Ideal R // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      J.1 ≤ (@IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R _ hR.isLocal) ^ n)
    (hRS : B.Contains (Spec (.of R))) (p : Spec (.of R) ⟶ S)
    (hp : ∀ J : { I : Ideal R // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J.1)) ≫ p = D.overS J)
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    Function.Surjective (fun f :
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
        ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (specOver hRS p)) ⟶ upliftedSheaf X hX =>
      formalSpectrumToSpec D hRS p hp ≫ f)
declarations.comment: surjectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.bijective_map_into_algebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQH.** For `R` a Noetherian complete local `S`-algebra and `X` an algebraic
space over `S`, restriction along `Spf R ⟶ Spec R` is a bijection
`Mor_S(Spec R, X) ⟶ Mor_S(Spf R, X)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_map_into_algebraicSpace
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    (hR : IsNoetherianCompleteLocalRing R)
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS R)
    (hD₁ : ∀ J : { I : Ideal R // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      ∃ n : ℕ, (@IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R _ hR.isLocal) ^ n ≤ J.1)
    (hD : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ J : { I : Ideal R // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      J.1 ≤ (@IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R _ hR.isLocal) ^ n)
    (hRS : B.Contains (Spec (.of R))) (p : Spec (.of R) ⟶ S)
    (hp : ∀ J : { I : Ideal R // TopologicalRing.IsWeakIdealOfDefinition I },
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk J.1)) ≫ p = D.overS J)
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    Function.Bijective (fun f :
      (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda (BigFppfOver.topology B S hS)).obj
        ((BigAffineFppf.inclusion B S hS).obj (specOver hRS p)) ⟶ upliftedSheaf X hX =>
      formalSpectrumToSpec D hRS p hp ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexedAffine_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQI**, the first conclusion. The source of a closed immersion of fppf sheaves over
`S` whose target is a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space is again a countably
indexed affine formal algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexedAffine_of_isClosedImmersion {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS X) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS Y
declarations.comment: that Y is a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_spfPresentation_continuousHom_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQI**, the correspondence part of the second conclusion. A closed immersion
`f : Y ⟶ X` of fppf sheaves over `S` whose target is a countably indexed affine formal
algebraic space is, after identifying `X` with `Spf A` and `Y` with `Spf C` for objects `A` and
`C` of `WAdm^count`, the formal spectrum of a continuous homomorphism `A ⟶ C` over `S`, itself
again a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_spfPresentation_continuousHom_of_isClosedImmersion {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (hX : IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS X) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    ∃ (P : SpfPresentation B S hS X) (Q : SpfPresentation B S hS Y)
      (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible P.ring),
      (nhds (0 : P.ring)).IsCountablyGenerated ∧
      TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible Q.ring ∧
      (nhds (0 : Q.ring)).IsCountablyGenerated ∧
      ∃ (eX : X ≅ formalSpectrum P.system) (eY : Y ≅ formalSpectrum Q.system)
        (g : ContinuousHom P.system Q.system),
        IsClosedImmersion B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA g) ∧
          f = eY.hom ≫ formalSpectrumMap hA g ≫ eX.inv
declarations.comment: that f corresponds to a morphism of WAdm^count

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosed_ker_and_quotientKerEquiv_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQI**, the quotient part of the second conclusion. Let `A` be an object of
`WAdm^count`, that is, a weakly admissible topological ring over `S` with a countable
fundamental system of neighbourhoods of `0`, let `C` be weakly admissible, and let
`g : A ⟶ C` be a continuous homomorphism over `S` whose formal spectrum is a closed immersion.
If `g` is taut, then `K = ker g` is a closed ideal of `A` and `g` identifies `A/K` with `C`
topologically, so the closed immersion is `Spf` of `A ⟶ A/K`.

Tautness is the one hypothesis not proved here: it is the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of
**Stacks 0AN5**, which this library does not carry. Everything else is proved.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_ker_and_quotientKerEquiv_of_isClosedImmersion
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
    (hcount : (nhds (0 : A)).IsCountablyGenerated)
    {D : QuotientSystem B S hS A} {E : QuotientSystem B S hS C} (g : ContinuousHom D E)
    (hg : IsClosedImmersion B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA g))
    (htaut : RingHom.IsTaut g.toRingHom) :
    IsClosed (RingHom.ker g.toRingHom : Set A) ∧
      ∃ e : (A ⧸ RingHom.ker g.toRingHom) ≃+* C,
        (∀ a : A, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (RingHom.ker g.toRingHom) a) = g.toRingHom a) ∧
          IsHomeomorph e
declarations.comment: the quotient by a closed ideal, given the tautness of Stacks 0AN5

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexedAffine_and_exists_closedIdealQuotient_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQI** in full, given the implication (1) ⟹ (3) of **Stacks 0AN5** as the
hypothesis `hAN5`. Let `X` be a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space over `S` and
let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of fppf sheaves over `S`. Then `Y` is a countably indexed
affine formal algebraic space, and `f` is `Spf` of a continuous homomorphism `g : A ⟶ C` of
objects of `WAdm^count` whose kernel `K` is a closed ideal of `A` and which identifies `A/K`
with `C` topologically; that is, `f` corresponds to `A ⟶ A/K`.

The hypothesis `hAN5` is exactly the implication of Stacks 0AN5 that a continuous homomorphism
of weakly admissible topological rings over `S` whose formal spectrum is a closed immersion —
hence representable by algebraic spaces — is taut. It is the one input this library does not
carry; the unconditional halves of the lemma are
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isCountablyIndexedAffine_of_isClosedImmersion` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_spfPresentation_continuousHom_of_isClosedImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCountablyIndexedAffine_and_exists_closedIdealQuotient_of_isClosedImmersion
    (hAN5 : ∀ {A C : Type u} [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
      [IsLinearTopology A A] [CommRing C] [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C]
      [IsLinearTopology C C] (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
      (_hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
      {D : QuotientSystem B S hS A} {E : QuotientSystem B S hS C} (g : ContinuousHom D E),
      IsClosedImmersion B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA g) → RingHom.IsTaut g.toRingHom)
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS X) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS Y ∧
      ∃ (P : SpfPresentation B S hS X) (Q : SpfPresentation B S hS Y)
        (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible P.ring),
        (nhds (0 : P.ring)).IsCountablyGenerated ∧
        TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible Q.ring ∧
        ∃ (eX : X ≅ formalSpectrum P.system) (eY : Y ≅ formalSpectrum Q.system)
          (g : ContinuousHom P.system Q.system),
          IsClosed (RingHom.ker g.toRingHom : Set P.ring) ∧
          (∃ e : (P.ring ⧸ RingHom.ker g.toRingHom) ≃+* Q.ring,
            (∀ a : P.ring,
              e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (RingHom.ker g.toRingHom) a) = g.toRingHom a) ∧
            IsHomeomorph e) ∧
          f = eY.hom ≫ formalSpectrumMap hA g ≫ eX.inv
declarations.comment: given the tautness of Stacks 0AN5

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsClosedImmersion.isCountablyIndexedAffine_and_exists_closedIdealQuotient
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a countably indexed affine formal algebraic space over `S` and let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a
closed immersion of fppf sheaves over `S`. Then `Y` is a countably indexed affine formal algebraic
space, and `f` is `Spf` of a continuous homomorphism `g : A ⟶ C` of objects of `WAdm^count` whose
kernel `K` is a closed ideal of `A` and which identifies `A/K` with `C` topologically; that is, `f`
corresponds to `A ⟶ A/K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsClosedImmersion.isCountablyIndexedAffine_and_exists_closedIdealQuotient
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hX : IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS X) (f : Y ⟶ X)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsCountablyIndexedAffine B S hS Y ∧
      ∃ (P : SpfPresentation B S hS X) (Q : SpfPresentation B S hS Y)
        (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible P.ring),
        (nhds (0 : P.ring)).IsCountablyGenerated ∧
        TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible Q.ring ∧
        ∃ (eX : X ≅ formalSpectrum P.system) (eY : Y ≅ formalSpectrum Q.system)
          (g : ContinuousHom P.system Q.system),
          IsClosed (RingHom.ker g.toRingHom : Set P.ring) ∧
          (∃ e : (P.ring ⧸ RingHom.ker g.toRingHom) ≃+* Q.ring,
            (∀ a : P.ring,
              e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (RingHom.ker g.toRingHom) a) = g.toRingHom a) ∧
            IsHomeomorph e) ∧
          f = eY.hom ≫ formalSpectrumMap hA g ≫ eX.inv

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosed_ker_and_quotientKerEquiv_of_isClosedImmersion'
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an object of `WAdm^count`, that is, a weakly admissible topological ring over `S`
with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of `0`, let `C` be weakly admissible, and let
`g : A ⟶ C` be a continuous homomorphism over `S` whose formal spectrum is a closed immersion.
Then `K = ker g` is a closed ideal of `A` and `g` identifies `A/K` with `C` topologically, so the
closed immersion is `Spf` of `A ⟶ A/K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_ker_and_quotientKerEquiv_of_isClosedImmersion'
    (hA : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A)
    (hC : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible C)
    (hcount : (nhds (0 : A)).IsCountablyGenerated)
    {D : QuotientSystem B S hS A} {E : QuotientSystem B S hS C} (g : ContinuousHom D E)
    (hg : IsClosedImmersion B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA g)) :
    IsClosed (RingHom.ker g.toRingHom : Set A) ∧
      ∃ e : (A ⧸ RingHom.ker g.toRingHom) ≃+* C,
        (∀ a : A, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (RingHom.ker g.toRingHom) a) = g.toRingHom a) ∧
          IsHomeomorph e
declarations.comment: the quotient by a closed ideal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasSurjectiveOnPullbackCharts_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**The chart homomorphisms of a closed immersion are surjective**, carrying nothing beyond
the closed immersion itself. This is the surjectivity clause of **Stacks 0AQI** on the pullback
charts of `f`.

The chart map `t : U ⟶ V` is a closed immersion because closed immersions are stable under base
change (**Stacks 0GHX**, `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosedImmersion_of_isPullback`), and
conjugating it by the presenting isomorphisms of the two charts leaves a closed immersion, an
isomorphism square being cartesian; so `Spf g` is a closed immersion. Its representability is
the first component of the closed-immersion predicate of Stacks 0ANP, so the implication
(1) ⟹ (3) of **Stacks 0AN5**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isTaut_of_isRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift_formalSpectrumMap`,
makes `g` taut. That implication carries the two set-theoretic conditions
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.QuotientSystem.HasLargeSite`, and both are free here: the chart
rings are Noetherian with adic topologies carrying quotient systems, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.mk_lt_cutoff_of_quotientSystem_of_isAdic` bounds each by the
cutoff of the site and
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasLargeSite_of_mk_lt_cutoff` supplies the condition. This is why
the surjectivity clause of Stacks 0AQI is not a missing input: it is blocked on nothing.

The passage from tautness to the presentation of the chart ring as a quotient is then the
quotient part of Stacks 0AQI,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isClosed_ker_and_quotientKerEquiv_of_isClosedImmersion`, whose
remaining inputs are free as well: the source is adic, so the powers of an ideal of definition
are a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero, and the target is weakly
admissible by `TopologicalRing.isWeaklyAdmissible_of_isAdic` applied to the ideal of definition
for which it is adically complete. Surjectivity is read off the resulting ring equivalence
`A ⧸ ker g ≃+* C`, which agrees with `g` on representatives.
declarations.comment: the surjectivity clause alone, on the pullback charts of a closed immersion, carrying nothing: the chart map is a closed immersion by Stacks 0GHX, conjugation by the presenting isomorphisms of the two charts preserves that, the implication (1) implies (3) of Stacks 0AN5 makes the chart homomorphism taut -- its two HasLargeSite conditions being free on chart rings, which are adic and carry quotient systems, by mk_lt_cutoff_of_quotientSystem_of_isAdic and hasLargeSite_of_mk_lt_cutoff -- and the quotient part of Stacks 0AQI, isClosed_ker_and_quotientKerEquiv_of_isClosedImmersion, turns the tautness into the presentation of the chart ring as a quotient. The adic and topologically finite type clauses of Stacks 0AQI are not asserted

declarations.name: Rig.CompletedPolynomialPresentation.injective_onH₁_chainMapInl_of_lci
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQJ.**  Let `A` be Noetherian, `I ⊆ A` an ideal, `B → C` a morphism of the
category (Stacks 0AL4), `B = A⟨x₁, …, x_r⟩ / J` a completed polynomial presentation and
`ψ : B⟨y₁, …, y_s⟩ ↠ C` a presentation of `C` over `B`.  Assume that `B / IⁿB → C / IⁿC` is a
local complete intersection homomorphism for every `n ≥ 1`.  Then the first map

`H⁻¹(NL^∧_{B/A} ⊗_B C) ⟶ H⁻¹(NL^∧_{C/A})`

of the six-term sequence of Stacks 0ALM is injective.  The map is the one induced on `H⁻¹` by
the left-hand chain map of that sequence, namely the chain map of
`Rig.CompletedPolynomialPresentation.combinedDifferential_comp_innerCotangentMap`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_onH₁_chainMapInl_of_lci
    (KB : CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex P)
    (KC : CompletedNaiveCotangentComplex
      (P.combinedPresentation s (ψ.restrictScalars A) hψ))
    (h : ∀ n : ℕ, RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (reductionMap B C (n + 1))) :
    Function.Injective (NaiveCotangent.chainMapInl _
      (P.combinedDifferential_comp_innerCotangentMap s ψ hψ KB KC)).onH₁

declarations.name: Rig.rigEtale_propertyIsLocalNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQL.** Rig-étaleness is a local property of arrows of `WAdm^Noeth`, in the sense
of Situation 0CBA in the Noetherian form of Remark 0ANI: it ascends along a completed étale
localization diagram, descends along one whose target-side horizontal map is faithfully flat,
and is preserved by finite products of targets.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQM.** A morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is *rig-étale* when every
morphism between affine, representable, étale charts of its source and target is induced by a
rig-étale continuous homomorphism of adic Noetherian topological rings.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRigEtale (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isRigEtale_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQN.** A rig-étale morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over
`S` is locally of finite type.

By the implication (1) ⟹ (4) of Stacks 0ANW it suffices that every affine representable étale
square over `f` has its upper map given by a taut, topologically of finite type morphism of
`WAdm^{count}`. The two charts of such a square are Noetherian (Stacks 0AKX), so every weakly
admissible ring presenting them is Noetherian and adic (Stacks 0AIC); rig-étaleness of `f` then
says that the presenting homomorphism is rig-étale, hence taut and topologically of finite type
(Stacks 0GBW).
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFiniteType_of_isRigEtale_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsRigEtale B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQQ.** A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of fppf sheaves on the big fppf site of `S` is
*rig-surjective* when every adic morphism `p : Spf R ⟶ Y` out of the formal spectrum of a
complete discrete valuation ring `R` lifts to `X` along the formal spectrum of an extension
`R ⊂ R'` of complete discrete valuation rings. Adic means representable by algebraic spaces,
which is the definition of an adic morphism, Stacks 0AQ3.

The source defines the notion for a morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces that
is locally of finite type. The predicate drops those standing hypotheses and asks for the same
lifting condition for any morphism of fppf sheaves. Under them it is the source's definition.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsRigSurjective (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSurjective.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQR**, carrying two hypotheses. A composite of rig-surjective morphisms of formal
algebraic spaces over `S` which are locally of finite type is locally of finite type and
rig-surjective: an adic point of the final target lifts through the second factor over an
extension of complete discrete valuation rings, that lift is again adic, and so lifts through
the first factor over a further extension; the two extensions compose to one.

Adicness of the intermediate lift is `hcancel`, which is **Stacks 0AQ0** for the second factor,
applied to the composite made representable by `hformalSpectrumMap`, which is **Stacks 0AN5**,
(3) implies (1); neither is available in this library.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRigSurjective.comp (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (hformalSpectrumMap : ∀ (A₁ A₂ : Type u) [CommRing A₁] [TopologicalSpace A₁]
      [IsTopologicalRing A₁] [IsLinearTopology A₁ A₁] [CommRing A₂] [TopologicalSpace A₂]
      [IsTopologicalRing A₂] (hA₁ : TopologicalRing.IsWeaklyAdmissible A₁)
      (D₁ : QuotientSystem B S hS A₁) (D₂ : QuotientSystem B S hS A₂)
      (φ : ContinuousHom D₁ D₂), RingHom.IsTaut φ.toRingHom →
      Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (formalSpectrumMap hA₁ φ).hom)
    (hcancel : ∀ {W : FppfSheaf B S hS} (q : W ⟶ Y),
      Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS (q.hom ≫ g.hom) →
      Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS q.hom)
    (hsf : IsRigSurjective B S hS f) (hsg : IsRigSurjective B S hS g) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (f ≫ g) ∧ IsRigSurjective B S hS (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: assuming Stacks 0AN5 and, for the second factor, Stacks 0AQ0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSurjective.comp_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQR.** A composite of rig-surjective morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over `S`
which are locally of finite type is locally of finite type and rig-surjective: an adic point of
the final target lifts through the second factor over an extension of complete discrete
valuation rings, that lift is again adic, and so lifts through the first factor over a further
extension; the two extensions compose to one.

Adicness of the intermediate lift is Stacks 0AQ0 for the second factor, applied to the
composite made representable by the implication (3) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0AN5. The hypothesis `hY`
is what Stacks 0AQ0 asks of the source of the second factor, and the source of Stacks 0AQR
assumes it of `Y` in the stronger form of a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRigSurjective.comp_of_isFormalAlgebraicSpace
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hY : IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (hsf : IsRigSurjective B S hS f) (hsg : IsRigSurjective B S hS g) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (f ≫ g) ∧ IsRigSurjective B S hS (f ≫ g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSurjective.of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQS.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of formal algebraic spaces
over `S` which are locally of finite type. A base change `p : W ⟶ Z` of `f` along `g` is
locally of finite type, and is rig-surjective as soon as `f` is.

An adic point of `Z` out of the formal spectrum of a complete discrete valuation ring becomes,
after composition with `g`, an adic point of `Y`, because `g` is representable by algebraic
spaces; a lift of it to `X` over an extension of complete discrete valuation rings pairs with
the point of `Z` to give a lift to `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRigSurjective.of_isPullback {W X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) (hg : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (hsf : IsRigSurjective B S hS f) :
    IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS p ∧ IsRigSurjective B S hS p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.hasRigSurjectiveOnPullbackCharts_of_isRigSurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQS** in the chart shape in which the proof of Stacks 0GD5 uses it: a
rig-surjective morphism has rig-surjective chart base changes, presented as formal spectra of
the chart homomorphisms. Nothing is carried.

A chart `b : V ⟶ Y` which is representable by algebraic spaces and étale is in particular
representable by algebraic spaces, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSurjective.of_isPullback_of_representable` makes the chart
base change `t` rig-surjective; local finite typeness of `f`, which Stacks 0AQS assumes, enters
that lemma only through the conclusion that the base change is locally of finite type, which is
not asserted here. The presenting isomorphisms of the chart are then stripped off by
Stacks 0AQT and its postcomposition companion, which is the step the module documentation used
to record as missing.
declarations.comment: the chart shape in which the proof of Stacks 0GD5 uses it, carrying nothing beyond rig-surjectivity of f: a chart which is representable by algebraic spaces and etale is in particular representable, so the base change of f along it is rig-surjective, and the presenting isomorphisms of the chart are stripped off by Stacks 0AQT and its postcomposition companion. Local finite typeness of f and of the chart, which the source assumes, is used by the source only for the conclusion that the base change is locally of finite type, which is not asserted here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSurjective.of_isPullback_of_representable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQS**, with both hypotheses that
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSurjective.of_isPullback` makes on local finite typeness
dropped. A base change of a rig-surjective morphism of formal algebraic spaces over `S` along
a morphism representable by algebraic spaces is rig-surjective.

An adic point of `Z` out of the formal spectrum of a complete discrete valuation ring becomes,
after composition with `g`, an adic point of `Y`, because `g` is representable by algebraic
spaces; a lift of it to `X` over an extension of complete discrete valuation rings pairs with
the point of `Z` to give a lift to `W`. Local finite typeness of `g` enters Stacks 0AQS only
through this use of representability, and local finite typeness of `f` only through the
conclusion that the base change is locally of finite type, which is not asserted here.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRigSurjective.of_isPullback_of_representable {W X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS}
    {p : W ⟶ Z} {q : W ⟶ X} {g : Z ⟶ Y} {f : X ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback p q g f)
    (hgrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom)
    (hsf : IsRigSurjective B S hS f) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS p
declarations.comment: rig-surjectivity alone, for a base change along a morphism assumed only representable by algebraic spaces rather than locally of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.IsRigSurjective.of_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQT.** If a composition of morphisms of formal algebraic spaces over `S` is
rig-surjective, then so is its second factor: a lift of an adic point of the final target to
the initial source is, after composition with the first factor, a lift to the intermediate
space.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsRigSurjective.of_comp (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X Y Z : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hgf : IsRigSurjective B S hS (f ≫ g)) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS g

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_of_isSurjective_of_isRepresentableEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQU.** A morphism of fppf sheaves over `S` which is representable by algebraic
spaces, étale and surjective is rig-surjective.

Let `p : Spf R ⟶ Y` be an adic morphism out of the formal spectrum of a complete discrete
valuation ring. The closed point of `Spf R` maps to a point of `Y`, which by surjectivity is
the image of a point of `X`; together they give a point of `Spf R ×_Y X`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_point_of_isPullbackULift`), and
`exists_lift_of_pointsULift_pullback_of_isRepresentableEtale` turns that point into the lift
the definition of rig-surjectivity asks for.

The source states this for locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces `X` and `Y`; neither
hypothesis is used, so neither is assumed. Nor is adicness of `p`: the lift exists for every
morphism out of the formal spectrum of a complete discrete valuation ring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_of_isRepresentableEtale_of_isSurjective'
declarations.doc:
A morphism of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces over `S` which is representable by
algebraic spaces, étale and surjective is rig-surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_of_isRepresentableEtale_of_isSurjective'
    {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hf : IsRepresentableEtale B S hS f) (hsurj : IsSurjective B S hS f) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_iff_forall_pullback_snd_of_isRepresentableEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQV.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of fppf sheaves over `S` which is locally of
finite type and let `{gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Y}` be a family of morphisms from formal algebraic spaces which
are representable by algebraic spaces and étale and which is jointly surjective on points (that
is, `∐ gᵢ` is surjective). Then `f` is rig-surjective if and only if each base change
`fᵢ : X ×_Y Yᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ` is rig-surjective.

This is `isRigSurjective_iff_forall_pullback_snd'` together with joint rig-surjectivity of the
family, which is the family form of Stacks 0AQU,
`isJointlyRigSurjective_of_isRepresentableEtale_of_isJointlySurjective`: the source's proof
applies Stacks 0AQU to `∐ gᵢ`, and that form avoids the coproduct by catching each adic point in
one member of the family.

The source states this for locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces `X`, `Y` and `Yᵢ`. The
proof uses that the `Yᵢ` are formal algebraic spaces and nothing more, so the locally Noetherian
hypotheses and the hypotheses on `X` and `Y` are omitted.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_iff_forall_pullback_snd_of_isRepresentableEtale (B : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) {I : Type v} {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (Yi : I → FppfSheaf B S hS) (g : ∀ i, Yi i ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (hYi : ∀ i, IsFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS (Yi i))
    (hg : ∀ i, IsRepresentableEtale B S hS (g i))
    (hcover : IsJointlySurjective B S hS Yi g) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS f ↔ ∀ i, IsRigSurjective B S hS (pullback.snd f (g i))
declarations.comment: for a morphism f : X ⟶ Y locally of finite type and a family of representable étale morphisms gᵢ : Yᵢ ⟶ Y from formal algebraic spaces with ∐ gᵢ surjective, f is rig-surjective if and only if every base change X ×_Y Yᵢ ⟶ Yᵢ is; the locally Noetherian hypotheses of the source are not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQW.** In the situation of Stacks 0GDB, let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a proper morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`, let `T` be a closed set of points of `X`, and let the restriction
`U' ⟶ U` of `f` to the open complements of `T` and of `T' = |f|⁻¹ T` be surjective. Then the
morphism of completions `f_{/T} : X'_{/T'} ⟶ X_{/T}` is rig-surjective.

An adic morphism `p : Spf R ⟶ X_{/T}` out of a complete discrete valuation ring `R` algebraizes
by Stacks 0GBU to a morphism `Spec R ⟶ X` whose fibre over `T` is the closed point, so its
generic point lies over `U`. The valuative step
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isExtension_lift_of_isProper_of_isSurjective` (Stacks 00PH,
0A40 and 0AP1) produces an extension `R ⊂ R'` of complete discrete valuation rings and a point
`Spec R' ⟶ X'` over `Spec R' ⟶ Spec R ⟶ X`. Restricted to `Spf R'` and paired with
`Spf R' ⟶ Spf R ⟶ X_{/T}`, it lands in `X'_{/T'}` because the completion square of Stacks 0APV
is cartesian, and this is the lift.

The source also assumes `X` locally Noetherian, so that `f_{/T}` is a morphism of locally
Noetherian formal algebraic spaces and the algebraization of Stacks 0GBU is available as stated;
neither use is needed here, and the statement is proved without that hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_completionSheafMap {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T) (hf : Space.IsProper B S hS f)
    (hsurj : Space.IsSurjective B S hS
      ((Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).fromPreimage f)) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_formalSpectrumMap
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I`, and let `C` be an
`I`-adically complete `A`-algebra. If `A/Iⁿ → C/IⁿC` is of finite type and flat for every `n`,
and faithfully flat for `n = 1`, then `Spf C → Spf A` is rig-surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_formalSpectrumMap
    {A C : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A] [IsLinearTopology A A]
    [TopologicalSpace C] [IsTopologicalRing C] [IsLinearTopology C C]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (hAadic : IsAdic I) (hAcomplete : IsAdicComplete I A)
    (hCadic : IsAdic (I.map (algebraMap A C)))
    (hCcomplete : IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)
    (hfinite : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ I ^ n) (C ⧸ (I ^ n).map (algebraMap A C)))
    (hflat : ∀ n : ℕ, Module.Flat (A ⧸ I ^ n) (C ⧸ (I ^ n).map (algebraMap A C)))
    (hfaithful : Module.FaithfullyFlat (A ⧸ I) (C ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A C)))
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (E : QuotientSystem B S hS C)
    (f : ContinuousHom D E) (hf : f.toRingHom = algebraMap A C) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS
      (formalSpectrumMap
        (TopologicalRing.isWeaklyAdmissible_of_isAdic hAadic hAcomplete) f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_formalSpectrumMap_iff_faithfullyFlat'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQY.** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal `I` whose
`I`-torsion vanishes, and let `C` be an `I`-adically complete `A`-algebra such that
`A/Iⁿ → C/IⁿC` is flat and of finite type for every `n`. Then `Spf C → Spf A` is rig-surjective
if and only if `A/I → C/IC` is faithfully flat.

Faithful flatness gives rig-surjectivity by Stacks 0AQX. Conversely, a closed point of
`Spec(A/I)` is a maximal ideal `I ⊆ 𝔪 ⊆ A`, and
`exists_isPrime_comap_eq_of_isRigSurjective'` contracts a prime of `C` onto it; so
`Spec(C/IC) → Spec(A/I)` meets every closed point, which for a flat map is faithful flatness
(Stacks 00HQ).
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_formalSpectrumMap_iff_faithfullyFlat' (I : Ideal A)
    (hAadic : IsAdic I) (hAcomplete : IsAdicComplete I A)
    (hCadic : IsAdic (I.map (algebraMap A C)))
    (hCcomplete : IsAdicComplete (I.map (algebraMap A C)) C)
    (hTorsion : Submodule.torsionBySet A A (I : Set A) = ⊥)
    (hfinite : ∀ n : ℕ, Algebra.FiniteType (A ⧸ I ^ n) (C ⧸ (I ^ n).map (algebraMap A C)))
    (hflat : ∀ n : ℕ, Module.Flat (A ⧸ I ^ n) (C ⧸ (I ^ n).map (algebraMap A C)))
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS A) (E : QuotientSystem B S hS C)
    (f : ContinuousHom D E) (hf : f.toRingHom = algebraMap A C) :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS
      (formalSpectrumMap
        (TopologicalRing.isWeaklyAdmissible_of_isAdic hAadic hAcomplete) f) ↔
      Module.FaithfullyFlat (A ⧸ I) (C ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A C))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.FractionalPowers.noAdicPoints_isRigSurjective_isDomain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AQZ.** Let `A = (⋃_{n ≥ 1} k[t^{1/n}])^∧` be the `t`-adic completion of the ring
of polynomials in the fractional powers of `t` over a field `k`, carrying its `t`-adic topology.
There are no adic morphisms `Spf R ⟶ Spf A` with `R` a complete discrete valuation ring; thus
every morphism `X ⟶ Spf A` is rig-surjective; and yet `A` is a domain and `t ∈ A` is not zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem noAdicPoints_isRigSurjective_isDomain [TopologicalSpace (Completion k)]
    (hA : _root_.IsAdic (Ideal.span {completionGenerator k}))
    (D : QuotientSystem B S hS (Completion k)) :
    (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [TopologicalSpace R],
      _root_.IsAdic (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) →
        IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R →
          ∀ (E : QuotientSystem B S hS R) (p : formalSpectrum E ⟶ formalSpectrum D),
            ¬ Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS p.hom) ∧
      (∀ {X : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ formalSpectrum D), IsRigSurjective B S hS f) ∧
      IsDomain (Completion k) ∧ completionGenerator k ≠ 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigSurjective_iff_factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AR0.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of formal algebraic
spaces over `S` with `X` and `Y` locally Noetherian, `f` locally of finite type and `f` a
monomorphism. Then `f` is rig-surjective if and only if every adic morphism `Spf R ⟶ Y`, with
`R` a complete discrete valuation ring, factors through `X`.

The forward implication uses that `X` and `Y` are fpqc sheaves, Stacks 0AQD,
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isSheaf_fpqc`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigSurjective_iff_factorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints {X Y : FppfSheaf B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hY : IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS Y)
    (hft : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f) [Mono f] :
    IsRigSurjective B S hS f ↔ FactorsAdicCompleteDvrPoints B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_completionSheafMap_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AR2.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`T ⊆ |X|` be closed, and let `U ⊆ X` be the open complement of `T` and `U' = f⁻¹U` (the
situation of Stacks 0GDB). If `X` is locally Noetherian, `f` is locally of finite type and
`U' → U` is étale, then the completion `f_{/T} : X'_{/T'} ⟶ X_{/T}` is rig-étale.

The proof is the source's: compatible étale atlases of `X` and `X'` by spectra of rings
(Properties of Spaces, Lemma 03FX; `exists_compatible_affineOver_atlases`), condition (4) of
Stacks 0GCZ for `f_{/T}` from them (`correspondsToRigEtaleMapAfterSourceCover_completionSheafMap`:
the reduction to the affine case and the affine case by part (1) of Stacks 0ALQ), and the
implication (4) ⟹ (1) of Stacks 0GCZ.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_completionSheafMap_of_isLocallyNoetherian
    {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X')
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X' ⟶ X) (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X))
    (hT : @IsClosed _ (Space.pointTopology B S hS X) T)
    (hXN : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X)
    (hf : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (het : Space.IsEtale B S hS (Space.openComplementRestriction B S hS f T)) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_completionSheafMap_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AR2.** Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `T ⊆ |X|`
be closed and let `U' ⟶ U` be the restriction of `f` to the open complements of `T' = |f|⁻¹T`
and `T`. If `X` is locally Noetherian, `f` is locally of finite type and `U' ⟶ U` is étale, then
`f_{/T} : X'_{/T'} ⟶ X_{/T}` is rig-étale.

The proof is the source's, through condition (4) of Stacks 0GCZ. Cover `X` by affine étale
charts `Spec A_k ⟶ X` (`exists_affine_etale_charts`) and each `Spec A_k ×_X X'` by affine étale
charts `Spec C_kl`; the completions `(Spec C_kl)_{/T}` cover `X'_{/T'}` (Stacks 0APV), each
factors through the chart `(Spec A_k)_{/T}` of `X_{/T}` by the completion of
`Spec C_kl ⟶ Spec A_k`, and that completion corresponds to a rig-étale map by the affine case
(`correspondsToRigEtaleMap_completionSheafMap_of_etaleAt`, which is part (1) of Stacks 0ALQ):
the chart map `Spec C_kl ⟶ Spec A_k` is locally of finite type, `A_k` is Noetherian, and the
chart map is étale over the complement of `T` because `U' ⟶ U` is.

No reduction to the affine case is assumed: the affine data that
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isRigEtale_completionSheafMap` takes as its hypothesis
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.ChartSquareReducesToIsEtaleOutside` is built here from the étale
charts of `X` and `X'`. That conditional form stays in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.CompletionRigEtale`, which this module imports
through `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.CompletionAlgebraicSpaceAtlas`, and it is
stated for arbitrary presheaves `X'`, `X` and an arbitrary set `T`, where the charts used here
need not exist.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRigEtale_completionSheafMap_of_isEtale {X' X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hXN : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) (hf : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS f)
    (het : Space.IsEtale B S hS (Space.openComplementRestriction B S hS f T)) :
    IsRigEtale B S hS (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS f T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_etale_completion_factorization
declarations.doc:
Let `X`, `X'`, `Y` be Noetherian affine schemes of the big fppf site over `S`, let `T ⊆ |X|`
be closed, let `f : X' ⟶ X` be locally of finite type and étale over `X ∖ T`, let `h : Y ⟶ X` be
a morphism and let `α : Y_{/T} ⟶ X'_{/T}` be a morphism over `X_{/T}`. Then there are an étale
morphism `b : Y' ⟶ Y` of affine schemes inducing an isomorphism `b_{/T} : Y'_{/T} ⟶ Y_{/T}` and
a morphism `a : Y' ⟶ X'` over `X` such that `α = a_{/T} ∘ b_{/T}⁻¹`.

Here `g_{/T}` is the completion along `T`, `Space.completionOverFunctor`, which sends `g : V ⟶ X`
to `V_{/g⁻¹T} ⟶ X_{/T}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_completion_factorization {X X' Y : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X)]
    [IsNoetherian ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X)]
    [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X')]
    [IsNoetherian ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X')]
    [IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y)]
    [IsNoetherian ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y)]
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS (yoneda.obj X))) (T_closed : IsClosed T)
    (f : X' ⟶ X) [LocallyOfFiniteType ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f)]
    (hf : ∀ p : Space.points B S hS (yoneda.obj X'),
      Space.pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj X') (yoneda.map f) p ∉ T →
        EtaleAt ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f) (Space.pointsToScheme B S hS X' p))
    (h : Y ⟶ X)
    (α : (Space.completionOverFunctor B S hS T).obj (Over.mk (yoneda.map h)) ⟶
      (Space.completionOverFunctor B S hS T).obj (Over.mk (yoneda.map f))) :
    ∃ (Y' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (_ : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Y'))
      (b : Y' ⟶ Y) (_ : Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map b))
      (a : Y' ⟶ X') (comm_ab : a ≫ f = b ≫ h)
      (_ : IsIso ((Space.completionOverFunctor B S hS T).map
        (Over.homMk (yoneda.map b) : Over.mk (yoneda.map b ≫ yoneda.map h) ⟶
          Over.mk (yoneda.map h)))),
      α = inv ((Space.completionOverFunctor B S hS T).map
          (Over.homMk (yoneda.map b) : Over.mk (yoneda.map b ≫ yoneda.map h) ⟶
            Over.mk (yoneda.map h))) ≫
        (Space.completionOverFunctor B S hS T).map
          (Over.homMk (yoneda.map a) (by simp only [Over.mk_hom, ← Functor.map_comp, comm_ab]) :
            Over.mk (yoneda.map b ≫ yoneda.map h) ⟶ Over.mk (yoneda.map f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_affine_algebraization_of_isRigEtale
declarations.doc:
Let `X = Spec R` be a Noetherian affine scheme over `S` in the big fppf
site, let `T ⊆ |X|` be closed, let `W` be a Noetherian affine formal algebraic space and let
`g : W ⟶ X_{/T}` be rig-étale. Then there are an affine scheme `X'` and a morphism
`f : X' ⟶ X` of finite type (locally of finite type and quasi-compact), étale at every point
lying over `X ∖ T`, and an isomorphism `X'_{/f⁻¹T} ≅ W` compatible with `f_{/T}` and `g`.
Moreover, if `g` is étale, that is representable by algebraic spaces and étale, then `f` is
étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_algebraization_of_isRigEtale
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (hR : B.Contains (Spec (.of R)))
    (s : Spec (.of R) ⟶ S)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS (yoneda.obj (affineOver B S hS hR s)))) (hT : IsClosed T)
    {W : FppfSheaf B S hS} (hWaff : IsAffineFormalAlgebraicSpace B S hS W)
    (hWnoeth : IsNoetherian B S hS W)
    (g : W ⟶ Space.completionSheaf B S hS (yoneda.obj (affineOver B S hS hR s)) T)
    (hg : IsRigEtale B S hS g) :
    ∃ (X' : BigFppfOver B S hS) (_ : IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X'))
      (f : X' ⟶ affineOver B S hS hR s)
      (e : Space.completionSheaf B S hS (yoneda.obj X')
          (Space.pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj X') (yoneda.map f) ⁻¹' T) ≅ W),
      LocallyOfFiniteType ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f) ∧
      QuasiCompact ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f) ∧
      (∀ p : Space.points B S hS (yoneda.obj X'),
        Space.pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj X') (yoneda.map f) p ∉ T →
          EtaleAt ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f) (Space.pointsToScheme B S hS X' p)) ∧
      e.hom ≫ g = Space.completionSheafMap B S hS (yoneda.map f) T ∧
      (IsRepresentableEtale B S hS g → Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isEtale_of_isEtale_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of the big fppf site over `S` which is locally of finite
type, let `X` be locally Noetherian, let `T` be a set of points of `X` and let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a
closed subscheme whose set of points is `T`. If `f` is étale at every point of `X'` outside
`|f|⁻¹ T` and the morphism of completions `f_{/T}` is étale, then `f` is étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtale_of_isEtale_completionSheafMap
    {X' X : BigFppfOver B S hS} (f : X' ⟶ X)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS (yoneda.obj X)))
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X)]
    (hiT : Set.range i = Space.pointsToScheme B S hS X '' T)
    (hf : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS (yoneda.map f))
    (haway : ∀ p : Space.points B S hS (yoneda.obj X'),
      Space.pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj X') (yoneda.map f) p ∉ T →
        AlgebraicGeometry.EtaleAt ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f)
          (Space.pointsToScheme B S hS X' p))
    (hetale : ∃ hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS (yoneda.map f) T).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun ⦃A C : Space.AlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS⦄ (g : A ⟶ C) ↦
          Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom)
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS (yoneda.map f) T).hom hrep) :
    Space.IsEtale B S hS (yoneda.map f)
declarations.comment: the étale clause: a morphism locally of finite type which is étale away from `T` and whose completion `f_{/T}` is étale is étale everywhere, by Tag 0A43 (`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleAt_of_etale_infinitesimalNeighbourhoods`) above the closed subscheme cut out by `T`. Stated for `f` locally of finite type over a locally Noetherian `X`, where the source has `f` of finite type over an affine Noetherian `X`. The existence clause of the tag is not stated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionModificationFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AR5.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S`, let `T ⊆ |X|` be
closed and let `U ⊂ X` be the open subspace with `|U| = |X| ∖ T`. Completion along `T` is a
functor from the morphisms `f : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces which are locally of finite type and
an isomorphism over `U` to the morphisms `g : W ⟶ X_{/T}` of formal algebraic spaces with `W`
locally Noetherian and `g` rig-étale.

The arrow map is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionOverFunctor`. The three conditions on the
value are proved: `X'_{/T'}` is a formal algebraic space by Stacks 0AIZ, it is locally Noetherian
by Stacks 0AQ1 (2) since `X'` is locally of finite type over the locally Noetherian `X`, and
`f_{/T}` is rig-étale by Stacks 0AR2 since `U' ⟶ U` is an isomorphism.

This is a new object and not a copy of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.completionFiniteTypeModificationFunctor`: that functor takes
three hypotheses (`h0AIZ`, `hnoeth`, `hred`), and this one needs none of them. When they are
given, the two functors are equal
(`completionFiniteTypeModificationFunctor_eq_completionModificationFunctor`).
declarations.statement:
def completionModificationFunctor {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T) (hXsp : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hX : Space.IsLocallyNoetherian B S hS X) :
    Space.FiniteTypeModification B S hS (Space.openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ) ⥤
      RigEtaleOverCompletion B S hS X T
declarations.comment: the completion functor under the source's hypotheses, X a locally Noetherian algebraic space and T closed; the three conditions placing f_{/T} in the right-hand category are proved by 0AIZ, 0AQ1 (2) and 0AR2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_factorization_of_openComplement_and_completion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AR6.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Z ⟶ Y` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
and let `T ⊆ |X|` be closed. Assume that `X` is locally Noetherian, that `g` is a monomorphism
and locally of finite type, that `f` restricted to the open complement of `T` factors through
`g`, and that `f` factors through `g` on the subfunctor of sections with point-set image in
`T`. Then `f` factors through `g`.

The last hypothesis is the factorization on the completion `X_{/T}` of Stacks 0AMC, stated on
the subfunctor whose sheafification that completion is by Stacks 0AIZ; see the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_of_openComplement_and_completion
    {X Y Z : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Z ⟶ Y)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hXnoeth : Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X
      (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    (hgmono : Mono g) (hgft : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS g)
    (hopen : ∃ v : ((Space.openSubspacesOrderIso B S hS X hX).symm
        ⟨Tᶜ, hT.isOpen_compl⟩).1.toFunctor ⟶ Z,
      v ≫ g = ((Space.openSubspacesOrderIso B S hS X hX).symm
        ⟨Tᶜ, hT.isOpen_compl⟩).1.ι ≫ f)
    (hcompletion : ∃ v : (Space.completionSubfunctor B S hS X T).toFunctor ⟶
        Z ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1},
      v ≫ Functor.whiskerRight g uliftFunctor.{u + 1} =
        (Space.completionSubfunctor B S hS X T).ι ≫
          Functor.whiskerRight f uliftFunctor.{u + 1}) :
    ∃ v : X ⟶ Z, v ≫ g = f
declarations.comment: the completion hypothesis is stated on the unsheafified subfunctor of sections with point-set image in `T` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.completionSubfunctor`), whose sheafification is the completion `X_{/T}` of Tag 0AMC by Tag 0AIZ, because the completion lands one universe above `Y` and so admits no morphism to `Y` in this library; no other hypothesis is carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.eq_of_eq_on_compl_of_completionSubfunctorMap_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AR7.** Let `X` and `Y` be locally Noetherian algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`T ⊆ |X|` and `T' ⊆ |Y|` be closed subsets and let `a, b : X ⟶ Y` be morphisms with
`|a| (T) ⊆ T'` and `|b| (T) ⊆ T'`. If `a` and `b` agree on the open subspace `X ∖ T` and the
induced morphisms of completions `a_{/T}, b_{/T} : X_{/T} ⟶ Y_{/T'}` agree, then `a = b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_of_eq_on_compl_of_completionSubfunctorMap_eq
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    (_hYnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    {T : Set (points B S hS X)} (hT : IsClosed T)
    {T' : Set (points B S hS Y)} (_hT' : IsClosed T')
    (a b : X ⟶ Y)
    (ha : pointsMap B S hS X a '' T ⊆ T') (hb : pointsMap B S hS X b '' T ⊆ T')
    (hcompl :
      (openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι ≫ a = (openSubspaceOfPoints B S hS X Tᶜ).ι ≫ b)
    (hcompletion : completionSubfunctorMap B S hS a T T' ha =
      completionSubfunctorMap B S hS b T T' hb) :
    a = b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_of_openComplement_and_completion
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over
`S`, let `T ⊆ |X|` be a closed subset and let `s, t : R ⟶ U` be two morphisms of algebraic
spaces over `X`. Assume

1. `R` and `U` are locally of finite type over `X`,
2. the base change of `s` and `t` to `X ∖ T` is an étale equivalence relation, and
3. the formal completion `(t_{/T}, s_{/T}) : R_{/T} ⟶ U_{/T} ×_{X_{/T}} U_{/T}` is an étale
   equivalence relation.

Then `(t, s) : R ⟶ U ×_X U` is an étale equivalence relation: it is a monomorphism, `t` and `s`
form an equivalence relation, and both are étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEtaleEquivalenceRelation_of_openComplement_and_completion
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hR : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS R)
    (hU : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U)
    (qR : R ⟶ X) (qU : U ⟶ X) (s t : R ⟶ U)
    (hs : s ≫ qU = qR) (ht : t ≫ qU = qR)
    (T : Set (Space.points B S hS X)) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hXnoeth : Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X
      (fun V : Scheme.{u} => _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian V))
    (hqR : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS qR)
    (hqU : Space.IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS qU)
    (hopen : IsEquivalenceRelation
      (Space.openSubspaceOfPointsRestrict B S hS t _ _
        (compl_subset_preimage_compl B S hS t qU qR ht T))
      (Space.openSubspaceOfPointsRestrict B S hS s _ _
        (compl_subset_preimage_compl B S hS s qU qR hs T)))
    (hopent : Space.IsEtale B S hS (Space.openSubspaceOfPointsRestrict B S hS t _ _
      (compl_subset_preimage_compl B S hS t qU qR ht T)))
    (hopens : Space.IsEtale B S hS (Space.openSubspaceOfPointsRestrict B S hS s _ _
      (compl_subset_preimage_compl B S hS s qU qR hs T)))
    (hcompletion : IsEquivalenceRelation
      (Space.completionSheafRestrict B S hS t _ _
        (preimage_subset_preimage_of_comp B S hS t qU qR ht T))
      (Space.completionSheafRestrict B S hS s _ _
        (preimage_subset_preimage_of_comp B S hS s qU qR hs T)))
    (hcomplt : ∃ hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS t (Space.pointsMap B S hS U qU ⁻¹' T)).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun ⦃A C : Space.AlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS⦄ (g : A ⟶ C) ↦
          Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom)
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS t (Space.pointsMap B S hS U qU ⁻¹' T)).hom hrep)
    (hcompls : ∃ hrep : Space.IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS s (Space.pointsMap B S hS U qU ⁻¹' T)).hom,
      Space.HasPropertyULift.{u + 1} B S hS
        (fun ⦃A C : Space.AlgebraicSpacesULift.{u + 1} B S hS⦄ (g : A ⟶ C) ↦
          Space.IsEtaleULift.{u + 1} B S hS g.hom)
        (Space.completionSheafMap B S hS s (Space.pointsMap B S hS U qU ⁻¹' T)).hom hrep) :
    Mono (relationMap B S hS qU s t (ht.trans hs.symm)) ∧ IsEquivalenceRelation t s ∧
      Space.IsEtale B S hS s ∧ Space.IsEtale B S hS t
declarations.comment: WHAT IS FORMALIZED: hypothesis (3) is read as saying that the formal completion `(t_{/T}, s_{/T})` is an *étale* equivalence relation — an equivalence relation whose two maps `s_{/T}` and `t_{/T}` are étale — and not merely an equivalence relation. THE LITERAL READING OF (3) IS FALSE: take `X = Spec k` and `T = |X|`, so that `X ∖ T` is empty and (2) is vacuous, and `U = 𝔸¹`, `R = U ×_X U`, `t = pr₀`, `s = pr₁`; then `X_{/T} = X`, `U_{/T} = U`, `R_{/T} = R`, so (3) says that the identity is an equivalence relation, (1) and (2) hold, and yet `s = pr₁ : 𝔸¹ × 𝔸¹ ⟶ 𝔸¹` is not étale, so the conclusion fails. THE ÉTALE READING IS THE ONE THE SOURCE'S OWN PROOF USES: "Since the formal completions of the maps `s`, `t` are étale, we see that `s` and `t` are étale for example by More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.12.3". Otherwise the statement is the tag's: hypothesis (2) is read as the restrictions of `s` and `t` to the subspaces cut out by the complements of the inverse images of `T`, which is the base change to `X ∖ T` by `AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.isPullback_ι_openSubspaceOfPoints_compl`, and (3) as the restriction morphisms of the completions of Tag 0AMC along those inverse images. No further hypothesis is added and no part of the conclusion is dropped: the conclusion carries monomorphy of `(t, s)`, the equivalence-relation structure, and étaleness of both `s` and `t`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FormalSpace.exists_factorization_isIso_completionSheafMap
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `T ⊆ |X|` be closed with open
complement `U = X ∖ T`, and let `f : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally
