registrations.comment: part (1), injectivity

registrations.name: TopologicalRing.exact_completionSubtype_completionQuotient
registrations.comment: part (1), exactness at the middle term

registrations.name: TopologicalRing.range_completionSubtype_eq_closure
registrations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFiniteTypeModification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AS2.** An algebraic space over `W`, locally of finite type over `W` and
unchanged over `W₀`.
declarations.statement:
def IsFiniteTypeModification {W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (W₀ : Subfunctor W)
    (X : Over W) : Prop
declarations.comment: the three defining conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.FiniteTypeModification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AS2.** The category of algebraic spaces over `W` which are locally of finite
type over `W` and isomorphisms over `W₀`.
declarations.statement: abbrev FiniteTypeModification {W : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (W₀ : Subfunctor W)
declarations.comment: the category they form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeModification_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AS2.** The three conditions of Stacks 0AS2: the source is an algebraic space,
the structure morphism is locally of finite type, and its base change to `W₀` is an
isomorphism. The tag is the set-builder expression delimiting the morphisms that satisfy
exactly these three conditions, so this equivalence is the whole of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeModification_iff :
    IsFiniteTypeModification B S hS W₀ X ↔
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X.left ∧ IsLocallyOfFiniteType B S hS X.hom ∧
        IsIso (pullback.snd X.hom W₀.ι)

declarations.name: valuationRing_directLimit
declarations.doc:
A filtered direct limit of valuation rings is a valuation ring: if `(G i, f i j)`
is a directed system of commutative rings over a directed index set in which every
`G i` is an integral domain and a valuation ring, then the colimit
`Ring.DirectLimit G f` is an integral domain and a valuation ring.

The conclusion is phrased as an existential over an `IsDomain` instance together with
`ValuationRing`, because `ValuationRing` is a typeclass whose statement presupposes
`[IsDomain _]`, and Mathlib does not automatically derive `IsDomain` for the colimit.
declarations.statement:
theorem valuationRing_directLimit
    {ι : Type*} [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (G : ι → Type*) [∀ i, CommRing (G i)] [∀ i, IsDomain (G i)]
    (f : (i j : ι) → i ≤ j → G i →+* G j)
    [DirectedSystem G fun i j h => f i j h]
    [∀ i, ValuationRing (G i)] :
    ∃ _ : IsDomain (Ring.DirectLimit G fun i j h => f i j h),
      ValuationRing (Ring.DirectLimit G fun i j h => f i j h)

declarations.name: Module.Flat.rTensor_injective_iff_injective_mapQ_smul_top
declarations.doc:
Let `f : M →ₗ[R] M'` be a map of `R`-modules with `M'` flat. Then `f` is universally
injective, that is `f ⊗ id_Q` is injective for every `R`-module `Q`, if and only if the induced
map `M/IM → M'/IM'` is injective for every finitely generated ideal `I ⊆ R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.rTensor_injective_iff_injective_mapQ_smul_top {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    [Small.{v} R] {M M' : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M']
    [Module.Flat R M'] (f : M →ₗ[R] M') :
    (∀ (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q], Function.Injective (f.rTensor Q)) ↔
      ∀ ⦃I : Ideal R⦄, I.FG →
        Function.Injective ((I • ⊤ : Submodule R M).mapQ (I • ⊤ : Submodule R M') f
          (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top I f))
declarations.comment:
`M/IM` is `M ⧸ I • ⊤` and the induced map is `Submodule.mapQ` along `f`; the
left-hand side spells out universal injectivity, which `Mathlib` has no name for.

declarations.name: Submodule.exists_fg_isLeast_mem_range_rTensor_subtype_of_mittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `M` be a flat Mittag-Leffler `R`-module, let `F` be an
`R`-module and let `x ∈ F ⊗[R] M`. Then among the submodules `N ⊆ F` with `x ∈ N ⊗[R] M` — that is,
with `x` in the range of `N ⊗[R] M → F ⊗[R] M` — there is a smallest one, and it is a finite
`R`-module.

Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of Proposition 059E: every map
`f : P → M` from a finitely presented `R`-module dominates and is dominated by a map `g : P → Q`
into a finitely presented `R`-module, that is `Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every
`R`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Submodule.exists_fg_isLeast_mem_range_rTensor_subtype_of_mittagLeffler
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Flat R M]
    (hML : ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
      (f : P →ₗ[R] M), ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q)
        (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q) (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N]
          [Module R N], LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N))
    {F : Type v} [AddCommGroup F] [Module R F] (x : F ⊗[R] M) :
    ∃ F' : Submodule R F, F'.FG ∧
      IsLeast {N : Submodule R F | x ∈ LinearMap.range (N.subtype.rTensor M)} F'

declarations.name: ModuleCat.mittagLeffler_pt_of_forall_mittagLeffler_of_forall_rTensor_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AS7.** Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `F : J ⥤ ModuleCat R` be a directed system
`(M i, f i j)` of `R`-modules over a nonempty directed preorder `J`, and let `c` be a colimit
cocone on `F`, so that `M = c.pt` is `colim_{i ∈ J} M i`. Assume every transition map is
universally injective, that is `f i j ⊗ id_T` is injective for every `R`-module `T`, and that every
`M i` is Mittag-Leffler. Then `M` is Mittag-Leffler. Being Mittag-Leffler is spelled out in the
intrinsic form 059E (1): every map `f : P → M` from a finitely presented module dominates and is
dominated by a map `g : P → Q` into a finitely presented module, domination meaning
`Ker(f ⊗ id_N) = Ker(g ⊗ id_N)` for every `R`-module `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ModuleCat.mittagLeffler_pt_of_forall_mittagLeffler_of_forall_rTensor_injective
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Small.{v} R] {J : Type w} [Preorder J] [IsDirectedOrder J]
    [Nonempty J] {F : J ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R}
    (hinj : ∀ ⦃i j : J⦄ (u : i ⟶ j) (T : Type v) [AddCommGroup T] [Module R T],
      Function.Injective ((F.map u).hom.rTensor T))
    (hML : ∀ i : J, ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
        [Module.FinitePresentation R P] (f : P →ₗ[R] F.obj i),
      ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q) (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q)
        (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
          LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N))
    {c : Cocone F} (hc : IsColimit c) :
    ∀ (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module.FinitePresentation R P]
        (f : P →ₗ[R] c.pt),
      ∃ (Q : Type v) (_ : AddCommGroup Q) (_ : Module R Q) (_ : Module.FinitePresentation R Q)
        (g : P →ₗ[R] Q), ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N],
          LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor N) = LinearMap.ker (g.rTensor N)
declarations.comment:
Mittag-Leffler is spelled out inline as condition (1) of 059E, as in 059M and 059N;
the directed system is a functor with a colimit cocone, as in 059E and 059W; universal injectivity
of `f i j` is injectivity of `(F.map u).hom.rTensor T` for every `T`, as in 058K (1). See the
module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.flat_quotient_pow_succ_of_flat_quotient_of_exact
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal and `M` an `R`-module. If `M/IM` is flat over `R/I` and the
multiplication map `M ⊗_R I^n/I^{n+1} → I^nM/I^{n+1}M` is injective for `n = 1, …, k`, then
`M/I^{k+1}M` is flat over `R/I^{k+1}`.

The injectivity of `M ⊗_R I^n/I^{n+1} → I^nM/I^{n+1}M` is spelled as the exactness of
`M ⊗_R I^{n+1} → M ⊗_R I^n → M/I^{n+1}M`, the first map being `lTensor M` of the inclusion
`I^{n+1} ⊆ I^n` and the second `m ⊗ x ↦ x • m` followed by the quotient map; see the module
docstring for why this is the same condition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_quotient_pow_succ_of_flat_quotient_of_exact {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (k : ℕ)
    (hflat : Module.Flat (R ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • (⊤ : Submodule R M))))
    (hexact : ∀ n, 1 ≤ n → n ≤ k →
      Function.Exact
        ((Submodule.inclusion (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right n.le_succ : I ^ (n + 1) ≤ I ^ n)).lTensor M)
        ((I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)).mkQ ∘ₗ
          (TensorProduct.rid R M).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (I ^ n).subtype.lTensor M)) :
    Module.Flat (R ⧸ I ^ (k + 1)) (M ⧸ (I ^ (k + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule R M)))
declarations.comment:
Both parts: part (1) is the case `k = 1`. The injectivity of
`M ⊗_R I^n/I^{n + 1} → I^nM/I^{n + 1}M` is stated as exactness of
`M ⊗_R I^{n + 1} → M ⊗_R I^n → M/I^{n + 1}M`, an equivalent form; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsContentIdeal
declarations.doc:
`I₀` is a *content ideal* of `x`: it is the least element of `S_x` under inclusion,
i.e. `x ∈ I₀ M` and any ideal `I` with `x ∈ I M` contains `I₀`. Here the submodule `I M`
of `M` is spelled `I • (⊤ : Submodule A M)`.

Flatness of `M` is not needed to state this, so the predicate is given for an arbitrary
module; for a flat module it is exactly the source's definition.
declarations.statement: def IsContentIdeal (x : M) (I₀ : Ideal A) : Prop

declarations.name: contentIdeal_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0ASB.** If a content ideal `I₀` of `x` exists, then `I₀` is finitely
generated.

The source states this for a flat module `M`, but flatness is never used: the content ideal is
by definition the least ideal `I` with `x ∈ I M`, and `x ∈ I₀ M` already exhibits `x` inside
`J M` for some finitely generated `J ≤ I₀`, whence `J = I₀` by minimality. The hypothesis is
therefore dropped, which only strengthens the statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem contentIdeal_fg {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (x : M) (I₀ : Ideal A) (h : IsContentIdeal x I₀) :
    I₀.FG

declarations.name: isContentIdeal_map_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0ASC.** A map between flat modules over a local ring which is injective modulo
the maximal ideal preserves content ideals of elements.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContentIdeal_map_of_injective_mapQ_maximalIdeal
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    {M N : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Flat A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module.Flat A N]
    (u : M →ₗ[A] N)
    (hu : Function.Injective
      (Submodule.mapQ (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A M))
        (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A N)) u
        (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top (maximalIdeal A) u)))
    {x : M} {I : Ideal A} (hx : IsContentIdeal x I) :
    IsContentIdeal (u x) I

declarations.name: exists_isContentIdeal_of_flat_isMittagLeffler
declarations.doc: **Stacks Tag 0ASD.** Every element of a flat Mittag-Leffler module has a content ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isContentIdeal_of_flat_isMittagLeffler
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    [Module.Flat A M]
    (hM : IsMittagLeffler.{u, max u v, v, max u v, max u v} A M) (x : M) :
    ∃ I : Ideal A, IsContentIdeal x I

declarations.name: nilradical_map_eq_henselization_and_strictHenselization
declarations.doc:
The nilradical of a henselization or strict henselization of a local ring is the extension
of the nilradical of the base ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nilradical_map_eq_henselization_and_strictHenselization
    (R Rh Rsh : Type u) [CommRing R] [CommRing Rh] [CommRing Rsh]
    [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rsh]
    [Algebra R Rh] [Algebra R Rsh]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization R (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) Rh]
    (κsep : Type v) [Field κsep] [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization R κsep Rsh] :
    Ideal.map (algebraMap R Rh) (nilradical R) = nilradical Rh ∧
      Ideal.map (algebraMap R Rsh) (nilradical R) = nilradical Rsh

declarations.name: ValuationRing.IsExtension
declarations.doc: An extension of valuation rings is an injective local ring homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
def IsExtension {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [ValuationRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) : Prop
declarations.comment: extension of valuation rings

declarations.name: ValuationRing.valueGroupMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical homomorphism `Γ_A → Γ_B` induced by an extension of valuation
rings. Here `K` and `L` are arbitrary fraction fields of `A` and `B`, respectively.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def valueGroupMap {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {K : Type w} {L : Type x}
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [ValuationRing B]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing B L]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : IsExtension f) :
    (ValueGroup A K)ˣ →* (ValueGroup B L)ˣ
declarations.comment: map on value groups

declarations.name: ValuationRing.IsWeaklyUnramified
declarations.doc:
An extension of valuation rings is weakly unramified when its canonical map on value
groups is bijective.
declarations.statement:
def IsWeaklyUnramified {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [ValuationRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : IsExtension f) : Prop
declarations.comment: weakly unramified

declarations.name: ValuationRing.residueDegree
declarations.doc:
The residue degree of an extension of valuation rings, namely `[κ_B : κ_A]` for the
residue-field map induced by the local homomorphism, and zero when that extension is infinite.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def residueDegree {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [ValuationRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : IsExtension f) : ℕ
declarations.comment: residue degree

declarations.name: ValuationRing.valueGroupMap_valuation
declarations.doc:
The canonical map on value groups sends the valuation class of every nonzero element of
the smaller valuation ring to the valuation class of its image. This is the commutative square
in the definition of an extension of valuation rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem valueGroupMap_valuation {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {K : Type w} {L : Type x}
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [ValuationRing B]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing B L]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : IsExtension f) (a : A) (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    ((valueGroupMap (K := K) (L := L) f hf)
      (Units.mk0 ((valuation A K) (algebraMap A K a)) (by simp [ha])) :
        ValueGroup B L) =
      (valuation B L) (algebraMap B L (f a))
declarations.comment: commutative value-group diagram

declarations.name: ext_valuation_rings_degree_ineq
declarations.doc:
Let `A ⊆ B` be an extension of valuation rings with fraction fields `K ⊆ L`, and assume the
field extension `L/K` is finite. Then:

1. the residue field extension `κ_A ⊆ κ_B` is finite (`Module.Finite`, i.e.
   `[κ_B : κ_A] < ∞`);
2. the value group `Γ_A` has finite index in `Γ_B`
   (`(valueGroupHom B K L).range.index ≠ 0`, i.e. `[Γ_B : Γ_A] < ∞`); and
3. `[Γ_B : Γ_A] · [κ_B : κ_A] ≤ [L : K]`.

The residue field degree `[κ_B : κ_A]` is computed with respect to the algebra structure on
`κ_B` over `κ_A` induced by Mathlib's `IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (algebraMap A B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ext_valuation_rings_degree_ineq
    (A B K L : Type*)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A] [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [ValuationRing B] [Field L] [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing B L]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hfin : Module.Finite K L) :
    letI : Algebra (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B) :=
      (ResidueField.map (algebraMap A B)).toAlgebra
    Module.Finite (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B) ∧
    (valueGroupHom B K L).range.index ≠ 0 ∧
    (valueGroupHom B K L).range.index * Module.finrank (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B)
      ≤ Module.finrank K L

declarations.name: ValuationRing.exists_eq_unit_mul_pow_of_flat_local
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local normal domains. Suppose every
height-one prime of `A` has a weakly unramified height-one prime of `B` lying over it. If an
element of `A` becomes an `n`th power times a unit in `B`, for `n > 1`, then it is already an
`n`th power times a unit in `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eq_unit_mul_pow_of_flat_local
    (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing B] [IsIntegrallyClosed B]
    [Algebra A B] [Module.Flat A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) (f : A) (h : B) (w : Bˣ)
    (hfh : algebraMap A B f = (w : B) * h ^ n)
    (hunramified : ∀ (p : Ideal A) (hp : p.IsPrime), p.height = 1 →
      ∃ (q : Ideal B) (hq : q.IsPrime), q.height = 1 ∧
        ∃ hlo : q.LiesOver p,
          (letI : p.IsPrime := hp
           letI : q.IsPrime := hq
           letI : q.LiesOver p := hlo
           letI : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime p) (Localization.AtPrime q) :=
             Localization.AtPrime.algebraOfLiesOver p q
           (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q)).ramificationIdx
             (Localization.AtPrime p) = 1)) :
    ∃ (g : A) (u : Aˣ), f = (u : A) * g ^ n

declarations.name: ValuationRing.isWeaklyUnramified_localization_atPrime_of_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0ASJ.** If `A` is a valuation ring, `A → B` is étale, and `m` is a
prime of `B` lying over the maximal ideal of `A`, then the canonical map from `A` to `Bₘ` is
a weakly unramified extension of valuation rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyUnramified_localization_atPrime_of_etale
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
    (m : Ideal B) [m.IsPrime] (hm : m.LiesOver (maximalIdeal A)) :
    ∃ (_ : IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime m))
      (_ : ValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime m))
      (h : IsExtension
        (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime m))),
      IsWeaklyUnramified (algebraMap A (Localization.AtPrime m)) h

declarations.name: ValuationRing.isWeaklyUnramified_henselization_and_strictHenselization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0ASK.** The henselization and strict henselization of a valuation ring are
valuation rings, and both canonical inclusions induce bijections on value groups.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeaklyUnramified_henselization_and_strictHenselization
    (A Ah Ash : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing Ah] [IsLocalRing Ah] [Algebra A Ah]
    [IsHenselization A (ResidueField A) Ah]
    (ksep : Type v) [Field ksep] [Algebra (ResidueField A) ksep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField A) ksep]
    [CommRing Ash] [IsLocalRing Ash] [Algebra A Ash] [Algebra Ah Ash]
    [IsScalarTower A Ah Ash] [IsHenselization A ksep Ash]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Ah Ash)] :
    ∃ (_ : IsDomain Ah) (_ : ValuationRing Ah)
      (_ : IsDomain Ash) (_ : ValuationRing Ash)
      (hAh : IsExtension (algebraMap A Ah))
      (hAsh : IsExtension (algebraMap Ah Ash)),
      IsWeaklyUnramified (algebraMap A Ah) hAh ∧
        IsWeaklyUnramified (algebraMap Ah Ash) hAsh

declarations.name: summand_sum_cyclic_iff_lifting
declarations.doc:
For a commutative ring `R` and an `R`-module `P`, `P` is a direct summand of a direct sum of
modules `R / f R` if and only if every linear map from `P` lifts along every short exact sequence
`0 → A → B → C → 0` satisfying `f A = A ∩ f B` for all `f ∈ R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem summand_sum_cyclic_iff_lifting
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] :
    IsSummandOfSumCyclic R P ↔ LiftingProperty R P

declarations.name: generalizedValuationRing_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a nonzero commutative ring, total divisibility, being a local Bézout ring, and total
inclusion of ideals are equivalent. In particular, all three properties hold for a valuation
ring.

declarations.name: finitePresentation_equiv_directSum_quotient_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
Every finitely presented module over a local Bézout ring is isomorphic to a finite direct
sum of quotients by principal ideals.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_equiv_directSum_quotient_span_singleton
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsBezout R] [IsLocalRing R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.FinitePresentation R M] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R),
      Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] ⨁ i : Fin n, R ⧸ Ideal.span {f i})

declarations.name: finitePresentation_summand_fin_directSum_quotient_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
Every finitely presented module over a commutative ring whose localizations at maximal ideals
are Bézout rings is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of quotients by principal ideals.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_summand_fin_directSum_quotient_span_singleton
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (hR : ∀ (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal], IsBezout (Localization.AtPrime m))
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.FinitePresentation R M] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R)
      (i : M →ₗ[R] ⨁ j, R ⧸ Ideal.span {f j})
      (p : (⨁ j, R ⧸ Ideal.span {f j}) →ₗ[R] M),
      p.comp i = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: IsElementaryDivisorDomain
declarations.doc:
`R` is an *elementary divisor domain* if for all `n, m ≥ 1` and every
`n × m` matrix `A` there exist invertible matrices `U` (size `n`) and `V`
(size `m`) such that `U * A * V` is in Smith normal form.
declarations.statement: class IsElementaryDivisorDomain (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop
declarations.comment:
(2) An elementary divisor domain: every rectangular matrix with at least one row and one
  column can be brought into Smith normal form by invertible row and column operations.

registrations.name: IsBezout
registrations.comment: (1) A Bézout domain: every finitely generated ideal is principal.

declarations.name: isBezout_of_isElementaryDivisorDomain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ASS**.
Every elementary divisor domain is a Bézout ring: if `R` is an elementary divisor
domain, then every finitely generated ideal of `R` is principal (`IsBezout R`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isBezout_of_isElementaryDivisorDomain {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsElementaryDivisorDomain R] : IsBezout R

declarations.name: isBezout_localization_and_valuationRing_atPrime_and_iff
declarations.doc:
Localizations of a Bézout domain are Bézout, its local rings are valuation rings, and an
arbitrary local domain is Bézout if and only if it is a valuation ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBezout_localization_and_valuationRing_atPrime_and_iff
    {R Rₘ A : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsBezout R]
    (M : Submonoid R) [CommRing Rₘ] [Algebra R Rₘ] [IsLocalization M Rₘ]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsLocalRing A] :
    IsBezout Rₘ ∧
      ValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧
      (IsBezout A ↔ ValuationRing A)

declarations.name: finite_submodule_free_and_finitePresentation_split_torsion
declarations.doc:
Over a Bézout domain, finite submodules of free modules are free. Every finitely presented
module splits as the direct sum of its finite free torsion quotient and its torsion submodule,
which is itself a summand of a finite direct sum of quotients by nonzero principal ideals.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_submodule_free_and_finitePresentation_split_torsion
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsBezout R] :
    (∀ (F : Type v) [AddCommGroup F] [Module R F] [Module.Free R F]
      (N : Submodule R F) [Module.Finite R N], Module.Free R N) ∧
    (∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.FinitePresentation R M],
      Module.Finite R (M ⧸ Submodule.torsion R M) ∧
      Module.Free R (M ⧸ Submodule.torsion R M) ∧
      Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] (M ⧸ Submodule.torsion R M) × Submodule.torsion R M) ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R),
        (∀ j, f j ≠ 0) ∧
        ∃ (i : Submodule.torsion R M →ₗ[R] ⨁ j, R ⧸ Ideal.span {f j})
          (p : (⨁ j, R ⧸ Ideal.span {f j}) →ₗ[R] Submodule.torsion R M),
          p.comp i = LinearMap.id)

declarations.name: finite_equiv_free_prod_directSum_quotient_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ASV**.
Every finite module over a principal ideal domain is isomorphic to the direct sum of a
finite-rank free module and finitely many cyclic modules defined by nonzero elements.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_equiv_free_prod_directSum_quotient_span_singleton
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsPrincipalIdealRing R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    ∃ (r n : ℕ) (f : Fin n → R),
      (∀ i, f i ≠ 0) ∧
        Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[R] (Fin r →₀ R) × ⨁ i : Fin n, R ⧸ Ideal.span {f i})

declarations.name: bezout_unimodular_completion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ASW**.
Over a Bézout domain `R`, any row `f : Fin n → R` whose entries generate the unit ideal is the
first row of some invertible `n × n` matrix over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bezout_unimodular_completion {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsBezout R] [IsDomain R]
    {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (f : Fin n → R)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) :
    ∃ M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R, IsUnit M.det ∧ ∀ j : Fin n, M 0 j = f j

declarations.name: IsContentIdeal.isPrincipal_of_valuationRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0ASX**, the principality assertion. A content ideal of an element of a module
over a valuation ring is a principal ideal.

The source states this for a finite module over an essentially finite type local algebra which
is flat over the valuation ring, but, as its proof shows, none of that is used: a content ideal
is finitely generated by Stacks 0ASB, and in a valuation ring every finitely generated ideal is
principal by Stacks 090Q. Flatness of the module is not needed either, for the same reason it is
not needed in Stacks 0ASB. Dropping the hypotheses only strengthens the statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsContentIdeal.isPrincipal_of_valuationRing
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    {x : N} {I : Ideal A} (hI : IsContentIdeal x I) : I.IsPrincipal
declarations.comment:
the principality assertion, unconditionally and in strengthened form: no
hypothesis beyond `ValuationRing A` is used, since a content ideal is finitely generated
(0ASB) and a valuation ring is Bézout (090Q).

declarations.name: exists_isContentIdeal_isPrincipal_of_valuationRing_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0ASX.** Let `A → B` be a local ring map of local rings which is essentially of
finite type, and let `N` be a finite `B`-module which is flat as an `A`-module. If `A` is a
valuation ring, then every element `x` of `N` has a content ideal `I ⊆ A` in the sense of
Stacks 0ASA, and that ideal is principal.

Existence is `exists_isContentIdeal_of_valuationRing` and principality is
`IsContentIdeal.isPrincipal_of_valuationRing`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isContentIdeal_isPrincipal_of_valuationRing_of_flat
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {N : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType A B]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower A B N]
    [Module.Finite B N] [Module.Flat A N]
    (x : N) :
    ∃ I : Ideal A, IsContentIdeal x I ∧ I.IsPrincipal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_flat_stratification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ASY.**

For a morphism of finite presentation `f : X ⟶ S` between quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes
and a finitely presented `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, the base carries a finite ascending chain of
quasi-coherent ideal sheaves of finite type whose first closed subscheme is a thickening of `S`
and whose last closed subscheme is empty, such that the pullback of `ℱ` to the fibre product of
`X` with each locally closed stratum is flat over that stratum.

The general case is reduced to the Noetherian case
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_flat_stratification_of_isNoetherian`; see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_flat_stratification {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S]
    (hf : FinitePresentation f) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (I : Fin (t + 1) → S.IdealSheafData),
      Stacks.Thickenings.IsThickening (I 0).subschemeι ∧
      (∀ i, Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsFiniteType (I i)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin t, I (Fin.castSucc i) ≤ I (Fin.succ i)) ∧
      I (Fin.last t) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i : Fin t,
        let Z := I (Fin.castSucc i)
        let V : S.Opens := (I (Fin.succ i)).support.compl
        let U : Z.subscheme.Opens := Z.subschemeι ⁻¹ᵁ V
        let g : U.toScheme ⟶ S := U.ι ≫ Z.subschemeι
        IsFlatOver (pullback.snd f g).toLRSHom.toShHom
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injectiveModuloMaximalIdealConclusion_of_henselianLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AT3.** In Situation 0AT0 with `A` henselian the lemma holds: if
`A → B` is a local homomorphism of local rings essentially of finite type, `M` is a flat
`A`-module, `N` is a finite `B`-module and `u : N → M` is an `A`-linear map whose reduction
`N/𝔪_A N → M/𝔪_A M` is injective, then `u` is `A`-universally injective, `N` is of finite
presentation over `B`, and `N` is flat over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem injectiveModuloMaximalIdealConclusion_of_henselianLocalRing
    (S : InjectiveModuloMaximalIdealSituation.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄}) [HenselianLocalRing S.A] :
    InjectiveModuloMaximalIdealConclusion.{u₅} S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyInjective_and_finitePresentation_and_flat_of_linearMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AT4.** Let `A → B` be a local homomorphism of local rings which is
essentially of finite type and let `u : N → M` be a `B`-linear map. If `N` is a finite
`B`-module, `M` is flat over `A`, and the induced map `N/𝔪_A N → M/𝔪_A M` is injective, then
`u` is universally injective over `A`, `N` is finitely presented over `B`, and `N` is flat over
`A`.

This is `HenselizationReduction.conclusions_of_henselian_cases` applied to the henselian case
Stacks 0AT3, `injectiveModuloMaximalIdealConclusion_of_henselianLocalRing`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_and_finitePresentation_and_flat_of_linearMap
    {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} {M : Type u₃} {N : Type u₄}
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [Algebra.EssFiniteType A B]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M] [Module.Flat A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower A B N] [Module.Finite B N]
    (u : N →ₗ[B] M)
    (hu : Function.Injective (Submodule.mapQ (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A N))
      (maximalIdeal A • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) (u.restrictScalars A)
      (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top (maximalIdeal A) (u.restrictScalars A)))) :
    UniversallyInjectivePoly.{_, w} (u.restrictScalars A) ∧ Module.FinitePresentation B N ∧
      Module.Flat A N
declarations.comment:
`N/𝔪_A N → M/𝔪_A M` is the `Submodule.mapQ` of `u` for `𝔪_A • ⊤`, and
`A`-universal injectivity is `UniversallyInjectivePoly` of `u` with scalars restricted to `A`.

declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AT6.** The standing situation of a finitely presented algebra `B`
over `A`, a multiplicative subset `S ⊆ B`, and a finitely presented module over a
localization of `B` at `S`.
declarations.statement: structure FinitelyPresentedLocalizedModuleSituation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isContentIdeal_of_pureSpreadout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AT7.** If a pure spreadout exists, every element of the localized
module has a content ideal over the base ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isContentIdeal_of_pureSpreadout
    (X : FinitelyPresentedLocalizedModuleSituation.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄})
    (hspread : Nonempty (PureSpreadout.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄, u₁} X)) (x : X.N) :
    ∃ I : Ideal X.A, IsContentIdeal x I
declarations.comment: content_ideals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyInjective_of_injective_mod_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AT7 (universal injectivity).** A map into a flat
module which is injective modulo each maximal ideal is universally injective,
provided the distinguished localized module admits a pure spreadout.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_of_injective_mod_maximalIdeal
    (X : FinitelyPresentedLocalizedModuleSituation.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄})
    (hspread : Nonempty (PureSpreadout.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄, u₄} X))
    {M : Type u₄} [AddCommGroup M] [Module X.A M] [Module.Flat X.A M]
    (u : X.N →ₗ[X.A] M)
    (hu : ∀ (m : Ideal X.A) [m.IsMaximal],
      Function.Injective
        (Submodule.mapQ (m • (⊤ : Submodule X.A X.N))
          (m • (⊤ : Submodule X.A M)) u
          (Submodule.smul_top_le_comap_smul_top m u))) :
    UniversallyInjective u
declarations.comment: universal_injectivity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.FinitelyPresentedLocalizedModuleSituation.exists_fg_ideal_localQuotientBaseChange_pureSpreadout
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AT8.** In the standing situation of Stacks 0AT6, for every prime `𝔭` of
the base ring there is a finitely generated ideal `I` of the local ring `A_𝔭`, contained in the
extension of `𝔭`, such that the base change of the situation to `A_𝔭 ⧸ I` carries a pure spreadout.

The test-module universe of the universal injectivity packaged in the pure spreadout is left free,
so the statement instantiates at any test universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fg_ideal_localQuotientBaseChange_pureSpreadout (p : Ideal X.A) [p.IsPrime] :
    ∃ I : Ideal (Localization.AtPrime p), I.FG ∧
      I ≤ p.map (algebraMap X.A (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∧
      ∃ Y : FinitelyPresentedLocalizedModuleSituation.{u₁, max u₁ u₂, max u₁ u₃,
          max u₁ (max u₃ u₄)},
        Nonempty (LocalQuotientBaseChange X Y p I) ∧
          Nonempty (PureSpreadout.{u₁, max u₁ u₂, max u₁ u₃, max u₁ (max u₃ u₄), u₅} Y)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyInjective_of_rTensor_residueField_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AT9**, unconditionally. In the finitely presented localized-module
situation, a linear map between flat modules which is injective on every residue-field fibre is
universally injective.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.universallyInjective_of_rTensor_residueField_injective_of_pureSpreadout`
with its `hAT8` hypothesis discharged by Stacks 0AT8, instantiated at the test-module universe that
binder pins.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_of_rTensor_residueField_injective
    (X : FinitelyPresentedLocalizedModuleSituation.{u₁, u₂, u₃, u₄})
    {M : Type u₄} [AddCommGroup M] [Module X.A M]
    [Module.Flat X.A X.N] [Module.Flat X.A M]
    (u : X.N →ₗ[X.A] M)
    (hu : ∀ (p : Ideal X.A) [p.IsPrime],
      Function.Injective (u.rTensor p.ResidueField)) :
    UniversallyInjective u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallerFlatnessIdeal
declarations.doc:
The ideal `I₂ = Ker (I → Γ(U, (I/I²)~))` of `A`, for an ideal `I` of `A` and an open
`U ⊆ Spec A`: the image in `A` of the kernel of the composite of `I → I/I²` with the map
taking a global conormal class to its sections over `U`.
declarations.statement:
def smallerFlatnessIdeal {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens) : Ideal A
declarations.comment: the ideal I₂

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.flat_quotient_smallerFlatnessIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0ATC.** Let `I` be an ideal of a commutative ring `A` and let
`U ⊆ Spec A` be a quasi-compact open. If `M/IM` is flat over `A/I` and `M~` is flat on `U`,
then `M/I₂M` is flat over `A/I₂`, where `I₂ = Ker (I → Γ(U, (I/I²)~))`.

The source assumes `A` local; locality is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_quotient_smallerFlatnessIdeal
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (I : Ideal A) (U : (Spec (.of A)).Opens)
    (hU : IsCompact U.1)
    (hquot : Module.Flat (A ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule A M)))
    (hflat : SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := (U : Scheme).sheaf)
      (show (U : Scheme).Modules from
        (tilde (ModuleCat.of A M)).restrict U.ι)) :
    Module.Flat (A ⧸ smallerFlatnessIdeal I U)
      (M ⧸ smallerFlatnessIdeal I U • (⊤ : Submodule A M))
declarations.comment: flatness modulo I₂

declarations.name: Stacks.flat_quotient_sectionsKernel
declarations.doc:
Let `I ⊆ A` be an ideal, `M` an `A`-module and `U = ⋃ i, D(f i)` a quasi-compact open of
`Spec A`. If `M/IM` is flat over `A/I` and `M` is flat over `U`, that is `M_{f i}` is flat over
`A_{f i}` for each `i`, then `M/I₂M` is flat over `A/I₂`, where `I₂ = Ker (I → Γ(U, I/I²))` is
`sectionsKernel I f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_quotient_sectionsKernel (I : Ideal A) {ι : Type w} [Finite ι] (f : ι → A)
    (hI : Module.Flat (A ⧸ I) (M ⧸ I • (⊤ : Submodule A M)))
    (hU : ∀ i, Module.Flat (Localization.Away (f i)) (Localization.Away (f i) ⊗[A] M)) :
    Module.Flat (A ⧸ sectionsKernel I f)
      (M ⧸ sectionsKernel I f • (⊤ : Submodule A M))

declarations.name: henselianPair_pi_iff
declarations.doc: A product of pairs is henselian if and only if each component pair is henselian.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianPair_pi_iff {J : Type u} (A : J → Type v) [∀ j, CommRing (A j)]
    (I : ∀ j, Ideal (A j)) :
    HenselianPair ((j : J) → A j) (Ideal.pi I) ↔
      ∀ j, HenselianPair (A j) (I j)

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_flat_algebra_not_filteredColimit
declarations.doc:
There is a commutative ring with a flat algebra which is the colimit of no filtered diagram of
finitely presented flat algebras; the ring may be chosen to be a finite type algebra over `𝔽_p`
for a prime `p`, or a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring whose residue field has
characteristic zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_flat_algebra_not_filteredColimit :
    (∃ (A : CommRingCat.{max u v}) (B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} A), Module.Flat A B ∧
      ∀ (J : Type v) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ CommAlgCat.{max u v} A),
        (∀ j, Algebra.FinitePresentation A (F.obj j) ∧ Module.Flat A (F.obj j)) →
          ∀ c : Cocone F, c.pt = B → IsEmpty (IsColimit c)) ∧
    (∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ ∃ (A : CommRingCat.{max u v}) (_ : Algebra (ZMod p) A),
      Algebra.FiniteType (ZMod p) A ∧ ∃ B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} A, Module.Flat A B ∧
        ∀ (J : Type v) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] (F : J ⥤ CommAlgCat.{max u v} A),
          (∀ j, Algebra.FinitePresentation A (F.obj j) ∧ Module.Flat A (F.obj j)) →
            ∀ c : Cocone F, c.pt = B → IsEmpty (IsColimit c)) ∧
    (∃ A : CommRingCat.{max u v}, ∃ hloc : IsLocalRing A,
      letI : IsLocalRing A := hloc
      IsNoetherianRing A ∧ ringKrullDim A = 1 ∧
        CharZero (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) ∧
          ∃ B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} A, Module.Flat A B ∧
            ∀ (J : Type v) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J]
              (F : J ⥤ CommAlgCat.{max u v} A),
              (∀ j, Algebra.FinitePresentation A (F.obj j) ∧
                Module.Flat A (F.obj j)) →
                ∀ c : Cocone F, c.pt = B → IsEmpty (IsColimit c))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.triangEnvelope_eq_iSup_and_isSaturated_and_le_iff
declarations.doc:
The triangulated envelope `⟨P⟩ = ⋃ₙ ⟨P⟩ₙ` of a nonempty object property `P` of a
triangulated category is the union over `n, m` of the subcategories `smd(add(P[-m, m])^{⋆ n})`;
it is closed under isomorphisms (strictly full), saturated (thick) and a triangulated
subcategory; and it is contained in a strictly full, saturated triangulated subcategory `Q`
exactly when `P` is, so that it is the smallest such subcategory containing `P`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem triangEnvelope_eq_iSup_and_isSaturated_and_le_iff
    (P : ObjectProperty C) [P.Nonempty] [IsTriangulated C] :
    (P.triangEnvelope = ⨆ n : ℕ, ⨆ m : ℕ,
        ((⨆ i ∈ Set.Icc (-(m : ℤ)) (m : ℤ),
          P.isoClosure.shift i).binaryProductsClosure.extensionProductIter n).retractClosure) ∧
      P.triangEnvelope.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms ∧ P.triangEnvelope.IsSaturated ∧
      P.triangEnvelope.IsTriangulated ∧
      ∀ Q : ObjectProperty C, Q.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms → Q.IsSaturated → Q.IsTriangulated →
        (P.triangEnvelope ≤ Q ↔ P ≤ Q)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.triangEnvelope_singleton_le_of_sums_of_extensions_of_summands
declarations.doc:
Let `E` be an object of a triangulated category and let `T` be a property of objects which
is inherited by finite direct sums, satisfies the two-out-of-three property for distinguished
triangles, is inherited by direct summands, and holds on all shifts of `E`. Then `T` holds on
every object of the triangulated subcategory `⟨E⟩` generated by `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem triangEnvelope_singleton_le_of_sums_of_extensions_of_summands
    [IsTriangulated C] (E : C) (T : ObjectProperty C)
    (_hsum : ∀ K L : C, T K → T L → T (K ⊞ L))
    (hext₁ : ∀ Tr ∈ distTriang C, T Tr.obj₂ → T Tr.obj₃ → T Tr.obj₁)
    (hext₂ : ∀ Tr ∈ distTriang C, T Tr.obj₁ → T Tr.obj₃ → T Tr.obj₂)
    (hext₃ : ∀ Tr ∈ distTriang C, T Tr.obj₁ → T Tr.obj₂ → T Tr.obj₃)
    (hsummand : ∀ K L : C, T (K ⊞ L) → T K ∧ T L)
    (hshift : ∀ n : ℤ, T ((CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor C n).obj E)) :
    (ObjectProperty.singleton E).triangEnvelope ≤ T

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_eq_triangEnvelope_singleton_regularModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ATI.** The perfect objects of `D(R)` form the smallest strictly full, saturated,
triangulated subcategory containing the regular module `R` in degree zero. Equivalently, `R[0]`
is a classical generator of the perfect derived category.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_eq_triangEnvelope_singleton_regularModule {R : Type u} [Ring R] :
    (IsPerfect : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R))) =
      (ObjectProperty.singleton
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of R R))).triangEnvelope

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedTensorHomDiagonal.isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ATK.** The canonical derived tensor--Hom diagonal
`K ⊗ᴸ RHom(M, L) ⟶ RHom(M, K ⊗ᴸ L)` is an isomorphism if `M` is perfect, if `K` is perfect, or
if `M` is pseudo-coherent, `L` is bounded below and `K` has Tor amplitude in `[a, ∞]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (a : ℤ)
    (h : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect M ∨ StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K ∨
      (StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent M ∧
        (∃ b : ℤ, DerivedCategory.IsGE L b) ∧
        ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (i : ℤ), i < a →
          IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj
            ((((CochainComplex.DerivedTensor.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct R).tensor.obj K).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj N)))))) :
    IsIso (StacksDraft.DerivedHom.derivedTensorHomDiagonal K L M)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap_comp
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0ATL.**  Derived base change for an outer rectangle is the composite of derived base
change for its two constituent squares.

For two vertically composable commutative squares of ringed spaces, the composite of the derived
pullback along the lower horizontal morphism of the inverse composition isomorphism of Tag 079W,
the derived base change map of the lower square, the derived pushforward along the upper
square's right-hand vertical of the derived base change map of the upper square, and the
composition isomorphism of Tag 079W for the rectangle's left-hand verticals, is the derived base
change map of the rectangle.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedBaseChangeMap_comp (sq₁ : k ≫ f = f' ≫ l) (sq₂ : l ≫ g = g' ≫ m)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    (derivedPullback m).map ((derivedPushforwardCompIso f g).inv.app K) ≫
        derivedBaseChangeMap l g' g m sq₂ ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ≫
        (derivedPushforward g').map (derivedBaseChangeMap k f' f l sq₁ K) ≫
        (derivedPushforwardCompIso f' g').hom.app ((derivedPullback k).obj K) =
      derivedBaseChangeMap k (f' ≫ g') (f ≫ g) m (comp_square k f' f l g' g m sq₁ sq₂) K

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChange.derivedBaseChangeMap_comp_horizontal
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0ATM.**  Derived base change for an outer rectangle is the composite of derived base
change for its two constituent squares.

For two horizontally composable commutative squares of ringed spaces, the composite of the
inverse composition isomorphism of Tag 0D5S for `h' ≫ h`, the derived pullback along `h'` of the
derived base change map of the right-hand square, the derived base change map of the left-hand
square, and the derived pushforward along `f''` of the composition isomorphism of Tag 0D5S for
`g' ≫ g`, is the derived base change map of the rectangle.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedBaseChangeMap_comp_horizontal (sq₁ : g ≫ f = f' ≫ h)
    (sq₂ : g' ≫ f' = f'' ≫ h')
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X))) :
    (derivedPullbackCompIsoCanonical h' h).inv.app ((derivedPushforward f).obj K) ≫
        (derivedPullback h').map (derivedBaseChangeMap g f' f h sq₁ K) ≫
        derivedBaseChangeMap g' f'' f' h' sq₂ ((derivedPullback g).obj K) ≫
        (derivedPushforward f'').map ((derivedPullbackCompIsoCanonical g' g).hom.app K) =
      derivedBaseChangeMap (g' ≫ g) f'' f (h' ≫ h)
        (hcomp_square g' g f'' f' f h' h sq₁ sq₂) K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ATN part (1): the diagonal of Stacks 0BYS is an isomorphism at a perfect source.**
For objects `K`, `L`, `M` of `D(O)` with `M` perfect,

`K ⊗^L_O RSheafHom(M, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(M, K ⊗^L_O L)`

is an isomorphism.

The only hypothesis is `X.IsPerfect M`, the site-level notion of Stacks 08G5: there is a complex
`N` representing `M` and a covering of the site on each member of which the restriction of `N`
receives a quasi-isomorphism from a strictly perfect complex. Nothing is assumed of `K` or `L`.

The instances in the ambient variable block are setup, not hypotheses on the lemma: a ringed site
whose slices admit sheafification and on which the tensor product of sheaves of modules is
additive and totalisable is what it takes for the objects in the statement — the derived tensor
product, the derived internal Hom, and their restrictions to the slices appearing in the
definition of perfection — to exist at all. A class needed only by the proof would have been an
extra hypothesis, and there is none.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal_of_isPerfect
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hM : X.IsPerfect M) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorHomDiagonal X K L M)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal_of_isPerfect_tensorFactor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ATN part (2): the diagonal of Stacks 0BYS is an isomorphism at a perfect tensor
factor.** For objects `K`, `L`, `M` of `D(O)` with `K` perfect,

`K ⊗^L_O RSheafHom(M, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(M, K ⊗^L_O L)`

is an isomorphism.

The only hypothesis is `X.IsPerfect K`, the site-level notion of Stacks 08G5: there is a complex
`A₀` representing `K` and a covering of the site on each member of which the restriction of `A₀`
receives a quasi-isomorphism from a strictly perfect complex. Nothing is assumed of `L` or `M`.
This is the same notion, with the same slack, that part (1) assumes of `M`.

The instances in the ambient variable block are setup, not hypotheses on the lemma, exactly as
for part (1): a ringed site whose slices admit sheafification and on which the tensor product of
sheaves of modules is additive and totalisable is what it takes for the objects named in the
statement to exist. A class needed only by the proof would have been an extra hypothesis, and
there is none.

The K-flat resolution is taken of `A₀` itself rather than of the chosen K-flat model of `K`, so
that the comparison between the criterion's model and the complex the covering resolves is a
quasi-isomorphism of complexes and the slice-level input can be assembled from chain maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal_of_isPerfect_tensorFactor
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorHomDiagonal X K L M)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_hasTorAmplitudeGE
declarations.doc:
**The diagonal of Stacks 0BYS is an isomorphism at a pseudo-coherent source, a
cohomologically bounded-below target and a tensor factor of Tor amplitude in `[a, ∞)`.** For
objects `K`, `L`, `M` of `D(O)` with `M` pseudo-coherent, the cohomology of `L` vanishing in
degrees `≪ 0` and `K` of Tor amplitude in `[a, ∞)`,

`K ⊗^L_O RSheafHom(M, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(M, K ⊗^L_O L)`

is an isomorphism.

Pseudo-coherence is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherent`, Tor amplitude in `[a, ∞)`
is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitudeGE` for the canonical derived
tensor product, and boundedness below is vanishing of the cohomology sheaves in degrees `≪ 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal_of_isPseudoCoherent_of_hasTorAmplitudeGE
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (a : ℤ)
    (hM : X.IsPseudoCoherent M)
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow L)
    (hK : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasTorAmplitudeGE
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X) K a) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorHomDiagonal X K L M)
declarations.comment: part (3), with the tensor factor of Tor amplitude in [a, ∞) rather than of finite Tor dimension

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal_of_isPseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0ATN part (3): the diagonal of Stacks 0BYS is an isomorphism at a pseudo-coherent
source, a cohomologically bounded-below target and a tensor factor of finite Tor dimension.**
For objects `K`, `L`, `M` of `D(O)` with `M` pseudo-coherent, the cohomology of `L` vanishing in
degrees `≪ 0` and `K` of finite Tor dimension,

`K ⊗^L_O RSheafHom(M, L) ⟶ RSheafHom(M, K ⊗^L_O L)`

is an isomorphism.

The three hypotheses are the site-level notions: pseudo-coherence is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsPseudoCoherent` of Stacks 08FT, finite Tor dimension is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasFiniteTorDimension` of Stacks 08FZ for the
canonical derived tensor product, and boundedness below is vanishing of the cohomology sheaves
in degrees `≪ 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_derivedTensorHomDiagonal_of_isPseudoCoherent
    (K L M : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hM : X.IsPseudoCoherent M)
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow L)
    (hK : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasFiniteTorDimension
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.canonicalDerivedTensorProduct X) K) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorHomDiagonal X K L M)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_isInvertible_tensor_iso_of_isDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ATP].** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme and let `K`, `K'` be dualizing
complexes on `X` ([Stacks, Tag 0A87]). Then `K'` is isomorphic to `K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_X} L` for some
invertible object `L` of `D(𝒪_X)` ([Stacks, Tag 0FFN]), the monoidal structure being that of
[Stacks, Tag 0FPT].

The proof is the source's, with `L = R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, K')`: `L` is invertible
(`Stacks.Duality.isInvertible_derivedSheafHom_of_isDualizingComplex`) and the evaluation
`L ⊗^𝐋 K ⟶ K'` is an isomorphism
(`Stacks.Duality.isIso_derivedSheafHomCounit_of_isDualizingComplex`), both because they hold
affine locally.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_tensor_iso_of_isDualizingComplex [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (K K' : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hK' : IsDualizingComplex K') :
    letI := Scheme.Modules.derivedMonoidal X
    ∃ L : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
      MonoidalCategory.IsInvertible L ∧ Nonempty (K' ≅ K ⊗ L)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_vcomp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ATQ] (Lemma 48.5.1): the base change maps of a vertical stack of two
cartesian squares compose to the base change map of the outer rectangle.** For

```
X' --k--> X
|f'       |f
Y' --l--> Y
|g'       |g
Z' --m--> Z
```

with both squares cartesian, the base change map `Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap`
of [Stacks, Tag 0AA6] for the rectangle — the square with horizontal edges `k` and `m` and
vertical edges `f' ≫ g'` and `f ≫ g` — is the horizontal composite of the base change maps of the
lower and of the upper square, the twisted inverse images along the two composite verticals being
read through the comparison `Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageCompIso` of [Stacks, Tag 0ATX].

The source's proof reduces the statement to the identity `ξ_rect = ξ_bot ≫ₕ ξ_top`, which is
`Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_vcomp`; the passage from that identity to
this one is the compatibility of `CategoryTheory.mateEquiv` with vertical composition, because
each base change map is the mate of the inverse of the corresponding `ξ`
(`Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_eq_mateEquiv_symm`).
declarations.statement:
theorem twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_vcomp (sq₁ : IsPullback k f' f l)
    (sq₂ : IsPullback l g' g m)
    [IsIso (twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange k f' f l hpushk hpushf hpushf' hpushl sq₁)]
    [IsIso (twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange l g' g m hpushl hpushg hpushg' hpushm sq₂)] :
    letI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_vcomp k f' f l g' g m hpushk hpushf
      hpushf' hpushl hpushg hpushg' hpushm hpushfg hpushf'g' sq₁ sq₂
    twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap k (f' ≫ g') (f ≫ g) m hpushk hpushfg hpushf'g' hpushm
        (sq₁.paste_vert sq₂) =
      ((TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ (twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap l g' g m hpushl hpushg hpushg'
              hpushm sq₂) ≫ₕ
          TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ (twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap k f' f l hpushk hpushf hpushf'
            hpushl sq₁)).whiskerTop
        (twistedInverseImageCompIso f g hpushf hpushg hpushfg).hom).whiskerBottom
        (twistedInverseImageCompIso f' g' hpushf' hpushg' hpushf'g').inv
declarations.comment: for the base change map of Stacks 0AA6 attached to the twisted inverse image f^x of Stacks 0A9E -- the right adjoint of Rf_* on D_QCoh -- and for the comparison (f then g)^x = g^x then f^x of Stacks 0ATX: the map of the outer rectangle of a vertical stack of two cartesian squares is the horizontal composite of the maps of the two squares, read through those comparisons. The source's quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness enter as the preservation of quasi-coherent cohomology by derived direct and inverse image along the morphisms of the diagram and as the existence of the six right adjoints, which is what Stacks 08D5 part (1) and Stacks 0A9E produce for a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism; Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageCompIsoOfQcqs is the pattern that discharges them. Invertibility of the transformation xi of Stacks 0A9K for each of the two squares is an instance argument, exactly as in Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap where the base change map is defined, and it is Stacks 0A9K that produces it for a Tor-independent square. What is NOT claimed is the passage from f^x to the f^! of a general compactification, Stacks.Duality.upperShriek, which needs the independence of the chosen compactification, Stacks 0AA0

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_paste_vert_app
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ATQ].** Consider a commutative diagram
```
X' --k--> X
|         |
f'        f
v         v
Y' --l--> Y
|         |
g'        g
v         v
Z' --m--> Z
```
of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes in which both squares are cartesian, `f` and `l`
are Tor independent and `g` and `m` are Tor independent. Then the base change maps
(Equation 48.5.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0AA6]) of the two squares compose to the base change map of
the outer rectangle: with `a`, `b`, `c` the right adjoints of `Rf_*`, `Rg_*`, `R(f ≫ g)_*` and
`a'`, `b'`, `c'` those of `Rf'_*`, `Rg'_*`, `R(f' ≫ g')_*`, for every `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Z)` the map
`Lk^* c(K) ⟶ c'(Lm^* K)` of the rectangle is

```
Lk^* c(K) = Lk^* a(b(K)) ⟶ a'(Ll^* b(K)) ⟶ a'(b'(Lm^* K)) = c'(Lm^* K),
```

the identifications `c = b ⋙ a` and `c' = b' ⋙ a'` being those of [Stacks, Tag 0ATX]
(`Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageCompIso`). The base change map of the rectangle is defined
because its `ξ` is invertible,
`Stacks.Duality.isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_paste_vert`.
declarations.statement:
theorem twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_paste_vert_app (sqT : IsPullback k f' f l)
    (sqB : IsPullback l g' g m) (hT : TorIndependent f l) (hB : TorIndependent g m)
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Z) :
    haveI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_paste_vert sqT sqB hT hB
    (twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap k (f' ≫ g') (f ≫ g) m
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs k)
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f ≫ g))
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f' ≫ g'))
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs m)
        (sqT.paste_vert sqB)).app K =
      (quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' k).map
          ((twistedInverseImageCompIso f g (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g)
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f ≫ g))).hom.app K) ≫
        (torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange sqT hT).app
          ((twistedInverseImage g (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g)).obj K) ≫
        (twistedInverseImage f' (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')).map
          ((torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange sqB hB).app K) ≫
        (twistedInverseImageCompIso f' g'
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f')
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g')
            (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f' ≫ g'))).inv.app
          ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' m).obj K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_hcomp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ATR] (Lemma 48.5.2): the base change maps of a row of two cartesian squares
compose to the base change map of the outer rectangle.** For

```
X'' --k'--> X' --k--> X
|f''        |f'       |f
Y'' --l'--> Y' --l--> Y
```

with both squares cartesian, the base change map `Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap`
of [Stacks, Tag 0AA6] for the rectangle — the square with horizontal edges `k' ≫ k` and `l' ≫ l` —
is the vertical paste of the base change maps of the right and of the left square, the derived
pullbacks along the two composite horizontals being read through the composition formula
`Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedPullbackCompIsoConj`.

Each base change map is the mate of the inverse of the corresponding `ξ`
(`Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_eq_mateEquiv_symm`), the rectangle's `ξ` is
the vertical paste of the two (`Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_hcomp`),
and the inverse of a vertical paste is the horizontal paste of the inverses; the passage between
the two pastes is `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedBaseChangePasting.mate_twoSquare_paste`, with the
composite adjunctions traded through the composition formulas, which are conjugate by
construction.
declarations.statement:
theorem twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_hcomp (sq₁ : IsPullback k' f'' f' l')
    (sq₂ : IsPullback k f' f l)
    [IsIso (twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange k' f'' f' l' hpushk' hpushf' hpushf''
      hpushl' sq₁)]
    [IsIso (twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange k f' f l hpushk hpushf hpushf' hpushl sq₂)] :
    letI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_hcomp k' k f'' f' f l' l hpushk'
      hpushk hpushkk hpushf'' hpushf' hpushf hpushl' hpushl hpushll sq₁ sq₂
    twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap (k' ≫ k) f'' f (l' ≫ l) hpushkk hpushf hpushf'' hpushll
        (sq₁.paste_horiz sq₂) =
      (((TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ (twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap k f' f l hpushk hpushf hpushf'
              hpushl sq₂) ≫ᵥ
          TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ (twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap k' f'' f' l' hpushk' hpushf'
            hpushf'' hpushl' sq₁)).whiskerLeft
        (quasiCoherentDerivedPullbackCompIsoConj l' l hpushl' hpushl hpushll
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' l')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' l)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' (l' ≫ l))).hom).whiskerRight
        (quasiCoherentDerivedPullbackCompIsoConj k' k hpushk' hpushk hpushkk
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' k')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' k)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPullback' (k' ≫ k))).inv)
declarations.comment: for the base change map of Stacks 0AA6 attached to the twisted inverse image f^x of Stacks 0A9E -- the right adjoint of Rf_* on D_QCoh: the map of the outer rectangle of a row of two cartesian squares is the vertical composite of the maps of the two squares, read through the composition formula for derived pullback along the two composite horizontal morphisms. The source's quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness enter as the preservation of quasi-coherent cohomology by derived direct and inverse image along the morphisms of the diagram and as the existence of the three right adjoints, which is what Stacks 08D5 part (1) and Stacks 0A9E produce for a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism. Invertibility of the transformation xi of Stacks 0A9K for each of the two squares is an instance argument, exactly as in Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap where the base change map is defined, and it is Stacks 0A9K that produces it for a Tor-independent square; the rectangle's needs no third input, by Stacks.Duality.isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_hcomp

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_paste_horiz_app
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ATR].** Consider a commutative diagram
```
X'' --g'--> X' --g--> X
 |          |         |
f''         f'        f
 v          v         v
Y'' --h'--> Y' --h--> Y
```
of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes in which both squares are cartesian, `f` and `h`
are Tor independent and `f'` and `h'` are Tor independent. Then the base change maps
(Equation 48.5.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0AA6]) of the two squares compose to the base change map of
the outer rectangle: with `k = g' ≫ g`, `m = h' ≫ h` and `a`, `a'`, `a''` the right adjoints of
`Rf_*`, `Rf'_*`, `Rf''_*`, for every `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` the map `Lk^* a(K) ⟶ a''(Lm^* K)` of the
rectangle is

```
Lk^* a(K) = L(g')^* Lg^* a(K) ⟶ L(g')^* a'(Lh^* K) ⟶ a''(L(h')^* Lh^* K) = a''(Lm^* K),
```

the identifications being the composition isomorphisms of derived pullback. The base change map
of the rectangle is defined because its `ξ` is invertible,
`Stacks.Duality.isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_paste_horiz`.
declarations.statement:
theorem twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_paste_horiz_app (sqR : IsPullback g f' f h)
    (sqL : IsPullback g' f'' f' h') (hR : TorIndependent f h) (hL : TorIndependent f' h')
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y) :
    haveI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_paste_horiz sqR sqL hR hL
    (twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap (g' ≫ g) f'' f (h' ≫ h)
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (g' ≫ g))
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f'')
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (h' ≫ h))
        (sqL.paste_horiz sqR)).app K =
      (quasiCoherentDerivedPullbackCompIso g' g).inv.app
          ((twistedInverseImage f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).obj K) ≫
        (quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' g').map
          ((torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange sqR hR).app K) ≫
        (torIndependentTwistedInverseImageBaseChange sqL hL).app
          ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' h).obj K) ≫
        (twistedInverseImage f'' (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f'')).map
          ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullbackCompIso h' h).hom.app K)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_grid_app
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ATS].** Consider a commutative diagram
```
X'' --k'--> X' --k--> X
 |          |         |
f''         f'        f
 v          v         v
Y'' --l'--> Y' --l--> Y
 |          |         |
g''         g'        g
 v          v         v
Z'' --m'--> Z' --m--> Z
```
of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes in which all squares are cartesian and
`(f, l)`, `(g, m)`, `(f', l')`, `(g', m')` are Tor independent pairs. Let `a, a', a''`,
`b, b', b''` be the right adjoints of `Rf_*, Rf'_*, Rf''_*`, `Rg_*, Rg'_*, Rg''_*`
([Stacks, Tag 0A9E]); label the squares `A` (top left), `B` (top right), `C` (bottom left) and
`D` (bottom right). The base change maps (Equation 48.5.0.1 of [Stacks, Tag 0AA6]) of the four
rectangles made of two squares give two transformations
`L(k')^* Lk^* a b ⟶ a'' b'' L(m')^* Lm^*`, namely `γ_{A+C} ∘ γ_{B+D}` and `γ_{C+D} ∘ γ_{A+B}`, and
these are equal: for every `K ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_Z)`,

* `γ_{A+C} ∘ γ_{B+D}` is `L(k')^* Lk^* a(b(K)) ≅ L(k')^* Lk^* c(K) ⟶ L(k')^* c'(Lm^* K) ⟶
  c''(L(m')^* Lm^* K) ≅ a''(b''(L(m')^* Lm^* K))`, with `c, c', c''` the right adjoints of
  `R(f ≫ g)_*, R(f' ≫ g')_*, R(f'' ≫ g'')_*` identified with `b ⋙ a`, … by
  [Stacks, Tag 0ATX];
* `γ_{C+D} ∘ γ_{A+B}` is `L(k')^* Lk^* a(b(K)) ≅ L(k' ≫ k)^* a(b(K)) ⟶ a''(L(l' ≫ l)^* b(K)) ⟶
  a''(b''(L(m' ≫ m)^* K)) ≅ a''(b''(L(m')^* Lm^* K))`, through the composition isomorphisms
  of derived pullback.

The base change maps of the rectangles are defined because their `ξ` are invertible
([Stacks, Tag 0ATR], [Stacks, Tag 0ATQ]).
declarations.statement:
theorem twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap_grid_app
    (sqA : IsPullback k' f'' f' l') (sqB : IsPullback k f' f l)
    (sqC : IsPullback l' g'' g' m') (sqD : IsPullback l g' g m)
    (hB : TorIndependent f l) (hD : TorIndependent g m) (hA : TorIndependent f' l')
    (hC : TorIndependent g' m') (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Z) :
    haveI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_paste_vert sqB sqD hB hD
    haveI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_paste_vert sqA sqC hA hC
    haveI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_paste_horiz sqB sqA hB hA
    haveI := isIso_twistedInverseImagePushforwardBaseChange_of_paste_horiz sqD sqC hD hC
    (quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' k').map ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' k).map
        ((twistedInverseImageCompIso f g (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f ≫ g))).inv.app K)) ≫
      (quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' k').map
        ((twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap k (f' ≫ g') (f ≫ g) m
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs k)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f ≫ g))
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f' ≫ g'))
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs m)
          (sqB.paste_vert sqD)).app K) ≫
      (twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap k' (f'' ≫ g'') (f' ≫ g') m'
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs k')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f' ≫ g'))
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f'' ≫ g''))
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs m')
          (sqA.paste_vert sqC)).app ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' m).obj K) ≫
      (twistedInverseImageCompIso f'' g''
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f'')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g'')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (f'' ≫ g''))).hom.app
        ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' m').obj ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' m).obj K)) =
    (quasiCoherentDerivedPullbackCompIso k' k).hom.app
        ((twistedInverseImage f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).obj
          ((twistedInverseImage g (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g)).obj
            K)) ≫
      (twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap (k' ≫ k) f'' f (l' ≫ l)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (k' ≫ k))
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f'')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (l' ≫ l))
          (sqA.paste_horiz sqB)).app
        ((twistedInverseImage g (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g)).obj K) ≫
      (twistedInverseImage f'' (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f'')).map
        ((twistedInverseImageBaseChangeMap (l' ≫ l) g'' g (m' ≫ m)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (l' ≫ l))
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g)
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g'')
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs (m' ≫ m))
          (sqC.paste_horiz sqD)).app K) ≫
      (twistedInverseImage f'' (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f'')).map
        ((twistedInverseImage g'' (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs g'')).map
          ((quasiCoherentDerivedPullbackCompIso m' m).inv.app K))
