declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriekCompIsoAtModel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ATX]: the canonical isomorphism `(g ∘ f)^! ≅ f^! ∘ g^!`**, for any
compactifications `k` of `g ∘ f`, `j` of `f` and `i` of `g`. It is the source's construction for a
choice of compactifications whose compactification of `Y` is `i` (that one exists is
[Stacks, Tag 0A9Z]), read through the canonical comparisons of [Stacks, Tag 0AA0].
declarations.statement:
def upperShriekCompIsoAtModel (k : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g).left))
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (i : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g.left)) :
    compactificationUpperShriek (f ≫ g) k ≅
      upperShriekPlusAtModel i ⋙ compactificationUpperShriek f j
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism (g o f)^! = f^! o g^! of upper shriek functors for composable morphisms f : X -> Y, g : Y -> Z of FTS S over a Noetherian S, at arbitrary compactifications k of g o f, j of f and i of g, as functors out of D^+_QCoh(O_Z), with g^! read in D^+_QCoh(O_Y) (Stacks 0A9I) and each f^! the functor Stacks.Duality.compactificationUpperShriek of Stacks 0A9Y/0AA0. It is the source's construction for a choice of compactifications through i: (j' o j)^* a b = j^* (j')^* a b -> j^* a' i^* b via the base change map of Stacks 0AA6, invertible by Stacks 0A9P (2), read through the canonical comparisons of Stacks 0AA0. Canonicity is proved, not assumed: Stacks.Duality.upperShriekCompIsoAtModel_choice says it is the source's isomorphism for every choice (the second half of the source's proof: the chase of squares A..F through Stacks 0ATQ and 0ATR, and a dominating choice from Stacks 0ATU), and Stacks.Duality.upperShriekCompIsoAtModel_naturality says it is compatible with the comparisons of Stacks 0AA0 in all three compactifications. The compactifications are arguments, as in Stacks 0AA0; that they exist is Stacks 0F41

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_canonical_upperShriekCompIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ATX]: there is a canonical isomorphism `(g ∘ f)^! → f^! ∘ g^!`.** For
composable morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y`, `g : Y ⟶ Z` of `AlgebraicGeometry.FTS S` over a Noetherian `S`
there is a family of isomorphisms `(g ∘ f)^!_k ≅ f^!_j ∘ g^!_i`, indexed by compactifications `k`
of `g ∘ f`, `j` of `f` and `i` of `g`, which is the source's construction for **every** choice of
compactifications, and which is compatible with the canonical comparisons of [Stacks, Tag 0AA0] in
all three compactifications — so it is independent of the choices made. The family is
`Stacks.Duality.upperShriekCompIsoAtModel`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_canonical_upperShriekCompIso :
    ∃ e : ∀ (k : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (f ≫ g).left))
        (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (i : CompactificationOf (Over.mk g.left)),
        compactificationUpperShriek (f ≫ g) k ≅ upperShriekPlusAtModel i ⋙
            compactificationUpperShriek f j,
      (∀ D : CompositionData f g, e D.outer D.inner D.base = D.compIsoAPI) ∧
      ∀ k k' j j' i i', compactificationUpperShriekIso (f ≫ g) k k' ≪≫ e k' j' i' =
        e k j i ≪≫ NatIso.hcomp (basePlusIsoAPI i i') (compactificationUpperShriekIso f j j')
declarations.comment: existence and canonicity of the isomorphism (g o f)^! = f^! o g^! for composable morphisms of FTS S over a Noetherian S, the upper shriek functors being those of Stacks 0AA0 on D^+_QCoh and g^! read in D^+_QCoh(O_Y): a family of isomorphisms indexed by compactifications of g o f, f and g that equals the source's construction for every choice of compactifications (Stacks.Duality.CompositionData.compIsoAPI) and is compatible with the comparisons of Stacks 0AA0 in all three compactifications. Nothing is assumed beyond the compactifications themselves, which are arguments as in Stacks 0AA0 (their existence is Stacks 0F41)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_upperShriekPseudofunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0ATY]**: in Situation 0F42 the constructions of [Stacks, Tag 0AA0] and
[Stacks, Tag 0ATX] define a pseudofunctor from `FTS S` into the 2-category of categories: there
is a pseudofunctor `(FTS S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat` whose value at `X` is `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, whose value at `f`
is the upper shriek functor `f^!` of [Stacks, Tag 0AA0] (at a compactification of `f`, which
exists by More on Flatness, Theorem 0F41; by [Stacks, Tag 0AA0] the choice does not matter up to
canonical isomorphism), and whose compositor at `f`, `g` is the canonical isomorphism
`(g ∘ f)^! ≅ f^! ∘ g^!` of [Stacks, Tag 0ATX]. It is `Stacks.Duality.upperShriekPseudofunctor`;
the axioms of a pseudofunctor are the conditions (a)–(d) of Categories, Definition 003N.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_upperShriekPseudofunctor :
    ∃ P : LocallyDiscrete (FTS S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ᵖ Cat.{u, u + 1},
      ∃ hobj : ∀ X : (FTS S)ᵒᵖ,
          P.obj ⟨X⟩ = Cat.of (quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusAtModel X.unop.left),
        (∀ {X Y : (FTS S)ᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y),
          eqToHom (hobj X).symm ≫ P.map ⟨f⟩ ≫ eqToHom (hobj Y) =
            (upperShriekPlusAtModel (cc f.unop)).toCatHom) ∧
        (∀ {X Y Z : (FTS S)ᵒᵖ} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z),
          HEq (Cat.Hom.toNatIso (P.mapComp ⟨f⟩ ⟨g⟩))
            (upperShriekCompIsoAtModelPlus (cc (g.unop ≫ f.unop)) (cc g.unop) (cc f.unop)))
declarations.comment: the full statement: Stacks.Duality.upperShriekPseudofunctor is a pseudofunctor LocallyDiscrete (FTS S)^op -> Cat (Mathlib's Pseudofunctor, i.e. Categories 003N with conditions (a) invertibility, (b), (c) unit laws and (d) cocycle condition as its axioms) over a Noetherian S, with object X |-> D^+_QCoh(O_X), morphism f |-> f^! of Stacks 0AA0 (the functor Stacks.Duality.compactificationUpperShriek of a compactification of f, read in D^+_QCoh, Stacks 0A9I; compactifications exist by Stacks 0F41) and compositor the canonical isomorphism (g o f)^! = f^! o g^! of Stacks 0ATX (Stacks.Duality.upperShriekCompIsoAtModel). The cocycle condition (d) is the source's proof, Stacks.Duality.upperShriekCompIsoAtModel_cocycle: a choice Zbar over T, Ybar over Zbar, Xbar over Ybar (0F41, 0A9Z), the squares A, B, C, and gamma_{A+B} = gamma_A o gamma_B (0ATR), gamma_{B+C} = gamma_C o gamma_B (0ATQ), gamma_A and gamma_C commuting by naturality. The unit (1_X)^! = id, which the source does not specify, is the one determined by the compositor of 1_X, and (b), (c) follow from (d). Nothing is assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriekIsoRestrictOfOpenImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AU0 (Lemma 48.17.1).** Let `j : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FTS S` whose underlying morphism of schemes is an open immersion. Then the
exceptional inverse image of `j` is restriction to `X`:

  `j^! ≅ j^* : D_QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.

Here `j^!` is computed at the compactification `X̄ = Y` of `Stacks.Duality.openCompactification`,
the one the source's proof chooses. The isomorphism is the source's: the right adjoint of
`R(𝟙_Y)_*` is the identity (`Stacks.Duality.upperShriekIsoDerivedPullbackOfOpenImmersion`), and
`Lj^*` is restriction along an open immersion
(`Stacks.Duality.restrictedDerivedRestrictIsoQuasiCoherentDerivedPullback`).
declarations.statement:
def upperShriekIsoRestrictOfOpenImmersion :
    upperShriek j (openCompactification j) ≅ OpenImmersion.restrictedDerivedRestrict j.left
declarations.comment: j^! = j^* with j^* the restriction to the open X, j^! computed at the compactification X-bar = Y that the source's proof chooses; over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base and on the unbounded D_QCoh

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.derivedCategoryBPlus_upperShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AU1 (Lemma 48.17.6).** In Situation 48.16.1 let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
morphism of `FTS S`. Then `f^!` maps `D⁺_Coh(𝒪_Y)` into `D⁺_Coh(𝒪_X)`. Here `f^!` is computed at
an arbitrary compactification `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_upperShriek
    {S : Scheme.{u}} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S] {X Y : FTS S} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f.left)) (E : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y.left)
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (fun M : Y.left.Modules ↦ _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent M) E.obj) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (fun M : X.left.Modules ↦ _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent M)
      ((upperShriek f j).obj E).obj

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.UpperShriekDuality.upperShriekDualityIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AU2.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0F42] — `S` Noetherian — let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes separated and of finite type over `S`, let `j` be a
compactification of `X` over `Y`, and let `K` be a dualizing complex on `Y`. Set
`D_Y(M) = R𝓗om(M, K)` and `D_X(E) = R𝓗om(E, f^!K)`. Then there is a canonical isomorphism

`f^!M ≅ D_X(Lf^* D_Y(M))`,

natural in `M ∈ D^+_Coh(𝒪_Y)`.
declarations.statement:
def upperShriekDualityIso :
    upperShriekStd f j ≅
      (plusCoh Y.left).ι ⋙ ((sheafHom Y.left).flip.obj K).rightOp ⋙ (pull f.left).op ⋙
        (sheafHom X.left).flip.obj (upperShriekDualizing f j hK)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.LocallySmall.upperShriek_closedImmersion_of_fts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AA2 (Lemma 48.17.4).** In Situation 48.16.1 — `S` a Noetherian scheme
and `FTS S` the schemes separated and of finite type over `S` — let `i : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of
`FTS S` whose underlying morphism of schemes is a closed immersion. Then
`i^!(-) = R𝓗om(𝒪_X, -)`:

1. `Ri_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` has a right adjoint;
2. the upper shriek `i^! = j^* ∘ a` of [Stacks, Tag 0A9Y] at the compactification `X̄ = X` that a
   proper morphism is (`Stacks.Duality.properCompactification`), with its right adjoint `a`
   *produced* by (1) and its quasi-coherence inputs discharged, agrees with `R𝓗om(𝒪_X, -)` on
   `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`;
3. for every right adjoint `a` of `Ri_*` the canonical comparison `a(K) ⟶ R𝓗om(𝒪_X, K)` — the
   mate of the counit of `a` under [Stacks, Tag 0A76] — is an isomorphism for every `K` in
   `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`.

The existence (1) is
`Stacks.Duality.LocallySmall.isLeftAdjoint_affineHomQuasiCoherentDerivedPushforward`, which builds
the right adjoint as `DQ_X ∘ R𝓗om(𝒪_X, -)` from the coherator of [Stacks, Tag 0CR0]; `X` is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, being of finite type over a Noetherian scheme. The
identification (2), (3) is [Stacks, Tag 0A9X] at this model
(`Stacks.Duality.LocallySmall.isIso_rightAdjointToDerivedSheafHom_app`), whose hypotheses —
pseudo-coherence of `i` — hold in Situation 48.16.1.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriek_closedImmersion_of_fts {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S] {X Y : FTS S}
    (i : X ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i.left] :
    (affineHomQuasiCoherentDerivedPushforward i.left).IsLeftAdjoint ∧
      IsDerivedSheafHomRightAdjoint i.left
        (upperShriek i (properCompactification i)) ∧
      ∀ (a : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y.left ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X.left)
        (adj : affineHomQuasiCoherentDerivedPushforward i.left ⊣ a)
        (K : (isBoundedBelowQuasiCoherent Y.left).FullSubcategory),
        IsIso ((rightAdjointToDerivedSheafHom i.left
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_isAffineHom i.left) a adj).app
            K.obj)
declarations.comment: clause (5): for a closed immersion f^! = RHom(O_X, -), at the locally small derived categories

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isNormalTensorPullbackRightAdjoint_of_fts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0AU3, clause (7).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme, let `Y` be an
object of `AlgebraicGeometry.FTS S` — a scheme separated and of finite type over `S` — and let
`D ⊆ Y` be an effective Cartier divisor, with closed immersion `i : D ⟶ Y` and normal sheaf
`𝒩 = i^*𝒪_Y(D)`. Let `a` be a right adjoint of `Ri_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_D) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`. Then `a`,
which is `i^!`, is `Li^*(-) ⊗^L_{𝒪_D} 𝒩[-1]` on bounded-below complexes with quasi-coherent
cohomology:

`i^!(-) = Li^*(-) ⊗_{𝒪_D} i^*𝒪_Y(D)[-1]`.

The proof is the section's own: clause (5) of the section, which is [Stacks, Tag 0AA2] and is
formalized as `Stacks.Duality.isDerivedSheafHomRightAdjoint_of_fts_closedImmersion`, identifies
`i^!` with `R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(𝒪_D, -)`; and [Stacks, Tag 0AA4],
`Stacks.Divisors.normalTensorDerivedSheafHomIso`, identifies that with
`Li^*(-) ⊗^L_{𝒪_D} 𝒩[-1]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormalTensorPullbackRightAdjoint_of_fts
    (a : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y.left ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory D.subscheme)
    (adj : affineHomQuasiCoherentDerivedPushforward D.subschemeι ⊣ a) :
    IsNormalTensorPullbackRightAdjoint D a
declarations.comment: clause (7) of Section 48.19: for the inclusion of an effective Cartier divisor into an object of FTS S, f^! is derived pullback tensored with the shifted normal sheaf i^*O_Y(D)[-1]. Both inputs are proved unconditionally: clause (5) of the same section (Tag 0AA2) as Stacks.Duality.isDerivedSheafHomRightAdjoint_of_fts_closedImmersion, and Tag 0AA4 as Stacks.Divisors.normalTensorDerivedSheafHomIso. As in clause (5), i^! is the explicit parameter a with its adjunction, the existence statement being Tag 0A9E

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_upperShriekFiniteIsoDerivedHomSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0AU3, clause (6).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and let
`f : Y ⟶ X` be a finite morphism of `FTS S`, with `f^!` computed at any compactification. Then
`f_* f^!(-) = R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(f_*𝒪_Y, -)` as functors `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(f_*𝒪_Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriekFiniteIsoDerivedHomSheaf :
    haveI := pseudoCoherent_of_isFinite_of_isLocallyNoetherian f.left
    Nonempty (upperShriekPlus f j ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙
        (derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardOverRingEquivalence f.left).functor ⋙
          ObjectProperty.ι _ ≅
      ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ (structureSheafModelEquiv X.left).inverse ⋙
        derivedHomSheaf f.left ⋙ (pushforwardRingModelEquiv f.left).functor)
declarations.comment: clause (6): for a finite morphism f : Y to X of FTS S and any compactification, f_* f^! = RHom(f_* O_Y, -) as functors from D^+_QCoh(O_X) to D(f_* O_Y), f_* read as an f_* O_Y-module through the equivalence of Tag 0AVW; from clause (2) and Tag 0AX2

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_upperShriekIsoPullbackTensorOfKoszulRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0AU3, clause (8).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a Koszul-regular immersion of codimension `c` into an object of `FTS S`: an
immersion whose canonical closed factor `i = f.liftCoborder : X ⟶ f.coborderRange` (a closed
immersion into an open of `Y`) has conormal sheaf finite locally free of rank `c`. Write `𝒩` for
the normal sheaf of `f`, the dual of the conormal sheaf of `i`. Then, with `f^!` computed at any
compactification,

`f^!(-) ≅ Lf^*(-) ⊗ᴸ_{𝒪_X} ∧^c 𝒩[-c]`

as functors on `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriekIsoPullbackTensorOfKoszulRegular [IsImmersion f.left]
    (hf : IsKoszulRegularImmersion f.left)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
      (R := X.left.ringCatSheaf) (Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf f.left.liftCoborder) c] :
    Nonempty (((ObjectProperty.ι _ : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel Y.left ⥤ _) ⋙
        quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' f.left ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _) ⋙
      (derivedTensor X.left).flip.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.left.Modules (c : ℤ)).obj
          (Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower (Stacks.Divisors.normalSheaf f.left.liftCoborder) c)) ≅
      (ObjectProperty.ι _ : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel Y.left ⥤ _) ⋙
        upperShriek f j ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _)
declarations.comment: clause (8): for a Koszul-regular immersion f : X to Y of codimension c into an object of FTS S (the conormal sheaf of its canonical closed factor into an open of Y finite locally free of rank c) and any compactification, f^!(-) = Lf^*(-) tensor wedge^c N[-c] as functors on D^+_QCoh(O_Y), N the normal sheaf; from Tag 0BR0 and Tag 0B6U (e)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.upperShriek_rightAdjoint_and_duality_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0AU3, clause (2).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of `FTS S`, with `f^!` computed at any compactification `j`.
Then `f^!` is the restriction of the right adjoint of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` to
`D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, and there is a canonical isomorphism

`Rf_* R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, f^!M) ≅ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*K, M)`

for all `K ∈ D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)` and `M ∈ D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`:

1. `f^!` carries `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` into `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)`;
2. for every right adjoint `a` of `Rf_*`, the functor `f^! : D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is
   isomorphic to the restriction of `a`;
3. the isomorphism, `Stacks.Duality.sheafHomUpperShriekIsoOfIsProper`, with the derived internal
   Homs and `Rf_*` read at the standard model.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperShriek_rightAdjoint_and_duality_of_isProper :
    (∀ M : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y.left, DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow M.obj →
        DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow ((upperShriek f j).obj M).obj) ∧
      (∀ (a : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y.left ⥤ quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X.left)
          (_ : DerivedPushforward.qcqsRestrictedDerivedPushforward f.left ⊣ a),
        Nonempty (upperShriekPlus f j ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ≅ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ a)) ∧
      ∀ (K : Std X.left) (_ : minusCoh X.left K) (M : (qcoh Y.left).FullSubcategory)
        (_ : @DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow Y.left.Modules _ _
          (PerfectApproximation.standardModel Y.left) M.obj),
        Nonempty ((push f.left).obj (((sheafHom X.left).obj (op K)).obj
            ((comparison X.left).inverse.obj
              ((upperShriek f j).obj ⟨(comparison Y.left).functor.obj M.obj, M.property⟩).obj)) ≅
          ((sheafHom Y.left).obj (op ((push f.left).obj K))).obj M.obj)
declarations.comment: clause (2) in full: for a proper morphism f of FTS S and any compactification, f^! carries D^+_QCoh into D^+_QCoh and is the restriction to D^+_QCoh of every right adjoint of Rf_* on D_QCoh, and Rf_* RHom(K, f^! M) = RHom(Rf_* K, M) for K in D^-_Coh(O_X) and M in D^+_QCoh(O_Y) (the sheafy trace of Tag 0B6H, invertible by Tag 0GEW)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_sheafHomDualizingIsoOfIsProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0AU3, clause (4)(c).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme, let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of `FTS S`, let `ω_Y` be a dualizing complex on `Y` and
`ω_X = f^!ω_Y` (at any compactification). Then
`Rf_* R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(K, ω_X) ≅ R𝓗om_{𝒪_Y}(Rf_*K, ω_Y)` for `K ∈ D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_sheafHomDualizingIsoOfIsProper {ω : Std Y.left}
    (hω : TwistedInverseImageDuality.IsDualizing ω) (K : Std X.left) (hK : minusCoh X.left K) :
    Nonempty ((push f.left).obj (((sheafHom X.left).obj (op K)).obj
        (upperShriekDualizing f j hω)) ≅
      ((sheafHom Y.left).obj (op ((push f.left).obj K))).obj ω)
declarations.comment: clause (4)(c): for a proper morphism f : X to Y of FTS S, a dualizing complex omega_Y on Y and omega_X = f^! omega_Y at any compactification, Rf_* RHom(K, omega_X) = RHom(Rf_* K, omega_Y) for K in D^-_Coh(O_X); clause (2) at M = omega_Y

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.nonempty_upperShriekIsoPullbackTensorOfSmoothOfIsProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Section 0AU3, clause (9).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a smooth proper morphism of relative dimension `d` of `FTS S`, with `f^!`
computed at any compactification. Then `f^!(-) ≅ Lf^*(-) ⊗ᴸ_{𝒪_X} Ω^d_{X/Y}[d]` as functors on
`D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`, where `Ω^d_{X/Y} = ∧^d Ω_{X/Y}` and `[d]` places it in degree `-d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperShriekIsoPullbackTensorOfSmoothOfIsProper :
    Nonempty (((ObjectProperty.ι _ : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel Y.left ⥤ _) ⋙
        quasiCoherentDerivedPullback' f.left ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _) ⋙
      (derivedTensor X.left).flip.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.left.Modules (-(d : ℤ))).obj
          (Scheme.Modules.exteriorPower (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials f.left) d)) ≅
      (ObjectProperty.ι _ : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel Y.left ⥤ _) ⋙
        upperShriek f j ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _)
declarations.comment: clause (9): for a smooth proper morphism f of relative dimension d of FTS S and any compactification, f^!(-) = Lf^*(-) tensor Omega^d_{X/Y}[d] as functors on D^+_QCoh(O_Y); from Tag 0B6U (e) (f is perfect), clause (2) and Tag 0BRT

registrations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_upperShriekPseudofunctor
registrations.comment: clause (1): the functors f^! of Tag 0AA0 on D^+_QCoh, with the canonical isomorphisms (g o f)^! = f^! o g^! of Tag 0ATX, form a pseudofunctor on FTS_S (Tag 0ATY)

registrations.name: Stacks.Duality.coherentDuality_spec
registrations.comment: clause (3): for a dualizing complex omega on a locally Noetherian scheme X (in particular an object of FTS_S), D = RHom(-, omega) is an anti-equivalence of D_Coh(O_X) with the canonical isomorphism id = D o D, exchanging D^+_Coh and D^-_Coh and inducing an anti-equivalence of D^b_Coh when X is quasi-compact (Tag 0A89)

registrations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingComplex_upperShriek_obj
registrations.comment: clause (4)(a): for f : X to Y in FTS_S and omega_Y a dualizing complex on Y, f^! omega_Y (at any compactification) is a dualizing complex on X (Tag 0AA3)

registrations.name: Stacks.Duality.UpperShriekDuality.upperShriekDualityIso
registrations.comment: clause (4)(b): for f : X to Y in FTS_S and K a dualizing complex on Y, f^! M = D_X(Lf^* D_Y(M)) naturally in M in D^+_Coh(O_Y), D_Y = RHom(-, K), D_X = RHom(-, f^! K) (Tag 0AU2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.DualizingBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AU4.** The standing situation of the section on glueing dualizing
complexes: a Noetherian scheme `S` together with a dualizing complex `ω_S^•` on it, in the
sense of [Stacks, Tag 0A87].
declarations.statement: structure DualizingBase
declarations.comment: the Situation: a Noetherian scheme with a chosen dualizing complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.UpperShriek.overlapCompareRestrict_cocycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AU6.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0AU4] let `X` be of finite type over
`S` and let `𝒰 : X = ⋃ U_i` be a finite covering of `X` by opens separated and of finite type
over `S`. Let `ω_i^•` be the local models and `φ_{ij} : ω_i^•|_{U_i ∩ U_j} ≅ ω_j^•|_{U_i ∩ U_j}`
the canonical comparisons of the discussion preceding Definition [Stacks, Tag 0AUA]. Then for
all `i, j, k`

`φ_{ik}|_{U_i ∩ U_j ∩ U_k} = φ_{jk}|_{U_i ∩ U_j ∩ U_k} ∘ φ_{ij}|_{U_i ∩ U_j ∩ U_k}`

in `D(𝒪_{U_i ∩ U_j ∩ U_k})`. Composition is written left to right, so the right hand side
below reads `φ_{ij}` followed by `φ_{jk}`.

The restrictions are `Stacks.Duality.UpperShriek.overlapCompareRestrict`, i.e. the conjugation
of `Stacks.Duality.UpperShriek.restrictCompare`; the proof identifies all three with
comparisons built directly on the triple overlap
(`Stacks.Duality.UpperShriek.overlapCompareRestrict_eq`, which is the coherence
[Stacks, Tag 0ATY]) and then cancels
(`Stacks.Duality.UpperShriek.localCompare_trans`).
declarations.statement:
theorem overlapCompareRestrict_cocycle (𝒰 : SeparatedCovering p ι) (i j k : ι) :
    A.overlapCompareRestrict hp ωS 𝒰 i k (𝒰.U i ⊓ 𝒰.U j ⊓ 𝒰.U k)
        (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left) inf_le_right) =
      A.overlapCompareRestrict hp ωS 𝒰 i j (𝒰.U i ⊓ 𝒰.U j ⊓ 𝒰.U k) inf_le_left ≪≫
        A.overlapCompareRestrict hp ωS 𝒰 j k (𝒰.U i ⊓ 𝒰.U j ⊓ 𝒰.U k)
          (le_inf (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right) inf_le_right)
declarations.comment: item (3) of the discussion before Definition 0AUA: the cocycle condition phi_ik = phi_jk after phi_ij for the canonical comparisons of the local models, restricted to the triple overlap U_i cap U_j cap U_k. RESTRICTED only in that the upper-shriek formalism of Stacks 0A9Y/0ATX/0ATY is the parameter UpperShriek, as in 0AUB and 0AUC; the coherence 0ATY, which the source cites for item (3), is its factorIso_assoc field

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Normalized.existsUnique_iso_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AU7]** In Situation 0AU4, let `X` be of finite type over `S` and `𝒰` a finite
open covering of `X` by schemes separated over `S`. A dualizing complex normalized relative to
`ω_S^•` and `𝒰` is unique up to unique isomorphism: for two of them, `(K, α_i)` and `(K', α'_i)`,
exactly one isomorphism `K ≅ K'` carries `α_i` to `α'_i` on every member.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_nagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) {ι : Type w}
    {𝒰 : SeparatedCovering p ι} (𝒩 𝒩' : Normalized UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS 𝒰) :
    ∃! e : 𝒩.complex ≅ 𝒩'.complex, ∀ i,
      (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek (𝒰.U i).ι (hp.isShriekable_ι _)).mapIso e ≪≫
        𝒩'.localIso i = 𝒩.localIso i

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Normalized.exists_existsUnique_iso_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AU8]** In Situation 0AU4, let `X` be of finite type over `S` and `𝒰`, `𝒱` two
finite open coverings of `X` by schemes separated over `S`. If `(K, α_i)` is a dualizing complex
normalized relative to `ω_S^•` and `𝒰`, there is a dualizing complex `(K', α'_j)` normalized
relative to `ω_S^•` and `𝒱`, and the two are canonically isomorphic: exactly one isomorphism
`K ≅ K'` carries the restriction of `α_i` to `U_i ∩ V_j` to that of `α'_j`, for all `i`, `j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_existsUnique_iso_nagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    {ι J : Type w} {𝒰 : SeparatedCovering p ι} (𝒱 : SeparatedCovering p J)
    (𝒩 : Normalized UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS 𝒰) :
    ∃ 𝒩' : Normalized UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS 𝒱,
      (haveI := hp.source_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex 𝒩'.complex.obj.obj) ∧
      ∃! e : 𝒩.complex ≅ 𝒩'.complex, ∀ i j,
        (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek (𝒰.U i ⊓ 𝒱.U j).ι (hp.isShriekable_ι _)).mapIso e ≪≫
          UpperShriek.nagata.restrictLocalIso hp ωS 𝒩'.complex
            (inf_le_right : 𝒰.U i ⊓ 𝒱.U j ≤ 𝒱.U j) (𝒱.shriekable j) (𝒩'.localIso j) =
        UpperShriek.nagata.restrictLocalIso hp ωS 𝒩.complex
          (inf_le_left : 𝒰.U i ⊓ 𝒱.U j ≤ 𝒰.U i) (𝒰.shriekable i) (𝒩.localIso i)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.Normalized.exists_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AU9]** In Situation 0AU4, let `X` be of finite type over `S` and `𝒰` a finite
open covering of `X` by schemes separated over `S`. Then there exists a dualizing complex
normalized relative to `ω_S^•` and `𝒰`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    {ι : Type w} (𝒰 : SeparatedCovering p ι) :
    ∃ 𝒩 : Normalized UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS 𝒰,
      haveI := hp.source_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex 𝒩.complex.obj.obj

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingComplex_normalizedDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUA], `ω_X^•` is a dualizing complex.** Let `S` be Noetherian with a
dualizing complex `ω_S^•` and `X` of finite type over `S`. The dualizing complex `ω_X^•`
normalized relative to `ω_S^•` is a dualizing complex on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_normalizedDualizingComplex :
    haveI := hp.source_noetherian
    IsDualizingComplex (normalizedDualizingComplex hp ωS hωS).complex.obj.obj
declarations.comment: ω_X^• is a dualizing complex on X

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.existsUnique_iso_normalizedDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUA], uniqueness up to unique isomorphism.** Let `S` be Noetherian with a
dualizing complex `ω_S^•` and `X` of finite type over `S`. For any complex `K` on `X` with
isomorphisms `β_U : K|_U ≅ (U → S)^! ω_S^•` for the opens `U ⊆ X` separated over `S`,
compatible with restriction, exactly one isomorphism `K ≅ ω_X^•` carries `β_U` to the
isomorphism `α_U` of `ω_X^•` for every such `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_normalizedDualizingComplex
    (𝒦 : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS) :
    ∃! e : 𝒦.complex ≅ (normalizedDualizingComplex hp ωS hωS).complex,
      ∀ (W : X.Opens) (hW : IsShriekable (W.ι ≫ p)),
        (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek W.ι (hp.isShriekable_ι W)).mapIso e ≪≫
          (normalizedDualizingComplex hp ωS hωS).localIso W hW = 𝒦.localIso W hW
declarations.comment: the pair (ω_X^•, α_U) is unique up to unique isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.existsUnique_iso_normalizedDualizingComplex_toNormalized
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUA], normalized relative to every covering.** Let `S` be Noetherian with a
dualizing complex `ω_S^•`, `X` of finite type over `S` and `𝒰 : X = ⋃ U_i` a finite open
covering by opens separated over `S`. Then `(ω_X^•, α_{U_i})` is a dualizing complex normalized
relative to `ω_S^•` and `𝒰` (`Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.toNormalized`), and it is the one
up to unique isomorphism: for every dualizing complex `(K, β_i)` normalized relative to `ω_S^•`
and `𝒰`, exactly one isomorphism `K ≅ ω_X^•` carries `β_i` to `α_{U_i}` for all `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_normalizedDualizingComplex_toNormalized {ι : Type w}
    (𝒰 : SeparatedCovering p ι) (𝒩 : Normalized UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS 𝒰) :
    ∃! e : 𝒩.complex ≅ ((normalizedDualizingComplex hp ωS hωS).toNormalized 𝒰).complex,
      ∀ i, (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek (𝒰.U i).ι (hp.isShriekable_ι _)).mapIso e ≪≫
          ((normalizedDualizingComplex hp ωS hωS).toNormalized 𝒰).localIso i = 𝒩.localIso i
declarations.comment: (ω_X^•, α_{U_i}) is normalized relative to ω_S^• and every finite covering by opens separated over S

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.normalizedDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUA]** Let `S` be Noetherian with a dualizing complex `ω_S^•` and `X` of finite
type over `S`. The dualizing complex `ω_X^•` normalized relative to `ω_S^•`: a complex on `X` with
isomorphisms `α_W : ω_X^•|_W ≅ (W → S)^! ω_S^•` for every open `W` separated over `S`,
compatible with restriction. It is unique up to unique isomorphism
(`Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.existsUnique_iso_ofCompactifications`) and normalized relative
to `ω_S^•` and every finite covering of `X` by opens separated over `S`
(`Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.toNormalized`).
declarations.statement:
def normalizedDualizingComplex {X S : Scheme.{u}} {p : X ⟶ S}
    (hp : IsFiniteTypeOverNoetherian p) (ωS : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel S)
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) :
    NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_normalized_of_normalized
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUB]** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme carrying `ω_S^•`, let `q : Y ⟶ S`
and `p = f ≫ q : X ⟶ S` be of finite type, and let `𝒱` and `𝒰` be coverings of `Y` and of
`X` by opens separated and of finite type over `S`, with each `U_k` carried by `f` into
`V_{idx k}`. If `ω_X^•` is normalized relative to `ω_S^•` and `𝒰`, and `ω_Y^•` is normalized
relative to `ω_S^•` and `𝒱`, then `ω_X^•` is normalized relative to `ω_Y^•` and `𝒰` read over
`Y`.

Normalization here is the primitive notion of the text of [Stacks, Tag 0AU5] -- the pair
`(K, α_i)` -- rather than the covering-free Definition [Stacks, Tag 0AUA], and it is the
notion the proof of 0AUB manipulates. That `ω_X^•` is again dualizing is not part of the
statement because `Normalized` does not record dualizing-ness; it is [Stacks, Tag 0AU8].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_normalized_of_normalized {𝒟 : Scheme.{u} → Type v}
    [∀ X : Scheme.{u}, Category.{v'} (𝒟 X)] (A : UpperShriek 𝒟) {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {q : Y ⟶ S} {p : X ⟶ S} (hpe : f ≫ q = p)
    (hp : IsFiniteTypeOverNoetherian p) (hq : IsFiniteTypeOverNoetherian q) (ωS : 𝒟 S)
    {ι : Type w} {J : Type w'} (𝒰 : SeparatedCovering p ι) (𝒱 : SeparatedCovering q J)
    (idx : ι → J) (hle : ∀ k, 𝒰.U k ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒱.U (idx k)) (𝒩X : Normalized A hp ωS 𝒰)
    (𝒩Y : Normalized A hq ωS 𝒱) :
    ∃ 𝒩 : Normalized A (hp.of_comp' hq hpe) 𝒩Y.complex (𝒰.overMid 𝒱 hp hq hpe idx hle),
      𝒩.complex = 𝒩X.complex
declarations.comment: assuming the upper-shriek formalism of Stacks 0A9E/0ATX/0ATY as the parameter UpperShriek, pending its landing

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.exists_relative_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUB]** In Situation 0AU4, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes of finite
type over `S` and `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` dualizing complexes normalized relative to `ω_S^•`. Then
`ω_X^•` is a dualizing complex normalized relative to `ω_Y^•`: `ω_Y^•` and `ω_X^•` are dualizing,
so `(Y, ω_Y^•)` is again as in Situation 0AU4, and `ω_X^•` carries isomorphisms
`ω_X^•|_W ≅ (W → Y)^! ω_Y^•` for every open `W` separated over `Y`, compatible with restriction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_relative_nagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS) :
    (haveI := hq.source_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex 𝒦Y.complex.obj.obj) ∧
    (haveI := hp.source_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex 𝒦X.complex.obj.obj) ∧
    ∃ 𝒦 : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata (hp.of_comp' hq hpe) 𝒦Y.complex,
      𝒦.complex = 𝒦X.complex

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.existsUnique_iso_shriekOfIsOpenImmersion_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUC], canonicity.** In Situation 0AU4, let `j : X ⟶ Y` be an open immersion
of schemes of finite type over `S` and `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` dualizing complexes normalized relative to
`ω_S^•`. Exactly one isomorphism `ω_X^• ≅ j^! ω_Y^•` carries the normalization `α_W` of `ω_X^•`
to that of `j^! ω_Y^•` (`shriekOfIsOpenImmersion`) for every open `W ⊆ X` separated over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_shriekOfIsOpenImmersion_nagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS) :
    ∃! e : 𝒦X.complex ≅
        (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek j (hq.isShriekable_of_isOpenImmersion j)).obj 𝒦Y.complex,
      ∀ (W : X.Opens) (hW : IsShriekable (W.ι ≫ p)),
        (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek W.ι (hp.isShriekable_ι W)).mapIso e ≪≫
          (𝒦Y.shriekOfIsOpenImmersion hpe hp).localIso W hW = 𝒦X.localIso W hW
declarations.comment: S Noetherian with dualizing complex ω_S, X → Y an open immersion of schemes of finite type over S; the unique isomorphism ω_X^• ≅ j^! ω_Y^• compatible with the normalizations

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.isoDerivedRestrictNagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUC]** In Situation 0AU4, let `j : X ⟶ Y` be an open immersion of schemes of
finite type over `S` and `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` dualizing complexes normalized relative to `ω_S^•`.
The canonical isomorphism `ω_X^• ≅ ω_Y^•|_X` in `D(𝒪_X)`: the unique isomorphism
`ω_X^• ≅ j^! ω_Y^•` compatible with the normalizations
(`existsUnique_iso_shriekOfIsOpenImmersion_nagata`), followed by `j^! = j^*`
([Stacks, Tag 0AU0]).
declarations.statement:
def isoDerivedRestrictNagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS) :
    𝒦X.complex.obj.obj ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor j).mapDerivedCategory.obj 𝒦Y.complex.obj.obj
declarations.comment: the resulting canonical isomorphism ω_X^• ≅ ω_Y^•|_X in D(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.isoDerivedRestrictNagata_eq
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUC], the canonical isomorphism is characterised by the normalizations**:
for any isomorphism `e : ω_X^• ≅ j^! ω_Y^•` compatible with the normalizations on every open of
`X` separated over `S`, `isoDerivedRestrictNagata` is `e` followed by `j^! = j^*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isoDerivedRestrictNagata_eq
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS)
    (e : 𝒦X.complex ≅
      (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek j (hq.isShriekable_of_isOpenImmersion j)).obj 𝒦Y.complex)
    (he : ∀ (W : X.Opens) (hW : IsShriekable (W.ι ≫ p)),
      (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek W.ι (hp.isShriekable_ι W)).mapIso e ≪≫
        (𝒦Y.shriekOfIsOpenImmersion hpe hp).localIso W hW = 𝒦X.localIso W hW) :
    isoDerivedRestrictNagata hpe hωS 𝒦X 𝒦Y =
      (ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _).mapIso e ≪≫
        UpperShriek.shriekObjIsoDerivedRestrict nagataCompactification j
          (hq.isShriekable_of_isOpenImmersion j) 𝒦Y.complex
declarations.comment: the canonical isomorphism ω_X^• ≅ ω_Y^•|_X is characterized through j^! = j^*

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingIsoRightAdjointObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AUD.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes of finite type over
the base of [Stacks, Tag 0AU4], with structure morphisms `q : Y ⟶ S` and `p : X ⟶ S` and
`f ≫ q = p`. Let `a` be the right adjoint of `Rf_*` of [Stacks, Tag 0A9E]. If `ω_X^•` and
`ω_Y^•` are normalized relative to `ω_S^•`, there is a canonical isomorphism
`a(ω_Y^•) ≅ ω_X^•`.

This is the argument of the source in the case where the schemes are separated over `S`: there
`ω_X^• = p^!ω_S^•` and `ω_Y^• = q^!ω_S^•`, the properness of `f` enters only through the
identification of `f^!` with `a`, and the composition comparison `f^! ∘ q^! ≅ p^!` — the
`factorIso` field of `Stacks.Duality.UpperShriek` — finishes it.
declarations.statement:
def dualizingIsoRightAdjointObj (A : UpperShriek 𝒟) {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {q : Y ⟶ S} {p : X ⟶ S} (hfq : f ≫ q = p)
    (hf : IsShriekable f) (hq : IsShriekable q) (hp : IsShriekable p)
    {a : 𝒟 Y ⥤ 𝒟 X} (hfa : A.shriek f hf ≅ a)
    (ωS : 𝒟 S) {ωX : 𝒟 X} {ωY : 𝒟 Y}
    (nX : ωX ≅ (A.shriek p hp).obj ωS) (nY : ωY ≅ (A.shriek q hq).obj ωS) :
    a.obj ωY ≅ ωX
declarations.comment:
RESTRICTED: the upper shriek formalism is a parameter, normalization is taken in
the separated form omega_X = p^! omega_S, and the identification of f^! with the right adjoint,
which is the only place properness is used, is a hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.twistedInverseImageObjIsoNagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUD]** In Situation 0AU4, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of schemes of
finite type over `S`, `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` the dualizing complexes normalized relative to `ω_S^•`,
and `a` the right adjoint of `Rf_*` ([Stacks, Tag 0A9E]). Then there is a canonical isomorphism
`a(ω_Y^•) ≅ ω_X^•`.
declarations.statement:
def twistedInverseImageObjIsoNagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) [IsProper f]
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS) :
    haveI := hq.source_noetherian
    haveI := hp.source_noetherian
    (twistedInverseImage f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).obj
        𝒦Y.complex.obj ≅ 𝒦X.complex.obj

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.normalizedUpperShriek
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUE], the closing remark on the separated case.** Let `X` be separated and
of finite type over a Noetherian scheme `S` with structure morphism `p`, and let `ω_S^•` be a
complex on `S`. Then `p^!ω_S^•` is normalized relative to `ω_S^•`: its restriction to each
member of a covering of `X` by opens separated over `S` is canonically the local model there,
compatibly on overlaps.
declarations.statement: def normalizedUpperShriek {ι : Type w} (𝒰 : SeparatedCovering p ι) : Normalized A hp ωS 𝒰
declarations.comment: the closing remark, first half only: for X separated over the base the complex p^! omega_S^bullet is normalized relative to omega_S^bullet. The second half of the remark, f_new^! K = f^! K, is NOT carried, and neither are parts (1), (3), (5), (6); parts (2) and (4) are elsewhere. RESTRICTED: the upper-shriek formalism of Stacks 0A9Y/0ATX/0ATY is the parameter UpperShriek, pending its landing

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.fNewShriekObjIsoDualizing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AUE, part (4).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes of finite
type over the base of [Stacks, Tag 0AU4] and let `ω_X^•` and `ω_Y^•` be the complexes
normalized relative to `ω_S^•`, [Stacks, Tag 0AU5]. Then

`f_new^! ω_Y^• ≅ ω_X^•`.

The computation is the source's: `D_Y(ω_Y^•) ≅ 𝒪_Y` because `ω_Y^•` is dualizing, `Lf^*` carries
the unit to the unit, and `D_X(𝒪_X) ≅ ω_X^•` by `Stacks.Duality.relativeDualObjUnit`. The
statement is not an identity by definition: `Stacks.Duality.fNewShriek` unfolds the left hand
side to `R𝓗om(Lf^* R𝓗om(ω_Y^•, ω_Y^•), ω_X^•)`, and the three steps above are what turn that
into `ω_X^•`.
declarations.statement:
def fNewShriekObjIsoDualizing (f : X ⟶ Y) (ωX : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (ωY : DerivedCategory Y.Modules)
    (eY : (relativeDual ωY).obj (op ωY) ≅ 𝟙_ (DerivedCategory Y.Modules))
    (ef : (derivedPullback f).obj (𝟙_ (DerivedCategory Y.Modules)) ≅
      𝟙_ (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) :
    (fNewShriek f ωX ωY).obj ωY ≅ ωX
declarations.comment:
part (4): omega_X is f_new^! of omega_Y for a finite-type morphism over the base.
RESTRICTED: the closed monoidal structure on the derived categories is an instance argument, and
the two inputs the source names are hypotheses -- the identification R Hom(omega_Y, omega_Y) =
O_Y coming from omega_Y being dualizing, and the unit half Lf^* O_Y = O_X of the monoidality of
the derived pullback

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.fNewShriekStructureObjIsoDualizing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AUE, part (2).** For a scheme `X` of finite type over the base of
[Stacks, Tag 0AU4], with structure morphism `π : X ⟶ S`, the complex normalized relative to
`ω_S^•` is what `π_new^!` does to `ω_S^•`:

`ω_X^• ≅ (X → S)_new^! ω_S^•`.

This is `Stacks.Duality.fNewShriekObjIsoDualizing` at the structure morphism, read in the
vocabulary of the Situation: the two inputs become `D_S(ω_S^•) ≅ 𝒪_S`, which is the homothety
condition of the dualizing complex `B.isDualizing` names, and `Lπ^* 𝒪_S ≅ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
def fNewShriekStructureObjIsoDualizing
    (eS : (relativeDual B.dualizing).obj (op B.dualizing) ≅
      𝟙_ (DerivedCategory B.scheme.Modules))
    (ep : (derivedPullback Xb.str).obj (𝟙_ (DerivedCategory B.scheme.Modules)) ≅
      𝟙_ (DerivedCategory Xb.scheme.Modules)) :
    (fNewShriek Xb.str Xb.dualizing B.dualizing).obj B.dualizing ≅ Xb.dualizing
declarations.comment:
part (2): omega_X is the new twisted inverse image of omega_S along the structure
morphism. RESTRICTED: the closed monoidal structure on the derived categories is an instance
argument, and the identification R Hom(omega_S, omega_S) = O_S implied by B.isDualizing together
with the unit half Lpi^* O_S = O_X of the monoidality of the derived pullback are hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.existsUnique_iso_upperShriekPlus_of_isSeparated_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUE], the closing remark, first half.** In Situation 0AU4, if `X` is
separated over `S`, with structure morphism `p`, the dualizing complex `ω_X^•` normalized
relative to `ω_S^•` is canonically isomorphic to `p^! ω_S^•`, for the upper shriek functor `p^!`
of any compactification `j` of `p` ([Stacks, Tag 0A9Y]): exactly one isomorphism
`ω_X^• ≅ p^!_j ω_S^•` carries the normalization `α_W` of `ω_X^•` to the canonical
`(p^! ω_S^•)|_W ≅ (W → S)^! ω_S^•` for every open `W` separated over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_upperShriekPlus_of_isSeparated_nagata {X S : Scheme.{u}} {p : X ⟶ S}
    {hp : IsFiniteTypeOverNoetherian p} {ωS : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel S}
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) [IsSeparated p]
    (𝒦 : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS) (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk p)) :
    haveI := hp.base_noetherian
    ∃! e : 𝒦.complex ≅ (upperShriekPlus (ftsHomOf p
        (isShriekable_of_isSeparated_of_isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian hp).separatedFiniteType
        (isSeparatedFiniteType_id S) (Category.comp_id p)) j).obj ωS,
      ∀ (W : X.Opens) (hW : IsShriekable (W.ι ≫ p)),
        (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek W.ι (hp.isShriekable_ι W)).mapIso
            (e ≪≫ (DominatingCompactification.upperShriekPlusIso (ftsHomOf p
              (isShriekable_of_isSeparated_of_isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian hp).separatedFiniteType
              (isSeparatedFiniteType_id S) (Category.comp_id p)) j
              (nagataCompactification p
                (isShriekable_of_isSeparated_of_isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian hp))).app ωS) ≪≫
          upperShriekLocalIso UpperShriek.nagata hp
            (isShriekable_of_isSeparated_of_isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian hp) ωS hW =
        𝒦.localIso W hW
declarations.comment: the closing remark, first half: omega_X = (X -> S)^! omega_S for X separated over S

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.fNewShriekObjIsoNagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUE] part (4).** In Situation 0AU4, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of schemes
of finite type over `S` and `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` the dualizing complexes normalized relative to
`ω_S^•` (for the upper shriek functors of Nagata compactifications). Then
`ω_X^• ≅ f_new^! ω_Y^•`.
declarations.statement:
def fNewShriekObjIsoNagata (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS) :
    stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X ≅
      (fNewShriekStd f (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X)
        (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦Y)).obj (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦Y)
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.fNewShriekStructureObjIsoNagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUE] part (2).** In Situation 0AU4, for `X` of finite type over `S` with
structure morphism `p : X ⟶ S` and `ω_X^•` the dualizing complex normalized relative to `ω_S^•`,
`ω_X^• ≅ (X → S)_new^! ω_S^•`, where `(X → S)_new^!` is formed with `ω_S^•` itself as the
normalized complex of `S`.
declarations.statement:
def fNewShriekStructureObjIsoNagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS) :
    stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X ≅
      (fNewShriekStd p (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X) (baseStdComplex ωS)).obj
        (baseStdComplex ωS)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.coherentDuality_spec_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUE] part (3).** In Situation 0AU4, for `X` of finite type over `S` and
`ω_X^•` normalized relative to `ω_S^•`, the duality `D_X = R𝓗om(-, ω_X^•)` is an involution of
`D_Coh(𝒪_X)`: it carries `D_Coh(𝒪_X)` into itself, is an anti-equivalence of it with
`id ≅ D_X ∘ D_X` given by biduality, exchanges `D^+_Coh` and `D^-_Coh`, and is an
anti-equivalence of `D^b_Coh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem coherentDuality_spec_nagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    (𝒦 : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS) :
    haveI := hp.source_noetherian
    cohStd X (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦) ∧
    (∀ M : Std X, cohStd X M →
      cohStd X ((dualInto (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦)).obj (op M))) ∧
    (coherentDuality X
      (isDualizing_stdComplex nagataCompactification hωS 𝒦)).IsEquivalence ∧
    IsIso (coherentBiduality X
      (isDualizing_stdComplex nagataCompactification hωS 𝒦)) ∧
    (∀ M : Std X, cohStd X M →
      (plusCoh X M ↔
        minusCoh X ((dualInto (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦)).obj (op M))) ∧
      (minusCoh X M ↔
        plusCoh X ((dualInto (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦)).obj (op M)))) ∧
    (boundedCoherentDuality X
      (isDualizing_stdComplex nagataCompactification hωS 𝒦)).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.fNewShriekPlusCohNagata_obj
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUE] part (5).** In Situation 0AU4, for a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes of
finite type over `S`, `f_new^!` is a functor `D^+_Coh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D^+_Coh(𝒪_X)` and
`f_new^! M = D_X(Lf^* D_Y(M))` for `M ∈ D^+_Coh(𝒪_Y)`: for such `M` the complex
`D_X(Lf^* D_Y(M))` lies in `D^+_Coh(𝒪_X)`, and it is the value of `f_new^!` at `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fNewShriekPlusCohNagata_obj (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj)
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS) (M : (plusCoh Y).FullSubcategory) :
    plusCoh X ((dualInto (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X)).obj (op ((pull f).obj
        ((dualInto (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦Y)).obj (op M.obj))))) ∧
      ((fNewShriekPlusCohNagata f hωS 𝒦X 𝒦Y).obj M).obj =
        (dualInto (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X)).obj (op ((pull f).obj
          ((dualInto (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦Y)).obj (op M.obj))))
declarations.comment: part (5)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.fNewShriekIsoRightAdjointNagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUE] part (6), first assertion.** In Situation 0AU4, for a proper morphism
`f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes of finite type over `S` and the dualizing complexes `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•`
normalized relative to `ω_S^•`, `f_new^!` is isomorphic to the restriction to `D^+_Coh(𝒪_Y)` of
the right adjoint `a` of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)` ([Stacks, Tag 0A9E]).
declarations.statement:
def fNewShriekIsoRightAdjointNagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) [IsProper f]
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS) :
    haveI := hq.source_noetherian
    haveI := hp.source_noetherian
    (plusCoh Y).ι ⋙ fNewShriekStd f (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X)
        (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦Y) ≅
      ObjectProperty.ιOfLE plusCoh_le_qcoh ⋙ rightAdjointStd f
declarations.comment: part (6), first assertion

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.fNewShriekSheafHomIsoNagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUE] part (6), the duality isomorphism.** In Situation 0AU4, for a proper
morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes of finite type over `S`, `K ∈ D^-_Coh(𝒪_X)` and
`M ∈ D^+_Coh(𝒪_Y)`, there is a canonical isomorphism
`Rf_* R𝓗om(K, f_new^! M) ≅ R𝓗om(Rf_* K, M)`.
declarations.statement:
def fNewShriekSheafHomIsoNagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) [IsProper f]
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS)
    (K : Std X) (hK : haveI := hp.source_noetherian; minusCoh X K)
    (M : (plusCoh Y).FullSubcategory) :
    (push f).obj (((sheafHom X).obj (op K)).obj
        ((fNewShriekStd f (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X)
          (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦Y)).obj M.obj)) ≅
      ((sheafHom Y).obj (op ((push f).obj K))).obj M.obj
declarations.comment: part (6), the isomorphism Rf_* RHom(K, f_new^! M) = RHom(Rf_* K, M)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.sheafHomDualizingIsoOfMinusCohNagata
declarations.statement:
def sheafHomDualizingIsoOfMinusCohNagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) [IsProper f]
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS)
    (K : Std X) (hK : haveI := hp.source_noetherian; minusCoh X K) :
    (push f).obj (((sheafHom X).obj (op K)).obj (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X)) ≅
      ((sheafHom Y).obj (op ((push f).obj K))).obj (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦Y)
declarations.comment: part (6), the isomorphism Rf_* RHom(K, omega_X) = RHom(Rf_* K, omega_Y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.upperShriekStdIsoFNewShriekNagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AUE], the closing remark, `f_new^! = f^!`.** In Situation 0AU4, let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be a separated morphism of schemes of finite type over `S` (for instance a morphism
between schemes separated over `S`) and `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` the dualizing complexes normalized
relative to `ω_S^•`. For every compactification `j` of `f`, the upper shriek functor `f^!` of
`j` ([Stacks, Tag 0A9Y]) satisfies `f^! K ≅ f_new^! K`, naturally in `K ∈ D^+_Coh(𝒪_Y)`.
declarations.statement:
def upperShriekStdIsoFNewShriekNagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) [IsSeparated f]
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS)
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk f)) :
    haveI := hq.source_noetherian
    UpperShriekDuality.upperShriekStd (ftsHomSelf (isShriekable_of_isSeparated hpe hp hq)) j ≅
      (plusCoh Y).ι ⋙ fNewShriekStd f (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦X)
        (stdComplex nagataCompactification 𝒦Y)
declarations.comment: the closing remark, second half: f_new^! K = f^! K for K in D^+_Coh

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.newShriekPseudofunctor
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0AU4], let `ω_X^•` be the dualizing complex
normalized relative to `ω_S^•` of each scheme `X` of finite type over `S`. The functors
`f_new^! = D_X ∘ Lf^* ∘ D_Y : D^+_Coh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D^+_Coh(𝒪_X)` and the arrows
`(g ∘ f)_new^! ⟶ f_new^! ∘ g_new^!` turn `D^+_Coh` into a pseudofunctor from the category of
schemes of finite type over `S` to the 2-category of categories: `X ↦ D^+_Coh(𝒪_X)`,
`f ↦ f_new^!`, with `mapComp` the inverse of the comparison
`f_new^! ∘ g_new^! ⟶ (g ∘ f)_new^!` given by the biduality `η_Y` ([Stacks, Tag 0A89]) and
`mapId` the inverse of `η_X : id ⟶ (id_X)_new^!`
(`Stacks.Duality.NewShriekPseudofunctor.comp`, `Stacks.Duality.NewShriekPseudofunctor.unit`,
`Stacks.Duality.newShriekPseudofunctor_map_obj_obj`).
declarations.statement:
def newShriekPseudofunctor {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian S]
    (ωS : quasiCoherentDerivedCategoryPlusOfModel S) (hωS : IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) :
    Pseudofunctor (LocallyDiscrete (SchemesOfFiniteTypeOver S)ᵒᵖ) Cat
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation.baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Essential finite presentation is preserved by base change.**  The target is written in the
canonical tensor-product model of the pushout; invariance under isomorphism identifies this with
any other model of the base change.
declarations.statement:
theorem baseChange {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {T : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T] [Algebra R S]
    (f : R →+* T) (h : f.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := R) (S := S) (A := S) (B := T)).toRingHom)
      |>.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation

declarations.name: exists_isLocalizationOfQuotientMap_mvPolynomial_atMaximal
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map of local rings, not necessarily local, that is essentially of finite
type. Then there are `n : ℕ` and a maximal ideal `𝔪 ⊆ R[x_1, …, x_n]` lying over the maximal ideal
of `R` such that `S` is a localization of a quotient of the local ring `R[x_1, …, x_n]_𝔪`,
compatibly with the `R`-algebra structures.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLocalizationOfQuotientMap_mvPolynomial_atMaximal
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsLocalRing R] [IsLocalRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.EssFiniteType R S] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (𝔪 : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)) (_ : 𝔪.IsMaximal),
      haveI : 𝔪.IsPrime := (‹𝔪.IsMaximal›).isPrime
      𝔪.comap (algebraMap R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)) = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ∧
      ∃ (g : Localization.AtPrime 𝔪 →+* S),
        g.comp (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime 𝔪)) = algebraMap R S ∧
        IsLocalizationOfQuotientMap g

declarations.name: Module.depth_eq_iSup_isWeaklyRegular_length
declarations.doc:
The `I`-depth of a finite `R`-module `M` is the supremum of the lengths of the sequences
`f₁, …, f_r ∈ I` such that `fᵢ` is a nonzerodivisor on `M/(f₁, …, f_{i-1})M`; that is, the
nonvanishing requirement `M/(f₁, …, f_r)M ≠ 0` on regular sequences and the case distinction
`I • M = M` in the definition of the depth may be dropped together.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_eq_iSup_isWeaklyRegular_length (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    depth R I M =
      ⨆ rs ∈ {rs : List R | (∀ r ∈ rs, r ∈ I) ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular M rs},
        (rs.length : ℕ∞)

declarations.name: Module.depth_lt_top
declarations.doc:
**Depth along an ideal is finite over a Noetherian ring.** If `R` is Noetherian, `M` is a
finite `R`-module and `I` is an ideal of `R` with `I • M ≠ M`, then `depth_I(M) < ∞`; that is,
the lengths of the `M`-regular sequences contained in `I` are bounded. The hypothesis
`I • M ≠ M` also forces `M ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_lt_top (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (hI : I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤) :
    depth R I M < ⊤

declarations.name: Module.depth_eq_iInf_depth_isLocalized_maximal
declarations.doc:
**Depth is the minimum of the depths of the localizations at the maximal ideals.** Let
`(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local ring, let `R → S` be a finite ring map and let `N` be a finite
`S`-module. Then the depth of `N` as an `R`-module along `𝔪` is the infimum, over the maximal
ideals `𝔪ᵢ` of `S`, of the depths of the localizations `N_{𝔪ᵢ}` over the local rings
`S_{𝔪ᵢ}`. Since `S` is semilocal the infimum is a minimum over a finite nonempty set, unless
`S` is the zero ring, in which case both sides are `⊤`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_eq_iInf_depth_isLocalized_maximal
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Module.Finite R S] {N : Type*} [AddCommGroup N] [Module S N] [Module.Finite S N]
    [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R S N]
    (Sₘ : MaximalSpectrum S → Type*) [∀ P, CommRing (Sₘ P)] [∀ P, Algebra S (Sₘ P)]
    [∀ P, IsLocalization.AtPrime (Sₘ P) P.asIdeal]
    (Nₘ : MaximalSpectrum S → Type*) [∀ P, AddCommGroup (Nₘ P)] [∀ P, Module S (Nₘ P)]
    [∀ P, Module (Sₘ P) (Nₘ P)] [∀ P, IsScalarTower S (Sₘ P) (Nₘ P)]
    (f : ∀ P, N →ₗ[S] Nₘ P) [∀ P, IsLocalizedModule P.asIdeal.primeCompl (f P)] :
    depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) N =
      ⨅ P : MaximalSpectrum S,
        haveI : IsLocalRing (Sₘ P) := IsLocalization.AtPrime.isLocalRing (Sₘ P) P.asIdeal
        depth (Sₘ P) (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Sₘ P)) (Nₘ P)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Abelian.comparison
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison data.** Its equivalence is `comparisonEquiv`, and its covariant
and contravariant maps are Yoneda composition with `Ext.mk₀` read through that equivalence.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def comparison : ExtOneComparison (C := C)
declarations.comment: the comparison itself; `isCanonicalExtOneComparison_comparison` is its defining properties and `eq_comparison_of_isCanonical` their uniqueness

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Abelian.isCanonicalExtOneComparison_comparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison is canonical.** `comparison` sends a short exact sequence to its derived
extension class, represents its covariant and contravariant maps by pushout and pullback of
short exact sequences, is natural in both variables, takes Baer sums to sums in `Ext¹`, and
matches the boundary maps of the two long exact `Ext` sequences.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCanonicalExtOneComparison_comparison :
    IsCanonicalExtOneComparison (comparison (C := C))
declarations.comment: the comparison has the announced properties: canonicity, representation of the two maps by pushout and pullback, naturality in both variables, additivity for Baer sums, and agreement with both connecting maps

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Abelian.eq_comparison_of_isCanonical
declarations.doc:
**The canonical comparison is unique.** Any comparison with the properties of
`IsCanonicalExtOneComparison` is `comparison`.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_comparison_of_isCanonical (c' : ExtOneComparison (C := C))
    (hc' : IsCanonicalExtOneComparison c') : c' = comparison
declarations.comment: uniqueness of the canonical comparison

declarations.name: dominates_iff_pushoutInl_universallyInjective
declarations.doc:
Let `f : M → N` and `g : M → M'` be maps of `R`-modules, and form the pushout
square `f' : M' → N'`, `g' : N → N'`. Then `g` dominates `f` if and only if `f'`
is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem dominates_iff_pushoutInl_universallyInjective
    {M N M' : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M']
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (g : M →ₗ[R] M') :
    Dominates.{u, u, u, u, u} f g ↔ UniversallyInjective (pushoutInl f g)

declarations.name: catenary_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem catenary_tfae (R : Type u) [CommRing R] :
    [ IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace (PrimeSpectrum R),
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
        IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace (PrimeSpectrum (Localization.AtPrime p)),
      ∀ (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal],
        IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace
          (PrimeSpectrum (Localization.AtPrime m)) ].TFAE
declarations.comment: catenary

declarations.name: universallyCatenary_tfae
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyCatenary_tfae (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    [ IsUniversallyCatenary R,
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], IsUniversallyCatenary (Localization.AtPrime p),
      ∀ (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal], IsUniversallyCatenary (Localization.AtPrime m) ].TFAE
declarations.comment: universally catenary

declarations.name: isCatenaryRing_iff_quotient_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian ring `R` is catenary if and only if `R ⧸ p` is catenary for every minimal prime
`p` of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCatenaryRing_iff_quotient_minimalPrimes
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsCatenaryRing R ↔
      ∀ p : Ideal R, (hp : p ∈ minimalPrimes R) →
        haveI : p.IsPrime := hp.1.1
        IsCatenaryRing (R ⧸ p)

declarations.name: isUniversallyCatenaryRing_iff_quotient_minimalPrimes
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian ring `R` is universally catenary if and only if `R ⧸ p` is universally catenary
for every minimal prime `p` of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyCatenaryRing_iff_quotient_minimalPrimes
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsUniversallyCatenaryRing R ↔
      ∀ p : Ideal R, (hp : p ∈ minimalPrimes R) →
        haveI : p.IsPrime := hp.1.1
        haveI : IsNoetherianRing (R ⧸ p) := inferInstance
        IsUniversallyCatenaryRing (R ⧸ p)

registrations.name: IsPrincipalIdealRing.isDedekindDomain
registrations.comment: a principal ideal domain is a Dedekind domain

declarations.name: isTorsionFree_of_injective_of_exact
declarations.doc:
For an injective exact pair of module maps, if the source and target modules are torsion-free,
then the middle module is torsion-free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_of_injective_of_exact
    {R : Type u} [Semiring R]
    {M : Type v} {M' : Type w} {M'' : Type x}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M']
    [AddCommGroup M''] [Module R M'']
    (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (g : M' →ₗ[R] M'')
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hfg : Function.Exact f g)
    [Module.IsTorsionFree R M] [Module.IsTorsionFree R M''] :
    Module.IsTorsionFree R M'

declarations.name: isTorsionFree_iff_isLocalized_maximal
declarations.doc:
A module over a domain is torsion-free if and only if its localization at every maximal ideal
is torsion-free over the corresponding localized ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_iff_isLocalized_maximal
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    (Rₚ : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Type w)
    [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], CommRing (Rₚ P)]
    [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Algebra R (Rₚ P)]
    [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], IsLocalization.AtPrime (Rₚ P) P]
    (Mₚ : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Type x)
    [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], AddCommMonoid (Mₚ P)]
    [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Module R (Mₚ P)]
    [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Module (Rₚ P) (Mₚ P)]
    [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], IsScalarTower R (Rₚ P) (Mₚ P)]
    (f : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], M →ₗ[R] Mₚ P)
    [∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], IsLocalizedModule.AtPrime P (f P)] :
    Module.IsTorsionFree R M ↔
      ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Module.IsTorsionFree (Rₚ P) (Mₚ P)

declarations.name: isTorsionFree_iff_exists_injective_to_finite_free
declarations.doc:
A finite module over a domain is torsion-free if and only if it embeds into a finite free
module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_iff_exists_injective_to_finite_free
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    Module.IsTorsionFree R M ↔
      ∃ N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R,
        Module.Finite R N ∧ Module.Free R N ∧
          ∃ f : M →ₗ[R] N, Function.Injective f

declarations.name: isTorsionFree_iff_finiteFreeEmbedding_iff_associatedPrimes_iff_propertyS1
declarations.doc:
For a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian domain, the following are equivalent: it is
torsion-free; it embeds into a finite free module; its only associated prime is zero; zero lies in
its support and it satisfies `(S₁)`; and zero lies in its support and it has no embedded associated
prime.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_iff_finiteFreeEmbedding_iff_associatedPrimes_iff_propertyS1
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M] :
    (Module.IsTorsionFree R M ↔
      ∃ N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R,
        Module.Finite R N ∧ Module.Free R N ∧
          ∃ f : M →ₗ[R] N, Function.Injective f) ∧
    ((∃ N : ModuleCat.{max u v} R,
        Module.Finite R N ∧ Module.Free R N ∧
          ∃ f : M →ₗ[R] N, Function.Injective f) ↔
      associatedPrimes R M = {⊥}) ∧
    (associatedPrimes R M = {⊥} ↔
      (⊥ : PrimeSpectrum R) ∈ Module.support R M ∧
        ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
          min 1 (Module.supportDim (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
              (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl M)) ≤
            (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
              (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
              (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl M) : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
    (((⊥ : PrimeSpectrum R) ∈ Module.support R M ∧
        ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
          min 1 (Module.supportDim (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
              (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl M)) ≤
            (Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
              (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal))
              (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl M) : WithBot ℕ∞)) ↔
      (⊥ : PrimeSpectrum R) ∈ Module.support R M ∧
        ∀ p ∈ associatedPrimes R M, Minimal (· ∈ associatedPrimes R M) p)

declarations.name: projective_of_finite_isTorsionFree
declarations.doc: A finite torsion-free module over a Dedekind domain is projective, hence finite locally free.
declarations.statement:
theorem projective_of_finite_isTorsionFree
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] [Module.IsTorsionFree R M] :
    Module.Projective R M

registrations.comment: (1), trivial torsion versus torsion-freeness

registrations.name: Module.free_iff_isTorsionFree
registrations.comment: (3), finite torsion-free modules over a PID are finite free

registrations.name: LinearMap.instIsTorsionFree
registrations.comment: the semilinear form specializes to linear maps over a domain

declarations.name: isTorsionFree_of_isReflexive_and_dualEval_isTorsion_and_injective_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AV0.** A reflexive module over a domain is torsion-free. For a finite module,
the kernel and cokernel of the canonical evaluation map into the double dual are torsion,
and that map is injective if and only if the module is torsion-free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_of_isReflexive_and_dualEval_isTorsion_and_injective_iff
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    (Module.IsReflexive R M → Module.IsTorsionFree R M) ∧
      (Module.Finite R M →
        Module.IsTorsion R (LinearMap.ker (Module.Dual.eval R M)) ∧
          Module.IsTorsion R
            (Module.Dual R (Module.Dual R M) ⧸ LinearMap.range (Module.Dual.eval R M))) ∧
      (Module.Finite R M →
        (Function.Injective (Module.Dual.eval R M) ↔ Module.IsTorsionFree R M))

declarations.name: reflexive_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AV1**.
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and `M` a finite `R`-module. The following are equivalent: `M` is
reflexive; `M_p` is a reflexive `R_p`-module for every prime `p`; `M_m` is a reflexive
`R_m`-module for every maximal ideal `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem reflexive_tfae
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    [ Module.IsReflexive R M,
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
        Module.IsReflexive (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl M),
      ∀ (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal],
        Module.IsReflexive (Localization.AtPrime m) (LocalizedModule m.primeCompl M)
    ].TFAE

declarations.name: isReflexive_iff_exists_finFree_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AV2.** A finite module over a Noetherian domain is reflexive if and only if it
fits into a short exact sequence `0 → M → F → N → 0` with `F` finite free and `N`
torsion-free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_iff_exists_finFree_shortExact
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    Module.IsReflexive R M ↔
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (N : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup N) (_ : Module R N),
        Module.IsTorsionFree R N ∧
          ∃ (f : M →ₗ[R] (Fin n → R)) (g : (Fin n → R) →ₗ[R] N),
            Function.Injective f ∧ Function.Exact f g ∧ Function.Surjective g

declarations.name: isReflexive_linearMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AV3.** Over a Noetherian domain, the module of linear maps from a finite module
into a finite reflexive module is reflexive.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_linearMap
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hN : Module.IsReflexive R N) :
    Module.IsReflexive R (M →ₗ[R] N)

declarations.name: Module.reflexiveHull
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AV4.** The reflexive hull of an `R`-module `M` is its double dual
`Hom_R(Hom_R(M, R), R)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Module.reflexiveHull (R : Type u) [CommSemiring R]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]

declarations.name: one_le_depth_and_two_le_depth_linearMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AV5.** If `M` and `N` are finite modules over a Noetherian local ring, then
`Hom(M, N)` has depth at least one (respectively, at least two) whenever `N` does.
declarations.statement:
theorem one_le_depth_and_two_le_depth_linearMap
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N] :
    ((1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) N →
      (1 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (M →ₗ[R] N)) ∧
    ((2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) N →
      (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth R (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (M →ₗ[R] N))

declarations.name: propertySk_linearMap_one_two_and_isTorsionFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AV6.** For finite modules `M` and `N` over a Noetherian ring, the module
`Hom_R(M, N)` inherits `(S₁)` and `(S₂)` from `N`; if the ring is a domain, it also
inherits the conjunction of torsion-freeness and `(S₂)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem propertySk_linearMap_one_two_and_isTorsionFree
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.Finite R N] :
    (PropertySkModule R N 1 → PropertySkModule R (M →ₗ[R] N) 1) ∧
      (PropertySkModule R N 2 → PropertySkModule R (M →ₗ[R] N) 2) ∧
      (IsDomain R → Module.IsTorsionFree R N → PropertySkModule R N 2 →
        Module.IsTorsionFree R (M →ₗ[R] N) ∧ PropertySkModule R (M →ₗ[R] N) 2)

declarations.name: injective_of_injective_localized_at_associatedPrimes
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 0AV7. If for every prime ideal `p` of the Noetherian ring `R` either
the localized map `φ_p : M_p → N_p` is injective or `p` is not an associated prime
of `M`, then `φ : M → N` is injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_of_injective_localized_at_associatedPrimes (φ : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (h : ∀ p : Ideal R, [p.IsPrime] →
      Function.Injective (LocalizedModule.map p.primeCompl φ) ∨ p ∉ associatedPrimes R M) :
    Function.Injective φ

declarations.name: bijective_of_bijective_localized_or_depth_two_and_notMem_associatedPrimes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AV8.** A map from a finite module over a Noetherian ring is bijective if, at
every prime, it is bijective after localization or the localized source has depth at least two
and the prime is not associated to the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_of_bijective_localized_or_depth_two_and_notMem_associatedPrimes
    {R M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] (φ : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (h : ∀ (p : Ideal R) (_ : p.IsPrime),
      Function.Bijective (LocalizedModule.map p.primeCompl φ) ∨
        2 ≤ Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))
          (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl M) ∧ p ∉ associatedPrimes R N) :
    Function.Bijective φ

declarations.name: bijective_of_bijective_localized_or_depth_two_of_isTorsionFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AV9.** A map from a finite nonzero module to a torsion-free module over a
Noetherian domain is bijective if, at every prime, either its localization is bijective or the
localized source has depth at least two.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_of_bijective_localized_or_depth_two_of_isTorsionFree
    {R M N : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] [Nontrivial M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.IsTorsionFree R N]
    (φ : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (h : ∀ (p : Ideal R) (_ : p.IsPrime),
      Function.Bijective (LocalizedModule.map p.primeCompl φ) ∨
        2 ≤ Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))
          (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl M)) :
    Function.Bijective φ

declarations.name: isReflexive_iff_localized_isReflexive_or_depth_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AVA.** A finite module over a Noetherian domain is reflexive if and only if, at
every prime, its localization is reflexive or has depth at least two.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_iff_localized_isReflexive_or_depth_two
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    Module.IsReflexive R M ↔
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime],
        Module.IsReflexive (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl M) ∨
          2 ≤ Module.depth (Localization.AtPrime p)
            (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))
            (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl M)

declarations.name: isReflexive_isTorsionFree_propertyS2_intersection_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AVB.** Let `R` be a Noetherian normal domain and `M` a finite `R`-module. The
following are equivalent: `M` is reflexive; `M` is torsion-free and satisfies `(S₂)`; and `M` is
torsion-free and equals the intersection of its localizations at the height-one primes inside
its generic fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_isTorsionFree_propertyS2_intersection_tfae
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsIntegrallyClosed R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    List.TFAE [
      Module.IsReflexive R M,
      Module.IsTorsionFree R M ∧ PropertySkModule R M 2,
      Module.IsTorsionFree R M ∧
        ∀ x : LocalizedModule (nonZeroDivisors R) M,
          x ∈ LinearMap.range (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (nonZeroDivisors R) M) ↔
            ∀ (p : Ideal R) (_ : p.IsPrime), p.height = 1 →
              ∃ (m : M) (s : R), s ∉ p ∧
                s • x = LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (nonZeroDivisors R) M m]

declarations.name: reflexiveHull_eq_iInf_localization_mod_torsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0AVC.** Let `R` be a Noetherian normal domain and `M` a finite `R`-module. Inside
the generic fibre, the reflexive hull `M⁎⁎` is the intersection over height-one primes `p` of
`M_p / (M_p)_tors`, and this is also the intersection of `(M / M_tors)_p`.

Membership in the three submodules is written elementwise, with the first condition using the
canonical localization of the evaluation map `M → M⁎⁎`.
declarations.statement:
theorem reflexiveHull_eq_iInf_localization_mod_torsion
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsIntegrallyClosed R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    ∀ x : LocalizedModule (nonZeroDivisors R) M,
      (((IsLocalizedModule.map (nonZeroDivisors R)
          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (nonZeroDivisors R) M)
          (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (nonZeroDivisors R)
            (Module.Dual R (Module.Dual R M)))
          (Module.Dual.eval R M)) x ∈
            LinearMap.range (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (nonZeroDivisors R)
              (Module.Dual R (Module.Dual R M)))) ↔
        ∀ (p : Ideal R) (_ : p.IsPrime), p.height = 1 →
          ∃ (m : M) (s : R), s ∉ p ∧
            s • x = LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (nonZeroDivisors R) M m) ∧
      ((∀ (p : Ideal R) (_ : p.IsPrime), p.height = 1 →
          ∃ (m : M) (s : R), s ∉ p ∧
            s • x = LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (nonZeroDivisors R) M m) ↔
        ∀ (p : Ideal R) (_ : p.IsPrime), p.height = 1 →
          ∃ (q : M ⧸ Submodule.torsion R M) (s : R), s ∉ p ∧
            s • x = Module.torsionQuotientToGenericFiber R M q)

declarations.name: Module.injective_iff_exact_linearYoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AVD.** An `R`-module `J` is injective if and only if its contravariant Hom
functor `Hom_R(-, J)` is exact.

Exactness of a functor out of `(ModuleCat R)ᵒᵖ` is tested after composing with the forgetful
functor to abelian groups, where the composite is the preadditive Yoneda functor at `J`, for
which Mathlib already characterises injectivity.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.injective_iff_exact_linearYoneda (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    (J : Type v) [AddCommGroup J] [Module R J] :
    Module.Injective R J ↔
      exactFunctor _ _ ((linearYoneda R (ModuleCat.{v} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R J))

declarations.name: Module.injective_iff_subsingleton_ext_one
declarations.doc:
