**Stacks 0AVE.** An `R`-module `J` is injective if and only if `Ext¹_R(M, J)` vanishes for
every `R`-module `M`.

Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.injective_iff_subsingleton_ext_one` is this criterion for an object of
an abelian category with an `Ext` theory; here it is read off for modules, the quantifier running
over `R`-modules rather than over objects of `ModuleCat R`. The two agree because every object of
`ModuleCat.{v} R` is `ModuleCat.of R` of its own carrier.
declarations.statement:
theorem Module.injective_iff_subsingleton_ext_one (R : Type u) [Ring R] [Small.{v} R]
    (J : Type v) [AddCommGroup J] [Module R J] :
    Module.Injective R J ↔
      ∀ (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M],
        Subsingleton (Abelian.Ext (ModuleCat.of R M) (ModuleCat.of R J) 1)

registrations.name: ModuleCat.injective_iff_subsingleton_ext_quotient_one
registrations.comment: injectivity is equivalent to vanishing Ext^1 from quotients by ideals

registrations.name: ModuleCat.ext_quotient_one_subsingleton_iff
registrations.comment: vanishing Ext^1 is equivalent to extending maps from ideals

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ExtSpectralSequence.exists_ext_homology_spectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AVH.** For `M` in an abelian category with enough injectives and `K` in its bounded
below derived category, there is a filtered complex `T` of abelian groups, together with the
filtration, cycle, boundary and induced-filtration data `Fil`, `Z`, `D`, `FH` of
[Stacks, Tag 012M], a spectral sequence `E` whose page at `(r, p, q)` is identified with the
canonical subquotient `Z_r^{p,q}/(D_r^{p,q} ⊓ Z_r^{p,q})` and whose differential is induced by the
differential of `T`, and isomorphisms `Hⁿ(T) ≅ Extⁿ(M, K)` and `E₂ⁱʲ ≅ Extⁱ(M, Hʲ(K))`, the latter
factoring through the canonical page-`2` subquotient. The spectral sequence is bounded, the
filtration it induces on each `Hⁿ(T)` is finite, it converges to `H^*(T)` (the differentials
vanish for `r ≫ 0` and the inclusions (012S) and (012T) for the stable cycles and boundaries are
equalities, which by [Stacks, Tag 012V] says exactly that `E_∞^{p,q}` is the graded piece
`gr^pHⁿ(T)`), and on each total-degree diagonal every page vanishes outside a finite range of
columns, so the spectral sequence degenerates there.

`T` is `Tot(Hom(M, I))` for `I` a Cartan-Eilenberg resolution ([Stacks, Tag 015I]) of a bounded
below complex of injective objects representing `K`, filtered by the second coordinate; the pages
are identified by [Stacks, Tag 0130] and the second page is rewritten with [Stacks, Tag 015J] and
`StacksDraft.DerivedCoyoneda.rightDerivedSmallCoyonedaIso`. The column vanishing is deduced from
the finiteness of the diagonals of the zeroth page, which propagates to every later page because
each page object is the homology of the previous one
(`CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.isZero_page_of_le`); it does not involve the stable cycles.

This is the `0AVH` endpoint; `exists_ext_homology_spectralSequence_of_data` is the same statement
with `Fil`, `Z`, `D`, `FH` universally quantified, with the `e₂`/`filteredE₂Iso` compatibility,
the differential compatibility and the column-vanishing conjuncts dropped, and with `E₂`
identified with `Ext` by an isomorphism not tied to the canonical subquotient.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ext_homology_spectralSequence
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [EnoughInjectives C]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] (M : C) (K : DerivedCategory.Plus C) :
    ∃ (T : FilteredObject (CochainComplex AddCommGrpCat.{w} ℤ) ℤᵒᵖ)
      (Fil : ∀ (_p n : ℤ), Subobject (T.X.X n))
      (_hFil : ∀ p n : ℤ, Fil p n = Subobject.mk ((T.filtration.ι.app (op p)).f n))
      (Z : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (T.X.X n))
      (_hZ : ∀ r p n : ℤ, Z r p n =
        Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (T.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (Fil (p + r) (n + 1)))
      (D : ∀ (_r _p n : ℤ), Subobject (T.X.X n))
      (_hD : ∀ r p n : ℤ, D r p n = Z (r - 1) (p + 1) n ⊔
        (Subobject.«exists» (T.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (Z (r - 1) (p - r + 1) (n - 1)))
      (FH : ∀ (n _p : ℤ), Subobject (T.X.homology n))
      (_hFH : ∀ n p : ℤ, FH n p =
        imageSubobject (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (T.filtration.ι.app (op p)) n))
      (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{w} 0)
      (pageIso : ∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (_ : n = p + q), (E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅
        cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)))
      (filteredE₂Iso : ∀ i j : ℤ,
        cokernel (Subobject.ofLE _ _
            (inf_le_right : D 2 i (i + j) ⊓ Z 2 i (i + j) ≤ Z 2 i (i + j))) ≅
          AddCommGrpCat.of (Abelian.zExt.{u, v, w} M
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{w, v, u} C j).obj
              (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.{w, v, u}.obj K)) i))
      (e₂ : ∀ i j : ℤ, (E.page 2 zero_le_two).X (i, j) ≅
        AddCommGrpCat.of (Abelian.zExt.{u, v, w} M
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor.{w, v, u} C j).obj
            (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.{w, v, u}.obj K)) i))
      (_abutmentIso : ∀ n : ℤ, T.X.homology n ≅
        AddCommGrpCat.of (DerivedCategory.Ext.{u, v, w}
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor.{w, v, u} C 0).obj M)
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.{w, v, u}.obj K) n)),
      (∀ i j : ℤ, (e₂ i j).hom =
        (pageIso 2 i j (i + j) zero_le_two rfl).hom ≫ (filteredE₂Iso i j).hom) ∧
      (∀ (r p q n : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (hn : n = p + q),
        ∃ δ : (Z r p n : AddCommGrpCat.{w}) ⟶ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1) : AddCommGrpCat.{w}),
          δ ≫ (Z r (p + r) (n + 1)).arrow = (Z r p n).arrow ≫ T.X.d n (n + 1) ∧
          cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right : D r p n ⊓ Z r p n ≤ Z r p n)) ≫
              (pageIso r p q n hr hn).inv ≫ (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) =
            δ ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE _ _ (inf_le_right :
                D r (p + r) (n + 1) ⊓ Z r (p + r) (n + 1) ≤ Z r (p + r) (n + 1))) ≫
              (pageIso r (p + r) (q - r + 1) (n + 1) hr (by omega)).inv) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, {p : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((E.page 0 le_rfl).X (p, n - p))}.Finite) ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ FH n a = ⊤ ∧ FH n b = ⊥) ∧
      (∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r), b ≤ r →
        (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q - r + 1) = 0) ∧
      (∀ p n : ℤ,
        IsGLB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
            Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.pullback (T.X.d n (n + 1))).obj (Fil (p + r) (n + 1)) ⊔
              Fil (p + 1) n)
          (kernelSubobject (T.X.d n (n + 1)) ⊓ Fil p n ⊔ Fil (p + 1) n) ∧
        IsLUB (Set.range fun r : ℕ =>
            Fil p n ⊓ (Subobject.«exists» (T.X.d (n - 1) n)).obj (Fil (p - r) (n - 1)) ⊔
              Fil (p + 1) n)
          (imageSubobject (T.X.d (n - 1) n) ⊓ Fil p n ⊔ Fil (p + 1) n)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧
        ∀ (r i j : ℤ) (hr : 0 ≤ r), i + j = n → (i < a ∨ b < i) →
          IsZero ((E.page r hr).X (i, j))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.ExtSpectralSequence.exists_ext_complex_spectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AVI.** If a bounded below complex `K` represents an object of the bounded below
derived category, there is a cohomological spectral sequence
`E₁ⁱʲ = Extʲ(M, Kⁱ)` abutting to `Extⁱ⁺ʲ(M, K)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ext_complex_spectralSequence
    (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [EnoughInjectives C]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} C] (M : C) (K : CochainComplex C ℤ)
    (hK : ∃ a : ℤ, K.IsStrictlyGE a) :
    ∃ (E : CohomologicalSpectralSequence AddCommGrpCat.{w} 1)
      (_e₁ : ∀ i j : ℤ, (E.page 1).X (i, j) ≅
        AddCommGrpCat.of (Abelian.zExt.{u, v, w} M (K.X i) j))
      (G : ∀ _p n : ℤ, Subobject
        (AddCommGrpCat.of
          (DerivedCategory.Ext.{u, v, w}
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor.{w, v, u} C 0).obj M)
            (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) n)))
      (hG : ∀ p p' n : ℤ, p ≤ p' → G p' n ≤ G p n),
      (∀ n : ℤ, ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ G a n = ⊤ ∧ G b n = ⊥) ∧
      ∀ p q : ℤ, ∃ r₀ : ℤ, 1 ≤ r₀ ∧ ∀ (r : ℤ) (hr : 1 ≤ r), r₀ ≤ r →
        (E.page r hr).d (p, q) (p + r, q + 1 - r) = 0 ∧
        (E.page r hr).d (p - r, q + r - 1) (p, q) = 0 ∧
        Nonempty ((E.page r hr).X (p, q) ≅
          cokernel (Subobject.ofLE (G (p + 1) (p + q)) (G p (p + q))
            (hG p (p + 1) (p + q) (by omega))))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.InjectiveDimension.hasFiniteInjectiveDimension_iff_residueField_ext_vanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AVJ.** A bounded below complex with finite cohomology over a Noetherian local ring
has finite injective dimension if and only if its Ext groups from the residue field vanish in all
sufficiently high degrees.
declarations.statement:
public lemma hasFiniteInjectiveDimension_iff_residueField_ext_vanishing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (ModuleCat.{v} R))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite R
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) i).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj K))) :
    HasFiniteInjectiveDimension (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj K) ↔
      ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
        Subsingleton
          (DerivedCategory.Ext
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj
              (ModuleCat.of R (Shrink.{v} (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))))
            (DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj K) i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_fromNormalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AVK.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be quasi-compact and quasi-separated with `X`
reduced. If the quasi-compact opens of `X` have finitely many irreducible components, the residue
field extension at every generic point of an irreducible component of `X` is finitely generated,
and `S` is Nagata, then the normalization of `S` in `X` is finite over `S`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_fromNormalization
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (hS : IsNagataScheme S)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [IsReduced X]
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    (hκ : ∀ x : genericPoints X,
      letI := (f.residueFieldMap x.1).hom.toAlgebra
      (⊤ : IntermediateField (S.residueField (f x.1)) (X.residueField x.1)).FG) :
    IsFinite f.fromNormalization

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AssociatedPointsMono.mono_of_stalk_injective_on_associatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AVL.** A morphism of quasi-coherent modules on a locally
Noetherian scheme is a monomorphism if it is injective on the stalk at every associated
point of its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_of_stalk_injective_on_associatedPoints
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {F G : X.Modules}
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : ∀ x : X,
      Function.Injective
        ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map
          ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf X.ringCatSheaf.obj).map f.val)).hom ∨
        x ∉ associatedPoints F) :
    Mono f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_stalk_isIso_or_depth_two_and_not_associated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AVM.** A map from a coherent sheaf to a quasi-coherent sheaf is an
isomorphism if, at every point, it is an isomorphism on stalks, or the source stalk has depth at
least two and the point is not associated to the target.

The clause on associated points is what settles the degenerate case, and it cannot be dropped:
Tag 00LI sets `depth_I(M) = ∞` when `IM = M`, hence `⊤` for `M = 0`
(`Module.depth_eq_top_of_subsingleton`), so for `F = 0` and `G` nonzero the alternative
`depth(F_x) ≥ 2` holds at every point on its own while `0 ⟶ G` is not an isomorphism. See
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_stalk_isIso_or_depth_two_and_not_associated_of_isTorsionFree`, which
is the integral, torsion-free case of Tag 0AVS, and the counterexample recorded alongside it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_stalk_isIso_or_depth_two_and_not_associated {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {F G : X.Modules} [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    [F.IsCoherent] (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : ∀ x : X,
      letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x) :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          (R := X.presheaf) F.val x
      IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map
        ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf X.ringCatSheaf.obj).map f.val)) ∨
      ((2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x) ∧
        x ∉ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints G)) :
    IsIso f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.WeakAssPushforward.not_isWeaklyAssociatedPoint_pushforward_of_not_mem_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AVN.** A point outside the image of a quasi-compact,
quasi-separated morphism is not weakly associated to the pushforward of a quasi-coherent
module.

Neither quasi-separatedness nor quasi-coherence is used in the proof.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_isWeaklyAssociatedPoint_pushforward_of_not_mem_range
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (s : S) (hs : s ∉ Set.range f) :
    ¬ IsWeaklyAssociatedPoint ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F) s

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mono_of_stalk_injective_on_weaklyAssociatedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AVP.** A map of quasi-coherent modules is a monomorphism if its map
on stalks is injective at every weakly associated point of its source.
declarations.statement:
theorem mono_of_stalk_injective_on_weaklyAssociatedPoints {X : Scheme.{u}} {F G : X.Modules}
    [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : ∀ x : X,
      (Function.Injective
        ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map
          ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf X.ringCatSheaf.obj).map f.val)).hom) ∨
        x ∉ Stacks.Divisors.weaklyAssociatedPoints F) :
    Mono f

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.IsTorsionSection
declarations.doc:
A local section of a module on a scheme is *torsion* if its germ at every point of its
domain is a torsion element of the stalk, i.e. is annihilated by a nonzero element of the
local ring.
declarations.statement: public def IsTorsionSection (F : X.Modules) {U : X.Opens} (s : Γ(F, U)) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.IsTorsionFree
declarations.doc: A module on a scheme is *torsion free* if every torsion local section vanishes.
declarations.statement: public def IsTorsionFree (F : X.Modules) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_of_stalk_isIso_or_depth_two_and_not_associated_of_isTorsionFree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AVS.** Let `X` be an integral locally Noetherian scheme and
`f : F ⟶ G` a map of quasi-coherent modules with `F` coherent and `G` torsion free. If at every
point the map on stalks is an isomorphism, or the stalk of `F` has depth at least two and, at
the generic point, that point is not associated to `G`, then `f` is an isomorphism.

Alternative (2) is the one of Tag 0AV8, the lemma the source's proof of this statement reduces
to: Tag 0AVS is proved there as a translation of Tag 0AV9 into the language of schemes, Tag 0AV9
as a special case of Tag 0AV8, and the alternative (2) of Tag 0AV8 reads `depth(M_p) ≥ 2`
together with `p ∉ Ass(N)`. Over an integral base with `G` torsion free the clause on associated
points holds of itself at every point other than the generic one, by
`eq_genericPoint_of_isAssociatedPoint_of_isTorsionFree`, which is why it is asked for here only
at the generic point; that single point is where it does its work, by
`exists_counterexample_to_displayed_statement_of_tag_0AVS`, which exhibits a map satisfying
alternative (2) of Tag 0AVS as displayed at every point and failing to be an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_of_stalk_isIso_or_depth_two_and_not_associated_of_isTorsionFree
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    {F G : X.Modules} [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsCoherent]
    (f : F ⟶ G) (hG : Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.IsTorsionFree G)
    (hf : ∀ x : X,
      let : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x) :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          (R := X.presheaf) F.val x
      IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map
        ((PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf X.ringCatSheaf.obj).map f.val)) ∨
      ((2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x))
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) F.val.presheaf x) ∧
        (x = genericPoint X → x ∉ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints G))) :
    IsIso f
declarations.comment:
alternative (2) in the form Tag 0AV8 gives it, namely depth at least two at a
  point not associated to the target, which is the form the source's proof of this statement
  reduces to through Tag 0AV9, and asked for only at the generic point, the one point of an
  integral base at which a torsion-free target can have an associated point

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.reflexiveHull
declarations.doc: The reflexive hull `F⁎⁎` of a module on a scheme: the dual of its dual.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable abbrev reflexiveHull (F : X.Modules) : X.Modules
declarations.comment: reflexive hull

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.toReflexiveHull
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `F ⟶ F⁎⁎` to the reflexive hull, bundled with the formula that
characterizes it: over an open `U` it sends a local section `f` to the functional on `F^∨|_U`
whose component at the terminal object of the slice site over `U` is evaluation at `f`.
declarations.comment: canonical map to the reflexive hull

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.isReflexive_iff_isIso
declarations.doc:
Reflexivity of `F` is invertibility of any morphism `F ⟶ F⁎⁎` satisfying the defining formula
of the canonical map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isReflexive_iff_isIso (F : X.Modules) (j : F ⟶ reflexiveHull F)
    (hj : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (f : Γ(F, U)) (lam : Γ(dualSheaf F, U)),
      (((j.val.app (op U)).hom f).app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).hom lam =
        (lam.app (op (Over.mk (𝟙 U)))).hom f) :
    IsReflexive F ↔ IsIso j
declarations.comment: reflexive predicate

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedAffinePushforward.derivedPushforwardOverRingCompRestrictScalarsIso
declarations.doc:
**The factorisation asserted by [Stacks, Tag 0AVW]**: the derived direct image `Rf_*` is
`Φ` followed by the functor `D(f_* 𝒪_X) ⥤ D(𝒪_S)` induced by restriction of scalars along
`𝒪_S ⟶ f_* 𝒪_X`.  Both functors are right derived functors of degreewise direct image, so they
agree by the uniqueness of right derived functors.

This is the second of the tag's two clauses, and the attribute carries a phrase naming it.  The
first clause — that `Φ` is an *equivalence* onto `D_QCoh(f_* 𝒪_X)` for `f` affine — is
`isEquivalence_derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardOverRing`.  The factorisation below holds for every
morphism of schemes, with no affineness needed, and is read on the whole derived categories
rather than on the quasi-coherent ones, so it is stronger than the source's clause on both
counts.
declarations.comment: the factorisation of Rf_* through D(f_*𝒪_X); the equivalence clause is proved in isEquivalence_derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardOverRing (QuasicoherentEquivalenceOverPushforwardRing.lean), on the whole derived categories

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedAffinePushforward.isEquivalence_and_factorisation_derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardOverRing
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AVW], the whole statement.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be an affine morphism of
schemes.  Then direct image induces an **equivalence**
`Φ : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(f_* 𝒪_X)`, and the composition of `Φ` with the functor
`D_QCoh(f_* 𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_S)` given by restriction of scalars along `𝒪_S ⟶ f_* 𝒪_X` **is**
`Rf_*`.

Both clauses are read on the quasi-coherent subcategories and under the source's condition that
`f` be affine, which is where the tag's own statement puts them; the existing registration on
`derivedPushforwardOverRingCompRestrictScalarsIso` carries the second clause alone, for every
morphism of schemes and on the whole derived categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_and_factorisation_derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardOverRing :
    (derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardOverRing f).IsEquivalence ∧
      Nonempty (derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardOverRing f ⋙
          derivedQuasicoherentScalarRestriction f ≅
        derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardAtModel f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isPseudoCoherentSite_pushforward_derivedStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
If a closed immersion of schemes `i : Z ⟶ X` is pseudo-coherent, then `Ri_* 𝒪_Z` is a
pseudo-coherent object of `D(𝒪_X)` at the ringed site of opens of `X`, in the sense of
[Stacks, Tag 08FT].
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentSite_pushforward_derivedStructureSheaf (hi : PseudoCoherent i) :
    (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPseudoCoherent
      ((modulePushforward
        (Stacks.ClosedImmersion.closedQuotientOfClosedImmersion i).i).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (RingedSite.derivedStructureSheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.ringedSite Z.sheaf)))
declarations.comment: for a closed immersion, at the site notion of pseudo-coherence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_iff_isPseudoCoherent_pushforward_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AVX.** A finite morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` is pseudo-coherent if and only if
the direct image `f_*𝒪_X` of its structure sheaf is a pseudo-coherent `𝒪_S`-module, that is, if
and only if the object of `D(𝒪_S)` it determines in degree zero is pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pseudoCoherent_iff_isPseudoCoherent_pushforward_unit {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [IsFinite f] :
    PseudoCoherent f ↔
      RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := S.toRingedSpace)
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor S.Modules 0).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)))

declarations.name: ModuleCat.subsingleton_ext_of_lt_ideal_depth
declarations.doc:
`Ext^i_R(N, M)` vanishes below the `I`-depth of `M` for **every** finite module `N`
annihilated by a power of `I`, not just for `N = R ⧸ I`: a power of `I` annihilating `N` forces
the support of `N` into `V(I)`, and Rees' theorem turns the vanishing of `Ext^j_R(R/I, M)` below
the depth into an `M`-regular sequence in `I` long enough to kill `Ext^i_R(N, M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ModuleCat.subsingleton_ext_of_lt_ideal_depth [IsNoetherianRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (I : Ideal R) (M N : ModuleCat.{v} R) [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hIM : I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤) {k : ℕ} (hk : I ^ k ≤ Module.annihilator R N) {i : ℕ}
    (hi : (i : ℕ∞) < Module.depth R I M) :
    Subsingleton (Ext N M i)
declarations.comment: Ext vanishing below depth for modules annihilated by an ideal power

declarations.name: Module.subsingleton_ext_of_lt_depth
declarations.doc: Ext from a finite module annihilated by a power of `I` vanishes below the `I`-depth.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_ext_of_lt_depth
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (I : Ideal R) (M N : ModuleCat.{v} R)
    [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R N]
    (hIM : I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤)
    (hN : ∃ n : ℕ, I ^ n ≤ Module.annihilator R N)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : (i : ℕ∞) < Module.depth R I M) :
    Subsingleton (Ext N M i)
declarations.comment: Ext vanishing below depth for modules annihilated by an ideal power

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.depth_eq_sInf_nontrivial_localCohomologyWithSupportIn
declarations.doc: Depth is the first degree with nonzero local cohomology supported on `V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem depth_eq_sInf_nontrivial_localCohomologyWithSupportIn
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} R) [Module.Finite R M]
    (hIM : I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤) :
    Module.depth R I M =
      sInf {n : ℕ∞ | ∃ i : ℕ, n = (i : ℕ∞) ∧
      Nontrivial
          (localCohomologyWithSupportIn
            R (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R))
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) 0).obj M)
              (i : ℤ))}
declarations.comment: equality of depth and the first nonzero local-cohomology degree

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.depth_eq_sInf_nontrivial_ext_and_localCohomology_and_subsingleton_ext
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ R` an ideal and `M` a finite
`R`-module with `IM ≠ M`. Then the three integers of the source are equal — `depth_I(M)`, the
least `i` with `Ext^i_R(R/I, M) ≠ 0`, and the least `i` with `H^i_{V(I)}(M) ≠ 0`, each of the
last two read as an infimum in `ℕ∞` — and moreover `Ext^i_R(N, M) = 0` for every `i` below
`depth_I(M)` and every finite `R`-module `N` annihilated by a power of `I`.

The source's `H^i_I(M)`, the cohomology of derived `I`-power torsion, is `H^i_{V(I)}(M)` here:
the two agree because `R` is Noetherian, by
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.isIso_compareSectionsWithSupportLocalCohomology_app`
([Stacks, Tag 0955]).
declarations.statement:
theorem depth_eq_sInf_nontrivial_ext_and_localCohomology_and_subsingleton_ext
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) [Module.Finite R M]
    (hIM : I • (⊤ : Submodule R M) ≠ ⊤) :
    Module.depth R I M =
        sInf {n : ℕ∞ | ∃ i : ℕ, n = (i : ℕ∞) ∧
          Nontrivial (Abelian.Ext (ModuleCat.of R (Shrink.{u} (R ⧸ I))) M i)} ∧
      Module.depth R I M =
        sInf {n : ℕ∞ | ∃ i : ℕ, n = (i : ℕ∞) ∧
          Nontrivial (localCohomologyWithSupportIn R (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R))
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) 0).obj M) (i : ℤ))} ∧
      ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{u} R) [Module.Finite R N], (∃ k : ℕ, I ^ k ≤ Module.annihilator R N) →
        ∀ i : ℕ, (i : ℕ∞) < Module.depth R I M → Subsingleton (Abelian.Ext N M i)
declarations.comment: the three-way equality and the moreover clause conjoined, with the local cohomology of the third quantity in the RΓ_{V(I)} model

registrations.name: Module.depth_eq_sInf_nontrivial_ext
registrations.comment: equality of depth and the first nonzero Ext degree

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.supportLocalCohomology_torsion_higher
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, part (2).** Higher local cohomology with support in `V(I)` of torsion
vanishes: `H^p_Z(M[I^∞]) = 0` for `p > 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportLocalCohomology_torsion_higher
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A)
    (p : ℤ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero ((supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I)))
declarations.comment: part (2), higher cohomology of the torsion submodule

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.supportLocalCohomology_quotient_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, part (2).** Quotienting by `I`-power torsion kills zeroth local cohomology
with support in `V(I)`: `H^0_Z(M/M[I^∞]) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportLocalCohomology_quotient_zero
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :
    IsZero ((supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ Ideal.primaryComponent M I)))
declarations.comment: part (2), degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.idealLocalCohomology_zero_iso_torsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0.** The zeroth local cohomology `H^0_I(M)` of `M` for the `I`-power torsion
theory is the `I`-power-torsion submodule `M[I^∞]` of `M`, by an isomorphism compatible with
the canonical map of `H^0_I(M)` into `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealLocalCohomology_zero_iso_torsion
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :
    ∃ e : (idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj M ≅
        ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I),
      e.hom ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.subtype (Ideal.primaryComponent M I)) =
        idealLocalCohomologyToModule.{u, v} A I hI M
declarations.comment: H^0_I is the torsion submodule

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.idealLocalCohomology_quotient_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, part (1).** Quotienting by the `I`-power-torsion submodule kills the zeroth
local cohomology for the `I`-power torsion theory: `H^0_I(M/M[I^∞]) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealLocalCohomology_quotient_zero
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :
    IsZero ((idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ Ideal.primaryComponent M I)))
declarations.comment: part (1), degree zero

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.idealLocalCohomology_torsion_higher
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, part (1).** Over a Noetherian ring the higher local cohomology of the
`I`-power-torsion submodule vanishes for the `I`-power torsion theory:
`H^p_I(M[I^∞]) = 0` for `p > 0`.

The source states this for an arbitrary ring. The Noetherian hypothesis added here cannot be
removed: for a finitely generated ideal of a non-Noetherian ring the assertion is false, by
part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0A6P]; the counterexample is
`Stacks.Duality.exists_not_isZero_idealLocalCohomology_primaryComponent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealLocalCohomology_torsion_higher
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A)
    (p : ℤ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero ((idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).obj
      (ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I)))
declarations.comment: part (1), higher cohomology of the torsion submodule

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.idealLocalCohomology_quotient_map_higher
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, part (1).** Over a Noetherian ring the quotient map `M ⟶ M/M[I^∞]` induces
an isomorphism `H^p_I(M) ≅ H^p_I(M/M[I^∞])` in every positive degree.

The source states this for an arbitrary ring. The Noetherian hypothesis added here cannot be
removed: taking an `I`-power-torsion `M`, so that `M/M[I^∞] = 0`, turns the assertion into the
vanishing of `Stacks.Duality.idealLocalCohomology_torsion_higher`, which part (3) of
[Stacks, Tag 0A6P] refutes over a non-Noetherian ring; the counterexample is
`Stacks.Duality.exists_not_isIso_idealLocalCohomology_map_mkQ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealLocalCohomology_quotient_map_higher
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A)
    (p : ℤ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsIso ((idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).map
      (ModuleCat.ofHom (Ideal.primaryComponent M I).mkQ))
declarations.comment: part (1), higher cohomology of the quotient

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.supportLocalCohomology_quotient_map_higher
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, part (2).** The quotient map `M ⟶ M/M[I^∞]` induces an isomorphism
`H^p_Z(M) ≅ H^p_Z(M/M[I^∞])` in every positive degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportLocalCohomology_quotient_map_higher
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (p : ℤ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsIso ((supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).map
      (ModuleCat.ofHom (Ideal.primaryComponent M I).mkQ))
declarations.comment: part (2), higher cohomology of the quotient

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.idealLocalCohomology_zero_iso_supportLocalCohomology_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0.** For a finitely generated ideal `I` and `Z = V(I)` the two zeroth local
cohomology modules agree, `H^0_I(M) = H^0_Z(M)`, compatibly with their canonical maps down
to `M`; the common value is the `I`-power-torsion submodule `M[I^∞]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealLocalCohomology_zero_iso_supportLocalCohomology_zero
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :
    ∃ e : (idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj M ≅
        (supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj M,
      e.hom ≫ supportLocalCohomologyToModule.{u, v} A I hI M =
        idealLocalCohomologyToModule.{u, v} A I hI M

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.localCohomology_divide_by_torsion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, the preamble and both parts.** Let `A` be a ring, let `I ⊆ A` be a finitely
generated ideal, let `M` be an `A`-module and let `Z = V(I)`. Then `H^0_I(M) = H^0_Z(M)`; the
common value `N` is the `I`-power-torsion submodule `M[I^∞]`, both identifications being
compatible with the canonical maps down to `M`; and, writing `M' = M/N`,

1. `H^0_I(M') = 0`, `H^p_I(M) = H^p_I(M')` and `H^p_I(N) = 0` for all `p > 0`;
2. `H^0_Z(M') = 0`, `H^p_Z(M) = H^p_Z(M')` and `H^p_Z(N) = 0` for all `p > 0`.

The two higher-degree clauses of part (1) carry the hypothesis that `A` is Noetherian, which
the source does not have, so this conjunction carries it too. That hypothesis cannot be dropped:
part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 0A6P] refutes those two clauses for a finitely generated ideal of a
non-Noetherian ring, by the argument in the module docstring. Everything else here — the
preamble and the whole of part (2) — holds over an arbitrary ring, and is stated that way by the
eight declarations this conjoins, each of which carries the tag for its own clause; they are
listed in the module docstring and in that of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Duality.DivideByTorsion`. The same statement over an arbitrary
ring, with the Noetherian hypothesis attached to those two clauses alone, conjoined with the
counterexamples to them, is
`Stacks.Duality.localCohomology_divide_by_torsion_corrected_and_counterexample`.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCohomology_divide_by_torsion
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :
    (∃ e : (idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj M ≅
        (supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj M,
      e.hom ≫ supportLocalCohomologyToModule.{u, v} A I hI M =
        idealLocalCohomologyToModule.{u, v} A I hI M) ∧
    (∃ e : (idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj M ≅
        ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I),
      e.hom ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.subtype (Ideal.primaryComponent M I)) =
        idealLocalCohomologyToModule.{u, v} A I hI M) ∧
    (IsZero ((idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ Ideal.primaryComponent M I))) ∧
        (∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsIso ((idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (Ideal.primaryComponent M I).mkQ))) ∧
        ∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsZero ((idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I)))) ∧
      (IsZero ((supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ Ideal.primaryComponent M I))) ∧
        (∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsIso ((supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (Ideal.primaryComponent M I).mkQ))) ∧
        ∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsZero ((supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I))))
declarations.comment: the preamble and both parts conjoined, over a Noetherian ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_not_isZero_idealLocalCohomology_primaryComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, part (1), the printed clause `H^p_I(N) = 0` is false.** There are a ring `A`,
a finitely generated (indeed principal) ideal `I`, a module `M` and a degree `p > 0` with
`H^p_I(M[I^∞]) ≠ 0`. The ring is necessarily not Noetherian, by
`Stacks.Duality.idealLocalCohomology_torsion_higher`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_isZero_idealLocalCohomology_primaryComponent :
    ∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{0} A) (p : ℤ),
      0 < p ∧ ¬ IsZero ((idealLocalCohomology.{0, 0} A I hI p).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I)))
declarations.comment: counterexample to part (1), higher cohomology of the torsion submodule, over a non-Noetherian ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_not_isIso_idealLocalCohomology_map_mkQ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, part (1), the printed clause `H^p_I(M) = H^p_I(M/M[I^∞])` is false.** There
are a ring `A`, a finitely generated (indeed principal) ideal `I`, a module `M` and a degree
`p > 0` for which the quotient map `M ⟶ M/M[I^∞]` does not induce an isomorphism on `H^p_I`.
The ring is necessarily not Noetherian, by
`Stacks.Duality.idealLocalCohomology_quotient_map_higher`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_isIso_idealLocalCohomology_map_mkQ :
    ∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{0} A) (p : ℤ),
      0 < p ∧ ¬ IsIso ((idealLocalCohomology.{0, 0} A I hI p).map
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (Ideal.primaryComponent M I).mkQ))
declarations.comment: counterexample to part (1), higher cohomology of the quotient, over a non-Noetherian ring

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.localCohomology_divide_by_torsion_corrected_and_counterexample
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW0, corrected, with the counterexample to the printed form.** Let `A` be a ring,
`I ⊆ A` a finitely generated ideal, `M` an `A`-module and `Z = V(I)`. Then
`H^0_I(M) = H^0_Z(M)`, the common value `N` being the `I`-power-torsion submodule `M[I^∞]`
(both identifications compatible with the canonical maps down to `M`), and, writing
`M' = M/N`,

1. `H^0_I(M') = 0`, and, when `A` is Noetherian, `H^p_I(M) = H^p_I(M')` and `H^p_I(N) = 0`
   for all `p > 0`;
2. `H^0_Z(M') = 0`, `H^p_Z(M) = H^p_Z(M')` and `H^p_Z(N) = 0` for all `p > 0`.

The source states the two positive-degree assertions of part (1) for every ring. They fail in
that generality: the last two conjuncts exhibit a ring, a principal ideal, a module and a
positive degree for which `H^p_I(M[I^∞]) ≠ 0`, and likewise one for which the quotient map
`M ⟶ M/M[I^∞]` is not an isomorphism on `H^p_I`. Everything else is stated, and holds, over an
arbitrary ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem localCohomology_divide_by_torsion_corrected_and_counterexample :
    (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A),
      (∃ e : (idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj M ≅
          (supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj M,
        e.hom ≫ supportLocalCohomologyToModule.{u, v} A I hI M =
          idealLocalCohomologyToModule.{u, v} A I hI M) ∧
      (∃ e : (idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj M ≅
          ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I),
        e.hom ≫ ModuleCat.ofHom (Submodule.subtype (Ideal.primaryComponent M I)) =
          idealLocalCohomologyToModule.{u, v} A I hI M) ∧
      (IsZero ((idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ Ideal.primaryComponent M I))) ∧
        (IsNoetherianRing A →
          (∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsIso ((idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).map
            (ModuleCat.ofHom (Ideal.primaryComponent M I).mkQ))) ∧
          ∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsZero ((idealLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I))))) ∧
      (IsZero ((supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI 0).obj
            (ModuleCat.of A (M ⧸ Ideal.primaryComponent M I))) ∧
        (∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsIso ((supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom (Ideal.primaryComponent M I).mkQ))) ∧
        ∀ p : ℤ, 0 < p → IsZero ((supportLocalCohomology.{u, v} A I hI p).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I))))) ∧
    (∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{0} A) (p : ℤ),
      0 < p ∧ ¬ IsZero ((idealLocalCohomology.{0, 0} A I hI p).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (Ideal.primaryComponent M I)))) ∧
    (∃ (A : Type) (_ : CommRing A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (M : ModuleCat.{0} A) (p : ℤ),
      0 < p ∧ ¬ IsIso ((idealLocalCohomology.{0, 0} A I hI p).map
        (ModuleCat.ofHom (Ideal.primaryComponent M I).mkQ)))
declarations.comment: the statement with part (1) in positive degrees over a Noetherian ring, and counterexamples to part (1) in positive degrees over a non-Noetherian ring

declarations.name: IsFormallyCatenary
declarations.doc:
A local ring `A` is formally catenary if, for every minimal prime `p` of `A`, the spectrum
of the quotient of its maximal-ideal-adic completion by the extension of `p` is
equidimensional.
declarations.statement: def IsFormallyCatenary (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] : Prop

declarations.name: not_isUniversallyCatenary_of_not_isFormallyCatenary
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW3.** A Noetherian local ring which is not formally catenary is not universally
catenary.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isUniversallyCatenary_of_not_isFormallyCatenary
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hA : ¬ IsFormallyCatenary A) : ¬ Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary A

declarations.name: flat_local_catenary_equidim_fibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW4 (1).** For a flat local map `A → B` of Noetherian local rings with
`B` catenary and `Spec(B)` equidimensional, the fibre `Spec(B / pB)` is
equidimensional for every prime `p ⊆ A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_local_catenary_equidim_fibre (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [Module.Flat A B]
    (hcat : IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace (PrimeSpectrum B))
    (hequi : SpecEquidimensional B)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] :
    SpecEquidimensional (B ⧸ p.map (algebraMap A B))

declarations.name: flat_local_catenary_equidim_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW4 (2).** For a flat local map `A → B` of Noetherian local rings with
`B` catenary and `Spec(B)` equidimensional, the base `A` is catenary and `Spec(A)`
is equidimensional.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_local_catenary_equidim_base (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [Module.Flat A B]
    (hcat : IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace (PrimeSpectrum B))
    (hequi : SpecEquidimensional B) :
    IrreducibleClosedsCodim.IsCatenarySpace (PrimeSpectrum A) ∧ SpecEquidimensional A

declarations.name: isUniversallyCatenary_of_isFormallyCatenary
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0AW5.** A formally catenary Noetherian local ring is universally catenary.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyCatenary_of_isFormallyCatenary
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (hA : IsFormallyCatenary A) : Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary A

declarations.name: isUniversallyCatenary_iff_isFormallyCatenary
declarations.doc:
**Ratliff's theorem (Stacks 0AW6).** A Noetherian local ring is universally catenary if and
only if it is formally catenary.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyCatenary_iff_isFormallyCatenary
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] :
    Ring.IsUniversallyCatenary A ↔ IsFormallyCatenary A

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_annihilator_iff_exists_power_annihilator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW8, equivalence of (2) and (3) for closed support.** For support `V(I)` in a
Noetherian ring, an ideal supported in `V(I)` annihilates local cohomology through degree `n`
exactly when a single power of `I` does so.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_annihilator_iff_exists_power_annihilator
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) (n : ℕ) :
    (∃ J : Ideal A,
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ⊆ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ (n : ℤ) → J ≤ Module.annihilator A
        (localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, v} A (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A))
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) 0).obj M) i)) ↔
      (∃ e : ℕ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ (n : ℤ) → I ^ e ≤ Module.annihilator A
        (localCohomologyWithSupportIn.{u, v} A (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A))
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) 0).obj M) i))
declarations.comment: equivalence of (2) and (3) for closed support

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.finite_localCohomologyWithSupportIn_iff_exists_annihilator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW8, equivalence of (1) and (2).** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring, `T ⊆ Spec(A)` a
subset stable under specialization, `M` a finite `A`-module and `n ≥ 0`. The local cohomology
modules `H^i_T(M)` are finite for every `i ≤ n` if and only if there is an ideal `J` with
`V(J) ⊆ T` annihilating `H^i_T(M)` for every `i ≤ n`.

Forward: a finite module is annihilated by its own annihilator, whose zero locus is its support,
and `H^i_T(M)` is supported in `T`. Backward: Faltings' induction on `n`, replacing `M` by
`M/Γ_T(M)` and using a nonzerodivisor in `J` to relate degree `i + 1` for `M` to degree `i` for
`M/fM`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_localCohomologyWithSupportIn_iff_exists_annihilator (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (T : Set (PrimeSpectrum A)) (hT : StableUnderSpecialization T)
    (M : ModuleCat.{max u v} A) [Module.Finite A (M : Type (max u v))] (n : ℕ) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ (n : ℤ) → Module.Finite A (localCohomologyWithSupportIn A T
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) 0).obj M) i)) ↔
      ∃ J : Ideal A, PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) ⊆ T ∧
        ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ (n : ℤ) → J ≤ Module.annihilator A (localCohomologyWithSupportIn A T
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) 0).obj M) i)
declarations.comment: equivalence of (1) and (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomology_finite_iff_localizations_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AW9.** For a finite module over a Noetherian ring, finiteness of
local cohomology through degree `n` can be checked after localization at every
prime ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem localCohomology_finite_iff_localizations_finite
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    (n : ℕ) :
    let hI : I.FG := Ideal.fg_of_isNoetherianRing I
    let RΓ := Dualizing.localCohomologyFunctor A I hI ⋙
      (Dualizing.derivedPowerTorsionProperty A I hI).ι
    let H := fun i : ℕ ↦
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) (i : ℤ)).obj
        (RΓ.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} A) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A M)))
    (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ n → Module.Finite A (H i)) ↔
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ n →
        Module.Finite (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal)
          (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl (H i))

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.isCoherent_pushforward_of_isNagataScheme
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWA].** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, let `j : U ⟶ X` be the
inclusion of an open subscheme with complement `Z`, and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_U`-module.
Assume (1) `X` is Nagata, (2) `X` is universally catenary, and
(3) `dim(𝒪_{closure{x}, z}) ≥ 2` for `x ∈ Ass(F)` and `z ∈ Z ∩ closure{x}`. Then `j_*F` is
coherent.

The proof runs the source's argument on the tag's own three assumptions. Assumption (1) makes
the normalization `π : Y ⟶ X` of `X` in `Spec κ(x)` finite, hence `G = π_*𝒪_Y` coherent;
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_mono_pullback_residueFieldNormalizationPushforward` supplies the
comparison monomorphism `i_{x,*}𝒪_{W_x} ⟶ G|_U`; assumptions (2) and (3) give `depth(G_z) ≥ 2`
on `Z` through
`AlgebraicGeometry.hasDepthTwoOutside_pushforwardUnitModule_fromSpecResidueField`; the depth-two
theorem `AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pushforward_of_mono_of_depth_ge_two` then makes
`j_*i_{x,*}𝒪_{W_x}` coherent at each associated point, which is the hypothesis of the
implication (1) ⇒ (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0BJZ].
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_pushforward_of_isNagataScheme {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (V : X.Opens) (F : V.toScheme.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hNagata : IsNagataScheme X)
    (hCat : X.IsUniversallyCatenary)
    (hdim : ∀ x : V.toScheme, x ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F →
      TwoLePointClosureDim V x) :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward V.ι).obj F).IsCoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pushforward_iff_two_le_ringKrullDim_stalk_pointClosure
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWB].** Let `j : U ⟶ X` be an open immersion with `X` locally Noetherian and
universally catenary, and suppose the formal fibres of `𝒪_{X, z}` satisfy `(S₁)` for every point
`z` outside `U`. For a coherent `𝒪_U`-module `ℱ`, the direct image `j_* ℱ` is coherent exactly
when `dim(𝒪_{closure {x}, z}) ≥ 2` for every associated point `x` of `ℱ` and every point `z` of
the reduced closure of `{j x}` lying outside `U`.

The associated-prime criterion of [Stacks, Tag 0BK3] is supplied by
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.isCoherent_pushforward_iff_forall_two_le_ringKrullDim`, and
`two_le_ringKrullDim_quotient_completedStalk_iff_two_le_ringKrullDim_stalk` collapses its
condition pointwise to the dimension of the local ring itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_pushforward_iff_two_le_ringKrullDim_stalk_pointClosure
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    {F : U.Modules} [F.IsCoherent]
    (hX : Scheme.IsUniversallyCatenary X)
    (hFibres : ∀ z : X, z ∉ j.opensRange →
      ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (X.presheaf.stalk z),
        HasSerreCondition
          (X.completedLocalRing z ⊗[X.presheaf.stalk z] q.asIdeal.ResidueField) 1) :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward j).obj F).IsCoherent ↔
      ∀ x : U, x ∈ Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F →
        ∀ y : (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
            (Closeds.closure ({j x} : Set X))).subscheme,
          (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
            (Closeds.closure ({j x} : Set X))).subschemeι y ∉ j.opensRange →
          2 ≤ ringKrullDim ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
            (Closeds.closure ({j x} : Set X))).subscheme.presheaf.stalk y)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CodimensionOneObstruction.not_isCoherent_pushforward_of_isAssociatedPoint
declarations.doc:
**First paragraph of [Stacks, Tag 0AWC].** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `U` an open
subscheme with complement `Z`, and `𝓕` an `𝒪_U`-module. Let `x` be a point of `U` associated to
`𝓕`, let `X'` be the reduced closed subscheme of `X` supported on the closure of `{x}`, and let
`z'` be a point of `X'` whose image lies in `Z` and at which `dim 𝒪_{X', z'} ≤ 1`. Then the direct
image of `𝓕` along `U → X` is not coherent.

`X'` is integral with generic point `x` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isIntegral_subscheme_vanishingIdeal_closure` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.subschemeι_genericPoint_vanishingIdeal_closure`, so a
point of `X'` whose image avoids `U` is exactly a point `z ∈ Z ∩ \overline{\{x\}}` of the cited
remark, and `𝒪_{X', z'}` is its `𝒪_{\overline{\{x\}}, z}`.

The remark assumes `𝓕` coherent; no hypothesis on `𝓕` is needed here.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isCoherent_pushforward_of_isAssociatedPoint [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    {U : X.Opens} (𝓕 : U.toScheme.Modules) {x : X} (hxU : x ∈ U)
    (hass : Stacks.Divisors.IsAssociatedPoint 𝓕 ⟨x, hxU⟩)
    {I : X.IdealSheafData}
    (hI : I = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal (Closeds.closure ({x} : Set X)))
    (z' : I.subscheme) (hzU : I.subschemeι z' ∉ U)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (I.subscheme.presheaf.stalk z') ≤ 1) :
    ¬ ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward U.ι).obj 𝓕).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: first paragraph

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CodimensionOneObstruction.not_isCoherent_pushforward_structureSheaf_of_isAssociatedPrime_completedStalk
declarations.doc:
**A one-dimensional associated prime of the completed local ring obstructs coherence of the
direct image of the structure sheaf.** Let `j : U → X` be an open immersion of integral locally
Noetherian schemes and let `z` be a point of `X` outside `U`. If the completion `𝒪^∧_{X, z}` has an
associated prime `𝔭` — a prime which is the annihilator of one of its elements — with
`dim(𝒪^∧_{X, z} ⧸ 𝔭) = 1`, then `j_* 𝒪_U` is not coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isCoherent_pushforward_structureSheaf_of_isAssociatedPrime_completedStalk
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {U : X.Opens}
    [Nonempty U.toScheme] {z : X} (hzU : z ∉ U)
    {p : PrimeSpectrum (X.completedLocalRingCat z)}
    (hp : IsAssociatedPrimeStacks (X.completedLocalRingCat z) (X.completedLocalRingCat z)
      p.asIdeal)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (X.completedLocalRingCat z ⧸ p.asIdeal) = 1) :
    ¬ ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward U.ι).obj (SheafOfModules.unit _)).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: second paragraph

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.CoherentPushforwardCriterion.not_isCoherent_pushforward_structureSheaf_of_isAssociatedPrime_completedStalk_le_one
declarations.doc:
**`j_* 𝒪_U` is not coherent when a completed local ring outside `U` has an associated prime
of dimension at most one.** Let `j : U → X` be the inclusion of a nonempty open subscheme of an
integral locally Noetherian scheme and let `z` be a point of `X` outside `U`. If the completion
`𝒪^∧_{X, z}` has an associated prime `𝔭` — a prime which is the annihilator of one of its
elements — with `dim(𝒪^∧_{X, z} ⧸ 𝔭) ≤ 1`, then `j_* 𝒪_U` is not coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isCoherent_pushforward_structureSheaf_of_isAssociatedPrime_completedStalk_le_one
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {U : X.Opens}
    [Nonempty U.toScheme] {z : X} (hzU : z ∉ U)
    {p : PrimeSpectrum (X.completedLocalRingCat z)}
    (hp : IsAssociatedPrimeStacks (X.completedLocalRingCat z) (X.completedLocalRingCat z)
      p.asIdeal)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (X.completedLocalRingCat z ⧸ p.asIdeal) ≤ 1) :
    ¬ ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward U.ι).obj (SheafOfModules.unit _)).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: second paragraph, for an associated quotient of the completion of dimension at most one

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.not_isCoherent_pushforward_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWC], the completed-local-ring obstruction to coherence.** Let `j : U ⟶ X` be
an open immersion of integral locally Noetherian schemes and suppose some point `z` outside the
image of `j` has an associated prime `𝔭` of the completed local ring `𝒪^∧_{X,z}` with
`dim(𝒪^∧_{X,z} ⧸ 𝔭) = 1`. Then `j_*𝒪_U` is not coherent.

This is the second paragraph of the remark, its `completed_local_ring_obstruction` clause, the
converse to [Stacks, Tag 0E9I].
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isCoherent_pushforward_structureSheaf {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion j] [IsIntegral U] [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (h : ∃ (z : X) (p : Ideal (AdicCompletion
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk z)))
        (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk z)))),
      z ∉ Set.range j.base ∧
      IsAssociatedPrimeStacks
        (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk z)))
          (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk z)))
        (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk z)))
          (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk z))) p ∧
      ringKrullDim (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk z)))
        (ToType (X.presheaf.stalk z)) ⧸ p) = 1) :
    ¬ ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward j).obj
      (SheafOfModules.unit.{u} U.ringCatSheaf)).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: completed_local_ring_obstruction

declarations.name: Dualizing.isNormalizedDualizingComplex_extendScalars_of_flat
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings for which the maximal
ideal of `A` generates the maximal ideal of `B`. Then the base change to `B` of a normalized
dualizing complex over `A` is a normalized dualizing complex over `B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNormalizedDualizingComplex_extendScalars_of_flat
    {A : Type u} {B : Type w} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (hmax : (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A B) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v w} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, max v w} K) :
    IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{w, max u v}
      ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, w, max u v w}
        (algebraMap A B)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)

declarations.name: Dualizing.support_canonicalModule
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian local ring with a normalized
dualizing complex `K`, let `d = dim(A)` and let `ω_A = H^{-d}(K)`. The support of `ω_A` is the
union of the irreducible components of `Spec(A)` of dimension `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem support_canonicalModule
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} K)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim A = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    Module.support A ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-(d : ℤ))).obj K) =
      ⋃₀ {C ∈ irreducibleComponents (PrimeSpectrum A) |
        topologicalKrullDim C = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)}
declarations.comment: (1): the support of ω_A is the union of the d-dimensional irreducible components

declarations.name: Dualizing.propertySkModule_canonicalModule
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian local ring with a normalized dualizing complex `K`, let `d = dim(A)`
and let `ω_A = H^{-d}(K)`. Then `ω_A` satisfies Serre's condition `(S₂)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem propertySkModule_canonicalModule {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} K) :
    let d := (ringKrullDim A).unbotD 0 |>.toNat
    let ω := (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-(d : ℤ))).obj K
    letI : Module.Finite A ω := hK.1.finiteCohomology (-(d : ℤ))
    PropertySkModule A ω 2
declarations.comment: (2): the canonical module ω_A satisfies Serre's condition (S₂)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isUniversallyCatenary_and_isDimensionFunction_associatedShiftFunction
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `K` a dualizing complex on `X`. Then `X` is
universally catenary, and the function `δ : X → ℤ` defined by `x ↦ δ(x)` such that
`ω^•_{X,x}⟦-δ(x)⟧` is a normalized dualizing complex over `𝒪_{X,x}` is a dimension function.

Here `δ` is `Stacks.Duality.associatedShiftFunction K`, and `ω^•_{X,x}` is the derived stalk of
`K` at `x`, computed degreewise on any complex `E` representing `K`
(`Stacks.Duality.derivedStalkOfComplex`). The second conjunct says that `δ(x)` is *the* integer
of the source: for every representative `E`, `ω^•_{X,x}⟦-n⟧` is a normalized dualizing complex
exactly when `n = δ(x)`. The third says that `δ` is a dimension function.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniversallyCatenary_and_isDimensionFunction_associatedShiftFunction
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {K : DerivedCategory X.Modules} (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsUniversallyCatenary X ∧
      (∀ (x : X) (E : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ), Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ≅ K) →
        ∀ n : ℤ, Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} (A := X.presheaf.stalk x)
            ((derivedStalkOfComplex x E)⟦-n⟧) ↔ n = associatedShiftFunction K x) ∧
      ∃ d : TopologicalSpace.DimensionFunction X, ∀ x : X, d x = associatedShiftFunction K x

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.qcqsTrace
declarations.doc:
**The trace map `Tr_f : Rf_* ∘ a ⟶ id`** of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes, where `a` is the right adjoint of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_X) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_Y)`
([Stacks, Tag 0A9E]): the counit of the adjunction `Rf_* ⊣ a`.
declarations.statement:
def qcqsTrace :
    twistedInverseImage f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f) ⋙
        quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f) ⟶
      𝟭 _
declarations.comment: the trace map Tr_f : Rf_* ∘ a ⟶ id of a morphism of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, the counit of the adjunction Rf_* ⊣ a of Tag 0A9E

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.twistedInverseImageAdjunction_homEquiv_symm_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**The trace map characterizes the right adjoint.** For a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of
quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes, the bijection
`Hom_X(L, a(K)) ⟶ Hom_Y(Rf_*L, K)` of the adjunction `Rf_* ⊣ a` sends `φ` to
`Tr_{f,K} ∘ Rf_*φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem twistedInverseImageAdjunction_homEquiv_symm_qcqs (L : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory Y)
    (φ : L ⟶ (twistedInverseImage f
      (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).obj K) :
    ((twistedInverseImageAdjunction f
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).homEquiv L K).symm φ =
      (quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward f
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)).map φ ≫
        (qcqsTrace f).app K
declarations.comment: the bijection Hom_X(L, a(K)) ⟶ Hom_Y(Rf_*L, K) characterizing the right adjoint is φ ↦ Tr_{f,K} ∘ Rf_*φ

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingModuleOf.shift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWH.** The dualizing complex is not unique. If `ω` is a dualizing
module of the dualizing complex `K`, realized in degree `n`, then for every integer `k` the
shifted complex `K⟦k⟧` is again a dualizing complex, its dualizing module is realized in degree
`n - k` and is isomorphic to `ω`, and for `k ≠ 0` the complex `K⟦k⟧` is not isomorphic to `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDualizingModuleOf.shift [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules] {ω : X.Modules}
    {K : DerivedCategory X.Modules} {n : ℤ} (h : IsDualizingModuleOf ω K n) (k : ℤ) :
    IsDualizingModuleOf ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules (n - k)).obj (K⟦k⟧))
        (K⟦k⟧) (n - k) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules (n - k)).obj (K⟦k⟧) ≅ ω) ∧
      (k ≠ 0 → IsEmpty (K⟦k⟧ ≅ K))
declarations.comment: the first half of the section's second warning: the dualizing complex is not unique. A shift of a dualizing complex is a dualizing complex, not isomorphic to it for a nonzero shift, with the same dualizing module in the shifted degree

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingModuleOf.exists_isInvertibleModule_iso_sheafTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWH.** On a connected locally Noetherian scheme the dualizing module
is unique up to tensoring by an invertible module: if `ω` is a dualizing module of the dualizing
complex `K` and `ω'` one of the dualizing complex `K'`, there is an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `ℒ`
with `ω' ≅ ω ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℒ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDualizingModuleOf.exists_isInvertibleModule_iso_sheafTensor [ConnectedSpace X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules] {ω ω' : X.Modules} {K K' : DerivedCategory X.Modules}
    {n n' : ℤ} (h : IsDualizingModuleOf ω K n) (h' : IsDualizingModuleOf ω' K' n') :
    ∃ ℒ : X.Modules, Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.IsInvertibleModule X.sheaf ℒ ∧
      Nonempty (ω' ≅ ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor X.sheaf).obj ω).obj ℒ)
declarations.comment: the second half of the section's second warning: the dualizing module is unique up to tensoring by an invertible module. Stated for a connected locally Noetherian scheme: on a disconnected one two dualizing complexes can shift by different amounts on different components and their dualizing modules then need not differ by a twist (counterexample Spec k disjoint union Spec k in the module documentation). The relation between the two complexes is proved, from Tag 0ATP and Tag 0FPG, not assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingModuleOf_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWH, the definition.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `K`
a dualizing complex on `X`. Let `n` be the smallest integer such that `H^n(K)` is nonzero; then
`H^n(K)` is the dualizing module `ω_X`. This is what `Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingModuleOf ω K n`
says: it holds exactly when `K` is a dualizing complex, `n` is the least degree with nonzero
cohomology, and `ω = H^n(K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingModuleOf_iff {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules] (ω : X.Modules) (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (n : ℤ) :
    IsDualizingModuleOf ω K n ↔ IsDualizingComplex K ∧
      IsLeast {i : ℤ | ¬ IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K)} n ∧
      ω = (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules n).obj K
declarations.comment: the definition the section states: omega_X = H^n(omega_X^bullet) with n the smallest integer such that H^n(omega_X^bullet) is nonzero, for a dualizing complex on a (locally) Noetherian scheme; IsDualizingModuleOf omega K n holds exactly when K is a dualizing complex, n is the least element of the set of degrees with nonzero cohomology, and omega is the cohomology sheaf in degree n

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isGreatest_neg_of_isDualizingModuleOf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWH.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme and let `ω` be a
dualizing module of the dualizing complex `K`, realized in degree `n`, the least degree in which
`K` has nonvanishing cohomology. Then `-n` is the maximal value of the dimension function attached
to `K` by [Stacks, Tag 0AWF], the function `δ = associatedShiftFunction K` with
`ω^•_{X,x}⟦-δ(x)⟧` a normalized dualizing complex over `𝒪_{X,x}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGreatest_neg_of_isDualizingModuleOf {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules] {ω : X.Modules} {K : DerivedCategory X.Modules} {n : ℤ}
    (hω : IsDualizingModuleOf ω K n) :
    IsGreatest (Set.range (associatedShiftFunction K)) (-n)
declarations.comment: the section's identification of the degree: -n is the maximal value of the dimension function attached to omega_X^bullet (Tag 0AWF), where n is the least degree in which the dualizing complex has nonvanishing cohomology. The dimension function is associatedShiftFunction K, which Tag 0AWF (isUniversallyCatenary_and_isDimensionFunction_associatedShiftFunction) shows is the normalizing shift of the derived stalks and a dimension function. Stated for a locally Noetherian scheme, which contains the source's Noetherian case

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingModuleOf.restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWH, the first warning.** Let `ω` be a dualizing module of the
dualizing complex `K` on `X`, realized in degree `n`, let `U ⊆ X` be open and let `ω_U` be a
dualizing module of the restriction `K|_U`, realized in degree `n_U`. Then `n ≤ n_U`; if
`n = n_U` then `ω|_U ≅ ω_U`; and if the degree changes, `n < n_U`, then `ω|_U` is zero while `ω_U`
is not, so `ω|_U` is not isomorphic to `ω_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDualizingModuleOf.restrict {ω : X.Modules} {K : DerivedCategory X.Modules} {n : ℤ}
    (h : IsDualizingModuleOf ω K n) (U : X.Opens) [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} U.toScheme.Modules]
    {ωU : U.toScheme.Modules} {nU : ℤ}
    (hU : IsDualizingModuleOf ωU
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) nU) :
    n ≤ nU ∧ (n = nU → Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj ω ≅ ωU)) ∧
      (n < nU → IsZero ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj ω) ∧ ¬ IsZero ωU ∧
        IsEmpty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj ω ≅ ωU))
declarations.comment: the section's first warning: the integer n may change on passing to an open U, and then the restriction of omega_X to U is not omega_U. The degree can only go up, the two modules agree when it does not change, and when it changes the restriction is zero while omega_U is not

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingModuleOf.restrict_of_associatedShiftFunction_genericPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWH, the closing remark on the first warning.** If the dimension
function attached to `K` ([Stacks, Tag 0AWF]) takes the same value at every generic point of `X`,
then the degree of the dualizing module does not change on passing to a nonempty open `U ⊆ X`,
and the restriction of the dualizing module of `K` is the dualizing module of `K|_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDualizingModuleOf.restrict_of_associatedShiftFunction_genericPoints
    {ω : X.Modules} {K : DerivedCategory X.Modules} {n : ℤ}
    (h : IsDualizingModuleOf ω K n)
    (hgen : ∃ c : ℤ, ∀ ξ ∈ genericPoints X, associatedShiftFunction K ξ = c)
    (U : X.Opens) (hne : (U : Set X).Nonempty) [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} U.toScheme.Modules]
    {ωU : U.toScheme.Modules} {nU : ℤ}
    (hU : IsDualizingModuleOf ωU
      ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) nU) :
    nU = n ∧ Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj ω ≅ ωU)
declarations.comment: the section's closing remark on the first warning: if the dimension function attached to omega_X^bullet (Tag 0AWF) maps every generic point of X to the same integer, the degree does not change on a nonempty open U and omega_X restricted to U is omega_U

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingModuleOf_relativeDualizingModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWI (Example 48.22.1).** Let `S` be affine with
`A = Γ(S, ⊤)` a Noetherian local ring, `ω_S^•` modelled on `S` by a normalized dualizing complex
`ω_A^•`, `f : X ⟶ S` proper and `ω_X^• = f^!ω_S^• = a(ω_S^•)`. Then `ω_X = H^{-dim X}(ω_X^•)` is a
coherent sheaf, and, `X` being nonempty, a dualizing module: `ω_X^•` is a dualizing complex and
`-dim X` is the least degree in which it has nonzero cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingModuleOf_relativeDualizingModule
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] (ωS : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory S)
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(S, ⊤)))
    (hω : Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} ω)
    (hmodel : IsTildeModelOnAnyModel ωS.obj ⊤ (isAffineOpen_top S) ω) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian f
    (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        ωS).IsCoherent ∧
      (Nonempty X → IsDualizingModuleOf
        (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f) ωS)
        (relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
          ωS).obj (-(natDim X : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: the whole example

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.normalizedDualizingModule
declarations.doc:
**The dualizing module `ω_X = H^{-dim(X)}(ω_X^•)`** of [Stacks, Tag 0AWJ]: the cohomology
sheaf in degree minus the dimension of `X` of a complex normalized relative to a chosen complex
on the base. Over a field, with `ω_S^• = k[0]`, this is the customary dualizing module of an
equidimensional scheme of finite type over `k`.
declarations.statement: def normalizedDualizingModule (𝒩 : Normalized A hp ωS 𝒰) : X.Modules
declarations.comment: the definition: omega_X = H^{-dim X}(omega_X^bullet) for the complex normalized relative to k[0]

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.normalizedUpperShriekOverField
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWJ]** For `X` separated and of finite type over a field `k` with structure
morphism `f : X ⟶ Spec(k)`, the complex `f^!𝒪_{Spec(k)}` is normalized relative to `k[0]`: this
is the identification `ω_X^• = f^!𝒪_{Spec(k)}` the example records, by [Stacks, Tag 0AUE].
declarations.comment: the second assertion: for X separated over k the normalized complex is f^! O_{Spec k}. RESTRICTED: the upper-shriek formalism of Stacks 0A9Y/0ATX/0ATY is the parameter UpperShriek, pending its landing

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isDualizingComplex_normalizedDualizingComplex_of_field
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWJ], the complex `ω_X^•`.** For `X` of finite type over a field `k`, the
dualizing complex `ω_X^•` normalized relative to `k[0]` (`k[0]` being a dualizing complex on
`Spec(k)`) is a dualizing complex, and it is unique up to unique isomorphism: any complex
normalized relative to `k[0]` is isomorphic to it by exactly one isomorphism compatible with
the normalizations.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_normalizedDualizingComplex_of_field :
    haveI := (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p).source_noetherian
    IsDualizingComplex (normalizedDualizingComplex (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
        (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k)))
        (isDualizingComplex_derivedStructureSheafPlus_of_field k)).complex.obj.obj ∧
    ∀ 𝒦 : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
        (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k))),
      ∃! e : (normalizedDualizingComplex (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
          (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k)))
          (isDualizingComplex_derivedStructureSheafPlus_of_field k)).complex ≅ 𝒦.complex,
        ∀ (W : X.Opens) (hW : IsShriekable (W.ι ≫ p)),
          (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek W.ι
              ((isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p).isShriekable_ι W)).mapIso e ≪≫
            𝒦.localIso W hW =
          (normalizedDualizingComplex (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
            (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k)))
            (isDualizingComplex_derivedStructureSheafPlus_of_field k)).localIso W hW
declarations.comment: omega_X^bullet, the dualizing complex normalized relative to k[0]

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleOfCompactifications_nagata_eq
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWJ], the module `ω_X`.** For `X` of finite type over a field `k`, the
dualizing module `ω_X` is `H^{-dim(X)}(ω_X^•)`, the cohomology sheaf in degree minus the dimension
of `X` of the dualizing complex normalized relative to `k[0]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModuleOfCompactifications_nagata_eq :
    dualizingModuleOfCompactifications nagataCompactification p =
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules
        (-(ENat.toNat ((topologicalKrullDim X).getD 0) : ℤ))).obj
        (normalizedDualizingComplex (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
          (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k)))
          (isDualizingComplex_derivedStructureSheafPlus_of_field k)).complex.obj.obj
declarations.comment: omega_X = H^{-dim X}(omega_X^bullet)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.existsUnique_iso_upperShriekPlus_of_field
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWJ], the separated case.** If `X` is separated and of finite type over a
field `k`, then `ω_X^• = f^! 𝒪_{Spec(k)}`, `f : X ⟶ Spec(k)` being the structure morphism and
`f^!` the upper shriek functor of [Stacks, Tag 0A9Y] at any compactification `j` of `f`: there is
exactly one isomorphism `ω_X^• ≅ f^!_j 𝒪_{Spec(k)}` which, followed by the comparison with the
Nagata compactification, carries the normalization of `ω_X^•` on each open `W` separated over `k`
to the canonical `(f^! 𝒪_{Spec(k)})|_W ≅ (W → Spec(k))^! 𝒪_{Spec(k)}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_iso_upperShriekPlus_of_field [IsSeparated p]
    (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk p)) :
    haveI := isNoetherian_spec_of_field k
    ∃! e : (normalizedDualizingComplex (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
        (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k)))
        (isDualizingComplex_derivedStructureSheafPlus_of_field k)).complex ≅
      (upperShriekPlus (ftsHomOf p (isShriekable_of_field p).separatedFiniteType
        (isSeparatedFiniteType_id _) (Category.comp_id p)) j).obj
        (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k))),
      ∀ (W : X.Opens) (hW : IsShriekable (W.ι ≫ p)),
        (UpperShriek.nagata.shriek W.ι
            ((isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p).isShriekable_ι W)).mapIso
            (e ≪≫ (DominatingCompactification.upperShriekPlusIso (ftsHomOf p
              (isShriekable_of_field p).separatedFiniteType (isSeparatedFiniteType_id _)
              (Category.comp_id p)) j
              (nagataCompactification p (isShriekable_of_field p))).app
              (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k)))) ≪≫
          upperShriekLocalIso UpperShriek.nagata (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
            (isShriekable_of_field p) (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k))) hW =
        (normalizedDualizingComplex (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
          (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k)))
          (isDualizingComplex_derivedStructureSheafPlus_of_field k)).localIso W hW
declarations.comment: for X separated over k, omega_X^bullet = f^! O_{Spec k}

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.normalizedDualizingComplexIsoRelativeDualizingComplexOfField
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWJ], the proper case: `ω_X^• = a(𝒪_{Spec(k)})`.** If `X` is proper over a
field `k`, the dualizing complex normalized relative to `k[0]` is the twisted inverse image
`a(𝒪_{Spec(k)})` of [Stacks, Tag 0A9E], that is, the relative dualizing complex `f^! ω_S^•` of
[Stacks, Tag 0AWI] for `S = Spec(k)` and `ω_S^• = k[0]`.
declarations.statement:
def normalizedDualizingComplexIsoRelativeDualizingComplexOfField [IsProper p] :
    haveI := isNoetherian_spec_of_field k
    haveI := (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p).source_noetherian
    (normalizedDualizingComplex (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
        (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k)))
        (isDualizingComplex_derivedStructureSheafPlus_of_field k)).complex.obj ≅
      relativeDualizingComplex p (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs p)
        (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))
declarations.comment: for X proper over k, omega_X^bullet = a(O_{Spec k}), the complex of Example 0AWI

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleOfCompactifications_nagata_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWJ], the proper case is a special case of [Stacks, Tag 0AWI].** If `X` is
proper over a field `k`, then `ω_X` is the relative dualizing module of [Stacks, Tag 0AWI] for
`S = Spec(k)` and `ω_S^• = k[0]` (a normalized dualizing complex over the local ring `k`); hence
`ω_X` is coherent and, `X` being nonempty, a dualizing module: `ω_X^•` is a dualizing complex and
`-dim(X)` is the least degree in which it has nonzero cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualizingModuleOfCompactifications_nagata_of_isProper [IsProper p] :
    haveI := isNoetherian_spec_of_field k
    haveI := (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p).source_noetherian
    Nonempty (dualizingModuleOfCompactifications nagataCompactification p ≅
        relativeDualizingModule p (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs p)
          (DerivedPushforward.derivedStructureSheaf (Spec (.of k)))) ∧
      (dualizingModuleOfCompactifications nagataCompactification p).IsCoherent ∧
      (Nonempty X → IsDualizingModuleOf
        (dualizingModuleOfCompactifications nagataCompactification p)
        (normalizedDualizingComplex (isFiniteTypeOverNoetherian_of_field p)
          (derivedStructureSheafPlus (Spec (.of k)))
          (isDualizingComplex_derivedStructureSheafPlus_of_field k)).complex.obj.obj
        (-(natDim X : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: for X proper over k, this is a special case of Example 0AWI

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingModuleOf.sheafHasPropertySk_two
declarations.doc:
