**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWK**, the `(S₂)` clause. The dualizing module of a dualizing complex
on a connected Noetherian scheme satisfies Serre's condition `(S₂)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsDualizingModuleOf.sheafHasPropertySk_two {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    [ConnectedSpace X] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules] {ω : X.Modules}
    {K : DerivedCategory X.Modules} {n : ℤ} (h : IsDualizingModuleOf ω K n) :
    SheafHasPropertySk X ω 2
declarations.comment: the (S₂) clause

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.IsDualizingModuleOf.supp_eq_and_isCoherent_and_sheafHasPropertySk_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWK.** Let `X` be a connected Noetherian scheme and let `ω` be a
dualizing module on `X`, the cohomology sheaf of a dualizing complex `K` in the leftmost degree
`n` in which `K` has nonvanishing cohomology. Then the support of `ω` is the union of the
irreducible components of maximal dimension with respect to any dimension function `δ`, and `ω`
is a coherent `𝒪_X`-module having property `(S₂)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsDualizingModuleOf.supp_eq_and_isCoherent_and_sheafHasPropertySk_two
    [ConnectedSpace X] (h : IsDualizingModuleOf ω K n) :
    (∀ δ : DimensionFunction X,
      (⟨ω.val, ω.isSheaf⟩ : RingedSpace.ModuleSheaf.{u} X.toRingedSpace).supp =
        {x : X | ∃ ξ ∈ genericPoints X, x ∈ closure {ξ} ∧
          ∀ η ∈ genericPoints X, δ η ≤ δ ξ}) ∧
      _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent ω ∧ SheafHasPropertySk X ω 2

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isNormalizedDualizingComplex_derivedStalkOfComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWL (Lemma 48.21.1).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme with a
dualizing complex `ω_S^•`, let `p : X ⟶ S` be of finite type, and let `ω_X^•` be normalized
relative to `ω_S^•`: every point has an affine open neighbourhood `U` with
`ω_X^•|_U ≅ (U ⟶ S)^! ω_S^•` for a compactification of `U` over `S`. Let `x ∈ X` be a closed
point and `s = p x`. If `ω_{S,s}^•` is a normalized dualizing complex over `𝒪_{S,s}`, then
`ω_{X,x}^•` is a normalized dualizing complex over `𝒪_{X,x}`. The source also asks that `s` be
closed; this is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormalizedDualizingComplex_derivedStalkOfComplex
    {S X : Scheme.{u}} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S] (p : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p]
    (ωS : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory S) (hωS : IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj)
    (ωX : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hωX : ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffine U.toScheme) (_ : x ∈ U)
      (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (ftsHomToBase (U.ι ≫ p)).left)),
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj ωX ≅
        ((upperShriek (ftsHomToBase (U.ι ≫ p)) j).obj ωS).obj))
    (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (hωSs : ∃ E : CochainComplex S.Modules ℤ, Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ≅ ωS.obj) ∧
      Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} (derivedStalkOfComplex (p x) E)) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian p
    ∀ E : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ, Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ≅ ωX) →
      Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} (derivedStalkOfComplex x E)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isNormalizedDualizingComplex_derivedStalkOfComplex_normalizedDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWL].** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme with a dualizing complex `ω_S^•`, let
`X` be of finite type over `S` and `ω_X^•` the dualizing complex normalized relative to `ω_S^•`.
If `x ∈ X` is a closed point lying over a closed point `s` of `S`, then `ω_{X,x}^•` is a
normalized dualizing complex over `𝒪_{X,x}` provided that `ω_{S,s}^•` is a normalized dualizing
complex over `𝒪_{S,s}`. Stalks are the derived stalks of representatives; the closedness of `s`
is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormalizedDualizingComplex_derivedStalkOfComplex_normalizedDualizingComplex
    (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (hωSs : haveI := hp.base_noetherian
      ∃ E : CochainComplex S.Modules ℤ, Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ≅ ωS.obj.obj) ∧
      Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u}
        (@derivedStalkOfComplex S (p x) (HasDerivedCategory.standard _) E)) :
    haveI := hp.source_noetherian
    ∀ E : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ,
      Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj E ≅ (normalizedDualizingComplex hp ωS hωS).complex.obj.obj) →
        Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u}
          (@derivedStalkOfComplex X x (HasDerivedCategory.standard _) E)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.associatedShiftFunction_sub_eq_trdeg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWM.** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme and let `ω_S^•` be a dualizing
complex. Let `f : X ⟶ S` be of finite type and let `ω_X^•` be the dualizing complex normalized
relative to `ω_S^•`. For all `x ∈ X`

`δ_X(x) - δ_S(f x) = trdeg_{κ(f x)} κ(x)`

where `δ_S`, resp. `δ_X`, is the dimension function of `ω_S^•`, resp. `ω_X^•`, of
[Stacks, Tag 0AWF] — here `Stacks.Duality.associatedShiftFunction`.

Universal catenarity of `S`, which [Stacks, Tag 02JW] needs, is *derived* from `hωS` by
[Stacks, Tag 0AWF] (`Stacks.Duality.isUniversallyCatenary_of_isDualizingComplex`). What is
carried are the three things this repository does not have:

* `δS`, `δX` with `hδS`, `hδX` — that the shift functions *are* dimension functions. This is
  the companion half of [Stacks, Tag 0AWF], which
  `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Duality/RelativeDualizing/AssociatedShiftFunction.lean` states
  explicitly that it does not prove; only the universally-catenary half is proved.
* `hClosedImage` — that `f` carries closed points to closed points, the source's reduction to a
  proper `f`.
* `hClosedPoint` — the identity at a closed point over a closed point, [Stacks, Tag 0AWL],
  proved as
  `Stacks.Duality.isNormalizedDualizingComplex_derivedStalkOfComplex_normalizedDualizingComplex`;
  what is missing is the bridge from that statement about normalized stalks to a value of
  `Stacks.Duality.associatedShiftFunction`.

The relation between `ω_X^•` and `ω_S^•` enters only through `hClosedPoint`, which is exactly
where the source uses it; the complex `ω_X^•` is otherwise a parameter.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedShiftFunction_sub_eq_trdeg {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [HasDerivedCategory S.Modules] [HasDerivedCategory X.Modules]
    (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    {ωS : DerivedCategory S.Modules} (hωS : IsDualizingComplex ωS)
    (ωX : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (δS : DimensionFunction S) (hδS : ∀ s : S, δS s = associatedShiftFunction ωS s)
    (δX : DimensionFunction X) (hδX : ∀ y : X, δX y = associatedShiftFunction ωX y)
    (hClosedImage : ∀ y : X, IsClosed ({y} : Set X) → IsClosed ({f y} : Set S))
    (hClosedPoint : ∀ y : X, IsClosed ({y} : Set X) → IsClosed ({f y} : Set S) →
      associatedShiftFunction ωX y = associatedShiftFunction ωS (f y))
    (x : X) :
    letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    associatedShiftFunction ωX x - associatedShiftFunction ωS (f x) =
      (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x)) : ℤ)
declarations.comment:
RESTRICTED: three inputs are explicit hypotheses. That the shift functions of the
two dualizing complexes are dimension functions is the unproved half of Tag 0AWF, carried as
dimension functions delta_S and delta_X together with hdS and hdX. That f carries closed points
to closed points -- the source's reduction to a proper f, through Nagata compactification and
Tag 0AUC -- is hClosedImage. The identity at a closed point over a closed point, Tag 0AWL, is
hClosedPoint; 0AWL itself is proved, but the bridge from normalized stalks to a value of
associatedShiftFunction is not. What is proved is the body of the lemma: universal catenarity
of S from Tag 0AWF, then that the difference of the two functions is determined by its values at
closed points, by Tag 02JW and Tag 02IB and Tag 02IL, and that the transcendence degree vanishes
at a closed point, by Tag 01TF

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.associatedShiftFunction_sub_eq_trdeg_of_upperShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWM (Lemma 48.21.2).** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme with a
dualizing complex `ω_S^•`, let `p : X ⟶ S` be of finite type, and let `ω_X^•` be normalized
relative to `ω_S^•`: every point has an affine open neighbourhood `U` with
`ω_X^•|_U ≅ (U ⟶ S)^! ω_S^•` for a compactification of `U` over `S`. Then for every `x ∈ X`,
`δ_X(x) - δ_S(p x) = trdeg_{κ(p x)} κ(x)`, where `δ_X`, `δ_S` are the dimension functions of
`ω_X^•`, `ω_S^•` ([Stacks, Tag 0AWF]).
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedShiftFunction_sub_eq_trdeg_of_upperShriek
    {S X : Scheme.{u}} [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian S] (p : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p]
    (ωS : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory S) (hωS : IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj)
    (ωX : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hωX : ∀ x : X, ∃ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffine U.toScheme) (_ : x ∈ U)
      (j : CompactificationOf (Over.mk (ftsHomToBase (U.ι ≫ p)).left)),
      Nonempty ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj ωX ≅
        ((upperShriek (ftsHomToBase (U.ι ≫ p)) j).obj ωS).obj))
    (x : X) :
    letI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian p
    letI := (p.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    associatedShiftFunction ωX x - associatedShiftFunction ωS.obj (p x) =
      (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (p x)) (X.residueField x)) : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.associatedShiftFunction_sub_eq_trdeg_normalizedDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWM].** Let `S` be a Noetherian scheme with a dualizing complex `ω_S^•`, let
`p : X ⟶ S` be of finite type and `ω_X^•` the dualizing complex normalized relative to `ω_S^•`.
For all `x ∈ X`, `δ_X(x) - δ_S(p x) = trdeg_{κ(p x)} κ(x)`, where `δ_S`, `δ_X` are the
dimension functions of `ω_S^•`, `ω_X^•` ([Stacks, Tag 0AWF]).
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedShiftFunction_sub_eq_trdeg_normalizedDualizingComplex (x : X) :
    haveI := hp.base_noetherian
    haveI := hp.source_noetherian
    letI := (p.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
    associatedShiftFunction (normalizedDualizingComplex hp ωS hωS).complex.obj.obj x -
        associatedShiftFunction ωS.obj.obj (p x) =
      (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (p x)) (X.residueField x)) : ℤ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.vanishing_and_support_relativeDualizingComplex
declarations.statement:
theorem vanishing_and_support_relativeDualizingComplex
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] (ωS : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory S)
    (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Γ(S, ⊤)))
    (hω : Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} ω)
    (hmodel : IsTildeModelOnAnyModel ωS.obj ⊤ (isAffineOpen_top S) ω) :
    let L := (relativeDualizingComplex f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
      ωS).obj
    (∀ i : ℤ, ¬ Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj L) →
      i ≤ 0 ∧ (((-i).toNat : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim X) ∧
    (∀ i : ℤ, topologicalKrullDim (_root_.SheafOfModules.supp
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj L)) ≤
      if i ≤ 0 then (((-i).toNat : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) else ⊥) ∧
    (relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f)
        ωS).IsCoherent ∧
    SheafHasPropertySk X (relativeDualizingModule f
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f) ωS) 2 ∧
    _root_.SheafOfModules.supp (relativeDualizingModule f
        (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f) ωS) =
      ⋃₀ {C ∈ irreducibleComponents X | topologicalKrullDim C = topologicalKrullDim X}

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.supp_relativeDualizingModule_eq_topDimensionalComponents
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWN, part (3).** Let `X/A` with `ω_X^•` and `ω_X` be as in
[Stacks, Tag 0AWI]. Then `Supp(ω_X)` is the union of the irreducible components of `X` of
dimension `dim(X)`, given the hypothesis `hcomp` that a point `x` satisfies
`dim(closure {x}) + dim(𝒪_{X,x}) = dim(X)` exactly when it lies on an irreducible component of `X`
of dimension `dim(X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supp_relativeDualizingModule_eq_topDimensionalComponents
    (hloc : HasNormalizedStalks (relativeDualizingComplex f hpush ωY).obj n)
    (hcomp : ∀ x : X, topologicalKrullDim (closure ({x} : Set X)) +
          ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = (n : WithBot ℕ∞) ↔
        x ∈ ⋃₀ {C ∈ irreducibleComponents X | topologicalKrullDim C = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)}) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.supp (relativeDualizingModule f hpush ωY) =
      ⋃₀ {C ∈ irreducibleComponents X | topologicalKrullDim C = (n : WithBot ℕ∞)}
declarations.comment: part (3): Supp(omega_X) is the union of the components of dimension dim(X). RESTRICTED: two explicit hypotheses. hloc is the local description of omega_X^bullet, a Stacks.Duality.HasNormalizedStalks; see part (1) for what it records and why. hcomp is a statement about a catenary Noetherian scheme with no dualizing complex in it -- that a point satisfies dim(closure {x}) + dim(O_{X,x}) = dim(X) exactly when it lies on an irreducible component of dimension dim(X); its analogue over a Noetherian local ring is the catenary step inside Dualizing.support_canonicalModule of Tag 0AWE, but the scheme-level statement is not proved here. The dualizing content is proved and is unconditional given hloc: supp_relativeDualizingModule_eq_setOf identifies Supp(omega_X) with the locus where that equality holds, by the lower degree bound of Tag 0A7U and the nonvanishing of the canonical module of Tag 0A7V on the stalk

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleRepresentableBy
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AWP].** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a Noetherian local ring and let `ω_S^•` be an
object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec A})` corresponding to a normalized dualizing complex `ω_A^•`. Let
`f : X ⟶ Spec A` be proper, `ω_X^• = f^×ω_S^•` and `ω_X = H^{-dim(X)}(ω_X^•)`, as in
Example [Stacks, Tag 0AWI]. Let `d` bound the dimension of the closed fibre `X_s` and suppose
`dim(X) = d + dim(A)`. Then `ω_X` represents the functor

  `ℱ ↦ Hom_A(H^d(X, ℱ), ω_A)`,   `ω_A = H^{-dim(A)}(ω_A^•)`,

on the quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-modules — so in particular on the coherent ones.

The represented functor is `ℱ ↦ Hom_A(H^d(X, ℱ), ω_A)` with `H^d(X, ℱ)` the classical sheaf
cohomology with its `A`-module structure, and the representation is
`Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleHomAddEquiv`, natural by
`Stacks.Duality.dualizingModuleHomAddEquiv_naturality`. Nothing is carried: part (1) of
[Stacks, Tag 0AWN], the vanishing of `H^i(ω_X^•)` below `-dim(X)` that the source's first
equality needs, is `Stacks.Duality.isGE_relativeDualizingComplex_of_closedFibre_dim_le`.
declarations.statement:
def dualizingModuleRepresentableBy :
    (((SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).ι ⋙
        Stacks.LocalCohomology.cohomologyOverBaseFunctor.{u, u} A f d).op ⋙
      yoneda.obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-(e : ℤ))).obj
        ((derivedGlobalSectionsQuasicoherent (CommRingCat.of A)).obj ωS))).RepresentableBy
      (⟨relativeDualizingModule f (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f) ωS,
        isQuasicoherent_relativeDualizingModule f
          (isQuasicoherent_homology_derivedPushforward_of_qcqs f) ωS⟩ :
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, in the setting of Example 0AWI with omega_X^bullet the twisted inverse image of omega_S^bullet (the relative dualizing complex of the 0AWI definition) and omega_A = H^{-dim A}(omega_A^bullet); the functor is represented on all quasi-coherent modules, which contain the coherent ones, and d may be any upper bound for dim(X_s) with dim(X) = d + dim(A)

declarations.name: Dualizing.depth_eq_least_nonzero_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWR.** The depth of a Noetherian local ring `A` with normalized
dualizing complex `ω_A` is the least `δ ≥ 0` with `H^{-δ}(ω_A) ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_eq_least_nonzero_homology {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, 0} K) :
    ∃ δ : ℕ,
      IsLeast
          {i : ℕ |
            ¬ IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) (-(i : ℤ))).obj K)}
          δ ∧
        Module.depth A (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A = (δ : ℕ∞)

declarations.name: Dualizing.isCohenMacaulay_tfae_dualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWS, equivalent conditions (1)--(3).** A Noetherian local ring is
Cohen--Macaulay exactly when its normalized dualizing complex is concentrated in one degree,
and exactly when it is its dualizing module placed in degree minus the dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulay_tfae_dualizingComplex {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, 0} K) :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing A,
        IsCohomologicallyConcentratedInOneDegree K,
        Nonempty
          (K ≅
            (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A)
              (-(localRingDimension A : ℤ))).obj (dualizingModule K)) ]
declarations.comment: equivalent conditions (1)--(3)

declarations.name: Dualizing.dualizingModule_isMaximalCohenMacaulay
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWS, final assertion.** Over a Cohen--Macaulay local ring, the
dualizing module of a normalized dualizing complex is maximal Cohen--Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dualizingModule_isMaximalCohenMacaulay {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, 0} K)
    (hA : IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing A) :
    Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay A (dualizingModule K)
declarations.comment: the dualizing module is maximal Cohen--Macaulay

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.sheafIsCohenMacaulay_homology_of_concentrated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWT, the Cohen--Macaulayness of the dualizing module.** If the
cohomology of a dualizing complex on a locally Noetherian scheme is concentrated in the single
degree `n`, then `H^n` of it is a Cohen--Macaulay `𝒪_X`-module in the sense of
[Stacks, Tag 0343].
declarations.statement:
public theorem sheafIsCohenMacaulay_homology_of_concentrated {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules]
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) (n : ℤ)
    (hn : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ n → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafIsCohenMacaulay X
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules n).obj K)
declarations.comment: the dualizing module is Cohen--Macaulay, at an arbitrary degree of concentration

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.exists_coherent_cohenMacaulay_iso_single_of_connected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWT, the final assertion, in full.** If `X` is connected and
Cohen--Macaulay then there is an integer `n` and a coherent Cohen--Macaulay `𝒪_X`-module
`ω_X = H^n(ω_X^•)` with `ω_X^• = ω_X[-n]`.

This is `Stacks.Duality.exists_coherent_iso_single_of_connected` together with the
Cohen--Macaulayness clause of the source, which that statement omits.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_coherent_cohenMacaulay_iso_single_of_connected {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [ConnectedSpace X] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules]
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K)
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X) :
    ∃ n : ℤ, _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules n).obj K) ∧
      AlgebraicGeometry.SheafIsCohenMacaulay X
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules n).obj K) ∧
      Nonempty (K ≅ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules n).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules n).obj K))
declarations.comment: the final assertion, in full

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isOpen_setOf_isCohenMacaulayLocalRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWT, clause (3), openness.** On a locally Noetherian scheme carrying a
dualizing complex, the set of points whose local ring is Cohen–Macaulay is open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpen_setOf_isCohenMacaulayLocalRing {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules] (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    IsOpen {x : X | IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)}
declarations.comment: clause (3), the Cohen--Macaulay locus is open

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isCohenMacaulay_cohenMacaulayLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWT, clause (3), the locus is Cohen–Macaulay.** The open subscheme of
points with Cohen–Macaulay local ring is a Cohen–Macaulay scheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulay_cohenMacaulayLocus {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules] (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay (cohenMacaulayLocus K hK).toScheme
declarations.comment: clause (3), the Cohen--Macaulay locus is Cohen--Macaulay

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isCohenMacaulayLocalRing_stalk_iff_concentrated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWT, clause (2).** On a locally Noetherian scheme carrying a dualizing
complex `K`, the local ring at `x` is Cohen–Macaulay exactly when the derived stalk `K_x` has a
single nonzero cohomology module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulayLocalRing_stalk_iff_concentrated {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules]
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) (x : X)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} (X.presheaf.stalk x))] :
    IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) ↔
      ∃ n : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ n → Limits.IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (ModuleCat.{u} (X.presheaf.stalk x)) i).obj
        ((AlgebraicGeometry.derivedStalkFunctor x).obj K))
declarations.comment: clause (2), the stalkwise criterion

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isCohenMacaulay_iff_locally_unique_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWT, clause (1).** A locally Noetherian scheme carrying a dualizing
complex `K` is Cohen–Macaulay exactly when `K` locally has a single nonzero cohomology sheaf:
every point has an open neighbourhood on which, for all but one degree, the cohomology sheaves
of `K` have vanishing stalks.

Vanishing of all the stalks over an open is vanishing of the restricted sheaf there, by
[Stacks, Tag 01AG] (`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isZero_iff_forall_isZero_stalkFunctor_obj`),
so this is the source's "`ω_X^•` locally has a unique nonzero cohomology sheaf".
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCohenMacaulay_iff_locally_unique_homology {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules]
    (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X ↔
      ∀ x : X, ∃ V : X.Opens, x ∈ V ∧ ∃ n : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ n → ∀ y ∈ V,
        Subsingleton
          (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj K).presheaf.stalk y)
declarations.comment: clause (1), locally a single nonzero cohomology sheaf, read stalkwise

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isCohenMacaulay_of_exists_coherent_dualizingModule
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme. If there exists a coherent sheaf `ω_X` such that
`ω_X[0]` is a dualizing complex on `X`, then `X` is a Cohen–Macaulay scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCohenMacaulay_of_exists_coherent_dualizingModule
    (h : ∃ omegaX : X.Modules, _root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent omegaX ∧
      IsDualizingComplex ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj omegaX)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsCohenMacaulay X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isGorenstein_Spec_iff
declarations.doc:
**The definition of a Gorenstein scheme agrees with that of a Gorenstein ring** (Section
0AWV). For a Noetherian ring `R`, the scheme `Spec R` is Gorenstein if and only if `R` is a
Gorenstein ring, i.e. all of its local rings are Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorenstein_Spec_iff (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsGorenstein (Spec R) ↔ Dualizing.IsGorensteinRing R
declarations.comment: the definition makes sense: for a Noetherian ring R, Spec R is a Gorenstein scheme if and only if R is a Gorenstein ring

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein
registrations.comment: the definition of the section: a scheme is Gorenstein if it is locally Noetherian and all of its local rings are Gorenstein

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsGorenstein
declarations.doc:
A scheme is Gorenstein if it is locally Noetherian and all of its local rings are
Gorenstein.
declarations.statement: public class IsGorenstein (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop extends IsLocallyNoetherian X

declarations.name: Dualizing.IsRegularLocalRing.isGorensteinLocalRing
declarations.doc: A regular local ring is Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularLocalRing.isGorensteinLocalRing (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A] : IsGorensteinLocalRing A
declarations.comment: regular local rings

declarations.name: Dualizing.IsRegularRing.isGorensteinRing
declarations.doc: A regular ring is Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularRing.isGorensteinRing (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [IsRegularRing A] : IsGorensteinRing A
declarations.comment: regular rings

declarations.name: Dualizing.isGorensteinRing_formalFibre_of_isDualizingComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AWY.** Every formal fibre of a Noetherian local ring admitting a
dualizing complex is Gorenstein.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGorensteinRing_formalFibre_of_isDualizingComplex
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) (hK : IsDualizingComplex K)
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] :
    ∃ h : IsNoetherianRing (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A ⊗[A] p.ResidueField),
      @IsGorensteinRing (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A ⊗[A] p.ResidueField)
        inferInstance h

declarations.name: Dualizing.isDualizingComplex_derivedHom_of_finite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AX0.** For a finite homomorphism of Noetherian rings and a dualizing
complex `ω` over the source, `RHom_A(B, ω)` is a dualizing complex over `B`.

Noetherianity of `B` follows from that of `A` and finiteness of `f`, but it is a hypothesis here
because `Dualizing.IsDualizingComplex` is only stated over a Noetherian ring, so the conclusion
cannot be written down without it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDualizingComplex_derivedHom_of_finite [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (hf : f.Finite) (ω : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A))
    (hω : IsDualizingComplex ω) :
    IsDualizingComplex ((derivedHom.{u, v, u} f).obj ω)

declarations.name: Dualizing.isNormalizedDualizingComplex_derivedHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AX1.** If `A → B` is a finite local homomorphism of Noetherian local
rings and `K` is a normalized dualizing complex over `A`, then `RHom_A(B, K)` is a normalized
dualizing complex over `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormalizedDualizingComplex_derivedHom
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] (hf : f.Finite)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} A))
    (hK : IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, v} K) :
    IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, v}
      ((derivedHom.{u, v} f).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedHomSheaf_finite_pseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 0AX2.** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a finite pseudo-coherent morphism of schemes. The
functor `R ℰom(f₊ 𝒪_Y, -) : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(f₊ 𝒪_Y)` maps `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into `D⁺_QCoh(f₊ 𝒪_Y)`.
If `X` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then on `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)` the functor `Φ ∘ a` agrees
with `R ℰom(f₊ 𝒪_Y, -)`, where `a` is the right adjoint of Stacks, Tag 0A9E for `f` and `Φ` is
the equivalence of Stacks, Tag 0AVW. The functors `a` and `Φ` are taken at the locally small
models and `R ℰom(f₊ 𝒪_Y, -)` at the standard one, compared along the identity-on-objects
equivalence of the two models.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedHomSheaf_finite_pseudoCoherent [IsFinite f] [PseudoCoherent f] :
    (∀ K : @DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) _ _
          (HasDerivedCategory.standard _),
        @DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) K →
          @DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus _ _ _ (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
            (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (pushforwardRingCatSheaf f))
            ((derivedHomSheaf f).obj K)) ∧
      ∀ [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X],
        haveI : CompactSpace Y := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace f
        haveI : QuasiSeparatedSpace Y := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated f
        Nonempty (ObjectProperty.ι (fun K : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X =>
              DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj) ⋙ twistedInverseImageQcqs f ⋙
            (derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardOverRingEquivalence f).functor ⋙
              ObjectProperty.ι _ ≅
          ObjectProperty.ι (fun K : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X =>
              DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj) ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙
            (structureSheafModelEquiv X).inverse ⋙ derivedHomSheaf f ⋙
              (pushforwardRingModelEquiv f).functor)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_of_isFinite_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
A finite morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` to a locally
Noetherian scheme is pseudo-coherent; in particular a finite morphism of Noetherian schemes is
pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem pseudoCoherent_of_isFinite_of_isLocallyNoetherian {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite f] : PseudoCoherent f
declarations.comment: parenthetical remark: a finite morphism of Noetherian schemes is pseudo-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedSheafHom_pushforwardStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
For a finite pseudo-coherent morphism `f : Y ⟶ X`, the derived internal Hom
`R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(f_* 𝒪_Y, -)` carries `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into `D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedSheafHom_pushforwardStructureSheaf (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite f]
    (hf : PseudoCoherent f) (K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) K) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj
        (op ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf))))).obj K)
declarations.comment: the preservation clause with quasi-coherence read over 𝒪_X rather than over f_* 𝒪_Y; the commutative-diagram clause is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedSheafHom_of_pseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a finite pseudo-coherent morphism of schemes and let
`derivedSheafHom : D(𝒪_X) ⥤ D(f_* 𝒪_Y)` be a functor whose composite with restriction of scalars
along `𝒪_X ⟶ f_* 𝒪_Y` is the derived internal Hom `R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(f_* 𝒪_Y, -)`, which is what
[Stacks, Tag 0BV1] says of the derived sheaf-Hom functor.  Then `derivedSheafHom` maps
`D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_X)` into `D⁺_QCoh(f_* 𝒪_Y)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBPlus_derivedSheafHom_of_pseudoCoherent (f : Y ⟶ X) [IsFinite f]
    (hf : PseudoCoherent f)
    (derivedSheafHom : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (pushforwardRing f.base Y.ringCatSheaf)))
    (hsplit : derivedSheafHom ⋙ (scalarRestriction f).mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedSheafHom X.sheaf).obj
        (op ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor X.Modules 0).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf)))))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf))
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) K) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (pushforwardRing f.base Y.ringCatSheaf))
      (derivedSheafHom.obj K)
declarations.comment: the preservation clause, for a derived sheaf-Hom functor given together with its identification of Tag 0BV1; the commutative-diagram clause is not proved

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pushforwardRightAdjointToDerivedInternalHom_and_comp_evaluationOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AX3 (Remark 48.11.5).** Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a finite morphism of
schemes with `X` locally Noetherian — in particular a finite morphism of Noetherian schemes —
let `a` be a right adjoint of `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_Y) ⥤ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, and let `K` be an object of
`D_QCoh^+(𝒪_X)`.  Then in the square

```
Rf_* a(K)                     --Tr_{f, K}-->   K
    ‖                                          ‖
R ℰom_{𝒪_X}(f₊ 𝒪_Y, K)            -->          K
```

the left edge — the comparison map `Rf_* a(K) ⟶ R ℰom_{𝒪_X}(f₊ 𝒪_Y, K)` of
[Stacks, Tag 0AX2], the transpose of the trace along the adjunction of [Stacks, Tag 0BV0]
obtained by deriving `restriction of scalars ⊣ ℰom_{𝒪_X}(f₊ 𝒪_Y, -)` — is an isomorphism, so
that it is the identification the source draws as an equality, and the square commutes: that
isomorphism followed by the map `R ℰom_{𝒪_X}(f₊ 𝒪_Y, K) ⟶ K` induced by `𝒪_X ⟶ f₊ 𝒪_Y` is the
trace map `Tr_{f, K}`, the counit of `Rf_* ⊣ a`.  The lower arrow is
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedInternalHomPushforwardEvaluationOne`, the right derived functor of the
evaluation at `1`, `ℰom_{𝒪_X}(f₊ 𝒪_Y, F) ⟶ F`, `φ ↦ φ(1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pushforwardRightAdjointToDerivedInternalHom_and_comp_evaluationOne
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (K : quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow K.obj) :
    IsIso (pushforwardRightAdjointToDerivedInternalHom f adj K) ∧
      pushforwardRightAdjointToDerivedInternalHom f adj K ≫
          (derivedInternalHomPushforwardEvaluationOne f).app K.obj =
        (adj.counit.app K).hom
declarations.comment: the whole remark, for every right adjoint a of Rf_* on D_QCoh and every adjunction exhibiting it: the comparison map Rf_* a(K) ⟶ R Eom_{O_X}(f_* O_Y, K) of Tag 0AX2 is an isomorphism (the left equality of the square) and, followed by the map R Eom_{O_X}(f_* O_Y, K) ⟶ K induced by O_X ⟶ f_* O_Y (the right derived functor of evaluation at 1), it is the trace Tr_{f, K}. Stated for f finite and X locally Noetherian, which contains the source's finite morphism of Noetherian schemes, and K in D_QCoh^+(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.NormalizedOnOpens.exists_finitePushforwardIso_trace_nagata
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AX4]** Let `S` be Noetherian with a dualizing complex `ω_S^•`, `f : X ⟶ Y` a
finite morphism of schemes of finite type over `S`, and `ω_X^•`, `ω_Y^•` the dualizing complexes
normalized relative to `ω_S^•`. Then `R𝓗om(f_* 𝒪_X, ω_Y^•)` lies in `D⁺_QCoh(f_* 𝒪_X)` and
`f_* ω_X^• ≅ R𝓗om(f_* 𝒪_X, ω_Y^•)` there, by an isomorphism through which the trace map
`Tr_f : Rf_* ω_X^• ⟶ ω_Y^•` of [Stacks, Tag 0B6X] is
`Rf_* ω_X^• = f_* ω_X^• = R𝓗om(f_* 𝒪_X, ω_Y^•) ⟶ ω_Y^•`, evaluation at `1` (the counit of
`res ⊣ R𝓗om(f_* 𝒪_X, -)`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePushforwardIso_trace_nagata
    (hωS : haveI := hp.base_noetherian; IsDualizingComplex ωS.obj.obj) [IsFinite f]
    (𝒦X : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hp ωS)
    (𝒦Y : NormalizedOnOpens UpperShriek.nagata hq ωS) :
    haveI := hq.source_noetherian
    haveI := hp.source_noetherian
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBPlus
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (pushforwardRing f.base X.ringCatSheaf))
        (((structureSheafModelEquiv Y).inverse ⋙ derivedHomSheaf f ⋙
          (pushforwardRingModelEquiv f).functor).obj 𝒦Y.complex.obj.obj) ∧
      ∃ e : ((derivedQuasicoherentPushforwardOverRingEquivalence f).functor.obj
          𝒦X.complex.obj).obj ≅ ((structureSheafModelEquiv Y).inverse ⋙ derivedHomSheaf f ⋙
            (pushforwardRingModelEquiv f).functor).obj 𝒦Y.complex.obj.obj,
        (ObjectProperty.ι _).map (traceOfCompactifications nagataCompactification hpe hωS 𝒦X 𝒦Y) =
          (derivedPushforwardOverRingCompRestrictScalarsIso.{u} f).hom.app
              𝒦X.complex.obj.obj ≫
            (scalarRestriction f).mapDerivedCategory.map e.hom ≫
            (scalarRestrictionAdjunctionLS f).counit.app 𝒦Y.complex.obj.obj

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.higherTrace
declarations.doc:
The higher trace on differential forms for a presentation
`S ≅ R[X]/(X ^ p - a)`.
declarations.comment: the trace map

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.higherTrace_apply_of_le
declarations.doc: The higher trace of `η₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ ηₜ ∧ xⁱ dx` vanishes for `i ≤ p - 2`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem higherTrace_apply_of_le (hp : p.Prime) [CharP Λ p] (a : R)
    (e : AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C a) ≃ₐ[R] S) (i : ℕ)
    (hi : i ≤ p - 2) (η : Fin t → Ω[R⁄Λ]) :
    higherTrace (t := t) hp a e
      (exteriorPower.ιMulti S (t + 1)
        (Fin.snoc (fun j => KaehlerDifferential.map Λ Λ R S (η j))
          ((e (AdjoinRoot.root (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C a))) ^ i •
            KaehlerDifferential.D Λ S
              (e (AdjoinRoot.root (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C a)))))) = 0
declarations.comment: values below the top power

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.higherTrace_apply_top
declarations.doc:
The higher trace of `η₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ ηₜ ∧ x^(p-1) dx` is
`η₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ ηₜ ∧ da`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem higherTrace_apply_top (hp : p.Prime) [CharP Λ p] (a : R)
    (e : AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C a) ≃ₐ[R] S)
    (η : Fin t → Ω[R⁄Λ]) :
    higherTrace (t := t) hp a e
      (exteriorPower.ιMulti S (t + 1)
        (Fin.snoc (fun j => KaehlerDifferential.map Λ Λ R S (η j))
          ((e (AdjoinRoot.root (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C a))) ^ (p - 1) •
            KaehlerDifferential.D Λ S
              (e (AdjoinRoot.root (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C a)))))) =
      exteriorPower.ιMulti R (t + 1)
        (Fin.snoc η (KaehlerDifferential.D Λ R a))
declarations.comment: value at the top power

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.higherTrace_smul_baseForm
declarations.doc:
The higher trace annihilates the image of
`S ⊗[R] Ω^{t+1}_{R/Λ} → Ω^{t+1}_{S/Λ}`.  The displayed elements are a generating family for
that image.
declarations.statement:
public theorem higherTrace_smul_baseForm (hp : p.Prime) [CharP Λ p] (a : R)
    (e : AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C a) ≃ₐ[R] S) (s : S)
    (η : Fin (t + 1) → Ω[R⁄Λ]) :
    higherTrace (t := t) hp a e
      (s • exteriorPower.ιMulti S (t + 1)
        (fun j => KaehlerDifferential.map Λ Λ R S (η j))) = 0
declarations.comment: vanishing on forms from the base

declarations.name: KaehlerDifferential.higherTrace_eq_of_presentations
declarations.doc:
The higher trace is independent of the presentation of `S` as an algebra obtained by
adjoining a `p`-th root. In particular, changing the chosen generator does not change the
canonical trace on higher relative differential forms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem higherTrace_eq_of_presentations (hp : p.Prime) [CharP Λ p]
    (a b : R)
    (e : AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C a) ≃ₐ[R] S)
    (f : AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C b) ≃ₐ[R] S) :
    higherTrace (t := t) (Λ := Λ) hp a e =
      higherTrace (t := t) (Λ := Λ) hp b f
declarations.comment: independence of presentation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_higherTraceExtension_relativeDifferentials
declarations.doc:
Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a finite dominant morphism of integral
schemes over `S` with `X` normal and locally Noetherian, let the extension of function fields
`L/K` that `f` induces be presented as `L ≅ K[x]/(xᵖ - a)`, and let `i = t + 1 ≥ 1`.  Then there
is a unique map of `𝒪_X`-modules

`Tr : f_*Ω^i_{Y/S} ⟶ (Ω^i_{X/S})^∨∨`

whose stalk at the generic point of `X` is the trace map of [Stacks, Tag 0AX5] on
`⋀ⁱ Ω_{L/Λ} ⟶ ⋀ⁱ Ω_{K/Λ}`, where `Λ` is the local ring of `S` below the generic point, the
left-hand side is the generic stalk of `f_*Ω^i_{Y/S}` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.genericPushforwardFormsEquiv` and the right-hand side is the generic stalk of
`Ω^i_{X/S}` by `AlgebraicGeometry.genericFormsStalkEquiv`.  The trace does not depend on the
presentation (`KaehlerDifferential.higherTrace_eq_of_presentations`), so quantifying over `a` and
`e` rather than fixing them is what makes `Tr` canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_higherTraceExtension_relativeDifferentials {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (q : X ⟶ S)
    (f : Y ⟶ X)
    {p t : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime)
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    [IsNormal X] [IsFinite f] [IsDominant f]
    [(Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentials q).IsCoherent]
    [CharP (ToType (S.presheaf.stalk (q.base (genericPoint X)))) p] :
    letI : Algebra (ToType (S.presheaf.stalk (q.base (genericPoint X)))) ↑X.functionField :=
      algebraStalkMap q (genericPoint X)
    letI : Algebra ↑X.functionField ↑Y.functionField := (functionFieldMap f).toAlgebra
    letI := genericBaseFunctionFieldAlgebra q f
    haveI := isScalarTower_genericBaseFunctionField q f
    ∀ (a : ↑X.functionField)
      (e : AdjoinRoot (Polynomial.X ^ p - Polynomial.C a) ≃ₐ[↑X.functionField]
        ↑Y.functionField),
      ∃! Tr : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
            (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms (f ≫ q) ((t + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) ⟶
          reflexiveHull (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms q ((t + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)),
        ∀ ω, ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab (genericPoint X)).map
              (Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf (X := X) Tr))
                (genericPushforwardFormsEquiv q f (t + 1) ω) =
            ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab (genericPoint X)).map
              (Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf (X := X)
                (toReflexiveHull (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms q
                  ((t + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ))).1))
              (genericFormsStalkEquiv q (t + 1)
                (KaehlerDifferential.higherTrace hp a e ω))
declarations.comment: the existence and uniqueness of the canonical trace map `f_*Ω^i_{Y/S} ⟶ (Ω^i_{X/S})^∨∨` whose stalk at the generic point is the trace map of [Stacks, Tag 0AX5], through the constructed identifications of both generic stalks

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AX8.** The standing data for the vanishing results: a
two-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain, a modification of its spectrum, and an
enumeration of the irreducible components of the special fibre.
declarations.statement: structure VanishingSituation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.exists_ne_zero_mem_maximalIdeal_factorization
declarations.doc:
A nonzero element of the maximal ideal which, along every irreducible component of the special
fibre, admits at some closed point of that component and of no other a factorization one factor of
which lies in the local maximal ideal and restricts to a nonzero function on the component.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ne_zero_mem_maximalIdeal_factorization
    (V : VanishingSituation.{u})
    (hdim : ∀ i : Fin V.numberOfComponents, topologicalKrullDim (V.component i) = 1) :
    ∃ a : V.A, a ≠ 0 ∧ a ∈ V.maximalIdeal ∧
      ∀ i : Fin V.numberOfComponents,
        ∃ y : componentScheme V i,
          IsClosed
              ({(Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
                (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι y} : Set V.X) ∧
          (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
              (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι y ∈ componentInSource V i ∧
          (∀ j : Fin V.numberOfComponents, j ≠ i →
            (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
                (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι y ∉ componentInSource V j) ∧
          ∃ g h : V.X.presheaf.stalk
              ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
                (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι y),
            g ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal _ ∧
            (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
                (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι.stalkMap y g ≠ 0 ∧
            ((StructureSheaf.toStalk V.A (V.f _) ≫ V.f.stalkMap _) a = g * h)
declarations.comment:
under the standing observation following Situation 0AX8 that every irreducible
component of the special fibre has dimension one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.exists_ne_zero_mem_maximalIdeal_factorization_of_le_topologicalKrullDim_specialFiber
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AX9.** A nonzero element of the maximal ideal which, along every
irreducible component of the special fibre, admits at some closed point of that component and of
no other a factorization one factor of which lies in the local maximal ideal and restricts to a
nonzero function on the component.

`hfib` is the standing exclusion of Section 54.7 (Situation 0AX8), transcribed. The section states
it in these words:

> If $X_s$ has dimension $0$, then $f$ is finite and hence an isomorphism. We will discard this
> uninteresting case.

So `hfib : 1 ≤ topologicalKrullDim V.specialFiber` is that sentence, and every later lemma of the
section is read under it. It appears as a binder here only because
`AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation` transcribes Situation 0AX8 itself, which states the
situation without the section's subsequent exclusion.

Nothing else is carried. The source passes that exclusion from the fibre to each of its
components through the geometric connectedness of `X_s`, which it has from the Stein
factorization — More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.6, [Stacks, Tag 0AY8], whose second conclusion is
not available unconditionally in this library (see
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/MoreMorphisms/SteinFactorization/NormalBase.lean`, where the
first conclusion `f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_S` is tagged and the second is given only over [Stacks, Tag 0G7X]).
That input is not needed: a zero-dimensional component is a point lying on no other component,
hence open in the special fibre and so a quasi-finite point of `f`, and a modification of the
spectrum of a normal local domain with such a point in its closed fibre is an isomorphism
(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsModification.isIso_of_isOpen_singleton_fiber`), whence the special fibre is
a single point of dimension zero, which `hfib` forbids. So `hfib` alone gives the observation
following Situation 54.7.1, that every component has dimension one, as
`AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.topologicalKrullDim_component_eq_one`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_ne_zero_mem_maximalIdeal_factorization_of_le_topologicalKrullDim_specialFiber
    (V : VanishingSituation.{u})
    (hfib : 1 ≤ topologicalKrullDim V.specialFiber) :
    ∃ a : V.A, a ≠ 0 ∧ a ∈ V.maximalIdeal ∧
      ∀ i : Fin V.numberOfComponents,
        ∃ y : componentScheme V i,
          IsClosed
              ({(Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
                (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι y} : Set V.X) ∧
          (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
              (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι y ∈ componentInSource V i ∧
          (∀ j : Fin V.numberOfComponents, j ≠ i →
            (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
                (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι y ∉ componentInSource V j) ∧
          ∃ g h : V.X.presheaf.stalk
              ((Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
                (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι y),
            g ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal _ ∧
            (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal
                (componentClosed V i)).subschemeι.stalkMap y g ≠ 0 ∧
            ((StructureSheaf.toStalk V.A (V.f _) ≫ V.f.stalkMap _) a = g * h)
declarations.comment: the lemma under the standing exclusion of Section 54.7 (Situation 0AX8): the case dim X_s = 0, discarded by the source, which notes there that f is then finite and hence an isomorphism. The geometric connectedness of the special fibre that the source reads off the Stein factorization is proved here where it is used: a zero-dimensional component is a point open in the special fibre, so Zariski's main theorem over the local base makes the modification an isomorphism and the special fibre a single point, which the exclusion rules out

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.exists_subset_invertibleCurveDegree_conormalOnComponent_pos
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0AX8] let `X` be normal and let `Z ⊆ X` be a nonempty effective
Cartier divisor contained set theoretically in the special fibre. Then there is a component `C_i`
of the special fibre with `C_i ⊆ Z` and `deg(𝒞_{Z/X}|_{C_i}) > 0`.

The proof is the source's. Let `a ∈ 𝔪` be the function of [Stacks, Tag 0AX9], with its points
`x_i ∈ C_i` and factorizations `a = g_i h_i` in `𝒪_{X, x_i}`. The local rings `𝒪_{X, ξ_i}` at the
generic points are discrete valuation rings; let `e_i` be the valuation of `a` and `d_i` that of
a local equation of `Z`, and pick `i` with `d_i / e_i` maximal (so `d_i > 0` and `C_i ⊆ Z`).
Then `a^{d_i}` vanishes at the generic points of `e_i Z`, all of which are generic points of
components of the special fibre, so it is a global section of `ℐ_{e_i Z}` because `e_i Z` is
`(S_1)` ([Stacks, Tags 0B3S, 0346, 0B3M]). Its restriction to `C_i` is nonzero, since `a^{d_i}`
generates `ℐ_{e_i Z}` at `ξ_i`, and vanishes at `x_i` by Krull's principal ideal theorem applied
to `g_i`; so `deg(𝒞_{e_i Z/X}|_{C_i}) > 0` by part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0B40], and this degree is
`e_i · deg(𝒞_{Z/X}|_{C_i})` ([Stacks, Tags 02OP, 0B3P, 0AYX]).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_subset_invertibleCurveDegree_conormalOnComponent_pos [IsNormal V.X]
    (I : V.X.IdealSheafData) [hI : Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I]
    (hne : I.supportSet.Nonempty)
    (hZs : I.supportSet ⊆ Set.range (V.f.fiberι V.closedPoint)) :
    ∃ i : Fin V.numberOfComponents, componentInSource V i ⊆ I.supportSet ∧
      0 < invertibleCurveDegree (V.base.residueField V.closedPoint)
        (componentToSpecResidueField V i)
        (topologicalKrullDim_componentScheme_le_one_of_isNormal V i)
        (conormalOnComponent V I i)
declarations.comment: the precise clause: in Situation 0AX8 with X normal, for a nonempty effective Cartier divisor Z of X contained set theoretically in the special fibre, there is a component C_i of the special fibre with C_i contained in Z and deg(C_{Z/X}|_{C_i}) > 0; the dimension-one observation following Situation 0AX8, the section built from Lemma 0AX9 and part (2) of Tag 0B40 are all proved in the library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.not_isTrivial_conormalSheaf_of_nonempty
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0AX8] with `X` normal, the conormal sheaf of a nonempty effective
Cartier divisor `Z ⊆ X` contained set theoretically in the special fibre is not trivial. If it
were, its restriction to the component `C_i ⊆ Z` provided by
`exists_subset_invertibleCurveDegree_conormalOnComponent_pos` would be isomorphic to `𝒪_{C_i}`
and so would have degree zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_isTrivial_conormalSheaf_of_nonempty [IsNormal V.X] (I : V.X.IdealSheafData)
    [Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I] (hne : I.supportSet.Nonempty)
    (hZs : I.supportSet ⊆ Set.range (V.f.fiberι V.closedPoint)) :
    ¬ SheafOfModules.IsTrivial I.subscheme.presheaf I.subscheme.ringCatSheaf.2
      (Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf I.subschemeι)
declarations.comment: the first clause: in Situation 0AX8 with X normal, the conormal sheaf of a nonempty effective Cartier divisor Z of X contained set theoretically in the special fibre is not trivial, derived from the precise clause since a trivial conormal sheaf restricts to a sheaf of degree zero on C_i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.firstCohomologyRestriction_injective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AXB].** In Situation 0AX8 with `X` normal, the restriction map
`H¹(X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ H¹(f⁻¹(U), 𝒪_X)` on the first cohomology of the structure sheaf is injective.

The source assumes `A` Nagata as well; the argument below does not use it. A class in the
kernel is represented, through an injective resolution `I` of `𝒪_X`, by a cocycle `c ∈ Γ(X, I¹)`
which has primitives on `f⁻¹(U)` and on the members of an open cover of `X` (locality of
cohomology, [Stacks, Tag 01E3]); `exists_d_eq_of_local_primitives` glues them, using the polar
lemma in place of the projective-bundle construction of the source's proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstCohomologyRestriction_injective [IsNormal V.X] :
    Function.Injective V.firstCohomologyRestriction
declarations.comment: in Situation 0AX8 with X normal, the restriction map H^1(X, O_X) -> H^1(f^{-1}(U), O_X) is injective; the source's Nagata hypothesis on A is not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.hom_residueFieldShift_derivedPushforwardStructureSheaf_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0AX8] with `X` normal, the group
`Hom_{D(A)}(κ[-1], Rf_*𝒪_X)` is zero: every morphism from `κ[-1]` to the derived direct image of
the structure sheaf, read in `D(A)` through the affine identification `D(A) = D_QCoh(𝒪_S)` of
[Stacks, Tag 06Z0], vanishes.

Leray over the base ring identifies that object with `RΓ(X, 𝒪_X)`, so this is
`hom_residueFieldShift_derivedGlobalSections_eq_zero` transported along
`derivedGlobalSectionsStructureSheafIsoPushforward`. The source also assumes `A` Nagata; that
hypothesis is not needed, since it enters the source's proof only through
[Stacks, Tag 0AXB].
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_residueFieldShift_derivedPushforwardStructureSheaf_eq_zero [IsNormal V.X]
    (α : V.residueFieldShift ⟶ V.derivedPushforwardStructureSheaf) : α = 0
declarations.comment: the vanishing of Hom_{D(A)}(kappa[-1], Rf_*O_X) with Rf_*O_X the ACTUAL derived direct image: the restricted unbounded derived direct image quasiCoherentDerivedPushforward applied to the structure sheaf of X in degree zero, an object of D_QCoh(O_S), carried into D(A) by the inverse of the derived sheafification equivalence of Tag 06Z0 (DualizingDivisor.tildeEquivalence, the affine identification D(A) = D_QCoh(O_S) that the tag invokes). The vanishing is the base carrier hom_residueFieldShift_derivedGlobalSections_eq_zero transported along Leray over the base ring (Tag 0D5W, DualizingDivisor.lerayIso), which identifies that object with the A-linear derived global sections RGamma(X, O_X). Stated for X normal without the Nagata hypothesis on A, which enters the source's proof only through Tag 0AXB and is not needed on the route taken here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.hom_residueFieldShift_derivedGlobalSections_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AXC.** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 0AX8] with `X` normal, every
morphism `κ[-1] ⟶ RΓ(X, 𝒪_X)` in `D(A)` is zero; that is, the group `Hom_{D(A)}(κ[-1], Rf_*𝒪_X)`
vanishes, the pushforward being read as the derived global sections `RΓ(X, 𝒪_X)`, which
`isDerivedPushforwardStructureSheaf_derivedGlobalSectionsStructureSheaf` identifies with
`Rf_*𝒪_X` by its cohomology. The source also assumes `A` Nagata; that is not needed here.

For a nonzero `a ∈ 𝔪` the triangle of `0 → 𝒪_X → 𝒪_X → 𝒪_X/a𝒪_X → 0` has `a • 𝟙` as its first
morphism, so `α` factors through `RΓ(X, 𝒪_X/a𝒪_X)`. In degree zero the factorisation is a global
section of `𝒪_X/a𝒪_X` annihilated by `𝔪`. Such a section dies over the punctured spectrum, so it
is zero by `eq_zero_of_res_preimagePuncturedSpectrum_eq_zero`, and in particular it is the image
of a global function of `X`. Two consecutive morphisms of the triangle then kill the restriction
of `α` along `A[-1] ⟶ κ[-1]`, and `Hom_A(𝔪, A) = A` kills `α`.

The source reaches the same lift through [Stacks, Tag 0AXB], whose proof needs the Nagata
condition to make a normalization finite. Here it comes from the vanishing of sections of
`𝒪_X/a𝒪_X` supported in the special fibre, which is proved directly by Lipman's argument from
[Stacks, Tag 0AX9], algebraic Hartogs and the fact that a proper integral curve has no nonconstant
functions.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_residueFieldShift_derivedGlobalSections_eq_zero (V : VanishingSituation.{u})
    [IsNormal V.X]
    (α : V.residueFieldShift ⟶ derivedGlobalSectionsStructureSheaf V.f) : α = 0
declarations.comment: the vanishing of Hom_{D(A)}(kappa[-1], Rf_*O_X), the pushforward being the derived global sections RGamma(X, O_X), which isDerivedPushforwardStructureSheaf_derivedGlobalSectionsStructureSheaf identifies with Rf_*O_X by its cohomology H^n(X, O_X); stated for X normal without the Nagata hypothesis on A, which is not needed. For a nonzero a in the maximal ideal the triangle of 0 -> O_X -> O_X -> O_X/aO_X -> 0 has first morphism a times the identity, so a morphism out of kappa[-1] factors through RGamma(X, O_X/aO_X); in degree zero that is a global section of O_X/aO_X annihilated by the maximal ideal, hence supported in the special fibre, hence zero by eq_zero_of_res_preimagePuncturedSpectrum_eq_zero (Lipman's argument from Tag 0AX9, used in place of Tag 0AXB), and Hom_A(m, A) = A over a Noetherian normal local domain of dimension at least two kills the morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.isZero_firstCohomology_of_properRightAdjoint_isoShiftTwo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AXD** (Grauert-Riemenschneider), for every normalized `ω_A^•` and
every `ω_X` normalized with respect to it. Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a two-dimensional Noetherian
normal local domain, `f : X ⟶ S = Spec(A)` a modification with `X` normal, and suppose `A` is
Nagata. Let `ω_A^•` be a normalized dualizing complex over `A`, and let `ω_X` be an
`𝒪_X`-module with `f^×(ω̃_A^•) ≅ ω_X[2]` — the dualizing module of [Stacks, Remark 0B4R],
normalized with respect to `ω_A^•`. Then `H¹(X, ω_X) = 0`, which over the affine base `S` is
`R¹f_*ω_X = 0`.

The source's hypothesis that `A` has a dualizing complex is carried by `ω_A^•` itself, which the
source may and does take normalized ([Stacks, Tag 0A7M]). That `ω_X` is coherent and a dualizing
module is not assumed: the isomorphism `f^×(ω̃_A^•) ≅ ω_X[2]` determines `ω_X` up to isomorphism,
and `AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.exists_isDualizingModule_properRightAdjoint_isoShiftTwo`
supplies a coherent such module, which is a dualizing module because `f^×` preserves dualizing
complexes ([Stacks, Tag 0AA3]).

The vanishing for that module is the source's argument,
`AlgebraicGeometry.VanishingSituation.isZero_firstCohomology_dualizingModule_of_isTildeDualizing`;
it passes to `ω_X` along the isomorphism `ω_X ≅ H⁰(ω_X[2][-2])` of the two modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_firstCohomology_of_properRightAdjoint_isoShiftTwo (V : VanishingSituation.{u})
    [IsNormal V.X]
    (hnag : IsNagataRing V.A)
    (ωA : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} V.A))
    (hωA : Dualizing.IsNormalizedDualizingComplex.{u, u} ωA) (ωX : V.X.Modules) :
    letI : IsProper V.f := V.modification.isProper
    letI : CompactSpace V.X := QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace V.f
    letI : QuasiSeparatedSpace V.X := quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated V.f
    Nonempty (((properRightAdjoint V.f).obj
          ((derivedTilde (CommRingCat.of V.A)).obj ωA)).obj ≅
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor V.X.Modules 0).obj ωX)⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) →
      IsZero (firstCohomologySheafAsBaseModule V.X V.f ωX)
declarations.comment: the conclusion R^1 f_* omega_X = 0 read over the affine base S = Spec(A) as the vanishing of H^1(X, omega_X) as an A-module, for every normalized dualizing complex omega_A^bullet over A and every O_X-module omega_X with f^times(omega_A^bullet-tilde) = omega_X[2], which is the dualizing module of Remark 0B4R normalized with respect to omega_A^bullet; the hypotheses are the Proposition's own: the Situation of Tag 0AX8, X normal, A Nagata, and the dualizing complex omega_A^bullet, taken normalized as the source does (Tag 0A7M). The source's proof is carried out in full: omega_X^bullet = omega_X[2] (Tags 0B3D, 0AWT, 0AWI), a nonzero R^1 f_* omega_X -> kappa gives a nonzero alpha : Rf_* omega_X^bullet -> kappa[1], and RHom_A(-, omega_A^bullet) carries it to a nonzero beta : kappa[-1] -> Rf_* O_X (Tags 0A7M, 0GEW, 0AA3), contradicting Tag 0AXC

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.firstStructureSheafCohomologyVanishes_of_isModification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AXF, the injectivity in the first conclusion.** For a modification
`q : Z ⟶ Y` of a normal integral scheme `Y`, the vanishing of `H¹(Z, 𝒪_Z)` implies the vanishing
of `H¹(Y, 𝒪_Y)`.

The source states this for modifications of the spectrum of a two-dimensional normal local
domain; neither the dimension nor the locality nor the affineness of the base is used, so it is
proved here for an arbitrary normal integral target. Only the injectivity half of the source's
exact sequence is proved: see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstStructureSheafCohomologyVanishes_of_isModification {Z Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsIntegral Y] [IsNormal Y] {q : Z ⟶ Y} (hq : IsModification q)
    (h : FirstStructureSheafCohomologyVanishes Z) :
    FirstStructureSheafCohomologyVanishes Y
declarations.comment: first conclusion, injectivity only: the map H¹(X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ H¹(X', 𝒪_{X'}) of the source's short exact sequence is injective, so a vanishing H¹ upstairs forces one downstairs. Generalized: the base is an arbitrary normal integral scheme, not the spectrum of a two-dimensional normal local domain. NOT proved, and not asserted by this entry: the surjectivity onto H⁰(X, R¹g_*𝒪_{X'}), which rests on Tag 02V7 in fibre dimension one. The tag's second and third conclusions are carried separately in AlgebraicGeometry.SemistableReduction.TwoModifications

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SemistableReduction.TwoModifications.exists_shortExact_firstCohomology
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AXF], first conclusion.**  There is a short exact sequence

  `0 ⟶ H¹(X, 𝒪_X) ⟶ H¹(X', 𝒪_{X'}) ⟶ H⁰(X, R¹g_*𝒪_{X'}) ⟶ 0`

of modules over `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`: the first map is injective and semilinear along `g^♯`, its image is
the kernel of the second, and the second is surjective and carries the `g^♯`-twisted action to
the action of `Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_firstCohomology :
    ∃ (θ : ((Scheme.sectionsFunctor S.X).rightDerived 1).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit S.X.ringCatSheaf)
          →ₛₗ[SeparableGoUp.sectionsRingHom S.g]
        ((Scheme.sectionsFunctor S.X').rightDerived 1).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit S.X'.ringCatSheaf))
      (ψ : (((Scheme.sectionsFunctor S.X').rightDerived 1).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit S.X'.ringCatSheaf)) →+
        (Scheme.sectionsFunctor S.X).obj (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward S.g).rightDerived 1).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit S.X'.ringCatSheaf))),
      Function.Injective θ ∧
        (∀ (r : Scheme.sectionsRing S.X) y,
          ψ (SeparableGoUp.sectionsRingHom S.g r • y) = r • ψ y) ∧
        (∀ y, ψ y = 0 ↔ ∃ x, θ x = y) ∧
        Function.Surjective ψ
declarations.comment: the short exact sequence 0 → H¹(X, 𝒪_X) → H¹(X', 𝒪_{X'}) → H⁰(X, R¹g_*𝒪_{X'}) → 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SemistableReduction.TwoModifications.topologicalKrullDim_supp_rightDerived_one_pushforward_le_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AXF], second conclusion.**  The support of `R¹g_*𝒪_{X'}` has dimension zero:
it is a finite set of closed points of `X`.  As everywhere in this development the source's
`dim = 0` is read as `≤ 0`, the support being allowed to be empty.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_supp_rightDerived_one_pushforward_le_zero :
    topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp
      (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward S.g).rightDerived 1).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit S.X'.ringCatSheaf))) ≤ 0
declarations.comment: dim(Supp(R¹g_*𝒪_{X'})) = 0, read as dimension at most zero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SemistableReduction.TwoModifications.nonempty_generatingSections_rightDerived_one_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AXF], third conclusion.**  `R¹g_*𝒪_{X'}` is generated by global sections.
Its support is a finite set of closed points, so a germ at any of them extends by zero to a
global section.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_generatingSections_rightDerived_one_pushforward :
    Nonempty ((((Scheme.Modules.pushforward S.g).rightDerived 1).obj
      (SheafOfModules.unit S.X'.ringCatSheaf)).GeneratingSections)
declarations.comment: R¹g_*𝒪_{X'} is generated by global sections

declarations.name: exists_nonzero_mem_isReduced_quotient_of_height_one_primes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AXH.** In a two-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain, finitely many
height-one prime ideals contain a common nonzero element whose principal quotient is reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nonzero_mem_isReduced_quotient_of_height_one_primes
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [IsIntegrallyClosed R] (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 2) (primes : Finset (Ideal R))
    (hprimes : ∀ p ∈ primes, p.IsPrime ∧ p.height = 1) :
    ∃ f : R, f ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ p ∈ primes, f ∈ p) ∧ IsReduced (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})

declarations.name: exists_isReduced_quotient_and_dvd_pow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AXI.** In a two-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain, every nonzero element of
the maximal ideal divides a power of an element whose principal quotient is reduced.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_isReduced_quotient_and_dvd_pow
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [IsIntegrallyClosed R] (hdim : ringKrullDim R = 2) {a : R}
    (_ha : a ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) (ha0 : a ≠ 0) :
    ∃ c : R, IsReduced (R ⧸ Ideal.span {c}) ∧ ∃ n : ℕ, a ∣ c ^ n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_length_quotient_baseToZeroSchemeSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AXJ.** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a local normal Nagata domain of dimension
two and let `a ∈ A` be nonzero. There is an integer `N` such that for every modification
`f : X ⟶ Spec A` with `X` normal the `A`-module

  `M_{X,a} = Coker(A ⟶ H⁰(Z, 𝒪_Z))`,

for `Z ⊂ X` the closed subscheme cut out by `a`, has length at most `N`.

A unit `a` cuts out the empty subscheme, so the cokernel vanishes. Otherwise `a` is replaced by
an element with reduced principal quotient: the cokernel is the `a`-torsion submodule of
`H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`, which is monotone in divisibility and whose length grows at most linearly along
powers, and `a` divides a power of a nonzero `c ∈ 𝔪` with `A ⧸ cA` reduced. For such a `c` the
bound is the length of the cokernel `B / (A ⧸ cA)` of the integral closure `B` of `A ⧸ cA` in
its total ring of fractions, and the hypothesis `hsub` converts a bound on that cokernel into
one on `M_{X,c}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bound_length_quotient_baseToZeroSchemeSections {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNormalDomain A] [IsNagataRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) {a : A}
    (ha : a ≠ 0)
    (hsub : ∀ c : A, c ≠ 0 → c ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A →
        _root_.IsReduced (A ⧸ Ideal.span {c}) → ∀ N : ℕ,
      Module.length (A ⧸ Ideal.span {c}) (normalizationCokernel (A ⧸ Ideal.span {c})) ≤ N →
        ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNormal X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)), IsModification f →
          Module.length A (globalSectionsAsBaseModule X f (zeroSchemeStructureSheaf X f c) ⧸
            LinearMap.range (baseToZeroSchemeSections X f c)) ≤ N) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNormal X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)), IsModification f →
      Module.length A (globalSectionsAsBaseModule X f (zeroSchemeStructureSheaf X f a) ⧸
        LinearMap.range (baseToZeroSchemeSections X f a)) ≤ N
declarations.comment: `hsub` carries the subquotient step: `M_{X,c}` embeds into `B / (A ⧸ cA)` because the closure of `Z ∩ f⁻¹(U)` is a spectrum between them (Stacks 0AB7) and `H⁰(Z, 𝒪_Z)` injects on it (Stacks 0AXB, absent from this library)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_uniform_bound_length_quotient_baseToZeroSchemeSections
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a local normal Nagata domain of dimension two and let `a ∈ A` be nonzero.
There is an integer `N` such that for every modification `f : X ⟶ Spec A` with `X` normal the
`A`-module

  `M_{X,a} = Coker(A ⟶ H⁰(Z, 𝒪_Z))`,

for `Z ⊂ X` the closed subscheme cut out by `a`, has length at most `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_bound_length_quotient_baseToZeroSchemeSections {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNormalDomain A] [IsNagataRing A] (hdim : ringKrullDim A = 2) {a : A}
    (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNormal X] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)), IsModification f →
      Module.length A (globalSectionsAsBaseModule X f (zeroSchemeStructureSheaf X f a) ⧸
        LinearMap.range (baseToZeroSchemeSections X f a)) ≤ N

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_quotient_baseToZeroSchemeSections_equiv_torsionBy
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AXK.** For a nonzero element `a` of a normal domain `A` and a
modification `f : X ⟶ Spec A`, the cokernel of `A ⟶ H⁰(Z, 𝒪_Z)`, for `Z ⊂ X` cut out by `a`, is
the `a`-torsion submodule of `H¹(X, 𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_quotient_baseToZeroSchemeSections_equiv_torsionBy [IsNormalDomain A]
    (hf : IsModification f) {a : A} (ha : a ≠ 0) :
    Nonempty ((globalSectionsAsBaseModule X f (zeroSchemeStructureSheaf X f a) ⧸
        LinearMap.range (baseToZeroSchemeSections X f a)) ≃ₗ[A]
      Submodule.torsionBy A (firstCohomologyAsBaseModule X f) a)

declarations.name: Stacks.ResolutionOfSurfaces.isReductionToRationalSingularitiesPossible_of_finite_of_isSeparable
declarations.doc:
Let `A ⟶ B` be a finite injective local map of local normal
Nagata domains of dimension two, let `K` and `L` be their fraction fields and assume `L/K`
separable. If reduction to rational singularities is possible for `A`, it is possible for `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReductionToRationalSingularitiesPossible_of_finite_of_isSeparable
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNormalDomain A] [IsNagataRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNormalDomain B] [IsNagataRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L]
    [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing B L]
    [Algebra K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L] [IsScalarTower A B L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
    (hdimA : ringKrullDim A = 2) (hdimB : ringKrullDim B = 2)
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B))
    (hA : IsReductionToRationalSingularitiesPossible A) :
    IsReductionToRationalSingularitiesPossible B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SeparableGoUp.isReductionToRationalSingularitiesPossible_of_finite_of_isSeparable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AXL.** Let `A → B` be a finite injective local ring map of local normal
Nagata domains of dimension two such that the induced extension of fraction fields is separable.
If reduction to rational singularities is possible for `A`, then it is possible for `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReductionToRationalSingularitiesPossible_of_finite_of_isSeparable (A B : Type u)
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNormalDomain A] [IsNagataRing A] [CommRing B]
    [IsLocalRing B] [IsNormalDomain B] [IsNagataRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B]
    [FaithfulSMul A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] (_hdimA : ringKrullDim A = 2)
    (hdimB : ringKrullDim B = 2)
    (hsep : letI := FractionRing.liftAlgebra A (FractionRing B)
      Algebra.IsSeparable (FractionRing A) (FractionRing B))
    (hA : IsReductionToRationalSingularitiesPossible A) :
    IsReductionToRationalSingularitiesPossible B

declarations.name: isTorsionFree_baseChange_of_flat
declarations.doc:
If `R` is a domain, `R'` is a flat `R`-algebra and `M` is a torsion-free `R`-module, then the
base change `R' ⊗[R] M` is a torsion-free `R'`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_baseChange_of_flat
    {R R' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    [IsDomain R] [Module.Flat R R']
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.IsTorsionFree R M] :
    Module.IsTorsionFree R' (TensorProduct R R' M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_genericPoint_irreducibleComponent_mapping_to
declarations.doc:
Every generic point of an irreducible component of the relative normalization of the target
in the source is the image of a generic point of an irreducible component of the source.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_genericPoint_irreducibleComponent_mapping_to
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    {x : f.normalization} {Z : Set f.normalization}
    (hZ : Z ∈ irreducibleComponents f.normalization) (hx : IsGenericPoint x Z) :
    ∃ (y : Y) (T : Set Y),
      T ∈ irreducibleComponents Y ∧ IsGenericPoint y T ∧ f.toNormalization y = x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sheafHasPropertySk_one_internalHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AXQ], part (1).** On a locally Noetherian scheme the internal hom of
coherent modules into a module satisfying Serre's condition `(S₁)` satisfies `(S₁)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sheafHasPropertySk_one_internalHom [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F G : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G]
    (H : SheafHom X.sheaf F G) (hG : SheafHasPropertySk X G 1) :
    SheafHasPropertySk X (internalHomOf H) 1
declarations.comment: hom_into_s1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sheafHasPropertySk_two_internalHom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AXQ], part (2).** On a locally Noetherian scheme the internal hom of
coherent modules into a module satisfying Serre's condition `(S₂)` satisfies `(S₂)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sheafHasPropertySk_two_internalHom [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F G : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G]
    (H : SheafHom X.sheaf F G) (hG : SheafHasPropertySk X G 2) :
    SheafHasPropertySk X (internalHomOf H) 2
declarations.comment: hom_into_s2

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.torsion_section_tfae
declarations.doc:
A section of a quasi-coherent module on an integral scheme is torsion at some stalk if
and only if it is torsion at every stalk; equivalently, its germ at the generic point and
its image in the pushforward from the generic point vanish.
declarations.statement:
theorem torsion_section_tfae
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (U : X.Opens) [Nonempty U] (s : Γ(F, U)) :
    let η := genericPoint X
    let hη : η ∈ U :=
      ((genericPoint_spec X).mem_open_set_iff U.isOpen).mpr
        (by simpa using (inferInstance : Nonempty U))
    letI : ∀ V : X.Opens, Decidable (η ∈ V) := fun V ↦ Classical.propDecidable _
    let isTorsionAt (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U) : Prop :=
      letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x) ↑(F.presheaf.stalk x) :=
        PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
          (R := X.presheaf) F.val x
      IsTorsionElement (R := X.presheaf.stalk x)
        (M := ↑(F.presheaf.stalk x)) (F.presheaf.germ U x hx s)
    List.TFAE [
      ∃ (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U), isTorsionAt x hx,
      ∀ (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U), isTorsionAt x hx,
      F.presheaf.germ U η hη s = 0,
      ((skyscraperPresheafStalkAdjunction (C := AddCommGrpCat.{u}) η).unit.app
        F.presheaf).app (op U) s = 0]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTorsionFree_iff_forall_isAffineOpen
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module on an integral scheme is torsion free if and only if its
sections on every affine open are torsion free over the ring of functions there.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_iff_forall_isAffineOpen
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsTorsionFree F ↔
      ∀ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → Module.IsTorsionFree Γ(X, U) Γ(F, U)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TorsionQuasicoherent.torsionSubmodule_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The first assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0AXT].** The torsion submodule sheaf of a
quasi-coherent module on an integral scheme is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
instance torsionSubmodule_isQuasicoherent :
    (torsionSubmodule F).toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: torsion_subsheaf_quasi_coherent

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TorsionQuasicoherent.isTorsionFree_torsionQuotient
declarations.doc:
**The second assertion of [Stacks, Tag 0AXT].** The quotient of a quasi-coherent module on
an integral scheme by its torsion subsheaf is torsion free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_torsionQuotient :
    ReflexiveModules.IsTorsionFree (torsionQuotient F)
declarations.comment: the quotient F/F_tors is torsion free

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTorsionFree_of_isFlat
declarations.doc: A flat quasi-coherent module on an integral scheme is torsion free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_of_isFlat {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (hF : SheafOfModules.IsFlat.{u, u, u, u} (O := X.sheaf) F) :
    IsTorsionFree F

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.isTorsionFree_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AXV.** The flat pullback of a torsion-free quasi-coherent module on an
integral scheme is torsion free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_modulePullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f]
    (G : Y.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] (hG : IsTorsionFree G) :
    letI : ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G).IsQuasicoherent :=
      @AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.modulePullback_isQuasicoherent X.toRingedSpace
        Y.toRingedSpace f.toLRSHom.toShHom G ‹G.IsQuasicoherent›
    IsTorsionFree ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTorsionFree_iff_forall_stalk
declarations.doc:
A quasi-coherent module on an integral scheme is torsion free precisely when its
stalk at every point is torsion free over the local ring at that point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_iff_forall_stalk
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    IsTorsionFree F ↔
      ∀ x : X,
        letI : Module (X.presheaf.stalk x) ↑(F.presheaf.stalk x) :=
          PresheafOfModules.instModuleCarrierStalkCommRingCatCarrierAbPresheafOpensCarrier
            (R := X.presheaf) F.val x
        Module.IsTorsionFree (X.presheaf.stalk x) ↑(F.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTorsionFree_middle_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
A short exact extension of torsion-free quasi-coherent modules on an integral
scheme is torsion free.
declarations.statement:
lemma isTorsionFree_middle_of_shortExact {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    (S : ShortComplex X.Modules) (hS : S.ShortExact)
    [S.X₁.IsQuasicoherent] [S.X₂.IsQuasicoherent] [S.X₃.IsQuasicoherent]
    (h₁ : IsTorsionFree S.X₁)
