    (h₃ : IsTorsionFree S.X₃) :
    IsTorsionFree S.X₂

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.isTorsionFree_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AXY.** The characterizations of a nonzero torsion-free coherent
module on a locally Noetherian integral scheme: torsion freeness, uniqueness of the generic
point as associated point, Serre's condition `(S₁)` with support at the generic point, and
absence of embedded associated points with support at the generic point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_tfae
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (hF : (SheafOfModules.supp F).Nonempty) :
    letI : F.IsQuasicoherent := isQuasicoherent_of_isCoherent F
    List.TFAE [
      IsTorsionFree F,
      Stacks.Divisors.associatedPoints F = {genericPoint X},
      genericPoint X ∈ SheafOfModules.supp F ∧ AlgebraicGeometry.SheafHasPropertySk X F 1,
      genericPoint X ∈ SheafOfModules.supp F ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.HasNoEmbeddedAssociatedPoints F]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isTorsionFree_sheafHom
declarations.doc:
**The torsion freeness clause of [Stacks, Tag 0AXZ].** On an integral scheme, the sheaf-hom
`SheafHom(F, G)` from a module of finite presentation into a quasi-coherent torsion free module
is torsion free.

The proof is the one of the source: torsion freeness of a quasi-coherent module on an integral
scheme is a condition on the stalks, the stalk of `SheafHom(F, G)` at `x` is
`Hom_{𝒪_{X,x}}(F_x, G_x)` by [Stacks, Tag 01CP], and a module of linear maps into a torsion free
module is torsion free.
declarations.statement:
theorem isTorsionFree_sheafHom {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] (F G : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] [G.IsQuasicoherent] (hG : IsTorsionFree G) :
    IsTorsionFree (sheafInternalHom (spaceRingedSite X.sheaf) F G)
declarations.comment: torsion freeness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sheafHom_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The quasi-coherence clause of [Stacks, Tag 0AXZ].** On a scheme, the sheaf-hom
`SheafHom(F, G)` from a module of finite presentation into a quasi-coherent module is
quasi-coherent.

This is the assertion of Schemes, [Stacks, Tag 01LA] which makes the statement of Tag 0AXZ
meaningful: torsion freeness is a notion for quasi-coherent modules. It is deduced from the
first clause of [Stacks, Tag 01CQ],
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.InternalHom.exists_locally_isoKernel_sheafInternalHom`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHom_isQuasicoherent (F G : X.Modules)
    [F.IsFinitePresentation] [G.IsQuasicoherent] :
    SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent (R := X.ringCatSheaf)
      (sheafInternalHom (spaceRingedSite X.sheaf) F G)
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReflexive_iff_sections_isReflexive
declarations.doc:
A coherent module on an integral locally Noetherian scheme is reflexive if and only if its
module of sections over every affine open is reflexive.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_iff_sections_isReflexive (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] :
    IsReflexive F ↔ ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → Module.IsReflexive Γ(X, U) Γ(F, U)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.isTorsionFree_of_isReflexive
declarations.doc: A reflexive module on an integral scheme is torsion free.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isTorsionFree_of_isReflexive [IsIntegral X] (F : X.Modules)
    (hF : IsReflexive F) : IsTorsionFree F
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.mono_toDoubleDual_iff_isTorsionFree
declarations.doc:
On an integral scheme, the canonical map of a coherent module to its double dual is a
monomorphism if and only if the module is torsion free.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mono_toDoubleDual_iff_isTorsionFree [IsIntegral X] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent] : Mono (toDoubleDual F) ↔ IsTorsionFree F
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ReflexiveModules.isReflexive_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AY3.**  For a coherent module `F` on a locally Noetherian scheme
`X`, the following are equivalent:

1. `F` is reflexive, that is, the canonical map `F ⟶ F^∨∨` is an isomorphism;
2. for every point `x` of `X` the stalk `F_x` is a reflexive `𝒪_{X,x}`-module;
3. the same for every *closed* point `x` of `X`.

Integrality of `X` is not needed: reflexivity of a module of finite presentation is detected on
stalks over an arbitrary commutative local ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isReflexive_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent] :
    [IsReflexive F,
      ∀ x : X, Module.IsReflexive (ringStalk X.sheaf x) (modStalk F x),
      ∀ x : X, x ∈ closedPoints X →
        Module.IsReflexive (ringStalk X.sheaf x) (modStalk F x)].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.sheafHom_isReflexive
declarations.doc:
On an integral locally Noetherian scheme, the internal Hom `SheafHom(ℱ, 𝒢)` of coherent modules
is reflexive as soon as `𝒢` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHom_isReflexive (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (F G : X.Modules) [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G]
    (hG : IsReflexive G) :
    IsReflexive (sheafInternalHom (spaceRingedSite X.sheaf) F G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReflexive_iff_stalk_isReflexive_or_depth_two
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AY5.** A coherent module on an integral locally Noetherian scheme is
reflexive if and only if at every point its stalk is either a reflexive module over the local
ring there or has depth at least two.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_iff_stalk_isReflexive_or_depth_two (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] :
    IsReflexive F ↔
      ∀ x : X, Module.IsReflexive (X.presheaf.stalk x) (F.presheaf.stalk x) ∨
        (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ Module.depth (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (F.presheaf.stalk x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isReflexive_isTorsionFree_propertyS2_extension_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme and let `F` be a coherent
`𝒪_X`-module. The following are equivalent:

1. `F` is reflexive;
2. `F` is torsion free and satisfies Serre's condition `(S₂)`;
3. there is an open subscheme `j : U → X` whose complement has codimension at least two at
   every point, such that `j^*F` is finite locally free and the canonical map `F → j_*j^*F` is
   an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isReflexive_isTorsionFree_propertyS2_extension_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X] (F : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsReflexive F,
      IsTorsionFree F ∧ SheafHasPropertySk X F 2,
      ∃ U : X.Opens,
        (∀ x : X, x ∉ U →
          (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ codimension (IrreducibleCloseds.closureSingleton x)) ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree (F.restrict U.ι) ∧
        IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction U.ι).unit.app F)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_lift_toReflexiveHull_iff_codimension_one
declarations.doc:
On an integral locally Noetherian normal scheme, a linear map of generic stalks extends to a
map into the reflexive hull of its target if and only if, at every point whose local ring has
dimension one, it carries the image of the source stalk into the image of the target stalk.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_lift_toReflexiveHull_iff_codimension_one (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsNormal X] (F G : X.Modules)
    [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F] [_root_.SheafOfModules.IsCoherent G]
    (T : (G.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X)) →ₗ[X.functionField]
      (F.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X))) :
    (∃ e : G ⟶ reflexiveHull F,
      ∀ m : G.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X),
        ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab (genericPoint X)).map
          (Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf (X := X) e)) m =
          ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor Ab (genericPoint X)).map
            (Scheme.Modules.Hom.mapPresheaf (X := X)
              (toReflexiveHull F).1)) (T m)) ↔
      ∀ x : X, ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1 →
        let h : genericPoint X ⤳ x := (genericPoint_spec X).specializes trivial
        Set.MapsTo T (Set.range (G.presheaf.stalkSpecializes h))
          (Set.range (F.presheaf.stalkSpecializes h))

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIso_c_of_isNormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AY8, first conclusion.**  Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a proper morphism from a
reduced scheme onto a normal integral scheme with generic point `ξ`.  If every generic point of
an irreducible component of `X` maps to `ξ` and `H⁰(X_ξ, 𝒪) = κ(ξ)`, then `f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_S`.

The second factor of the Stein factorization is an isomorphism, and the first already satisfies
`f'_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_{S'}` by clause (3) of [Stacks, Tag 03H2].
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_c_of_isNormal (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [IsIntegral S]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNormal S] [IsReduced X]
    (hgen : ∀ x : X, x ∈ genericPoints X → f x = genericPoint S)
    (hΓ : IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (S.residueField (genericPoint S))).inv ≫
      (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (genericPoint S)).appTop)) :
    IsIso f.c
declarations.comment: pushforward of the structure sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.SteinFactorization.geometricallyConnected_of_isNormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AY8, the second conclusion.**  Under the hypotheses of Tag 0AY8 — `f`
proper, `S` integral and normal, `X` reduced, every generic point of `X` over the generic point
`ξ` of `S`, and `H⁰(X_ξ, 𝒪) = κ(ξ)` — the morphism `f` has geometrically connected fibres.

The proof follows the source: the second factor `π : S' ⟶ S` of the Stein factorization is an
isomorphism
(`Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIso_fromNormalization_of_isNormal`), so the fibres of `f` are those
of the first factor, and their geometric connectedness is clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 03H2],
`Stacks.SteinFactorization.geometricallyConnected_toNormalization_of_isProper`.

The first conclusion, `f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_S`, is `Stacks.SteinFactorization.isIso_c_of_isNormal`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyConnected_of_isNormal
    (f : X ⟶ S) [IsProper f] [IsIntegral S] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNormal S] [IsReduced X]
    (hgen : ∀ x : X, x ∈ genericPoints X → f x = genericPoint S)
    (hΓ : IsIso ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (S.residueField (genericPoint S))).inv ≫
      (f.fiberToSpecResidueField (genericPoint S)).appTop)) :
    GeometricallyConnected f
declarations.comment: the second conclusion, that f has geometrically connected fibres.  The first conclusion, f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_S, is isIso_c_of_isNormal

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.moduleSymbol_self_eq_negOne_pow_length
declarations.doc: The symbol of a nonzerodivisor `a` with itself is `(-1) ^ length (M / aM)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleSymbol_self_eq_negOne_pow_length
    {A : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    (a : A) (ha : IsSMulRegular M a)
    (hdim : Module.supportDim A M = 1) :
    moduleSymbol a a ha ha hdim =
      (-1 : (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)ˣ) ^
        moduleLength A (M ⧸ (LinearMap.lsmul A M a).range)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.KeyFormulaSituation
declarations.doc:
**The situation preceding the key formula, Stacks 0AYB.** On an integral, locally Noetherian
scheme `X`, two invertible `𝒪_X`-modules `L` and `N` with nonzero meromorphic sections `s` and
`t`, together with a locally finite family `{Z_i}` of prime divisors of `X` large enough that
`s` generates `L` and `t` generates `N` at the generic point of every prime divisor outside the
family, and, for each `i`, chosen generators `s_i` of `L_{ξ_i}` and `t_i` of `N_{ξ_i}` at the
generic point `ξ_i` of `Z_i`.

The ratios `f_i = s / s_i` and `g_i = t / t_i`, the orders of vanishing, the restrictions
`s_i|_{Z_i}` and `t_i|_{Z_i}` and the tame symbols `∂_{B_i}(f_i, g_i)` are determined by these
data, and are constructed from them below.

A meromorphic section is given by its value in the generic stalk, and is nonzero exactly when
that value is; see the module documentation.
declarations.comment: the situation preceding the key formula: two invertible modules with nonzero meromorphic sections, and a family of prime divisors with chosen local generators

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.KeyFormulaData.keyFormula_iff_forall_component_coheight_one
declarations.doc:
**The key formula is local at the codimension-one points of the family.** It holds if and
only if its two coefficients agree at the image of every codimension-one point of every member
`Z_i`.

This is the step of the source's proof that says "since we are proving the equality of cycles we
may argue one coefficient at a time", and it is only that step. At such a point `x` the local
ring `𝒪_{X, x}` has dimension two, only the finitely many members of the family through `x`
contribute to either side, and the source derives the resulting identity of coefficients from the
Key Lemma Stacks 0EAX on `𝒪_{X, x}`. That derivation is not carried out here: the identity of
coefficients stands on the right hand side of the equivalence, so this declaration proves the
equivalence and not the key formula.

Stacks 0EAX itself is proved, as
`Stacks.Chow.finsum_fracTameSymbolOrderAt_canonical_eq_zero`. The step from it to the identity of
coefficients goes through the dictionary between `X` and `A = 𝒪_{X, x}` described in the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem keyFormula_iff_forall_component_coheight_one [LocallyOfFiniteType p] :
    D.KeyFormula C p ↔ ∀ (i : D.Index) (z : (D.component i).subscheme), Order.coheight z = 1 →
      D.leftCoeff C p ((D.component i).subschemeι.base z) =
        D.tameSymbolCoeff C p ((D.component i).subschemeι.base z)
declarations.comment: the localization step of the source's proof: the equality of the two cycles is equivalent to the equality of their coefficients at the codimension-two points of the family

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.KeyFormulaSituation.keyFormula_toKeyFormulaData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYC for the situation of Stacks 0AYB.** The key formula holds for the cycle-level
data of the sheaf-level situation: the difference of the two Chern-class cycles is the locally
finite sum of the principal divisors of the tame symbols `∂_{B_i}(f_i, g_i)` on the members of the
family.

At a codimension-two point `x` of a member of the family the two coefficients are compared by the
local reciprocity law Stacks 0EAX on `A = 𝒪_{X, x}`, read at the pair of coordinates of `s` and
`t` taken from trivializations of `L` and `N` near `x`: that sum vanishes, the members of the
family carry all of it, and the difference between its summands and the summands of the right
hand side of the key formula is the change-of-generator correction of Stacks 0EAN and Stacks
02SH, which is the left hand side. See the module documentation.
declarations.statement: theorem keyFormula_toKeyFormulaData : (ℱ.toKeyFormulaData C p).KeyFormula C p
declarations.comment: the key formula itself, for the sheaf-level situation of Stacks 0AYB: the difference of the two Chern-class cycles equals the sum of the principal divisors of the tame symbols

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsRelativeNormalization.hasEtaleLocalProperty_isReduced
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYF.** The normalization of an algebraic space `X` in a reduced algebraic space
`Y` is reduced.

Reducedness is asked of an algebraic space as the étale-local property of schemes of Tag 03E6.
The reduction of the normalization is constructed here rather than taken as an input: it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.reduction`, the reduced induced structure of Tag 03IQ on the whole
point set of `X'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEtaleLocalProperty_isReduced (hnorm : IsRelativeNormalization B S hS f ν f')
    (hX' : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X') (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T) :
    HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X' fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_localRingDimension_eq_zero_pointsMap_toNormalizationInQcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYG.**  Let `f : Y ⟶ X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` and let `Y ⟶ X' ⟶ X` be the normalization of `X` in `Y`
(Stacks 0822).  Every point `x'` of `|X'|` of codimension `0` (Stacks 04NA) is the image under
`f' : Y ⟶ X'` of a point of `|Y|` of codimension `0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_localRingDimension_eq_zero_pointsMap_toNormalizationInQcqs
    (x' : points B S hS (normalizationInQcqs B S hS f hfqc hfqs).1)
    (hx' : localRingDimension B S hS x' = 0) :
    ∃ y : points B S hS Y.1, localRingDimension B S hS y = 0 ∧
      pointsMap B S hS Y.1 (toNormalizationInQcqs f hfqc hfqs).hom y = x'
declarations.comment: the printed word schemes is read as algebraic spaces, as the section, the notation |X'|, |Y| and the reference to 04NA require; codimension 0 is localRingDimension = 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffine_isNormal_isIntegral_etaleChart
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYH.** Let `X` be a normal integral algebraic space over `S`. Every point of
`|X|` is in the image of an étale morphism to `X` from a normal integral affine scheme.

An affine étale chart through the point is shrunk to an affine open which is normal and
integral by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isAffineOpen_isNormal_isIntegral_of_isAffine_etaleChart`,
and that open is an object of the chosen big site by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.exists_affineOpen_restrict`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffine_isNormal_isIntegral_etaleChart (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hnormal : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun Y : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsNormal Y))
    (hintegral : IsIntegralSpace B S hS X) (x : points B S hS X) :
    ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (φ : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X),
      IsAffine ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
      IsNormal ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
      IsIntegral ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
      (MorphismProperty.presheaf (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS))) φ ∧
      x ∈ Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj U) φ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_fSharp_and_connectedPullback_of_isNormal_of_isIntegralSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYI.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` such that

1. `f` is proper,
2. `Y` is integral (Stacks 0AD4, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsIntegralSpace`) with generic point `ξ`,
3. `Y` is normal,
4. `X` is reduced,
5. every generic point of an irreducible component of `|X|` maps to `ξ`,
6. `H⁰(X_ξ, 𝒪) = κ(ξ)`: for the monomorphism `Spec κ(ξ) ⟶ Y` from the spectrum of the residue
   field at `ξ` (Stacks 0EMW) and the fibre `X_ξ = X ×_Y Spec κ(ξ)`, pullback of global functions
   `κ(ξ) = Γ(Spec κ(ξ), 𝒪) ⟶ Γ(X_ξ, 𝒪)` along the projection is bijective.

Then

* `f_* 𝒪_X = 𝒪_Y`: the canonical map `𝒪_Y ⟶ f_* 𝒪_X` (Stacks 03G8) is an isomorphism;
* `f` has geometrically connected fibres: for every field `k` and every morphism `Spec k ⟶ Y`, the
  fibre `X ×_Y Spec k` has connected point space.  Taking `Spec k ⟶ Spec κ(y) ⟶ Y` for the field
  extensions `k` of the residue field at a point `y`, this says that the fibre `X_y` is
  geometrically connected over `κ(y)`.

Normality and reducedness are the étale-local properties of schemes of Stacks 03E6, as elsewhere
in the library.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_fSharp_and_connectedPullback_of_isNormal_of_isIntegralSpace
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hf : IsProper B S hS f.hom) (hYint : IsIntegralSpace B S hS Y.1)
    {ξ : points B S hS Y.1} (hξ : IsGenericPoint ξ Set.univ)
    (hYnormal : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsNormal T))
    (hXred : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced T))
    (hgen : ∀ x ∈ genericPoints (points B S hS X.1), pointsMap B S hS X.1 f.hom x = ξ)
    (h6 : Function.Bijective (globalFunctionsMap B S hS (pullback.snd f
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (residueFieldMorphism B S hS Y.1 hYint.2.1 ξ) :
        schemeSpace ((residueFieldRepresentative B S hS Y.1 hYint.2.1 ξ).1.siteObject B S hS Y.1) ⟶
          Y)))) :
    IsIso (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f).fSharp ∧
      ∀ p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS Y.1,
        ConnectedPullback B S hS f.hom (fieldMorphism B S hS Y.1 p)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isIntegralModification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYJ, case (1).** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a Noetherian local domain of dimension at
least one and let `f : X → Spec A` be a modification. Then the special fibre `X_κ` has
dimension at most `dim(A) - 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isIntegralModification [IsDomain A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] (hdim : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hS X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hS))
    (hf : IsIntegralModification B (Spec (.of A)) hS hX
      (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B (Spec (.of A)) hS _)
      (isIntegralSpace_yoneda_baseTerminal A B hS) f) :
    dimension B (Spec (.of A)) hS
        (fieldFibre B (Spec (.of A)) hS f (residueFieldPoint A B hS))
        (isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre hX (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B (Spec (.of A)) hS _) f
          (residueFieldPoint A B hS)) + 1
      ≤ ringKrullDim A
declarations.comment: case (1), f a modification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYJ, case (4).** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a Noetherian local domain of dimension at
least one and let `f : X → Spec A` be a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite
type, with `X` decent, such that the points of `|X|` lying over the generic point of `Spec A`
are exactly the generic points of the irreducible components of `|X|`. Then the special fibre
`X_κ` has dimension at most `dim(A) - 1`.

The bound is proved one point of `X_κ` at a time: base change identifies the dimension of
`X_κ` at a point with the relative dimension of `f` over the closed point there, an affine
étale chart turns that into the dimension of the fibre of an affine scheme of finite type over
`Spec A`, and the generic hypothesis transported to the chart is the hypothesis of the
commutative-algebra bound on the special fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hdim : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hgen : ∀ x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X,
      x ∈ genericPoints (points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X) ↔
        pointsToScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA)
            (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X f x) = genericPoint (Spec (.of A)))
    (hfib : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA
      (fieldFibre B (Spec (.of A)) hA f (residueFieldPoint A B hA))) :
    dimension B (Spec (.of A)) hA
        (fieldFibre B (Spec (.of A)) hA f (residueFieldPoint A B hA)) hfib + 1
      ≤ ringKrullDim A
declarations.comment: case (4), X decent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isIntegralSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYJ, case (3).** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a Noetherian local domain of dimension at
least one and let `f : X → Spec A` be a morphism of algebraic spaces which is locally of finite
type, with `X` integral, such that exactly one point of `|X|` lies over the generic point of
`Spec A`. Then the special fibre `X_κ` has dimension at most `dim(A) - 1`.

This is case (4): an integral algebraic space is decent and its space of points is
irreducible, so its generic points are the points whose closure is everything, and there is
one of them because the points of codimension zero are dense. The image of such a point both
specialises to and generalises the generic point of `Spec A`, hence equals it, and uniqueness
identifies it with the point lying over the generic point. Quasi-separatedness, which the
source also assumes, is not needed for this reduction.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isIntegralSpace
    [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (hdim : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hone : ∃! x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X,
      pointsToScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA)
        (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X f x) = genericPoint (Spec (.of A)))
    (hfib : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA
      (fieldFibre B (Spec (.of A)) hA f (residueFieldPoint A B hA))) :
    dimension B (Spec (.of A)) hA
        (fieldFibre B (Spec (.of A)) hA f (residueFieldPoint A B hA)) hfib + 1
      ≤ ringKrullDim A
declarations.comment: case (3), X integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYJ, case (4)**, with the algebraicity of the special fibre supplied rather than
assumed: it is the base change of `f` along the residue-field point, so
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre_residueFieldPoint` provides it and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim' [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hdim : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f)
    (hdec : IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hgen : ∀ x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X,
      x ∈ genericPoints (points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X) ↔
        pointsToScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA)
            (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X f x) = genericPoint (Spec (.of A))) :
    dimension B (Spec (.of A)) hA
        (fieldFibre B (Spec (.of A)) hA f (residueFieldPoint A B hA))
        (isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre_residueFieldPoint A B hA hX f) + 1
      ≤ ringKrullDim A
declarations.comment: case (4), X decent, at the source's hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isIntegralSpace'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYJ, case (3)**, with the algebraicity of the special fibre supplied rather than
assumed, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre_residueFieldPoint`; this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isIntegralSpace` with
that witness.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isIntegralSpace'
    [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (hdim : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA))
    (hf : IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f)
    (hint : IsIntegralSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (hone : ∃! x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X,
      pointsToScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA)
        (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X f x) = genericPoint (Spec (.of A))) :
    dimension B (Spec (.of A)) hA
        (fieldFibre B (Spec (.of A)) hA f (residueFieldPoint A B hA))
        (isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre_residueFieldPoint A B hA hX f) + 1
      ≤ ringKrullDim A
declarations.comment: case (3), X integral, at the source's hypotheses

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isAlteration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYJ, case (2).** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a Noetherian local domain of dimension at
least one and let `f : X → Spec A` be an alteration of algebraic spaces, Stacks 0ADA. Then the
special fibre `X_κ` has dimension at most `dim(A) - 1`.

This is case (3). An alteration is proper, hence locally of finite type, and its source is
integral, so all that is needed is that exactly one point of `|X|` lies over the generic point
of `Spec A`. Being an alteration, `f` is quasi-finite at the generic point of `|X|` by
Stacks 0ADB, and condition (5) of Stacks 0AD5 turns that into the statement that the generic
point is the only point of `|X|` above the generic point of `|Spec A|`; the comparison map
from the points of the representable base to `Spec A` is injective, so that is uniqueness of
the point above `genericPoint (Spec A)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isAlteration
    [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (hdim : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA))
    (halt : IsAlteration B (Spec (.of A)) hA f) :
    dimension B (Spec (.of A)) hA
        (fieldFibre B (Spec (.of A)) hA f (residueFieldPoint A B hA))
        (isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre_residueFieldPoint A B hA
          (halt.isAlgebraicSpace_source B (Spec (.of A)) hA) f) + 1
      ≤ ringKrullDim A
declarations.comment: case (2), f an alteration

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_alteration_or_generic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYJ.** Let `(A, 𝔪, κ)` be a Noetherian local domain of dimension at least one
and let `f : X → Spec A` be a morphism of algebraic spaces satisfying at least one of: (1) `f`
is a modification, Stacks 0AD8; (2) `f` is an alteration, Stacks 0ADA; (3) `f` is locally of
finite type, `X` is integral, and exactly one point of `|X|` maps to the generic point of
`Spec A`; (4) `f` is locally of finite type, `X` is decent, and the points of `|X|` mapping to
the generic point of `Spec A` are the generic points of the irreducible components of `|X|`.
Then the special fibre `X_κ` has dimension at most `dim(A) - 1`.

The source's hypothesis is this disjunction, and the four clauses are four theorems (clause (1)
is `dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isIntegralModification`,
the others are above), so the proof is the case distinction. Clause (1) needs no decency witness:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsIntegralModification` derives it from the integrality it asserts.
The source also assumes `f`
quasi-separated in clause (3); that is omitted, because
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_isIntegralSpace`
does not need it.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_fieldFibre_add_one_le_ringKrullDim_of_alteration_or_generic
    [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (hdim : 1 ≤ ringKrullDim A)
    {X : (BigFppfOver B (Spec (.of A)) hA)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X)
    (f : X ⟶ yoneda.obj (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA))
    (hf :
      IsIntegralModification B (Spec (.of A)) hA hX
        (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B (Spec (.of A)) hA _)
        (isIntegralSpace_yoneda_baseTerminal A B hA) f ∨
      IsAlteration B (Spec (.of A)) hA f ∨
      (IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f ∧
        IsIntegralSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X ∧
        ∃! x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X,
          pointsToScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA)
            (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X f x) = genericPoint (Spec (.of A))) ∨
      (IsLocallyOfFiniteType B (Spec (.of A)) hA f ∧
        IsDecentSpace B (Spec (.of A)) hA X ∧
        ∀ x : points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X,
          x ∈ genericPoints (points B (Spec (.of A)) hA X) ↔
            pointsToScheme B (Spec (.of A)) hA (baseTerminal B (Spec (.of A)) hA)
              (pointsMap B (Spec (.of A)) hA X f x) = genericPoint (Spec (.of A)))) :
    dimension B (Spec (.of A)) hA
        (fieldFibre B (Spec (.of A)) hA f (residueFieldPoint A B hA))
        (isAlgebraicSpace_fieldFibre_residueFieldPoint A B hA hX f) + 1
      ≤ ringKrullDim A

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isRegularSection_iff_forall_associatedPoint_notMem_maximalSmul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AYL.** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme, `L` an invertible
`𝒪_X`-module and `s ∈ Γ(X, L)`. Then `s` is a regular section if and only if `s` does not vanish
at any associated point of `X`, i.e. its germ at every associated point avoids `𝔪_x L_x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularSection_iff_forall_associatedPoint_notMem_maximalSmul
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian X] (L : X.Modules)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property L]
    (s : L.sections) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsRegularSection X.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property s ↔
      ∀ x ∈ schemeAssociatedPoints X,
        (L.presheaf.Γgerm x).hom (s.eval (op ⊤)) ∉ Stacks.ModuleStalk.maximalSmul L x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleSheafGeneral.exists_effectiveCartierDivisors_tensor_invertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AYM**, the general clause. On a Noetherian scheme `X` carrying an
ample invertible module `ℒ`, every invertible `𝒪_X`-module `𝒩` is the sheaf `𝒪_X(D - D')` of a
difference of two effective Cartier divisors, and `D` and `D'` may both be chosen disjoint from
any prescribed finite subset `E` of `X`.

`𝒩 ≅ 𝒪_X(D - D') = 𝒪_X(D) ⊗ 𝒪_X(D')^{⊗ -1}` is stated here in the equivalent multiplicative
form `𝒩 ⊗ 𝒪_X(D') ≅ 𝒪_X(D)`; see the module documentation. The case `D' = ∅` for `X`
quasi-affine is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effectiveCartierDivisor_invertibleSheaf_of_isQuasiAffine`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_effectiveCartierDivisors_tensor_invertibleSheaf [IsNoetherian X] (L : X.Modules)
    [IsInvertibleModule X L] (hL : IsAmple X L) (N : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X N]
    {E : Set X} (hE : E.Finite) :
    ∃ D D' : X.IdealSheafData,
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D ∧
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D' ∧
      Disjoint E D.supportSet ∧ Disjoint E D'.supportSet ∧
      Nonempty ((N ⊗ Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' D' : X.Modules) ≅
        Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' D)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_effectiveCartierDivisor_invertibleSheaf_of_isQuasiAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AYM**, the quasi-affine clause. On a Noetherian quasi-affine scheme
every invertible `𝒪_X`-module `𝒩` is isomorphic to the invertible sheaf `𝒪_X(D)` of an effective
Cartier divisor `D`, and `D` may be chosen disjoint from any prescribed finite subset `E` of `X`.
This is the case `D' = ∅` of the general statement `𝒩 ≅ 𝒪_X(D - D')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_effectiveCartierDivisor_invertibleSheaf_of_isQuasiAffine
    [IsNoetherian X] [X.IsQuasiAffine] (N : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj X.ringCatSheaf.property N]
    {E : Set X} (hE : E.Finite) :
    ∃ D : X.IdealSheafData,
      Stacks.Divisors.IsEffectiveCartierDivisor D ∧
      Disjoint E D.supportSet ∧
      Nonempty (N ≅ Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' D)
declarations.comment: quasi-affine case with empty negative divisor

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveBundleSplitting.exists_modification_hasInvertibleFiltration'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AYP.** Let `X` be an integral scheme and `ℰ` a finite locally free
`𝒪_X`-module of rank `r`. There is a modification `f : X' ⟶ X` such that `f^*ℰ` has a filtration
`0 = ℰ_0 ⊆ ℰ_1 ⊆ … ⊆ ℰ_r = f^*ℰ` by finite locally free submodules whose successive quotients
are invertible `𝒪_{X'}`-modules.

This is `exists_modification_hasInvertibleFiltration_of_epi` with its one input, the epimorphy
of the tautological map of a projective bundle, supplied by `epi_tautologicalMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_modification_hasInvertibleFiltration' (r : ℕ) (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
    (E : X.Modules)
    (hE : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (f : X' ⟶ X), IsModification f ∧
      HasInvertibleFiltration X' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E) r

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree
declarations.doc:
The degree of a finite locally free sheaf of constant rank on a proper scheme of
dimension at most one over a field.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def curveDegree (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (_hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E : X.Modules) (rank : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E rank] : ℤ
declarations.comment: finite locally free case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.invertibleCurveDegree
declarations.doc:
The degree of an invertible sheaf on a proper scheme of dimension at most one over a
field: its Euler characteristic minus the Euler characteristic of the structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def invertibleCurveDegree (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (_hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (L : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L] : ℤ
declarations.comment: invertible case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_add_of_shortExact_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field and let `X` be a scheme proper over `k` of dimension at most one. For a
short exact sequence `0 ⟶ ℰ₁ ⟶ ℰ₂ ⟶ ℰ₃ ⟶ 0` of locally free `𝒪_X`-modules of finite constant
ranks `r₁`, `r₂`, `r₃`, `deg(ℰ₂) = deg(ℰ₁) + deg(ℰ₃)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem curveDegree_add_of_shortExact_of_isProper (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (S : ShortComplex X.Modules) (hS : S.ShortExact) (r₁ r₂ r₃ : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} S.X₁ r₁]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} S.X₂ r₂]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} S.X₃ r₃] :
    curveDegree k f hdim S.X₂ r₂ =
      curveDegree k f hdim S.X₁ r₁ + curveDegree k f hdim S.X₃ r₃
declarations.comment: deg(ℰ₂) = deg(ℰ₁) + deg(ℰ₃) for a short exact sequence of locally free modules of finite constant rank on a proper scheme of dimension at most one over a field

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_add_of_shortExact_of_cohomologyFiniteDimensional
declarations.doc:
**Additivity of the degree along a short exact sequence.** For a short exact sequence
`0 ⟶ ℰ₁ ⟶ ℰ₂ ⟶ ℰ₃ ⟶ 0` of finite locally free `𝒪_X`-modules of constant ranks `r₁`, `r₂`, `r₃`
on a scheme `X` proper over a field `k` and of dimension at most one,
`deg(ℰ₂) = deg(ℰ₁) + deg(ℰ₃)`.

The single hypothesis `hfin` is [Stacks, Tag 02O6] for `X`; everything else the source uses —
additivity of the Euler characteristic, additivity of the constant rank, and the empty
scheme — is discharged. `hfin` is now itself a theorem, so the tag is additionally registered on
the form that takes no finiteness hypothesis at all,
`AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_add_of_shortExact_of_isProper` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Variety/Curve/DegreeAdditivityUnconditional.lean`, which applies
this theorem to
`AlgebraicGeometry.forall_finiteDimensional_cohomologyOverField_of_isProper`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem curveDegree_add_of_shortExact_of_cohomologyFiniteDimensional (k : Type u)
    [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (hfin : CohomologyFiniteDimensionalOverFieldOn k f) (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (S : ShortComplex X.Modules) (hS : S.ShortExact) (r₁ r₂ r₃ : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} S.X₁ r₁]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} S.X₂ r₂]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} S.X₃ r₃] :
    curveDegree k f hdim S.X₂ r₂ =
      curveDegree k f hdim S.X₁ r₁ + curveDegree k f hdim S.X₃ r₃
declarations.comment: deg(ℰ₂) = deg(ℰ₁) + deg(ℰ₃); `hfin` is [Stacks, Tag 02O6] for `X`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_generatingSections_of_support_dim_le_zero
declarations.doc:
A coherent sheaf with support of dimension at most zero on a locally Noetherian
scheme is generated by global sections.

This is also clause (1) of Stacks 0AYT, in a form more general than that clause states it: Stacks
0AYT takes `X` proper over a field `k`, which gives `IsLocallyNoetherian X` through
`LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian`, so the condition here is strictly weaker than the
clause's and the clause follows by instantiation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_generatingSections_of_support_dim_le_zero
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hF : topologicalKrullDim (SheafOfModules.supp F) ≤ 0) :
    Nonempty F.GeneratingSections
declarations.comment:
(1), ℱ is generated by global sections.  Stated for a locally Noetherian X, which
is weaker than the clause's `X proper over a field k` (properness gives IsLocallyNoetherian via
LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian), so the clause follows by instantiation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.suppStalkDirectSumAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYT] (2): `H⁰(X, ℱ)` is the direct sum of the stalks of `ℱ` along its
support.** For `f : X ⟶ Spec k` proper and `ℱ` coherent on `X` with `dim (supp ℱ) ≤ 0`,

  `Γ(X, ℱ) ≅ ⨁_{x ∈ Supp ℱ} ℱ_x`

as abelian groups, the isomorphism being the one assembled from the germ maps
(`AlgebraicGeometry.suppGermHom`) followed by the identification of the product of a finite
family with its direct sum.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def suppStalkDirectSumAddEquiv :
    Γ(F, ⊤) ≃+ ⨁ x : ↥(_root_.SheafOfModules.supp F), (Scheme.Modules.presheaf F).stalk x.1
declarations.comment: (2), at the `Γ(ℱ, ⊤)` spelling of `H⁰(X, ℱ)`; the `H⁰` spelling is `AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyOverFieldZeroEquivDirectSumSuppStalk`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyOverFieldZeroEquivDirectSumSuppStalk
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYT] (2), read at `H⁰(X, ℱ)`.** Composing
`AlgebraicGeometry.suppStalkDirectSumAddEquiv` with the identification of degree-zero cohomology
with global sections gives

  `H⁰(X, ℱ) = ⨁_{x ∈ Supp ℱ} ℱ_x`.

It is an `Equiv` rather than an additive equivalence because
`AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyOverFieldZeroEquivSections`, the only identification of
`H⁰(X, ℱ)` with `Γ(ℱ, ⊤)` this library has, is one: `Γ(ℱ, ⊤)` carries no `Module k` instance
and the comparison is stated at the level of types. The additive structure of the decomposition
is in `AlgebraicGeometry.suppStalkDirectSumAddEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cohomologyOverFieldZeroEquivDirectSumSuppStalk :
    (cohomologyOverField k f F 0 : Type u) ≃
      ⨁ x : ↥(_root_.SheafOfModules.supp F), (Scheme.Modules.presheaf F).stalk x.1
declarations.comment: (2), at the `H⁰(X, ℱ)` spelling; the additive structure of the same decomposition is on `AlgebraicGeometry.suppStalkDirectSumAddEquiv`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cohomologyOverField_of_topologicalKrullDim_supp_le_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYT] (3): the higher cohomology of a coherent module whose support has
dimension at most zero vanishes.** For `f : X ⟶ Spec k` proper and `ℱ` coherent on `X` with
`dim (supp ℱ) ≤ 0`, the `k`-vector space `Hⁱ(X, ℱ)` is zero for every `i > 0`.

The module is the direct image of a coherent module on its scheme-theoretic support
([Stacks, Tag 02OM]), that support is affine, Serre vanishing ([Stacks, Tag 01XB]) kills the
higher cohomology there, and a closed immersion does not change cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_cohomologyOverField_of_topologicalKrullDim_supp_le_zero (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent]
    (hF : topologicalKrullDim (_root_.SheafOfModules.supp F) ≤ 0) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    IsZero (cohomologyOverField k f F i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.eulerCharacteristic_eq_finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_of_supp_le_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYT] (4): the Euler characteristic of a coherent module whose support has
dimension at most zero is the dimension of its space of global sections.** For
`f : X ⟶ Spec k` proper and `ℱ` coherent on `X` with `dim (supp ℱ) ≤ 0`,

  `χ(X, ℱ) = dim_k H⁰(X, ℱ)`.

This is the source's "we have (4) by definition of the Euler characteristic `χ(X, ℱ)` and (3)":
`AlgebraicGeometry.eulerCharacteristic` is by definition the alternating sum
`∑ⁿ (-1)ⁿ dim_k Hⁿ(X, ℱ)`, clause (3) kills every term with `n > 0`, and a sum supported on `{0}`
is its value there.
declarations.statement:
theorem eulerCharacteristic_eq_finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_of_supp_le_zero (k : Type u)
    [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (F : X.Modules)
    [F.IsCoherent] (hF : topologicalKrullDim (_root_.SheafOfModules.supp F) ≤ 0) :
    eulerCharacteristic k f F = (Module.finrank k (cohomologyOverField k f F 0) : ℤ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_eulerCharacteristic_tensorSheaf_eq_rank_mul
declarations.doc:
**Clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0AYT].** Let `k` be a field, `X` a proper scheme over `k` and
`ℱ` a coherent sheaf with `dim Supp ℱ ≤ 0`. Then

  `χ(X, ℱ ⊗ ℰ) = n · χ(X, ℱ)`

for every locally free module `ℰ` of rank `n`.

This is the clause in the argument order the source writes it in, with the coherent factor
first; the Euler
characteristic requires its argument to be coherent, so the conclusion also supplies that. The
other order, which the chain above this clause consumes, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_eulerCharacteristic_tensorSheaf_eq_mul_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank`,
and the two differ by `Stacks.SheafOfModules.TensorPresentations.tensorSheafSwap`.

The clause string is on the attribute because the other four clauses of Tag 0AYT are not proved
here: clause (1) is registered on
`AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_generatingSections_of_support_dim_le_zero`, and clauses (2), (3) and
(4) in `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Cohomology.ZeroDimensionalSupport.Vanishing`, on
`AlgebraicGeometry.suppStalkDirectSumAddEquiv` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyOverFieldZeroEquivDirectSumSuppStalk`, on
`AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_cohomologyOverField_of_topologicalKrullDim_supp_le_zero` and on
`AlgebraicGeometry.eulerCharacteristic_eq_finrank_cohomologyOverField_zero_of_supp_le_zero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eulerCharacteristic_tensorSheaf_eq_rank_mul [IsProper f] (F : X.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsCoherent F]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (_root_.SheafOfModules.supp F) ≤ 0) (E : X.Modules) (n : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E n] :
    ∃ h : ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨((X.toRingedSpace)).presheaf,
        ((X.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F)).obj (E))).IsCoherent,
      @eulerCharacteristic k _ X f _ ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨((X.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((X.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (F)).obj (E))) h =
        (n : ℤ) * eulerCharacteristic k f F
declarations.comment: tensor_rank

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_pullback_eq_of_bijOn_genericPointsOne
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYU], the "more generally" statement.** Let `k` be a field and let
`g : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism over `k` between schemes proper over `k` and of dimension at most one
which induces a bijection between the generic points of the one-dimensional irreducible
components of `X'` and those of `X`, and isomorphisms of local rings at the points of `X'`
involved. Let `ℰ` be finite locally free of constant rank `n` on `X`. Then

`deg(g^*ℰ) = deg(ℰ)`.

`hbij` and `hstalk` are the tag's own hypotheses — the bijection on the generic points of the
one-dimensional components and the isomorphisms of local rings at the corresponding points — and
the source's "more generally" clause implies its first, birational, sentence, which is not
separately derived here. The finiteness input [Stacks, Tag 02O6] over a field is not assumed: it
is `AlgebraicGeometry.cohomologyFiniteDimensionalOverField_of_isProper`. The projection formula
[Stacks, Tag 01E8] at `g`, the source's displayed equation `g_*g^*ℰ ≅ ℰ ⊗_{𝒪_X} g_*𝒪_{X'}`, is
proved rather than assumed, by `projectionFormula_iso_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank` above.

The proof is the source's. The bijection on generic points makes `g` finite, so the cohomology of
`X'` is read on `X` through `g_*`; the isomorphisms of local rings make the kernel and the
cokernel of `𝒪_X ⟶ g_*𝒪_{X'}` vanish at the generic points of the one-dimensional components,
hence give them zero-dimensional support, so clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0AYT] applies at both;
and the computation of `CurveDegreeInvariance/Basic.lean` collapses the difference of the two
degrees to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_pullback_eq_of_bijOn_genericPointsOne (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (p' : X' ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProper p'] [IsProper p]
    (hdimX' : topologicalKrullDim (X' : Type u) ≤ 1)
    (hdimX : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1)
    (g : X' ⟶ X) (hgOver : g ≫ p = p')
    (hbij : Set.BijOn g (genericPointsOne X') (genericPointsOne X))
    (E : X.Modules) (n : ℕ) [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E n]
    (hstalk : ∀ z ∈ genericPointsOne X', IsIso (g.stalkMap z)) :
    @curveDegree k _ X' p' _ hdimX' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj E) n
        (isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback g E n) =
      curveDegree k p hdimX E n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_pullback_eq_of_bijOn_genericPointsOne_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYU], the "more generally" statement, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's
own.** Let `k` be a field and let `g : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism over `k` between schemes proper
over `k` and of dimension at most one which induces a bijection between the generic points of
the one-dimensional irreducible components of `X'` and those of `X`, and isomorphisms of the
local rings at the points of `X'` involved. Let `ℰ` be finite locally free of constant rank `n`
on `X`. Then

`deg(g^*ℰ) = deg(ℰ)`.

`hbij` and `hstalk` are the tag's own hypotheses, and they are all that
`curveDegree_pullback_eq_of_bijOn_genericPointsOne` takes: [Stacks, Tag 02O6] over a field and
the projection formula at `g` are proved there rather than carried.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_pullback_eq_of_bijOn_genericPointsOne_of_isProper (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X' X : Scheme.{u}} (p' : X' ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsProper p'] [IsProper p]
    (hdimX' : topologicalKrullDim (X' : Type u) ≤ 1)
    (hdimX : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1)
    (g : X' ⟶ X) (hgOver : g ≫ p = p')
    (hbij : Set.BijOn g (genericPointsOne X') (genericPointsOne X))
    (E : X.Modules) (n : ℕ) [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E n]
    (hstalk : ∀ z ∈ genericPointsOne X', IsIso (g.stalkMap z)) :
    @curveDegree k _ X' p' _ hdimX' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj E) n
        (isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback g E n) =
      curveDegree k p hdimX E n
declarations.comment: the 'more generally' statement, with no hypothesis beyond the tag's own

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_eulerCharacteristic_tensorSheaf_eq_fiberRank_mul_curveDegree_add_of_isCurve
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYV], with no hypothesis.** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper curve
over `k` with generic point `ξ`, let `ℰ` be finite locally free of rank `n` and let `ℱ` be
coherent. Then

`χ(X, ℰ ⊗ ℱ) = r·deg(ℰ) + n·χ(X, ℱ)`,

where `r = dim_{κ(ξ)} ℱ_ξ` is the rank of `ℱ` at the generic point.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_eulerCharacteristic_tensorSheaf_eq_fiberRank_mul_curveDegree_add_of_isCurve

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegreeDevissage.curveDegree_eq_finsum_componentDegree
declarations.doc:
The degree of a finite locally free module of constant rank on a scheme proper over a field
and of dimension at most one is the multiplicity-weighted sum of its degrees on the reduced
one-dimensional components:

`deg(ℰ) = ∑ᶠ ξ, m(ξ) · deg(ℰ|_{C(ξ)})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_eq_finsum_componentDegree [IsProper f]
    (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E : X.Modules) (rank : ℕ)
    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E rank] :
    curveDegree k f hX E rank =
      ∑ᶠ ξ : genericPointsOne X,
        (componentMultiplicity X ξ : ℤ) * componentDegree k f hX E rank ξ

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegreeDevissage.exists_curveDegree_eq_finsum
declarations.doc:
The component formula for the degree in existential form: each reduced one-dimensional
component is proper over the base, has dimension at most one and carries a restriction of `ℰ`
that is again finite locally free of the same rank, and the component formula holds with respect
to those three proofs.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_curveDegree_eq_finsum [IsProper f]
    (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E : X.Modules) (rank : ℕ)
    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E rank] :
    ∃ (hproper : ∀ ξ : genericPointsOne X, IsProper (reducedComponentι X ξ ≫ f))
      (hdimC : ∀ ξ : genericPointsOne X, topologicalKrullDim (reducedComponent X ξ) ≤ 1)
      (hrank : ∀ ξ : genericPointsOne X,
        _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (reducedComponentι X ξ)).obj E) rank),
      curveDegree k f hX E rank =
        ∑ᶠ ξ : genericPointsOne X,
          (componentMultiplicity X ξ : ℤ) *
            @curveDegree k _ (reducedComponent X ξ) (reducedComponentι X ξ ≫ f)
              (hproper ξ) (hdimC ξ)
              ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (reducedComponentι X ξ)).obj E) rank (hrank ξ)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegrees.curveDegree_eq_finsum_componentDegree_of_stalk_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AYW**, with the first paragraph of the source proof discharged from the
reduction to a finite family of closed subschemes.

The family `Zs` is the source's `Xᵢ`, the scheme-theoretic closures of the complements of the
other components, enumerated by `0, …, N - 1`; `σ` picks out the member attached to a given
one-dimensional component, and `hzero` says the remaining members — the zero-dimensional
components — contribute nothing.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_eq_finsum_componentDegree_of_stalk_bijective
    {Zs : ℕ → Scheme.{u}} (ι : ∀ j, Zs j ⟶ X) [∀ j, IsClosedImmersion (ι j)] (N : ℕ)
    (σ : genericPointsOne X → Fin N) (hσ : Function.Injective σ)
    (Z : Set X) (hZfin : Z.Finite) (hZcl : ∀ x ∈ Z, IsClosed ({x} : Set X))
    (hbij : ∀ x ∉ Z, Function.Bijective (ConcreteCategory.hom
      ((_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.stalkAddCommGroupFunctor X.ringCatSheaf x).map
        (Scheme.Modules.pushforwardUnitSeriesMap ι N))))
    (hirreducible : ∀ ξ : genericPointsOne X,
      @curveDegree k _ (Zs (σ ξ)) (ι (σ ξ) ≫ f) _
          (le_trans (IsClosedImmersion.isClosedEmbedding
            (ι (σ ξ))).isInducing.topologicalKrullDim_le hX)
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (ι (σ ξ))).obj E) rank
          (_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback (ι (σ ξ)) E rank) =
        (componentMultiplicity X ξ : ℤ) * componentDegree k f hX E rank ξ)
    (hzero : ∀ j : Fin N, (∀ ξ : genericPointsOne X, σ ξ ≠ j) →
      @curveDegree k _ (Zs j) (ι j ≫ f) _
        (le_trans (IsClosedImmersion.isClosedEmbedding
          (ι j)).isInducing.topologicalKrullDim_le hX)
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (ι j)).obj E) rank
        (_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback (ι j) E rank) = 0) :
    curveDegree k f hX E rank =
      ∑ᶠ ξ : genericPointsOne X,
        (componentMultiplicity X ξ : ℤ) * componentDegree k f hX E rank ξ
declarations.comment: the component formula, from the reduction to the irreducible case

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ComponentDegrees.curveDegree_eq_finsum_componentDegree_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYW].** The degree of a finite locally free module of constant rank on a
proper scheme of dimension at most one over a field is the multiplicity-weighted sum of its
degrees on the reduced one-dimensional components.

The four steps are: the degree is the quantity `D(𝒫) = χ(𝒫 ⊗ ℰ) − n·χ(𝒫)` of
[Stacks, Tag 0AYU] at `𝒫 = 𝒪_X`; `D` is additive along the dévissage of [Stacks, Tag 01YF]
applied to `𝒪_X`; at each layer `D` is the weighted sum of the component degrees, the weights
being the lengths of the layer at the generic points; and those lengths add up to the
multiplicities.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_eq_finsum_componentDegree_of_isProper (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f] (hX : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (E : X.Modules) (rank : ℕ)
    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E rank] :
    _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree k f hX E rank =
      ∑ᶠ ξ : genericPointsOne X,
        (componentMultiplicity X ξ : ℤ) * componentDegree k f hX E rank ξ
