declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_tensorSheaf_eq_add
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYX] on a proper curve.** For `ℰ` and `𝒱` finite locally free of constant
ranks `n` and `m` on a proper curve over a field,

`deg(ℰ ⊗ 𝒱) = m · deg(ℰ) + n · deg(𝒱)`.

**No hypothesis beyond the source's own**, apart from the curve hypothesis discussed in the
module docstring. The rank of the tensor product is
`AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_tensorSheaf`, and the two instances
of [Stacks, Tag 02O6] over a field that [Stacks, Tag 0AYV] needs are supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.forall_finiteDimensional_cohomologyOverField_of_isProper`.

The proof is the arithmetic of [Stacks, Tag 0AYX]: the Euler characteristic of `ℰ ⊗ 𝒱` is
`m · deg(ℰ) + n · χ(𝒱)` by [Stacks, Tag 0AYV], whose rank input is the fibre rank of `𝒱` at the
generic point and hence `m`; every degree is then unfolded into Euler characteristics by
`AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_eq_eulerCharacteristic_sub`, where the identity is linear
arithmetic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem curveDegree_tensorSheaf_eq_add
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve k f] [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E V : X.Modules) (n m : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E n]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} V m] :
    @curveDegree k _ X f _ hdim
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
          ⟨((X.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((X.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (E)).obj (V))) (n * m)
        (SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_tensorSheaf X E V n m) =
      (m : ℤ) * curveDegree k f hdim E n + (n : ℤ) * curveDegree k f hdim V m
declarations.comment: on a proper curve; the whole tag, on a proper scheme of dimension at most one, is AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_tensorSheaf_eq_add_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_tensorSheaf_eq_add_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one
declarations.doc:
For `ℰ` and `𝒱` finite locally free of constant ranks `n` and `m` on a scheme `X` proper of
dimension at most one over a field `k`,

`deg(ℰ ⊗ 𝒱) = m · deg(ℰ) + n · deg(𝒱)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_tensorSheaf_eq_add_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsProper f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E V : X.Modules) (n m : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E n]
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} V m] :
    @curveDegree k _ X f _ hdim
        ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor ⟨((X.toRingedSpace)).presheaf,
            ((X.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (E)).obj (V))) (n * m)
        (SheafOfModules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_tensorSheaf X E V n m) =
      (m : ℤ) * curveDegree k f hdim E n + (n : ℤ) * curveDegree k f hdim V m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_and_curveDegree_tensorSheaf_invertibleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AYY].** Let `k` be a field, let `X` be a proper scheme of dimension at most
one over `k` and let `D` be an effective Cartier divisor on `X`. Then `D` is finite over
`Spec(k)`, of degree

`deg(D) = dim_k Γ(D, 𝒪_D)`,

and for a finite locally free `ℰ` of rank `n`,

`deg(ℰ(D)) = n · deg(D) + deg(ℰ)`,  where `ℰ(D) = ℰ ⊗_{𝒪_X} 𝒪_X(D)`.

The three assertions are about one and the same number `dim_k Γ(D, 𝒪_D)`: it is the rank of the
finite locally free morphism `D ⟶ Spec(k)` — which is what "finite of degree `deg(D)`" asserts —
and it is the coefficient of `n` in the twist formula.

Finiteness and the degree are `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_divisorSubscheme` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_divisorSubscheme`. The twist formula is
[Stacks, Tag 0AYX], i.e.
`AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_tensorSheaf_eq_add_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one`,
at `ℰ` and `𝒪_X(D)`, whose `deg(𝒪_X(D))` term is
`AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_invertibleSheaf_eq_finrank_globalSections`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFinite_and_curveDegree_tensorSheaf_invertibleSheaf (E : X.Modules) (n : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E n] :
    letI : Algebra k Γ(D.subscheme, ⊤) :=
      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ (D.subschemeι ≫ f).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
    IsFinite (D.subschemeι ≫ f) ∧
      Stacks.Morphisms.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank (D.subschemeι ≫ f)
          (Module.finrank k Γ(D.subscheme, ⊤)) ∧
        @curveDegree k _ X f _ hdim
            ((((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor
              ⟨((X.toRingedSpace)).presheaf, ((X.toRingedSpace)).IsSheaf⟩).obj (E)).obj
              ((Stacks.Divisors.invertibleSheaf' D)))) n
            (isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_tensorSheaf_invertibleSheaf D E n) =
          (n : ℤ) * (Module.finrank k Γ(D.subscheme, ⊤) : ℤ) + curveDegree k f hdim E n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_pullback_eq_degreeOver_mul
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a nonconstant morphism of proper curves over `k` and
let `ℰ` be a finite locally free `𝒪_Y`-module of constant rank `n`. Then

`deg(f^*ℰ) = deg(X/Y)·deg(ℰ)`,

where `deg(X/Y) = [R(X) : R(Y)]` is `AlgebraicGeometry.degreeOver` ([Stacks, Tag 02NY]) and `deg`
is `AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree` ([Stacks, Tag 0AYR]).
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_pullback_eq_degreeOver_mul (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (πX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (πY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k πX] [IsCurve k πY] [IsProper πX] [IsProper πY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ πY = πX) (hnc : ¬ ∃ y : Y, ∀ x : X, f.base x = y)
    (E : Y.Modules) (n : ℕ) [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E n] :
    @curveDegree k _ X πX _ (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := πX)))
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E) n (isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback f E n) =
      (@degreeOver X Y f _ _ (locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k πX πY f hf)
          (isDominant_of_not_constant k πX πY f hnc) : ℤ) *
        curveDegree k πY (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := πY))) E n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_pullback_eq_degreeOver_mul_of_isFiniteLocallyFree
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a nonconstant morphism of proper curves over `k` and
let `ℰ` be a finite locally free `𝒪_Y`-module. Then

`deg(f^*ℰ) = deg(X/Y)·deg(ℰ)`,

where `deg(X/Y) = [R(X) : R(Y)]` is `AlgebraicGeometry.degreeOver` ([Stacks, Tag 02NY]) and `deg`
is `AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree` ([Stacks, Tag 0AYR]), both degrees taken at the fibre rank of
`ℰ` at the generic point of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_pullback_eq_degreeOver_mul_of_isFiniteLocallyFree (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (πX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (πY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsCurve k πX] [IsCurve k πY] [IsProper πX] [IsProper πY]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ πY = πX) (hnc : ¬ ∃ y : Y, ∀ x : X, f.base x = y)
    (E : Y.Modules)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) E] :
    letI _hrank : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E
        (Scheme.Modules.fiberRank E (genericPoint (Y : Type u))) :=
      Scheme.Modules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_of_fiberRank_eq E
        (Scheme.Modules.fiberRank E (genericPoint (Y : Type u)))
        (genericPoint (Y : Type u)) rfl
    @curveDegree k _ X πX _ (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := πX)))
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj E)
        (Scheme.Modules.fiberRank E (genericPoint (Y : Type u)))
        (isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pullback f E
          (Scheme.Modules.fiberRank E (genericPoint (Y : Type u)))) =
      (@degreeOver X Y f _ _ (locallyOfFiniteType_of_isCurve_comp k πX πY f hf)
          (isDominant_of_not_constant k πX πY f hnc) : ℤ) *
        curveDegree k πY (le_of_eq (IsCurve.topologicalKrullDim_eq_one (f := πY))) E
          (Scheme.Modules.fiberRank E (genericPoint (Y : Type u)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowDegree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AZ1.** The degree homomorphism `A_0(X) ⟶ ℤ` on the zeroth Chow group
of a scheme `X` proper over a one-point base with vanishing dimension function — the spectrum of a
field.

This is the definition of Stacks 0AZ1 verbatim: proper pushforward `p_* : A_0(X) ⟶ A_0(S)` of
Stacks 0GU8, which exists by Stacks 02S2
(`Stacks.Chow.properPushforwardFactorsThroughRationalEquivalence_of_isProper`), composed with the
identification `A_0(S) = ℤ` of `Stacks.Chow.chowGroupBaseEquivInt`, which sends the fundamental
cycle of the base to one.
declarations.statement: def chowDegree (s : C.S) : chowGroup C p 0 →+ ℤ
declarations.comment: the degree homomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.chowGroupBaseEquivInt
declarations.doc:
For a one-point base with vanishing dimension function — the spectrum of a field — the
degree of a zero cycle is an isomorphism `A_0(S) ≅ ℤ`, sending the fundamental cycle to `1`.
declarations.statement: def chowGroupBaseEquivInt (s : C.S) : chowGroup C (𝟙 C.S) 0 ≃+ ℤ
declarations.comment: the identification of the Chow group of the base with the integers

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.cycleDegree_eq_sum_finrank
declarations.doc:
The degree `Stacks.Chow.cycleDegree` of a zero cycle on a scheme proper over a field,
presented as a finite sum `α = ∑ n_i [Z_i]` over integral closed subschemes of delta-dimension
zero, is `∑ n_i dim_k Γ(Z_i, 𝒪_{Z_i})`, where `dim_k Γ(Z_i, 𝒪_{Z_i})` is the degree of
`Z_i → Spec(k)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycleDegree_eq_sum_finrank [IsProper p] (s : (fieldChowSituation k).S)
    (α : CycleGroup (fieldChowSituation k) p 0) {J : Type*} [Fintype J]
    (W : J → X.IdealSheafData) (hW : ∀ i, IsIntegral (W i).subscheme) (n : J → ℤ)
    (hDim : ∀ i, schemeDeltaDimension (fieldChowSituation k) ((W i).subschemeι ≫ p) = (0 : EInt))
    (hα : α.1 = ∑ i, @Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.single X _ ℤ (Classical.decEq X) _
      (genericPointOf (W i) (hW i)) (n i)) :
    cycleDegree (fieldChowSituation k) p s α =
      ∑ i : J, n i *
        (letI : Algebra k Γ((W i).subscheme, ⊤) :=
          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ ((W i).subschemeι ≫ p).appTop).hom.toAlgebra
        (Module.finrank k Γ((W i).subscheme, ⊤) : ℤ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.curveDegree_eq_chowDegree_firstChernCapOnCycles_fundamental
declarations.doc:
**Equation [Stacks, Tag 0BRY]**, in the orientation of the source:
`deg(ℰ) = deg(c₁(ℰ) ∩ [X]_1)` for `ℰ` finite locally free of constant rank on a proper scheme of
dimension at most one over a field, with `c₁(ℰ) ∩ -` the operation of Stacks 02U5 at the Chern
classes of Stacks 02U0 and `deg` the degree of Stacks 0AZ1.

Two conventions are fixed here. In rank zero Stacks 02U5 defines no `c₁`; the total Chern class
of a module of rank zero is `1`, so `c₁ = 0`, and `GenuineChern.firstChernCapOnCycles` is zero
there by definition. The operation of Stacks 02U5 extends `[W] ↦ i_*(c₁(i^*ℰ) ∩ [W])` over
cycles through representatives of the classes of Stacks 02U0 (`GenuineChern.chowRep`); the choice
does not matter here, since `[X]_1` is a finite sum of fundamental cycles of one-dimensional
components and on each the class is the one of Stacks 02U0
(`GenuineChern.chernCapOnCycles_integral_cycle`).
declarations.statement:
theorem curveDegree_eq_chowDegree_firstChernCapOnCycles_fundamental
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1) (E : X.Modules) (r : ℕ)
    [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u} E r] :
    curveDegree k p hdim E r =
      chowDegree (fieldChowSituation k) (fieldChowSituation_dimensionFunction_eq_zero k) p
        (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)
        (chowGroupCast (fieldChowSituation k) p (show (1 : ℤ) - 1 = 0 by simp)
          (GenuineChern.firstChernCapOnCycles (fieldChowSituation k) p E r 1
            (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) p (𝟙 X) 1)))

declarations.name: tor_finite_of_noetherian
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring and let `M`, `N` be finite
`R`-modules. Then `Tor_p^R(M, N)` is a finite `R`-module for every `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tor_finite_of_noetherian (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (M N : ModuleCat.{u} R) [Module.Finite R M] [Module.Finite R N] (p : ℕ) :
    Module.Finite R (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} R) p).obj M).obj N)

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.properPushforward_coherentSheafCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AZD.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of varieties over a field `k` and let
`F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose support has dimension at most `n`. Then proper pushforward
of `n`-cycles carries the cycle of `F` to the cycle of its direct image: `f_* [F]_n = [f_* F]_n`.

This is Stacks 02R6 at the Chow situation `Stacks.Chow.fieldChowSituation k`, whose base is
`Spec k` and whose dimension function vanishes; over that base the delta-dimension of the
support of `F` is its dimension.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_coherentSheafCycle (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (sX : X ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [IsVariety k sX]
    (sY : Y ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [IsVariety k sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsCoherent] (n : ℤ)
    (hFn : schemeDeltaDimension (fieldChowSituation k)
      ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ sX) ≤ (n : EInt)) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sY
    haveI := ProperCoherenceWitness.isCoherent_pushforward f F
    properPushforward (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY f hf n
        (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf (fieldChowSituation k) sX F n hFn) =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf (fieldChowSituation k) sY
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F) n
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforward_le
          (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY f hf F hFn)
declarations.comment: cycle identity for a coherent sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.properPushforward_closedSubschemeCycle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AZD.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a proper morphism of varieties over a field `k` and let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed subscheme of dimension at most `n`. Then proper pushforward of
`n`-cycles carries the cycle of `Z` to the cycle of the direct image of its structure sheaf:
`f_* [Z]_n = [f_* 𝒪_Z]_n`.

Here `𝒪_Z` is read as the coherent `𝒪_X`-module `i_* 𝒪_Z`, and `f_* 𝒪_Z` as the direct image of
that module along `f`. This is Stacks 02R6, part (1), at the Chow situation
`Stacks.Chow.fieldChowSituation k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem properPushforward_closedSubschemeCycle (k : Type u) [Field k] {Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [IsVariety k sX]
    (sY : Y ⟶ (fieldChowSituation k).S) [IsVariety k sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f]
    (hf : f ≫ sY = sX) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (n : ℤ)
    (hZ : schemeDeltaDimension (fieldChowSituation k) (i ≫ sX) ≤ (n : EInt)) :
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian X := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX
    haveI : IsLocallyNoetherian Y := LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sY
    haveI := ProperCoherenceWitness.isCoherent_pushforward f
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))
    properPushforward (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY f hf n
        (cycleAssociatedToClosedSubscheme (fieldChowSituation k) sX i n) =
      cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf (fieldChowSituation k) sY
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))) n
        (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforward_le (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY f hf
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (Ample.unitModule Z))
          (schemeDeltaDimension_reducedSupport_pushforwardStructureSheaf_le
            (fieldChowSituation k) sX i hZ))
declarations.comment: closed subscheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_of_isVariety
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AZF.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a flat morphism of varieties over a field `k` and set
`r = dim X - dim Y`. If `F` is a coherent sheaf on `Y` whose support has dimension at most `k`,
then

`f^*[F]_k = [f^*F]_{k+r}`.

The dimension of the support is read as the delta-dimension of the base situation `Spec k`, which
over a field is the dimension; see
`Stacks.Chow.flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_of_isVariety'` for the topological
form.
declarations.statement:
theorem flatPullback_cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf_of_isVariety (k : Type u) [Field k]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsVariety k sX] [IsVariety k sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f] (hbase : f ≫ sY = sX) (r : ℕ)
    (hr : topologicalKrullDim X = topologicalKrullDim Y + (r : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (F : Y.Modules) [hF : F.IsCoherent] (j : ℤ)
    (hFj : schemeDeltaDimension (fieldChowSituation k)
      ((reducedSupport F).subschemeι ≫ sY) ≤ (j : EInt)) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType f := locallyOfFiniteType_of_isVariety_comp k sX sY f hbase
    flatPullback (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY f hbase r
        (relativeDimension_of_flat_of_isVariety k sX sY f hbase r hr) j
        (cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf (fieldChowSituation k) sY F j hFj) =
      @cycleAssociatedToCoherentSheaf X (fieldChowSituation k) sX inferInstance
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F)
        (@AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback X Y
          (LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian sX) f F hF)
        (j + (r : ℤ))
        (schemeDeltaDimension_support_pullback_le (fieldChowSituation k) sX sY f hbase r
          (relativeDimension_of_flat_of_isVariety k sX sY f hbase r hr) F j hFj)

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.closedPointFibreDifferences
declarations.doc:
The basic rational equivalences of Section 43.8: the differences `[W_a]ₖ - [W_b]ₖ`, for `a`,
`b` an arbitrary pair of distinct closed points of `ℙ¹` and `W ⊆ X ×_S ℙ¹_S` an integral closed
subscheme of relative dimension `k + 1` contained in neither `X × a` nor `X × b`.
declarations.statement:
def closedPointFibreDifferences (Kf : Type u) [Field Kf] [IsAlgClosed Kf]
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (hC : C.S = AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of Kf))
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ) :
    Set (CycleGroup C p k)
declarations.comment: the basic rational equivalences `[W_a]_k - [W_b]_k` of Section 43.8, over an ARBITRARY pair of distinct closed points `a`, `b` of `P^1`. A closed point is a point of `P^1` whose singleton is closed, `X × a` is the image of `Stacks.Chow.closedPointSection`, and the fibre `W_a` is the scheme-theoretic preimage of `W` along that section, viewed as a closed subscheme of `X` as the source does. Proper intersection of an integral `W` of relative dimension `k + 1` with `X × a` and `X × b` is expressed by asking that `W` be contained in neither.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints
declarations.doc:
The group of `k`-cycles rationally equivalent to zero of Section 43.8: the subgroup of
`Zₖ(X)` generated by the differences `[W_a]ₖ - [W_b]ₖ` over all pairs of distinct closed points
of `ℙ¹`, that is, the cycles `∑ nᵢ([W_{i, aᵢ}]ₖ - [W_{i, bᵢ}]ₖ)`.
declarations.statement:
def rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints (Kf : Type u) [Field Kf] [IsAlgClosed Kf]
    (C : ChowSituation.{u}) (hC : C.S = AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of Kf))
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] (k : ℤ) :
    AddSubgroup (CycleGroup C p k)
declarations.comment: the group of `k`-cycles rationally equivalent to zero of Section 43.8, the cycles `∑ nᵢ([W_{i, aᵢ}]_k - [W_{i, bᵢ}]_k)` with an ARBITRARY pair of distinct closed points `aᵢ`, `bᵢ` of `P^1` for each `i`, as in `Stacks.Chow.closedPointFibreDifferences`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints_eq_rationalEquivalencesByFibres
declarations.doc:
**The traditional choice `a = 0`, `b = ∞` gives the same group.** On a variety over an
algebraically closed field the group of `k`-cycles rationally equivalent to zero of Section 43.8,
built from arbitrary pairs of distinct closed points of `ℙ¹`, is generated by the fibre
differences `Stacks.Chow.fibreDifferences` at the single pair `0`, `∞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints_eq_rationalEquivalencesByFibres (Kf : Type u)
    [Field Kf] [IsAlgClosed Kf] (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (hC : C.S = AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of Kf)) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsVariety Kf (p ≫ eqToHom hC)] (k : ℤ) :
    rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints Kf C hC p k = rationalEquivalencesByFibres C p k
declarations.comment: the remark of Section 43.8 that the pair of closed points may be moved to any pair we like, the traditional choice being `a = 0`, `b = ∞`: the group `Stacks.Chow.rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints` built from arbitrary pairs of distinct closed points equals the group `Stacks.Chow.rationalEquivalencesByFibres` built from the pair `0`, `∞`. The source moves the pair by the 2-transitivity of the automorphism group of `P^1`; here the equality goes through the group of cycles rationally equivalent to zero of Chow homology, which both groups equal.

declarations.name: Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorCycles_subset_and_closure_eq_rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AZI.** Let `X` be a variety over an algebraically closed field, and
let `k` be an integer. The principal divisor `div_V(f)` of a nonzero rational function `f` on an
integral closed subscheme `V ⊆ X` of dimension `k + 1`, viewed as a `k`-cycle on `X`, is
rationally equivalent to zero in the sense of Section 43.8; conversely these principal divisors
generate the group of `k`-cycles rationally equivalent to zero in that sense.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalDivisorCycles_subset_and_closure_eq_rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints
    (Kf : Type u) [Field Kf] [IsAlgClosed Kf] (C : ChowSituation.{u})
    (hC : C.S = AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (CommRingCat.of Kf)) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : X ⟶ C.S) [LocallyOfFiniteType p]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsVariety Kf (p ≫ eqToHom hC)] (k : ℤ) :
    principalDivisorCycles C p k ⊆ rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints Kf C hC p k ∧
      AddSubgroup.closure (principalDivisorCycles C p k) =
        rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints Kf C hC p k
declarations.comment: both assertions, against the group of Section 43.8 (`Stacks.Chow.rationalEquivalencesByClosedPoints`, generated by `[W_a]_k - [W_b]_k` over ARBITRARY pairs of distinct closed points `a`, `b` of `P^1`): every principal divisor `div_W(f)` of a nonzero rational function on a `(k + 1)`-dimensional integral closed subscheme `W ⊆ X` lies in it, and the subgroup these principal divisors generate is all of it. `X` is a variety over an algebraically closed field `Kf`; principal divisors are pushed forward to cycles on `X` as `Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorPushforward`, and `principal divisor` is `Stacks.Chow.principalDivisorCycles`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isVariety_and_topologicalKrullDim_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AZM.** Let `X` and `Y` be varieties over an algebraically closed
field `k`. Then the product `X ×_{Spec k} Y` is a variety and its dimension is the sum of the
dimensions of `X` and of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isVariety_and_topologicalKrullDim_pullback (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsVariety k f] [IsVariety k g] :
    IsVariety k (pullback.fst f g ≫ f) ∧
      topologicalKrullDim ↑(pullback f g) = topologicalKrullDim X + topologicalKrullDim Y
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, both of its conclusions: for `X` and `Y` varieties over an algebraically closed field `k` — the source's own hypothesis, and one the first conclusion needs, since over a field that is not algebraically closed a product of two varieties can be reducible (`AlgebraicGeometry.gaussianRationals_product_not_isVariety` below) — the product `X ×_{Spec k} Y`, with structure morphism the first projection followed by the structure morphism of `X`, is again a variety, AND its dimension is `dim X + dim Y`. A variety is `AlgebraicGeometry.IsVariety`: integral, separated, locally of finite type and quasi-compact over the field, so the first conclusion carries the integrality and separatedness of the product. Dimensions are `topologicalKrullDim`, valued in `WithBot ℕ∞`, and the formula is an equation there. The first conclusion is also Stacks 05P3, `AlgebraicGeometry.isVariety_pullback`; the second holds over an arbitrary field, `AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_pullback_of_isVariety`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_component_pullback_lower_bounds
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AZN.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of varieties over a field, let
`Z ⊆ Y` be a closed subvariety, presented by the ideal sheaf `I`, and let `W` be an irreducible
component of the scheme-theoretic inverse image `f⁻¹(Z) = X ×_Y Z`. Then:

1. if `f` is a regular immersion of codimension `c`, then `dim Z ≤ dim W + c`, that is, `W` has
   dimension at least `dim Z - c`;
2. if `f` is a local complete intersection morphism of relative dimension `r`, and `Z` has
   dimension `d`, then `W` has dimension `m` with `d + r ≤ m`.

Dimensions are `topologicalKrullDim`, valued in `WithBot ℕ∞`, which has no subtraction: the
source's `dim W ≥ d - c` in part (1) is accordingly a relation between the two dimensions,
`dim Z ≤ dim W + c`. In part (2) the relative dimension `r` is an integer, negative for a
regular immersion, so there the two dimensions are produced as the natural numbers they are and
`d + r ≤ m` is an inequality in `ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem topologicalKrullDim_component_pullback_lower_bounds
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [IsVariety k sX] [IsVariety k sY] (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ sY = sX)
    (I : Y.IdealSheafData) [IsIntegral I.subscheme]
    (W : Set (pullback f I.subschemeι : Scheme.{u}))
    (hW : W ∈ irreducibleComponents (pullback f I.subschemeι : Scheme.{u})) :
    (∀ [IsImmersion f], Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.IsRegularImmersion f →
        ∀ (c : ℕ) [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
          (Stacks.Conormal.conormalSheaf f) c],
          topologicalKrullDim I.subscheme ≤ topologicalKrullDim W + (c : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
      (∀ r : ℤ, IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphismOfRelativeDimension f r →
        ∃ d m : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim I.subscheme = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧
          topologicalKrullDim W = (m : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ (d : ℤ) + r ≤ (m : ℤ))
declarations.comment: both bounds in one statement, for a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of varieties over a field, a closed subvariety `Z ⊆ Y` presented by an ideal sheaf, and `W` an irreducible component of the scheme-theoretic inverse image `f⁻¹(Z) = X ×_Y Z`. (1) when `f` is a regular immersion whose conormal sheaf is finite locally free of rank `c` — the source's codimension — `dim Z ≤ dim W + c`; (2) when `f` is a local complete intersection morphism of relative dimension `r`, in the sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphismOfRelativeDimension`, `d + r ≤ m` for `d = dim Z` and `m = dim W`. The regular-immersion data of (1) and the local complete intersection data of (2) are the source's own, and each binds inside its own clause, as in the source. Dimensions are `topologicalKrullDim`, valued in `WithBot ℕ∞`, which has no subtraction, so the source's `dim W ≥ d - c` is spelled as the relation `dim Z ≤ dim W + c`; in (2) the relative dimension is an integer and may be negative, so the two dimensions are produced as the natural numbers they are — both are transcendence degrees of residue fields over the base field — and `d + r ≤ m` is an inequality in `ℤ`. The two bounds are `AlgebraicGeometry.topologicalKrullDim_le_component_pullback_add_of_isRegularImmersion` and `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphismOfRelativeDimension.exists_add_le_topologicalKrullDim`. The relative-dimension condition here replaces `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOfRelativeDimension`, which imposes its rank condition also over the empty open and is therefore unsatisfiable for `r ≥ 1`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.add_topologicalKrullDim_le_add_topologicalKrullDim_of_irreducibleComponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0AZP.** Let `X` be a nonsingular variety over an algebraically closed
field and let `V, W ⊆ X` be closed subvarieties of dimensions `r` and `s`. Then every irreducible
component `Z` of `V ∩ W` satisfies `r + s ≤ dim X + dim Z`, that is, has dimension at least
`r + s - dim X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem add_topologicalKrullDim_le_add_topologicalKrullDim_of_irreducibleComponent
    [IsAlgClosed k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsVariety k f] (hX : IsRegular X)
    (I J : X.IdealSheafData) [IsIntegral I.subscheme] [IsIntegral J.subscheme]
    (Z : Set ↥((I.support : Set X) ∩ (J.support : Set X)))
    (hZ : Z ∈ irreducibleComponents ↥((I.support : Set X) ∩ (J.support : Set X))) :
    topologicalKrullDim I.subscheme + topologicalKrullDim J.subscheme ≤
      topologicalKrullDim X + topologicalKrullDim Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IntersectProperly
declarations.doc:
Two irreducible closed subsets of a scheme **intersect properly** when their intersection
has at most the expected dimension, namely `dim (W ∩ V) ≤ dim W + dim V - dim X`.
declarations.statement: public def IntersectProperly (W V : IrreducibleCloseds X) : Prop
declarations.comment: closed subvarieties

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicCycle.IntersectProperly
declarations.doc:
Two algebraic cycles **intersect properly** when every pair of components occurring in them
with a nonzero coefficient intersects properly.
declarations.statement: public def IntersectProperly {R : Type*} [Zero R] (α β : AlgebraicCycle X R) : Prop
declarations.comment: cycles

declarations.name: Stacks.Intersection.intersectionMultiplicity
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AZR.** The intersection multiplicity `e(X, V · W, Z)` of two closed subschemes of a
scheme at a point: the alternating sum `∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ length Torᵢ(𝒪_W, 𝒪_V)` of the lengths of the
`Tor` modules of their local rings over the local ring of the ambient scheme. For `V` and `W`
closed subvarieties of a nonsingular variety which intersect properly and `x` the generic point
of an irreducible component `Z` of `V ∩ W`, this is the coefficient of `Z` in `V · W`.
declarations.statement: def intersectionMultiplicity {X : Scheme.{u}} (V W : X.IdealSheafData) (x : X) : ℚ
declarations.comment: the definition of the intersection multiplicity `e(X, V · W, Z)`, the displayed alternating sum of lengths of the local `Tor` modules `Torᵢ^{𝒪_{X, Z}}(𝒪_{V, Z}, 𝒪_{W, Z})` over the local ring at the generic point of `Z`, formed for two quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals at a point of any scheme. Its agreement with the coefficient of `Z` in the intersection product is `AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.subvarietyIntersectionProduct_apply`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.subvarietyIntersectionProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AZR: the intersection product of two closed subvarieties.** Let `X` be a regular
scheme of dimension `n`, locally of finite type over a field, and let `W`, `V` be closed
subvarieties of dimensions `s` and `r` which intersect properly. Their intersection product is
the cycle

`W · V = ∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ [Torᵢ^{𝒪_X}(𝒪_W, 𝒪_V)]_{r + s - n}`.

Each summand is a cycle because the `Tor` sheaves are coherent and supported in dimension at most
`r + s - n` (`schemeDeltaDimension_torSheaf_subvariety_le_sub`), and only the summands with
`i ≤ n` are nonzero (`subvarietyIntersectionProduct_eq_sum`).
declarations.statement:
def subvarietyIntersectionProduct (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (sX : X ⟶ (Stacks.Chow.fieldChowSituation K).S) [LocallyOfFiniteType sX]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (hX : IsRegular X) (W V : IrreducibleCloseds X) {r s n : ℕ}
    (hW : topologicalKrullDim (W : Set X) = (s : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hV : topologicalKrullDim (V : Set X) = (r : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hXd : topologicalKrullDim X = (n : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hWV : AlgebraicGeometry.IntersectProperly W V) : AlgebraicCycle X ℤ
declarations.comment: the definition of the intersection product `W · V = ∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ [Torᵢ^{𝒪_X}(𝒪_W, 𝒪_V)]_{r + s - dim X}` of two closed subvarieties `W`, `V` of dimensions `s` and `r` of a nonsingular variety `X` which intersect properly, from the source's data alone: the support bound that makes each `[Torᵢ]_{r + s - dim X}` a cycle is proved from proper intersection by `schemeDeltaDimension_torSheaf_subvariety_le_sub`. The ambient scheme is any regular scheme of finite dimension locally of finite type over a field.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.subvarietyIntersectionProduct_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AZR: `W · V = ∑ e(X, V · W, Z) [Z]`.** Let `X` be a nonsingular variety of dimension
`n` over an algebraically closed field and let `W`, `V` be closed subvarieties of dimensions `s`
and `r` which intersect properly. Then the cycle `W · V` is the formal linear combination of the
irreducible components `Z` of `V ∩ W` with coefficients the intersection multiplicities
`e(X, V · W, Z) = ∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ length_{𝒪_{X, Z}} Torᵢ^{𝒪_{X, Z}}(𝒪_{V, Z}, 𝒪_{W, Z})`: its
coefficient at the generic point of such a component is `e(X, V · W, Z)`, and at every other
point it is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem subvarietyIntersectionProduct_apply (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsAlgClosed K]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsVariety K sX] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (hX : IsRegular X) (W V : IrreducibleCloseds X) {r s n : ℕ}
    (hW : topologicalKrullDim (W : Set X) = (s : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hV : topologicalKrullDim (V : Set X) = (r : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hXd : topologicalKrullDim X = (n : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hWV : AlgebraicGeometry.IntersectProperly W V) (z : X) :
    open Classical in
    (subvarietyIntersectionProduct K sX hX W V hW hV hXd hWV z : ℚ) =
      if z ∈ (W : Set X) ∩ (V : Set X) ∧
          ∀ y ∈ (W : Set X) ∩ (V : Set X), z ∈ closure ({y} : Set X) → y = z then
        Stacks.Intersection.intersectionMultiplicity
          (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal ⟨(V : Set X), V.isClosed⟩)
          (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal ⟨(W : Set X), W.isClosed⟩) z
      else 0
declarations.comment: the description of the intersection product `V · W` as the formal linear combination `∑ e_Z Z` of the irreducible components `Z` of `V ∩ W` with coefficients the intersection multiplicities `e_Z = e(X, V · W, Z) = ∑ᵢ (-1)ⁱ length Torᵢ^{𝒪_{X, Z}}(𝒪_{W, Z}, 𝒪_{V, Z})`, the multiplicity being `Stacks.Intersection.intersectionMultiplicity` at the generic point of `Z` (the lengths of `Torᵢ(𝒪_{W, Z}, 𝒪_{V, Z})` and `Torᵢ(𝒪_{V, Z}, 𝒪_{W, Z})` agree). The generic points of the components of `V ∩ W` are the points of `V ∩ W` that are a specialization of no other point of `V ∩ W`, and the components all have dimension `r + s - dim X` by Tag 0AZP.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.derivedCategoryBMinus_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AZS] part (2).** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme. If `K` and `L` are
in `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)` then so is `K ⊗ᴸ_{𝒪_X} L`.

Being in `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)` is equivalent to being pseudo-coherent ([Stacks, Tag 08E8]), and the
derived tensor product of two pseudo-coherent objects is pseudo-coherent
([Stacks, Tag 09J3]). Reading the equivalence backwards needs the cohomology sheaves of the
derived tensor product to be quasi-coherent, which is [Stacks, Tag 08DX]; the bound above is
`a + b` for bounds `a` and `b` of the two factors.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryBMinus_derivedTensor (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (K L : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus (fun F : X.Modules => F.IsCoherent) K)
    (hL : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus (fun F : X.Modules => F.IsCoherent) L) :
    DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryBMinus (fun F : X.Modules => F.IsCoherent)
      (((derivedTensor X).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: part (2): D⁻_Coh is closed under the derived tensor product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.isCoherent_torSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AZS] part (1).** Let `X` be a locally Noetherian scheme. If `ℱ` and `𝒢` are
coherent `𝒪_X`-modules then so is `Tor_p^{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)` for every `p`.

A coherent module placed in degree `0` lies in `D⁻_Coh(𝒪_X)`, so part (2) applies to the two
factors and every cohomology sheaf of their derived tensor product is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_torSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (F G : X.Modules)
    (hF : F.IsCoherent) (hG : G.IsCoherent) (p : ℕ) : (torSheaf X F G p).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: part (1): the Tor sheaves of two coherent modules are coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.supp_torSheaf_subset_inter
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AZT]: the Tor sheaves are supported on `Supp(ℱ) ∩ Supp(𝒢)`.** Away from
the support of either factor the corresponding stalk vanishes, and then so does the stalk of
every `Tor_p^{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)`.

No hypothesis on `X` or on the two modules is needed: the argument is the stalkwise computation
of the derived tensor product on K-flat representatives.
declarations.statement:
theorem supp_torSheaf_subset_inter (X : Scheme.{u}) (F G : X.Modules) (p : ℕ) :
    SheafOfModules.supp (torSheaf X F G p) ⊆
      SheafOfModules.supp F ∩ SheafOfModules.supp G
declarations.comment: the Tor sheaves are supported on the intersection of the supports of the two modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.isCoherent_torSheaf_of_isRegular
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0AZT]: the Tor sheaves of two coherent modules on a regular scheme are
coherent.** A regular — that is, nonsingular — scheme is locally Noetherian, by the
characterization of regularity as local Noetherianity together with regularity of all the local
rings, so [Stacks, Tag 0AZS] part (1) applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_torSheaf_of_isRegular (X : Scheme.{u}) (hX : IsRegular X)
    (F G : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsCoherent) (hG : G.IsCoherent) (p : ℕ) :
    (torSheaf X F G p).IsCoherent
declarations.comment: the Tor sheaves of two coherent modules on a regular scheme are coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.torSheafStalkIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AZT: the stalk of a Tor sheaf is the Tor module of the stalks.** For `𝒪_X`-modules
`ℱ` and `𝒢` on a scheme `X` and a point `x`, the stalk at `x` of `Tor_p^{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)` is
`Tor_p^{𝒪_{X, x}}(ℱ_x, 𝒢_x)`. No hypothesis on `X`, `ℱ` or `𝒢` is needed.
declarations.statement:
def torSheafStalkIso (X : Scheme.{u}) (F G : X.Modules) (p : ℕ) (x : X) :
    letI : MonoidalCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := RingCat.{u})
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.sheaf).obj x)) :=
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlatStalkCriterion.monoidalStalkModuleCat X.sheaf x
    letI : MonoidalPreadditive (ModuleCat.{u} (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := RingCat.{u})
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.sheaf).obj x)) :=
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.KFlatStalkCriterion.monoidalPreadditiveStalkModuleCat X.sheaf x
    (Scheme.Modules.stalkFunctor X x).obj (torSheaf X F G p) ≅
      ((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := RingCat.{u})
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.sheaf).obj x)) p).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.stalkFunctor X x).obj F)).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.stalkFunctor X x).obj G)
declarations.comment: the stalk clause: the stalk at `x` of `Tor_p^{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)` is the Tor module `Tor_p^{𝒪_{X, x}}(ℱ_x, 𝒢_x)` of the two stalks over the local ring, with no hypothesis on the scheme or the two modules. The local ring is the `RingCat`-valued stalk of the structure sheaf, which is the ring the stalk functor takes its modules over. The coherence and support clauses are `isCoherent_torSheaf_of_isRegular` and `supp_torSheaf_subset_inter`; the vanishing clause for `p > dim X` is NOT carried, see the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.TorFormula.isZero_torSheaf_of_lt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0AZT: the Tor sheaves of a regular scheme vanish above its dimension.** If every
local ring of `X` is regular and `dim X ≤ d`, then `Tor_p^{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢) = 0` for every `p > d` and
all `𝒪_X`-modules `ℱ`, `𝒢`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_torSheaf_of_lt (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hreg : ∀ x : X, IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (F G : X.Modules) (d p : ℕ) (hd : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hdp : d < p) :
    IsZero (torSheaf X F G p)
declarations.comment: the vanishing clause: on a scheme all of whose local rings are regular and whose dimension is at most `d`, the Tor sheaf `Tor_p^{𝒪_X}(ℱ, 𝒢)` vanishes for `p > d`. The source states it for a nonsingular variety with the bound `dim X`, which is the case `d = dim X` of this; the bound is a parameter here because the dimension of a general scheme need not be finite. No hypothesis on the two modules is needed, where the source assumes them coherent. The coherence, support and stalk clauses are `isCoherent_torSheaf_of_isRegular`, `supp_torSheaf_subset_inter` and `torSheafStalkIso`.

declarations.name: Ideal.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity
declarations.doc:
The Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity `e_I(M, d)`: `d !` times the coefficient of degree `d`
of the rational polynomial eventually computing `length_R (M / I ^ (n + 1) M)`.

When `R` is Noetherian local, `M` is finite, `I` is an ideal of definition, and `d` is at
least the dimension of the support of `M`, this is zero if the inequality is strict and is
`d !` times the leading coefficient otherwise.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def Ideal.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (d : ℕ) : ℚ
declarations.comment: the multiplicity `e_I(M, d)`

declarations.name: Ideal.hilbertSamuelMultiplicityOfModule
declarations.doc:
The multiplicity `e_I(M)` of `M` for `I`, obtained by taking the coefficient in the
Hilbert–Samuel degree of `M`. For a finite module over a Noetherian local ring that degree is the
dimension of the support (`Module.hilbertSamuelDegree_eq_supportDim`), so this is
`e_I(M, dim(Supp(M)))`. The zero module, of degree `-∞`, is read in degree zero, where its
multiplicity is zero.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable abbrev Ideal.hilbertSamuelMultiplicityOfModule {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    [IsLocalRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : ℚ
declarations.comment: the multiplicity `e_I(M)`

declarations.name: Ideal.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity_additive_of_exact
declarations.doc:
Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity in degree `d` is additive in a short exact sequence of
finite modules, provided `d` is at least the dimension of the support of the middle term.
declarations.statement:
theorem hilbertSamuelMultiplicity_additive_of_exact
    {R M' M M'' : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module.Finite R M']
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    [AddCommGroup M''] [Module R M''] [Module.Finite R M'']
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : IsIdealOfDefinition I) (d : ℕ)
    {f : M' →ₗ[R] M} {g : M →ₗ[R] M''}
    (hf : Function.Injective f) (hfg : Function.Exact f g) (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    (hd : Module.supportDim R M ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    I.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity M d =
      I.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity M' d + I.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity M'' d

declarations.name: Ideal.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity_eq_finsum_localizedLength_mul
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be an ideal of definition in a Noetherian local ring `R`, and let `M` be a
finite `R`-module. In every degree at least the dimension of the support of `M`, its
Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity is the sum, over primes `p` with `dim(R / p)` equal to that
degree, of the multiplicity of `R / p` weighted by `length_{R_p}(M_p)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hilbertSamuelMultiplicity_eq_finsum_localizedLength_mul
    {R M : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : IsIdealOfDefinition I) (d : ℕ)
    (hd : Module.supportDim R M ≤ d) :
    I.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity M d =
      ∑ᶠ p : {p : PrimeSpectrum R // ringKrullDim (R ⧸ p.asIdeal) = d},
        ((Module.length (Localization.AtPrime p.1.asIdeal)
          (LocalizedModule p.1.asIdeal.primeCompl M)).toNat : ℚ) *
          I.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity (R ⧸ p.1.asIdeal) d

registrations.name: Polynomial.fwdDiff_iter_degree_eq_factorial
registrations.comment: the `r`-th forward difference of `P` is `r! a`

registrations.name: fwdDiff_iter_eq_sum_shift
registrations.comment: the `r`-th forward difference as the alternating sum, at `t - r`

declarations.name: Ideal.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity_eq_alternatingSum_koszulHomology_length
declarations.doc:
If an ideal of definition `I` is generated by `f : Fin r → A`, then its Hilbert–Samuel
multiplicity in degree `r` on a finite module is the Euler characteristic of the homology of
the Koszul complex on `f` with coefficients in that module.
declarations.statement:
theorem hilbertSamuelMultiplicity_eq_alternatingSum_koszulHomology_length
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (M : Type*)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    (hI : IsIdealOfDefinition I) (hf : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f)) :
    I.hilbertSamuelMultiplicity M r =
      ∑ i : Fin (r + 1), (-1 : ℚ) ^ (i : ℕ) *
        ((Module.length A ((Koszul.seqComplexTensor f M).homology (i : ℕ))).toNat : ℚ)
